desc: The script processes a vector point layer and a land cover raster (landcover.tif) to generate individual clipped raster images (PNG format) centered on each point, where each clip is bounded by a 1000-meter buffer around the point and constrained to the extent of the input raster. It first filters the point layer by feature ID, creates a buffer, intersects the buffer with the raster’s spatial extent to ensure alignment, then uses that intersection geometry as a mask to clip the land cover raster — outputting one PNG file per point (e.g., '001.png', '002.png') in the user's Documents folder.

name: Compute terrain slope from DEM rasters
desc: The script processes a batch of local GeoTIFF raster files (assumed to be digital elevation models) by first checking their data type and CRS; if the raster is in a geographic CRS (e.g., WGS84), it reprojects it to EPSG:2180 (a Polish national projection) using GDAL warp with bilinear resampling and 30 m target resolution; then it computes slope (in degrees) using QGIS's native:slope algorithm; outputs are slope rasters saved in a 'slopes' subfolder with prefix 'slope_', preserving input filenames.

name: Compute minimum distance buffers
desc: The script computes a distance matrix between features in a GeoPackage point layer (random.gpkg), extracting the minimum distance ('MIN') for each source point to any target point; it then creates variable-radius circular buffers around each point using that minimum distance as the buffer radius, and adds the resulting polygon layer to the QGIS project. The workflow relies entirely on QGIS processing algorithms (qgis:distancematrix and native:buffer) operating on vector geometry, with no raster or remote sensing analysis involved.

name: Count points in grid cells
desc: The script creates a regular grid over the buffered extent of an input point layer ('punkty_adresowe.gpkg'), then counts the number of points falling within each grid cell. The output is a polygon layer (temporary) where each grid cell has an attribute 'NUMPOINTS' representing the count of address points it contains. The resulting layer is added to the QGIS project. Key operations include extent buffering (100 map units), grid creation with fixed ncols=21 and nrows=30, and point-in-polygon counting using native QGIS processing algorithms.

name: Optimize transmitter coverage distances
desc: The script performs an iterative stochastic optimization to determine optimal buffer distances for three radio/TV transmitters (nadajniki) such that the number of covered address points (punkty_adresowe) is maximized while penalizing distance variance — i.e., it seeks a balanced, equitable spatial coverage configuration. It outputs a final buffered polygon layer representing the union of three optimized-distance buffers around transmitter points, added to the QGIS project.

name: Extract elevation profile along cross-section
desc: The script generates a distance-elevation profile by sampling a digital elevation model (DEM) at regular intervals (100 m) along a vector line layer named 'przekroj' (Polish for 'cross-section'). It first creates points spaced every 100 meters along the input line geometry, then samples the 'dem.tif' raster at those points to extract elevation values (prefixed as 'Z_1'), and finally plots the resulting longitudinal profile (distance vs. elevation) using matplotlib.

name: Derive slope position indices from DEM
desc: The script computes five topographic indices—slope height (HO), valley depth (HU), normalized height (NH), standardized height (SH), and midslope position (MS)—from a local DEM raster file (dem.tif) using SAGA GIS's 'relativeheightsandslopepositions' algorithm. It then generates 1000 random vector points within the DEM’s spatial extent and samples all five derived rasters at those points. Finally, it converts the sampled point attributes into a pandas DataFrame and plots kernel density estimates (KDE) for each index to visualize their statistical distributions.

name: Model least cost pathways
desc: The script constructs a least-cost path model for infrastructure routing (e.g., roads, utilities) by integrating land cover resistance, road networks (major/secondary), buildings, rural areas, and buffer zones. It reprojects all inputs to EPSG:32736, clips and resamples land cover to study extent and pixel size, reclassifies land cover into cost values (e.g., water=0.01, built-up=0.75, forest=0.15), rasterizes vector features (roads, buildings, start/end points, buffers) with distinct cost or binary weights, merges and clips rasters to the study area, and computes proximity to buildings — ultimately preparing cost surface and source/target rasters (start_region, end_region) for downstream least-cost path analysis (e.g., using GRASS r.cost or SAGA Least Cost Path). Outputs are two clipped rasters: 'start_region' (rasterized and clipped start points) and 'end_region' (rasterized and clipped end points), both aligned to the study site and pixel size.

name: Plan retention tree groups
desc: The script plans ecologically optimized retention tree groups within user-defined planning areas (polygon inputs) by integrating multiple spatial datasets: a Canopy Height Model (CHM) for tree detection, Depth-to-Water (DTW) raster for hydrological sensitivity, forest grid polygons for stand-level attributes (e.g., fertility class, mean diameters/heights), vegetation zones for biogeoclimatic classification, and water body polygons for distance-based ecological weighting. It applies an ecosystem service valuation model (runEssModel) that weights phosphorus retention (Pret), DTW-index, tree diversity (Ds), and dead wood potential (DWP) — each configurable via ordinal weighting levels — to prioritize trees. Final outputs are: (1) a point layer of selected retention trees (with CHM-derived height, location, and weighted scores), styled with 'reTree4.qml'; and (2) a polygon layer of clustered retention tree groups generated via point-to-area aggregation ('reTree' buffer/convex hull), styled with 'retreet_areas.qml'.

name: Plan retention tree groups
desc: The script plans ecologically optimized retention tree areas within user-provided harvesting polygons (sites). It integrates CHM (Canopy Height Model) and DTW (Depth-to-Water) rasters with vegetation zone polygons and forest grid polygons to identify individual tree locations via height- and terrain-informed deduction (treeDeduct), computes ecosystem service indicators (e.g., structural diversity, deadwood potential, hydrological sensitivity) using 30 m buffers (ecosystemIndicators), then spatially clusters trees into retention groups based on weighted ecological criteria (ds_w, gc_w, dwp_w, dtw_w) and target density (treecount pcs/ha) using spatialPlanning. Outputs are two vector layers: (1) point layer of proposed retention trees, and (2) polygon layer of grouped retention tree clusters (‘retention tree groups’), both styled with QGIS QML files.

name: Identify retention tree areas
desc: The script converts input tree point data (species, diameter) into ecologically weighted retention tree groups. It performs spatial buffering and cleaning to create candidate planning areas, clips raster (DTW — depth-to-water) and vector layers (forest grid, vegetation zones, water bodies) to each area, joins ecological attributes, computes distance to water, and runs an ecosystem services scoring model (runEssModel2points) that weights phosphorus retention, DTW index, tree diversity, and dead wood potential to select and group trees as retention areas. Outputs are: (1) refined tree points with ecological scores and retention assignments, styled with 'reTree4.qml'; and (2) polygonized retention tree groups (buffered and dissolved clusters), styled with 'retreet_areas.qml'.

name: Calculate hydrocarbon reserves from top surface and OWC polygon
desc: The script calculates hydrocarbon (HC) reserves by analyzing the vertical distance between a top reservoir surface (TVD raster) and an oil-water contact (OWC) polygon. It converts the raster to points within the OWC polygon, bins elevation values into 5 depth intervals, computes area per interval using cell area, applies P90/P50/P10 volumetric uncertainty scaling factors (0.8×, 1.0×, 1.2×), and outputs a CSV table with depth intervals and corresponding cumulative reserve volumes in million cubic meters (converted from m² × thickness assumption via fixed interval binning). The workflow assumes constant vertical thickness per bin and uniform areal distribution of cells; no explicit thickness raster is used — thickness is derived solely from TVD range division.

name: Clip precipitation raster by extent
desc: The script clips geospatial rasters (primarily precipitation, temperature, elevation, slope, road density, fault density, PPP, and population) to a 2-degree bounding box (1-degree buffer in each direction) centered on input latitude/longitude coordinates. It uses QGIS GDAL raster clipping ('gdal:cliprasterbyextent') to extract subregions from local file-based datasets (e.g., GeoTIFFs, NetCDFs) and saves them as new GeoTIFF files in a processed directory. The core workflow is spatial subsetting of static and time-varying environmental/hazard/socioeconomic layers for event-pair analysis (e.g., natural hazard pairs from EM-DAT), with explicit handling of time-dependent variables like GPCC precipitation (1988–2018) and Berkeley Earth temperature (annual anomaly), and static layers like Glo30 elevation and GMTED slope. Outputs are clipped .tif files named by pair_id and map_name (e.g., '12345_prcp.tif').

name: Transfer GPS waypoints and tracks
desc: The script transfers GPS navigation data (waypoints, tracks, and routes) between Garmin GPS devices (ETREX/XL12 series) and QGIS. It downloads GPX files from connected Garmin devices or mounted Garmin GPX directories (e.g., D:/Garmin/GPX), converts them to shapefiles (point, line, or route layers) in EPSG:25830, and loads them into QGIS. Conversely, it uploads selected QGIS vector layers (points or lines/polylines) by reprojecting them to WGS84 (EPSG:4326), converting to GPX format using ogr2ogr with Garmin-specific options (e.g., FORCE_GPX_TRACK:YES), and writing them to Garmin devices via gpsbabel.exe over USB/COM ports or copying GPX files to standard Garmin GPX directories. Outputs include GPX files, reprojected shapefiles (.shp), and loaded QGIS layers.

name: Calculate catchment areas for points
desc: The script calculates catchment (upslope drainage) areas for input point locations using a digital elevation model (DEM). It iterates over unique values in an optional field (or feature IDs), extracts each point, runs SAGA's 'upslopearea' algorithm to generate a raster catchment, polygonizes the raster, selects only pixels with DN=100, and saves each catchment as a vector layer (GPKG or Shapefile). Outputs include a directory of catchment layers and a list of output layer URIs.

name: Extract polygon centerline skeleton
desc: The script implements the Chordal Axis algorithm to compute a topologically correct medial axis (skeleton/centerline) of input polygon geometries. It first tessellates each polygon into Delaunay triangles using QGIS 3D tessellation, then classifies triangles by adjacency (isolated, terminal, sleeve, junction), computes triangle-specific centerlines (e.g., from centroid to mid-sides for junctions, between mid-sides for sleeves), merges them, and optionally applies geometric corrections: iterative pruning of short branches relative to junction width, T-junction straightening (merging collinear branches), and X-junction reconstruction (pairing nearby T-junctions via sleeve chains). Outputs are a LineString layer representing the corrected centerline and a MultiPolygon layer of the input tessellation.

name: Simplify line and polygon geometries
desc: The script implements a QGIS processing algorithm for geometry simplification using an enhanced Douglas-Peucker algorithm with topological constraint validation (simplicity, intersection, sidedness). It accepts LineString or Polygon vector layers as input, applies tolerance-based vertex reduction, normalizes multi-part and Z/M geometries, and outputs simplified features while preserving spatial relationships. Outputs include the simplified feature layer and statistics on features processed, vertices deleted, iterations performed, and optional structural validation status.

name: Extract 3D building footprints
desc: The script extracts 3D building geometries (pand3d) from the Dutch 3DBAG WFS service for the Amsterdam Centrum district (Stadsdeel_code = 'A'), reprojects them from RD New (EPSG:28992) to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) using a precise Helmert transformation, and refactors field names and types—including renaming hyphenated height attributes (e.g., 'ground-0.00' → 'ground_0_00') and standardizing data types—to produce a cleaned, georeferenced GeoPackage (bag_3d_centrum.gpkg) suitable for 3D urban analysis and integration with global GIS workflows.

name: Extract polygon centerline skeleton
desc: The script computes the chordal axis (centerline skeleton) of input polygon layers using Delaunay triangulation and topological analysis of triangle adjacency. It first tessellates each polygon into triangles using QGIS's 3D tessellation algorithm, then constructs a spatial index of triangles, classifies triangle types (isolated, terminal, sleeve, junction), computes centerlines per triangle type, merges them, and optionally applies geometric corrections for T-junctions and X-junctions. Outputs are a line layer representing the chordal axis and a multi-polygon layer of the triangulation.

name: Compute zonal elevation statistics
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, min, max) of elevation values from an SRTM DEM raster over fixed seismic zone polygons. It first repairs invalid geometries in the input vector layer 'seismic_zones.shp', then runs 'native:zonalstatisticsfb' to calculate elevation statistics per polygon, and saves the result—including new attribute fields prefixed 'elevation_'—to a GeoPackage named 'seismic_zones_with_elevation3.gpkg'. The workflow uses PyQGIS with QGIS processing algorithms and exits cleanly.

name: Analyze seismic zone topography
desc: The script processes a seismic zones shapefile by fixing geometry errors and then computes zonal statistics (count, sum, mean) of elevation values from an SRTM digital elevation model raster. The output is a vector layer with added attributes prefixed 'zonal_stats_' containing aggregated elevation metrics per seismic zone polygon.

name: Generate hillshade from clipped SRTM
desc: The script clips an SRTM digital elevation model (srtm.tif) using a shoreline vector mask (shoreline.shp), then generates a hillshade raster (hillshade.tif) from the clipped DEM using azimuth 300°, vertical angle 40°, and Z-factor 1. The output is a hillshade geotiff saved to the local data directory.

name: Assign polygon boundary identifiers to points
desc: The script assigns polygon boundary identifiers (from the 'iso' field in the polygon layer) to point features based on spatial intersection. It loads two GeoPackage layers — a polygon layer ('stl.gpkg') and a points layer ('pts.gpkg') — adds them to the QGIS project, creates a new string field 'poly_boundary' in the points layer, and populates it using QGIS aggregate expression with 'concatenate' to collect all intersecting polygon 'iso' values. Then it computes statistics by category (grouping points by 'poly_boundary') and writes results to 'Stats.gpkg', followed by deleting all statistical fields except the grouping field, producing a final output GeoPackage ('output.gpkg') containing only the points with their assigned boundary identifiers.

name: Score language overlap proximity
desc: The script computes a linguistic proximity scoring metric for minor language points relative to major language polygons. It first identifies spatial overlaps between minor language points and three categories of major language polygons (both_ab_lng, type_a_lng, type_b_lng), then calculates distances from each point to the boundary of minimal circles enclosing matching type_a language polygons (D) and to the nearest line geometry of those same polygons (b), computes D-b differences, applies a logarithmic transformation (fxa = 21.6679 * ln(101 - 100*(D-b)/D)) per overlap, extracts up to three ISO codes from type_b overlaps (lngb1–lngb3), retrieves corresponding confidence scores ('confidenceB') from an external layer 'Danny_score_e1e6d035_60c8_4fb7_9c0a_da935ec21eea' filtered by country and code, and concatenates them into a final comma-separated 'fxb' field. Output is a vector layer with added scoring fields including 'fxb'.

name: Clip photos by region boundary
desc: The script clips a vector layer named 'photos' (containing photo file paths in a 'photo' attribute) to individual administrative or thematic regions defined in a 'regions' vector layer, using attribute-based extraction ('region' field) followed by geometric clipping. For each region, it exports the resulting subset of photo paths as symbolic links (JPG files numbered sequentially) into region-named subdirectories under 'handoff_images/'. No geospatial rasters or time-series analysis is performed; the workflow is purely vector-based spatial subsetting and filesystem organization of existing photo references.

name: Preprocess landslide conditioning factors
desc: The script preprocesses landslide conditioning factor (LCF) raster layers for landslide susceptibility modeling in the Wayanad study area. It converts lithology and geomorphology vector datasets (lithology_prj.shp and geomorphology_prj.shp) into rasters using GDAL's rasterize algorithm, assigning pixel values based on the 'UID_NOTATI' and 'Geom_class' attribute fields respectively, at 12.5 m resolution aligned to the extent of the slope.tif raster. All input rasters (slope.tif, aspect.tif, curvature.tif, rr.tif, lithoraster.tif, geomraster.tif) are then clipped to the boundary of the study area defined by wyd_output.shp using GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer with nodata=9999, crop-to-cutline=True, and resolution preserved. The outputs are clipped GeoTIFFs suffixed with '_clipped' (e.g., slope_clipped.tif), ready for use as LCF layers in subsequent susceptibility modeling. No satellite imagery, time-series analysis, or classification is performed — only vector-to-raster conversion and spatial clipping. Study area: Wayanad; time range: not specified; data sources: all local file-based rasters and shapefiles — no GEE Earth Engine assets or remote sensing collections are used.

name: Calculate landslide susceptibility frequency ratio
desc: The script performs landslide susceptibility modeling by reclassifying six raster layers (slope, aspect, curvature, relative relief, geomorphology, and lithology) into categorical classes, then computes the frequency ratio for each class as the ratio of landslide point frequency to area percentage. It uses QGIS processing algorithms including 'native:reclassifybytable', 'native:rasterlayeruniquevaluesreport', 'native:rastersampling', and 'qgis:statisticsbycategories' to generate reclassified rasters, pixel count/area CSVs, sampled landslide point shapefiles, and statistical summaries. Final outputs are merged CSV tables containing frequency ratios per class for each factor.

name: Model landslide susceptibility using frequency ratio weighting
desc: The script performs a frequency ratio-based weighted overlay analysis to generate a landslide susceptibility map. It reclassifies six input thematic rasters—slope, aspect, curvature, rainfall (rr), geomorphology, and lithology—using precomputed frequency ratio values derived from landslide point data (landslidepts_prj.shp) and their spatial association with each class. Each raster is reclassified via 'native:reclassifybytable' to assign frequency ratio values to respective class intervals. The reclassified rasters (RSlp1.tif, RAsp1.tif, Rcur1.tif, RRr1.tif, RGm1.tif, RLith1.tif) are then summed pixel-wise using QGIS Raster Calculator to produce a final continuous 'weighted.tif' raster representing integrated landslide susceptibility. The output is a single susceptibility index raster added to the QGIS map canvas as 'landslide susceptibility'.

name: Sample DGM1 raster values at surveyed points
desc: The script extracts elevation values from a DGM1 (Digital Terrain Model, 1 m resolution) raster at the precise geographic locations of field-surveyed ground control points (GOK), then exports the matched point coordinates, measured elevations (NHN), and corresponding DGM1 raster values to a CSV file for error assessment and DGM correction. It handles coordinate system transformation between the survey layer and DGM raster, robustly retrieves raster values via QgsRasterDataProvider.identify(), and writes results with columns: Easting, Northing, Elevation (measured), DGM (raster-sampled).

name: Generate line grid and style lines
desc: The script generates a regular line grid (10 km spacing) over a user-defined extent in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), fixes geometries of an input line layer, adds a sequential ID field to it, and applies consistent dashed gray line styling (0.20 mm width, RGB 191,191,191) to both the output grid and the processed input line layer using QgsProcessingLayerPostProcessorInterface. It does not perform geospatial analysis, modeling, or remote sensing — only vector geometry generation, cleaning, attribute augmentation, and cartographic styling.

name: Snap points to lines and split lines
desc: The script loads point and line vector layers from local Shapefiles, snaps the points to the nearest line within a 10-unit tolerance using 'snapgeometries' (behavior=3: prefer closest vertex/segment), buffers the snapped points by 0.00001 decimal degrees to create small polygons, converts those buffers to closed linestrings, then uses those linestrings to split the original line layer via 'splitwithlines'. The final output is a new loaded vector layer named 'Split_Lines', containing the original line segments cut at the snapped point locations — enabling topological editing for network analysis or feature alignment tasks.

name: Clip DEM and generate hillshade
desc: The script clips an SRTM digital elevation model (srtm.tif) using a shoreline vector layer (shoreline.shp) to mask the raster to coastal extents, then computes a hillshade raster from the clipped DEM using GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer and QGIS's native:hillshade algorithms with Z_FACTOR=2, AZIMUTH=300, and V_ANGLE=40. Outputs include a clipped DEM and a hillshade raster loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Compute average elevation in seismic zones
desc: The script computes the average elevation (mean raster value) within each polygon of a seismic zones vector layer, using an SRTM digital elevation model raster. It first fixes invalid geometries in the input vector layer, then performs zonal statistics (mean) to calculate average elevation per zone, and adds the resulting layer with new attributes prefixed 'Avg_Elevation_' to the QGIS project.

name: Clip DEM and generate hillshade
desc: The script clips an SRTM digital elevation model (DEM) raster using a shoreline vector layer as a mask, then generates a hillshade visualization from the clipped DEM with specified z-factor (2), azimuth (300°), and vertical angle (40°). The outputs are a clipped DEM raster and a hillshade raster loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Calculate SCS curve number
desc: The script computes the Soil Conservation Service (SCS) Curve Number (CN) for subbasins by integrating land cover class, soil hydrologic group (HSG), and their spatial intersection. It reprojects and fixes geometries of input vector layers (subbasins, land cover, soil type), performs sequential intersections to attribute land cover and soil properties to subbasin polygons, assigns retardance coefficients, runoff coefficients (e.g., 'AS', 'CN', 'GPF'), HSG values based on soil texture ('A'–'D'), Manning’s n values, and finally calculates CN using standardized NRCS lookup logic conditioned on land cover and HSG. Output is a vector layer with per-polygon CN values, area (in hectares), and supporting attributes including 'class_name', 'type', 'HSG', 'n_value', 'ret-c', and 'area_has'.

name: Calculate SCS curve number
desc: The script computes the Soil Conservation Service (SCS) Curve Number (CN) for subbasins by integrating land cover and soil type vector layers. It reprojects both layers to a common CRS (EPSG:32651), fixes geometries, performs sequential intersections to spatially join land cover class names and soil type attributes to subbasins, assigns hydrologic soil group (HSG) codes based on soil 'type' field values, assigns retardance coefficients and runoff coefficients using lookup logic, adds Manning’s n and CN values via case-based field calculations using standardized SCS-CN tables per land cover–HSG combination, and computes polygon area in hectares. The final output is a vector layer ('Curve Number') containing all derived attributes (HSG, CN, n_value, ret-c, area_has, etc.) per intersected polygon — no raster or time-series processing occurs; all inputs are static vector datasets with no embedded temporal metadata. Study area, satellite data, imagery, or time range are not specified — only generic vector inputs ('Subbasins', 'Land Cover', 'Soil Type') are used.

name: Plot river transect WSE profiles
desc: The script generates cross-sectional plots of Water Surface Elevation (WSE) along river centerline transects, overlaying multiple RAS (River Analysis System) WSE rasters (e.g., from different storm events or typhoon scenarios like 'Ty. Odette') against a baseline terrain elevation profile. For each input river centerline feature (named, e.g., 'Transect_1'), it samples elevation values at 1-meter intervals, extracts terrain and all matching WSE rasters (via glob pattern 'SB*/WSE*.tif'), constructs distance–elevation arrays, and saves a publication-ready PNG figure showing terrain (black line) and WSE curves (colored lines) with labeled legends (e.g., 'Ty. Odette', 'Ty. Odette-Post'), axis labels ('Station (m)', 'WSE (m)'), and tight layout.

name: Map flood depth and velocity at sample points
desc: The script processes HEC-RAS hydraulic model output rasters (Depth, Velocity, and Depth × Velocity) from multiple simulation scenarios (SB-* subfolders), samples raster values at predefined field survey points (sample_point.shp), applies standardized QGIS layer styles for visualization, and exports styled map images (PNG) for each raster-scenario combination. It automates layer loading, styling, point-based raster sampling, temporary layer cleanup, and layout-based image export to a structured directory per raster type.

name: Extract yardang landforms
desc: The script processes vector polygon layers representing yardang features in the Qaidam Basin, performing merging, buffering (with zero distance), dissolving, and multipart-to-singlepart conversion to produce cleaned, topologically consistent single-part polygon geometries of yardangs. It specifically handles two batches (690 and 691) — first merging dozens of individual output shapefiles (e.g., 691_o1.shp through 691_o100.shp) into a single layer, then applying geometric cleaning (buffer 0 + dissolve) to eliminate slivers and overlaps, followed by splitting multipart polygons into individual features. The final outputs are standardized shapefiles (e.g., merge_690.shp, merge_691.shp) suitable for morphometric analysis or GIS-based yardang mapping.

name: Identify service coverage area
desc: The script computes a buffer zone (user-specified distance) around an input point layer (e.g., proposed or existing facilities), clips road/line layers to that buffer, dissolves and measures total road length within the buffer, counts overlapping point features (e.g., population points, demand locations) inside the buffer polygon, and generates a summary report with area (km²), road length (km), and point count. Outputs include three renamed layers: 'Area_Cobertura' (buffer polygon with area attribute), 'Ruas_Atingidas' (dissolved clipped roads with length attribute), and 'Pontos_Sobrepostos' (polygon layer with NUMPOINTS count field), plus a QMessageBox summary and optional text report. All operations are performed client-side in QGIS using native processing algorithms; no remote sensing data, satellite imagery, or time-series analysis is involved.

name: Extract points within India boundary
desc: The script extracts point features from a ZIP file (likely containing vector data) that intersect with the India national boundary shapefile using QGIS's 'native:extractbylocation' algorithm. It then generates a georeferenced PNG image of a print layout named 'print', which includes both the extracted points layer and the India boundary layer. The output is a static, georeferenced map image ('print7.png') showing the spatial relationship between the extracted points and the national boundary.

name: Extract points within India boundary
desc: The script extracts point features from a ZIP file (likely containing vector data) that intersect with the India boundary shapefile using QGIS's 'native:extractbylocation' algorithm. It then generates a georeferenced PNG image of a print layout named 'print', which includes both the extracted points layer and the India boundary layer. The output is a static map image ('/Users/nilay/Downloads/print8.png') with georeferencing, metadata, and antialiasing enabled.

name: Detect active fire locations
desc: The script downloads the latest MODIS Collection 6.1 active fire shapefile for South East Asia (7-day interval), extracts fire points intersecting a user-provided input vector layer (e.g., administrative boundary or area of interest), and exports a print layout containing the extracted fire points overlaid on an India boundary layer as a georeferenced image (e.g., PNG, TIFF). The core output is a spatially filtered fire point dataset and its visual representation.

name: Clip DEM and generate hillshade
desc: The script clips a digital elevation model (SRTM) raster using a shoreline vector layer as a mask, then generates a hillshade raster from the clipped DEM using specified illumination parameters (azimuth=300°, vertical angle=40°, z-factor=1). The output is a hillshade GeoTIFF saved to a temporary path and loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Analyze seismic zone topography
desc: The script processes a vector layer of seismic zones and a digital elevation model (SRTM) raster to compute zonal statistics—specifically mean elevation—for each seismic zone polygon. It first fixes invalid geometries in the input shapefile, then performs zonal statistics using the SRTM raster (band 1) to calculate the mean value per zone, storing results in memory. The output is a vector layer with an added attribute field (prefixed '_') containing the mean elevation values.

name: Load SRTM DEM tiles
desc: The script loads SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission) digital elevation model (DEM) raster tiles matching the current QGIS map canvas extent using a prebuilt grid vector layer (srtm_grid.gpkg). It extracts intersecting grid cells, resolves corresponding .hgt filenames, loads valid raster layers from a local folder, and either adds a single raster layer or builds and loads a GDAL virtual raster (VRT) mosaic when multiple tiles are required. Outputs include one or more loaded DEM raster layers named 'DEM' at the bottom of the layer tree, and optionally a missing-tiles vector layer if some SRTM tiles are absent.

name: Track daily animal movement paths
desc: The script processes GPS collar data from cattle in the FireGraze dry season 2023 study to generate daily track lines (as LineString geometries in EPSG:28352), sorted chronologically per day, and computes daily summary statistics: total distance walked (km), maximum time gap between pings (minutes), and min/mean/max inter-ping distance (m) and speed (km/h). Outputs are a GeoPackage layer with daily track features and an Excel spreadsheet containing all attribute summaries.

name: Clip GPS points to paddock boundaries
desc: The script processes CSV-formatted GPS point data (with Latitude/Longitude columns) collected from August 2021 to March 2022, clips each file’s point layer to the spatial extent of Rocklands_paddocks polygon boundaries (a GeoPackage), and saves the resulting clipped points as individual GeoPackage files in a heatmap_points directory. It then loads each clipped layer into the QGIS interface. The core operation is vector-based spatial clipping (point-in-polygon containment), not raster analysis, modeling, or time-series aggregation.

name: Calculate waterpoint proximity per paddock
desc: The script computes, for each paddock polygon in the 'Mt_Sanford_Paddocks' layer, a clipped raster where each pixel value represents the Euclidean distance (in map units) to the nearest waterpoint located within that paddock. It achieves this by: (1) spatially subsetting waterpoints intersecting each paddock; (2) rasterizing those points to a binary (0/1) raster at 10 m resolution aligned to the paddock’s bounding box; (3) computing a GDAL proximity raster (distance-to-1 pixels); and (4) clipping the resulting distance raster to the exact paddock geometry (not just its bounding box). Outputs are individual GeoTIFF files named after each paddock (e.g., 'PDK_NAME.tif') stored in the specified local directory, with nodata set to -9999.

name: Quantify pasture biomass and soil moisture within livestock home ranges
desc: The script computes median, minimum, and maximum values of Cibo TC (Canopy Cover) and Cibo TSDM (Total Standing Dry Matter) raster layers intersecting three probabilistic home range polygons (50%, 75%, 95%) and the full paddock boundary for cattle in Big Mudgee, NSW. It processes time-ordered geopackage files containing vector layers ('homerange' and 'paddock'), matches them to monthly Cibo raster products by date logic (accounting for Australian financial/seasonal year alignment), performs zonal statistics, and exports results to a CSV with columns for paddock ID, year, month, layer type (TC/TSDM), and per-zone statistics (median/min/max).

name: Calculate maximum distance to water
desc: The script calculates the maximum Euclidean distance from any point within each input paddock polygon to the nearest water point (e.g., bore, trough, dam) using vector–raster geoprocessing. It first harmonizes CRS between input layers (paddocks and water points), then for each paddock: (1) extracts intersecting water points, (2) rasterizes them at user-specified resolution (e.g., 25 m), (3) computes a GDAL proximity raster (distance in meters), (4) clips the proximity raster to the paddock boundary, and (5) extracts the local maximum distance value. Outputs include: (a) one clipped proximity GeoTIFF per paddock (named by paddock ID or field-derived name), (b) an optional Excel report listing paddock name, area (ha), number of waterpoints, and max distance to water (km), and (c) optionally loads and styles rasters in QGIS with a gradient color ramp scaled to the global maximum DTW (rounded up). The analysis is purely geometric — no satellite imagery, time series, or spectral data is used; inputs are user-provided vector layers only. Study area, time range, satellite/sensor/bands, and specific geographic location are not specified in the code.

name: Calculate water point proximity raster
desc: The script computes, for each paddock polygon, a raster where each pixel value represents the Euclidean distance to the nearest water point located within that paddock. It achieves this by (1) spatially filtering water points that intersect each paddock, (2) rasterizing those points into a binary (0/1) raster at 10 m resolution aligned to the paddock’s bounding box, (3) computing a GDAL proximity raster from the binary raster (distance in map units), and (4) clipping the resulting distance raster to the exact paddock geometry. Outputs are individual GeoTIFF files named after paddock names (e.g., 'PaddockA.tif'), each containing a clipped proximity raster with nodata = -9999. No satellite or time-series data is used; inputs are static vector layers (paddocks and water points) provided by the user. Study area, time range, satellite/sensor, and bands are not specified in the code.

name: Calculate water point proximity raster
desc: The script computes, for each paddock polygon, a raster where each pixel value represents the Euclidean distance (in map units) to the nearest water point located within that paddock. It achieves this by: (1) spatially aligning input paddocks and water points via on-the-fly reprojection to a common CRS (prioritizing paddock CRS or defaulting to EPSG:9473 if both are geographic); (2) iterating per paddock; (3) extracting water points intersecting the paddock; (4) rasterizing those points to a binary (0/1) raster at 25 m resolution using the paddock’s bounding box as extent; (5) computing a GDAL proximity raster from the binary raster; and (6) clipping the proximity raster to the exact paddock geometry. Outputs are individual GeoTIFF files named after each paddock (e.g., 'PaddockA.tif'), containing clipped proximity distances, saved to a user-specified folder. No satellite, temporal, or external geospatial data sources are used — only vector inputs (paddocks and water points) provided by the user. Study area, time range, and sensor/band information are not specified.

name: Calculate water proximity distance
desc: The script calculates, for each paddock polygon, the maximum distance from any location within the paddock to the nearest water point. It does so by: (1) ensuring both input layers (paddocks and water points) are in a common projected CRS (prioritizing paddock CRS, or using EPSG:9473 if both are geographic); (2) iterating per paddock; (3) extracting water points intersecting that paddock; (4) rasterizing those points into a binary 1/0 raster at user-specified resolution (default 25 m); (5) computing a Euclidean distance (proximity) raster from the binary raster; (6) clipping the proximity raster to the exact paddock geometry; and (7) exporting each clipped proximity raster as a GeoTIFF named after the paddock. Outputs are individual GeoTIFF files — one per paddock containing ≥1 water point — where pixel values represent distance (in map units) to the nearest water point. No time-series, no satellite imagery, no classification: purely vector-to-raster proximity analysis using local QGIS GDAL algorithms. Study area, time range, and satellite data sources are not specified — inputs are arbitrary user-provided vector layers.

name: Calculate maximum distance to water
desc: The script calculates the maximum Euclidean distance (in kilometers) from any point within each input paddock polygon to the nearest water point, using vector-to-raster proximity analysis. It processes user-provided vector layers: a polygon layer of paddocks and a point layer of water points. The workflow includes CRS harmonization (handling geographic/projected mismatches by reprojecting to either the paddock CRS or EPSG:9473 Australian Albers), per-paddock spatial filtering of water points, rasterization of water points at user-specified resolution (default 25 m), GDAL proximity raster generation (distance in meters), clipping the proximity raster to each paddock’s geometry, and computing the maximum pixel value (i.e., max distance) within each clipped raster. Outputs are: (1) one GeoTIFF proximity raster per paddock (named after paddock name or generic 'Paddock_i'), saved to a user-specified folder; and (2) an optional Excel spreadsheet ('Max_dist_to_water.xlsx') reporting for each paddock: name, area (ha), number of contained water points, and max distance to water (km). No satellite, temporal, or spectral data is used — all inputs are local vector layers with no embedded time dimension or sensor metadata.

name: Extract land type areas
desc: The script extracts and calculates land type areas for property paddocks, optionally including dissolved whole-property boundaries and watered areas buffered from waterpoints. It performs spatial intersection between land types and paddock geometries, dissolves land types by a user-specified unit field, transforms CRS to projected (GDA2020 Albers if source is geographic), computes area using either ellipsoidal or planar methods, and exports results in user-selected vector formats (gpkg, shp, json, kml, kmz). Outputs include polygon layers with area attributes (m², ha, km², %) and optional loading into QGIS project.

name: Extract land type areas
desc: The script extracts and calculates land type (e.g., land systems or map units) area statistics for three nested spatial contexts: (1) the entire property (via dissolved paddocks), (2) individual paddocks, and (3) optional watered areas (buffered around waterpoints at 3km or 5km radii). It performs geometric intersection between land type polygons and each context geometry, computes area metrics (m², ha, km², % of context), and exports results as vector files (GPKG/SHP/GeoJSON/KML/KMZ) with attribute tables containing land unit names, geometry, and area statistics. Area calculation supports both planar (projected CRS) and ellipsoidal (geographic CRS + GDA2020 Albers transformation) methods.

name: Extract land type areas
desc: The script computes the area (in m², ha, km², and %) of intersecting land system or land unit polygons (e.g., soil types, land systems) within user-provided property paddocks, the dissolved whole-property boundary, and user-defined watered areas (3 km and/or 5 km buffers around waterpoints). It performs geometric intersection, area calculation (ellipsoidal or planar), percent-of-paddock computation, and exports layered vector outputs — one per analysis scope (property, paddock, watered area) — with attributes including original land unit fields plus derived area metrics.

name: Extract land type areas
desc: The script extracts and calculates land system/unit areas for property, paddock, and watered areas using vector polygon layers (land types, paddocks, waterpoints). It transforms layers to a common CRS (EPSG:9473 if input is geographic), dissolves land types by unit field, computes intersections between land types and paddocks/watered buffers (3km/5km), measures areas using ellipsoidal or planar methods, appends area metrics (m², ha, km², %), saves outputs in user-specified vector formats (gpkg/shp/json/kml/kmz), and optionally exports a summary spreadsheet. Outputs include multiple vector layers named e.g., 'Property_land_types', 'Paddock_land_types', 'Paddock_3km_WA_land_types', and an XLSX report.

name: Generate TIN interpolation surface
desc: The script generates a raster surface using TIN (Triangulated Irregular Network) interpolation based on randomly sampled points inside input polygons. It first creates random points within the input polygon layer, assigns each point a random integer value (1–100) in a new field named 'INTERP', then performs TIN interpolation on those points to produce an output raster with specified pixel size (0.1°) and extent (131.881193298, 132.997064303, -13.996373726, -12.094533450) in EPSG:4326. No real-world geophysical variable is modeled — the values are synthetic (random), and the interpolation serves as a geometric surface generation exercise.

name: Summarize TSDM pixel counts by district
desc: The script computes pixel count and percentage summaries for two raster layers—AussieGRASS Total Standing Dry Matter (TSDM) and TSDM Percentile—within pastoral districts of Australia. It applies region-specific classification thresholds (Northern vs. Southern districts) to categorize TSDM into low, low-moderate, moderate, and high classes, and TSDM percentile into below average, average, and above average classes. Districts are clipped individually using vector mask layers, rasters are loaded and counted via NumPy boolean operations, and results are aggregated into two memory vector layers with attribute fields for counts and percentages. Finally, both summary layers are exported to an Excel workbook (.xlsx or .ods) with two sheets.

name: Convert GPS points to polygons
desc: The script converts a CSV file containing GPS points (longitude, latitude) into closed linear paths grouped and ordered by 'id', then joins attributes from an existing QGIS layer named 'xrf_data' using the 'id' field, fixes geometries, and finally converts the resulting lines into polygons. The output is a polygon layer derived from point sequences, with attributes joined from the 'xrf_data' layer.

name: Compute centroids of world map features
desc: The script initializes a QGIS application instance, registers native processing algorithms, and runs the 'native:centroids' algorithm on the built-in QGIS world map dataset ('/usr/share/qgis/resources/data/world_map.gpkg') to compute centroid points for each feature. The output is saved as 'centroids.gpkg'. No buffer or other spatial operations are executed; only the centroid process is active per uncommented code.

name: Divide rural parcel by road
desc: The script divides a single rural property polygon (Parcela) using a road feature (Estrada), which can be either a line or polygon. If the road is a line, it buffers it using a user-defined domain width (in meters), reprojects to SIRGAS2000 if needed, and computes the geometric difference between the parcel and the buffered road area. It then updates the parcel layer’s geometry with the resulting multipolygon and optionally adds virtual vertices ('V', method 'PA1') to the Vertice layer where new boundary points appear in the difference geometry but not in the original parcel. Validation ensures exactly one parcel and one road feature, matching CRS (with reprojection if needed), and non-overlap checks.

name: Assess linear project impact area
desc: The script computes the spatial extent and percentage of habitat impact caused by linear infrastructure projects (e.g., roads, pipelines) on sensitive ecological features: BAEA (Burrowing Owl) nests (804 m buffer), BUOWL (Burrowing Owl) habitats (300 m buffer), Raptor nests (402 m buffer), and GBH (Great Blue Heron) rookeries (no buffer — direct overlay). It buffers linear projects using a dynamic width field 'row_width', calculates their total area in hectares, then sequentially subtracts overlapping buffered zones and rookery polygons to isolate the non-overlapping impacted area. Finally, it computes 'impact_ha' (impacted area in ha) and 'impact_pct' (percentage of linear project area that remains outside all protected/buffered features), outputting a vector layer with these metrics.

name: Detect attribute discontinuity in network
desc: The script detects discontinuities of a user-specified attribute (e.g., pipe diameter, material code, flow direction) along a line-type vector network by topologically analyzing vertex adjacency and attribute consistency. It first splits the input line layer at all intersections (using 'split with lines' on itself), then isolates segments with and without valid attribute values. For segments *with* the attribute, it extracts start/end vertices, identifies shared (junction) vertices via coordinate-based aggregation (X+Y sum + count), and flags vertices where ≥2 segments meet — indicating potential attribute transitions. For segments *without* the attribute, it extracts their endpoints and filters those that coincide with junctions *but are not connected to any attributed segment*, identifying candidate 'source' or 'break' points. Finally, it performs spatial intersection and buffering-based point-in-polygon counting to isolate isolated endpoints where an attributed segment terminates adjacent to a non-attributed segment — these are output as discontinuity locations (points). The final output is a point layer marking locations where the selected continuous attribute abruptly starts, stops, or changes across network topology.

name: Generate parcel-centered topographic contours and slope rasters
desc: The script automates creation of a QGIS project for civil engineering projects in Humboldt County, CA, centered on a user-specified APN. It selects and clips vector layers (parcels, roads, streams, zoning, hazards, etc.) and raster layers (NAIP 2022 imagery, USGS 1m/10m DEMs) to a 5000-ft buffer around the parcel centroid. It generates contour shapefiles at 2-, 10-, 20-, 40-, and 100-ft intervals from the clipped DEM, computes slope rasters (percent and degree), and organizes all layers into thematic QGIS layer groups (BACKGROUND LAYERS, SATELLITE IMAGERY, TOPOGRAPHY). Outputs include a fully styled QGIS project file (.qgz), clipped shapefiles, georeferenced rasters (clipped NAIP, DEM, slope), and contour vectors — all stored in a standardized folder hierarchy under O:/Projects_Civil3D or P:/_Information/OP_PROJECT_CREATOR/Destination.

name: Translate eUVM parking area attributes to OSM schema
desc: The script converts a QGIS vector layer of eUVM (elektronische UVM – electronic urban traffic management) parking area polygons into an OpenStreetMap (OSM)-compliant representation by mapping eUVM attributes (e.g., 'ausrichtung', 'anzahl_parkplaetze', 'category', 'geltungszeit_ladezone', 'strassenname') to standardized OSM key-value pairs (e.g., 'amenity=parking', 'orientation=parallel', 'restriction=no_parking', 'restriction:conditional=loading_only @ (Mo-Fr 07:00-19:00)', 'maxstay=yes', 'street:name=...'). It handles time interval parsing and normalization (e.g., German weekday abbreviations → ISO codes, time padding, interval merging), adds data quality warnings for ambiguous cases (e.g., weekday jumps or repeated days), optionally drops original eUVM fields (retaining only 'polygon_id' and OSM keys), reprojects to EPSG:25833 (ETRS89 / UTM zone 33N), and outputs a new temporary QGIS layer named 'output_parking_areas_translated_aussenstadt'.

name: Clip and buffer hydrographic network
desc: The script performs a vector clipping operation on an input hydrographic layer using a clip polygon layer, then filters the clipped layer by 'Descripc' attribute values corresponding to three river hierarchy levels ('Red hídrica Nivel 1 (Principal)', 'Red hídrica Nivel 2 (Secundaria)', 'Red hídrica Nivel 3 (Terciaria)'), assigns distinct blue colors to each level, and generates buffered polygon layers at distances of 100m, 50m, and 20m respectively. Outputs include three styled clipped line layers and three corresponding buffered polygon layers added to the QGIS project.

name: Generate DTM using TIN interpolation
desc: The script produces a high-resolution digital terrain model (DTM) by performing TIN (Triangulated Irregular Network) interpolation on multi-source elevation data: EMODnet bathymetry points (converted from a raster ASC file), Ordnance Survey Terrain 50 spot heights, contour lines, and land-water boundary features. It reprojects bathymetric points from WGS84 (EPSG:4326) to OSGB 1936 (EPSG:27700), clips them to the study area’s water polygon, integrates them with terrestrial elevation features, performs TIN interpolation at 10 m resolution, and outputs two clipped rasters: a full-study-area DTM (terrain.tif) and a sector-specific DTM clipped to the N4 Marine Plan area (terrain_N4.tif).

name: Compute viewshed visibility from wind turbines
desc: The script performs viewshed analysis for offshore wind turbine scenarios (25, 50, 75, and 100 turbines) placed within the N4 sectoral marine plan area. It generates regularly spaced turbine point distributions using QGIS regular points, computes individual observer-based viewsheds (using GDAL’s viewshed algorithm with terrain DEM, observer height = turbine hub height + 50 m, target height = 1.65 m, max distance = 45 km), accumulates overlapping viewsheds via raster algebra, clips results to the study area and land boundary (study_area_bdline), reclassifies distance-based visibility values into six normalized classes (0.0–1.0) per turbine count using scenario-specific distance thresholds, and finally computes zonal statistics (mean, min, max, std, sum, count) of the reclassified viewshed rasters over 100-m buffers around designated heritage viewpoints (e.g., Callanish Standing Stones, Arnol Blackhouses). Outputs include: (1) turbine distribution layers (GPKG), (2) cumulative clipped & reclassified viewshed rasters (GeoTIFF), (3) viewpoint centroids layer (GPKG), (4) zonal statistics tables linked to viewpoints (GPKG).

name: Count overlapping cables on infrastructure
desc: The script computes the number of cable features that spatially overlap (contain, are contained by, or intersect) each infrastructure line feature. It first buffers cable lines by a tiny distance (1e-7 degrees) to handle topological imprecision, assigns unique integer IDs to both cables and infrastructure, performs a one-to-many spatial join based on geometric predicates (contains/within/overlap), aggregates results per infrastructure ID to collect comma-separated cable IDs, and finally calculates the count of overlapping cables as a new integer field 'n_overlaps' added to the output infrastructure layer.

name: Map administrative boundary changes
desc: The script processes vector layers representing 'ATP AP', 'New AP', and 'Old AP' (likely administrative polygons — e.g., Ukrainian administrative units or occupied territories) alongside 'Ukraine provinces' to derive three key outputs: (1) 'new_line' — line features representing newly gained boundaries (via difference of dissolved new AP minus itself, though logically flawed — likely intended as boundary extraction); (2) 'Old_line' — similarly derived lines for old boundaries; (3) 'PinsAp' — point features (generated via 'points along geometry' on line differences, filtered by intersection with buffered AP layers) labeled as 'Ukr gains' or 'Ru gains', indicating contested or shifted control points; and (4) 'AP output' — cleaned, multipart-to-singlepart, area-filtered (>1 m²) polygonal administrative units after splitting by provincial boundaries, hole removal, and geometry standardization. The workflow emphasizes topological cleaning (buffering, dissolve, delete holes, fix geometries), spatial differencing to isolate change-related lines, point sampling along those lines, attribution by spatial relationship to buffered AP layers, and final provincial subdivision and validation.

name: Extract and compare territorial control lines
desc: The script processes vector layers representing 'New SM' and 'Old SM' (likely 'Status Map' or 'Sector Map' — interpreted as frontline or territorial control boundaries in Ukraine) to derive four outputs: (1) 'New Lines SM' — newly gained frontlines/territorial lines; (2) 'Old Lines SM' — previously held lines (though algorithmically identical to New Lines due to self-difference error); (3) 'SM output' — merged result of difference and split geometries, intended to represent updated territorial control polygons/lines; (4) 'Pins SM' — point features labeled 'Ukr gains' or 'Ru gains' placed along line segments, derived via buffering, splitting, and spatial intersection with points generated at 0.006° intervals (~660 m), indicating localized territorial gains by each side. The workflow includes filtering out 'Ukrainian Armed Forces' named features, dissolving, buffering, splitting Ukrainian provinces (especially isolating Crimea via regex), deleting holes, and performing geometric differences and merges — all focused on delineating and attributing changes in de facto administrative/military control lines within Ukraine, particularly Crimea and contested regions.

name: Snap network elements to infrastructure points
desc: The script improves geometric consistency of telecom infrastructure vector layers by snapping endpoints and vertices of aerial boxes, ducts, distribution cables, fiber cables, and drop cables to reference infrastructure points (e.g., Paal/poles, DP/distribution points, Termination_Box, Riser, CO/central office, HP/home pass-through points). It applies geometry fixing (via 'native:fixgeometries') before snapping and uses QGIS native snap behavior 'Move end points only, prefer aligning nodes' (behavior=4) or 'Prefer aligning nodes, don't insert new vertices' (behavior=2) with a tolerance of 0.005 map units. Inputs are named export layers with UUID suffixes (e.g., 'export___Aerial_Box_7e1866a9_d55d_4c7e_87b4_07e7c651728d'), indicating they originate from external data exports — not satellite or sensor data. No study area, time range, satellite imagery, or spectral analysis is involved; this is a pure vector topology correction workflow for utility network GIS data. Outputs are five snapped vector layers: snapped_aerialboxes, snapped_dCables, snapped_fCables, snapped_dropCables, and snapped_dDucts.

name: Identify road-river intersection structures
desc: The script identifies potential infrastructure structures (e.g., bridges, culverts) by computing geometric intersections between input line layers — 'Cours_eau' (rivers/streams) and 'Routes' (roads) — then merges those intersection points with an existing 'Structures' point layer. It applies a 50 m buffer around the merged points, dissolves overlapping buffers, computes centroids of the dissolved polygons, and finally filters only those centroids located within 100 m of any river geometry. The output is a refined point layer ('New_structures') representing candidate infrastructure features spatially associated with both road-river crossings and proximity to watercourses.

name: Join PtRef with lotic width data
desc: The script filters point features (PtRef) that intersect with river network segments sharing the same 'Id_UEA' and where 'Valide_bv' is true, then joins the filtered points with a separate lotic modification layer ('PtRef_Mod_Lotique') on the 'Id_PtRef' field to attach 'Largeur_mod' (width) attributes. The output is a vector layer ('PtRef_largeur') containing only the matched points enriched with width information.

name: Compute river corridor sinuosity index
desc: The script computes the IQM (Indice de Qualité des Milieux) F5 index—a sinuosity-related indicator—by generating perpendicular transects along river network segments, measuring their intersection lengths with a predefined riparian zone polygon layer ('Bande_riveraine_polly'), and classifying the resulting width array into five ordinal classes (0–4) based on continuity and minimum width thresholds (15 m and 30 m). It outputs a copy of the input river network line layer with an added integer field 'Indice F5' representing the computed score per segment.

name: Reproject and extract Maharashtra districts
desc: The script loads GADM administrative boundary datasets (districts and villages) and a hospitals point dataset for Maharashtra, validates their integrity, reprojects all layers to UTM zone 43N (EPSG:32643), and extracts only the 36 districts belonging to Maharashtra using an attribute filter on 'NAME_1'. Outputs are GeoPackage files: districts_utm.gpkg, villages_utm.gpkg, hospitals_utm.gpkg, and maharashtra_districts.gpkg.

name: Assess hospital accessibility for villages
desc: The script evaluates spatial accessibility of healthcare infrastructure in Maharashtra, India, by buffering hospitals by 5 km, calculating total coverage area as a percentage of the state, identifying villages outside this buffer (i.e., underserved), and aggregating hospital counts per district. Key outputs include: (1) a 5 km hospital service area polygon layer, (2) a list of underserved villages (those not intersecting any hospital buffer), (3) district-level hospital count statistics with top-5 ranking, and (4) coverage area quantification (km² and % of Maharashtra’s ~307,713 km² land area).

name: Detect line dangle endpoints
desc: The script identifies dangle (over/under-shoot) endpoints in a line layer by performing topological analysis: it extracts line endpoints, removes those that intersect other lines or fall within a buffered polygon boundary (mask), buffers remaining candidate points by a user-defined tolerance, counts how many original lines intersect each buffered point, and retains only points intersecting exactly one line—then computes centroids of those buffers as final over/under-shoot point locations. The output is a point feature class representing topologically invalid line endpoints requiring manual review or correction.

name: Expand landslide inventory cells
desc: The script expands a landslide inventory raster by buffering all cells with value 1 (representing landslide occurrences) by 10 raster cells, then rasterizes the buffered vector geometry back to a new aligned raster ('inventario_expandido.tif') matching the original inventory's extent, resolution, and projection. The output is a binary or integer raster where original landslide cells and their 10-cell neighborhood are marked (burned as 0 in rasterization, though logic implies intended retention of spatial context for susceptibility modeling).

name: Identify suitable houses
desc: The script performs multi-criteria suitability analysis for residential locations based on distance constraints from two user-selected vector layers (e.g., roads, rivers, protected areas). It buffers each criteria layer by user-defined distances and filters a target ‘houses’ vector layer using topological predicates — either retaining houses *inside* the buffer (‘No more than’) or *outside* (‘No less than’) — resulting in an output vector layer named ‘Sutable Houses’ with a feature count reported to the QGIS message bar.

name: Generate flood damage units
desc: The script generates three vector layers of flood damage units (DamUnit3, DamUnit4, DamUnit5) by spatially aggregating flood risk raster values within buffered channel zones. It first reprojects and resamples the primary flood risk raster (A) to a user-defined damage unit cell size, converts it to polygons, clips to a buffer around SWAT+ channel vectors, assigns unique IDs, then performs zonal statistics against up to five flood risk rasters (A–E) to compute summed risk values per polygon. These are scaled by pixel area (using user-provided pixel size in meters) to estimate total damage per unit, then aggregated by damage unit ID. DamUnit3 uses only rasters A–C; DamUnit4 adds D if provided; DamUnit5 adds E if provided. Outputs are attribute-rich polygon layers with summed damage estimates per unit for multi-return-period flood risk assessment.

name: Estimate flood damage mitigation potential
desc: The script computes flood risk mitigation metrics by statistically analyzing flood discharge time series (from SWAT+ hydrological model outputs stored in SQLite) to derive channel-specific flood frequency statistics (mean, stddev), then calculates flood quantiles (MDFTa–e) using Gumbel distribution parameters (UBC, ABC, USC, ASC), followed by probability of inundation (PIa–e) and average population change (AvgPobChg3/4/5) under multiple return periods; it also computes expected annual damage difference (EADD3/4/5) across return period combinations and aggregates results spatially to administrative units (Adm_id) for risk prioritization.

name: Extract polygon boundary edges
desc: The script processes an input vector layer of polygons and generates a new polygon layer representing the 'edges' — i.e., a buffered outline strip along each polygon boundary. It achieves this by: (1) converting multipart geometries to singlepart; (2) fixing and simplifying geometries (with 0.0001 m tolerance); (3) computing inward and outward buffers at half the user-specified width (in tenths of millimeter); (4) differencing the external buffer from the internal buffer to yield a centered edge strip; (5) dissolving the resulting strips; and (6) appending a fixed attribute 'h' = braille.DIM['f'] (likely for tactile map rendering). The output is a polygon feature sink with geometry representing uniform-width edge bands tracing original polygon perimeters.

name: Count retail stores near stations
desc: The script counts the number of retail establishments (stored in the 'retail' attribute of mesh features) within a 500-meter buffer around specified railway stations. It loads station names from a CSV file, selects corresponding station features from a QGIS vector layer named 'N02-20_Station_XY' using attribute matching on field 'N02_005', creates a buffered polygon layer, selects intersecting mesh features from the 'MESH' layer, sums the 'retail' values of those selected mesh features, and writes the per-station store counts back to the input CSV as 'number_of_stores'. Output is a CSV file containing station names and associated retail store counts.

name: Compute concave hull geometry
desc: The script computes a concave hull polygon from an input point layer using Delaunay triangulation, edge-length filtering based on an alpha threshold (0–1), removal of triangles with edges longer than alpha × maximum edge length, and dissolution of remaining triangles. It optionally removes interior rings (holes) and splits multipart geometries into singleparts. The output is a vector polygon layer representing the concave hull.

name: Classify terrain features from LiDAR point clouds
desc: The script performs supervised classification of LiDAR point cloud data into five terrain classes (e.g., ground, vegetation, buildings) using a hexagonal grid–based deep learning model (HexTerrainNet). It groups input 3D points (with X, Y, Z, intensity, return info, and RGB) into hexagons of size 1.0 unit, computes 6 statistical features (mean, std, min, max, 25th/75th percentile) per input feature (Z, Intensity, ReturnNumber, NumberOfReturns, Red, Green, Blue), plus geometric and spectral aggregations (e.g., height range, NDVI-like index, brightness), resulting in a 52-dimensional feature vector per hexagon. The trained PyTorch model outputs class logits; predictions are mapped back to original points. Final output is a CSV with 'predicted_label' (re-mapped to binary: classes 2/3 → 0, class 4 → 1), loaded as a styled QGIS point layer with a QML file ('punkty_PBC_new.qml') for visualization.

name: Estimate building roof slope and height
desc: The script processes LiDAR-derived point cloud data to estimate roof slope (in degrees) and building height (in meters) for each building in the 'budynki_z_szer_elew_front' layer. It segments roof points (Classification_6_with_IDs) and ground points (Classification_2_bufor_with_IDs) by cadastral parcel (ID_DZIALKI) and building ID (ID_BUDYNKU), applies robust RANSAC-based plane fitting with DBSCAN segmentation for slope estimation, filters outliers using MAD and IQR, computes representative ground and roof heights, and writes results ('nachylenie_chmura', 'wysokosc', 'pewnosc_nachylenia', 'metoda_nachylenia', 'liczba_punktow') directly into the building layer attributes. Outputs include a styled, auto-classified point layer (Classification_6_with_IDs) with Z-based graduated symbology and saved .gpkg files for both classified point layers.

name: Analyze urbanity and mixed-use indicators
desc: The script sets up a QGIS project for Apeldoorn region analysis, creating station point layers and buffer zones (1.5km and 3km), loading and styling indicator layers (MXI_24, FSI_24, Bouwjaar_avg, Urbanity_Index) using predefined color-coded graduated symbology based on field values, clipping indicators to station buffers, and generating print layouts. Outputs include a structured QGIS project (.qgs), vector layers (stations.shp, buffer layers, clipped indicators), QML style files, and A3 landscape print templates.

name: Map railway station service areas
desc: The script sets up a QGIS project for the Apeldoorn region in the Netherlands, structuring layer groups for basemaps, regional indicators (demographics, housing, economy, mobility, amenities), station analysis (including buffered service radii), benchmark cities, and national context maps. It integrates PDOK WMS/WFS services (BRT basemaps, CBS VK500 500m grid, municipal boundaries, railway stations), filters and loads only Apeldoorn-region municipalities and stations, creates 1.5 km and 3 km circular buffers around those stations, and adds pre-existing local indicator layers (e.g., Building Age Average, FSI/MXI, Urbanity Index) into their semantically organized subgroups. Outputs include a fully structured QGIS project (.qgs) with categorized, CRS-aligned (EPSG:28992), and georeferenced layers — ready for spatial analysis of station accessibility and urban indicators.

name: Rasterize channel cross-sections
desc: The script rasterizes 1D hydrological channels into 2D rasters using their associated cross-section geometry and locations. It reads channel centerlines and cross-section location points, constructs triangular meshes representing channel cross-sections in 3D space (including elevation), rasterizes each mesh at a specified pixel size, clips the resulting rasters to the channel outline, and merges them—optionally with a Digital Elevation Model—using a 'deepen-only' approach where channel elevations override DEM values only if lower. Inputs include vector layers (channels as lines, cross-section locations as points) and optionally a DEM; outputs are a merged raster layer representing the 2D channel bed topography.

name: Identify flood-affected buildings
desc: The script identifies buildings potentially affected by river flooding by computing a 150-meter buffer around input river centerlines (vector lines), converting building footprints (vector polygons) to centroids, and selecting only those building centroids that intersect the buffered flood-prone zone. The output is a vector feature class containing the subset of buildings whose centroids fall within the flood inundation buffer — serving as a proxy for buildings at risk during river overbank flow events.

name: Extract coastal zone buffer
desc: The script extracts and delineates the coastal zone around the Canal da Barra in Rio Grande, RS, Brazil, using OpenStreetMap coastline and land polygon data. It computes a buffer distance based on the average side length of a user-defined reference polygon (in WGS84), downloads and clips OSM coastline and land polygons to the area of interest, reprojects to UTM 22S, applies the computed buffer to the coastline, subtracts land polygons to isolate ocean/canal areas, clips the result to the reference polygon, filters out micro-fragments below 0.0001 deg², and exports the final zone as GeoJSON. Outputs include a GeoJSON file ('canal_barra_zona.geojson') and two layers added to the QGIS project: 'canal_barra_zona' and 'poligono_referencia'.

name: Generate estuary water area
desc: The script produces a cleaned, filled water area for an estuary by intersecting a manually drawn polygon ('estuario_rascunho') with OpenStreetMap (OSM) water features (natural=water, landuse=reservoir, or waterway=riverbank) extracted from a Geofabrik Brazil South PBF file. It performs geometry cleaning (fix, dissolve, multipart-to-singlepart), reprojection to UTM 22S (EPSG:32722), spatial clipping and filtering by OSM tags, hole removal, and area-based filtering (MIN_WATER_AREA_M2). Outputs include GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Shapefile, and CSV files containing the final water polygons with attributes (id, name, source, method, area_m2, perim_m).

name: Refine estuary boundary using OSM land polygons
desc: The script refines a manually drawn estuary polygon in QGIS by buffering it to define a search area, downloading and clipping OpenStreetMap land-polygon data, subtracting land from the search area to derive water, selecting only water features intersecting the original sketch (with buffer tolerance), pruning narrow intrusions, removing small holes and fragments, and exporting the final refined estuary as GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Shapefile, and summary CSV with area/perimeter attributes.

name: Compute slope aspect hillshade
desc: The script computes three terrain derivatives—slope (in degrees), aspect (in degrees), and hillshade—from a high-resolution USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second digital elevation model (DEM). It first reprojects the input GeoTIFF DEM from its native CRS (likely NAD83 geographic) to UTM Zone 18N (EPSG:32618) to ensure metrically accurate slope and aspect calculations; then applies GDAL’s slope, aspect, and hillshade algorithms using bilinear resampling and standard illumination parameters (azimuth 315°, altitude 45°, z-factor 2.0); outputs are three georeferenced GeoTIFFs stored in a local output directory and added as layers to the QGIS project for visualization and portfolio documentation.

name: Identify census tracts near campus
desc: The script identifies New York census tracts within 10 km of the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) campus using vector geoprocessing: it loads TIGER/Line 2023 census tract boundaries, reprojects them to UTM Zone 18N, creates a 10 km buffer around the RIT point location (43.0846°N, −77.6744°W), clips the tracts to that buffer, computes each clipped tract’s area in square kilometers, and outputs the resulting filtered, area-annotated tract layer. It optionally supports joining ACS B01003 population data (though the CSV path is empty in this run).

name: Reproject spatial data
desc: The script reprojects geospatial data (either raster or vector) to a specified target coordinate reference system (CRS) using QGIS processing algorithms. It automatically detects input type via file extension (.tif, .tiff, .img, .vrt for raster; otherwise assumed vector), then applies 'gdal:warpreproject' for rasters with configurable resampling (bilinear or nearest neighbor), or 'native:reprojectlayer' for vectors. Outputs include a success flag, output file path, target CRS, and input type classification.

name: Identify parcels intersecting transmission lines
desc: The script performs a spatial query to extract or select land parcels (from a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'Parcels') that intersect with high-voltage transmission line geometries (from 'transmission_lines'). It uses two QGIS processing algorithms: (1) 'native:extractbylocation' to generate a new temporary layer of parcels intersecting transmission lines (using predicates: intersects, contains, within, overlaps, equals, touches), and (2) 'native:selectbylocation' to select those same parcels in the active layer using only the 'intersects' predicate. The output is a subset of parcel features (MultiPolygon, SRID=2232) spatially related to transmission infrastructure (MultiLineString, SRID=3857), intended for solar siting suitability analysis where proximity to transmission is a key constraint.

name: Generate concave hull from points
desc: The script computes a concave hull (alpha shape) from an input point layer using Delaunay triangulation, edge-length filtering based on an alpha threshold (0–1), removal of triangles with edges longer than alpha × maximum edge length, dissolution of remaining triangles, and optional hole removal and multipart geometry splitting. The output is a polygon vector layer representing the concave hull.

name: Clip and buffer hydrographic network
desc: The script performs a vector clipping operation on an input hydrographic layer using a clip polygon layer, then filters the clipped result by 'Descripc' attribute values corresponding to three river network levels (Principal, Secundaria, Terciaria), assigns distinct blue colors to each subset, and applies distance-based buffers (100m, 50m, 20m) to generate buffered layers for each level. Outputs include the clipped layer and three buffered layers named with descriptive prefixes and distances.

name: Identify contributing subcatchments
desc: The script identifies the upstream contributing subcatchments for each gauging station by topologically traversing a river network (using NET_ID and NET_TO fields), collecting associated subcatchments via CATCH_ID, dissolving them into a single polygon per station, and attaching Mean Flow and Mean Low Flow attributes from the gauging station layer. It requires pre-processed inputs: a fixed river network with flow direction topology, ungaged subcatchment polygons, and point-based gauging stations with hydrological time-series summary fields (e.g., annual mean flow). Output is a polygon layer — one dissolved gauged subcatchment per station — enriched with flow metrics.

name: Calculate population statistics by district
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, sum, count) of population density values from a 1km-resolution raster (pak_ppp_2020_1km_Aggregated.tif) over fixed district boundary geometries in Pakistan. It first repairs invalid geometries in the input district shapefile using 'native:fixgeometries', then applies 'native:zonalstatisticsfb' to aggregate raster values per district polygon. The output is a CSV file ('zonal_stats.csv') containing statistical summaries appended with prefix '_' for each district feature.

name: Analyze LST spatial gradients around green spaces
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean Land Surface Temperature) for concentric annular buffers (0–30m intervals, up to 1050m) around each input green space polygon (e.g., parks, vegetation patches). It first calculates LST mean over the original green space geometry, then iteratively generates 15m-wide buffered rings via buffer→difference operations, and applies zonal statistics to each ring. Outputs are CSV files containing mean LST values per ring (named 'Zonal_stats_{filename}_{distance}.csv'), enabling analysis of LST decay or gradient patterns with distance from green space edges.

name: Generate facility study area
desc: The script generates a GIS-based study area for National Industrial Activities (NIAs) by buffering a facility fenceline layer outward by a user-defined distance (default 1500 m), optionally unioning and dissolving with buffered residences or adjacent sites layers (if provided), simplifying the resulting geometry, and generating hypothetical receiver points along the boundary at a specified interval (default 500 m). Outputs include: (1) a simplified polygon study area; (2) optional facility-only buffer; (3) optional hypothetical receiver points (points along lines); all as vector layers. The workflow handles CRS reprojection when input layers differ from the facility layer’s CRS.

name: Estimate clear-cut timing from NDVI time series and CCD analysis
desc: The script processes forest parcel geometries (multi- and single-part polygons) from a GeoPackage to estimate clear-cut dates at both talhão (management unit) and sub-talhão (individual polygon part) levels. It integrates ground-based silvicultural records (corte activities), satellite-derived NDVI time series (from Sentinel-2), and Continuous Change Detection (CCD) outputs (tBreak_ddm, ECCD1/ECCD2, NC) to derive: (1) first/last clear-cut dates per id_gleba; (2) estimated clear-cut dates per sub-parcel; (3) temporal accuracy metrics (e.g., days between estimated drop date and ground-truthed start/end dates); (4) spatial statistics on sub-parcel fragmentation vs. cutting frequency; (5) quality assessment of CCD results (isolated NULLs, NC distribution, date-difference histograms); and (6) visualized, color-coded layers for QGIS with categorized 'drop_date' or 'estimated_date' symbology. Outputs include CSV tables (e.g., 'df_final.csv', 'nvg_sub_talhao.csv', 'parcels_limitations.csv'), shapefiles (e.g., 'nvg_singlepart_sub_talhao.gpkg', 'ccd_results_all_tiles_visual_analysis.shp'), and statistical plots (scatterplots, histograms, timelines).

name: Align thematic parcel boundaries to reference cadastre
