desc: The script aligns user-provided thematic vector boundary layers (e.g., heritage zones, land use polygons) to authoritative reference boundary datasets (e.g., Belgian GRB, Dutch BRK, OSM, or local cadastral layers) using geometric alignment strategies. It computes overlap-relevant intersections and differences, generates corrected geometries, produces diff layers (diff_plus/diff_min), and optionally creates a review-ready correction layer flagging features exceeding a configurable REVIEW_PERCENTAGE change threshold. Alignment is governed by parameters including RELEVANT_DISTANCE (m), Open Domain strategy, Snap strategy, and prediction-enabled multi-distance evaluation.

name: Calculate rural land location factor
desc: The script calculates the Factor de Localització (Location Factor) for rural land valuation in Catalonia, Spain, following Royal Decree 1492/2011. It computes U1 (population-based factor) by spatially aggregating census population values (censvalor) from municipal census layers within two concentric buffers (4 km and 4–40 km) around a user-selected point; U2 (distance decay factor) from manually entered road distance (d); and U3 (landscape and land use coefficient) from user-entered coefficients p (paisatge) and t (usos). The final output is the multiplicative composite FL = U1 × U2 × U3, displayed in a QGIS message box with validation warnings for out-of-range inputs (d > 60 km, p > 2, t > 7). Intermediate GIS layers (buffers, clipped municipalities, aggregated summary tables) are generated and styled but subsequently removed.

name: Generate ICA 100-40 FRZ safety zones
desc: The script generates regulated airport safety zones (ICA 100–40 FRZ) around runway centerlines, implementing the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 14-compliant obstacle limitation surfaces: a 40°-wide wedge-shaped ‘FRZ’ (Final Approach and Take-off Zone) extending 3550 ft from runway ends, plus concentric lateral buffer zones at <100 ft (2350 ft radius), <200 ft (2960 ft), and <300 ft (3570 ft) — all clipped to exclude overlapping FRZ areas. It computes azimuth-corrected wedge buffers per vertex (with angle correction for runway end orientation), performs geometric differences and unions to isolate non-overlapping annular segments, appends a 'tipo' attribute labeling each zone (e.g., '<100 ft', 'FRZ'), merges all geometries, adds auto-incrementing IDs, and outputs a styled vector layer with fields AUTO, nome, and tipo.

name: Merge KLC landscape layers
desc: The script loads multiple vector layers from a GeoPackage file (klc_buffer_wdpa_54009.gpkg), filters out layers with 'sites' in the name, reprojects invalid layers to EPSG:54009, standardizes attributes by retaining only a generated 'KLC_ID' and adding an 'Area_km2' field (computed via QgsDistanceArea), merges all cleaned layers into a single vector layer named 'KLC_new', computes geometry-based area, appends metadata fields ('KLC_name', 'Comments', 'target_PAs', 'fid_klc') by joining with external JSON files (KLC_name.txt, KLC_comments.txt, KLC_PA.txt), reprojects the final layer to EPSG:4326, saves it as a new GeoPackage (klc_YYYYMMDD_proposal.gpkg), and prepares it for rasterization (e.g., for 30-arcsecond grid export).

name: Quantify shrubland density within buffered interest region
desc: The script quantifies shrubland density (embroussaillement) within a user-defined region of interest by first thresholding a raster layer at >0.5m height to create a binary shrub presence mask, then buffering the region of interest by 200m, intersecting it with a vector-based habitat/milieu map, and finally computing zonal statistics (mean, sum, count) of the shrub mask over each milieu polygon. Outputs include a masked raster layer ('Embroussaillement > 0.5m'), a cropped and styled vector layer ('milieux_hongrin'), and zonal statistics attached as attributes to the vector layer.

name: Create empty boundary layer
desc: The script creates an empty vector layer (point/line/polygon) in WGS84 (EPSG:4326) CRS, initialized from a fixed global bounding box extent (-60.0146,-39.2569,-24.5053,-3.6157), then filters it to retain only features where "id" = 99 (though the source layer has no real attributes — this expression yields an empty feature collection), and finally refactors fields to produce a clean, attribute-empty, geometry-capable vector layer named 'Desenhar Nova Área' for manual digitization of property or implementation areas in QGIS.

name: Refactor and dissolve geospatial features
desc: The script refactors heterogeneous vector inputs (polygons, lines, points) representing a single contracted area into a topologically clean, dissolved polygon layer with standardized attributes. It performs geometry conversion (polygons→lines→explode→polygonize), spatial attribute joining (centroid-based association), ID field injection, dissolution by ID, and field standardization (adding 'id' and 'dt_arquivo' fields). The output is a validated, HorusBI-compliant shapefile named per the pattern 'AAA-UF0001-01', ready for upload to the HorusBI platform.

name: Refactor implementation area geometry
desc: The script refactors and standardizes vector geometries (points, lines, or polygons) representing an agroforestry implementation area into a single, topologically correct polygon feature class suitable for submission to the Horus monitoring system. It handles two workflows: (1) for non-linear plantings, it merges inputs, converts polygons to lines, explodes and polygonizes them, then joins attributes via centroid-based spatial association and dissolves by generated ID; (2) for linear plantings (e.g., rows), it rejects polygons, converts points-to-paths or merges lines, filters out-of-Brazil features using a UTM grid shapefile, reprojects each UTM zone (18–25) to its appropriate CRS, applies buffered line-to-polygon conversion per zone, merges results, and dissolves. Outputs include a standardized polygon layer with mandatory fields: 'id' (e.g., 'BEL-SP0001-01'), 'culturas', 'outros', 'dt_implant', 'dt_arquivo', and 'tipo' (fixed to 1 for implemented area).

name: Calculate planimetric area by UTM zone
desc: The script calculates the planimetric area (in hectares) of input polygon features by first identifying the dominant UTM zone for each polygon using intersection with a national UTM grid layer ('br_grade_utm_wgs.shp'), then reprojecting each polygon subset to its corresponding UTM CRS (EPSG:31978–31985 for zones 18–25), computing geometry area in square meters, converting to hectares (dividing by 10,000), aggregating per polygon ID via sum, and outputting a dissolved layer with fields 'UTM' (zone number) and 'areaha_utm' (total area in ha). Input polygons outside Brazil trigger an error output and early termination.

name: Convert lines to polygons
desc: The script converts input line vector layers into closed polygon geometries by first reprojecting the layer to EPSG:4326, then exploding multi-part and curved lines into single-segment lines, followed by polygonization (i.e., forming polygons from planar line networks that enclose areas), and finally outputting a cleaned polygon feature class with preserved attributes — intended for submission via the Horus environmental monitoring system.

name: Merge and convert vector layers to polygons
desc: The script merges multiple input vector layers—polygons, lines, and points—into a single unified polygon layer. Polygons are merged directly; lines are converted to polygons using an external lineToPolygon algorithm (likely by closing lines or buffering); points are converted to polygons using an external pointToPolygon algorithm that respects grouping and sequencing fields (e.g., to reconstruct polygon boundaries from ordered GPS points). All outputs are reprojected to EPSG:4326, merged, and passed through a field refactoring step (with no field mappings applied) to produce a clean, geometry-normalized polygon feature sink for ingestion into the Horus system.

name: Convert points to polygons
desc: The script converts an input point vector layer into polygon features by first reprojecting the points to EPSG:4326, then connecting them into closed paths (lines) using a grouping field and sequence ordering field, and finally polygonizing those lines into valid polygons. The output is a polygon vector layer ('refatorado') preserving original attributes, intended for representing enclosed areas (e.g., field boundaries, plot perimeters, or administrative zones) derived from ordered boundary points.

name: Remove street view stop points
desc: The script removes GPS points corresponding to vehicle stops during Street View image collection by identifying clusters of points with timestamps (extracted from filename strings) that fall within a user-defined battery-swap time threshold (e.g., 150 seconds); it buffers initial and final points in temporal sequences, counts point density per buffer, joins counts back to the original point layer, and filters out points where density <6 — effectively eliminating stationary or low-mobility capture locations. Output is a cleaned point vector layer with duplicate geometries removed.

name: Generate vector grid from extent
desc: The script generates a vector grid (points, lines, rectangles, diamonds, or hexagons) aligned to a geographic coordinate system (EPSG:4326) using user-defined scale-based spacing (e.g., 0.025° for 1:25k), derived from the bounding box of an input vector layer. It optionally separates vertical and horizontal grid lines, adds a 'ROTULO' field containing rounded longitude values (for points/lines), and outputs the grid as one or more vector layers (full grid, vertical lines, horizontal lines) in the specified target CRS.

name: Join land parcel attributes to geometry
desc: The script performs a tabular join between a vector layer of land parcels ('izuch_A', containing polygon geometries) and a CSV table ('izuch', containing attribute data), using the 'ukID' field as the join key. It then validates geometry integrity, fixes invalid geometries if necessary, removes specified redundant fields (e.g., 'field_14', 'IDотчетаРГФ', 'nom_1000'), and exports the cleaned, joined layer as a GeoPackage in Pulkovo 1942 (EPSG:4284). The final output is a validated, attribute-enriched polygon layer representing land parcels with associated reporting and classification metadata.

name: Generate slope map from DTM
desc: The script generates a slope map (expressed as percent grade) from a digital terrain model (DTM) raster input. It first clips the DTM to a user-defined extent and resamples it to a specified output cell size using GDAL translate; then computes slope (in degrees) via QGIS native:slope; resamples the slope raster using mode-based aggregation (GDAL warpreproject with resampling method 6); converts slope from degrees to percent grade using the formula 100 × tan(slope_in_radians); and finally applies lower and upper percentile limits to clamp output values, producing a clipped, resampled, unit-converted, and thresholded slope raster.

name: Quantify rasterization quality
desc: The script evaluates the fidelity of rasterizing a source vector layer (e.g., irrigation polygons) into a raster, using a mask vector layer to define the valid domain. It computes per-category area statistics from the clipped vector geometry and compares them against the corresponding pixel-based area counts from the masked rasterized output. The core metric is the root-mean-square error (RMSE) of area differences normalized by total mask area (expressed as a percentage quality index), and outputs a table listing each unique value (from the burned field), its vector-derived area, raster-derived area, and squared error.

name: Clip raster or vector data
desc: The script performs spatial clipping of either raster or vector geospatial data using a mask layer. For raster input, it uses GDAL's 'cliprasterbymasklayer' algorithm with LZW compression and cutline cropping; for vector input, it uses QGIS's native 'clip' algorithm. The output is a clipped temporary layer returned as a file path or memory layer reference.

name: Fill raster no-data values
desc: The script performs two sequential GDAL-based geoprocessing operations: first, it fills no-data (null/NaN) pixel values in the input raster using an inverse distance weighted interpolation method via gdal:fillnodata; second, it clips the filled raster to the geometry of a provided mask layer using gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer, with cropping enabled and LZW compression applied to the output. The final output is a clipped, no-data-filled raster aligned to the mask’s extent and geometry.

name: Rasterize vector layers over output raster
desc: The script merges multiple vector layers (e.g., administrative boundaries, land use polygons, or constraint zones) from a QGIS project into a single vector layer, then burns a fixed value (0) into the project’s existing output raster using those merged vectors as a mask—effectively restricting or masking the raster to areas covered by the vectors. The output is a modified raster where pixels under the vector geometries retain (or are overwritten with) the burn value, and the merged vector layer is also returned for reference.

name: Model urban heat island intensity
desc: The script models urban heat island (UHI) intensity across Washington, DC using spatial interpolation (IDW and KDE) of point temperature observations (sample points and weather stations), integrates multi-layer geospatial analysis—including green space buffer decay zones, impervious surface classification, building density per census tract, DBSCAN-based hot spot clustering, zonal temperature statistics per census tract, proximity to green spaces/stations, variable-width road heat buffers, and a socioeconomic heat equity index—and outputs styled vector/raster layers, a print layout, and a comprehensive JSON report summarizing UHI patterns, vulnerability gaps, and technical methods.

name: Construct linear stream flow graph
desc: The script constructs a directed graph (DiGraph) representing the topological flow connectivity of linear hydrographic features (stream segments), where each segment is a node and flow direction (upstream → downstream) defines directed edges. It loads a GeoPackage layer 'RH_L' containing stream segments, assigns stable original and new FIDs, extracts start and end vertices of each segment, spatially indexes start vertices, and iteratively identifies downstream connections by matching end vertices to nearby start vertices within a tolerance (0.001² map units). Outputs include a GML file (Hydro_XXXX_l.gml) and a Python pickle file (Hydro_XXXX_l.pickle) of the NetworkX DiGraph for watershed delineation workflows.

name: Trace downslope flow paths
desc: The script computes the complete downslope flow path (trajectory) of individual raindrop-like points ('gouttes') across a high-resolution hydrographic network derived from LiDAR-based digital elevation models. It first locates each input point within a Hydrographic Delineation Unit (UDH), snaps it to the nearest stream segment or raster cell center, optionally buffers and snaps to the nearest stream within a user-defined radius, then traces the full downstream path by traversing a precomputed directed graph (GML) of stream segments — combining upstream-split segments (if the point falls directly on a stream or junction) with all downstream-connected segments extracted via NetworkX edge DFS. Outputs are MultiLineString features representing the full flowpath per droplet, attributed with the droplet ID, UDH code, and total path length in km, projected in EPSG:6622 (NAD83(CSRS) / MTM zone 8).

name: Delineate watershed boundaries for point/polygon occurrences
desc: The script delineates hydrologically connected watersheds for user-provided occurrence features (lines or polygons) using high-resolution LiDAR-derived D8 flow direction rasters and a vector hydrographic network (RH_L) with a sub-watershed index (S_UDH). It rasterizes each occurrence per intersecting S_UDH, applies Whitebox Tools' Watershed algorithm to extract the contributing area, polygonizes the result, repairs geometries, dissolves fragments, removes sliver holes, and optionally adds upstream S_UDHs by traversing a directed stream network graph. Outputs are multi-polygon watershed features in EPSG:6622 (NAD83(CSRS) / Quebec Lambert), each attributed with the original occurrence ID, UDH code, and area in hectares.

name: Compute centroid-based buffered dissolved polygons
desc: The script processes a vector layer by first computing centroids of its features, then buffering those centroids with a fixed distance of 1,000,000 map units, and finally dissolving the resulting buffers into a single multipart geometry. It includes CRS validation (rejecting geographic coordinate systems), uses QgsProcessingMultiStepFeedback for progress tracking, and returns the dissolved buffer layer as the output. All steps are executed via QGIS native algorithms ('native:centroids', 'native:buffer', 'native:dissolve') within a custom multistep processing algorithm.

name: Clip and buffer hydrographic networks
desc: The script performs geoprocessing on hydrographic network layers and administrative boundary layers in QGIS. It first clips the hydrographic layer using the selected boundary layer, then filters the clipped result by a 'Descripc' field containing 'Principal', 'Secundaria', or 'Terciaria', applies configurable distance buffers to each subset, assigns distinct fill symbology per type, and adds all resulting layers to the QGIS project. Outputs include a clipped hydrographic layer and three buffered layers (Principal, Secundaria, Terciaria) with specified distances and colors.

name: Detect LiDAR ground misclassification errors
desc: The script detects erroneous misclassifications of ground points (class 2) in LiDAR point clouds—specifically those incorrectly labeled as non-ground (e.g., buildings, class 6) or missing from the ground layer—by extracting sol (ground) and bati (building) points, rasterizing them into a binary surface model, identifying zero-value ‘hole’ polygons (i.e., areas with no ground/building points), applying morphological opening/closing to filter noise, and selecting candidate error polygons based on area thresholds, convexity (>0.55), and elongation (>2); outputs include: (1) corrected LAS file containing only classes 2+6, (2) rasterized surface model, (3) hole polygons before/after morphological filtering, (4) oriented minimum bounding boxes (OMBB) with elongation metrics, (5) final candidate error polygons, and (6) if truth data is provided, evaluation metrics (precision, recall, F-score) comparing detected polygons against ground-truth points.

name: Generate spatial grid over input area
desc: The script generates a vector grid (points, lines, or rectangular polygons) aligned to the extent of an input polygon layer, with user-defined horizontal and vertical spacing. It creates the full grid using QGIS's native:creategrid algorithm, then clips it to intersect only with the input polygon geometry using native:extractbylocation. The output is a feature sink containing the clipped grid features.

name: Generate multi-width road buffers
desc: The script generates a single GeoPackage (FGB) file containing road buffers with class-specific widths (37m, 33.25m, 28.25m, 27m) applied to road centerlines from a shapefile ('全道路リンク標高.shp'), where each buffer width corresponds to a road width class (R22_005 = 1–4). It reprojects the input from JGD2011 (EPSG:4612) to JGD2011 / Japan Plane Rectangular CS VII (EPSG:6675) for accurate meter-based buffering, applies per-class filtering and buffering (with √2/2 scaling and flat end caps), merges all class buffers, and reprojects the final output back to the original CRS (EPSG:4612). The output is a merged, multi-width buffered polygon layer representing road influence zones across the Hokuriku region.

name: Clip aerial imagery by road buffer polygons
desc: The script processes high-resolution aerial raster images by spatially clipping them to road buffer polygons derived from a vector file (FGB format). It first clips the road buffer layer to the extent of each aerial image, dissolves the resulting buffered polygons into a single geometry, then uses that dissolved polygon as a mask to crop the aerial image to the road-adjacent area. Outputs are clipped GeoTIFFs (one per input aerial image) and corresponding clipped/dissolved vector files (in FlatGeobuf format) representing the road buffers intersecting each image footprint.

name: Buffer vector features with smoothing
desc: The script takes an input vector layer, first applies geometry smoothing using the native QGIS smoothgeometry algorithm (with 2 iterations, 0.25 offset, and max angle 180°), then performs a dissolved buffer operation around the smoothed geometries using a user-specified distance (default 300.0 map units); the output is a single-part polygon feature class representing the buffered area, with all input features merged into one geometry.

name: Interpolate bathymetric DEM from point soundings
desc: The script interpolates a bathymetric digital elevation model (DEM) from sparse bathymetric point measurements using an anisotropic inverse distance weighting (IDW) method aligned with flow direction along a centerline. It first transforms point coordinates into a curvilinear S–N coordinate system relative to a user-provided river or channel centerline and ROI polygon, then performs flow-aligned interpolation (accounting for anisotropy ratio and max search distance), rasterizes the interpolated points at a specified cell size, and optionally evaluates model accuracy via RMSE against original points within the ROI. Outputs include a GeoTIFF DEM (or temporary raster layer) and optionally a difference layer and RMSE value.

name: Invert clip to extract outside area
desc: The script performs an inverted clipping operation: given a source vector layer and a user-defined extent (bounding box), it first creates a polygon layer from the extent, assigns WGS84 projection, clips the source layer to that extent, then computes the difference between the extent polygon and the clipped result—yielding the portion of the extent polygon that does *not* intersect the source layer. The output is a vector feature class representing the 'outside' or 'complement' region of the source layer within the specified extent.

name: Extract municipal land cover and ecosystem layers
desc: The script selects 49 Colombian municipalities by their numeric codes (MPIO_CDPMP) from a national political boundary shapefile (MGN_MPIO_POLITICO.shp), saves the selection as a new vector layer (municipios_seleccionadosp.shp), then performs spatial clipping of two thematic geospatial datasets — 'Ecosistemas' (ecosystem types) and 'Coberturas' (vegetation cover) — first collectively and then individually per municipality. For each municipality, it generates separate GPKG files (e.g., 'Ecosistemas_76109_Buenaventura.gpkg') containing only the portions of those thematic layers intersecting that municipality’s boundary. Outputs include: (1) a consolidated clipped layer for all selected municipalities, and (2) 49 municipally partitioned GPKG files for both ecosystems and vegetation cover, stored in dedicated output directories with sanitized filenames.

name: Clip ecosystems and vegetation cover by community councils
desc: The script selects specific community councils (by ID) from a titled community council shapefile, then performs spatial clipping of two thematic vector layers—'Ecosistemas' (ecosystems) and 'Coberturas' (vegetation cover)—against each selected council polygon individually. For each council, it generates a separate GeoPackage file containing only the portions of ecosystems and vegetation cover intersecting that council’s boundary. Outputs include: (1) a filtered shapefile of selected councils ('Consejo_seleccionados.shp'), (2) clipped ecosystem layers per council (e.g., 'Ecosistemas_Nombre.gpkg'), and (3) clipped vegetation cover layers per council (e.g., 'Coberturas_Nombre.gpkg'), all saved to dedicated subdirectories and optionally loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Generate IMSGS standard grid
desc: The script generates a polygon grid layer conforming to the Indonesian Multiscale Grid System (IMSGS) standard, using either a user-defined bounding box in WGS84 (λmin, λmax, φmin, φmax) or the extent of an input vector AOI layer. It supports six predefined angular resolutions (30'×30', 15'×15', 7'30"×7'30", 2'30"×2'30", 30"×30", 5"×5") referenced to a fixed origin at (90°E, −15°S). The output is a GeoPackage/shapefile-compatible vector layer with polygons and a uniquely structured alphanumeric ID field ('IMGSID') computed via hierarchical tiling logic based on centroid coordinates — e.g., 'KKBBCDEFGGHH' for 5" resolution — encoding column/row indices across nested subdivisions. Optional spatial extraction by the input AOI geometry is performed before ID assignment.

name: Extract land type areas
desc: The script extracts and calculates land system/unit areas for property, paddock, and watered areas using vector overlay operations (intersection, dissolve, buffer) on input polygon and point layers. It supports ellipsoidal or planar area calculation, transforms layers to EPSG:9473 if input CRS is geographic, and optionally exports results to multiple vector formats (gpkg, shp, json, kml, kmz) and a summary spreadsheet. Outputs include layered vector files per analysis unit (property, paddocks, watered zones at 3km/5km radii) with attributes: land unit name, area in m²/ha/km², and percentage of parent geometry.

name: Summarize fire risk by district
desc: The script computes counts and percentages of pixels classified as low, moderate, and high fire risk within each pastoral district polygon using a raster layer ('AussieGRASS Fire Risk raster') and exports the results to an Excel spreadsheet. It clips the fire risk raster to each district, reads pixel values via GDAL numeric array operations, classifies pixels into risk categories (0–20: low; 20–30: moderate; 30–40: high; -2: water; 0: nodata; 253: firescars), calculates counts and normalized percentages per class, validates with a checksum, and writes district-level summary statistics to a spreadsheet.

name: Calculate maximum distance to water
desc: The script calculates the maximum Euclidean distance from any point within each input paddock polygon to the nearest water point (e.g., bore, trough, dam) using vector-to-raster proximity analysis. It first harmonizes CRS between paddock (polygon) and water point (point) layers — handling geographic/projected mismatches by reprojecting to a common projected CRS (EPSG:9473 if both are geographic; otherwise aligns to the projected layer’s CRS). For each paddock containing ≥1 water point, it: (1) subsets water points intersecting the paddock; (2) rasterizes them into a binary mask at user-defined resolution (5–100 m); (3) computes a GDAL proximity raster (distance in map units); (4) clips the proximity raster to the paddock geometry; (5) extracts the local maximum distance (in meters) per paddock; and (6) derives a global maximum across all paddocks. Outputs include: (a) one clipped proximity raster (.tif) per analyzed paddock, named after the paddock (with sanitised field values), stored in a user-specified folder; (b) an optional Excel report ('Max_dist_to_water.xlsx') listing paddock name, area (ha), water point count, and max distance to water (km); and (c) optional loading/styling of rasters in QGIS with a gradient color ramp scaled to the global maximum. No satellite, temporal, or spectral data is used — inputs are purely user-provided vector layers (paddocks + water points), with no embedded time dimension, imagery, or remote sensing bands.

name: Calculate pasture growth medians by district
desc: The script creates an Excel spreadsheet containing stacked, median monthly pasture growth values for each pastoral district across three financial years. It processes .img raster files from a user-specified directory, groups them by financial year (current and two prior FYs), computes cumulative zonal statistics (mean and median) over pastoral district polygons, and appends long-term median reference values for northern and southern districts. Output is a multi-sheet Excel file with columns: Financial_year, Calendar_year, Month, District, Cumulative_mean, Long_term_median, Cumulative_median.

name: Calculate district burnt percentage
desc: The script calculates the percentage of each pastoral district that has been burnt, using a firescar polygon layer and a pastoral districts polygon layer. It performs geometry fixing on the firescar layer, applies a temporal filter (month > 6) to isolate the financial year (July–June), runs vector overlap analysis to compute burnt area per district, then repeats the overlap without filtering for the calendar year (January–December). Results are compiled into two memory layers — one for financial year and one for calendar year — each containing district name, total district area (km²), burnt area (km²), and percentage burnt. These are exported to an Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx or .ods) with separate sheets for each year.

name: Summarize relative growth percentile by district
desc: The script computes pixel counts and percentages for seven relative growth percentile classes (0–10, 10–20, ..., 90–100) within each pastoral district polygon using an input percentile growth raster. It clips the raster to each district, counts pixels in each class (excluding special values 253, 254, 255, and -999), calculates class percentages of valid pixels, validates percentage sum, and exports results to an Excel spreadsheet with columns for district name, class counts, class percentages, and a check-sum percentage.

name: Summarize TSDM pixel counts by district
desc: The script creates an Excel workbook with two summary sheets: one reporting pixel counts and percentages for TSDM raster classes (low, low-moderate, moderate, high) per pastoral district, and another for TSDM percentile raster classes (below average, average, above average). It clips rasters to each district polygon, applies region-specific thresholds (Northern/Southern/Custom scales) to classify TSDM values, computes counts and percentages excluding water (-2, 254) and firescar (253), and exports results to Excel using QGIS's native export-to-spreadsheet algorithm.

name: Summarize total pasture growth by district
desc: The script stacks monthly growth rasters from a specified folder (financial year), clips the summed raster to each pastoral district, and classifies pixel counts into four growth classes (Low, Low/moderate, Moderate, High) using region-specific thresholds (Northern Scale, Southern Scale, or Custom Scale). It computes both absolute counts and percentages per class per district and exports the results to an Excel spreadsheet. Input includes a folder of .img rasters, a vector layer of pastoral districts with 'DISTRICT' field, and a custom matrix parameter defining regional scales and district-to-region mapping.

name: Calculate railway length within boundary
desc: The script calculates the total length (in km) of railway features intersecting a user-provided GeoJSON boundary. It loads railway data from an ArcGIS FeatureServer (NIC Street MapServer, layer ID 20), handles pagination if direct provider fails, reprojects to match the boundary’s CRS, clips the railway geometry to the boundary, computes per-segment and total lengths in kilometers using metric measurement (EPSG:3857), appends 'len_km' and 'total_km' fields to the clipped layer, and exports the result as a GeoJSON file named 'BharatMaps_RailLengths.geojson' with full attribute preservation.

name: Extract road network length within boundary
desc: The script extracts, merges, and clips road infrastructure layers (National Highway, State Highway, Major Road, and GQ NS EW corridors) from Bharat Maps 2024 (admin2024 ArcGIS MapServer) to a user-provided administrative or custom boundary (GeoJSON/SHP), then saves the resulting clipped road vector as a GeoJSON file named 'BharatMaps_RoadLengths.geojson' — intended for downstream road length calculation, density analysis, or infrastructure mapping in India.

name: Extract schools within boundary
desc: The script downloads school point features from the NIC Street REST service (MapServer layer 0) in paginated GeoJSON batches, saves the raw collection to disk, loads it into QGIS, reprojects it to match the user-provided boundary CRS if necessary, clips the schools layer to the boundary geometry, and saves the clipped result as a GeoJSON file. Key outputs include 'schools_raw.geojson' and 'schools_clipped.geojson', both generated via QGIS processing algorithms ('native:reprojectlayer' and 'native:clip') and OGR vector writing.

name: Package and deliver geospatial layers
desc: The script orchestrates on-demand geospatial data extraction, clipping, reprojection, styling, and packaging from a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database (schema 'acervo_descripcion_1') into user-specified output formats (SHP, KML, GEOJSON, GEOPACKAGE, or GeoTIFF). It retrieves vector layers referenced in a master view ('mapa_master_vw'), classifies them by geometry type (point/line/polygon), clips them to a user-provided WKT geometry ('geom_descarga'), applies attribute normalization (e.g., populating a 'describe' field with layer name), handles binary field exclusion for Shapefile compatibility, applies QML styles (copied or embedded in GeoPackage), and optionally fetches and crops a WMS raster layer ('alta_res_1m') at 1m resolution via a configured WMS endpoint. Outputs are written to a time- and request-id–based temporary directory ('D:/Z_PRUEBAS_MASTER_MAP/Temporales/{idPeticion}/').

name: Calculate basin topographic attributes
desc: The script calculates topographic attributes for each watershed polygon in the 'Basins_A.shp' layer, including area (km²), maximum vertex-to-gauge distance (km), flow direction angle (deg), Schumm elongation ratio (–), and stream density (km/km²). It computes these by geometrically processing basin boundaries and gauge points, clipping river networks to individual basins, and deriving metrics from vertex coordinates, planimetric geometry, and intersected linear features. Outputs are written directly into new fields of the input basin vector layer.

name: Calculate basin topographic and geologic attributes
desc: The script processes pre-delineated catchment polygons (from 'Subbasin_merge.py') to compute basin-scale hydro-geomorphic attributes: (1) topographic — area, maximum vertex-to-gauge distance (L), flow direction angle, Schumm elongation ratio (Re), and stream density (D); (2) geologic — dominant GLiM lithology class ('gc_dom') and fractional coverage of 13 geological classes ('gc_XX_fra') derived via intersection with the GLiM global lithological map; all values are written into new fields of the input basin polygon layer's attribute table. The script assumes prior execution of basin delineation and operates per-basin via iterative filtering and geometric analysis using QGIS Processing algorithms (e.g., 'native:clip', 'native:intersection').

name: Generate urban planning zoning certificate
desc: The script generates a Certificato di Destinazione Urbanistica (CDU) — an official Italian urban planning zoning certificate — by spatially intersecting selected cadastral parcels (from a local vector layer named 'terreni_catastali') with urban planning layers organized in a QGIS layer tree group. It extracts attribute information (e.g., 'descrizione', 'nome', 'riferimento legislativo', 'articolo') from intersecting features, computes intersection area (m²) and percentage of parcel area, filters out intersections < 1 m² if enabled, and composes a styled HTML report exported as PDF (and optionally ODT). Outputs include: (1) a georeferenced A4 PDF containing textual zoning information, optional logo, protocol/richiedente/data fields, legal notes, and an embedded map image (500×500 px) centered on the selected parcels; (2) optionally, an ODT version of the same content. The process uses QGIS native and GDAL vector processing algorithms ('native:clip', 'gdal:clipvectorbypolygon'), relies entirely on local vector data loaded in the QGIS project, and performs no remote sensing or time-series analysis.

name: Merge OSPAR fisheries disturbance layers
desc: The script merges two OSPAR fisheries disturbance vector layers ('CNS' and 'NCS') from the QSR2023_BH3_Disturbance_Layers_VMS.gpkg dataset. It first fixes geometries for both layers, reprojects them to EPSG:4326, builds spatial indexes, adds a categorical 'label' field ('CNS' or 'NCS') to distinguish source layers, merges the labeled layers into a single feature collection, assigns a unique integer ID ('ess_unique_id') using row number, and applies a final geometry fix to ensure topological validity. The primary output is 'sl1_bh3_merged_disturbance' — a clean, unified, WGS84-reprojected vector layer of marine fisheries/disturbance features ready for downstream R analysis in MSFD (Marine Strategy Framework Directive) reporting.

name: Extract and classify OSPAR sub-regions
desc: The script processes the OSPAR Level 2 Reporting Units (2018) vector dataset to extract nine specific L2 regions (e.g., 'L2.2.7', 'L2.3.2'), fixes geometries, reprojects to EPSG:4326, filters by region code, refactors attributes to assign subregion labels ('NNS'/'NCS') for both 2018 and 2025 classification schemes, flags membership in either temporal boundary definition ('2018_bound'/'2025_bound'), and dissolves the features — producing a single multipart polygon layer where geometries are merged by shared boundary flags and classification fields, intended as input for downstream R-based spatial analysis.

name: Dissolve Scottish marine assessment areas
desc: The script processes a vector layer of Scottish Assessment Areas (Marine) to produce two outputs: (1) a reprojected version in EPSG:4326, and (2) a dissolved single-polygon geometry representing the total marine assessment area for Scotland, with its area calculated in square kilometers (scottish_region_areakm2). The workflow includes geometry validation, reprojection, spatial index creation, dissolution (with no grouping fields), and field refactoring to compute and store the area attribute.

name: Clip and dissolve OSPAR subregions by Scottish waters
desc: The script clips OSPAR sub-regional boundaries (2018 and 2025 versions) using dissolved Scottish marine/territorial region boundaries, then performs spatial intersection, dissolution by temporal boundary flags ('2018_bound' and '2025_bound'), area calculation in km², geometry fixing, multipart promotion, and final total-area aggregation per year — producing six distinct output layers: two clipped-and-dissolved subregion layers (2018/2025), two clipped non-dissolved layers (scottish-waters_2018/2025), and two dissolved total-area summary layers (dissolved 2018/2025 total_areakm2), all with area-calculated attributes for R analysis.

name: Clip disturbance by 2018 area boundaries
desc: The script clips a merged disturbance layer (SL1 BH3) first by a user-defined grid (e.g., 10×10 cells covering the disturbance extent), then clips the gridded disturbance by a dissolved 2018 area calculation polygon layer. The final output is a vector layer ('Clipped output 2018') containing only the portions of the disturbance that intersect the 2018 study area — effectively spatially constraining disturbance features to the 2018 analysis boundary for downstream R analysis.

name: Clip disturbance areas by 2025 area
desc: The script clips a merged disturbance layer ('SL1 BH3 merged disturbance') using a grid and then further clips the gridded output by a dissolved 2025 area calculation layer ('Dissolved 2025 area calc'). It first creates a rectangular polygon grid aligned to the extent of the disturbance layer, with spacing determined by expression '@extent_width' and fixed vertical spacing. Then it clips the disturbance layer by that grid, and finally clips the resulting gridded disturbance features by the dissolved 2025 area polygon layer. The output is a vector feature class ('Clipped output 2025') containing only the portions of the disturbance layer intersecting the 2025 area.

name: Merge and dissolve protected marine areas
desc: The script processes two vector layers—MPA_SCOTLAND_4326 (Marine Protected Areas) and SAC_SCOTLAND_4326 (Special Areas of Conservation)—both in EPSG:4326. It standardizes field schemas via refactor, filters SACs where 'MPA_NETWOR' = 'Y', and filters MPAs with 'UPDATED' ≤ '2020-12-31' (excluding post-2020 sites like Red Rocks and Longay). After geometry fixing, the layers are merged into a single vector layer ('merged_protected_areas') retaining NAME, PA_CODE, STATUS, UPDATED, and MPA_NETWOR fields. Finally, all geometries are dissolved into a single multipart polygon ('dissolved_protected_areas'), retaining only STATUS, MPA_NETWOR, and a newly derived GEOGRAPHIC field (though not explicitly computed in code — inferred from context as likely a placeholder or error; actual output fields are STATUS and MPA_NETWOR only, per final refactor). The outputs are prepared for downstream R analysis of Scotland’s consolidated protected marine area extent and network status.

name: Clip and assign subregions to features
desc: The script processes a clipped 2018 vector layer of ecological or land-use features (identified by 'ess_unique_id' and 'original_areakm2') by spatially joining it with a dissolved subregions boundary layer (containing 'subreg2018' codes), then slimming attribute fields, removing duplicate features by 'ess_unique_id', calculating the clipped area in km², and replacing null/blank 'subreg2018' values with 'NNS'. Outputs include: (1) a slimmed version retaining only 'ess_unique_id' and 'original_areakm2'; (2) a joined layer with subregion assignments; (3) a de-duplicated version; (4) a final output layer with clipped area ('clipped_to_2018_boundary_by_feature_areakm2') and cleaned 'subreg2018' (defaulting blanks to 'NNS'); and (5) a duplicates check layer. All outputs are vector geometries prepared for downstream R analysis.

name: Clip and assign subregions to features
desc: The script processes a clipped vector layer of features (e.g., ecological or land units identified by 'ess_unique_id') and assigns them to administrative or ecological subregions (labeled 'subreg2025') via spatial intersection. It first refactors the input to retain only 'ess_unique_id' and 'original_areakm2', then joins subregion attributes (one-to-many), removes duplicate features by 'ess_unique_id', and finally computes the clipped area (in km²) for each feature as 'clipped_to_2025_boundary_by_feature_areakm2'. Outputs include: (1) a slimmed feature layer with minimal fields, (2) a joined layer with subregion assignment, (3) a de-duplicated version, and (4) the final layer with computed clipped area — all intended for downstream R-based aggregation and analysis.

name: Identify features within MPAs
desc: The script performs a spatial join to identify which ecological features (e.g., habitat patches or conservation units) fall within the boundaries of dissolved Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) for 2018. It first builds spatial indexes on both the feature layer (clipped to 2018 subregions, with attributes including 'ess_unique_id', 'original_areakm2', 'subreg2018', and 'clipped_to_2018_boundary_by_feature_areakm2') and the MPA layer (a single-feature dissolved polygon layer), then executes a one-to-one 'intersect' join to attach MPA attributes (if any) to each feature — producing an output layer ('MPA_subregion_information_2018') enriched with spatial membership information for downstream R analysis.

name: Identify features within MPAs
desc: The script identifies geospatial features (e.g., ecological or management units) that intersect with Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) using a spatial join operation. It first builds spatial indexes on both the input features layer (features_clipped_with_area_subregion_2025) and the dissolved MPA layer (MPA_dissolved_layer), then refactors fields to retain specific attributes (ess_unique_id, original_areakm2, subreg2025, clipped_to_2025_boundary_by_feature_areakm2), and finally performs a one-to-one 'intersect' spatial join to attach MPA attributes to features. The output is a vector layer (MPA_subregion_information_2025) containing joined attributes from both layers.

name: Retrieve buildings and BBR attributes
desc: The script retrieves building footprints within a user-defined polygon AOI from the Danish GeoDanmark60 WFS service (layer 'gdk60:Bygning'), then enriches each building with official BBR (Building and Dwelling Register) attributes — specifically construction year ('byg026Opførelsesår'), building use code ('byg021BygningensAnvendelse'), and total building area ('byg038SamletBygningsareal') — by querying the Datafordeler BBR REST API using the 'BBRUUID' field. It computes a derived 'Thermonet' classification ('Yes'/'No') based on BBRUUID presence, non-zero area, and residential building code (<200), applies categorized symbology (red for 'Yes', gray for 'No'), exports buildings to GeoJSON, and optionally retrieves, processes (dissolve → clip → split), and exports roads ('gdk60:Vejmidte') within the same AOI as simplified linestrings with black single-symbol rendering.

name: Assign hierarchical levels to pipe network
desc: The script constructs a hierarchical level structure for a thermonet (geothermal heat exchange) pipe network by identifying the root pipe closest to a source area polygon, building a topological graph of connected pipe segments (within 1 m), and performing a breadth-first traversal that assigns 'Level' values based on proximity and segment length — longest neighbor inherits same level, others increment — resulting in a GeoJSON output layer where dissolved pipe features are grouped and labeled by assigned level, with ellipsoidal length attributes recalculated and symbology applied.

name: Model waterway navigation transition probabilities
desc: The script models navigational flow on a directed canal network by computing: (1) an initial probability distribution over nodes based on proximity to pollution sources; (2) a transition matrix encoding directional movement probabilities derived from wind direction data and edge geometry (angle); (3) node-level 'getting stuck' probabilities combining dead-end topology, sharp corners, shore features (houseboats/vegetation), and water vegetation; and (4) beta coefficients representing the proportion of each waterway segment that can be blocked (i.e., catching probability = (canal_width − max_boat_width)/canal_width, capped at 0). Outputs include vector layers annotated with init_probability, transition_probability, catching_probability, stuck_probability, and impact_factor — all visualized in QGIS.

name: Model boat navigation probability
desc: The script models probabilistic navigation behavior of boats in a directed canal network in Delft, computing initial distribution (based on proximity to producers), transition probabilities (using wind direction data and edge angles), catching probabilities (based on canal width vs. boat width), and stuck probabilities (based on dead ends, sharp corners, shore types, and water vegetation). It outputs a GeoJSON layer of network nodes with attributes: init_probability, transition_probability (on edges), catching_probability, dead_ends, sharp_corners, shore_boats, shore_vegetation, water_vegetation, and stuck_probability.

name: Model boat movement probability
desc: The script models probabilistic boat movement across a directed canal network in Groningen, Netherlands. It computes initial distribution probabilities based on proximity to source points, transition probabilities along network edges using wind direction data and edge angles, catching probabilities based on canal width versus boat width, and stuck probabilities incorporating dead ends, sharp corners, shore types (e.g., houseboats, vegetation), and water vegetation. Outputs are written as attributes to a GeoJSON node layer: 'init_probability', 'transition_probability' (on edges), 'catching_probability', 'stuck_probability', and 'impact_factor'.

name: Compute road network slope
desc: The script computes slope values for road network edges by segmenting them into fixed-length segments, sampling elevation values from a digital elevation model (DEM), calculating slope as absolute rise over run (expressed in percent), and aggregating min/mean/max slope per original edge. It outputs segmented line layers with slope attributes, aggregated edge-level slope statistics, very steep segment subsets, and summary statistics in JSON format. The workflow uses QGIS processing algorithms (splitlinesbylength, extractspecificvertices, rastersampling), GeoPandas for aggregation, and config-driven visualization with custom slope ranges and colors.

name: Partition polygon into equal subregions
desc: The script partitions a given input polygon (identified by numeric ID) into N_DIV (e.g., 3) spatially contiguous, approximately equal-area sub-polygons using a Voronoi tessellation seeded by K-means clustered regular point samples. It first generates a regular grid of points within the polygon’s bounding box, clips them to the polygon boundary, clusters the interior points into N_DIV groups via K-means, computes the centroid (mean coordinate) of each cluster, constructs Voronoi polygons around those centroids, and finally clips the Voronoi polygons to the original polygon geometry — yielding N_DIV non-overlapping, topology-aware sub-polygons saved as GeoPackage files (e.g., 'polygon_1.gpkg').

name: Compute electric vehicle charging station coverage
desc: The script computes multi-distance service areas (500 m, 1000 m, 1500 m) around electric vehicle charging stations within a specified city boundary using road network data (roads_scooter), then aggregates road-length coverage per town/district to derive percentage-based coverage statistics. It loads monthly station CSV data (with lat/lon), reprojects to EPSG:3826, clips to city boundary, performs service area analysis via QGIS native 'serviceareafromlayer', dissolves results in batches for performance, and chains 'sumlinelengths' operations to compute cumulative covered road length per district. Outputs are written to a GeoPackage with four layers: towns_coverage (town polygons with reach percentages), sa_500/sa_1000/sa_1500 (dissolved service-area lines), and stations (clipped and reprojected points).

name: Clip polygon layers for CAD export
desc: The script performs vector-based spatial clipping of one polygon layer (e.g., parcels, land units) by another polygon layer (e.g., boundary, zone, or AOI), reprojects the clipped result to a user-specified CRS, exports it as a shapefile (.shp) and optionally as a DXF file, and attempts automated import into AutoCAD via MAPIMPORT — including optional layer assignment. It is a QGIS plugin dialog workflow for GIS-to-CAD interoperability targeting civil engineering, surveying, or planning workflows where clipped vector geometries must be transferred into CAD environments.

name: Generate CAD annotation script
desc: The script processes a vector layer of Hexatronics addresses to generate (1) a labeled GIS layer named 'CD_Details' with formatted AutoCAD-style paragraph-break text (using '\P' for line breaks), (2) a CSV file containing CD_Details text plus WGS84 longitude/latitude coordinates (computed via centroid and reprojection), and (3) an AutoCAD .scr script that places -MTEXT annotations at geometry insertion points (centroid for non-point geometries) with fixed width 150.0, using robust error handling for missing fields, empty values, CRS mismatches, and filesystem paths. The workflow includes geometry fixing, optional attribute filtering, optional reprojection, field refactoring with regex-based parsing of 'T_N' (e.g., extracting 'R123' as ROUTE# and trailing digits after '-' as DUCT#), labeling setup in QGIS, and deterministic .scr generation with UCS reset, layer creation, and zoom-to-extent.

name: Annotate FTTH conduit segments
desc: The script processes vector GIS layers representing fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) infrastructure—including DAPs (Distribution Access Points), TOBYs (Terminal On Box Y), handholes, distribution conduits, drop conduits, addresses, and house drops—to generate georeferenced annotation labels for CAD/GIS output. It reprojects layers to a common CRS, maps drop conduits to inherit RT-style prefixes (e.g., 'RT1') from distribution conduits connected at DAPs based on spatial proximity (50-ft snap tolerance), resolves 1-WAY/2-WAY conduit types case-insensitively from 'TYPE' fields, computes segment lengths in feet, splits conduits at DAP/TOBY/handhole locations using cross-lines, and outputs a CSV containing labeled point features: DAP labels (e.g., 'DIG 4\'X4\' PIT\PRT1-2-WAY\PSTA.'), TOBY labels (with inferred street addresses and GPS placement logic), and conduit segment labels (e.g., 'BORE & PLACE (87\')\PRT1-HEX-2-WAY'). All geometry is stabilized with no editing transactions—hence 'NO CRASH'—and includes robust field name case-insensitive lookup ('ELEMENTID', 'ELEMENT_ID', 'TYPE').

name: Split polygon into spatially balanced parts
desc: The script splits a user-provided input polygon feature into a specified number of spatially contiguous, approximately equal-area sub-polygons using a geometric clustering and partitioning workflow: (1) generates random points uniformly distributed inside the input polygon; (2) applies k-means clustering to group those points into the requested number of clusters; (3) computes a concave hull (k-nearest neighbor method) for each cluster to approximate its spatial extent; (4) computes centroids of those concave hulls; (5) generates Voronoi polygons around those centroids to define tessellated influence zones; and (6) intersects the Voronoi polygons with the original input polygon to produce the final set of non-overlapping, topologically valid, spatially balanced sub-polygons. The output is a vector feature class (polygon geometry) containing the splitted parts.

name: Extract NDVI polygons above threshold
desc: The script processes an input NDVI raster to isolate pixels with values > 0.5, saves the thresholded raster as a GeoTIFF, converts it to vector polygons via raster-to-vector polygonization (GDAL), and filters out polygons with 'value' = 0 — resulting in a shapefile containing only contiguous areas where NDVI exceeds 0.5, suitable for mapping high-vegetation-cover zones.

name: Quantify aspect-based segmentation metrics
desc: The script computes four landslide susceptibility-related spatial metrics—Aspect Uniformity (V), Spatial Autocorrelation of Aspect (I), Landslide Area Ratio (A), and Landslide Density (D)—for each input Slope Unit (SU) polygon layer. It derives aspect from a DEM, computes sin/cos rasters for vectorial aspect aggregation, performs zonal statistics to obtain summed sin/cos values per SU, calculates V as the weighted mean circular variance of aspect, constructs adjacency matrices using topological touching (via STRtree), computes I as a normalized spatial autocorrelation index of aspect deviation, aggregates landslide point counts and polygon overlaps to derive A (fraction of SU area overlapped by landslide polygons) and D (inverse of mean landslide point density per occupied SU), normalizes and fuses all metrics into a final Segmentation Metric (S = A × D × F, where F is a composite score of V and I). Outputs are CSV files: 'aspect_segmentation.csv' (V, I, F per SU) and 'segmentation_metric.csv' (A, D, F, S per SU).

name: Map dominant drought class by municipality
desc: The script processes a pre-existing drought monitoring vector layer ('dezembro25') for Paraíba state, Brazil, to resolve spatial overlaps among drought severity classes (s4–si) using topological difference operations—ensuring hierarchical exclusivity (most severe classes take precedence). It intersects the corrected drought polygons with municipal boundaries ('MunicipiosPB_WGS'), computes area per municipality–class combination, identifies the dominant (largest-area) drought class per municipality, and outputs (1) a categorized municipal map layer symbolized by drought severity, and (2) an Excel table listing each municipality, its dominant drought class code and name, and the corresponding area in m².

name: Identify landslide-prone contour areas
desc: The script processes contour polygons (e.g., topographic or landslide scarps) to identify and cluster geomorphologically unstable, velocity- and slope-informed segments. It first filters contours by area (>0.001 km²) and velocity (mean heatmap value >3.0), excludes/excludes areas overlapping mining concessions ('areecava'), then intersects remaining contours with slope units to compute proportional coverage per unit. Contours are split into portions ≥30% and <30% of their total area within a slope unit, joined and dissolved by composite ID (ID_contour-ID_SU), and cleaned of join artifacts. Final outputs include: (1) refined contour polygons ('contour_finali') with updated IDs and area metrics; (2) clustered AOIs ('AOI') derived from DBSCAN on contour vertices, representing spatially coherent instability zones; (3) clustered attribute table ('DATACLUSTER') containing median/min/max velocity (from 'heatmap2'), slope statistics, and binary intersection flags with hazard layers (frane_poly_opendata, PAI pericolosità, railways, roads, ISTAT localities). The workflow integrates zonal statistics, geometric intersection/difference, clustering, and overlay-based hazard exposure assessment.

name: Map land cover transitions
desc: The script processes vector layers named with '_FINAL' suffix (e.g., 'Leste_2019_FINAL', 'Oeste_2023_FINAL') representing classified land cover maps for different years and sectors (Leste/Oeste). It renames the 'DN' field to year-specific class fields (e.g., 'Class2019'), then performs sequential pairwise vector intersections across sorted years to compute spatiotemporal land cover transition histories (e.g., (5,5,4) = class 5 in 2019 → 5 in 2021 → 4 in 2023). Outputs are: (1) a shapefile containing all intersected polygons with class history attributes (for spatial audit), and (2) a CSV aggregating total area (ha) per unique class transition sequence — formatted as columns 'CLASSE_20xx', ..., 'area_ha' — intended for Sankey diagram generation in R.

name: Calculate CORINE land cover area by buffer zone
desc: The script computes the total area (in square meters) of each valid CORINE Land Cover (CLC) class (e.g., classes 1, 2, 3, 11, etc.) within user-defined 1km buffer zones. It does so by polygonizing the CORINE 2018 raster (100m resolution), intersecting the resulting land cover polygons with vector buffer zones (which must contain a 'Name' field), filtering for only valid CLC categories, calculating geometry areas, and aggregating results per buffer zone and land cover class. The final output is a CSV file listing 'Buffer', 'LandCover', and 'Area_m2' for each combination.

name: Summarize line length within polygons
desc: The script computes the total (and optionally count, mean, median) length of line features intersecting each polygon in a reference polygon layer, filters out polygons with insufficient total line length (based on user threshold), and outputs a polygon-based summary layer enriched with original polygon attributes. It performs intersection, geometric length calculation in projected CRS, aggregation by polygon ID, and attribute join—producing a vector layer where each feature represents a polygon with zonal line statistics and its original non-ID attributes.

name: Calculate area-weighted composite curve numbers
desc: The script calculates area-weighted composite curve numbers (CN) for hydrological modeling by intersecting subbasin, land use, and soils vector layers; it uses a user-provided CSV or Excel lookup table mapping land use codes and soil hydrologic groups (A/B/C/D) to CN values; performs reprojection to EPSG:3361; computes weighted CN per subbasin as Σ(CN_i × Area_i) / Σ(Area_i); outputs a shapefile with 'CN_Comp' and 'Area_acres' fields, plus detailed and summary CSV files containing per-polygon land use/soil/area/CN breakdowns.

name: Calculate area-weighted composite runoff coefficients
desc: The script calculates area-weighted composite runoff coefficients (C values) for catchments using the Rational Method by intersecting catchment, land use, and soils layers, then applying slope- and soil-group-specific C values from a user-provided lookup table. It performs reprojection to EPSG:3361, two sequential vector intersections (land use × soils, then result × catchments), computes weighted C values per catchment based on area and lookup-derived coefficients, and outputs a shapefile with 'C_Comp' and 'Area_acres' fields plus detailed and summary CSV files.

name: Filter CAR analysis areas and intersect with MapBiomas Alerta
desc: The script filters the CAR (Cadastro Ambiental Rural) dataset to retain only polygons where the attribute 'des_condic' contains the substring 'analise', then intersects those filtered polygons with the MapBiomas Alerta (MP) layer. It dissolves the resulting intersection by 'cod_imovel' (property ID), retains only that field, reprojects the geometry to EPSG:31982 (UTM Zone 22S, used in Brazil), calculates the area in hectares, and saves the final vector layer as a GeoPackage named 'results_pyqgis.gpkg'. The output is a dissolved, area-calculated, UTM-projected vector layer of rural properties in 'analysis' status overlapped with MapBiomas Alerta detections.

name: Extract outside area of polygon boundary
desc: The script performs vector-based spatial clipping to extract features from input layers that lie *outside* a user-defined polygon boundary layer. It first computes the intersection (inside portion) between each input layer and the polygon, then subtracts that intersection from the original input layer using a difference operation, resulting in a new shapefile containing only geometries exterior to the polygon. Outputs are ESRI Shapefiles saved to a local Windows directory with naming convention '_clipped_outside.shp'.

name: Extract land cover segmentation masks
desc: The script extracts georeferenced RGB imagery patches (PNG) and corresponding binary segmentation masks (PNG) for land cover classes from a WMS-served basemap, using LCDB (Land Cover Database) vector polygons as ground truth. It first spatially filters the LCDB layer by intersecting with a dissolved area mask derived from a raster index, dissolves by 'Class_2018', generates random sample points inside those dissolved polygons, buffers them into 112×112 m rectangles, intersects those buffers with the original filtered LCDB to extract class-specific geometry per sample, and renders both full-scene RGB patches (from WMS) and class-exclusive binary masks (black background, white foreground for each class present in the buffer) at fixed output resolution (bb_size/out_res). Outputs include: (1) classification images (clfRoot/*.png), (2) per-class segmentation masks (maskRoot/*_{class}_{id}.png), and (3) per-image class-count text files (clfRoot/*.txt) listing counts of each class observed in that bounding box.

name: Pivot IECH and smoke exposure indicators by NUTS3 unit
desc: The script transforms long-format CSV tables containing IECH (Environmental Health Index), smoke days, recurrence, population, and scenario data into wide-format CSVs keyed by NUTS3 administrative units (e.g., 'unit_id' or 'NUTS_ID'), then joins them spatially to a NUTS3 vector layer (EPSG:3763) to produce a geopackage ('nuts3_iech.gpkg') with all indicators as attributes per polygon, alongside a QGIS project file and metadata report.

name: Extract Portugal NUTS3 boundaries
desc: The script filters a GeoPackage containing NUTS3 administrative boundaries for the European Union to isolate only those features where CNTR_CODE='PT' (Portugal) and LEVL_CODE=3 (NUTS level 3), removes redundant unit_id_* columns if present, saves the result as a new GeoPackage (nuts3_iech_PT.gpkg), and creates a QGIS project (.qgz) configured in EPSG:3763 (Portuguese Transverse Mercator) with the filtered layer loaded. It also generates a JSON report with metadata including feature count, field count, timestamps, and I/O paths.

name: Integrate NUTS3 socioeconomic and health indicators
desc: The script loads and spatially joins five wide-format CSV tables (IECH, REC, SMOKE, POP, SCEN_mean) — containing socioeconomic, health behavior, demographic, and climate scenario variables — to a filtered and reprojected NUTS level-3 administrative boundary layer for Portugal (PT), producing a single GeoPackage vector layer (nuts3_iech.gpkg) where each NUTS3 feature carries all tabular attributes; it also generates a QGIS project file for visualization and a JSON report with metadata including feature count, CRS (EPSG:3763), and filter expression used.

name: Reproject point coordinates
desc: The script creates three hard-coded geographic points in WGS84 (EPSG:4326), reprojects them to the Portuguese national coordinate reference system EPSG:3763 (ETRS89 / Portugal TM06), and saves both the original and reprojected point layers into a GeoPackage file for debugging purposes. It does not perform geospatial analysis, modeling, or remote sensing — only coordinate transformation and I/O validation.

name: Prepare SUEWS urban typology database
desc: The script prepares input data for the SUEWS (Surface Urban Energy and Water Balance Scheme) model by generating site-specific parameter files from user-provided geospatial layers and a local Excel-based typology database. Key workflow steps include: (1) reading a regional/country-level typology database (database.xlsx) containing surface parameters (e.g., albedo, emissivity, u-values), profiles (traffic, population, energy use), and codes; (2) aggregating land cover fractions (LCF), building/vegetation morphology (IMP/IMPveg), and DSM/DEM rasters per polygon grid using zonal statistics and raster clipping; (3) computing roughness parameters (z0, zd) using Kent et al. (2017b) methodology combining building and vegetation frontal/plan area indices and height statistics; (4) optionally applying SPARTACUS vertical layering to generate GridLayout.nml files; (5) writing SUEWS-formatted text files (SUEWS_SiteSelect.txt, SUEWS_NonVeg.txt, SUEWS_Veg.txt, etc.) and nml files (InitialConditions.nml, GridLayout.nml). Outputs include a full SUEWS input directory with SiteSelect.txt, multiple SUEWS_*.txt files, GridLayout*.nml, InitialConditions*.nml, and supporting metadata files. The study area is not specified in the code — no explicit geographic coordinates, place names, or bounding boxes are embedded; inputs are fully user-defined via QGIS layer selection and database lookups.

name: Prepare SUEWS urban typology database
desc: The script prepares input data for the SUEWS (Surface Urban Energy and Water Balance Scheme) model by generating grid-specific configuration files. It reads user-selected polygon grids (e.g., urban zones or model domains), aggregates morphological (DSM/DEM-derived building/vegetation heights, roughness parameters z0/zd), land cover fractions (LCF), and typology-based surface properties from a local Excel database (database.xlsx). Key geospatial operations include raster clipping, zonal statistics (mean height, pixel count), wall detection from DSM–DEM differencing, Spartacus vertical layering (if enabled), and typology blending/aggregation. Outputs include: GridLayoutXXX.nml (for SPARTACUS-enabled runs or copied default), SUEWS_NonVeg.txt, SUEWS_Veg.txt, SUEWS_AnthropogenicEmission.txt, SUEWS_Water.txt, SUEWS_Conductance.txt, SUEWS_Snow.txt, SUEWS_Soil.txt, SUEWS_Irrigation.txt, SUEWS_SiteSelect.txt (containing lat/lon, fractions, roughness, population, traffic, etc.), InitialConditions.nml (leaf cycle– and soil moisture–adjusted), and supporting files (ESTMinput.nml, SUEWS_SPARTACUS.nml, etc.). The study area is not specified in the code; inputs are fully user-provided via QGIS interface (polygon layer, DSM, DEM, met file, database selections).

name: Calculate impervious fraction by catchment
desc: The script calculates the area-weighted fraction of impervious surface for each input catchment polygon, using zoning/land use polygons (e.g., 'LDR', 'NC', 'RU') and optional road corridors. It maps zone codes to predefined impervious percentages (e.g., 'NC': 90.0%, 'RU': 5.0%), assigns a default impervious percentage to unzoned or missing areas, optionally incorporates roads with a user-defined impervious percentage (default 50%), computes the weighted average imperviousness per catchment based on intersecting zone/road area proportions, and outputs a new vector layer of catchments with an added 'imp_percent' attribute representing the final fraction impervious (as a percentage value).

name: Generate Panchayat Property Map
desc: The script generates official Panchayat Property Maps (PPMs) for rural land administration in Andhra Pradesh, India. It processes user-provided plot (property parcel) and plinth (built-up) shapefiles to derive standardized cartographic outputs: (1) cleaned and CRS-validated Plot_Shapefile with 'Ref_Col' (property ID) field; (2) Plot_Boundary and Plot_ExplodeLines (with length attributes); (3) Builtup_Shapefile (intersection of plinth and plot layers) with calculated built-up area ('b_sqmts'); (4) Builtup_Boundary and Builtup_ExplodeLines; (5) Plot_Vertices; and (6) a QGIS print layout ('A4_PPM_TEMPLATE') configured with atlas-driven page generation per property parcel, rule-based symbology, custom labeling, and preloaded style files (e.g., Plot_Explode_Style.qml). All outputs are saved atomically to the project folder and loaded into the QGIS project with visibility toggling and layer styling applied.

name: Quantify boundary simplification effects
desc: The script evaluates geometric and topological changes induced by Douglas-Peucker simplification (using 'Distance' method) on a provincial administrative boundary polygon (R8 in the Philippines). For each tolerance value (0.5–2.5 km), it computes: (1) vertex count reduction, (2) 2D area (km²) and perimeter (km) of original vs. simplified geometries, (3) derived ratios (vertices/area, perimeter/area), and (4) spatial agreement (%) as the intersection-over-union (IoU) of original and simplified polygons — all exported to a CSV with per-tolerance metrics.

name: Select features by location and attribute
desc: The script performs spatial and attribute-based subsetting of large Oracle-hosted geospatial tables from the BC Government Warehouse (BCGW) to generate optimized QGIS vector layers. It uses Oracle Spatial SQL (SDO_RELATE, SDO_INSIDE, SDO_ANYINTERACT) to execute Select By Location operations (‘Completely Within’ and ‘Intersect’) and Select By Attribute queries directly against remote BCGW tables—avoiding full table loads. Outputs are in-memory QGIS vector layers (polygons, lines, points) with appropriate geometry type, SRID (3005), and field schemas, derived from BCGW views such as WHSE_CADASTRE.CBM_CADASTRAL_FABRIC_PUB_SVW, WHSE_ADMIN_BOUNDARIES.EBC_PROV_ELECTORAL_DIST_SVW, WHSE_BASEMAPPING.TRIM_TRANSPORTATION_LINES, and WHSE_BASEMAPPING.NTS_BC_WATER_LINES_125M. Additional QGIS-native geoprocessing (union, intersection, line splitting) is applied post-subset. The study area is explicitly British Columbia (BC), as evidenced by BCGW schema names, SRID 3005 (BC Albers Equal Area), and electoral district abbreviations (e.g., 'KLW' for Kelowna-West). No time range is used—the data are static administrative/cadastre/transportation/water layers. All operations are database-side filtering followed by QGIS client-side vector layer instantiation and optional overlay; no raster, satellite, or temporal analysis occurs.

name: Download SSURGO soils hydrologic groups
desc: The script downloads SSURGO (Soil Survey Geographic) soil spatial data (MapUnitPoly geometries) from USDA-NRCS WFS and tabular component attributes (including dominant component name, percentage, and hydrologic soil group — HSG A/B/C/D or combinations) from the Soil Data Access (SDA) REST API for a user-provided AOI. It merges spatial polygons with dominant-component HSG attributes, filters out non-dominant components, handles None/'None' HSG values (representing water/pits), and outputs: (1) a vector layer of clipped soil polygons enriched with mukey, musym, muname, compname, comppct_r, and hydgrp; and (2) an optional high-resolution PNG map visualizing polygons colored by HSG (with dedicated styling for Water/Pits) and overlaid with the AOI boundary.

name: Recalibrate hexagonal grid borders
desc: The script recalibrates split hexagonal grid cells by identifying and reassigning boundary hexes based on their spatial relationship to domain extents. It computes the bounding extent of each input hex layer (hex1–hex10), converts those extents to lines, extracts hexes intersecting those boundary lines (i.e., edge hexes), merges and dissolves all extracted edge hexes by GRID_ID to form a unified boundary polygon layer, then computes centroids of the dissolved boundaries. For each original hex layer, it (1) removes interior hexes (via difference with the dissolved boundary layer), and (2) selects boundary-aligned hexes by intersecting the dissolved boundary layer with centroids falling within that layer’s original extent — finally merging the retained boundary hexes with the differenced interior hexes to produce 10 corrected output layers (out1–out10), each representing a domain-specific recalibrated hexagonal grid where border hexes are consistently assigned to their correct domain based on centroid-in-extent logic and shared boundary alignment.

name: Generate AGOpenGPS section file
desc: The script converts QGIS vector layers (field boundary and weed polygons) into an AGOpenGPS-compatible Sections.txt file. It generates two nested grids (small and large quadrats) within the field boundary, computes the area without weeds via geometric difference, extracts grid cells fully inside the weed-free area, removes large-grid cells already covered by small-grid cells using set difference, merges remaining sections (large-grid patches, small-grid-only patches, and boundary-aligned patches), and exports them as a text file with local-meter coordinates relative to a StartFix origin (read from AGOpenGPS Fields.txt). Each section is written as a 5-line block: number of vertices (5), RGB color, then four 3D points (Easting,Northing,0) in clockwise order (0→3→1→2), derived from polygon vertices converted from WGS84 to local meters using latitude-dependent meter-per-degree scaling. The output Sections.txt is directly loadable into AGOpenGPS to display pre-applied sections.

name: Offset line features geometrically
desc: The script offsets selected line features in a QGIS vector layer by a user-specified distance (in meters) to the left, right, or both sides. It handles CRS unit validation (reprojecting to EPSG:3857 if non-metric), applies QGIS's native offset algorithm with configurable segments and join style, and appends the resulting offset line geometries as new features into the original editable layer. Outputs are modified vector layer features representing parallel offset lines.

name: Transform LADM-COL 1.2 geopackage layers
desc: The script performs an ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) workflow on a Colombian Land Administration Domain Model (LADM-COL 1.2) GeoPackage to validate and restructure spatial and attribute data. It extracts non-null T_Id features from 24 administrative, cadastral, and zoning layers (e.g., CC_Limite_Municipio, AV_ZHGU, lc_predio), renames and standardizes output table names (e.g., 'Zona_homo_geoeconomicaurbana'), and executes multi-step attribute joins: (1) links land parcels (lc_terreno) to basic administrative units (col_uebaunit) and then to predios (lc_predio) to populate lc_predio; (2) joins predio type codes via col_unidadadministrativabasicatipo; (3) propagates derecho (rights) relationships through baunit joins and resolves derecho tipo using iliCode; (4) processes construction units (lc_unidadconstruccion) by joining with lc_construccion, lc_caracteristicas, and lc_construccionplantatipo, then computes a derived 'planta_total' field by concatenating iliCode and planta_ubicacion; (5) joins address records (extdireccion) to predios. Outputs are written into a new GeoPackage with standardized, non-null, joined, and enriched tables adhering to LADM-COL 1.2 semantics and naming conventions.

name: Transform LADM-COL 1.0 geospatial data
desc: The script performs an ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) workflow to restructure, join, filter, and standardize raw GeoPackage layers conforming to the Colombian Land Administration Domain Model (LADM-COL) version 1.0. It maps inconsistently named input layers (e.g., 'seleccioneconstruccion (2)') to canonical LADM table names (e.g., 'lc_unidadconstruccion'), executes attribute joins using baunit/t_id keys to link spatial units (terreno, construccion, unidadconstruccion) with administrative and legal objects (predio, derecho, tipo_predio), filters non-null T_Id features, corrects geometries, reprojects all output layers to EPSG:9377 (MAGNA-SIRGAS / Colombia Bogota zone), updates spatial metadata in gpkg_geometry_columns, and applies SQL-based ilicode mapping for LC_Derecho types — producing a validated, CRS-consistent, schema-aligned GeoPackage ready for LADM-compliant land administration systems.

name: Validate cadastral unit geometry
desc: The script performs ETL validation and transformation of Colombian cadastral data from an input GeoPackage, extracting non-null features (by 'T_Id') from administrative and zoning layers (e.g., municipalities, corregimientos, urban perimeters, homogeneous zones), then joins land parcel ('lc_terreno'), predio ('ilc_predio'), derecho ('ilc_derecho'), unidad de construcción ('lc_unidad'), and associated type tables using foreign key relationships (e.g., 'baunit', 'ue_cr_terreno', 'cr_caracteristicasunidadconstruccion'). It constructs validated output layers including 'CC_Limite_Municipio', 'Zona_homo_geoeconomicaurbana', 'lc_predio', 'Lc_Tipo_predio', 'lc_derecho_tipo', 'Extdireccion', and 'lc_unidadconstruccion' — the latter enriched with a calculated 'piso_total' field concatenating 'iliCode_2' and 'planta_ubicacion'. All outputs are written to a new GeoPackage with standardized table names and geometry-preserving joins.

name: Fetch SRTM elevation data
desc: The script downloads SRTMGL1 (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission Global 1 arc-second) digital elevation model (DEM) files from NASA's USGS Earthdata archive, merges multiple HGT tiles covering the user-defined geographic extent, clips the resulting raster to the input extent, and converts it into a point vector layer with elevation values (‘alti’) in the target Cartesian CRS. Outputs include both a clipped DEM raster and an elevation point vector layer.

name: Calculate road traffic emission
desc: The script computes road-level traffic-related emission values (e.g., noise or pollutant emission proxies) by joining precomputed emission/level values (LW_ROADS) — generated externally via a Groovy-based NoiseModelling workflow — to an input road vector layer.
