desc: The script generates a riparian buffer zone (suojakaista) along waterbodies for forest management in Finland. It takes an input polygon layer ('Leimikko', i.e., forest stand parcels), queries background rasters via an internal interface (named 'suojakaista_taustarasterit', 'RUSLE', 'WB_Finland', 'DEM'), computes the waterline boundary from those rasters, and constructs a variable-width buffer zone using minimum (5–20 m) and mean (5–50 m) distance parameters. The output is a vector polygon layer ('Suojakaista-alue') representing the proposed buffer zone, styled with a QGIS QML file ('suojakaista_style1.qml'). The workflow includes: (1) dissolving input features; (2) per-feature raster data retrieval via `feature2layer` and `getWater`; (3) waterline extraction via `getWaterline`; (4) buffer generation via `getBufferzone`. All operations are executed within QGIS Processing Framework, not GEE — despite the prompt referencing 'GEE script', this is a QGIS Python plugin with no Google Earth Engine code. Data sources are internal/proprietary Finnish geospatial services (e.g., 'WB_Finland' likely refers to national water body dataset; 'RUSLE' is the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation raster; 'DEM' is a digital elevation model); satellite/sensor/band details are not exposed in the code and are handled opaque by backend interfaces. Study area is explicitly Finland (via 'Suomen metsäkeskus' — Finnish Forest Centre, email domain 'metsakeskus.fi', and 'WB_Finland').

name: Generate riparian buffer zone
desc: The script generates a riparian buffer zone (suojakaista) along waterbodies using a combination of background raster datasets accessed via an interface. It takes an input polygon layer ('Leimikko', i.e., forest stand parcels), dissolves it, retrieves rasters named 'suojakaista_taustarasterit', 'RUSLE', 'WB_Finland', and 'DEM' for each feature, computes the waterline boundary from those rasters, and applies a custom buffer algorithm ('getBufferzone') that incorporates minimum and mean width constraints and optionally a cost-based retention percentage threshold. The output is a vector polygon layer ('Suojakaista-alue') representing the proposed buffer zone, styled with a QGIS .qml file. The study area is explicitly Finland (via 'Suomen metsäkeskus', 'WB_Finland', and 'RUSLE' — a Finnish RUSLE implementation), and the workflow relies on external modules ('getWater', 'getWaterline', 'getBufferzone') not shown in this script but implied to perform hydrological and cost-distance analysis. No satellite imagery or time-series processing is present; all data sources are static, national-scale Finnish raster datasets. Final output is a vector feature sink.

name: Extract river network from DEM
desc: The script extracts a vector river network from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) by performing hydrological preprocessing (depression breaching and sink filling), computing D8 flow direction and accumulation, thresholding flow accumulation to delineate channels, building reach-level topology (FromN/ToN nodes), and populating a line vector layer with 22 mandatory D-CASCADE attributes—including reach_id, Slope, Length, elevations at upstream/downstream nodes (el_FN/el_TN), contributing area (Ad), and initialized sediment transport parameters (Wac, Q, n, D16/D50/D84, etc.). Output is a shapefile-compatible line vector layer ready for input into the D-CASCADE sediment transport model.

name: Generate vector-based tile boundaries
desc: The script processes input GeoJSON vector layers representing administrative or thematic boundaries (e.g., land parcels, murabba units), computes group keys based on attribute logic (e.g., 'M', 'MN', 'B', 'Type' fields), dissolves and cleans nested/contained geometries, and exports XYZ tile directories (PNG tiles) covering zoom levels 10–20 for web mapping. Outputs include cleaned outline layers with group-key labeling, styled QGIS layers, and raster tile directories with blank-tile cleanup.

name: Generate terrain elevation and slope visualization
desc: The script loads and styles three local raster datasets—elevation (DEM), slope, and hillshade—derived from terrain analysis, and optionally generates and styles contour lines from the DEM. It constructs a layered QGIS map stack with pseudo-color elevation rendering using a custom blue-to-red divergent ramp (0–100 m range stretched via sigma=2.2), grayscale hillshade (opacity=0.35), and pseudo-color slope (0–45° range, green-to-blue ramp). Contours are generated via GDAL’s contour algorithm at user-defined intervals (default 5.0 m), labeled every 10 m, and styled with graduated line symbology using Viridis/Spectral/Turbo color ramps. The study area is implicitly defined by the input rasters located in 'context_30km' — indicating a 30 km buffer zone — and the KML loading logic points to 'Higuerones', a known locality in Puerto Rico. Outputs include styled raster/vector layers added to a QGIS layer group named 'Terrain stack', plus optional KML overlays loaded into a top-level group named 'Higuerones KML'. No satellite or remote sensing data is used: all inputs are precomputed local GeoTIFFs (terrain_elevation.tif, terrain_slope.tif, terrain_hillshade.tif).

name: Compute parcel-level flood water fraction
desc: The script computes monthly water/overflow fraction per agricultural parcel using pre-generated binary raster masks (water_mask_YYYY-MM-DD.tif or overflow_mask_YYYY-MM-DD.tif) derived from Sentinel-1 (S1) SAR data at 10 m resolution. It performs zonal statistics (mean, sum, count) over polygon parcels to extract wet_fraction (proportion of water-covered pixels), wet_pixels (count of water pixels), and valid_pixels (total non-NoData pixels) for each month in the specified range. Inputs are local GeoTIFF rasters stored in a structured directory (e.g., 'masks/' or 'overflow/'), not GEE assets; the script runs entirely in QGIS using QgsZonalStatistics. The outputs are two CSV files: long-format (one row per parcel-month) and wide-format (one row per parcel, columns per month’s wet_fraction), plus a log file. No GEE code is present — this is a QGIS Python script that consumes locally generated S1-derived flood masks.

name: Cluster building polygons by comp_id
desc: The script groups individual building footprint polygons (from a vector layer named 'singlepart_polys') by the attribute 'comp_id', dissolves geometries per group into MultiPolygons, filters out groups with fewer than MIN_COUNT (1) constituent polygons, appends a 'num_features' count field, applies random categorical symbology per comp_id, and exports the result as a styled GeoPackage layer ('Clustered_Groups.gpkg') embedded with renderer metadata. The output is a clustered, attribute-filtered, and visually categorized vector layer of building group envelopes.

name: Detect polygon layer overlaps
desc: The script detects geometric overlaps (intersection polygons) between vector polygon layers in QGIS using Earth Engine-like spatial logic implemented locally. It supports two modes: (1) self-overlaps (self-intersections) within a single polygon layer, and (2) cross-layer overlaps between two distinct polygon layers. Input layers are sourced from the current QGIS project; no remote GEE assets or satellite imagery are accessed. The workflow includes spatial indexing (QgsSpatialIndex) for efficient candidate search, geometry intersection computation (QgsGeometry.intersection), area filtering (minimum area in m² or ha), optional inclusion of source feature attributes, and output as a new memory vector layer with red semi-transparent fill symbology. Outputs include a polygon layer of overlap geometries, attribute table with IDs, layer names, feature IDs, and areas (m² and ha), plus summary statistics (count and total overlap area). No time-series, raster data, or external geospatial APIs are involved — it is purely vector-based topological analysis within QGIS.

name: Export infrastructure layers to map package
desc: The script prepares QGIS vector layers for export into a standardized map package format. It selects visible vector layers (points, lines, polygons) from the current QGIS project, optionally filters by selection, applies geometry simplification (1.5 m tolerance), exports them as ESRI Shapefiles and WGS84 GeoJSON files, enriches GeoJSON with symbology properties (fill color, stroke color, stroke width, opacity), stores symbology metadata in an SQLite database (Symbologie.db), generates a configuration JSON file containing site metadata (entrepreneur, chantier name, WFS info, date, geometry counts), and packages all artifacts (shapefiles, GeoJSONs, SQLite, JSON) into a ZIP archive. The script interfaces with a custom .NET DLL (Recup_data.dll) for license management and FTP upload, and uses SQLite databases (ms_machine-tracking-point.Sqlite, User.conf) to manage client/chantier metadata. No remote sensing or Earth observation data is loaded, processed, or analyzed — all inputs are local QGIS vector layers and configuration databases.

name: Fill polygon holes
desc: The script processes vector polygon layers in QGIS to remove interior rings (holes) based on area thresholds. It counts holes per polygon, optionally filters holes by maximum area (in hectares, square meters, or square kilometers), and either modifies the source layer in-place or creates a new memory layer without the selected holes. The tool uses QGIS native processing (via `native:deleteholes` logic implemented manually) and provides preview statistics and progress feedback. No remote sensing data, satellite imagery, or temporal analysis is involved — it operates purely on local vector geometry. Study area, time range, satellite/sensor/bands, and external geospatial data sources are not specified.

name: Generate forest sampling grid
desc: The script generates a systematic, randomly offset sampling grid (point layer) for forest inventory planning according to Quebec's MRNF (Ministère des Ressources naturelles et de la Faune) standards. It takes a user-selected QGIS vector layer of polygon features (e.g., forest stands or management units) as input, computes the total territory area (in hectares), calculates the required number of plots using the MRNF formula n = (t² × CV²) / E² (where t is Student’s t-value, CV is coefficient of variation, and E is maximum tolerated error), derives inter-plot spacing as √(territory_area_in_m² / n), and then places points on a regular grid with random origin within the first cell. Points are filtered to retain only those falling inside the union of input polygons. Outputs include: (1) a shapefile of plot points with MRNF-compliant attributes (NO_VIREE, NO_PLACET, RAYON_M, SURFACE_M2, X, Y); (2) optional report (.txt) summarizing parameters, calculations, and metadata; and (3) optional automatic addition of the point layer to the QGIS map canvas with red circular symbology. The script operates entirely within QGIS desktop using PyQGIS — no Earth Engine server-side computation, no satellite imagery, no time-series analysis, and no remote sensing data ingestion.

name: Reproject vector layers
desc: The script reprojects selected QGIS vector layers from their source coordinate reference system (CRS) to a user-specified target CRS. It supports batch processing of multiple layers, optional selection-based feature filtering, and output to Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, or in-memory layer formats. The workflow includes CRS validation, coordinate transformation using QgsCoordinateTransform, geometry reprojection per feature, field preservation, and optional automatic addition of outputs to the QGIS project. Outputs include newly created vector layers with updated geometries and CRS, along with success/warning summaries.

name: Compute shortest path along road network
desc: The script computes the shortest geometric path between the start and end vertices of a selected road segment (identified by gid = 1 in the 'route_client' layer) using QGIS's network analysis capabilities. It first extracts the first and last vertices of the input line feature, adds their x/y coordinates to attribute table, then uses QgsVectorLayerDirector and Dijkstra’s algorithm on the original line layer (treated as a graph) to compute the least-cost path (by Euclidean distance). The output is a memory-based LineString vector layer representing the shortest traversable route along the network, added to the QGIS project.

name: Assess wetland vulnerability index
desc: The script computes a normalized Wetland Vulnerability Index (WVI) by integrating three domain layers — Exposure (Land Cover, NDBI, Population), Sensitivity (Degradation, Ecosystem), and Resilience (NDVI, MNDWI) — using weighted linear combination. It first calculates domain-specific rasters (Exposure, Sensitivity, Resilience) via GDAL raster calculator with user-defined weights, then combines them into a raw vulnerability score using domain-level weights (Exposure, Sensitivity, Resilience), and finally normalizes the result to [0,1] range using min-max scaling. Outputs include four rasters: Exposure, Sensitivity, Resilience, and the final normalized Wetland Vulnerability Index (WVI), optionally styled with QGIS layer styles.

name: Compute wetland vulnerability index
desc: The script computes a Wetland Vulnerability Index (WVI) by combining three user-provided raster inputs — Exposure, Resilience, and Sensitivity — using domain-specific weights (default: 0.40, 0.20, 0.40 respectively) in a weighted linear combination: WVI = (Exposure × wₑ) + (Sensitivity × wₛ) + (Resilience × wᵣ). It then normalizes the resulting index to the [0,1] range using min-max scaling (i.e., (value − min) / (max − min)) and applies a QGIS layer style. The final output is a single-band normalized raster representing spatially explicit wetland vulnerability scores.

name: Validate traffic signal point positions
desc: The script validates the positional accuracy of traffic signal points collected via QField by buffering road centerlines (5 meters), selecting only those points that fall within the buffered road polygons, and then assigning municipality names from administrative boundaries to each validated point. Outputs include a validated point shapefile, a CSV export with geometry as XYZ coordinates, and intermediate layers for visualization and quality control.

name: Estimate demand catchment by travel time
desc: The script computes isochrones (travel-time polygons) around candidate retail shop locations using the ORS Tools plugin in QGIS, then spatially joins these isochrones with census-based demand points (LSOA-level population data) to determine which population falls within each travel-time threshold (1–30 minutes) for each shop. It aggregates total population per shop-time combination (e.g., 'shop_5_10' = shop ID 5, 10-min isochrone) and outputs a CSV table listing each unique shop-time-id pair with its associated total demand (population), enabling spatial accessibility analysis and retail catchment modeling.

name: Compute agricultural suitability statistics by county
desc: The script computes the mean agricultural suitability value (from a raster dataset 'suit/hdr.adf') for each U.S. county (from 'USA_adm2.shp'). It first reprojects the suitability raster to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), then cleans the county vector layer by dropping non-essential administrative fields, adds a unique integer ID field ('cid'), and runs zonal statistics (mean) to summarize suitability per county. The final output is a CSV file ('counties_agrisuit.csv') containing all original county attributes plus the computed mean suitability value (stored in a field prefixed with '_' — e.g., '_mean'). Study area is the United States (implied by 'USA_adm2.shp'); no time dimension is present; data sources are local raster and vector files (no satellite imagery or temporal filtering).

name: Compute agricultural suitability zonal statistics
desc: The script computes mean agricultural suitability values (from the 'suit' raster dataset) for US counties. It reprojects the 'suit' raster from its native projection to EPSG:4326, processes a US county boundary shapefile (USA_adm2.shp) by dropping non-essential attribute fields and adding a unique autoincremental 'cid' field, then performs zonal statistics (mean only) to summarize the suitability raster values per county polygon. The outputs are (1) a reprojected 'agrisuit' raster in EPSG:4326, and (2) a vector layer 'counties' with added 'cid' and '_mean' attributes containing the zonal mean suitability score per county. Study area is the United States; data sources are a local raster 'hdr.adf' (likely from the Global Agro-Ecological Zones or GAEZ suitability model) and the GADM USA level-2 administrative boundaries. No time dimension is present; no satellite, sensor, or spectral bands are involved — this is a static, non-remote-sensing, biophysical suitability raster analysis.

name: Calculate country area in square kilometers
desc: The script computes the area (in km²) of each country polygon from the Natural Earth 10m Admin 0 Countries dataset. It drops all fields except 'ADMIN' and 'ISO_A3', reprojects the vector layer from WGS 84 to World Cylindrical Equal Area (ESRI:54034), fixes invalid geometries, then adds a new field 'km2area' using the field calculator with the expression 'area($geometry)/1000000'. The final output is a CSV file containing only the 'ADMIN', 'ISO_A3', and 'km2area' fields, written to 'C:/Users/se.4537/Dropbox/PoliteconGIS/LBS_2020/PhD/lecture_2/gis_data/_output/country_areas.csv'. The study area is global (all countries), no time dimension is involved, and no satellite, sensor, or band data is used — only static administrative boundary vector data.

name: Calculate country area in square kilometers
desc: The script computes the area (in km²) of administrative country polygons from the Natural Earth 'ne_10m_admin_0_countries' dataset. It first drops redundant attribute fields, reprojects the vector layer to an equal-area projection (ESRI:54034), fixes invalid geometries, calculates a new field 'km2area' using the planar area of each geometry divided by 1,000,000 (to convert m² → km²), and finally reprojects the result back to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for output as a vector layer with the computed area attribute.

name: Clean language boundary geometry
desc: The script cleans a vector layer of language boundaries (langa.shp) by fixing invalid geometries, adding a unique auto-incrementing GID field, copying the 'NAME_PROP' attribute into a new shorter-named field 'lnm', and dropping all other attributes except 'GID', 'ID', and 'lnm'. The final output is a simplified shapefile (wlds_cleaned.shp) containing only those three fields and topologically valid geometries.

name: Compute country-level population density statistics
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean values) of four raster datasets — land quality, 1500 AD population density, 1990 AD population density, and 2000 AD population density — over country boundaries (admin-0 level) from Natural Earth. It fixes geometries and retains only 'ADMIN' and 'ISO_A3' attributes before running zonal statistics. The output is a CSV file ('country_level_zs.csv') containing country names (ADMIN), ISO-A3 codes, and mean values for each raster prefixed as 'lqua_', 'pd15_', 'pd19_', and 'pd20_'. Study area is global (countries shapefile), time range is explicitly 1500 AD, 1990 AD, and 2000 AD for population layers; land quality has no temporal annotation. Data sources include HYDE population rasters (1500, 1990, 2000 AD), a custom land quality raster, and Natural Earth admin-0 countries — all non-satellite, GIS-derived raster/vector products. No satellite, sensor, or spectral band processing occurs.

name: Calculate country area in square kilometers
desc: The script computes the area (in km²) of each country polygon from the Natural Earth 10m Admin 0 Countries vector dataset. It drops all fields except 'ne_10m_adm', 'ADMIN', and 'ISO_A3'; reprojects the layer to World Cylindrical Equal Area (ESRI:54034) for accurate area calculation; fixes invalid geometries; then adds a new field 'km2area' using the expression 'area($geometry)/1000000' and exports the result to a CSV file at 'C:/Users/se.4537/Dropbox/PoliteconGIS/LBS_2020/PhD/lecture_3/gis_data/_output/country_areas.csv'. The study area is global (all countries), no time dimension is involved, and no satellite, sensor, or band data is used — it is a pure vector-based geoprocessing workflow on static administrative boundaries.

name: Generate grid-cell country intersection polygons
desc: The script generates a global 2.5°×2.5° regular grid in WGS84, intersects it with Natural Earth Admin-0 country boundaries, dissolves resulting fragments by grid cell ID, cleans topological errors using GRASS v.clean (snap tool), fixes geometries, and outputs a cleaned, attribute-minimized vector layer (vcountries.shp) where each feature is a single polygon per grid cell representing the union of all country overlaps within that cell — effectively producing a grid-aligned, country-masked, topology-corrected spatial partition for spatial aggregation or zonal analysis.

name: Extract language-free virtual country areas
desc: The script processes vector layers to isolate portions of 'virtual countries' (vcountries) that do not intersect with language distribution polygons (TEMP_wlds), using GRASS v.overlay with 'not' operator (operator=2), followed by geometry fixing, dissolving by cell-id (a_cid), field renaming to 'cid', and attribute cleanup. It separately processes the intersected portions (TEMP_int) to produce a harmonized version retaining only the 'cid' field. Outputs are two cleaned shapefiles: TEMP_nolangs (areas of virtual countries with no language coverage) and TEMP_withlangs (areas of virtual countries overlapping languages), both topologically cleaned and attribute-minimal.

name: Calculate virtual country land and water area
desc: The script computes the total land area (km²) for each virtual country (defined by polygon features with attribute 'a_cid') and the intersecting water area (km²) from global lake polygons (Natural Earth 10m lakes). It performs geometry cleaning, reprojection to World Cylindrical Equal Area (ESRI:54034), area calculation via field calculator, intersection between virtual countries and lakes, dissolution by country ID, and outputs two CSV files: 'vcareas.csv' (country total areas) and 'vcwaterareas.csv' (country-specific water-covered areas).

name: Compute centroid-to-coast distance
desc: The script computes the Euclidean distance from the geographic centroids of virtual countries (vcountries) — each associated with language data — to the nearest point on the Natural Earth 10m coastline. It outputs a CSV file containing, for each vcountry centroid, its ID (cid), latitude and longitude coordinates (cent_lat, cent_lon), and the latitude and longitude of the nearest coastal point (coast_lat, coast_lon). The workflow involves geometry fixing, centroid generation, coordinate export, GRASS v.distance-based proximity analysis, vertex extraction to isolate coastal endpoints, field renaming and cleanup, and final attribute consolidation into a tabular CSV.

name: Compute population density zonal statistics
desc: The script computes mean zonal statistics (mean values) of population density rasters (1500 AD, 1990 AD, 2000 AD) for two vector layers: 'virtual countries' (vcountries.shp) and 'virtual countries without languages' (vcnolangs.shp). It applies geometry fixing to both shapefiles, then runs QGIS zonal statistics (statistic ID 2 = mean) for each population raster, appending prefixed columns (e.g., 'pd15_', 'pd19_', 'pd20_') to the attribute tables. Finally, it exports the updated vector attribute tables — now containing mean population density per polygon — as CSV files (vc_level_zs.csv and vcnl_level_zs.csv). The workflow intentionally skips large climate/elevation rasters and focuses only on the three HYDE population density datasets.

name: Generate grid-cell country intersection polygons
desc: The script generates a global 0.5°×0.5° regular grid (WGS84), intersects it with cleaned administrative boundaries of countries (from Natural Earth 10m), dissolves resulting fragments by grid cell ID, cleans topological errors, and outputs a shapefile (dyadcells.shp) containing one polygon per grid cell that overlaps land territory — each assigned a unique integer 'cid' — effectively producing a vector-based, land-masked, globally consistent spatial discretization for dyadic or cell-level analysis.

name: Join language data to dyad cells
desc: The script spatially joins language boundary polygons (from TEMP_wlds.shp) to dyadic administrative cell polygons (dyadcells.shp) using a containment predicate (‘within’ or ‘intersects’, default predicate 0), retains only the 'cid' (cell identifier) and 'GID' (language identifier) fields in the output CSV, and writes the result to langs_in_dyadcells.csv. It first repairs invalid geometries in both input layers to ensure robust topological operations, then performs the spatial join, and finally drops all non-essential attribute fields to produce a minimal many-to-many mapping table linking dyad cells to languages present within them.

name: Calculate virtual country water area
desc: The script computes the area of water bodies (lakes) intersecting with pre-defined virtual country cells (dyadcells.shp) and outputs two CSV files: (1) 'dyadareas.csv' containing the total area (km²) of each virtual country cell projected to World Cylindrical Equal Area (ESRI:54034), and (2) 'dyadwaterareas.csv' containing the summed water-covered area (km²) per virtual country cell ID ('cid'). Input data includes Natural Earth 10m lakes (vector, global coverage), and dyad cells — a custom gridded partitioning of the world surface into equal-area cells ('dyadcells.shp'), likely derived from a dyadic geopolitical unit scheme. The workflow involves geometry fixing, reprojection, GRASS v.clean and v.overlay for robust vector intersection, dissolve by cell ID, field calculation of areas in km², and field cleanup. No time dimension is involved; all operations are static spatial overlays. Study area is global (inferred from use of Natural Earth global lakes and 'world cylindrical equal area' CRS).

name: Calculate centroid-to-coast distance
desc: The script computes the shortest Euclidean distance from the centroids of dyadic administrative units (‘dyadcells’) to the nearest point on the Natural Earth 10m coastline. It outputs: (1) a shapefile of dyad centroids with coordinates (dyadcentroids.shp), (2) a line vector layer representing the shortest distance from each centroid to the coast (distance.shp), (3) a joined attribute table linking each dyad centroid to its nearest coastal point, and (4) a CSV file (dyadcentroids_closest_coast.csv) containing for each dyad: its ID (cid), centroid latitude/longitude (cent_lat, cent_lon), and the latitude/longitude of the nearest coastal point (coast_lat, coast_lon). The workflow uses QGIS Processing algorithms including geometry fixing, centroid generation, GRASS v.distance for nearest-point line creation, vertex extraction, attribute joining, and field calculations — all operating on vector inputs only. No remote sensing imagery, time-series, or raster analysis is involved. Study area is implied by input paths and filenames but not geographically bounded in code; data sources are local vector files: Natural Earth 10m coastline and user-provided ‘dyadcells.shp’. No satellite, sensor, or band information is present.

name: Extract population density values at dyad centroids
desc: The script extracts raster-based population density values (from HYDE 1500 AD, 1990 AD, and 2000 AD datasets) at point locations representing geopolitical dyads (centroids of country-pair units), producing separate CSV files (dyads_evtp_pd15.csv, dyads_evtp_pd19.csv, dyads_evtp_pd20.csv) containing the original dyad attributes plus the extracted raster values; it also drops auxiliary coordinate fields (xcoord, ycoord) from the input centroid layer before extraction.

name: Intersect rivers with watersheds
desc: The script performs a vector intersection between a river layer and a watershed (basin) layer loaded from QGIS project layers. It first identifies the watershed and river layers by keyword matching in layer names (e.g., 'cuencas', 'ríos', 'basins', 'rivers'), then validates and repairs invalid geometries in the watershed layer via simplification and tiny buffer (0.000001), followed by a QGIS-native 'qgis:intersection' operation. The output is a memory-based vector layer containing only river segments that intersect the corrected watershed polygons, added to the QGIS project as a temporary layer. No raster or time-series processing occurs; all operations are vector-based and spatially explicit within the loaded layers.

name: Generate Tanaka contours from DEM
desc: The script generates Tanaka-style illuminated contour lines from a digital elevation model (DEM) raster input in QGIS. It first extracts elevation contours at a user-defined interval, optionally filters short segments by length and smooths geometry using iterative angular constraints, then explodes multilines into single-segment features, computes azimuth for each segment, assigns a unique FID, and applies Tanaka shading logic: stroke color varies with HSL lightness based on the absolute angular deviation of contour orientation from the dominant illumination direction (45°), and stroke width scales with the deviation from perpendicularity to illumination — producing visually enhanced, 3D-like terrain representation. Outputs include a styled vector layer added to the QGIS project and exported as GeoPackage or Shapefile.

name: Model dam breach hydrographs
desc: The script models dam breach hydrographs for both water and tailings dams. It computes breach parameters (peak discharge, time to peak, average breach width, hydrograph length) using empirical methods (Froehlich 1995/2008, MMC, ANA-LNEC), generates time-series hydrographs (TR66, parabolic, triangular), estimates sediment-laden tailings hydrographs using predefined scenario curves (TAILINGS_HYDROGRAPHS, TAILINGS_SEDIMENT_CV), calculates breach volumes (Vrmin/Vrave/Vrmax, Larrauri, Rico, Piciullo), and exports/import XML configuration files for FLO-2D. Outputs include interactive matplotlib plots, GeoPackage-injected time series data for inflow boundaries, computational domain grids (via square_grid), and raster-sampled elevation/roughness layers.

name: Rasterize polygon vector layers
desc: The script rasterizes polygon vector layers (GeoPackage files) into GeoTIFF rasters using GDAL's rasterize algorithm. It processes only polygon geometries, filters by minimum area (>100 km²), applies a 1000-meter buffer around each layer's extent, and outputs rasters at 50-meter resolution with pixel value 1 for burned features and 0 for nodata. Input vectors are read from a local folder path under the user's Documents directory; output filenames are derived by replacing '.gpkg' with '.tif'.

name: Rasterize polygon vector layers
desc: The script rasterizes GeoPackage (.gpkg) polygon vector files into aligned TIFF rasters using GDAL's rasterize algorithm. For each polygon layer, it computes a buffered bounding box extent based on the first feature's geometry area and bounding box dimensions, calculates a resolution (in pixels) as the rounded square root of the buffered extent's area divided by 1e6, and writes a binary raster (burn value = 1) with matching width/height/resolution. Output rasters are named by replacing '.gpkg' with '.tif'. Only polygon geometries are processed; non-polygon layers use the unbuffered bounding box.

name: Interpolate digital elevation model
desc: The script performs iterative cubic spline interpolation on a point layer (probkowanie.gpkg) containing elevation samples (field 'SAMPLE_1') to generate nsteps=20 realizations of a DEM raster surface. Each realization is produced by first randomly subsampling the input points (80 points per iteration), then applying SAGA's 'interpolatecubicspline' with fixed parameters (K=140, cell size=100 m, extent matching the original layer). Finally, it computes ensemble statistics — mean and standard deviation — across all 20 interpolated rasters, producing two final output rasters: a mean DEM and its spatial standard deviation (uncertainty surface).

name: Compute aspect and slope from elevation raster
desc: The script processes raster inputs to compute terrain derivatives: Aspect (using QGIS aspect algorithm) or Slope (using GDAL slope algorithm with percent units). For vector inputs, it rasterizes the geometry using GDAL rasterize (with burn value 1, resolution 10×10, extent matching mask_layer) and then computes Euclidean distance (proximity) to rasterized features up to 20,000 georeferenced units. Outputs are temporary raster layers returned as file paths or layer references.

name: Reclassify suitability raster
desc: The script reclassifies a continuous input suitability raster into discrete suitability classes (e.g., low/medium/high) based on user-defined value ranges (MANUAL method) or equal-interval binning (not yet implemented), then clips the reclassified raster to a vector mask layer. It outputs a clipped, reclassified raster with LZW-compressed GeoTIFF encoding, intended for suitability mapping applications such as habitat, agriculture, or land-use planning.

name: Clip vector layer to hemisphere
desc: The script clips an input vector layer to the visible hemisphere centered at a user-specified latitude/longitude using orthographic projection. It constructs a hemispheric clipping polygon by generating points on a circle of radius ~6371 km in orthographic space, transforming them back to the source CRS, handling edge cases (equatorial/antimeridian/polar centers), closing polygons across the antimeridian when needed, and performing a vector intersection. The output is a vector layer containing only geometries intersecting the hemisphere.

name: Convert ST_B10 to land surface temperature
desc: The script applies radiometric calibration formulas to Landsat Collection 2 Surface Reflectance (SR) and Surface Temperature (ST) bands stored as local GeoTIFFs. It processes files matching patterns SR_B1.TIF through SR_B7.TIF using formula_sr (linear scaling: (0.0000275*A)-0.2), ST_B10.TIF using formula_st ((0.00341802*A)+149) to convert digital numbers to land surface temperature (LST) in Kelvin, and ST_EMIS.TIF using formula_emis (A*0.0001) to scale emissivity. Each input file is replaced in-place with a rescaled output file prefixed 'SC_' (e.g., SC_ST_B10.TIF), confirming radiometric correction of LST and emissivity products for Barranquilla.

name: Convert Band 8 radiance to reflectance
desc: The script processes Landsat Level 1 TIF files (specifically 'T1_B8.TIF') using metadata from associated MTL.json files to convert top-of-atmosphere (TOA) radiance to TOA reflectance. It reads radiometric rescaling coefficients (REFLECTANCE_MULT_BAND_8, REFLECTANCE_ADD_BAND_8), sun elevation, and Earth–Sun distance; computes sin(sun_elevation); and applies a GDAL raster calculator formula: (reflectance_mult * A + reflectance_add) / sin(sun_elevation). The output is a new GeoTIFF file prefixed with 'SC_' (e.g., 'SC_LC08_L1TP_..._T1_B8.TIF'), and the original B8 TIF is deleted after processing. No cloud masking, atmospheric correction, or classification is performed — only radiometric calibration to unitless reflectance.

name: Clip surface reflectance values
desc: The script applies a raster calculator operation to clip pixel values of Sentinel-2 or Landsat-like surface reflectance (SR) bands to the range [0, 2], replacing out-of-range values (< 0 or > 2) with -9999 NoData. It processes individual GeoTIFF files matching specific band names (e.g., SR_B2.TIF through SR_B7.TIF, B8.TIF, ST_EMIS.TIF) in nested directories under '/Users/jonny.sanchez/Documents/tesis/5-clean_outliers/santa_marta', overwrites each input file with a new 'CO_' prefixed version, and deletes the original. The formula '(A >= 0) * (A <= 2) * A + ((A < 0) + (A > 2)) * -9999' implements conditional clamping using GDAL's raster calculator via QGIS Processing.

name: Fill thermal and reflectance raster no-data
desc: The script processes individual GeoTIFF files (SR_B2.TIF through SR_B7.TIF, B8.TIF, ST_EMIS.TIF) located in subdirectories under '/Users/jonny.sanchez/Documents/tesis/6-fill_data/santa_marta'. For each matching file, it applies GRASS 'r.fillnulls' with method=1 (bilinear interpolation), edge=3, npmin=600, segmax=300 to fill nodata pixels, outputs a new file prefixed with 'FN_', and deletes the original input file. The processing is performed using QGIS Processing Framework with GRASS GIS backend; no cloud masking, temporal filtering, or classification occurs — only gap-filling of single-band rasters.

name: Compute land cover density masks
desc: The script processes a classified raster (ExtraTrees.TIF) to generate six binary density rasters per folder: one for each land cover class (0–5), where each output raster (e.g., c0_sea_water.TIF) represents the spatial density (via 5-cell neighborhood averaging) of pixels assigned to that class. It does so by first applying GDAL Raster Calculator to isolate each class (e.g., A==0), then smoothing with GRASS r.neighbors (method=0, size=5), and finally deleting intermediate binary rasters. The outputs are six named GeoTIFFs per subfolder under '/Users/jonny.sanchez/Documents/tesis/9-cover_density/barranquilla', explicitly mapped to 'Agua de mar', 'Agua dulce', 'Construcciones', 'Nubes', 'Suelo desnudo', and 'Vegetación'.

name: Extract surface temperature and emissivity
desc: The script performs raster sampling of multiple georeferenced rasters (including LST.TIF, ST_EMIS.TIF, NDVI.TIF, NDWI.TIF, NDBI.TIF, and land cover class rasters like c0_sea_water.TIF through c5_vegetation.TIF) onto a vector layer of meteorological stations stored in a GeoPackage. It sequentially applies QGIS's 'native:rastersampling' algorithm to extract pixel values at station locations, appending columns with prefixes (e.g., 'lst_', 'st_emissivity_') to the vector layer. Intermediate GeoPackage files are generated and chained; only the final output ('estaciones_meteorologicas_final.gpkg') retains all sampled attributes. The workflow is driven by file name matching (case-insensitive) within a root directory and relies on local raster files—not GEE assets—so no Earth Engine API calls are present.

name: Convert DXF to Orange-compliant shapefiles
desc: The script converts AutoCAD DXF files—originating from French DFT (Dossier de Fourniture Technique) submissions—into standardized ESRI Shapefile outputs required by ORANGE (a major French telecom operator). It performs layer-type-based routing (Point/LineString/Polygon), applies domain-specific QGIS Processing Model algorithms (dxf_to_shapes_model_aer and dxf_to_shapes_model_gc) for AER (aerial) and GC (underground) network variants, merges outputs, applies consistent styling (e.g., 'support_aer.qml'), refactors field schemas to match ORANGE’s mandatory attributes ('ref_comman', 'num_siren', 'operateur', 'type'), and packages final layers (support.shp, cable.shp, bpe.shp, and optional _gcor variants) into ZIP archives—one with only GCOR-labeled layers and one without.

name: Convert DXF cable and pole layers to standardized shapefiles
desc: The script processes AutoCAD DXF-derived vector layers (cables as lines, labels as points) to generate three standardized GIS output layers: (1) 'support' — deduplicated cable vertex points enriched with infrastructure type (e.g., FT_APPUI, FT_APTIERS) and numbering from label buffers; (2) 'cable' — non-GCOR cable segments annotated with ref_commande, operateur (e.g., ORANGE), and siren; (3) 'cable_GCOR' — GCOR-labeled cable segments similarly annotated; and (4) 'bpe' — pole features (PF) classified via text-based labeling (e.g., 'MM', 'PB') and spatially joined to buffered point labels. Key workflow steps include attribute-based extraction (e.g., filtering by Layer='GCOR'), ratio-based bounding box classification (0.769→ORANGE poles, 0.757→ATHD, 0.571→ENEDIS), vertical-line detection via y-difference calculation on exploded polygon boundaries, line–line intersection to locate support points along cables, and multi-stage spatial joins to propagate INSEE codes and PF types using buffer-based location matching.

name: Convert DXF engineering layers to standardized GIS features
desc: The script converts AutoCAD DXF files (imported as QGIS vector layers) into standardized, attribute-enriched GIS feature classes for telecom infrastructure: (1) 'cable_GCOR' (GCOR-labeled cables with ref_comman/num_siren/operateur fields), (2) 'cable' (non-GCOR cables with same metadata), (3) 'support_GCOR' (vertices of GCOR cables, classified as FT_CHOPE supports), (4) 'bpe' (boundary point elements — PF-type points joined to buffered 'type_pf' labels), and (5) 'support' (deduplicated centroids of chambers + ORANGE/ATHD pole intersections + number-tagged points, enriched with type_chambre and numero). It uses geometric operations (buffering, line intersections, polygon-to-lines, explode, centroids), regex-based text classification ('MM','M','PB', etc. → 'type_pf'; 5-digit codes → 'insee'; FT-prefixed or numeric → 'numero'), ratio-based pylon detection (0.769 for ORANGE, 0.757 for ATHD), and spatial joins to assign attributes from labels to infrastructure features.

name: Generate H3 hexagonal grid from layer extent
desc: The script generates a series of H3 geohash-based hexagonal grids (at user-specified resolutions 0–9) that cover the geographic extent (bounding box polygon) of the currently active QGIS vector layer — optionally restricted to selected features. It reprojects the input layer to a geographic CRS (EPSG:4617), computes the axis-aligned bounding rectangle, uses h3.polyfill_polygon to fill that rectangle with H3 hexagons at each resolution, converts each H3 ID to its boundary polygon in WGS84 decimal degrees, and writes each resolution level to a separate ESRI Shapefile with 'id' attribute; all outputs are added to the QGIS project.

name: Hexagon binning of point features
desc: The script performs hexagonal spatial binning (hexabinning) of vector point features using the H3 geospatial indexing system. It reprojects the input layer to WGS84 (EPSG:4617), computes H3 hexagons covering the layer’s extent at user-specified resolution(s), generates polygon shapefiles for each hexagon grid, counts the number of input points per hexagon using QGIS's 'Count Points in Polygon' algorithm, saves both the empty hexagon grid and the count-augmented shapefile (with 'numpoints' attribute), loads the count layer into QGIS, and applies a graduated (quantile-based) Blues color ramp symbology to visualize point density. Outputs are ESRI Shapefiles (e.g., 'layerName_Hex6.shp' and 'layerName_Hex6_count.shp') stored in a dedicated subfolder ('hexabinned_datasets/') within the working directory.

name: Convert LST raster to Celsius
desc: The script converts a raw satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST) raster layer from digital numbers (DN) to physical temperature values in degrees Celsius using a linear radiometric calibration formula: LST(°C) = (DN × 0.00341802) − 124.15. It then vectorizes the resulting Celsius raster into polygon features representing contiguous temperature zones, applies Chaikin’s smoothing algorithm (3 iterations) to eliminate pixelated jagged boundaries, and applies a dynamically classified graduated symbology (5 equal-interval classes, inverted RdYlGn color ramp) to the final GeoPackage vector layer for visual thermal pattern analysis.

name: Convert point layer to polygon
desc: The script converts a vector point layer from a GeoPackage into a single closed polygon shapefile by computing the centroid of the points, sorting them angularly around that centroid to form a convex hull-like boundary, and writing the resulting polygon geometry to an ESRI Shapefile. Input is a QGIS vector layer loaded via OGR from a GeoPackage; output is a shapefile with one polygon feature and an 'id' attribute.

name: Generate 5-meter hydrographic reference network
desc: The script creates a refined hydrological reference network with a standardized 5-meter width by integrating and processing vector datasets: (1) hydrographic surface polygons (e.g., natural water bodies and reservoirs), (2) an existing reference hydrographic segment network, (3) exutoire (outlet) buffer zones, and optionally (4) a watershed zone boundary. It performs topological network analysis—including node identification, connectivity fixing, network measurement from outlets, Hack and Strahler stream ordering—and applies geometric and attribute-based filters (e.g., minimum length inside water surface ≥30%, removal of isolated Strahler rank 1 segments <500 m connecting to rank ≥3 streams, and elimination of short outlet streams <10,000 m). The final output is a cleaned, topologically consistent, single-width (5 m) linear hydrographic network layer saved as a GeoPackage.

name: Extract connected hydrographic network
desc: The script constructs a topologically connected reference hydrographic network by starting from buffered outlet points (exutoire) and selecting all upstream/downstream connected stream reaches (troncons) from a corrected BD TOPO IGN hydrographic dataset. It first removes duplicate geometries, identifies network nodes (NODEA/NODEB), selects reaches intersecting the outlet buffer, then applies connected component selection to retain only the hydrologically connected subset. It further simplifies the network to a principal stem (single-path upstream route to source) and aggregates reaches into continuous segments between network junctions (intersections), producing two outputs: (1) a troncon-level layer preserving original BD TOPO geometry and attributes (minus NODEA/NODEB), and (2) a segment-level layer where linear features are merged between confluences, with working fields (GID, LENGTH, CATEGORY, NODEA, NODEB) removed. All outputs are saved to a GeoPackage.

name: Fix hydrographic network connections
desc: The script fixes hydrographic network connections by adding features from a source GeoPackage layer (identified by 'cleabs' ID) to a target GeoPackage layer, avoiding duplicates. It loads both layers via QGIS OGR driver, removes duplicate geometries from the source, identifies IDs present in both layers using 'cleabs' attribute filtering, and appends only non-overlapping features to the target layer using QgsVectorLayer.edit() and addFeatures(). Output is a modified target layer with updated hydrographic connections.

name: Fix hydrographic network connection and flow direction
desc: The script fixes topological connectivity and flow direction of hydrographic line features by copying features from a source GeoPackage layer into a target GeoPackage layer and reversing the geometry (polyline) direction for features identified by 'cleabs' ID. It removes duplicate geometries from the source, identifies features not already present in the target layer using the 'cleabs' attribute, adds those missing features, and then reverses the polyline vertex order for all source-identified features in the target layer to correct flow direction. Output is an updated target layer with added features and inverted line directions.

name: Fix hydrographic network flow direction
desc: The script corrects the geometric direction (i.e., vertex order) of line features in a target hydrographic layer (`troncon_hydrographique_cours_d_eau_corr`) by reversing the polyline geometry for features whose `cleabs` identifier matches those present in a source correction layer (`troncon_hydrographique_corr_dir_ecoulement`). It loads both layers from GeoPackage files, removes duplicate geometries from the source, extracts `cleabs` IDs, filters the target layer by those IDs using an SQL expression, and reverses each matching feature's polyline. The output is an in-place edit of the target GeoPackage layer with corrected flow direction.

name: Fix hydrographic network geometry
desc: The script updates geometries in a target hydrographic layer (troncon_hydrographique_cours_d_eau_corr) by replacing modified line features with corrected geometries from a source layer (troncon_hydrographique_corr_geom), using 'cleabs' (a unique identifier) to match features. It first removes duplicate geometries from the source, then filters both layers by 'cleabs', and programmatically overwrites target feature geometries with corresponding source geometries via QgsVectorLayer.edit() and changeGeometry(). The output is an in-place geometric correction of the target GeoPackage layer.

name: Remove canal features from hydrographic network
desc: The script processes a corrected hydrographic network layer (troncon_hydrographique_cours_d_eau_corr) by identifying network nodes, extracting outlets intersecting a buffered exutoire (outlet) layer, filtering out canal-related features based on the 'nature' attribute (excluding 'Canal', 'Conduit forcé', 'Conduit buse', and 'Ecoulement canalisé'), merging the outlet and non-canal network segments, and then applying network connectivity correction using the fct:fixnetworkconnectivity algorithm with the merged subset. The final output is a cleaned hydrographic network layer with canals removed and topologically fixed, saved back to the original GeoPackage under a new layer name (e.g., troncon_hydrographique_cours_d_eau_corr_suppr_canal).

name: Remove canal and multichannel features
desc: The script removes hydrographic features (specifically 'canal' and 'multichannel' segments) from a target hydrographic layer (troncon_hydrographique_cours_d_eau_corr) by identifying matching features in a source correction layer (troncon_hydrographique_corr_suppr_canal_multichenal) using the 'cleabs' identifier field. It first deduplicates geometries in the source layer, extracts all 'cleabs' values, constructs a filter expression to select matching features in the target layer, deletes those features in-place, and commits the edits. The output is a modified GeoPackage layer with those hydrographic segments removed.

name: Split LiDAR raster into buffered tiles
desc: The script splits a source LiDAR raster (provided as a VRT file) into 1° × 1° WGS84-aligned GeoTIFF tiles with configurable buffer overlap (bufferX/bufferY = 0.000139°), using GDAL warp with cubic resampling and LZW compression. Each tile is named in the format 'NxxExxx' or 'SxxWxxx' (e.g., 'N81E000'), generated via dynamic WKT polygon construction in memory using QGIS Python API, written temporarily as GeoJSON for cutline masking, then warped and saved. The output consists of georeferenced, overlapping, compressed GeoTIFF tiles covering the longitude range [-33, 36] and latitude range [26, 82] (WGS84).

name: Aggregate recreation area attributes
desc: The script performs a spatial aggregation on a vector layer 'RECAREAACTIVITIES_V' using geometry as the grouping key (via geom_to_wkt($geometry)), collapsing duplicate geometries into single features while preserving and concatenating specific attributes: 'OBJECTID' (first value), 'RECAREANAME' (concatenated unique values separated by ';'), and all other listed fields (e.g., 'LATITUDE', 'LONGITUDE', 'ACTIVITYNAME', 'OPENSTATUS') using 'first_value' or 'concatenate_unique' aggregations. The output is written to 'OUTPUT_FILE'. No raster operations, time-series analysis, or remote sensing calculations are present — it is purely a vector attribute consolidation workflow using QGIS's native aggregate algorithm.

name: Compute mean radiant temperature
desc: The script computes mean radiant temperature (TMRT) using the SOLWEIG model via the UMEP QGIS plugin. It processes high-resolution raster inputs (bDSM, cDSM, DEM, wall_aspect, wall_height, LULC, SVF, and meteorological data) by tiling, buffering, clipping, and running SOLWEIG per tile; then debuffers and merges the TMRT outputs. Key workflow steps include GDAL-based raster slicing with buffering, SVF file clipping and zipping, SOLWEIG execution with fixed biophysical and human parameters (e.g., ALBEDO_WALLS=0.2, EMIS_GROUND=0.95, UTC=-4), and final GDAL-based merging of debuffered TMRT rasters (e.g., Tmrt_2023_208_0900D.tif). Outputs are merged GeoTIFFs of TMRT for specific date/time combinations.

name: Compute mean radiant temperature
desc: The script computes mean radiant temperature (TMRT) using the SOLWEIG model via the UMEP QGIS plugin. It processes high-resolution raster inputs (bDSM, cDSM, DEM, wall_aspect, wall_height, LULC, and SVF rasters) in tiled, buffered chunks to mitigate edge effects. For each tile, it slices buffered input rasters, packages clipped SVF files into a ZIP archive, runs SOLWEIG with fixed biophysical and meteorological parameters (e.g., ALBEDO_WALLS=0.2, UTC=-4, meteo_hot_typical.txt), debuffers the resulting TMRT outputs (e.g., Tmrt_2023_208_0900D.tif) to restore correct georeferencing, and merges all debuffered TMRT rasters by time/type using GDAL VRT and Translate. Outputs include debuffered per-tile TMRT rasters and final merged GeoTIFFs (e.g., Tmrt_2023_208_0900D_merged_final.tif).

name: Merge cadastral parcel polygons
desc: The script merges all polygon features in the QGIS vector layer named 'Wyniki wyszukiwania ULDK' into a single polygon, populating new fields ID_DZIALKI (concatenated TERYT values), NUMER_DZIALKI (concatenated nr_dzialki values), and POLE_EWIDENCYJNE (summed area in m²). It then reprojects the layer to the project CRS if needed, saves it as a GeoPackage named 'granica_terenu.gpkg', reloads it into the QGIS project, applies a QML style file 'style/granica terenu planowanej inwestycji.qml', and finally merges all features in the newly loaded 'granica_terenu' layer if more than one exists.

name: Create linear infrastructure layers
desc: The script creates two vector layers with line geometry ('olz' and 'wymiarowanie') in GeoPackage format within the QGIS project directory, applies predefined QML styles, adds a 'l' (length) field with automatic $length calculation for the 'wymiarowanie' layer, and leaves both layers in editing mode. It uses QgsVectorLayer with memory provider, QgsVectorFileWriter to export as GPKG, QgsProject to add layers, and QgsDefaultValue to set dynamic length computation.

name: Classify roof types from building predictions
desc: The script classifies building roof types (e.g., 'płaski', 'dwuspadowy', 'czterospadowy') by joining AI-generated building-level predictions (from external CSV: building_predictions.csv) with a QGIS vector layer of buildings ('budynki_z_szer_elew_front'), then interactively validates and refines classifications using a GUI dialog. It outputs: (1) a CSV file ('klasyfikacja_dachow.csv') logging ID_BUDYNKU → roof category mappings; (2) a joined and styled vector layer ('budynki_parametry') with added 'Kategoria' and corrected 'nachylenie' values for flat roofs; (3) an additional joined layer for point cloud data ('Classification_6_with_roofsKategories'); and (4) GeoPackage exports of all derived layers. Critical preprocessing includes ID normalization (replacing '/' with '_'), join validation, ID-matching diagnostics, and automatic fallback handling for missing prediction fields ('PREDYKCJA', 'PEWNOSC').

name: Extract and label polygon vertices
desc: The script processes a polygon vector layer in QGIS by extracting its vertices, filtering out those with distance = 0 (likely duplicate or start/end points), sorting the remaining vertices counter-clockwise starting from the southernmost vertex, assigning alphabetical labels (A, B, C, ..., AA, AB, etc.), and saving the result as a GeoPackage point layer named 'wierzcholki.gpkg' in the project folder. It applies optional QML styling, adds the layer to the QGIS project, and automatically enables editing mode. The workflow uses QGIS Processing Toolbox's 'native:extractvertices', manual geometry ring ordering, coordinate tolerance-based feature matching, and QgsVectorFileWriter for GPKG export.

name: Aggregate land parcels by building overlap
desc: The script performs spatial aggregation of land parcels ('dzialki') based on shared buildings ('budynki') within a 200 m buffer around an analysis boundary ('granica_obszaru_analizowanego'). It first creates the buffer, selects parcels and buildings intersecting it, then groups parcels that share at least one building (with ≥10% intersection area), merges their geometries into multipolygons, and computes aggregated attributes (ID_DZIALKI, NUMER_DZIALKI, NUMER_OBREBU, POLE_EWIDENCYJNE). Unaggregated parcels are retained as-is. The output includes two final GeoPackage layers: 'dzialki_zgodne_z_funkcja' (parcels filtered by user-selected building function types like 'rodzaj_zabudowy') and 'budynki_zgodne_z_funkcja' (corresponding buildings), both styled with QML and further processed by spatially filtering out parcels and buildings overlapping a separate 'granica_terenu' layer — i.e., removing parcels fully inside or partially overlapping it (via difference) and removing buildings >10% overlapped by 'granica_terenu'. All intermediate memory layers are cleaned up.

name: Apply QML style to vector layer
desc: The script applies a QML style file to a QGIS vector layer named 'wymiary', saves the layer as a GeoPackage file in the project directory, removes the original temporary layer from the project, reloads the saved GeoPackage layer, and refreshes its symbology. The QML style path is hardcoded as 'style/wymiary - grubsza strzalka.qml' relative to the script directory.

name: Export active layer to GeoPackage
desc: The script exports the currently active QGIS vector layer to a GeoPackage file in the same directory as the saved QGIS project. It retrieves the active layer via iface.activeLayer(), constructs an output path using the layer name and project directory, writes the layer using QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormatV3 with GPKG driver and UTF-8 encoding, removes the original temporary layer from the project, and reloads the saved GeoPackage layer back into the project. Success or failure is reported via print statements.

name: Apply polygon population to buildings
desc: The script takes postcode polygon layers with a 'projected_population' attribute and a filtered buildings layer, computes geometric overlap between each polygon and buildings, and distributes the polygon's population across building points proportionally to overlap area (with thresholds at 0.3 and 0.7). It outputs a point layer where each point represents a building (or polygon centroid if no building overlap), annotated with 'count' (assigned population) and 'overlap' (fractional area overlap). The geometry of output points is either the centroid of the intersecting area or the building's centroid for high-overlap cases.

name: Calculate polygon overlap percentage
desc: The script computes the percentage of area overlap between each feature in an input vector layer and all features in a comparison vector layer. It iterates over input features, uses bounding box filtering to optimize spatial search, calculates intersection area divided by input feature area for each overlapping comparison feature, sums these ratios, and appends the total overlap percentage as a new 'overlap' field to each output feature. The output is a vector layer with identical geometry and attributes as the input, plus the computed overlap value.

name: Extract and merge cadastral boundary GML files
desc: The script downloads region-specific cadastral vector data (GML format) from the Italian Agenzia delle Entrate WFS service, recursively extracts nested ZIP archives containing _map.gml (cadastral map boundaries) and _ple.gml (cadastral parcel boundaries) files, then merges all MAP files into a single GeoPackage layer per province (e.g., 'AQ_map_unito.gpkg') and all PLE files into another (e.g., 'AQ_ple_unito.gpkg'), preserving official cadastral geometry and attributes for administrative and land registry use.

name: Merge cadastral map and parcel layers
desc: The script downloads, extracts, and merges Italian cadastral GML files (MAP = cadastral maps; PLE = land parcels) for a user-selected Italian region from the Agenzia delle Entrate WFS service. It organizes extracted GMLs by type (MAP/PLE), merges all files of each type into a single vector layer using QGIS native merge algorithm, filters attributes to retain only 'fid', 'gml_id', and 'ADMINISTRATIVEUNIT', exports the result in user-specified format (GML/GPKG/Shapefile/GeoJSON), and optionally loads the outputs into QGIS. The workflow includes full temporary file management, error-resilient cleanup, and timing reporting.

name: Download cadastral parcel boundaries
desc: The script downloads cadastral parcel geometries from the Italian Agency of Revenue's WFS service (https://wfs.cartografia.agenziaentrate.gov.it/inspire/wfs/owfs01.php) within a user-drawn polygon on the QGIS canvas. It parses GML responses, extracts INSPIRE ID, comune (municipality code), foglio (map sheet number), and LABEL (parcel identifier), constructs WKT polygons from gml:posList coordinates, validates geometries, and loads them into a memory vector layer with four fields: inspireid_localid, comune, foglio, particella. Output is a QGIS vector layer named 'Particelle Catastali' added to the project.

name: Generate villa layout scenarios
desc: The script performs a complete feasibility analysis for villa development on a land parcel, integrating terrain analysis (slope, aspect, flow accumulation, hillshade), constraint mapping (buildable envelope), suitability scoring (weighted by slope, view, access, drainage), regulatory compliance (setbacks, max building percentage, spacing), and deterministic placement of villas across three scenarios: Premium (65% of max, 12m spacing), Balanced (85% of max, 10m spacing), and Max Yield (100% of max, 8m spacing). Outputs include GeoPackage, DXF, CSV, JSON, and TXT files containing villa footprints, metadata, summary reports, and QGIS-layered results loaded into the current project.

name: Generate villa suitability and compliance maps
desc: The script performs integrated terrain analysis (slope, aspect, flow accumulation, hillshade), constraint mapping (setbacks, steep slopes, drainage exclusion), suitability scoring (weighted combination of slope, view, access, drainage), and regulatory compliance calculation (max villa count, buildable area percentage, scenario-based layout targets) for residential villa development. It auto-detects input files (DEM.tif, boundary.gpkg, road.shp), runs modular geoprocessing steps using QGIS processing algorithms and raster/vector operations, outputs georeferenced rasters (e.g., suitability_combined.tif, slope_degrees.tif) and vectors (e.g., buildable_envelope.gpkg), generates a timestamped summary report (PHASE2_SUMMARY.txt), and loads key results into QGIS with layer grouping and visibility settings.

name: Analyze terrain suitability for villa placement
desc: The script performs an end-to-end geospatial feasibility analysis for residential villa development on hillside terrain. It loads a DEM and boundary vector, validates CRS alignment, computes slope, aspect, hillshade, and drainage (Phase 1), applies regulatory constraints (setbacks, slope limits) to generate a buildable envelope (Phase 2), calculates multi-factor suitability scores (slope, view, access, drainage) with configurable weights, detects elevation- and slope-based zoning regulations (e.g., 'Green Zone Residential' on Koh Phangan), derives site-adaptive villa product sizes (villa/compact/studio classes) and spacing from buildable area and terrain geometry, places villas in three scenarios (Premium, Balanced, MaxYield) using contour-aware terracing logic, and exports DXF, GeoPackage, CSV, JSON, and (optionally) a PDF feasibility report with maps and QC validation.

name: Analyze terrain suitability for villa layout
desc: The script performs integrated terrain analysis, constraint mapping, and regulatory-compliant suitability scoring to determine realistic villa capacity on a parcel. It computes slope, aspect, flow accumulation, and hillshade from a DEM; applies setbacks, steep-slope exclusions, and hydrologic constraints; scores suitability based on slope, view, access, and drainage using configurable weights; enforces Green Zone regulations (70% building coverage cap, min spacing, max height); applies GM-specific corrections including rectangular spacing modeling, dynamic geometry efficiency based on parcel compactness, and fragmentation-aware capacity estimation; and outputs a validated GM Corrections Test Report with 10-point validation, QGIS-loaded rasters/vectors, and three scenario-based villa counts (Premium/Balanced/Maximum).

name: Generate villa layout scenarios
desc: The script performs a complete feasibility analysis for villa development on a parcel, integrating terrain analysis (slope, aspect, flow, hillshade), constraint mapping (buildable envelope), suitability scoring (weighted by slope, view, access, drainage), regulation-based capacity calculation (Green Zone Residential rules), and spatial placement of villas across three scenarios: Premium (65% of max, 12m spacing), Balanced (85% of max, 10m spacing), and Max Yield (100% of max, 8m spacing). Outputs include GeoPackage (QGIS), DXF (SketchUp), CSV (spreadsheet), JSON (metadata), and TXT (summary report), with all layers automatically loaded into QGIS under 'Phase 3 - Villa Layouts' and 'Context' groups.

name: Generate terrain analysis from DEM
desc: The script auto-detects a user-provided DEM/DTM raster (e.g., DEM.tif or DTM.tif) and computes four core terrain derivatives: slope (in degrees), aspect (compass direction), flow accumulation (using GRASS r.watershed), and hillshade (with azimuth=315°, altitude=45°). It optionally incorporates orthomosaic, boundary, and road vector layers for context but does not use them in the terrain calculations. Outputs are GeoTIFFs saved to an auto-created 'outputs' subfolder, with metadata (CRS, dimensions, statistics) printed and all valid results loaded into QGIS map canvas.

name: Generate terrain slope profile sections
desc: The script generates three client-ready longitudinal terrain profile sections along the long axis of a parcel boundary, using a DTM raster to extract elevation profiles, compute local slopes in degrees and percentage, annotate run/rise segments with blue brackets, label datum elevations, and produce stacked profile charts (PNG/PDF) alongside a branded QGIS print layout with location map, grid, north arrow, scale bar, and summary statistics.

name: Analyze terrain slope profiles for development feasibility
desc: The script performs intelligent terrain section analysis on a high-resolution DTM to assess land development feasibility. It identifies practical high/low points (filtered by percentile to exclude outliers), calculates dominant slope direction and azimuth, generates four terrain-driven cross-sections (A: main fall-line; B & C: parallel building corridors; D: cross-slope for camber analysis), samples elevation along each section, applies optional smoothing (Savitzky-Golay or moving average), computes local slope statistics (avg, 95th percentile, max), classifies slope as Gentle/Moderate/Steep using degree thresholds (≤10°, ≤20°), and produces plain-English development interpretations including optimal building corridors, drainage recommendations, access strategy, terrace guidance, and risk zone identification. Outputs include a GeoPackage of intelligent profile lines, a text report with LANDWISE SLOPE SUMMARY, matplotlib elevation-vs-distance charts, and a branded QGIS print layout (A3) with location map, sidebar branding, and export to PNG/PDF.

name: Classify slope terrain
desc: The script computes slope from a digital elevation model (DEM) in degrees, classifies it into five standardized LandWise slope classes (0–5°, 5–15°, 15–25°, 25–35°, 35°+), applies professional cartographic styling (color ramp, opacity, hillshade blending), generates a fully branded A3 print layout with legend, scale bar, north arrow, and grid, and exports high-resolution PNG (4000px) and PDF (300 DPI) deliverables alongside slope statistics (area %, ha, pixel count per class), technical report, and JSON metadata — all following the LandWise Technical Specification & Map Style Standard.

name: List shapefile layers from folder
desc: The script scans a user-specified folder recursively for .shp files, retrieves their encoding information using QGIS's native:shpencodinginfo algorithm, loads each as a QgsVectorLayer with appropriate text encoding (falling back to ISO-8859-1 if encoding is undetermined), validates the layer, and returns a list of valid QgsVectorLayer objects—without adding them permanently to the QGIS project. It is designed as a preprocessing step for the 'import_survey_data.model3' workflow.

name: Output polygons with area-weighted mean
desc: The script sets up an output shapefile for disaggregation analysis, loading it either from a file path or as a QgsVectorLayer, reprojecting it to a specified EPSG code, validating the presence of a user-defined ID field, and computing feature areas and ID mappings. It prepares the layer for subsequent area-weighted aggregation or disaggregation operations by building a pandas Series mapping numeric feature IDs to user-specified string IDs and associating polygon areas with those IDs.

name: Calculate morphometric roughness parameters
desc: The script computes morphometric parameters (zH, fai, pai, zHmax, zHstd, zd, z0, wai) from DSM and DEM rasters clipped to polygon grid features. It uses imageMorphometricParms_v1 and RoughnessCalcFunctionV2 modules to derive building height statistics, surface roughness length (z0), zero-plane displacement (zd), and wall area index (wai). Outputs include per-grid anisotropic parameter text files and a consolidated isotropic summary file, with optional attribute addition to the input vector layer.

name: Calculate LCZ fractions and aerodynamic parameters
desc: The script computes Local Climate Zone (LCZ) fractional coverage and aerodynamic parameters (e.g., roughness length z0, displacement height zd, wai) for each input grid polygon by clipping a land cover raster to the polygon’s bounding box using gdal.Translate, masking and processing the clipped raster with LCZ_fractions class, and exporting three tabular outputs: LCFGrid_isotropic.txt (8-class LCZ fractions), build_MPGrid_isotropic.txt (building-related aerodynamic parameters), and veg_MPGrid_isotropic.txt (vegetation-related aerodynamic parameters); it also optionally appends these results as attributes to the input vector layer.

name: Compute land cover fractions from grid polygons
desc: The script computes land cover fractions (Paved, Buildings, Evergreen Trees, Deciduous Trees, Grass, Bare Soil, Water) for each input polygon feature by clipping and analyzing a land cover raster grid. It supports two modes: using the centroid point with a circular radius buffer (imid=1), or clipping the raster to the polygon geometry. Outputs include per-feature anisotropic results in text files and an isotropic summary file, plus optional attribute addition to the input vector layer. The script performs no-data handling, result normalization to ensure fractional sums equal 1.0, and uses GDAL Translate instead of gdalwarp for raster clipping.

name: Reclassify urban typology classes
desc: The script reclassifies vector layer attribute values (e.g., land cover or urban class codes) into standardized urban typology names and IDs using a lookup database. It reads a QGIS vector layer, extracts unique values from a selected attribute field, maps them to typology names and integer IDs via a predefined database dictionary ('db_dict'), adds two new fields ('TypolName' as string and 'TypolID' as integer), populates them based on user-defined mappings in comboboxes (comboBoxClass1–comboBoxClass22 → comboBoxNew1–comboBoxNew22), writes the result to a new shapefile, and loads it into the QGIS project. The workflow is triggered via UI buttons and relies on PyQGIS APIs for layer handling, field editing, and file I/O.

name: Prepare UWG urban input data
desc: The script prepares urban input data for the Urban Weather Generator (UWG) model by processing polygon grid layers, land cover fraction (LCF) text files, and building morphology (IMP) text files. It reads grid IDs from vector layer attributes, matches them to LCF and IMP records, computes urban parameters (e.g., bldHeight, bldDensity, verToHor, grasscover, treeCover), optionally intersects with building type polygons to assign urban building type fractions and construction eras, sets climate zone and rural vegetation cover, and generates UWG-formatted input files (one per grid ID) in the specified output directory. Outputs are ASCII text files named with a user-defined prefix and grid ID.

name: Calculate footprint overlap area
desc: The script calculates the spatial overlap among aerial imagery footprint polygons using QGIS's 'Join Attributes by Location Summary' tool with intersection predicate, then removes duplicate geometries to produce a cleaned overlap layer. Input is a vector polygon layer representing aerial imagery footprints; output is a vector layer containing summarized overlap attributes and deduplicated geometries.

name: Keep selected attribute fields
desc: The script filters a vector layer to retain only user-specified attribute fields, dropping all others. It uses QGIS's 'qgis:deletecolumn' algorithm with a list of fields to remove, derived by comparing the full field list against the user-selected 'Fields to keep' parameter. The output is a new vector layer containing only the specified fields and original geometries.

name: Clip raster images by vector mask
desc: The script clips raster images (.tif files) located in a specified folder using a shapefile as a mask layer. It loads the shapefile and each raster into QGIS, then applies the 'gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer' processing algorithm to produce masked rasters named with a 'recortada_' prefix. The script validates both input layers before clipping and clears the QGIS project cache after each operation.

name: Calculate NDVI from raster bands
desc: The script calculates the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) using a raster calculator operation in QGIS. It loads two single-band raster layers—NIR (from 'C:/B4.tif') and RED (from 'C:/B3.tif')—and applies the formula '(A-B)/(A+B)' where A is the NIR band and B is the RED band. The result is saved as a new GeoTIFF file at 'C:/NDVI.tif'. No classification, time-series analysis, or spatial filtering is performed; the task is strictly pixel-wise spectral index computation.

name: Reproject polygon layers and compute area
desc: The script processes all loaded vector polygon layers in the QGIS project, reprojects them to ESRI:102033 (USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area Conic), adds an 'area_ha' field, computes and populates each feature's area in hectares, and exports each resulting layer as a separate GeoPackage file with '_reprojetado' suffix to a specified local directory. The workflow uses QGIS Processing Toolbox's 'native:reprojectlayer', QgsVectorFileWriter for export, and direct geometry.area() calculation.

name: Filter satellite-detected deforestation alerts
desc: The script loads multiple DETER shapefiles from a local directory, filters vector features where the 'SATELLITE' attribute equals 'AMAZONIA1' or 'AMAZONIA-1', and exports each filtered selection as a new shapefile (e.g., 'layername_selected.shp'). It uses QGIS Python API (PyQGIS) to load layers into the current project, apply attribute-based selection via QgsVectorLayer.selectByExpression(), and write only selected features using QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormat() with onlySelected=True.

name: Compute raster statistics for current extent
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, min, max, std, sum, count) for the currently active raster layer over the current map canvas extent using a temporary memory polygon layer. It outputs a CSV file and displays the average value (elevation, inferred from 'elev_' prefix) in a success message bar; if no intersection exists or the active layer is not a raster, it shows appropriate warning or error messages.

name: Export features as GeoJSON files
desc: The script exports each feature from a GeoPackage vector layer into individual GeoJSON files named after the feature's 'NAME' attribute, removes the 'crs' property from each GeoJSON, stores the resulting GeoJSON string in a new 'geojson' field of the original layer, and writes all feature attributes—including the newly added GeoJSON string—to a CSV file. It uses QGIS PyQGIS APIs to load, edit, and write vector data, and relies on filesystem operations for folder creation and file I/O.

name: Smooth Voronoi polygons for point-based administrative units
desc: The script generates smoothed, boundary-constrained Voronoi tessellations from input point features (e.g., settlements, monitoring stations, or administrative centroids), using a multi-stage geometric processing workflow: (1) filtering input points and base polygon layer; (2) generating raw GRASS Voronoi polygons; (3) clipping to the base map extent; (4) densifying edges; (5) perturbing vertices stochastically within a user-defined tolerance to break straight-line rigidity; (6) reconstructing closed polygonal paths per unique ID group; (7) buffering and re-clipping to soften corners and ensure topological integrity within the base boundary; and (8) joining original point attributes back to the final smoothed polygons. The output is a vector layer of smoothed, non-overlapping, topology-clean Voronoi-derived polygons aligned to a base geographic boundary (e.g., country or region), preserving per-point attribute associations via join on a unique field.

name: Calculate vertex distances from points to polygons
desc: The script computes, for each point feature in the 'repoints' layer, the farthest and nearest Euclidean distances (in km) from that point to all vertices of each polygon in the 'repolygons' layer whose 'iso' ID matches the comma-separated list in the 'overlaps' field of the point. It outputs a memory point layer named 'vertexdistances' with attributes including point ISO, overlapping polygon IDs, count of overlaps, comma-separated farthest and nearest distances per polygon, count of distances computed, and a boolean flag indicating whether all distances were successfully calculated. The result layer is exported to CSV and added to the QGIS project.

name: Merge and dissolve country polygons
desc: The script loads a vector layer of country boundaries, filters it to select only specified countries (e.g., 'Country A', 'Country B'), merges their geometries into a single feature, dissolves internal boundaries to produce one contiguous polygon per selection, and adds the resulting dissolved polygon layer to the QGIS map canvas. It does not perform raster analysis, time-series processing, or remote sensing computation — it is purely a vector geometry aggregation workflow for administrative boundary synthesis.

name: Clip raster by mask polygons
desc: The script clips a raster named 'lahtodata_v3' using individual polygon features from a vector layer named 'segtrain_35k', producing one clipped GeoTIFF per feature (named by its 'fid' attribute) in the output folder '/run/nvme/job_5369942/tmp/v3_segtrain_35k/'.
