It uses QGIS PyQGIS to dynamically create memory vector layers per feature and invokes GDAL's 'gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer' algorithm with fixed CRS EPSG:3067. Output files are skipped if already exist.

name: Partition watershed into catchments
desc: The script partitions a SWAT hydrological modeling project into separate catchment-based projects by analyzing subbasin drainage chains and drainage areas from the Reach table. It assigns CatchmentIds to subbasins using a maxSubCatchment threshold (10000 sq km), creates catchment-specific SQLite databases with filtered Watershed, Reach, MonitoringPoint, hrus, uncomb, ElevationBand, pcp, tmp, wgn, and MasterProgress tables, updates subbasin IDs to local catchment basin numbering, generates catchments.shp via dissolve, and writes inlets.shp at subbasin outlets where subbasin == catchment and downstream subbasin exists. Outputs include per-catchment QGIS project files (.qgs), SQLite databases, TxtInOut/TablesOut directories, and spatial layers (subs.shp, rivs.shp, catchments.shp, inlets.shp).

name: Join CSV attributes to vector layer
desc: The script loads a CSV file returned by a WPS process as a delimited text layer in QGIS, then performs a table join between that CSV and a user-selected vector layer using a specified field from the vector layer and the first field of the CSV. The join is executed via the 'qgis:joinattributestable' processing algorithm and loaded into the project. The script handles UI widget inputs (QgsMapLayerComboBox and QgsFieldComboBox) to identify the target layer and join field.

name: Join CSV attributes to vector layer
desc: The script loads a CSV output from a WPS process as a delimited text layer in QGIS, then joins its first field to a user-selected vector layer using QGIS's 'qgis:joinattributestable' algorithm. The join is performed based on a user-selected field from the vector layer and the first field of the CSV, with non-matching records retained. The joined result is loaded as a temporary layer.

name: Identify cloud-free wind-calmed areas
desc: The script processes ERA5 reanalysis data ('Total cloud cover' and '10m wind speed') to compute multi-year monthly medians (and optionally standard deviations), applies user-defined thresholds to identify spatially contiguous areas meeting cetacean survey feasibility criteria (e.g., cloud cover ≤ 0.2 or wind speed ≤ 8 m/s), masks results using land (for live cetaceans) or buffered coastline (for stranded cetaceans), and outputs georeferenced raster maps and vector shapefiles ('suitable area(s)') representing optimal optical satellite acquisition zones over water — all tailored per cetacean type (live/stranding), location, data type, and statistic.

name: Identify live cetacean monitoring suitable areas
desc: The script identifies spatially explicit 'SUITABLE AREA(S)' for live cetacean monitoring by intersecting ERA5-derived monthly 'Total Cloud Cover' and '10m Wind Speed' vector layers that have been thresholded (e.g., cloud ≤20% and wind ≤5 m/s); it further merges and dissolves these with cloud-thresholded areas for stranded/floating cetaceans to produce integrated suitability maps for 'live cetaceans and/or floating carcasses, and stranded cetaceans'. Outputs are shapefiles (e.g., '_final_aoi_cloud20_wind5_live.shp', '_float_and_strand.shp') stored in location-specific folders, styled with colorblind-accessible dashed-fill symbology, and overlaid with EEZ, land, and image extent base layers for cartographic interpretation.

name: Simplify building footprints by buffer subtraction
desc: The script processes building footprint vector data to simplify geometry by first computing minimum bounding geometries (convex hulls), dissolving them into a single polygon, converting multiparts to single parts, then subtracting street buffer polygons (5 m wide) via geometric difference. It filters resulting polygons by minimum area (50 m²), adds geometry attributes (area, perimeter), drops redundant fields, and joins maximum building height attributes from the original building layer using spatial join-by-location (‘contains’ predicate). The final output is a cleaned, simplified, area-filtered, height-annotated building footprint GeoPackage (`cleaned.gpkg`).

name: Calculate raster mean values per grid
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean pixel value) of a raster layer over a vector grid layer using QGIS's native zonal statistics algorithm. It extracts the date from the raster filename (e.g., 'MERGED-202304-fv02' → '202304'), appends it as a prefix to the output field (e.g., '202304_mean'), saves each result as a CSV with fields 'adm_0', 'Lat', 'Lon', and the date-prefixed mean, then merges all CSVs on shared geographic identifiers ('adm_0', 'Lat', 'Lon') into a single combined_output.csv. Inputs are loaded by name from the current QGIS project, grouped under 'Grid' (vector) and '2000-2015' (raster group).

name: Dissolve country boundary layers
desc: The script iterates through vector layers (shapefiles) in a QGIS project group named 'Countries', extracts the layer name as a country identifier, runs the native QGIS dissolve algorithm with no grouping fields to merge all geometries into a single feature, saves the dissolved output as a new shapefile in a country-named subdirectory under 'C:/Users/nikolaus/Desktop/Script_testing/Countries Dissolve/', and loads each dissolved layer into a new QGIS layer group called 'Dissolved Layers'. The processing uses QgsProject.instance(), QgsLayerTreeGroup, QgsVectorLayer, and the 'native:dissolve' algorithm via QGIS Processing Framework.

name: Dissolve country boundary layers
desc: The script iterates through vector layers (shapefiles) in a QGIS project group named 'Countries', extracts each layer's name by parsing its string representation, runs the native QGIS 'dissolve' algorithm with no attribute fields specified (full geometric dissolution), saves the dissolved output as a new shapefile in a country-named subdirectory under 'C:/Users/nikolaus/Desktop/Script_testing/Countries Dissolve/', creates or finds a 'Dissolved Layers' group in the project, and loads each dissolved layer into that group. The output includes dissolved country boundary shapefiles and their corresponding loaded vector layers in QGIS.

name: Clean vector topology errors
desc: The script performs vector topology cleaning on the currently active QGIS vector layer using GRASS v.clean. It applies a suite of cleaning tools (break, snap, rmdangle, prune, rmarea, etc.) with configurable thresholds and parameters, then loads the cleaned output layer into the QGIS project with a predefined symbology style (persil_cleaned.qml). The workflow relies on QGIS PyQGIS API, GRASS 7 processing algorithms, and user interaction via a custom dialog.

name: Compute least cost path
desc: The script computes a least cost path between two user-specified points using a digital elevation model (DEM) and a friction cost raster. It first runs GRASS r.walk.coords to generate a direction raster based on elevation and friction, then uses GRASS r.drain with that direction raster and reversed start coordinates to trace the optimal path from destination back to source. The output is a vector line layer representing the least cost path.

name: Dissect and dissolve polygon overlaps
desc: The script detects geometric overlaps in a single input polygon layer using self-intersection analysis; it then optionally dissects overlapping polygons into non-overlapping parts (by splitting at intersection boundaries) and/or dissolves selected overlaps based on adjacency criteria (largest adjacent, smallest adjacent, or largest common boundary). Outputs include: (1) a temporary 'Intersected' vector layer containing dissected polygons with cleaned geometries and area attributes, saved as a shapefile with timestamped filename; (2) a 'Dissolved' vector layer resulting from elimination of selected overlaps, also saved as a timestamped shapefile; and (3) interactive zoom-to-selection of overlapping features in QGIS. The workflow relies on QGIS native and SAGA NextGen processing algorithms (e.g., 'sagang:polygonselfintersection', 'qgis:eliminateselectedpolygons'), geometry fixing, attribute filtering, and auto-increment ID assignment for topological disambiguation.

name: Clip raster by extent
desc: The script loads a raster layer ('landcover.img') to retrieve and print its spatial extent, then clips another raster ('elevation.tif') to a specified bounding box (-1308804, 1402816, 4297746, 5885036) using GDAL's cliprasterbyextent algorithm, producing a clipped output raster ('clipped2.img'). The clipping uses a nodata value of 999 and default data type. No classification, time-series analysis, or thematic modeling is performed — only geometric subsetting.

name: Clip elevation raster by extent
desc: The script loads an elevation raster layer from a local GeoTIFF file, retrieves and prints its spatial extent (x-minimum, x-maximum, y-minimum, y-maximum), then clips the same raster to a specified bounding box (440000, 460000, 4030000, 4045000) using GDAL's cliprasterbyextent algorithm, outputting a new clipped GeoTIFF file. The clipping uses a NODATA value of 999 and default data type.

name: Assign template polygon identifiers
desc: The script sets up an output shapefile for disaggregation by loading it either from disk or as a QgsVectorLayer, reprojecting it to a specified EPSG code, validating the presence of a user-specified ID field, building a mapping from numeric feature IDs to string-based identifiers, and computing polygon areas. It supports area-weighted aggregation downstream by precomputing feature areas and establishing consistent labeling via the ID field.

name: Execute SQL on vector layers
desc: The script executes a user-provided SQL query on one or more input vector layers using QGIS's virtual layer provider. It supports defining unique ID and geometry fields, specifying geometry type (including 'No geometry'), and setting CRS. Input layers may be temporarily written to disk if not in the current project (e.g., from modeler context). The output is a new vector layer containing features resulting from the SQL query execution.

name: Generate hypsometric curves
desc: The script computes hypsometric curves for polygon features intersecting a digital elevation model (DEM). It extracts elevation values within each polygon, bins them into user-defined vertical intervals (step), calculates cumulative area (or percentage) for each bin, and exports CSV files containing cumulative area/percentage versus elevation. The algorithm uses GDAL for raster I/O, OGR for vector geometry handling, and NumPy for array masking and statistics; it supports both absolute area (m²) and percentage outputs, and handles nodata values and feature-raster intersection logic.

name: Export vector layer to SpatiaLite
desc: The script exports a vector layer to a SpatiaLite database by connecting to a Spatialite provider, configuring export options (e.g., overwrite, spatial index creation, geometry column name, field case conversion, string length constraints), and using QgsVectorLayerExporter to write features. It supports optional primary key specification, encoding, forced single-part geometries, and spatial index generation post-import. The output is a persisted vector table in a SpatiaLite database file.

name: Generate points along line
desc: The script generates point features at raster pixel centroids that lie along input line vector features. It uses a raster layer to define the pixel grid and transforms line segment endpoints into pixel coordinates using the raster's geotransform, then applies a line-drawing algorithm (Bresenham-like) to identify all intersected pixels and convert their centers back to map coordinates. Output is a point vector layer with attributes 'id', 'line_id', and 'point_id', created via QGIS Processing framework as a PyQGIS algorithm named 'Generate points (pixel centroids) along line'.

name: Execute and load PostGIS SQL
desc: The script executes a user-provided SQL query against a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database connection and loads the resulting dataset as a QGIS vector layer. It resolves the named database connection, constructs a QgsDataSourceUri with the SQL subquery as a virtual table, specifies geometry and ID fields, creates a QgsVectorLayer from the URI, validates it, and adds it to the QGIS project's temporary layer store and layer loading queue. The output is a vector layer derived directly from the SQL result.

name: Calculate building heat loads
desc: The script calculates annual, winter, and daily building heat loads for polygon building footprints using BBR attributes (BuildYear, BuildCode, BBRarea, BBRUUID), lookup in a local Danish Heat Atlas CSV file, and rule-based Thermonet eligibility. It outputs a filtered GeoJSON containing only buildings eligible for Thermonet ('Thermonet' = 'Yes') with updated fields including heat load values, and a DAT file formatted for pythermonet input with hardcoded COP and cooling parameters.

name: Generate pipe topology for thermonet
desc: The script generates a pipe topology file for a district heating network (thermonet) by processing two input vector layers: main pipes with hierarchical 'Level' field and service pipes with 'id.lokalId' heatpump identifiers. It reprojects layers to a projected CRS (EPSG:3857), computes geometry lengths, resolves heatpump ID connectivity based on spatial proximity (buffer distance of 0.1 m for service pipes and 1 m for higher-level main pipes), deduplicates IDs, and outputs a GeoJSON layer with fields Section, SDR, Trace_(m), Number_of_traces, Max_pressure_loss_(Pa), and HP_ID_vector — plus a tab-separated DAT file with identical attributes for use in pythermonet.

name: Connect buildings to thermonet pipes
desc: The script computes the shortest service pipe connections between buildings with 'Thermonet' = 'Yes' and the nearest thermonet pipe segment, generating a line layer where each feature represents the shortest distance geometry between a building's nearest point and the nearest point on a pipe. It filters buildings by attribute, builds a spatial index for efficient pipe candidate search, iterates over pipe segments to compute ellipsoidal distances, preserves all input attributes in the output, and applies custom symbology (black line with red start-point marker). The output is used as input to the 'Pipe Topology' tool.

name: Compute radiance per population and area
desc: The script computes zonal statistics of radiance (from a raster layer) over polygon features, then calculates normalized radiance values per population (radiance sum divided by population field, scaled by 1000) and per unit area (radiance mean divided by pixel area, scaled by 1e6). It supports two modes: 'Per population' and 'Per area'. Outputs a vector layer with original attributes plus two new double fields: 'rad_pop' and 'rad_surf', styled with a Plasma graduated color ramp based on the active mode.

name: Remove dark zones from satellite imagery
desc: The script preprocesses a satellite raster image to remove dark zones (e.g., shadows, low-illumination areas) by clipping to an optional extent zone, computing band-wise majority pixel values within that zone, generating a binary mask where at least one RGB band exceeds its majority value, and applying the mask to retain only illuminated pixels. The output is a cleaned raster with dark zones zeroed out, preserving original band structure and data type (UInt16).

name: Analyze radiance per grid cell
desc: The script computes total radiance from a satellite image (using red, green, and blue bands weighted by luminance coefficients: 0.2989, 0.5870, 0.1140) and aggregates statistics per grid cell (user-provided or generated rectangle/diamond/hexagon grid). It identifies illuminated cells via majority pixel thresholding, segments lit areas via raster calculation, polygonizes them, extracts intersecting grid cells, and computes zonal statistics (mean, sum, etc.) for total radiance and individual RGB bands. Outputs include a vector layer with radiance statistics per grid cell, an indicator field ('indice_pol') classifying cells into 5 quantile-based radiance levels, and an optional output raster of total radiance.

name: Export vector layers to Shapefile
desc: The script exports vector layers from the current QGIS project to Shapefile format, converting encoding to UTF-8 using ogr2ogr, copying associated .dbf/.prj/.shx files, and repopulating features with field mapping (e.g., lowercased source field names to destination fields) and injecting an 'FCODE' attribute derived from layer name. It operates on all layers in the project, writes outputs to a timestamped subfolder under 'C:\Users\pedromartins\Missoes\003\exporttest\', and uses QgsVectorLayer, QgsFeature, and subprocess.call for ogr2ogr.

name: Perform multivariate clustering analysis
desc: The script performs multivariate clustering on vector input layers (points or polygons) using the K-means algorithm. It accepts user-specified numeric fields for clustering, supports optional spatial masking via a polygon layer, determines optimal cluster count using Calinski-Harabasz pseudo F-statistic across 2–30 clusters, and outputs both a clustered vector layer with a 'Cluster' attribute and an evaluation table listing pseudo F-statistics per candidate number of clusters. Clustering uses sklearn's KMeans with 'k-means++' initialization by default.

name: Natural Neighbour interpolation
desc: The script performs Natural Neighbour (Sibson) interpolation on point vector data using a convex hull–constrained, BallTree-accelerated discrete algorithm. It accepts a point layer and numeric field, computes interpolated values on a regular grid at user-specified cell size, masks output optionally with a polygon layer, and exports the result as a GeoTIFF raster with proper georeferencing and NoData handling. The implementation uses SciPy's ConvexHull and matplotlib.path.Path for hull masking, scikit-learn's BallTree for nearest-neighbor queries, and GDAL for raster I/O.

name: Analyze spatial clustering of raster values
desc: The script performs semi-automated spatial pattern analysis on a raster layer masked by a vector boundary: (1) it clips the input raster to the mask, (2) converts clipped pixels to points with 'VALUE' attribute, (3) computes Local Moran's I to classify spatial associations (HH/LL/HL/LH/NS), (4) filters out outliers (HH, LL, NS) into a separate output, (5) applies K-means multivariate clustering on the non-outlier points using only the 'VALUE' field, (6) interpolates clustered point values via Natural Neighbor to produce a continuous surface, and (7) evaluates interpolation accuracy by comparing estimated 'VALUE' against measured/reference values from a numeric field in the mask layer — all outputs are vector layers (except interpolated map raster) supporting plot-level spatial diagnostics and uncertainty-aware mapping.

name: Export embargo term polygons
desc: The script exports polygon features from a QGIS vector layer to standardized vector files (Shapefile, GPKG, or KML) for upload to the Cadastro, Arrecadação e Fiscalização System (Sicafi). It filters and validates input features by embargo term number ('NUM_TEI') and series ('SERIE_TEI'), removes all other fields, renames the required fields, supports exporting either all features to a single file or one file per feature, and optionally compresses outputs into ZIP archives containing all associated format-specific files (e.g., .shp + .shx + .dbf). The algorithm includes duplicate detection on the embargo term field and loads generated files into the QGIS project upon completion.

name: Extract Kerala administrative boundary
desc: The script extracts the administrative boundary of Kerala state from a GADM level-1 shapefile (gadm41_IND_1.shp) using QGIS's native 'extractbyattribute' algorithm, filtering by the 'NAME_1' field equal to 'Kerala'. It initializes QGIS in headless mode, sets up processing with native algorithms, runs the attribute-based vector extraction, and writes the result to 'outputs/kerala_boundary.shp'. The workflow includes error/warning logging via a custom QgsProcessingFeedback subclass.

name: Clip DEM to Kerala boundary
desc: The script clips a digital elevation model (DEM) raster of Kerala, India, using a vector boundary layer (GADM Level 1 administrative units) filtered to the state of Kerala. It loads the raster ('kerala_dem.tif') and vector ('gadm41_IND_1.shp'), filters the vector layer to retain only features where NAME_1 = 'Kerala', ensures CRS alignment between layers, and performs a raster-by-mask-layer clip operation using GDAL or QGIS native clipping algorithms. The output is a georeferenced GeoTIFF ('clipped_dem.tif') containing only the elevation data spatially intersecting Kerala's administrative boundary.

name: Calculate Euclidean distance raster
desc: The script calculates, for each cell in a raster grid, the Euclidean distance to the closest source feature (e.g., points, lines, or polygons) from an input vector layer. It first rasterizes the vector layer into a binary mask using GDAL's RasterizeLayer, then computes proximity distances using GDAL's ComputeProximity with optional maximum distance and georeferenced output. The output is a georeferenced raster where pixel values represent distances in map units (e.g., meters), with nodata = -9999.

name: Extract raster pixels by attribute expression
desc: The script performs pixel-wise conditional filtering of a raster layer using a user-defined QGIS expression (e.g., 'value > 0'). It reads input raster band data via GDAL, evaluates the expression for each pixel value in context (with 'value' and layer name as fields), retains pixels where the expression evaluates to true, and writes the result to a new GeoTIFF with identical georeferencing, data type, and nodata handling. The output is a masked raster where qualifying pixels retain their original values and non-qualifying pixels are set to nodata.

name: Apply fuzzy membership function
desc: The script transforms an input raster into a 0 to 1 scale indicating membership strength in a set using one of three fuzzification algorithms: Linear, J-shaped, or Sigmoidal. It reads the raster band pixel-by-pixel, computes min/max values, applies the selected function to normalize values, optionally inverts the result (IsDecrease), scales output by a user-defined integer, and writes the result as a Float32 GeoTIFF with preserved georeferencing and nodata handling.

name: Convert vector to raster
desc: The script converts a vector layer to a raster dataset using GDAL's RasterizeLayer function. It accepts an input vector layer, optional attribute field for burn-in values, user-defined extent and cell size, and raster data type (Float32/Float64/Int32). It computes raster dimensions from extent and cell size, creates a GeoTIFF with proper geotransform and projection, fills with nodata (-9999), then rasterizes features—either burning attribute values if a field is specified or defaulting to 1. Outputs a single-band raster file.

name: Extract kernel statistics from raster
desc: The script computes kernel-based statistical metrics (real, max, min, std, sum, average, mean) from a raster layer around point features, using a user-defined buffer radius in pixels. It first imports and aligns the raster and vector layers, identifies pixel locations of points, applies scipy.ndimage generic filters to compute spatial statistics over square kernels, and writes the resulting statistics as attributes to a new point vector layer in EPSG:3857. The output is a shapefile with one point per input point and eight attribute fields including 'real' (original raster value) and six derived kernel statistics.

name: Compute PS statistics and plot distribution
desc: The script intersects two user-provided polygon layers (Polygon 1 and Polygon 2) to define a masking region, clips a point layer (PS) to that intersection, computes a new numeric field for the clipped points using a user-defined QGIS expression formula, exports descriptive statistics (median, std, max, etc.) of that field to a CSV file, and generates an interactive histogram (via Plotly) of the field’s value distribution saved as an HTML file.

name: Model biodiversity dispersal corridors
desc: The script models species dispersal across a landscape by generating a friction surface from land cover layers (e.g., agriculture, forests, infrastructure) and computing cost-distance accumulation from biodiversity reservoirs (polygon features). It produces two primary outputs: (1) a 'Friction' raster where pixel values represent resistance to movement (based on user-defined coefficients per land cover class or interval), and (2) a 'Dispersion' raster generated via GRASS r.cost, showing cumulative cost distance from reservoir centroids up to a user-specified maximum cost threshold — effectively mapping potential ecological corridors and connectivity pathways.

name: Calculate urban environmental indicators
desc: The script computes three urban environmental indicators—cooling (rafraichissement), runoff (ruissellement), and biodiversity (biodiversité)—by aggregating classified land cover pixels (10-class EVA or 8-class legacy system) within user-defined calculation zones (parcels or automatically generated 'ilots'). It performs zonal histogram analysis on a classification raster (either input directly or vector-rasterized), computes class-wise percentages and surface areas, then applies fixed per-class coefficients to derive weighted indicator scores per zone. Outputs are a vector layer with attributes 'coef_raf', 'coef_bio', and 'coef_rui' attached to each parcel/ilot polygon, named according to input configuration (e.g., 'Indi_En_V2.2_vec_10_ilot').

name: Plan riparian buffer zone
desc: The script computes riparian buffer zones along waterbodies within user-defined planning areas (vector polygons). It retrieves background rasters ('suojakaista_taustarasterit', 'RUSLE', 'WB_Finland', 'DEM') via an interface, extracts waterlines from those rasters, and generates vector buffer zones using minimum and average width parameters and suspended solid retention percentage. The output is a vector layer of riparian zones styled with a QML file.

name: Compare DEM elevation bias by group
desc: The script compares two digital elevation models (DEMs) — DEM A and DEM B — by sampling elevation differences along buffered centerline features, grouping results by an optional attribute field from the centerline layer. It computes per-feature statistics (bias, RMSE, min/max diff, std dev), applies outlier exclusion based on a configurable |diff| threshold, flags features where absolute mean bias exceeds a user-defined significance threshold, and aggregates statistics per group. Outputs include an HTML report with per-group summary cards and feature-level tables, plus an optional vector layer of sampled points annotated with elevations, differences, nodata/exclusion flags, and group values.

name: Compute stream order for networks
desc: The script computes Hack, Strahler, and Shreve stream orders for line vector files representing stream networks. It scans a folder for OGR-readable line files (e.g., .gpkg, .shp, .geojson), detects network topology via endpoint snapping, auto-identifies outlets based on upstream length, reverses geometries as needed to ensure consistent flow direction, and writes ordered outputs to GeoPackage files with fields 'hack', 'strahler', 'shreve', 'network_id', and 'reversed'. Processing uses Shapely for geometry operations and QgsProcessingAlgorithm for QGIS integration.

name: Filter stream segments by count or distance
desc: The script filters segmented stream vector files (e.g., GeoPackage, Shapefile) in bulk using either a segment count threshold (seg_num ≤ N) or a downstream distance threshold (mile_range start < X). It reads each input file, validates required fields ('seg_num' or 'mile_range'), parses values, applies the filter, and writes a new GeoPackage with '_filtered.gpkg' suffix containing only kept features. Output files preserve source geometry, attributes, CRS, and safely remap 'fid' to 'src_fid' to avoid field name conflicts.

name: Filter stream segments by table reference
desc: The script filters segmented stream vector files (e.g., GeoPackage, Shapefile) in bulk using a CSV or XLSX reference table. It matches features based on a user-specified field (e.g., 'stream_seg_id') against values in the reference table using either partial or exact string matching, then writes filtered outputs as GeoPackage files—one per input file—with matching features either kept or deleted. Output filenames follow the pattern '<source_stem>_table_filtered.gpkg' (though code writes as '<source_stem>.gpkg'), and the script handles field name conflicts (e.g., remapping 'fid' → 'src_fid').

name: Segment stream centerlines
desc: The script segments stream centerline vector files (e.g., GeoPackage, Shapefile) into equal-length intervals measured from the downstream endpoint outward. It processes all OGR-readable line vector files in a specified input folder, validates geometry type and required name field, orients each LineString/MultiLineString downstream-first using vertex order assumptions, cuts features into segments of user-defined length (in miles or kilometers), and writes segmented outputs to GeoPackage files with new attributes: seg_num (1-based downstream index), mile_range (e.g., "0-1 mi"), and stream_seg_id (e.g., "Bear_Creek_mile_01"). Geodetic length measurement is performed via QgsDistanceArea with ellipsoid support (default GRS80), and CRS-native units are converted to meters where needed.

name: Segment streams into 1-mile reaches and filter first 5 miles
desc: The script processes vector stream layers (GPKG format) from an input folder, applying the QGIS stream_segmenter plugin to: (1) divide each stream feature into contiguous 1-mile segments (outputting segmented GPKG files in the 'miles' folder); (2) filter those segments to retain only those within the first 5 miles downstream from the start point (using distance-based filtering mode, outputting filtered GPKG files in the 'miles-filtered' folder); and (3) add or update a 'channel' field in both segmented and filtered outputs by extracting the prefix before the first '-' or '_' from the 'UnitNo' attribute (e.g., 'CH001-MAIN' → 'CH001'). All operations are batched over geopackages and executed natively via PyQGIS in standalone mode.

name: Generate cross-sectional profiles along river axis
desc: The script processes input survey tracks (e.g., bathymetric or geodetic transects) and a reference river axis line to generate ordered, regularly spaced cross-sectional lines perpendicular to the axis. It computes longitudinal abscissas along the axis, optionally resamples track points at fixed distances (either strictly spaced or preserving original vertices), assigns section IDs, projects points onto the axis-aligned geometry, and imports elevation values from a DEM to attribute each section with terrain height (e.g., 'zfond'). The final output is a vector layer of oriented section lines, ordered by section ID, with geometry, abscissa, and DEM-derived elevation attributes.

name: Interpolate cross-section lines
desc: The script interpolates a regular grid of cross-sectional lines along a river axis using input cross-section polylines, a centerline (axis), and optional constraint lines. It first converts input sections to points, then interpolates new points at specified longitudinal (m) and lateral (m) spacing relative to the axis, preserving section identification via 'sec_id' and longitudinal abscissa ('abs_long'); finally, it reconstructs interpolated cross-section lines from the ordered points grouped by 'abs_long' and sorted by point ID ('p_id'), outputting a vector layer of interpolated line features aligned with the river's geometry.

name: Interpolate cross-section points
desc: The script interpolates point-based river cross-section data along a defined axis line to generate a regularly spaced, densified set of 3D points (with elevation and optional layer attributes) for hydraulic modeling. It refactors input section points to conform to TatooineMesher’s expected field schema (e.g., 'Zzfond', 'Zlayer1'), optionally merges and augments constraint lines (including left/right bank envelopes derived from section ordering), then invokes an external Python CLI ('densify_cross_sections.py') to perform longitudinal and lateral interpolation using user-specified step sizes (in meters). The output is a shapefile of interpolated points with geometry and Z-attributes, reprojected to match the input sections’ CRS.

name: Generate cross-sectional profile lines and points
desc: The script prepares hydrographic survey inputs for PreCourlis modeling by georeferencing and projecting vector layers (hydro-axis, survey tracks), importing them with a DEM to generate perpendicular cross-sectional profile lines spaced every 100 m along the axis, then converting those lines into point features (e.g., for elevation sampling). It also adds a sedimentological layer attribute ('zfond') to the profile lines. Key outputs are: (1) a GeoJSON file of profile lines (profiles_lines.geojson), (2) a GML file of profile points (profiles_points.gml), (3) a modified georeference file (test.georef), and (4) projected shapefiles (axeHydroBief1.shp, tracesBief1.shp, riveDroiteBief1.shp, riveGaucheBief1.shp) all in EPSG:27563.

name: Analyze GNSS receiver noise
desc: The script calculates the positional noise of a GNSS receiver in steady (stationary) state by computing the centroid, standard deviations in x and y directions (σx, σy), and the Distance Root Mean Square (DRMS) from a set of input point features. It outputs a centroid point layer and a circular polygon layer centered at the centroid with radius equal to DRMS, annotated with DRMS, std_x, and std_y values.

name: Create polygon with holes
desc: The script takes an outer polygon layer and a set of inner polygon layers (holes) and constructs a single QgsPolygon geometry where the inner polygons are defined as holes within the outer polygon. It processes the first feature from the outer polygon source as the exterior ring and iterates over all features in the holes source to extract their outer rings as interior rings (holes), then creates a new QgsPolygon object and writes it to the output sink.

name: Convert geometries to normalized segments
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm converts input line or polygon vector layers into a new line layer where each feature is a normalized segment—oriented with origin at the westernmost point, or southernmost if tied. For polygons, it extracts boundary segments; for lines, it breaks them into constituent edge segments. Optionally removes duplicate geometries to ensure segment unicity. The output retains original attributes and is renamed with '-Segments' (and '-Unicity' if enabled).

name: Assess raster surface accuracy
desc: The script assesses the absolute accuracy of a digital surface model (raster) by comparing its elevation values against ground control points from a CSV file containing x, y, z coordinates. It loads the CSV as point geometry, samples raster values at each point location, computes absolute vertical error (|z_point - z_raster|), calculates the root-mean-square error (EMQ), classifies accuracy into A–D categories based on EMQ thresholds (1.67, 3.33, 4.0, 5.0), and outputs a point layer with error attributes and error-based symbology.

name: Compute raster comparison error zones
desc: The script computes pairwise spatial intersections of raster bounding boxes, generates 200m-spaced point grids within each intersection polygon, samples pixel values from the two overlapping rasters at each point, calculates the root mean square error (RMSE) of differences between corresponding pixel values, and outputs vector polygon layers named after the raster pair with an 'Eqz' (error) attribute. All output layers are grouped under 'Saída Script' in the QGIS project.

name: Displace buildings away from roads
desc: The script displaces building point features away from road line features to maintain a minimum safe distance (32.5 meters) while respecting a maximum allowable displacement (user-defined, default 100 units). It iterates over each building vertex, computes its closest point on nearby road segments, and adjusts the vertex coordinates outward along the perpendicular direction to satisfy the minimum distance constraint; if the resulting displacement exceeds the user-specified maximum, the original location is retained. The output is a new point layer of displaced buildings, styled with a QML file ('edificacoes.qml').

name: Detect line geometry discontinuities
desc: The script detects topological errors in line vector layers relative to a polygon boundary (moldura). It creates a buffer around the polygon boundary, then identifies: (1) disconnected line segments with matching 'nome' attribute whose endpoints fall within the buffer and are within a user-defined tolerance distance; and (2) adjacent line segments with mismatched 'nome' attributes whose endpoints lie within the buffer. Errors are output as point features labeled with descriptive error types ('Erro de geometria desconectada', 'Erro de geometrias conectadas com conjuntos de atributos distintos'). Input parameters include moldura (polygon), linhas (line), tolerance (distance threshold), and buffer distance.

name: Extract overlapping boundary intersections
desc: The script processes two polygon vector layers—'Camada de Edificações' (buildings) and 'Camada de Molduras' (boundaries)—to identify overlapping line geometries between boundaries, then buffers each building by a user-defined distance and computes intersections between those buffers and the overlapping boundary lines. The output is a vector layer containing line features resulting from these intersections, filtered to retain only LineString geometries.

name: Export land cover dataset
desc: The script exports georeferenced image-label patch pairs from a raster layer and vector layer defining ROIs (regions of interest). It rasterizes vector features (e.g., land cover classes) into binary or class-coded masks aligned with the input raster, then extracts non-overlapping or strided windows (patches) of specified size from both raster and mask layers. Patches are saved as NumPy arrays (.npy) in separate 'images' and 'labels' subdirectories. The workflow uses QGIS Processing's gdal:rasterize algorithm, rasterio for low-level I/O and windowed reads, and a custom database (ROIs database file) to query bounding boxes intersecting the raster extent.

name: Load raster images from dataset
desc: The script loads raster images referenced in a vector layer's attribute field (IMAGE_ATTRIBUTE) into QGIS, optionally grouping them by a user-defined expression (GROUP_EXPRESSION) and organizing them under a 'Dataset Images' layer group. It supports filtering by selected features, extent, and prevents duplicate loading when UNIQUE_LOAD is enabled. Outputs are the IDs of the loaded QgsRasterLayer instances.

name: Visualize network kernel density
desc: The script computes and visualizes network-constrained kernel density estimation (NKDV) for input point features (e.g., traffic incidents, crime events, or service locations) along a road network. It downloads or loads an OpenStreetMap-based street graph, projects points onto the nearest edges, splits edges into uniform-length segments (lixels), computes density values per lixel using a configurable kernel (Gaussian, Triangular, Epanechnikov, or Quartic), and outputs a styled GeoPackage layer where each lixel segment is colored by its computed density value — enabling fast, accurate, and cartographically refined density visualization on transportation networks.

name: Visualize temporal kernel density on road networks
desc: The script performs Network Temporal Kernel Density Visualization (NTKDV) on point event data (e.g., traffic incidents, GPS traces) projected onto OpenStreetMap-derived road networks. It partitions road edges into lixels (linear pixels), computes spatiotemporal kernel density estimates using Epanechnikov or Quartic kernels across user-defined time slices (either uniformly spaced or manually specified), and outputs a series of styled GeoPackage/Shapefile layers — one per time slice — where each lixel is attributed with its density value and rendered with Turbo color ramp and graduated line symbology in QGIS. The workflow includes automatic time parsing, network caching, geometry projection, distance computation, and CRS-aware output reprojection to EPSG:4326.

name: Compute spatiotemporal kernel density
desc: The script computes spatiotemporal kernel density estimation (STKDV) on point features with longitude, latitude, and time attributes. It aggregates input point data, converts time to Unix timestamps, filters by user-defined start/end datetime range, applies a spatial-temporal Gaussian kernel with configurable bandwidths (meters for space, days for time), generates per-time-slice raster heatmaps at specified pixel dimensions, applies pseudocolor styling using QGIS color ramps, and adds each raster layer to the QGIS project. Outputs are multiple GeoTIFF raster layers named with timestamps, each representing kernel density values over a geographic grid.

name: Extract elevation precipitation geology
desc: The script extracts environmental attributes at river segment center points by sampling elevation (ELE) from a raster, precipitation (PRE) from another raster, and geology (GEO) from an intersecting polygon layer. It creates a new point layer with these three added attributes, applies blue symbology (3 mm size), and outputs the enriched segment centers layer. The workflow includes raster value sampling via QgsRasterDataProvider.identify(), spatial indexing for polygon intersection, and attribute assignment based on point-in-polygon containment.

name: Interpolate missing Z values on line
desc: The script interpolates missing Z (elevation) values on line Z vector layers in QGIS. It first fills missing Z values at line endpoints via extrapolation using the nearest valid Z values, then linearly interpolates remaining interior missing Z values based on cumulative 3D Euclidean distances along the line. Input is a LineZ layer and a user-defined NoData Z value (default 0); output is a new LineZ layer with all Z values populated where possible. The algorithm handles edge cases (e.g., all-NoData lines or no missing values) and reports processing details per feature via QGIS feedback.

name: Extract elevation from AHN WCS
desc: The script retrieves elevation values from the PDOK AHN WCS service (https://service.pdok.nl/rws/ahn/wcs/v1_0) for each input point feature. It supports two coverages: 'dtm_05m' (Digital Terrain Model) and 'dsm_05m' (Digital Surface Model). For each point, it transforms coordinates to the native CRS of the selected coverage (EPSG:28992), constructs a GetCoverage request for a 2-cell bounding box around the point, downloads the resulting GeoTIFF via GDAL in-memory buffer, reads the pixel value at the point location using geotransform and raster band access, handles NODATA, rounds to 2 decimal places, and appends the elevation as a new double-precision attribute to the output point layer. Output is a point layer with identical geometry and CRS as input, plus the user-specified elevation attribute.

name: Analyze watershed morphometric parameters
desc: The script performs hydrological basin analysis using vector and raster inputs to compute morphometric parameters (e.g., basin area, stream length, slope, hypsometric integral) and their geomorphic interpretations. It clips a DEM to the basin boundary, computes slope statistics, identifies the pour point from the highest-order Strahler stream segments, calculates parameters via external `calculate_parameters()` function, and generates a hypsometric curve with HI and stage classification via `generate_hypsometric_curve()`. Outputs include a point-based attribute table (with Parameter, Value, Unit, Interpretation fields) anchored at the pour point, plus temporary hypsometric curve files (e.g., CSV, plot images) saved in QGIS temp folder. All operations are CRS-consistent, and no remote sensing time-series or satellite-derived indices are computed — inputs are local GIS layers only (not GEE ImageCollections). Study area, time range, satellite data, and explicit geographic names are not specified in the code.

name: Simulate dam flood water depth
desc: The script simulates flood inundation depth by subtracting a DEM's elevation values from a user-specified flood level (defined as DEM minimum + input water level in meters). It optionally clips the DEM to a user-defined study extent, computes per-pixel water depth (zero or positive where elevation < flood level, otherwise NoData), and outputs a raster of water depth. It also reports total flooded area, total water volume, and maximum water depth. The algorithm includes terrain-aware feedback (e.g., warning for elevation ranges >1000 m) and uses native QGIS raster block iteration for memory-efficient processing.

name: Perform kriging interpolation on point data
desc: The script performs geostatistical kriging interpolation on vector point data using Ordinary or Universal Kriging, with configurable variogram models (linear, power, gaussian, spherical, exponential) and presets. It reads point geometry and Z-value attributes, estimates variogram parameters from spatial distances and value variance, constructs a regular grid based on user-defined extent and cell size, executes kriging to produce interpolated surface rasters, applies optional min/max value constraints, and writes the result as a GeoTIFF raster with proper georeferencing and CRS. Outputs include a single raster layer representing the interpolated surface.

name: Calculate point coordinates in multiple formats
desc: The script calculates and adds coordinate information to a point layer in various formats: UTM X/Y in the layer's native CRS, decimal degrees (DD_Lat/DD_Lon), and two Degrees Minutes Seconds variants (DMS_Lat/DMS_Lon and Lat_DMS/Lon_DMS). It supports either modifying the input layer in-place or writing a new output layer. Coordinate transformations use QgsCoordinateTransform from the layer's CRS to EPSG:4326 (WGS84), and DMS conversion functions format latitude/longitude with directional suffixes (N/S/E/W) using precise rounding and zero-padding.

name: Quantify nitrogen and phosphorus purification value
desc: The script calculates the water purification ecosystem service value for nitrogen (NitroPurVal_channel) and phosphorus (PhoshPurVal_channel) removal in river channels, using SWAT+ model output from baseline and restoration scenarios. It computes channel-scale nutrient retention capacity (CWAN/CWAP) via first-order kinetic equations incorporating flow, temperature, and nutrient concentration gradients; ranks top n monthly retention increments per channel (ntop); aggregates the top values to derive mean annual phosphorus and nitrogen purification capacity per channel; and monetizes this capacity using a power-law cost function (149.34 × (capacity/10000)^0.69 × 1000), discounted over life expectancy with actualisation rate, plus annual operation/maintenance costs. Outputs are two vector layers (one per nutrient) joined to the input channel shapefile (rivs1), each containing the monetary valuation per channel feature.

name: Quantify nitrogen and phosphorus purification capacity
desc: The script quantifies the landscape-scale water purification service for nitrogen (NitroPurVal_land) and phosphorus (PhoshPurVal_land) in the Forth catchment, Scotland. It computes the annualized economic value of nutrient removal by comparing baseline (BAU) and restoration (full peat) SWAT+ model scenarios. The workflow extracts SWAT+ monthly output tables (channel_sd_mon, lsunit_nb_mon, lsunit_wb_mon, lsunit_ls_mon) from SQLite databases, calculates nutrient concentrations (CNin, CPin, CNout, CPout) per landscape unit (LSU), derives water purification capacity (CWAN/CWAP) using a temperature-corrected first-order decay model with channel flow and area, ranks top n (ntop) monthly values per LSU, computes mean purification increment (PCWAinc/NCWAinc), and applies an economic valuation formula incorporating actualisation rate, life expectancy, and operation/maintenance costs to generate spatially explicit valuation layers.

name: Geocode address list
desc: The script geocodes a list of addresses from a vector table input using the HERE Geocoding API. It reads an address field, constructs API requests with stored HERE credentials, parses the JSON response to extract location coordinates (lat/lng) and address components (country, city, street, etc.), and outputs a point layer in WGS84 (EPSG:4326) with attributes including original ID, address string, geometry, and quality metrics (relevance, field scores). The algorithm is implemented as a QGIS Processing algorithm named 'Geocode List'.

name: Calculate residential unit capacity per parcel
desc: The script calculates the expected number of residential units (NEW_CAPACITY) and dwelling units per acre (DU_PER_AC) for each parcel based on its zoning classification, parcel attributes (e.g., acres, square footage, transit proximity), and a zoning lookup table. It uses custom domain classes (Zone, Parcel, MBTACalculator) and a zoning-to-parcel mapping function (make_zones) to apply regulatory logic (including optional removal of parking minimums near transit). The output is a vector layer with original parcel geometry and attributes augmented by two new numeric fields.

name: Extract building vertex coordinates
desc: The script processes a vector layer of LOD-1 buildings (polygons or TINZ geometries) to extract all geometry vertices, optionally clip them to a user-defined extent, assign sequential row IDs, transform vertex coordinates from EPSG:3301 (Estonian national coordinate system) to UTM zone 35N (EPSG:32635), and export the resulting point features—including X_UTM, Y_UTM, and optional Z values—as a CSV file with 'row_id' as the first field. It is specifically designed for Estonian national spatial data infrastructure workflows where input is in EPSG:3301 and output requires metric UTM coordinates for downstream building modeling or BIM integration.

name: Rasterize vector layers to topographic masks
desc: The script generates binary (0/1) raster masks from user-selected vector layers, aligned to the spatial extent and resolution of a specified Estonian DTM tile (e.g., '54752_dtm_1m'). It uses GDAL's rasterize tool to burn vector geometries into a fixed-size (4033×4033 pixel) georeferenced TIFF at the DTM’s CRS and extent, then converts each TIFF to an 8-bit grayscale PNG with pixel values scaled to 0–255 (where input geometry = 255, background = 0), optimized for ingestion into Unreal Engine. Output PNGs are named after the source vector layer names and saved to a user-specified folder.

name: Extract road vertex coordinates
desc: The script processes one or more input vector line layers representing roads, standardizes their attribute schemas (resolving string field length inconsistencies across layers), merges them, removes duplicate geometries, extracts all vertices of the resulting road lines, assigns a unique row ID to each vertex, computes UTM X and Y coordinates (transforming from EPSG:3301 — Estonian Coordinate System 1997 — to EPSG:32635 — WGS84 UTM zone 35N), and exports the final vertex table as a CSV with columns ordered as ['row_id', 'X_UTM', 'Y_UTM'] followed by all original attributes. The output is a georeferenced point CSV suitable for downstream spatial analysis or integration into GIS databases.

name: Download and process DEM
desc: The script downloads a digital elevation model (DEM) from either NASA's APEX/Appeears API (for ASTER GDEM V003) or OpenTopography's global DEM API, based on an input polygon extent with optional buffering. It supports multiple DEM products including SRTM, AW3D30, COP30, EU_DTM, and ASTGTM_V003. If 'Add Geoid' is enabled, it applies EGM96 geoid correction by sampling the geoid value at the raster center and adding it to the DEM using GDAL Raster Calculator. Outputs a GeoTIFF DEM file, optionally geoid-corrected.

name: Generate drone flight plans
desc: The script generates two distinct drone flight plans (KMZ and related files) for DJI Matrice 400 (Zenmuse L2 sensor, double-grid pattern, 20 m spacing) and DJI Mavic 3M (single-line grid, default 50 m AGL or 85 m DTM-following altitude), both centered on a user-provided coordinate. It renames the Mavic 3M output files with '_M3M' suffix, removes redundant L2 boundary/points/GPX/report files, and rewrites the Mavic report filename to include '_M3M_report'. Outputs are written to a user-specified folder as KMZ, KML, GeoPackage, GPX, and TXT report files.

name: Dissolve distribution area by biodiversity field
desc: The script dissolves vector polygon features representing species distribution areas from EASIN data based on user-selected attribute fields (e.g., 'specie', 'country', 'provider'). It uses QGIS's native:dissolve algorithm to merge adjacent or overlapping geometries sharing identical values in the specified biodiversity field(s), producing a simplified, aggregated vector layer of dissolved distribution zones.

name: Calculate environmental statistics for species distribution
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, median, standard deviation, etc.) of an environmental raster variable (e.g., temperature, altitude, precipitation) over polygon features representing species distribution. It uses QGIS's native zonal statistics algorithm with configurable band selection and field name prefixing. Inputs include a vector layer of species distribution (polygon), an environmental raster (single or multi-band), a selected band, and a custom field name prefix; output is the input vector layer augmented with statistical fields.

name: Identify flood-prone buildings
desc: The script identifies buildings potentially at risk of flooding by buffering rivers by 150 meters, computing building centroids, extracting those centroids that intersect the river buffer, and sampling elevation (DTM) values at those buffered building locations. Outputs are: (1) a vector layer of building centroids within the flood buffer zone ('Estrazione'), and (2) a point layer with sampled DTM elevation values ('Campionato_valore') for further flood depth or vulnerability analysis.

name: Estimate floodwater depth
desc: The script estimates floodwater depth by subtracting a clipped DEM from a distance-transformed flood boundary raster: (1) clips the input DEM to the flood polygon extent; (2) converts the flood polygon to polylines; (3) rasterizes those polylines; (4) extracts DEM elevation values along the rasterized boundary; (5) computes Euclidean distance from the boundary to interior cells using GRASS r.grow.distance; (6) calculates gross water depth as the difference between the distance-derived surface (interpreted as water surface elevation proxy) and the underlying DEM; (7) applies a Gaussian filter to smooth the resulting depth raster; and outputs a filtered flood depth raster (waterDepthFiltered.sdat). The methodology assumes inland riverine flooding and relies on topographic gradients to infer water surface slope from the inundation boundary.

name: Identify basin areas using slope-based concave hulls
desc: The script identifies potential basin areas by first applying a slope high-pass filter to a digital slope raster (e.g., derived from DEM), then sampling filtered slope values at regularly spaced points within a user-defined extent, and finally generating concave and convex hulls around points where the filtered slope equals 1 (i.e., steep terrain). It outputs reclassified slope rasters, sampled point shapefiles, and polygon shapefiles (concave/convex hulls) enriched with zonal statistics (e.g., mean, max slope) — enabling identification of topographically enclosed low-lying areas partially bordered by inclined terrain.

name: Import flood damage data
desc: The script imports geospatial vector data from remote flatgeobuf sources (hosted at https://storage.googleapis.com/skadesokonomi-dk-data/) into a PostgreSQL database, using QGIS Processing framework. It reads layer metadata from 'fdlayers.json', selects layers by user choice (e.g., based on 'dbkode', 'adresse', and 'provider'), clips them spatially using 'native:extractbylocation' against a user-provided polygon layer, writes results to PostgreSQL tables with auto-generated schema/table names derived from parameter table entries, creates spatial indexes, and optionally loads resulting layers into QGIS. Outputs include updated PostgreSQL tables and optionally opened QGIS layers.

name: Classify flood depth pixels
desc: The script converts a flood depth raster layer into vector polygons where each polygon represents a group of contiguous raster pixels with identical (rounded) depth values. It applies optional unit conversion (cm → m), classification binning (rounding to nearest multiple of a user-defined cm threshold), and optionally merges adjacent pixels into larger polygons. The resulting polygons are exported to a PostgreSQL database table with standardized field names (e.g., 'vanddybde_m' for depth in meters, 'geom' for geometry), and metadata (schema/table name, primary key, depth field, geometry field) is registered in an admin parameter table ('fdc_admin.parametre') for downstream flood damage cost modeling.

name: Convert flood depth raster to polygon pixels
desc: The script converts a user-provided flood depth raster layer into vector polygons (one per pixel), rescales depth values (centimeters → meters if specified), names the output PostgreSQL table using a dynamically constructed string combining return period, year, climate scenario, and optional suffix, imports the polygons into a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database schema, and updates administrative parameter tables in the same database to register the new flood dataset’s geometry, primary key, and depth field names for downstream flood damage cost modeling.

name: Convert vector layer to MUTM
desc: The script converts a QGIS vector layer from any UTM or projected CRS to Nepal Modified UTM (MUTM) using either a 7-parameter Helmert or 3-parameter Molodensky datum shift. It exports the input layer to a temporary shapefile, applies the selected transformation via an external converter module, packages the result into a ZIP file containing the reprojected shapefile, and loads the output layer into the QGIS canvas. The output includes metadata such as MUTM zone, feature count, method used, and source CRS.

name: Export layer bounding boxes
desc: The script exports a vector layer named 'Extents' containing polygon bounding boxes and metadata (layer name, CRS, source path, geometry type, feature count) for all vector and raster layers currently loaded in the QGIS project. It constructs an in-memory memory layer with predefined fields, iterates over project layers, computes extents (using layer extent for spatial layers or map canvas extent for non-spatial layers), populates features with metadata, and writes the result to a user-specified output vector file using QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormatV2.

name: Detect pond depressions in DEM
desc: The script detects topographic depressions (ponds/sinks) in a digital elevation model (DEM) raster by applying a sink-filling algorithm, computes pond depth as the difference between filled and original DEM, polygonizes valid depth areas (depth > MIN_DEPTH), filters polygons by minimum area, assigns unique IDs (PONDid), and calculates key hydro-geomorphic attributes: maximum/minimum pond elevation (PONDRLmax/PONDRLmin), pond volume (PONDvolume = DEPTH_sum × pixel_area), depth statistics (DEPTH_sum, DEPTH_mean, DEPTH_max), and pond area (PONDarea); outputs include a vector layer of pond outlines with rich attribute table and optional filled/depth rasters.

name: Resample Copernicus land cover to 1km
desc: The script resamples Copernicus Global Land (CGLS) vegetation biophysical products (e.g., NDVI, FAPAR, LAI) from native 333 m resolution to 1 km resolution while preserving the spatial extent and temporal consistency of existing 1 km time series. It applies two parallel resampling workflows: (1) 'average' resampling for continuous variables (e.g., NDVI), including scaling and georeferenced cropping to a global bounding box (−180° to 180° longitude, −60° to 80° latitude); and (2) 'mode' resampling for categorical or discrete land cover values, applied after reclassification using a user-defined lookup table (e.g., '[-0.08,0.92,1,0.92,255,0]'). The outputs are combined via raster multiplication ('A@1 * B@1') and exported as a compressed GeoTIFF. The script is designed specifically for Copernicus PROBA-V (pre-July 2020) and Sentinel-3 (post-July 2020) vegetation products, with explicit handling of resampling method selection and reclassification logic. Study area is global (fixed bounding box), no temporal filtering is performed — input raster is assumed pre-selected. Final output is a single resampled GeoTIFF at 1 km resolution.

name: Dissolve features by attribute and sum field
desc: The script performs a dissolve operation on vector features based on a user-selected attribute field, then computes the sum of values from another user-selected numeric field for each dissolved group. It uses QGIS Processing's native:dissolve algorithm, aggregates sums via Python dictionary accumulation, and outputs a new vector layer with dissolved geometries and summed attributes.

name: Generate points inside polygons
desc: The script generates point features at raster pixel centroids that fall within input polygon geometries. It uses GDAL to read raster geotransform information, computes bounding box-aligned pixel indices for each polygon, converts pixel coordinates to map coordinates, and tests point-in-polygon containment using QgsGeometry's prepared geometry engine. The output is a point vector layer with attributes 'id', 'poly_id', and 'point_id', created via QgsFeatureSink in the raster's CRS.

name: Calculate urban heat island extent
desc: The script prepares geospatial inputs for urban heat island (UHI) analysis by organizing raster data (LST, DEM, land cover, soil texture, canopy height, hydrologic soil group, LCZ) and computing the calculation extent from Landsat-derived LST imagery. It extracts EPSG and city name from folder structure, reorganizes input files into data/results subfolders, matches rasters by keywords and EPSG, transforms the LST raster extent to EPSG:4326, and constructs a parameter dictionary for the 'ExtractionDuFichierCsvPourOutilIa' QGIS processing algorithm — which outputs a CSV file containing UHI-related metrics.

name: Identify wetland areas near streams
desc: The script identifies wetland areas adjacent to water streams by buffering stream vector layers, intersecting or differencing with a consolidated ecosystem layer (CEL), and optionally filtering the CEL to retain only specific land-cover classes (e.g., 'Buèiny', 'Lužní a mokøadní lesy', 'Mìstské zelené plochy'). It performs geometry correction, clipping to stream extent, dissolution of fields, buffering of streams, and field difference operations. The final output is a vector layer named 'mokrad' representing wetland-like areas around watercourses, added to the QGIS project.

name: Generate tree line contours based on slope-dependent spacing
desc: The script generates contour-based tree lines (treelines) for anti-erosion measures by iteratively computing isolines from a digital elevation model (DEM), calculating 3D distances between successive isolines, estimating local slope, and dynamically adjusting inter-line spacing using three slope-dependent distance thresholds (A/B/C). It processes field-block vector layers clipped to DEM extent, separates polygons, computes elevation-specific contours, samples points along contours, calculates shortest 3D distances between isolines, validates geometry, simplifies and offsets lines, and merges final treeline outputs into a single GeoPackage. Outputs include validated treeline geometries, intermediate calculation folders (contours, points, shortest lines, buffers, simplified/offset lines), error logs, and a consolidated 'all_layers.gpkg'.

name: Generate stratified random validation plots
desc: The script generates a Collect Earth Online (CEO) upload CSV of stratified random plots from user-provided PFF forest and primary forest rasters. It constructs a three-class stratum raster (0=non-forest, 1=forest_only, 2=primary) by summing binary forest and primary rasters, samples specified numbers of pixels per stratum using numpy random sampling, converts pixel centers to WGS84 coordinates via GDAL geotransform and optional QgsCoordinateTransform, and writes a CSV with PLOTID, CENTER_LON, CENTER_LAT, and optionally STRATUM. It optionally outputs a sidecar CSV with stratum pixel counts and area (ha/kha) for area-weighted accuracy analysis.

name: Compute primary forest area statistics
desc: The script computes total and per-zone area (in kha) for binary raster layers representing primary forest, pre-connectivity forest, and input forest. It uses GDAL to read rasters, QGIS processing algorithms to reproject and rasterize vector zones, and NumPy to mask and sum pixels equal to 1. Outputs include a CSV table with per-zone or total area values and optionally a vector layer joined with area statistics.

name: Generate aspect-slope composite map
desc: The script computes aspect and slope rasters from an input DEM, reclassifies both into ordinal categories (aspect into 8 cardinal directions + 'no preference' label; slope into 5 gradient classes), sums the reclassified rasters to produce a combined aspect-slope index raster (values 10–88), and applies a user-selected, aspect-preference-driven color ramp for visualisation — resulting in a single pseudo-colored raster layer named 'Aspect-Slope – [preference]' with custom interpolated color mapping. Intermediate outputs include optional standalone aspect and slope rasters.

name: Generate scaled STL terrain models
desc: Generates one or more STL (stereolithography) 3D printable files from a digital elevation model (DEM) raster layer, where each STL corresponds to a feature in an input vector layer (e.g., polygons representing administrative units or land parcels); the script clips the DEM by each vector feature, computes a uniform scale factor ensuring all resulting terrain models fit within the user-specified 3D printer bed dimensions (accounting for line width resolution), and exports scaled, base-included STLs with configurable model height and base thickness.

name: Generate scaled STL terrain models
desc: The script generates one or more 3D printable STL files from a digital elevation model (DEM) raster layer, clipped and scaled to fit within user-specified total width and length constraints (in mm), using vector features (e.g., polygons) to define individual model boundaries. Each STL is generated with uniform model height and base thickness, and all models are proportionally downscaled by a single global scale factor computed from the merged extent of all clipped rasters — ensuring their combined footprint fits the target print bed dimensions while respecting the user’s 3D printer line width. Outputs are STL files saved to a user-specified folder.

name: Analyze urban heat island intensity
desc: The script computes urban heat island (UHI) intensity by calculating the temperature difference between urban grid cells (from TARGET model output files named *_<gid>_UMEP_TARGET.txt) and rural reference data (from _metdata_UMEP.txt), then aggregates results using user-specified statistics (mean, max, median, 75th/95th percentile) over a vector polygon grid. It optionally rasterizes the statistical results to a GeoTIFF and/or appends them as attributes to the input polygon layer. Input includes TARGET model run folder, polygon grid with ID field, time-of-day filtering (diurnal/daytime/nighttime), and optional single-night analysis.

name: Analyze urban heat island effect
desc: The script computes urban heat island (UHI) intensity by calculating the difference between UWG-modeled urban air temperature and rural reference temperature during nighttime hours, then aggregates results spatially using a user-provided polygon grid. It supports multiple statistical measures (mean, max, median, 75th/95th percentile) over specified date ranges or single nights, outputs a raster grid of UHI statistics, and optionally appends results to the input polygon layer's attribute table.

name: Generate Digital Surface Model
desc: The script generates a Digital Surface Model (DSM) by combining a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) raster with building height information from either a user-provided polygon layer (with numeric height field) or OpenStreetMap (OSM) building footprints. It performs coordinate system validation, extent clipping, zonal statistics to extract terrain elevation under buildings, computes building height above sea level (height_asl), sorts polygons by height to prevent lower buildings from overwriting higher ones during rasterization, and rasterizes the sorted polygons onto a DEM-aligned grid. Outputs include a DSM raster (OUTPUT_DSM) and optionally an OSM-derived shapefile (OUTPUT_POLYGON) with cleaned large polygons removed.

name: Calculate urban morphometric parameters
desc: The script calculates urban morphometric parameters—including roughness length (z0), displacement height (zd), plan area index (pai), frontal area index (fai), mean building height (zH), maximum building height (zHmax), and standard deviation of building height (zHstd)—from digital surface models (DSM/DEM) and vector polygon grids. It supports multiple roughness calculation methods (e.g., Raupach, Bottema, MacDonald), directional (anisotropic) and isotropic analysis, optional wall area index (wai) computation, and SUEWS/SS-specific parameters (e.g., vegetation/building height partitioning, scaling factors). Outputs include per-grid ASCII text files (anisotropic and isotropic), an aggregated isotropic summary file, and optional attribute table updates in the input polygon layer.

name: Calculate urban morphometric parameters
desc: The script calculates urban morphometric parameters (e.g., zH, fai, pai, z0, zd, wai) from DSM/DEM rasters centered on a user-defined point or point layer feature. It performs raster clipping around the point of interest, computes directional and isotropic morphometric indices using image-based morphometric algorithms, applies multiple roughness length calculation methods (e.g., Raupach, MacDonald), and outputs text files with anisotropic and isotropic parameter tables, plus optional output vector layers for the point and buffer polygon. Inputs include DSM (with/without ground), DEM, optional building-only DSM, search distance, wind direction interval, and roughness method selection.

name: Calculate land cover fractions
desc: The script calculates land cover fractions (e.g., Paved, Buildings, EvergreenTrees, DecidiousTrees, Grass, Baresoil, Water, plus optional IrrGrass and Concrete) for each polygon in an input vector grid layer, using a UMEP-formatted land cover raster. It supports two search methods: centroid-based circular buffer (with configurable distance) or polygon-envelope clipping, and optionally computes directional (anisotropic) fractions at user-defined wind-direction intervals. Outputs include per-grid ASCII text files with directional fractions, an isotropic summary file, and optional attribute table updates to the input polygon layer.

name: Calculate land cover fractions from point
desc: The script calculates anisotropic and isotropic land cover fractions (e.g., Paved, Buildings, EvergreenTrees, DecidiousTrees, Grass, Baresoil, Water, plus optional IrrGrass and Concrete) within a user-defined radius around a point location using a UMEP-formatted land cover raster grid. It clips the raster to the search radius, applies angular sector-based aggregation (by wind direction interval), computes class fractions per sector and overall, and outputs two text files (anisotropic and isotropic fractions), plus optional vector layers for the point of interest and circular study area polygon.

name: Generate tree canopy and trunk DSM
desc: The script generates 3D vegetation raster layers—Canopy Digital Surface Model (CDSM) and Trunk Zone DSM (TDSM)—from a point vector layer containing tree attributes (type, total height, trunk height, diameter) and optional raster inputs (building grid, DSM, DEM, existing CDSM/TDSM). It uses the makevegdems.vegunitsgeneration function to synthesize tree geometry per point, rasterizes them onto a common grid aligned with input rasters, enforces unit consistency (meters or feet), validates CRS alignment between vector and raster layers, checks pixel resolution compatibility, and outputs two georeferenced rasters: CDSM_GRID_OUT and TDSM_GRID_OUT.

name: Prepare UWG urban weather input
desc: The script prepares Urban Weather Generator (UWG) input files for urban heat island modeling by processing polygon grids, intersecting them with building type layers, reading land cover and morphology data from text files, computing urban parameters (e.g., building height, density, vegetation fractions), mapping climate zones, and generating per-grid UWG configuration files in the specified output directory.

name: Calculate urban wind field
desc: The script calculates 3D spatial variations of wind speed and direction in an urban context using 2.5D building and vegetation vector data. It accepts building polygons with roof height attributes and/or vegetation polygons with crown base/top height and wind attenuation attributes; applies a vertical wind profile (power law, urban, or user-defined CSV); discretizes the domain using horizontal and vertical resolutions; performs physics-based wind flow modeling (via external Java-based solver in MainCalculation.main); and outputs 2D wind speed rasters/vectors at specified heights and/or 3D wind fields in NetCDF format. Outputs include georeferenced rasters, vector layers styled with predefined QGIS styles, metadata files (RunInfoURock_*.txt), and optional loading into QGIS.

name: Compute effective mesh size
desc: The script computes ecological fragmentation metrics—primarily Effective Mesh Size (MESH_SIZE), CBC-effective Mesh Size (CBC_MESH_SIZE), Landscape Division (DIVI), Splitting Index (SPLI), Coherence (COH), Splitting Density (SDEN), and Net Product (NPRO)—from vector land cover and fragmentation layers. It processes input layers through clipping, selection, buffering, and overlay operations (e.g., difference, intersection, dissolve, multi-to-single part), rasterizes vector data with an ALL_TOUCH fix when needed, and aggregates patch-level geometry statistics per reporting unit. Outputs include a vector layer with computed metrics per feature (or globally) and optional variation layers from pairwise metric differences.

name: Generate hillshade and contour lines
desc: The script computes a hillshade raster from an input digital elevation model (DEM) using azimuth 300° and vertical angle 40°, then derives contour lines at 10-unit elevation intervals from the hillshade output (though note: contouring is incorrectly applied to the hillshade raster instead of the original DEM, which is a logical flaw; the intended purpose remains topographic visualization and line extraction). Outputs are a hillshade raster ('hill') and a vector line layer of contours ('contour').

name: Identify illegal mining areas
desc: The script identifies illegal mining areas in the Amazon rainforest using RGB satellite imagery from Planet and a pre-trained U-Net model with MobileNetV2 encoder. It reads the input raster, crops it into 128×128 patches, normalizes pixel values to [0,1], performs inference using TensorFlow's saved_model, aggregates predictions via overlapping patch averaging, applies a 0.5 threshold to generate a binary mask, and writes the output as a GeoTIFF raster with original georeferencing. The output is a binary prediction mask indicating locations with evidence of illegal mining.

name: Generate hachure points from DEM
desc: The script generates a vector point layer where each point lies along elevation contours extracted from a DEM, with attributes for elevation (ELEV), contour ID (ID), distance along contour (distance), contour direction (angle), slope steepness (slope_1), and aspect direction (aspect_1); these attributes are used in QGIS geometry generator styling to render monochrome hachure lines perpendicular to contours, with length modulated by slope and opacity modulated by aspect (simulating hillshading from north).

name: Adjust raster geotransform by pixel shift
desc: The script manually shifts a raster image's geotransform in X (longitude) and Y (latitude) directions by user-specified pixel offsets without resampling. It either overwrites the input file in place (updating only the geotransform header via GDAL GA_Update) or writes a new file using GDAL CreateCopy, adjusting the top-left corner coordinates based on pixel size and input shifts. The algorithm handles ENVI driver quirks and removes auxiliary .aux.xml files. Output is a georeferenced raster with shifted alignment.

name: Extract SAM2 image features
desc: The script encodes raster imagery using the SAM2 (Segment Anything Model 2) vision encoder to generate deep visual features — specifically 'image_embed' and 'high_res_feats' — for geospatial analysis. It supports input rasters of arbitrary size, automatically resampling to target CRS/resolution, computing band statistics for value rescaling, and processing either full images (<1024×1024) or tiled patches (≥1024×1024) via GDAL. Outputs include GeoTIFFs of encoded features with georeferenced metadata (bounding box, CRS, transform), CSV index files tracking patch geometry and parameters, and a JSON log of all algorithm inputs and project settings. The workflow integrates QGIS Processing Framework, PyTorch, GDAL, rasterio, and pyproj.

name: Classify covariates into percentiles
desc: The script classifies a numeric field in a vector polygon layer into percentile-based classes (e.g., quartiles or deciles) using numpy's percentile function. It computes bin thresholds, adds a new integer field to the input layer, assigns class labels based on which bin the original field value falls into, and commits the edits. The output is the CRS of the modified layer, and the layer is reloaded in the QGIS project.

name: Clean point inventory using slope raster
desc: The script cleans a point inventory layer by filtering points based on local slope values extracted from a raster. It resamples the input raster to match a user-defined extent, counts point density per pixel, applies a moving window maximum filter over slope values with a buffer radius in pixels, masks out pixels where slope is below a user-defined minimum threshold or where no points exist, and outputs a cleaned point vector layer containing only points falling within valid (non-masked) pixels.

name: Sample point locations within polygon
desc: The script performs spatial sampling of input point features within a user-defined contour polygon mask.
