It outputs a new memory vector layer named 'segmented_lines_with_intersections' containing the segmented lines and a Boolean attribute 'intersects' indicating whether each segment's buffer intersects the reference layer.

name: Export polygon features as shapefiles
desc: The script exports individual polygon features from the active QGIS vector layer into separate GeoJSON-formatted shapefiles, named sequentially with a base prefix '\no_s_' and incrementing numeric suffix starting at 30. Each feature is written to a new memory-based QgsVectorLayer with CRS EPSG:4612 (JGD2011), then saved using QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormat with UTF-8 encoding and GeoJSON driver. The output path is hardcoded to 'C:\Users\kyohe\ishikawa_QGISimageclipPolygon\0102\SamePolygonSize_areaO\PolygonSHP_nodamage'.

name: Split polygon features by ID
desc: The script splits a single QGIS vector layer named 'sq_test' into individual GeoJSON FeatureCollection files (saved as .fgb), each containing one feature from the original layer. It iterates over all features in the layer, creates a new in-memory polygon layer for each feature, adds that feature to it, and writes it to disk with sequentially numbered filenames (e.g., 'a13_rotated_test_0.fgb', 'a13_rotated_test_1.fgb'). The output CRS is EPSG:4612 (JGD2000 / Japan Plane Rectangular CS XIII), and the input layer is assumed to be loaded in the current QGIS project.

name: Align clipped road buffer images
desc: The script processes vector polygon layers (in .fgb format) representing road buffers, clips a specified raster layer ('a1_clipped') to each polygon using GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer algorithm, rotates the clipped TIFF image to align with the polygon's dominant edge orientation (computed from the first and fourth vertices), converts it to PNG with alpha transparency, crops to the bounding box of non-transparent pixels, and saves the result. Outputs are aligned, cropped PNG images named after each input .fgb file.

name: Detect points inside damaged polygons
desc: The script detects which point features from a QGIS vector layer ('suzu_all') fall within each polygon in a set of .fgb files located in the 'Damaged' subdirectory. It records the mapping between each polygon filename and the FIDs of contained points into a CSV file. Additionally, it clips raster layers (TIF) using each polygon as a mask and saves rotated/cropped PNG outputs aligned to polygon edge orientation. The core geospatial operation is QgsGeometry.contains() for point-in-polygon testing.

name: Remove overlapping square polygons at intersections
desc: The script clips intersection node points to the extent of each wide-area aerial raster image, then identifies square polygon layers matching the node layer's identifier (e.g., 'a1', 'a2'), computes Intersection over Union (IoU) between polygons containing the same node, and removes polygons with IoU ≥ 0.7. Outputs are new FlatGeobuf files (e.g., 'SquarePatchPolygons/a1_IntersectionDeleted.fgb') containing only non-overlapping square polygons, saved per raster image in a directory named after the acquisition date ('0105').

name: Generate road-aligned square polygons
desc: The script clips a vector road layer (DRM_suzu_ONLYurban_NOTsunami) to the bounding box of each raster layer in the QGIS project, then generates rotated square polygons centered along each clipped road segment. The square size is determined by the 'R22_005' road width class attribute using a predefined meter-to-degree conversion (1° ≈ 111,000 m), and squares are placed at intervals equal to half the square side length. Output layers are named 'Square_[original_layer_name]' and added to the QGIS project; all results are saved under 'AllPolygon' (implied by comment), and processing timestamps are logged to a text file.

name: Extract intact building patches from aerial imagery
desc: The script processes QGIS raster layers and corresponding square polygon vector layers (in .fgb format) to clip, rotate, and export individual building patches classified as 'Intact' into PNG files. It identifies each raster layer by alphanumeric ID (e.g., 'a13'), matches it with corresponding .fgb files containing single square polygons, computes the rotation angle from polygon edge geometry, clips the raster using GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer, rotates the clipped TIFF to align the square patch upright, crops transparent margins, and saves as PNG. Outputs are rotated, cropped PNG images per polygon, saved in class- and region-specific directories (e.g., Intact/suzu_all), along with timing logs.

name: Split damage-classified polygons
desc: The script splits pre-classified square polygon vector layers (intact, house_collapse, other_damage) into individual FlatGeobuf (.fgb) files per polygon feature. It identifies layers by name patterns (e.g., 'intact', 'house_collapse'), extracts alphanumeric IDs from layer names (e.g., 'a1', 'b2'), iterates over each feature, creates a memory vector layer per feature with copied schema and geometry, and writes each as a separate .fgb file in class-specific output directories. Output paths are constructed using layer ID, damage class, and feature index (e.g., 'a1_Intact_0.fgb').

name: Generate aligned square polygons along road centerlines
desc: The script generates a memory-based polygon layer of rotated, aligned squares spaced at regular intervals (0.0003 degrees) along a clipped road centerline vector layer named 'road_centerline_clipped'. Each square is oriented to match the local tangent angle of the road line at its center point. Adjacent squares are geometrically aligned by translating the current square so that a selected vertex pair (determined by quantizing the angular difference between consecutive squares into 45° bins) coincides, then correcting the center point to ensure precise placement. The output is a new QGIS vector layer '正方形ポリゴン' added to the project.

name: Generate road centerlines from road edges
desc: The script generates road centerlines from road edge data stored in GML-formatted XML files (FG-GML-553656-RdEdg-20230701-0001.xml). It parses GML with namespaces for 'gml' and 'fgd', extracts coordinate lists from <gml:posList> elements within <fgd:RdEdg> features, constructs QgsGeometry polyline features, identifies parallel edge pairs using distance (<10m) and directional similarity (<30° angle difference), computes centerlines by averaging corresponding vertices of paired edges, and saves the resulting centerline LineString features to a FlatGeobuf (.fgb) file with CRS EPSG:6668. Output includes a vector layer named 'Road_Centerlines' with 'id' and 'length' attributes.

name: Generate road centerlines from road edge data
desc: The script reads road edge data from a GML/XML file (FG-GML-553656-RdEdg-20230701-0001.xml) containing Japanese national base map road edge features, parses gml:posList coordinates into QgsPointXY geometries, identifies parallel road edge pairs using distance (<10m) and angular similarity (<30°), computes centerlines by averaging corresponding polyline vertices, and adds the resulting centerline LineString features as a memory layer named 'Road_Centerlines' to the QGIS project with fields 'id' and 'length'.

name: Generate road centerline geometry
desc: The script constructs a simple two-point polyline representing a road centerline using hardcoded QgsPointXY coordinates (136.7302309, 37.1218538) and (136.7314150, 37.1218780), creates a QgsFeature with that LineString geometry, and saves it to a FlatGeobuf (.fgb) file at the specified output path using QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormatV3 with FlatGeobuf driver. No input layers or external data are read; the centerline is synthetically generated.

name: Generate road-aligned square patches
desc: The script generates square polygon patches aligned to road centerlines using width and orientation derived from road attributes (R22_005) and geometry. It reads a road centerline shapefile and a precomputed buffer polygon layer, reprojects the road layer to EPSG:6675, iteratively places squares along each road segment at intervals equal to their width, rotates each square to match the local road angle, and retains only those squares intersecting the buffer layer. Final output is a FlatGeobuf file of squares reprojected to EPSG:4612, saved in the 'SquarePatches' folder.

name: Generate pedestrian walksheds from transit stops
desc: The script generates walkshed polygons (buffered, network-constrained, concave-hull refined, and route-dissolved) for public transit stops using a pedestrian street network. It processes stops grouped by 'rte' (route ID), computes service areas via QGIS native network analysis ('serviceareafromlayer'), refines geometry using convex and concave hulls, clips and dissolves by route, and outputs GeoPackage files for walksheds, dissolved walksheds, and service area lines — all batched to manage memory.

name: Generate transit stop walksheds
desc: The script generates pedestrian catchment areas (walksheds) for public transit stops using a street network dataset. It first buffers all stops at 804.672 meters (½ mile), clips and splits the pedestrian network to that buffered extent, then performs service area analysis (shortest-path network traversal) from each stop to identify reachable network segments within the walking distance. For each route (grouped by 'rte' field), it computes individual walksheds via concave hull refinement of service lines, merges them into route-level dissolved polygons, and outputs three geopackage layers: (1) individual walksheds per stop, (2) dissolved walksheds per route, and (3) the traversed network segments ('service lines'). The workflow relies on QGIS native algorithms including buffer, clip, splitlinesbylength, serviceareafromlayer, convexhull, concavehull, and dissolve.

name: Map freshman source distribution
desc: The script generates a thematic map of freshman student origin locations using QGIS Python bindings. It loads a Chinese provincial administrative boundary shapefile (EPSG:4326), joins it with CSV-based student count data by province name, applies quantile-based graduated color rendering (RdYlBu color ramp) to visualize student counts per province, and exports a layout containing the map, title, legend, north arrow, and scale bar as a PNG image.

name: Map freshman student origins
desc: The script generates a thematic map of freshman student origins using QGIS Python bindings. It loads a Chinese provincial administrative boundary shapefile, joins it with CSV-based student count data by province name, applies graduated color symbology (RdYlBu ramp) based on student counts using quantile classification, and exports the result as a high-resolution PNG image via a print layout containing map, legend, scale bar, and title. Inputs include a shapefile (china.json), a CSV (freshman_source.csv), and outputs are a QGZ project file and a PNG image.

name: Generate thematic map from GeoJSON
desc: The script generates a thematic map from a GeoJSON vector file using PyQGIS, classifying features by a specified attribute field (e.g., 'name') and rendering each unique value with a distinct color. It initializes QGIS, loads the GeoJSON layer, computes unique attribute values, assigns colors via QgsCategorizedSymbolRenderer, sets up a QgsLayout with a map item covering the layer's extent, and exports the layout to a static image (e.g., PNG). The output is a rendered thematic map image.

name: Identify triangle corner points
desc: The script identifies corner points of a triangle formed by a set of input point features using bounding coordinate extremes (min/max x/y). It loads a QGIS vector layer named 'Extracted Points', extracts all point geometries, determines the points with minimum/maximum x and y coordinates, collects them as candidate corners (allowing duplicates to be deduplicated via set), and outputs those points both to console and as a new memory vector layer named 'triangle_corners'. The logic relies solely on coordinate extremum detection—not geometric triangulation or convex hull—and includes two auxiliary functions for collinearity/segment membership testing that are defined but not invoked in the executed workflow.

name: Assess property suitability for energy infrastructure
desc: The script evaluates land parcels in Bendigo, Australia for suitability as energy infrastructure sites by integrating proximity to transmission lines, solar radiation potential, and parcel area—while excluding protected lands, built-up areas, and restricted planning zones. It performs vector-based spatial erasure (multidifference), centroid generation for raster sampling, and lays groundwork for standardized 0–100 suitability scoring across criteria; outputs include an erased property layer (Property_Suitability.gpkg), a point layer of property centroids (Property_Point.gpkg), and intermediate dissolved exclusion layers.

name: Calculate coastal vulnerability index
desc: The script calculates a Coastal Vulnerability Index (CVI) using six geospatial raster inputs: mean tide range (m), mean wave height (m), relative sea-level rise rate (mm/yr), shoreline erosion/accretion rate (m/yr), geomorphology, and coastal slope (%). It first resamples all rasters to align with the geomorphology raster using nearest-neighbor resampling via 'native:alignsingleraster', then computes the CVI as the square root of the product of the six standardized rasters divided by 6 using 'gdal:rastercalculator'. The output is a single floating-point raster representing the Coastal Vulnerability Index.

name: Unify isochrone polygons with derived boundaries
desc: The script processes an input vector layer of isochrone polygons by first converting them to lines, then polygonizing those lines to create new polygons (likely filling gaps or holes), and finally performing a union operation between the original isochrone polygons and the newly polygonized features. The output is a unified vector layer where overlapping or adjacent geometries are merged, preserving all attributes from both inputs, intended to produce a topologically consistent boundary representation of the isochrone area.

name: Compute isochrone polygon union
desc: The script processes isochrone polygons (e.g., travel-time catchments around infrastructure points like water fountains 'fontanelle') to compute a topologically cleaned, area-filtered, and aggregated summary layer. It converts input isochrone polygons to lines, re-polygonizes them to resolve overlaps and slivers, unions them with the original polygons to capture intersections and gaps, filters resulting fragments by minimum area (>1.0 m²), then groups and counts overlapping isochrones per unique area class — assigning a count ('nro') and concatenated list of source IDs ('ids', stripped of 'tp_' prefix) — finally dissolving by 'ids' and removing redundant 'ID' field. The output is a simplified vector layer where each feature represents a spatially contiguous zone sharing the same set of contributing isochrones (e.g., overlapping service areas), with attributes summarizing cardinality and membership.

name: Dissolve classify and label land cover classes
desc: The script processes vector layers representing land cover classification (with DN attribute values 1–5) by dissolving geometries by the 'DN' field, calculating area in hectares, adding descriptive labels based on DN values, and applying a fixed five-class categorical symbology with predefined colors and labels. Outputs are GeoPackage vector layers named '<original_name>_dissolvido.gpkg', added to the QGIS project tree directly above their source layers, with updated attribute tables and rendered styles.

name: Apply NDVI-based discrete pseudocolor styling
desc: The script recuts all raster layers in the QGIS project using a vector mask layer named 'buffer_total', saves the clipped rasters as GeoTIFFs to a specified local directory (G:\Meu Drive\PA458_ByPolygons\final\sem_urb), loads each clipped raster back into the project, inserts it above its original layer in the layer tree, and applies a discrete 5-class NDVI-oriented pseudocolor renderer using band 3 (as defined by BANDA_NDVI = 3) with fixed class breaks and predefined color labels and hex codes. The output includes styled, masked rasters visualized with categories ranging from 'Não-Vegetação/Água' to 'Saudável e Vigoroso'.

name: Classify vegetation health status
desc: The script converts loaded raster layers into vector polygons classified into five vegetation health classes (from 'Não-Vegetação/Água' to 'Saudável e Vigoroso') using equal-interval reclassification of raster band values (band 1 for single-band rasters, band 3 for multi-band rasters), followed by polygonization. It applies a predefined color-coded categorized symbology on the output GeoPackage vector layers based on the 'DN' field and inserts them above their source rasters in the QGIS layer tree. Output files are saved as .gpkg in 'G:\Meu Drive\PA458_ByPolygons\final\sem_urb'.

name: Fix and dissolve polygonized MBES survey shapes
desc: The script processes shapefiles derived from multibeam echosounder (MBES) data: it first fixes invalid geometries (e.g., self-intersections, ring errors) using QGIS's native:fixgeometries algorithm with method '0 — Try to fix geometries (default)', then dissolves all features into single-part polygons per input shapefile (no attribute-based grouping), and finally merges all dissolved shapefiles into a single unified shapefile (abp49_id001-054_merged.shp) in EPSG:32634. The workflow targets vector geometry integrity and topological simplification of seafloor polygon interpretations, not raster analysis or time-series modeling.

name: Dissolve parcels by zoning
desc: The script processes a QGIS vector layer named 'fbc-parcels', dissolving its features based on the 'fbc_zoning' attribute field, then converts the resulting multipart geometries into single-part features. The output is a new in-memory vector layer named 'fbc_large_zones' added to the QGIS project, representing spatially contiguous zones grouped by zoning classification.

name: Reclassify urban typology attributes
desc: The script reclassifies categorical attribute values in a QGIS vector layer (e.g., land cover or urban typology codes) by mapping original field values (e.g., 'Residential', 'Commercial') to standardized typology names and IDs from an internal database ('db_dict['Types']'). It reads a selected vector layer, extracts unique values from a user-specified attribute field, populates up to 22 class-mapping comboboxes (Old Class → New Class), constructs reclassification dictionaries, adds two new fields ('TypolName' as String and 'TypolID' as Integer), applies the mapping to populate those fields, saves the result as a new shapefile, and loads it into the QGIS project. The workflow is triggered via GUI buttons and relies on PyQt and QgsVectorLayer/QgsVectorFileWriter APIs.

name: Reproject raster layer to vector CRS
desc: The script reprojects a raster layer to match the coordinate reference system (CRS) of a given vector layer using GDAL's warpreproject algorithm. It emits progress updates during processing and validates the resulting reprojected raster layer. The workflow includes defining reprojection parameters (source CRS, target CRS, resampling method, nodata value), simulating progress, executing the transformation via processing.run, and emitting the resulting QgsRasterLayer object upon success or None upon failure.

name: Map localist mapper activity zones
desc: The script analyzes OpenStreetMap (OSM) node edit history to identify and map three types of mapper activity per grid cell: (1) '@localist' — mappers with concentrated, locally weighted activity in their core zones (enhanced by neighbor-grid activity thresholds and multiplicative weighting), (2) '@activist' — the most *recently* active mapper per grid (weighted by edit timestamp decay: 1.0 for <1 yr, down to 0.05 for ≥5 yrs), and (3) '@master' — the mapper with the highest raw edit count per grid. It computes grid-level metrics including '@nodecount' (total edits), '@agesum' (time-weighted edit sum), and '@currentness' (normalized time-weighted average). Outputs include updated grid vector layer attributes, a dissolved single-part 'localist' thematic map (grouping contiguous grids sharing the same '@localist'), and an optional CSV user statistics table listing per-user total edits, time-weighted edits, grid coverage, and counts of localist/activist/master grid assignments.

name: Convert vector layer to GPX format
desc: The script converts an input vector layer (points, lines, or polygons) into a GPX file suitable for GPS devices. It first fixes geometries, converts polygons to lines if needed, optionally dissolves non-point features (unless a name field is specified), splits multipart points into singleparts, refactors the attribute table to include a 'name' field (either a static display name or dynamic field value), and writes the result using GDAL’s GPX driver with extensions enabled and forced GPX tracks. The output is a valid GPX file containing waypoints (for points), tracks (for lines), or routes — with metadata conforming to GPX 1.1 schema.

name: Classify urban polygon changes by density type and comparison category
desc: The script performs a combinatorial attribute-based classification and spatial processing of an input vector layer named 'poligonos', filtering features by three categorical fields: 'Densidade' (e.g., 'Densa', 'Pouco densa', 'Loteamento vazio'), 'Tipo' (e.g., 'Área Urbanizada', 'Vazio intraurbano'), and 'Comparacao' (e.g., 'Adição', 'Densificação', 'Subtração'). For each unique combination, it selects matching polygons, executes a spatial self-join (using 'contains' predicate), dissolves the resulting geometries, and splits multi-part polygons into single parts — exporting each result as a separate shapefile named 'poligonos_<Densidade>_<Tipo>_<Comparacao>.shp'. The output is a set of 132 (3×4×11) georeferenced, topologically cleaned, single-part polygon layers representing distinct urban change–density–land use categories.

name: Generate hillslopes and floodplain rasters
desc: The script generates left/right hillslope rasters and valley depth rasters from channel and D8 flow direction rasters using TauDEM and QGIS raster operations; it also generates floodplain rasters via DEM inversion, branch-length analysis, or channel buffering. Key outputs include 'slopes.tif' (hillslope identifiers), 'depths.tif' (valley depths), and buffered or inverted-method floodplain rasters (e.g., 'bufferflood*.tif'). Processing involves clipping rasters with a shapefile, calculating flow accumulation on inverted DEM, identifying channel heads and sides, and propagating elevation-based drainage values.

name: Generate road-based service areas
desc: The script computes network-based allocation zones (subnets) from a point layer (e.g., facilities, substations, or access points) and a road network layer using GRASS v.net.alloc. It then processes the allocated line segments to extract unique vertices per allocation zone, constructs Voronoi polygons from those vertices, and dissolves them by allocation category (cat) to produce contiguous polygonal service areas — each representing the region of the road network closest to a given input point. The output is a vector layer of non-overlapping, topology-aware subnet polygons derived from network distance, not Euclidean distance.

name: Count point features within dissolved polygons
desc: The script dissolves a base polygon layer (e.g., administrative or thematic boundaries) and then, for each selected point layer, subsets points by a categorical field (e.g., land cover type, species ID), counts occurrences per category within each dissolved polygon, outputs individual shapefiles with integer count fields, exports each to CSV, and finally merges all CSVs into a single consolidated CSV file where columns represent counts of distinct point categories per polygon — enabling cross-tabulated spatial aggregation of point data by polygon and attribute class.

name: Generate hillslope and floodplain rasters
desc: The script generates hillslope rasters (left/right hillslopes and headwater areas) and floodplain/upslope area rasters from channel and D8 flow direction rasters using TauDEM-derived hydrological inputs. Key methods include clipping rasters with a mask layer, computing inverted DEM-based ridges via PitFill/D8FlowDir/AreaD8, calculating channel heads and side points via flow tracing, propagating hillslope identifiers and valley depths through drainage paths, and generating floodplain rasters either via buffered channels or DEM inversion. Outputs include 'slopes.tif' (hillslope raster with encoded reach/side identifiers), 'depths.tif' (valley depths), and 'bufferflood*.tif' (floodplain rasters).

name: Convert SU 3D geometry to polygon
desc: The script converts a 3D OBJ mesh file—representing the top surface of an archaeological Stratigraphic Unit (SU)—into two cleaned, attribute-enriched 3D polygon shapefiles: one in local coordinates (e.g., arbitrary site grid) and one georeferenced to EPSG:32632 (UTM zone 32N). It uses Blender (with BlenderGIS addon) in headless mode to import the OBJ and export an initial shapefile; then applies QGIS processing steps—including geometry fixing, dissolving, hole removal, coordinate translation (by fixed delta: ΔX=452000, ΔY=4413000), projection assignment, and field population (Year, Trench = floor(SU/1000)*1000, SU) —to produce final 3D polygon layers for archaeological spatial documentation and integration into GIS projects.

name: Convert 3D OBJ surface to 3D polygon
desc: The script converts a 3D Wavefront OBJ file—representing the top surface of an archaeological Stratigraphic Unit (SU)—into two cleaned, attribute-enriched 3D polygon shapefiles: one in local coordinates (unprojected, retained for internal use) and one projected to EPSG:32632 (UTM zone 32N), with fields 'Year', 'Trench' (derived as floor(SU_number/1000)*1000), and 'SU' (user-provided integer). The workflow uses Blender (via BlenderGIS addon) in headless mode to import the OBJ and export an initial 3D shapefile ('POLYGONZ'), then applies QGIS geometry cleaning steps (fix geometries → dissolve → delete holes → fix again), followed by coordinate translation (ΔX=452000, ΔY=4413000), CRS assignment, and field population. Output files are saved to a user-specified folder and loaded into QGIS for verification.

name: Generate aggregated isochrones for transit accessibility
desc: The script computes multi-temporal isochrones (travel-time polygons) from point locations using the OpenTripPlanner (OTP) routing engine via HTTP API calls. For each input point feature, it iterates over a user-defined datetime range at specified intervals (e.g., every 300 seconds), constructs OTP isochrone request URLs with configurable parameters (mode, walk speed, wheelchair, maxWalkDistance, etc.), downloads zipped shapefile responses, validates geometries, and aggregates results using one of three modes: (1) Max Dissolve (dissolving by time), (2) All Union (spatial union + statistical summary per time bin), or (3) No Agg Raw (individual isochrone polygons per datetime). Outputs a memory vector layer containing all isochrone geometries plus rich metadata attributes — including source feature fields, AggIsochrone_UID/ID, error logs, base URL, datetime range, request interval, requested dates/times, total requests, and time-derived statistics (e.g., time_min, time_mean, time_stddev) — enabling quantitative analysis of temporal accessibility variation.

name: Generate bounded polygons from frame and delimiter layers
desc: The script generates bounded polygon features by using a selected polygon frame layer as the outer boundary and one or more line or polygon delimiter layers to internally partition or constrain the geometry. It merges all delimiter geometries (converting polygon boundaries to lines), dissolves and fixes them, polygonizes the resulting line network, clips the resulting polygons to the frame layer, optionally removes overlaps with input delimiter polygons, and outputs a memory vector layer with fields 'id' (UUID), 'description' (NULL-initialized), and 'area_otf' (area in square meters calculated in EPSG:31985), grouped under 'istools-output' in the QGIS layer tree.

name: Generate polygons from vector layers
desc: The script generates polygons by clicking on the map canvas in QGIS, using visible line and polygon layers from the current project. It collects valid geometries, converts polygon boundaries to lines if needed, runs the 'qgis:polygonize' algorithm on a temporary line layer, identifies the resulting polygon that contains the clicked point, and adds it to a dedicated memory-based output layer named 'Generated Polygons' (translated) within an 'istools-output' layer group. The output layer includes fields for ID, description, and area calculated in EPSG:31985 (SIRGAS 2000 / UTM zone 23S), with red semi-transparent symbology.

name: Convert RGB raster to color-based polygons
desc: The script converts an RGB raster layer named 'map' into a vector layer where each unique RGB color (encoded as R*65536 + G*256 + B) is represented by a single dissolved polygon (i.e., one multipolygon per distinct color). It achieves this by: (1) locating the input raster in the QGIS project; (2) computing a single-band integer raster via raster calculator using band 1 (R), band 2 (G), and band 3 (B) with 8-bit assumptions; (3) polygonizing the resulting integer raster, assigning each pixel’s value to the 'DN' field; (4) dissolving all geometries sharing the same 'DN' value into unified polygons; and (5) adding the final dissolved vector layer named 'map_provinces' to the QGIS project. The output is a thematic vector layer where each feature corresponds to a unique color class — typical for manually digitized or symbolically rendered thematic maps (e.g., land cover legends encoded as RGB pixels).

name: Generate aggregated isochrones for transit accessibility
desc: The script generates aggregated isochrones—polygonal areas representing reachable locations within specified travel times—from point features (e.g., origins like homes or stations) using OpenTripPlanner (OTP) via HTTP API requests. It iterates over user-defined datetime ranges (with configurable intervals), constructs OTP isochrone URLs with parameters including transportation modes (e.g., WALK, TRANSIT), walk/bike speeds, wheelchair accessibility, and precision settings, downloads zipped shapefile responses, processes geometries (fixing, unioning, dissolving), and appends rich metadata to output features—including AggIsochrone_UID, AggIsochrone_ID, AggIsochrone_Error, AggIsochrone_URL, AggIsochrone_From/To datetimes, request interval, requested dates/times, and time-aggregated statistics (e.g., time_mean, time_stddev) depending on selected aggregation mode (MaxDissolve, AllUnion, or NoAggRaw). The output is a memory-based QgsVectorLayer (MultiPolygon, EPSG:4326) with input attributes preserved and new fields appended; no satellite, remote sensing, or Earth observation data is used—the only geospatial input is the user-provided vector layer of origin points, transformed to WGS84. Study area, time range, and data sources are not specified in the code and depend entirely on user configuration and OTP server deployment (e.g., 'https://api.digitransit.fi/routing/v1/routers/hsl/' is shown as an example server URL but is not hardcoded as the active source).

name: Generate hillslope and floodplain rasters
desc: The script generates hillslope rasters (left/right hillslopes and headwater areas) and floodplain/upslope rasters from channel and D8 flow direction rasters using TauDEM and QGIS raster processing. Key methods include clipping rasters with a clipper shapefile, computing inverted DEM-based ridges via PitFill/D8FlowDir/AreaD8, calculating valley depths and hillslope identifiers by tracing flow paths from channel heads and sides, and generating floodplain rasters either via channel buffering or DEM inversion/branch length methods. Outputs include 'slopes' and 'depths' GeoTIFF rasters, buffered floodplain shapefiles/rasters, and clipped intermediate rasters.

name: Generate Sentinel-2 RGB composite
desc: The script creates an RGB true-color composite raster from Sentinel-2 Level-2A JP2 band files (B04/Red, B03/Green, B02/Blue) using QGIS's GDAL merge algorithm. It extracts the acquisition date (YYYYMMDD) from the filename, writes the merged output to a TIFF file named with that date, and loads the resulting composite into the current QGIS project as a raster layer. Input paths explicitly reference Sentinel-2 L2A SAFE structure with tile T31TFJ and acquisition timestamp 2025-05-18.

name: Extract topographic profiles along transects
desc: The script extracts elevation values at regular intervals (5 m spacing) along vector transect lines from a digital elevation model ('detrended_dem') in QGIS. It samples DEM values using QgsRasterDataProvider.sample(), constructs point features with attributes including line ID, distance along transect, elevation (Z), and coordinates (X,Y), stores all points in a memory vector layer, and exports the result to a GeoPackage file named 'transects_profiles.gpkg'. The script explicitly names input layers as 'transects_300m' and 'detrended_dem', and outputs a single point layer containing all sampled profile points.

name: Compute new polling area boundaries
desc: The script computes updated polling area boundaries by intersecting clipped old geometries (previously adjusted) with new geometries, using attribute-based matching (fednum ↔ RidingFi_1) to associate corresponding features. It performs geometric difference operations between clipped old geometries and matched old geometries, then intersects the resulting subtracted geometries with the new geometry features. The output is a vector layer of polygon features representing the final computed polling areas.

name: Calculate integrated valley bottom width
desc: The script calculates integrated valley bottom width by intersecting a centerline vector layer with segmented valley-bottom polygon layers from a GeoPackage. It computes the area of each polygon segment, segments the centerline using geometric intersection, calculates the length of each centerline segment within each polygon, and derives an integrated width as area divided by length (int_width_m). Outputs include a new GeoPackage layer 'integrated_line.gpkg' containing the segmented centerline features with attributes 'area_m', 'length_m', and 'int_width_m'.

name: Generate SWAT+ to MODFLOW connections
desc: The script intersects SWAT+ HRU polygons and channel/reach lines with a MODFLOW active grid (structured, NROW=125, NCOL=222, NLAY=3), computes area fractions for HRU-to-grid cell overlaps and line-length fractions for channel-to-grid cell intersections, filters connections by minimum area fraction (0.05), maps grid IDs to row/column indices using integer division/modulo arithmetic, assigns default MODFLOW layer (1), and exports a GeoPackage table with attributes: swat_obj_type ('hru' or 'channel'), swat_obj_id (hru_id or reach_id), mf_layer, mf_row, mf_col, fraction (for HRUs), and length_m (for channels). The output is used for coupling SWAT+ hydrologic modeling with MODFLOW6 groundwater simulation.

name: Resolve polygon layer overlaps
desc: The script detects and resolves geometric overlaps between multiple input polygon layers in QGIS, using datetime fields (automatically detected from field names and content) to prioritize the most recent feature where overlaps occur. It validates layer geometry types and CRS consistency, identifies overlapping areas via QGIS native intersection processing, compares datetime values across overlapping features using a comprehensive list of 64+ datetime formats, and outputs a resolved polygon layer where only the latest-dated feature is retained per overlap region. Outputs include an in-memory overlap visualization layer and a saved ESRI Shapefile of the resolved polygons.

name: Resolve polygon layer overlaps
desc: The script resolves spatial overlaps between multiple input polygon layers in QGIS, using either datetime-based priority (detecting and parsing datetime fields from layer attributes using a comprehensive list of 64+ datetime formats) or user-defined layer priority. It detects overlapping geometries via spatial indexing and intersection operations, then creates a resolved output layer by subtracting overlapping areas from lower-priority layers. Key methods include invalid geometry fixing, automatic datetime field detection, parallelizable batch feature processing, and progress-aware UI feedback. Outputs include an overlap visualization layer and a cleaned output shapefile with overlaps removed.

name: Convert HiHydroSoil soil properties to SPHY format
desc: The script converts HiHydroSoil raster datasets (field capacity, saturation capacity, permanent wilting point, wilting point, and saturated hydraulic conductivity for topsoil and subsoil) into PCRaster format with scaled values (multiplied by 0.0001) and resampled to EPSG:32719 at 500 m resolution and a fixed extent (380681.000, 413181.000, 6339419.000, 6381419.000). It uses QGIS GDAL warp for reprojection/resampling and rasterio for scaling and PCRaster export.

name: Tile DEM by boundary intersection
desc: The script tiles a digital elevation model (DEM) raster into 512×512 pixel GeoTIFF tiles aligned to the input DEM's coordinate system and pixel geometry, but only saves tiles whose bounding rectangles intersect a reprojected city boundary polygon. It loads the DEM and boundary shapefile using PyQGIS, reprojects the boundary to match the DEM’s CRS if needed, unions all boundary geometries, iterates over regular grid-aligned tile extents, checks intersection with the unioned boundary geometry, and uses gdal_translate with -projwin to extract each valid tile. Outputs are individual GeoTIFF files named 'tile_i_j.tif' saved to a specified output directory.

name: Resample bathymetric raster data
desc: The script resamples raster layers from an ESRI geodatabase containing NOAA LIDAR bathymetry mosaics to a uniform target resolution (50 meters) using GDAL's warpreproject algorithm with nearest-neighbor resampling. It loads the geodatabase into QGIS, iterates over all raster layers, preserves their CRS, and exports each resampled raster as a GeoTIFF in the specified output folder. The output includes resampled GeoTIFF files named with the original layer name suffixed by '_resampled.tif'.

name: Compute wetland vegetation water index statistics
desc: The script computes temporal statistics (mean, range, and optionally min, max, standard deviation) from a stack of vegetation/water index raster layers (e.g., NDVI, NDWI) stored as GeoTIFFs in a user-specified directory. It loads all .tif files as QgsRasterLayer objects, computes their combined extent, then runs GRASS r.series with method=0 (mean) and method=9 (range); if fewer than 3 input rasters exist, it merges only mean and range outputs; otherwise, it additionally computes min (method=3), max (method=6), and std dev (method=8), then merges all five outputs into a single multi-band GTiff with Int16 type and -9999 nodata. The output is a multi-temporal statistical raster summarizing vegetation/water index behavior over time.

name: Compute raster series statistics
desc: The script computes a statistical time-series raster (e.g., mean, median, etc.) from all GeoTIFF files in a user-specified directory using GRASS GIS's r.series algorithm in QGIS. It first loads all .tif files as QgsRasterLayer objects, aggregates their spatial extents to define the output region, and runs r.series with method=3 (mean), no null handling (-n=False), and a broad data range. The output is a single raster representing the per-pixel mean across the input stack.

name: Export RGB raster to KMZ
desc: The script exports selected RGB raster layers from QGIS to KMZ format by first reprojecting them to EPSG:4326 using GDAL's warp reprojection, then converting the reprojected raster to a KML SuperOverlay (KMZ) using gdal.Translate with PNG encoding. The output is a KMZ file named after the layer and saved in a fixed local directory.

name: Visualize binary change detection
desc: The script launches a QGIS/PyQt GUI application for interactive visualization of binary change detection results. It loads and reprojects three user-provided raster inputs (past image, latest image, and change result) into EPSG:3857, overlays them with an OpenStreetMap basemap, and enables real-time transparency adjustment per layer via sliders. The core functionality centers on rendering and interactively exploring spatially aligned pre-change, post-change, and detected-change rasters for qualitative assessment.

name: Detect individual tree positions
desc: The script converts a Canopy Height Model (CHM) raster into vector layers representing individual tree positions and canopy polygons. It applies thresholding on CHM height (default 2.0 m), normalizes the CHM, performs normalized cross-correlation with a custom 5×5 Gaussian-like template kernel, identifies local maxima via dilation/masking, and detects tree tops using both cross-correlation peak locations and OpenCV's SimpleBlobDetector on inverted normalized CHM. Outputs include: (1) a point layer with X/Y coordinates, similarity score, tree height, and algorithm label ('CC' or 'Bl'); (2) an optional polygon layer for tree canopies; (3) an optional raster output of the normalized cross-correlation response map styled with a QML file.

name: Co-register CHM rasters
desc: The script performs co-registration of two raster layers (CHM input register and CHM input reference) using SIFT and ORB feature detection and matching. It extracts keypoints, computes descriptors, matches features between the rasters, estimates homography via RANSAC, and outputs a vector point layer of detected keypoints in the source CRS. The algorithm is implemented as a QGIS Processing algorithm with parameters for input rasters and maximum keypoints, and includes timing feedback during execution.

name: Reclassify and combine NLCD land cover
desc: The script processes NLCD (National Land Cover Database) raster data for Alaska to reclassify tree canopy classes (41, 42, 43) into a unified forest class, warp both tree canopy and land cover rasters to EPSG:4326, combine them using conditional pixel replacement, replace urban/clutter classes with grass-related codes, reclassify urban classes (21–24) into simplified urban types (10, 1, 2), apply GRASS median filtering to clean urban features, merge cleaned urban and grass layers, upsample the result by factor 8 using GDAL Warp, smooth with GRASS r.neighbors (size=11, method=median), and compress to 8-bit LZW TIFF. Outputs include 11 intermediate and final rasters named with suffixes like '_Trees-Combined', '_Tree_Canopy_4326', '_Grass-Only_4326', '_Reclassed-Urban_4326', '_Urban-Only_4326', '_Combined-Clean_4326', '_Combined-Clean-HD_4326', '_Smoothed-HD_4326', and '_Smoothed-HD-Compressed_4326'.

name: Assess reservoir-keypoint proximity significance
desc: The script evaluates whether the spatial arrangement of reservoirs relative to predefined keypoints within a catchment boundary is statistically non-random. It computes the median distance from each reservoir to its nearest keypoint, then performs a Monte Carlo simulation (1000 iterations) generating random point sets within the catchment polygon and recalculating the median match distance for each set. The p-value is derived as the fraction of random iterations yielding a median distance ≤ the actual observed median. Outputs include the actual median distance, average random median distance, p-value, and a significance conclusion (p < 0.05).

name: Extract UHI CSV data
desc: The script prepares input data for an Urban Heat Island (UHI) analysis tool by organizing raster files (LST, DEM/MNT, land cover, soil texture, canopy height, hydrologic soil group, LCZ/climatic zone) and a city-specific CSV output file. It infers EPSG and city name from folder naming convention (e.g., 'Paris_32632'), reorganizes raw files into structured 'data' and 'results' folders, identifies rasters by keyword matching in filenames, transforms the LST raster extent to EPSG:4326 for AOI definition, and constructs a parameter dictionary consumed by the QGIS algorithm 'ExtractionDuFichierCsvPourOutilIa'. The final output is a CSV file named after the city (e.g., 'Paris.csv') written to the results folder.

name: Clip non-forest mask by territory
desc: The script clips a single non-forest mask raster ('non_forest_mask_2024') to individual territory boundaries defined in a vector layer ('terramaz_boundary'), using each territory's 'zone' attribute (e.g., 'cotriguacu', 'paragominas') to name and save separate clipped GeoTIFF files. It uses QGIS's GDAL 'cliprasterbymasklayer' algorithm with LZW compression, outputs one raster per zone to a specified local directory, and optionally adds each result as a valid raster layer to the QGIS project.

name: Reproject risk map rasters
desc: The script reprojects four named raster layers ('cotriguacu_riskmap', 'guaviare_riskmap', 'paragominas_riskmap', 'madre_de_dios_riskmap') from their native CRS to EPSG:4326 using GDAL's warpreproject algorithm in QGIS. It applies bilinear resampling, LZW compression, and preserves input data type and NoData value (0). Outputs are GeoTIFF files saved to a local Windows directory with '_epsg4326.tif' suffixes, and optionally added back to the QGIS project as new raster layers.

name: Merge and mask satellite image stacks
desc: The script batch processes satellite imagery by merging multiple raster files per ID from a CSV input table, then clips each merged raster to a user-provided masking shapefile using GDAL's merge and cliprasterbymasklayer algorithms. It deletes intermediate merged rasters after masking. The workflow is executed in QGIS Python console using processing.run() with fixed GDAL algorithm parameters and no dynamic time or band selection logic.

name: Generate hillslope and floodplain rasters
desc: The script generates hillslope rasters (left/right sides and headwater areas) and floodplain rasters from channel networks and D8 flow direction rasters using TauDEM-derived inputs (filled DEM, flow directions, accumulation). It supports three floodplain methods: buffering channels by drainage-area-dependent widths, inverting the DEM to derive ridge flow paths and accumulations, or using branch-length thresholds from distance-to-outlet rasters. Outputs include valley depths raster, hillslope identification raster, and floodplain/upslope classification raster.

name: Model river bathymetry surface
desc: The script models high-resolution bathymetric surfaces for selected British Columbia river regions (e.g., T09UWS, T10UDA) using in-situ bathymetric point measurements (ellipsoidal height 'z_el'/'ellipsoida') and river boundary vector data. It performs multilevel B-spline interpolation (SAGA 'grid_spline' module) on WGS84 points to generate a continuous raster surface, clips it to the river corridor, reprojects the surface and points to regional UTM-based CRS (EPSG:3156 or EPSG:3157), re-runs interpolation at 10 m ground resolution, clips again, and tiles the final clipped surface into VRT-aligned GeoTIFFs — retaining only tiles intersecting bathymetric points. Outputs include: (1) QGIS project with styled bathymetry points and clipped surface rasters (WGS84 and projected), (2) CSV files for SDB/SNAP processing containing reprojected coordinates and depths, (3) tiled GeoTIFFs for downstream hydrodynamic or remote sensing applications.

name: Compute elevation-based volume curves
desc: The script computes a series of cut-and-fill volumes for a clipped DEM by iteratively applying horizontal reference planes (contour levels) from minimum to maximum elevation in 10% increments of the total elevation range. It uses QGIS’s native:rastersurfacevolume algorithm to calculate volumetric earthwork (fill volume above, cut volume below each level), converts results to km³, and exports a CSV table with columns: Level (m), Fill Volume (km³), Cut Volume (km³), Net Volume (km³). The workflow relies on GDAL raster clipping and QGIS raster statistics, not satellite or time-series data.

name: Calculate heap volume from DEM
desc: The script calculates cut and fill volumes for heap polygons using a digital elevation model (DEM). It first clips the input DEM to the heap polygon layer, then iteratively computes surface volume at elevation levels spaced by a user-defined step using QGIS's native:rastersurfacevolume algorithm. Volumes are converted from cubic meters to cubic kilometers, separated into fill and cut components, and exported to a CSV file with columns for elevation level, fill volume, cut volume, and net volume.

name: Extract water level and inundation depth from rasters
desc: The script extracts water level (in cm) and inundation depth (lame_eau) from GeoPackage-stored raster layers, matched to user-provided point features using date-based correspondence. It supports two modes: (1) interval mode — duplicates each input point for every date in a user-specified date range and samples corresponding rasters; (2) field mode — matches each point’s date attribute to the nearest raster (named by water level in cm) and samples a single raster value per point. Outputs include a new QGIS vector layer with added fields 'date_releve_terrain', 'niveau_eau_cm', and 'lame_eau', added to the current project.

name: Clip climate raster by country boundary
desc: The script clips NetCDF climate raster files (e.g., ERA5_dry_days.nc, ERA5_mean_temp.nc) using country-level shapefiles (e.g., KEN_adm0.shp, UGA_adm0.shp) via GDAL's 'cliprasterbymasklayer' algorithm in QGIS. It outputs clipped rasters named with country prefix and original filename (e.g., 'KEN_a_ERA5_dry_days.nc'), then loads each clipped raster as a layer into the current QGIS project.

name: Identify thermal refugia patches
desc: The script identifies spatially contiguous thermal refugia patches by polygonizing a binary thermal patch mask raster (value = 1), filtering by minimum area, computing the mean surface temperature (from a co-located thermal raster) within each patch via zonal statistics, calculating the centroid (in WGS84 lon/lat), and exporting both a QGIS vector layer of polygons with attributes (area, mean temperature, lon, lat) and a CSV table listing patch ID, centroid coordinates, area, and mean temperature.

name: Generate administrative-boundary-constrained heatmaps
desc: The script downloads GADM administrative boundary shapefiles for a user-specified country, generates 200 random points inside the highest- and lowest-level administrative polygons (e.g., country-level '0.shp' and region/province-level '2.shp'), computes a kernel density heatmap raster (using fixed radius=1, pixel size=0.005°) from those points, and clips the resulting heatmap to the original administrative boundary geometry — producing a clipped GeoTIFF heatmap visually representing point-density intensity constrained by political boundaries.

name: Classify land cover in APA
desc: The script classifies land cover in an Área de Preservação Ambiental (APA) in Araguaína-TO using a pre-defined MapBiomas Collection 8 legend. It loads a TIFF raster and a study area shapefile, clips the raster to the vector boundary, and applies a categorized renderer to the vector layer using hexadecimal color codes mapped to MapBiomas land cover classes. The output includes a QGIS project file with the styled vector layer and a clipped raster.

name: Clip orthoimagery by polygon
desc: The script crops GeoTIFF orthophotos using a vector polygon boundary (clipping_polygon.shp) via GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer algorithm in QGIS. It iterates over all .tiff files in the input folder, validates each raster, applies clipping with CROP_TO_CUTLINE=True and KEEP_RESOLUTION=True, compresses output as JPEG, and saves clipped rasters to the OUTPUT_FOLDER. The clipping shapefile is explicitly loaded and validated, and processing feedback is used for execution control.

name: Calculate 99th percentile raster values
desc: The script calculates the 99th percentile value of pixel intensities within each polygon feature from a raster layer, using QGIS processing tools (gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer) and GDAL/Numpy for statistical computation. It clips the raster to each vector polygon geometry (with on-the-fly CRS transformation), reads the clipped raster data, filters out NoData values, computes the 99th percentile, and appends this value as a new field 'pct_99' to the output shapefile while preserving original vector geometries and attributes.

name: Map solar radiation distribution
desc: The script processes precomputed solar radiation raster files (e.g., '2020_Average.tif', monthly 'YYYY_MM.tif') by clipping them to Brazil’s national boundary (BR_Pais_2021.shp), applying Turbo pseudocolor rendering with 255 classes, and generating publication-ready PNG maps (800×800 px) that include dynamic min/max value labels, month abbreviation label, and units ('kWh/m²/day'). It uses QGIS layout export to produce georeferenced, styled visualizations for time-series solar radiation assessment over Brazil — no GEE server-side computation occurs; the script is purely a QGIS desktop automation workflow for raster styling, clipping, and map composition.

name: Convert raster to polygon grid
desc: The script converts an active single-band Byte-type raster layer in QGIS into a vector polygon grid layer, where each pixel becomes a square polygon with side length equal to the raster's pixel size. It reads the raster's extent, dimensions, and pixel values via QgsRasterDataProvider.block(), constructs QgsRectangle geometries for each pixel, assigns the pixel value as a 'CLASE' integer attribute, and adds the resulting memory vector layer to the QGIS project.

name: Recrop Landsat imagery with mask
desc: The script processes Landsat Level-1 TIF files by parsing their filenames to extract satellite, acquisition date, path/row, and product identifiers; generates new .rst filenames following a custom naming convention (e.g., '20250106_L8_2547_121_QB.rst'); clips each raster to a vector mask (wb_30_20.shp) using QGIS GDAL cliprasterbymasklayer; computes CRC-32 checksums for both input TIF and output RST files; and logs all operations and checksums in a CSV file. Inputs are local filesystem TIFs, outputs are clipped RST files and a control CSV.

name: Generate aligned working box
desc: The script generates a vector-based Working Box (bounding polygon) aligned to a raster layer's pixel grid, using the extent of a vector layer with configurable margin percentage. It validates that exactly two visible layers are present (first vector, second raster), share the same CRS, the raster has square pixels, and the vector extent is fully contained within the raster extent. The Working Box is computed by expanding the vector extent by a user-defined margin (20%), snapping coordinates to the raster's pixel grid, and creating a memory vector layer with attributes storing the names of input layers and margin value. Output is a new QGIS vector layer named 'wb-20-{pixel_size}' with no-fill, solid red border symbology.

name: Animate flood water level and velocity
desc: The script creates a temporal animation of flood simulation results by importing MIKE 2D velocity and water level vector layers from a File Geodatabase, transforming them into SQLite-spatial tables ('velo' and 'wlevel') with time-stamped geometries, filtering by minimum thresholds (min_v, min_w), applying scaling factors (faktor_v), and loading styled layers into QGIS. It reads simulation timing metadata from 'report_info.xml', computes time steps using ReportStart and ReportInterval, inserts time-interval polygons/lines into spatial tables, and adds a TopPlusOpen WMS basemap. Outputs include two temporal vector layers in a SQLite database and QGIS project layers styled with QML files.

name: Import Hystem-Extran simulation results
desc: The script imports hydraulic simulation results from a Firebird database (Hystem-Extran v8) into the QKan SQLite database, specifically extracting overflow statistics (frequency, count, volume) for manholes ('schaechte') by joining HE8 result tables (LAU_MAX_S, LANGZEITKNOTEN) with QKan's 'schaechte' table. It creates and populates a spatial table 'ResultsSch' with POINT geometry, then loads it as a QGIS vector layer named 'Überstau Schächte' under the 'Ergebnisse' group, applying user-selected QML styling (e.g., 'ueberstauhaeufigkeit.qml' or 'ueberstauvolumen.qml').

name: Join census attributes to census tracts
desc: The script joins a CSV-based U.S. Census dataset (ACS_12_5YR_S1901_with_ann.csv) to a shapefile of census tracts (hancock_tracts.shp) using the GEOid2 field from the CSV and GEOID field from the shapefile. It performs a vector attribute join in QGIS via QgsVectorJoinInfo, caches the join in memory, and writes the joined result to a new shapefile (joined.shp). The output confirms field count increased from 12 to 142, verifying successful attribute enrichment of spatial census tract boundaries with demographic/economic census variables.

name: Convert shapefile to KML
desc: The script converts a local Shapefile ('hancock.shp') to KML format using PyQGIS QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormat, reprojecting it to EPSG:4326. It also optionally writes the same layer to GeoJSON. The input path '/qgis_data/hancock/hancock.shp' and output paths '/qgis_data/hancock/hancock.kml' and '/qgis_data/hancock/hancock.geojson' confirm the conversion task with coordinate system transformation.

name: Compute least cost path
desc: The script computes a least cost path between two points using a digital elevation model (DEM) as input terrain data. It first calculates a cumulative cost raster from the start point using GRASS r.cost.points, then merges start and end point vector layers, and finally applies SAGA's least cost paths algorithm using the cost raster and DEM to generate a vector line layer representing the optimal path. Outputs include the accumulated cost raster ('cost.tif'), merged point layer ('merge.shp'), least cost path line ('path.shp'), and profile points ('profilePts.shp').

name: Geolocate photos on map
desc: The script extracts GPS coordinates from EXIF metadata of JPEG photos in a specified directory (/qgis_data/photos/), converts DMS-formatted GPS values to decimal degrees, creates a memory-based QGIS point vector layer with EPSG:4326 CRS, populates it with points representing photo locations, and adds an OpenUrl action to launch each photo file. The output is a QGIS vector layer named 'Geotagged Photos' displayed in the map canvas with clickable photo links.

name: Rectangularize building footprints
desc: The script adjusts imprecise building footprint polygons to make them more rectangular by identifying the top-right vertex of each input polygon, computing slopes and intercepts of adjacent edges, deriving perpendicular lines, and calculating intersection points to construct a new rectangle aligned with the dominant edge orientation. It reads an irregular building footprint shapefile, processes each feature's geometry using coordinate arithmetic and line geometry operations, constructs a 5-point rectangular polygon per input feature, and writes the result to a memory layer named 'Rectangles'. The output is a vector layer of rectified building footprints.

name: Simplify segmentation line geometry
desc: The script simplifies a vector line layer representing image segmentation boundaries by topologically merging lines adjacent to small polygons (area < 30 units) into those surrounding larger polygons. It achieves this through a multi-step GIS workflow: (1) deriving the input layer’s extent and converting it to a bounding polygon boundary; (2) unioning that boundary with the input segmentation lines; (3) polygonizing the resulting line network to reconstruct polygons; (4) computing polygon areas; (5) selecting and eliminating small polygons (<30 area units) by merging them with neighboring larger polygons; (6) converting the merged polygons back to lines; (7) applying a tiny buffer (1e-5) to the original extent boundary; and (8) computing the symmetrical difference between the new simplified lines and the buffered extent boundary — effectively extracting only the interior simplified segmentation lines, excluding the outer frame. The output is a cleaned, topology-consistent line vector layer with reduced complexity, optimized for cartographic generalization or downstream vector processing.

name: Generate travel time isochrones
desc: The script computes travel time isochrones from starting points along a road network, using road speed attributes to rasterize roads, assign off-road speeds, calculate per-pixel travel time in minutes or hours, and generate a cost-distance raster representing cumulative travel time. It then applies discrete color-ramped styles for user-defined time intervals (e.g., 5,15,30 minutes) and optionally supports vector isochrone generation (currently commented out). Inputs include a vector roads layer with speed field, vector starting points, resolution, and extent; output is a styled raster of travel time in minutes.

name: Extract and process OSM street networks
desc: The script extracts OpenStreetMap (OSM) vector data from a local 'map.osm' file, parsing lines (streets, footways, cycleways), points (crossings, amenities, bus stops), and polygons (buildings, parking, green areas, sidewalks). It performs attribute-based filtering (e.g., highway types, amenity tags), CRS reprojection, lane number estimation using tag parsing and graph-based propagation, street displacement via GRASS v.generalize, and snapping/dangling-end correction against a user-provided extent. Outputs include GeoJSON files for streets_laned, streets_displaced, snapped_streets, crossing_lines, sidewalk_lines, crossing_points, point_POI, bus_stop, buildings, parkings, green, and sidewalk_area.

name: Merge shapefile layers from folder
desc: The script merges multiple vector shapefiles from a specified folder into a single output vector layer, preserving the geometry type and field schema of a user-provided template layer. It recursively or non-recursively searches for files matching a pattern (default '*.shp'), loads each as a QgsVectorLayer, validates geometry type compatibility, maps template field names to source layer fields case-insensitively, copies attributes accordingly (filling missing fields with null), and writes all features to a new vector output using VectorWriter. The output is a unified vector layer with consistent schema and geometry.

name: Validate land cover classification accuracy
desc: The script performs comprehensive accuracy assessment of a classified raster map against reference point data. It extracts class values at point locations, constructs an error (confusion) matrix, and computes over 30 validation metrics including Overall Accuracy, Producer/User Accuracies, Kappa coefficients (standard, weighted, conditional), Classification Success Index (CSI/GCSI), Ground Truth Index (GT), entropy-based measures (AMI, NMI, EC), Aickin's alpha, and disagreement components (QD, AD). Outputs include 'error_matrix.txt', 'global_indexes.csv', and 'per_class_indexes.csv' saved to the specified output folder.

name: Digitize geological map units
desc: The script digitizes geological map units from RGB or paletted raster maps using semi-automatic color-based segmentation. It intersects a user-provided polygon (or uses full raster extent), reads the clipped RGB pixel data, applies K-Means clustering to group similar colors into geological unit candidates, performs morphological smoothing to remove scanning artifacts, vectorizes the clustered labels into polygons via GDAL Polygonize, sieves small polygons using GDAL SieveFilter, and clips all resulting polygons strictly to the input study area boundary. Outputs include a list of QgsGeometry polygons per cluster ID, hex-formatted centroid colors for styling, the source CRS WKT, and the number of clusters used.

name: Assign stream order to catchments
desc: The script computes catchment boundaries from a depressionless DEM using GRASS r.watershed, rasterizes a drainage line vector layer (with 'ORDER' attribute) to a matching resolution and extent, then assigns the maximum stream order value from the drainage raster to each catchment polygon's corresponding raster cells. The final output is a catchment raster where each cell's value represents the highest stream order intersecting that catchment. Temporary rasters are cleaned up after processing.

name: Visualize optimization investment decisions
desc: The script visualizes geospatial outputs from an optimization model, specifically investment decisions for process units, storage units, and distribution networks. It reads CSV files containing field IDs, production rates, inventory levels, and flow rates; matches them to grid coordinates using a gridded polygon layer; generates time-sliced CSVs per technology and major time period; converts them into point vector layers (for process/storage) and line vector layers (for distribution flows); and optionally applies temporal demand variation to a demand layer. Outputs include shapefiles for each technology-time combination and concatenated CSVs with coordinate-embedded geometry.

name: Compute RUSLE erosion potential
desc: The script implements the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) model in QGIS to estimate soil erosion potential. It first computes the LS factor using the Mitasova algorithm on a filled-sinks DEM, applying user-defined sheet and rill erosion factors. Then it constructs a raster algebra expression combining LS with K (soil erodibility), C (cover management), and R (rainfall erosivity) factors—either as input rasters or single-value parameters—and executes the formula via GDAL's raster calculator. Outputs are two rasters: the LS factor map and the final RUSLE soil loss estimate (in tons/ha/year or equivalent units).

name: Calculate drainage undercapacity for wastewater systems
desc: The script computes undercapacity metrics for wastewater drainage systems by spatially joining planning, drinking water, and pollution unit datasets to catchment polygons, then calculating summed inflows (e.g., AW_15_24_G, POC_O_M3_G) and propagating them upstream via hierarchical node relationships (e.g., 'VAN_KNOOPN' receiving from 'K_ONTV_VAN'). It identifies overlapping plans (plancap overlap), replaces nulls with zeros, computes hardened surface area per connection type (GEM/HWA/NAG/OBK/VGS), and derives undercapacity indicators (e.g., POC_O_M3_O, IN_DWA_POC) and infrastructure performance indices (e.g., PI_*_G). Outputs include a finalized 'eindresultaat.gpkg' layer with standardized fields, aliases, and cleaned attributes — used for hydraulic capacity assessment and planning support in Dutch municipal wastewater management.

name: Estimate floodwater depth
desc: The script estimates water depth across a flooded area by generating a triangulated irregular network (TIN) surface from elevation-sampled points along the flood boundary, smoothing the TIN, subtracting it from a clipped high-resolution DEM (MERIT 90m), and masking/clipping the resulting depth raster to the original flood polygon while enforcing non-negative values. Outputs include a final depth raster ('depth_final.sdat') representing estimated inundation depth in meters.

name: Derive protected site boundaries
desc: The script processes vector GIS layers to derive and refine administrative and protected area boundaries (e.g., 'site-ja', 'zone-ja', 'gga-ja') through sequential clipping and difference operations. It starts from input shapefiles (Adp.shp, Gwp.shp, vast_az.shp, gga.shp, bes_arch_site.shp, wrzja.shp, wrzneen.shp) located in local file paths under 'G:/geo-ict-Qgis/', constructs a bounding box from the 'Adp' layer, clips other layers to that extent, then performs cascading set-difference operations (e.g., ADP minus site → siteneen; siteneen minus gebieden → gganeen; gganeen minus zone → zoneneen; etc.) to isolate non-overlapping or conditionally included zones. Final outputs are cleaned, mutually exclusive polygon layers ('cleanzone', 'cleangga', 'cleansite') representing 'yes' subsets (e.g., 'zone-ja') for visualization and integration with pre-processed WRZ (Wetenschappelijke Raad voor het Rijkslandschap?) layers. No remote sensing imagery, time-series, or spectral analysis is used — all operations are vector-based geometric Boolean logic in QGIS Processing Toolbox (qgis:clip, qgis:difference, saga:difference). CRS is explicitly set to EPSG:31370 (Belge 1972 / Lambert 72), confirming Belgium as the geographic context. Study area is not named explicitly but inferred from CRS, path structure, and layer names (e.g., 'wrz' likely refers to Belgian 'Wetenschappelijke Raad voor het Rijkslandschap').

name: Generate catchment mask grid
desc: The script generates a regular 5 km × 5 km fishnet grid aligned to the British National Grid (EPSG:27700) covering a user-provided catchment boundary shapefile; it assigns SHETRAN_ID = 0 to grid cells intersecting the catchment and SHETRAN_ID = -9999 to all others; then pivots the attribute table into a raster-like 2D integer array (Y-indexed descending, X-indexed ascending), appends an ESRI ASCII grid header (ncols, nrows, xllcorner, yllcorner, cellsize, NODATA_value), and saves it as a space-delimited text file ('final_mask_SHETRAN.txt') compatible with SHETRAN hydrological modeling software.

name: Generate minimum and mean DEM for SHETRAN
desc: The script generates two SHETRAN-compatible DEM files: one containing the minimum elevation per grid cell and another containing the mean elevation per grid cell, both derived from zonal statistics of a raster DEM (DEM.tif) over a catchment mask vector layer (catchm_mask.shp). It uses QGIS's SAGA 'Raster statistics for polygons' algorithm, pivots the resulting attribute table by X (columns) and Y (rows), sorts Y in descending order to match SHETRAN's expected grid orientation, saves numeric matrices as text files, and prepends ESRI ASCII grid headers (ncols, nrows, xllcorner, yllcorner, cellsize, NODATA_value). The outputs are final_dem_min_SHETRAN.txt and final_dem_mean_SHETRAN.txt.

name: Generate land cover input for SHETRAN
desc: The script generates a land cover input file for the SHETRAN hydrological model by performing zonal histogram analysis of a land cover raster (LandCover.tif) over a catchment grid vector layer (catchm_mask.shp). It identifies the dominant land cover class per grid cell, replaces value 0 with -9999 as no-data, pivots the result into a spatial grid aligned by X and Y coordinates, adds ESRI ASCII grid header metadata (ncols, nrows, xllcorner, yllcorner, cellsize, NODATA_value), and saves the final output as a text file (final_land_cover_SHETRAN.txt). The process uses QGIS Python API (qgis:zonalhistogram) and PyQGIS initialization.

name: Calculate drainage system undercapacity
desc: The script calculates hydraulic undercapacity (underbemaling) for drainage infrastructure by spatially joining planning and utility datasets (plancap, drinkwater, VE, verhard oppervlak) to catchment polygons (hoofdbemalingsgebieden), then computing summed inflows per node (VAN_KNOOPN) based on hierarchical upstream relationships defined in dictionaries (d_K_ONTV_VAN, l_K_ONTV_VAN). It identifies overlapping plans (PLANCAP_OVERLAP), replaces NULL values with 0, computes area-weighted statistics (e.g., HA_GEM_G, POC_O_M3_O), and populates an output layer 'eindresultaat.shp' with fields including AW_15_24_O (undercapacity for 2015–2024 plan area), DWR_ONBG (undercapacity for drinking water), X_VE_ONBG (undercapacity for pollution units), IN_DWA_POC (pump capacity deficit), and PI-based metrics. Outputs include joined statistics layers (STATS_DRINKWATER, STATS_PLANCAP, STATS_VE), intersected impervious surface layers (VERHARD_OPP_INTERSECT), and aggregated CSV/shapefile summaries.

name: Count points within polygons by date
desc: The script counts the number of point features (e.g., observations or events) falling within each polygon feature, then identifies the earliest date among those points per polygon and exports a subset of points corresponding to that minimum date per polygon. It adds a count field to the polygon layer, builds a spatial index for efficient point-in-polygon testing, writes intermediate results to temporary shapefiles named by polygon ID and min date, and finally merges outputs into a single result vector layer. The log file tracks processing steps and errors.

name: Sum attribute values by layer
desc: The script computes the sum of a user-specified attribute expression across selected vector layers, optionally filtering features using a QGIS expression and clipping to a polygon layer. It processes only layers matching geometry type filters (polygon, line, or point), applies optional feature selection (selected features only), evaluates the sum expression per feature, accumulates totals per layer and overall, and exports results to a CSV table with layer names and sums.

name: Cluster vector features by attribute value
desc: The script performs k-means clustering on a user-specified numeric attribute field (default 'diff_mean') of an input vector layer using scipy's kmeans implementation. It supports both random and ordered (evenly spaced across the data range) initial centroids. After clustering, it assigns cluster IDs ('cluster' field) and then sorts clusters by their attribute value ranges to assign interpretable, ordered class labels ('class' field) — where class 0 corresponds to the cluster with the lowest attribute values and higher classes correspond to progressively higher values. The output is a vector layer with two new integer fields: 'cluster' (raw k-means assignment) and 'class' (sorted, workflow-ready labeling).

name: Detect large linear feature changes
desc: The script detects significant geometric changes between two vector line layers (e.g., roads, rivers, pipelines) by buffering each layer and computing geometric differences. It identifies line segments from the Original_Layer that lie outside the buffer of the Updated_Layer (and vice versa), splits multipart geometries, filters segments by minimum length outside buffer (50 m), and writes qualifying features to two output vector layers with error metadata fields. The workflow includes fixed-distance buffering, geometry difference operations, multipart handling, and optional feature deletion based on ID matching.

name: Export vector layer field information
desc: The script exports metadata about the fields (attributes) of an input vector layer to a CSV file, including field index, name, type, type name, length, precision, comment, and alias. It creates a memory vector layer with these field descriptors, writes it to a CSV file with a CSVT sidecar, and loads the resulting CSV as a vector layer in QGIS. The algorithm is implemented as a QGIS Processing tool named 'export_field_infos' under the 'Vectors' group.

name: Calculate road network length within region
desc: The script calculates the total length of road network lines intersecting or contained within a user-provided polygon region. It first reprojects both the road network (line) and region (polygon) layers to the project's CRS, then uses QGIS's 'Sum line lengths' algorithm to compute the sum of road lengths per polygon feature (storing result in a new 'LENGTH' attribute), and outputs a polygon layer with this aggregated length value attached to each region feature.

name: Compare road network lengths
desc: The script computes and compares the total length of two input line vector layers (Road Network 1 and Road Network 2) within each polygon feature of a user-provided region layer, using the region’s ID field for spatial aggregation. It runs the 'Road Network Length' model twice (once per road network) to obtain summed line lengths per region, joins the two resulting length tables on the Region ID field, and calculates a new field 'lenDIFF' as the difference ('length' − 'length_2') between the two networks’ lengths per region. The output is a vector layer (polygon or geometry-agnostic) containing the original region geometries plus attributes: region ID, length of Road Network 1, length of Road Network 2, and their difference.

name: Analyze gun crime and shot spotter incidents per ward
desc: The script analyzes 2017 gun-related crime incidents and Shot Spotter-detected gunshots in Washington, D.C., aggregated by 2012 election wards. It filters crime data for 'GUN' method and Shot Spotter data for year 2017, performs spatial joins to assign incidents to wards, and computes incident counts per 10,000 people using 2010 population data (POP_2010). Outputs include printed statistics per ward showing gun crimes per 10,000 people and Shot Spotter incidents per 10,000 people in 2017.

name: Compute Largest Empty Circle radii
desc: The script computes the Largest Empty Circle (LEC) radii for a set of input point sites by calculating the Euclidean distance from each Voronoi polygon vertex to its nearest site. It first removes duplicate geometries, generates Voronoi polygons bounding the sites, extracts and deduplicates their vertices, assigns unique IDs to cleaned sites and vertices, computes bounding geometry statistics (diagonal, max search distance, lag distance), performs nearest-hub distance analysis (HubDist) from vertices to sites, and outputs: (1) LEC point layer with HubDist radii, (2) bounding geometry polygon, (3) cleaned sites with Sites_ID, (4) cleaned vertices with Vertices_ID, (5) Voronoi polygons, and (6) HTML statistics report of HubDist values (min, max, mean, std, etc.).

name: Perform ordinary kriging interpolation
desc: The script performs ordinary kriging interpolation on point data ('LEC' layer) using a variogram model and spatial parameters (e.g., lag distance, max search distance, block size) to generate a prediction raster and optional variance raster. It retrieves default parameter values (lag_dist_default, max_search_dist_default, formula_default) from pre-existing project layers named 'Bounding Geometry' and 'Variogram Results'. The kriging is executed via the SAGA GIS 'saga:ordinarykriging' algorithm within QGIS Processing Framework, with configurable inputs including field selection, grid cell size, block kriging toggle, and search constraints.

name: Generate contour lines and polygon areas
desc: The script processes a pre-computed kriging raster (e.g., interpolated elevation or concentration surface) to generate contour lines at user-defined intervals, converts those lines into closed polygons, dissolves polygons by contour elevation (Z) value, computes polygon area and number of parts, and finally counts the number of input point sites (e.g., sampling locations) falling within each contour-derived polygon — outputting both the contour line vector layer and an attribute-enriched polygon layer with area and site count per isoline.

name: Map gun crime rates by ward
