desc: The script retrieves USDA SSURGO soil polygon data (including Hydrologic Soil Group - HSG - codes in 'hydgrpdcd') for multiple user-defined watershed basins, intersects the national soil dataset with each basin geometry, analyzes HSG and soil series (musym/muname) distributions per basin, and outputs: (1) individual GeoPackage layers of clipped soil polygons per basin, (2) a combined GeoPackage of all retrieved soil polygons, and (3) a plain-text summary report listing HSG counts and soil types for each basin. It does not compute Curve Numbers directly but provides the foundational HSG spatial data required for CN derivation.

name: Retrieve USDA soil survey data
desc: The script retrieves spatially explicit USDA Soil Survey (SSURGO) data for a user-selected Area of Interest (AOI) vector layer in QGIS. It reprojects the AOI to WGS84 (EPSG:4326), converts its extent to WKT polygon format, and submits a SQL query via the USDA Soil Data Access (SDA) REST API to fetch soil attributes—including hydric group (hydgrpdcd), slope, drainage class, available water storage, flooding frequency, and dozens of other SSURGO-standard fields—along with geometry (mupolygongeo). The returned features are assembled into a memory vector layer with exactly 42 predefined string-typed fields matching the CN Generator tool’s schema, then geometrically processed (fix geometries → clip to AOI → reproject back to original CRS → fix again) and saved as a GeoPackage. Finally, it loads the result into QGIS and attempts to apply Hydrologic Soil Group (HSG)-based symbology, reporting counts per HSG in the output summary.

name: Retrieve USDA soil polygons with hydrologic soil group
desc: The script retrieves spatial soil polygon data from the USDA Soil Data Access (SDA) REST API for a user-selected vector layer (AOI), including all standard SSURGO attributes—especially Hydrologic Soil Group (HSG) encoded in the 'hydgrpdcd' field. It reprojects the AOI to WGS84, queries SDA using WKT-based spatial intersection, parses JSON response into a memory vector layer with 43 string-typed soil attributes, validates and fixes geometries, clips results to the AOI, saves as GeoPackage, and reports summary statistics including HSG distribution and soil map unit (MUSYM) names with associated HSG values.

name: Calculate NDVI from NIR and red bands
desc: The script computes the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from user-provided NIR and red raster layers using GDAL’s raster calculator with a scaled formula ((A/10000.0) - (B/10000.0)) / ((A/10000.0) + (B/10000.0)), applies a binary threshold (NDVI > 0 → 1), and vectorizes the thresholded result into polygons; it then calculates and appends a 'Ratio' field representing the area proportion of each polygon class relative to the total area, outputting three artifacts: (1) a continuous NDVI raster, (2) a binary threshold raster, and (3) a classified vector layer with per-polygon area ratios.

name: Extract longest skeleton lines
desc: The script processes a shapefile of 'camellones' (ridged agricultural beds) to compute their Voronoi skeletons using GRASS GIS v.voronoi.skeleton, then identifies and exports the longest line segment per polygon_id group. It simplifies input geometries first, adds a length attribute to the skeleton layer, groups features by 'polygon_id', retains only the longest line per group, and saves the result as a new shapefile. Outputs include a skeleton layer with length field and a filtered longest-line layer saved to 'longest_line_output.shp'.

name: Measure camellon width perpendicular to centerline
desc: The script measures the width of agricultural ridges (camellones) by generating points along a centerline, computing polygon-specific orientation angles using length-weighted axial circular mean, creating perpendicular lines within each polygon at each point, and calculating the length of those perpendicular segments as ridge widths. Outputs include a shapefile of perpendicular line segments with attributes (polygon_id, distance along centerline, width) and a CSV file listing polygon_id, distance, and measured width.

name: Estimate housing and population from platform area
desc: The script calculates the area (in square meters) of polygon features representing platforms, estimates the number of houses by dividing area by 500 m² per house (using floor division), and derives population as 5 persons per house. It appends these computed fields ('sqm', 'houses', 'pop') to a new memory vector layer with identical geometry and original attributes, then exports the result as both a shapefile and a CSV (with WKT geometry). The input is a local shapefile named 'platforms.shp' located in a 'spatial_data/shapefiles/platforms/' subdirectory relative to the QGIS project file.

name: Compute surviving heights from DEM
desc: The script computes average elevation metrics (point elevation, neighborhood minimum, and neighborhood maximum) for each polygon in a 'camellones' (ridges or raised beds) layer using a digital elevation model (DEM). It samples the DEM at point locations associated with each polygon, applies a 4m spatial window to compute local min/max elevations, filters out zero and NoData values, and aggregates statistics per polygon_id. Outputs include a CSV file with averaged elevation metrics per polygon and a new shapefile of the original polygons enriched with three new fields: avg_elev, avg_min_elev, and avg_max_elev.

name: Calculate transit delay rate by neighbourhood
desc: The script computes the ratio of transit delays to transit stops within each Toronto neighbourhood boundary, using point-in-polygon counting and field-based arithmetic. It loads neighbourhood polygons (Neighbourhoods - 2952.gpkg), TTC delay events (delays_qgis.gpkg), and GTFS stop locations (stops.txt), counts delays and stops per neighbourhood, then calculates and stores 'delay_rate' = delay_count / stop_count (0 if no stops). Output is a GeoPackage layer 'delay_rate_by_neighbourhood.gpkg' with attributes: original neighbourhood geometry + 'delay_count', 'stop_count', and 'delay_rate' (double).

name: Extract monthly and annual precipitation
desc: The script processes a NetCDF file containing precipitation data (variable 'pre') to extract user-selected monthly rasters (e.g., 2020_Mouth_07.tif) and optionally generate two annual summary rasters: total accumulated precipitation (Annual_Total.tif) and daily mean precipitation (Annual_Daily_Avg.tif). It reads longitude/latitude metadata via GDAL NETCDF subdatasets, reprojects to EPSG:4326, applies data cleaning (masking values outside [-9000, 10000]), flips and transposes arrays for correct orientation, computes month-length-weighted annual totals, and saves outputs as GeoTIFFs added to the QGIS project.

name: Extract annual and monthly precipitation
desc: The script processes a NetCDF file containing precipitation data (variable 'pre') to compute annual total precipitation (weighted by days in each month) and annual daily mean precipitation. It also optionally extracts individual monthly precipitation rasters based on user-specified comma-separated month numbers (e.g., '1,6,12'). Input is a single NC file; geographic metadata (longitude, latitude, EPSG:4326) is extracted via GDAL NETCDF subdataset syntax. Outputs are GeoTIFFs written to a temporary directory and auto-loaded into QGIS as raster layers: one for annual total, one for annual daily average, and zero or more for selected months. The script includes data cleaning (masking values outside [-9000, 10000)), array orientation correction (transpose + fliplr), and proper georeferencing using computed geotransform and WKT projection.

name: Classify vegetation trend dynamics
desc: The script performs two optional tasks: (1) converts NDVI rasters to Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) using a pixel-wise binary model (FVC = min(1, max(0, (NDVI - Soil_NDVI) / (Veg_NDVI - Soil_NDVI))); and (2) generates a five-class vegetation trend map by combining slope (trend magnitude), p-value (statistical significance), and user-defined P_limit threshold. Classification logic assigns values 1–5 based on sign of slope and p-value ranges: 1=significant degradation (p<0.05 & slope<0), 2=minor degradation (0.05≤p<P_limit & slope<0), 3=stable (p≥P_limit), 4=minor improvement (0.05≤p<P_limit & slope>0), 5=significant improvement (p<0.05 & slope>0). Outputs include FVC rasters (if enabled) and a final classified raster 'Veg_Trend_5Class_Final.tif', automatically loaded into QGIS.

name: FVC long-term trend analysis
desc: The script performs non-parametric trend analysis on a time series of FVC (Fractional Vegetation Cover) rasters to compute Theil-Sen slope (annual change rate) and Modified Mann-Kendall p-value (statistical significance) per pixel. It reads stacked GeoTIFF files from an input folder, applies validity filtering (-0.1 to 1.1), requires ≥10 valid observations per pixel, uses scipy.stats.theilslopes and pymannkendall.modified_mk_test (with fallback to original_test), processes data in row-wise chunks via ThreadPoolExecutor (9 workers), and outputs two aligned GeoTIFFs: one for slope values and one for p-values, both with -9999.0 as NoData. Input extent is optional; if provided, analysis is clipped accordingly.

name: Standardize NDVI V2 raster data
desc: The script performs automated preprocessing of NDVI V2 series raster datasets, including spatial topology repair via dual buffering (buffer ±0.05), coordinate system reprojection to a user-specified CRS (default ESRI:102025), resampling to user-defined resolution (e.g., 1000m), and physical value conversion by applying scale factor 0.0001 to raw pixel values. Outputs are renamed TIFF files following 'NDVImax{year}_{resolution}' naming convention (e.g., 'NDVImax2020_1km.tif') and automatically added to the QGIS project.

name: Compute wind turbine shadow hours
desc: The script computes annual worst-case shadow hours cast by wind turbine generators (WTGs) on flat terrain using solar position modeling and geometric shadow accumulation. It reads turbine locations, rotor diameter, and hub height from a QGIS vector layer; generates hourly solar azimuth and elevation timestamps for a given year and timezone (Europe/Rome); calculates shadow extent per timestep across a buffered raster grid; accumulates total shadow hours per cell; and outputs a styled GeoTIFF raster with pseudo-color rendering. Input CRS must be projected (metric), and output includes automatic no-data handling (-9999.0) and map layer addition to QGIS project.

name: Calculate kappa coefficient for classification accuracy
desc: The script calculates the Kappa Index of Agreement (KIA) to assess classification accuracy by comparing a classification raster layer against a reference raster layer using QGIS's native:kappaindex algorithm. It loads two raster layers (identical in this case, both pointing to 'continuous_values.tif'), validates them, runs the kappa index calculation, saves the output as a GeoPackage containing the error matrix and KIA value, and loads the resulting vector layer into the QGIS project. The script explicitly states its purpose in comments: 'Kappa calculation requires classification and reference grids' and uses the 'native:kappaindex' algorithm which produces an error matrix and KIA.

name: Process urban infrastructure layers
desc: The script processes three vector datasets representing urban infrastructure in China: (1) validates and converts city point geometries (from multipoint to single-point), (2) generates minimum enclosing circles around road segments and reprojects them to WGS84 (EPSG:4326), and (3) tessellates building footprints into triangular meshes. All processed layers are then merged into a single integrated vector layer (integrated_analysis.shp) for multi-representation spatial analysis of human settlements and built environment features.

name: Rasterize sampling points to grid
desc: The script converts a GeoJSON point vector layer ('sampling_points.geojson') into a raster using QGIS's GDAL Rasterize algorithm. It burns the 'value' field from the points into a Float32 raster with 0.5-degree pixel resolution, aligned to the input layer's extent, and assigns NoData = -9999. The output is saved as 'point_raster_from_points.tif' and loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Calculate moon surface slope
desc: The script calculates slope from a lunar digital elevation model (DEM) file (e.g., 'PIA12927.tif') using QGIS-based geoprocessing or manual numpy gradient methods. It loads the DEM as a QgsRasterLayer, computes slope in degrees using either GDAL's 'gdal:slope' algorithm (via QGIS Processing) or manual finite-difference gradients, then generates terrain assessment metrics (min/mean/max/std/slope percentiles), landing suitability classification ('Good'/'Challenging'), and risk level ('Low'/'Medium'/'High') based on mean slope thresholds (5°, 15°, 30°). Outputs include a slope raster (or numpy array), slope statistics text file, and a structured JSON report with metadata, statistics, thresholds, and moon-specific interpretations stored in 'json_results/slope_analysis_results.json'.

name: Detect debris flow paths
desc: The script detects debris flow initiation and path zones on lunar terrain using slope thresholding applied to a precomputed DEM. It loads a local raster DEM file (e.g., 'lunar_slope.tif', 'lunar_aspect.tif', or 'terrain_output.tif'), calculates slope and hillshade using GDAL algorithms, generates a binary debris flow path raster via raster calculator (where slope > threshold), and converts the result to a vector shapefile. The analysis is explicitly optimized for lunar terrain (slope_threshold=18.0), and outputs include slope.tif, hillshade.tif, debris_flow_paths.tif, and debris_flow_paths.shp — all saved locally in 'debris_path_output/'. No satellite imagery, time-series, or Earth-based geospatial data is used; inputs are pre-generated local rasters with no metadata about origin, acquisition date, or projection beyond CRS inference from QGIS layer loading. Study area is not specified beyond 'lunar' context.

name: Calculate terrain ruggedness index
desc: The script calculates Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI) from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) using multiple QGIS processing algorithms: SAGA Terrain Ruggedness Index, GDAL focal statistics (standard deviation and range), and QGIS raster calculator with custom approximation. It loads the DEM, computes TRI layers with configurable neighborhood size (default 3x3), analyzes ruggedness zones by categorizing mean TRI values into LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/VERY HIGH classes, and generates a comprehensive text report containing layer metadata, statistics, methodology, formula explanation, categories, and recommendations. Outputs include four TRI rasters (tri_saga.tif, tri_focal.tif, tri_range.tif, tri_calculator.tif) and a detailed analysis report (terrain_ruggedness_analysis_report.txt).

name: Detect scarps and headwalls
desc: The script detects scarps and headwalls using multi-parameter terrain analysis on a Digital Elevation Model (DEM). It loads a local DEM file (e.g., 'lunar_slope.tif', 'lunar_aspect.tif', or 'terrain_output.tif'), then computes GDAL-based terrain derivatives: slope (degrees), hillshade (visual enhancement), curvature (morphometric edge detection), aspect (orientation), and Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI). Detection applies raster algebra (logical AND) across user-configurable thresholds on slope (>25.0°), curvature (>0.0008), and TRI (>0.3), producing a binary scarp/headwall raster. This is vectorized into a shapefile ('scarps_headwalls.shp') for manual editing. Outputs include seven geospatial files (slope.tif, hillshade.tif, curvature.tif, aspect.tif, tri.tif, scarps_headwalls.tif, scarps_headwalls.shp) and a comprehensive text report with statistics, methodology, and recommendations. The script explicitly targets lunar terrain (evidenced by DEM filenames 'lunar_slope.tif' and 'lunar_aspect.tif' and comment 'Optimized for lunar terrain'), and no satellite, sensor, or temporal metadata is embedded — all inputs are pre-processed local rasters.

name: Calculate moon surface slope
desc: The script calculates slope from a lunar digital elevation model (DEM) TIFF file using three fallback methods: QGIS processing GDAL slope algorithm, manual numpy gradient-based calculation, or simple statistical estimation. It loads the raster into QGIS, computes slope in degrees, analyzes terrain suitability for moon landing based on mean slope thresholds (<5° excellent, <15° acceptable, >15° challenging), saves slope output (raster or numpy array), generates statistics (min/max/mean/std), and produces a lunar slope analysis report with risk level classification. Input is a single TIF file (e.g., 'PIA12927.tif'), and outputs include slope rasters/numpy arrays, statistics text files, and a formatted TXT report.

name: Transform LADM-COL 1.0 geospatial data
desc: The script performs an ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) process on a Colombian Land Administration Domain Model (LADM-COL) v1.0 GeoPackage to validate and restructure spatial and attribute data for compliance with the LADM-COL 1.0 standard. It extracts non-null features (filtering by 'T_Id IS NOT NULL') from cadastral and administrative boundary layers (e.g., municipalities, corregimientos, barrios, urban/rural sectors, homogenous zones), then executes a series of attribute joins across core LADM tables — linking terreno (land parcels) to predio (real estate units) via uebaunit, joining predio types, rights (derecho), construction units (unidadconstruccion), constructions (construccion), and addresses (direccion) using foreign key relationships (e.g., baunit ↔ t_id, tipo ↔ t_id). It also computes a derived field 'planta_total' by concatenating iliCode and planta_ubicacion. The output is a cleaned, joined, and standardized GeoPackage containing renamed and enriched layers aligned with LADM-COL 1.0 semantics and naming conventions (e.g., 'CC_Limite_Municipio', 'lc_predio', 'Zona_homo_fisicaurbana', 'lc_unidadconstruccion').

name: Transform cadastral model layers
desc: The script performs an ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) process on a Colombian cadastral GeoPackage (GPKG) to standardize, validate, and enrich spatial layers for internal modeling. It extracts non-null features (using 'T_Id is not NULL') from 25 administrative, zoning, and cadastral layers (e.g., CC_Limite_Municipio, AV_ZHGU, lc_terreno), then executes multi-step attribute joins to link units (uebaunit), parcels (ilc_predio), rights (ilc_derecho), addresses (extdireccion), and construction units (lc_unidad) with their respective type codes (iliCode) from domain tables. Critical outputs include: (1) cleaned geometry tables with consistent naming (e.g., 'Zona_homo_geoeconomicaurbana'), (2) joined parcel-layer 'lc_predio', (3) enriched 'lc_derecho_tipo' with right-type iliCode, (4) fully constructed 'Extdireccion' with formatted 'direccion_completa' using street hierarchy logic and fallbacks, and (5) 'lc_unidadconstruccion' with computed 'piso_total' field. All outputs are written to a new GeoPackage with schema-aligned table names and geometry columns.

name: Compute ISO9613 LpA Raster
desc: The script computes a sound pressure level A-weighted (LpA) raster in dB over a DEM grid using 3D distance, manual atmospheric absorption, and simplified ground effect attenuation. It supports point sources with LwA or octave-band spectra, optional linear barriers with height-defined diffraction modeling, and configurable meteorological parameters (temperature, humidity, pressure). Key steps include source-spectrum construction (flat, turbine-shaped, or field-based), barrier profile selection via line-of-sight intersection, broadband or octave-band propagation loss calculation (ISO 9613-1/2), and tiled raster computation with nodata handling. Output is a GeoTIFF LpA raster aligned to the input DEM window.

name: Compute ISO9613 sound pressure level
desc: The script computes A-weighted sound pressure level (LpA in dB) at receptor points using the ISO 9613-2 standard for outdoor sound propagation. It processes point sources and receptors, samples elevation from a DEM, optionally applies atmospheric absorption (using temperature, humidity, pressure), ground effect attenuation (simplified or octave-band), and barrier diffraction modeling (via single-screen approximation with line barriers). Inputs include source LwA or octave-band sound power levels, source/receptor heights, barrier geometry and height, and DEM raster. Output is a vector layer of receptors with an added 'LpA_dB' field.

name: Generate contour lines from elevation data
desc: The script generates contour lines from Copernicus GLO-30 global 30-meter DEM tiles hosted on AWS. It calculates which 1°×1° tiles intersect the user-defined area of interest (EPSG:4326 extent), downloads them as COGs, clips them to the AOI using GDAL Warp, merges the clipped rasters, optionally applies TPI-guided Gaussian smoothing (None/Low/Medium/High), converts elevation units (metres/feet), and generates vector contour lines using GDAL ContourGenerate. Outputs include a styled vector layer with rule-based symbology (index/normal contours) and optional hillshade-based Elevation Overlay raster layer with preconfigured QML styling (Dodge blend mode, cubic resampling, hillshade renderer).

name: Generate implement swath polygon
desc: The script processes input line features (e.g., tractor or machinery pass trajectories) by exploding multi-part lines into single segments, then creates a buffer polygon around each segment with a user-defined width equal to half the implement size (e.g., 16 m → 8 m radius), producing a continuous or segmented polygon layer representing the spatial footprint ('rastro') of agricultural implements such as sprayers, spreaders, or tillage tools. Output is a vector polygon layer named 'Rastro_Implemento' in the same CRS and field schema as the input line layer.

name: Generate implement track from line layer
desc: The script generates a 'rastro' (track) polygon layer from an input line vector layer by first exploding multiline features into single parts, then applying a buffer operation with a distance equal to half the provided 'tamanhoimplemento' value. It supports saving output to memory or to disk (shapefile), preserves user preferences for last used layer ID and implement width, validates input geometry type (must be LineGeometry), and handles selected features only mode. Outputs include a newly added QgsVectorLayer named 'Rastro_Implemento' or custom name, optionally styled and loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Analyze land parcel overlay
desc: The script performs spatial intersection analysis between a reference land parcel (first polygon from the 'Imóvel' layer) and multiple user-provided vector layers (e.g., protected areas, zoning, environmental constraints). It computes geometric intersections, preserves original attributes with sanitized field names (truncated to 10 chars, prefixed on conflict), and outputs two products: (1) a summary report table containing per-layer statistics — 'id_imovel', 'camada', 'area_m2', and 'percent' of parcel area overlapped; and (2) a polygon feature layer of all intersected geometries, enriched with the original attributes from each source layer (mapped via name-sanitized field correspondence). The workflow includes spatial filtering ('extractbylocation'), geometry validation ('fixgeometries'), and precise attribute alignment using field name mapping derived from input layer schemas.

name: Generate multiscale riparian and circular buffers
desc: The script automates the generation of multi-scale spatial buffers—both circular (around point-based field collection sites) and riparian (along linear water features)—using adaptive, spreadsheet-driven parameters. It detects and matches site-specific polygons (e.g., watersheds, contribution areas) to collected points via ID field matching; clips buffers to those polygons; classifies resulting buffers as either valid 'Local Contribution Areas' (LCA) or 'extrapolated areas' based on area comparison with the source polygon; optionally applies difference operations (e.g., removing river lines from riparian buffers); and outputs georeferenced shapefiles organized in a hierarchical directory structure (e.g., '1BUFFER_CIRCULAR', '7RB_Temporary', '9RBLCA'). All results are loaded into QGIS with standardized symbology for visual interpretation.

name: Detect plant species in drone imagery
desc: The script performs AI-assisted detection of plant species (e.g., by common name and scientific name) in drone-captured raster imagery. It applies preprocessing, runs object detection using a pre-trained model, outputs polygon bounding boxes with attributes including biome, category, confidence score, class ID, dimensions, and optionally common/scientific names. It styles the output vector layer with categorized outlines and white-haloed labels, and optionally generates a PDF report summarizing detections. Inputs include a raster layer, confidence threshold, and optional report path; outputs are a styled polygon vector layer and optionally a PDF report.

name: Plan drone flight paths for vegetation mapping
desc: The script generates optimized lawn-mower-style drone flight paths over a user-defined polygon area (AOI), oriented either parallel or perpendicular to a specified line or two-point direction. It computes waypoints based on drone camera specifications (e.g., DJI Mavic 3E/3T sensor geometry, focal length, resolution), flight altitude, speed, and overlap settings; respects mission time limits and corner chamfering; outputs Litchi-compatible CSV files, vector layers for paths and waypoints, and an orientation preview line. All outputs are saved in structured folders (CSVs under VOOS_*, SHPs under SHP) with automatic styling and project loading in QGIS.

name: Assign dominant land cover class
desc: The script assigns the dominant (majority) and subdominant (second majority) land cover class to each input polygon based on underlying raster pixel values, along with their proportional coverage (%). It uses either a built-in 34-class Somalia land cover legend or a user-provided CSV legend mapping pixel values to class codes and names. The output is a vector layer with added fields: dominant_class_code, dominant_class_name, dominant_pixel_value, dominant_coverage_pct, subdominant_class_code, subdominant_class_name, subdominant_pixel_value, and subdominant_coverage_pct.

name: Detect target infrastructure polygons
desc: The script identifies candidate target polygons for infrastructure planning by analyzing spatial relationships among three input layers: 'Postes' (utility poles), 'Iluminação pública' (public lighting fixtures), and 'Rede BT' (low-voltage power distribution network). It filters poles that are within a maximum distance of BT infrastructure but outside a minimum distance from public lighting, groups qualifying poles into square clusters, applies external buffering, subtracts buffered IP and FlyTap pole geometries as exclusion masks, and outputs only resulting polygons above a minimum area threshold. The output is a vector layer of target polygons in EPSG:3857.

name: Load ship route telemetry with wind analysis
desc: The script loads a GeoJSON or JSON file containing ship route waypoints with embedded telemetry and environmental properties (e.g., wind speed components 'u_wind_speed'/'v_wind_speed', currents 'u_currents'/'v_currents', fuel consumption, speed, time). It constructs two QGIS memory layers: (1) a point layer ('Ship Waypoints (Telemetry)') with attributes including ID, timestamp, step duration, coordinates, speed, fuel rate, step/total distance/fuel, wind/current magnitude, and wind resistance; and (2) a line layer ('Ship Route Path') visualizing the full route as a polyline. Wind speed is computed from u/v components using Euclidean norm; distances are measured on WGS84 ellipsoid; cumulative fuel is integrated per leg. The point layer includes an HTML map tip displaying telemetry and environmental metrics. Both layers are added to the current QGIS project.

name: Classify land cover with RF
desc: The script performs supervised classification of multiband raster imagery using Random Forest, incorporating spectral bands (R,G,B,NIR,SWIR1,SWIR2), derived spectral indices (e.g., NDVI, EVI2, NBR, BSI, ARVI), and optional local entropy texture features. It supports stratified random sampling from polygon training zones, robust feature scaling, blockwise inference, and post-processing (small-patch removal and mode filtering). Outputs include a classified raster (0=NoData, classes start at 1), optional trained model (.joblib + metadata JSON), and metrics report (OOB/validation accuracy, kappa, confusion matrix, classification report).

name: Classify field in quantiles
desc: The script classifies a numeric attribute field of a vector polygon layer into quantile-based classes (e.g., quartiles or deciles) by computing percentile thresholds, assigning integer class labels to features based on value ranges, and adding the new classification field directly to the input layer's attribute table. It uses QgsVectorLayer editing, numpy percentile calculation, and QGIS Processing framework integration; outputs include the modified layer with the new integer field and CRS information.

name: Clean points by raster kernel value
desc: The script filters a point vector layer ('Inventory') using a raster ('Slope') by applying a moving maximum kernel (size = 2*BufferRadiousInPxl+1) to the raster, then masks points where the kernel-maximized raster value is below 'minSlopeAcceptable'. Points are retained only if they fall within raster cells where the kernel-maximized slope meets the threshold and the original raster cell is valid (not nodata). The output is a cleaned point vector layer containing only qualifying points.

name: Convert points to grid raster
desc: The script converts a vector point layer into a raster grid by counting point occurrences within each raster cell of an input raster. It reads the input raster's geotransform and projection, extracts point geometries, maps them to raster pixel indices using coordinate arithmetic, and increments cell values for each point falling within the specified extent. The output is a GeoTIFF raster where pixel values represent point counts per cell, with NoData value -9999.

name: Convert polygon grid to raster
desc: The script converts a vector polygon layer (grid) into a raster grid with user-defined pixel width (w) and height (h). It computes the extent of the input polygon layer, calculates raster dimensions based on the extent and pixel size, initializes a float32 raster array filled with -10, writes it to a GeoTIFF output with correct geotransform and projection (inherited from input), and sets NoData value to -9999. The output is a raster file representing the grid geometry as a regular raster with uniform cell size.

name: Sample training validation points
desc: The script randomly samples training and validation point datasets from an input point layer, constrained so that no pixel (defined by user-specified width/height) contains both training and validation points. It rasterizes the input points, clips to a contour polygon mask, converts points to pixel indices, partitions indices based on user-defined percentage, and outputs two shapefiles: one for training points and one for validation points. The workflow uses GDAL rasterization and clipping, NumPy array indexing, and QGIS vector layer I/O.

name: Calculate kernel statistics from raster
desc: The script calculates kernel-based statistical metrics (real, max, min, std, sum, average, range) from a raster layer around input point features, using a user-defined buffer radius in pixels. It reads a raster and point vector layer, clips/aligns the raster to a contour polygon extent, identifies pixel locations corresponding to points, applies scipy.ndimage generic filters with square kernels of size (2*radius+1), extracts values at point locations, and writes results as attributes in a new shapefile with point geometries.

name: Classify presence-absence confusion matrix
desc: The script computes a confusion matrix for a binary classification problem using a vector layer of covariates and a dependent variable field. It calculates True Positives (0), True Negatives (1), False Positives (2), and False Negatives (3) by applying a cutoff threshold (either percentile-based or Youden index-derived) to an 'Index' field against a binary 'Field of dependent variable' (0 = absence, >0 = presence). The output is a GeoPackage file containing the original features augmented with a 'tptnfpfn' integer field encoding the confusion matrix class, preserving geometry and other attributes.

name: Validate QGIS processing integration assumptions
desc: The script validates three critical assumptions for GeoLineage Phase 1.5: (1) reliability of monkey-patching processing.run() to intercept algorithm execution, (2) layer ID persistence and uniqueness across chained native:buffer → native:dissolve → native:savefeatures steps, and (3) feasibility of detecting export/save events via QgsVectorFileWriter signals, QgsProject layer signals, and QgsVectorLayer edit signals — all within a headless Flatpak QGIS environment. Outputs include a structured log of intercepted processing calls, layer ID fingerprints, signal enumeration results, and a summary report identifying that export detection must rely on processing.run() interception (e.g., of native:savefeatures) rather than silent writeAsVectorFormat calls.

name: Detect flood extent change
desc: The script detects and quantifies spatiotemporal changes in flood extent in Jakarta by computing spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, MNDWI, NDBI, SAVI) from Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery for two dates (25 October 2024 and 28 May 2025), generating temporal difference rasters (e.g., DIFF_NDWI), and assembling a 25-band stacked raster (spectral bands × 2 + indices × 2 + 5 differences) optimized for supervised classification of inundated vs. non-inundated areas. Outputs include visual composites (RGB, IRC, IRC_agriculture), per-date index maps, difference rasters, and a ready-to-classify multiband stack.

name: Detect monotonic trend in raster time series
desc: The script performs pixel-wise Mann-Kendall and Seasonal Mann-Kendall trend analysis on a user-provided, time-ordered stack of raster layers (e.g., NDVI, precipitation, temperature). It computes Kendall's Tau, p-value, Sen's Slope, and a binary significance mask for each pixel. Inputs must share identical extent, resolution, and CRS; layers must be chronologically ordered. Outputs are four GeoTIFF rasters: sens_slope.tif, p_value.tif, kendall_tau.tif, and significance_mask.tif, written to a specified folder and auto-loaded into QGIS.

name: Assess urban infrastructure risk
desc: The script performs a multi-step urban spatial analysis in QGIS using vector and raster GIS operations: (1) buffers critical infrastructure points to define safety perimeters; (2) counts point-of-interest (POI) density per administrative or planning zone via spatial join; (3) generates a kernel density heatmap from environmental sensor locations weighted by AQI values; (4) computes Euclidean distance from each zone centroid to the nearest emergency facility (filtered by 'emergency' category); and (5) calculates a composite environmental risk score per zone integrating population density, flood risk class, NDVI-derived vegetation penalty, and count of warning-status sensors within the zone. Outputs include buffered polygon layers, attribute-enriched zone layers, a heatmap raster, console-printed distance metrics, and a tabulated risk index with breakdowns.

name: Package QGIS project layers
desc: The script packages a QGIS project (.qgz) by exporting vector layers to GeoPackage(s), copying local raster files and associated sidecars, embedding layer styles into GeoPackages, preserving media assets (e.g., SVG, images), remapping all layer sources and asset paths relative to the output archive, and generating a ZIP package containing the remapped project, GeoPackages, rasters, media, styles, and an audit PDF/HTML report. It applies filtering (skip empty, duplicate, remote layers), supports grouping vectors by layer tree path into separate GeoPackages, retains filtered subsets optionally, and logs success/skipped/failed items.

name: Detect raster time-series change points
desc: The script detects abrupt temporal shifts in a time-ordered stack of aligned rasters using Pettitt's non-parametric change point test. It validates raster alignment (size, geotransform, CRS), loads pixel time series into a stack, applies vectorized Pettitt testing per pixel to compute change step, magnitude, direction, p-value, and segment means, then writes nine spatial outputs including change_step.tif, change_time.tif, change_magnitude.tif, direction.tif, p_value.tif, significance_mask.tif, pettitt_k.tif, before_mean.tif, and after_mean.tif — all georeferenced to the first input raster’s geometry. Outputs are written as GeoTIFFs with LZW compression and accompanied by a structured text report.

name: Identify infrastructure management targets
desc: The script identifies management-target infrastructure facilities by evaluating whether their service area population falls below a minimum threshold. It loads a gridded population layer (with BAU and SN1 scenario years: 2025–2040), scans POI vector files (e.g., shapefiles, GeoPackages) from a user-specified folder, optionally applies facility-specific service radii and minimum catchment populations (or defaults), computes population sums within buffered geometries using spatial indexing and point-in-polygon containment, and outputs per-facility GeoPackage layers with binary management status columns (_b25, _b30, ..., _s40). Each output feature retains original attributes plus scenario-specific 0/1 flags indicating 'management required' (1) if service-area population < threshold.

name: Calculate facility accessibility index
desc: The script calculates facility accessibility ("향유도") for administrative districts (si-gun-gu) using population grids and point-of-interest (POI) facility layers. It loads population data across four future years (2025–2040) under two scenarios (BAU: T_25–T_40; SN1: pop_2025–pop_2040), computes service areas via buffer analysis around each POI layer, aggregates covered population per district, and derives accessibility as the ratio of served population to total district population. Outputs include a tabular result (facility × district × scenario-year) and an optional enriched district polygon layer with per-facility, per-year accessibility values.

name: Map canopy vegetation extent and height
desc: The script maps the spatial extent of canopy vegetation (LiDAR classification class 5) over Grigny, France, by merging and filtering four LAS point cloud files to retain only ground-filtered vegetation points, rasterizing them at 1 m resolution, vectorizing the resulting binary presence raster into polygons, repairing geometries, and computing zonal mean height statistics against a normalized Digital Surface Model (nDSM); outputs include a 1-m vegetation presence raster, a shapefile of vegetation polygons with area attributes, and a statistics-enhanced shapefile with weighted-mean canopy height (in meters), min/max heights, and total vegetated surface area (m²/km²).

name: Extract building footprints from LiDAR classification
desc: The script extracts building footprints (class 6) from four LAS files using PDAL to filter and rasterize LiDAR points, then vectorizes the resulting binary raster, computes building polygon areas, fixes geometries, and calculates zonal statistics (mean height) against a normalized Digital Surface Model (nDSM). Outputs include a presence raster (batiments_classe_6.tif), raw and fixed building polygons (batiments_polygones.shp, batiments_polygones_fixed.shp), and a statistics layer with area-weighted mean building height (batiments_polygones_stats.shp).

name: Classify flood hazard levels
desc: The script classifies flood hazard into four levels (0=Low, 1=Medium, 2=High, 3=Very High) using input depth (m) and velocity (m/s) rasters. It computes depth-velocity product (d*v), applies threshold logic with configurable epsilon tolerance and inclusive boundaries, handles raster alignment via GDAL Warp resampling (Nearest/Bilinear/Cubic), masks NoData and near-zero values, and outputs a UInt8 GeoTIFF with gray single-band encoding (no palette). The algorithm supports auto-derivation of depth/velocity rasters from an active layer’s name pattern (e.g., '_d_HR_Max', '_V_HR_Max') and includes fallback sibling-file lookup.

name: Extract inundation boundary from flood depth raster
desc: The script processes a TUFLOW-simulated flood depth raster to generate a closed polygon vector layer representing the inundation boundary. It first applies a raster calculator to create a binary mask where depth exceeds a user-defined cutoff (default 0.05 m), then polygonizes the mask, filters for flooded pixels (DN = 1), dissolves contiguous areas into seamless polygons, and optionally simplifies (Douglas-Peucker) and smooths (Chaikin algorithm) the resulting geometry before outputting a clean, topologically valid inundation boundary layer.

name: Compute peak flow and volume from TUFLOW output
desc: The script loads TUFLOW plot output (PO) line shapefiles derived from raster grids, reads associated CSV time-series files containing flow data, computes peak flow (QP) and total volume (QV) per feature using trapezoidal integration, updates the PO line layer attributes with QP and QV values, saves the updated layer as a new shapefile (_QP.shp), applies styling, and inserts it into the QGIS project layer tree. Input CSVs are resolved relative to the PO layer path, and ID matching uses robust normalization and variant generation (e.g., 'Q123', '123', '00123').

name: Sample depth level velocity at points
desc: The script samples raster values (Depth, Level, Velocity) from d/h/v grid rasters and terrain elevation from DEM layers at user-provided point locations. It extracts scenario base names from grid layer names (e.g., 'EX_100YR_CC_24hr_MHWS10+1m_Baseline_003'), locates corresponding d/h/v rasters by pattern-matching filenames in the same directory, samples values using QgsRasterLayer.dataProvider().sample(), and writes results to a memory vector layer with fields ID, X, Y, Terrain, Depth, Level, Velocity. Outputs are saved as PLOT_P_Sampled.shp files per scenario and loaded into QGIS with styling, while paths and layer names are stored in global QGIS variables for downstream use.

name: Sample raster elevation at vertices
desc: The script samples Z (elevation) values from one or more raster layers at the vertices of input vector geometries (points, lines, or polygons) in QGIS. It supports densification, polygon ring selection (exterior-only), closure vertex inclusion, band selection, and multiple rasters with 'last valid wins' or separate-field sampling logic. Outputs a new PointZ layer with attributes including Z value, optional raster source name ('z_src'), optional source feature ID ('src_fid'), and optional vertex index ('v_idx'). Progress feedback and batched writes ensure responsiveness.

name: Sample raster elevation values on grid
desc: The script samples Z (elevation or value) from one or more raster layers at regularly spaced grid points (dx = dy), optionally clipped to a polygon or user-defined extent. It supports two output modes: 'last valid wins' (single Z field + optional source name) or 'separate fields' (one field per raster). Outputs a new PointZ vector layer with geometry (x, y, z) and attribute fields including ID, Z, and optionally raster source name. Sampling respects CRS transformations, nodata handling, user-defined band selection, and optional value-range filtering (e.g., to exclude near-zero values).

name: Export XMDF mesh dataset
desc: The script reads an XMDF mesh file using QGIS's MDAL driver, optionally locates a companion .2dm mesh geometry file, lists available dataset groups and their timestep counts, lets the user select a group (via dialog or parameter), resolves a timestep index (0 = last), estimates output GeoTIFF size based on mesh extent and user-defined grid size, warns if estimated size exceeds 1 GB, and rasterizes the selected dataset group at the chosen timestep to a GeoTIFF using QGIS's native:rasterizemeshdataset algorithm. Outputs include the exported GeoTIFF raster and registration of the layer in the QGIS project.

name: Convert DSM to DTM
desc: The script converts a Digital Surface Model (DSM) raster to a Digital Terrain Model (DTM) using Progressive Morphological Filtering to remove non-ground features (e.g., buildings, vegetation). It reads the input DSM, optionally reprojects from geographic to UTM for metric kernel sizing, applies the dsm_to_dtm algorithm with user-specified radius (meters) and slope (0=auto), preserves original geotransform (including rotation/skew), and writes a losslessly compressed GeoTIFF output with PREDICTOR=3, DEFLATE compression, and tiled layout. The nodata value is clamped to -9999.0 for cross-software compatibility.

name: Monitor deforestation temporal series
desc: The script loads and visualizes cloud-filtered satellite imagery (Landsat 5/8/9 or Sentinel-2) over a user-defined area of interest (AOI) for a specified date range. It applies sensor-specific cloud masking, atmospheric correction scaling, and RGB band compositing (e.g., SR_B3/SR_B2/SR_B1 for Landsat 5; B4/B3/B2 for Sentinel-2), then generates XYZ tile layers for each valid image and adds them to the QGIS project as raster layers named with acquisition date and satellite type. Outputs are time-stamped preview layers in QGIS, not exported products.

name: Generate global grid index
desc: The script builds a global rectangular polygon grid in EPSG:4326 covering [-180,180] × [-90,90] with configurable cell size (default 0.4°), assigning each cell a two-letter row label (AA, AB, …) and a zero-padded three-digit column label (001, 002, …); it creates an in-memory QGIS vector layer named 'global_grid_index' with fields 'row_value' and 'col_value', populates it with non-overlapping rectangular polygons, and adds it to the current QGIS project.

name: Adaptively grid leucena occurrence points
desc: The script computes point counts of leucena occurrence points within a polygon grid ('grid-leucenas'), then recursively subdivides cells with >6 points into quadrants (up to two levels) to produce an adaptive hierarchical grid layer named 'adaptive_grid'. It updates NUMPOINTS on the source grid, assigns hierarchical GRID_IDs (e.g., '12-3', '12-3-2'), sets grid_status to 'not finished yet' or 'no point', and renumbers fid sequentially. The output is a new in-memory vector layer added to the QGIS project.

name: Estimate above ground carbon
desc: The script estimates Above Ground Carbon (AGC) in tons C/ha using a Random Forest regression model trained on field-measured AGB (ton/ha) points and raster-derived spectral features: RED, NIR, and kNDVI. It computes kNDVI pixel-wise using RBF kernel with σ = 0.5 × (NIR + RED), extracts RED and NIR band values at sample points via raster sampling, converts AGB to AGC using IPCC 2006 factor (×0.47), trains RF on [RED, NIR, kNDVI], and applies the model to predict AGC across the full RED/NIR raster extent. Outputs include a GeoTIFF raster of predicted AGC (Ton C/ha), plus summary statistics (total AGC, area with AGC > 0, mean AGC/ha, R², RMSE).

name: Classify multiscale topographic position
desc: The script implements a QGIS Processing algorithm for multiscale topographic position classification, which categorizes terrain into nine classes (e.g., Lowland hollow, Upland knoll) based on raster input. It applies a fixed categorical renderer using predefined HSV-based color palettes, handles raster input materialization (including JP2-to-GeoTIFF conversion), manages vector input normalization and export to GeoPackage, enforces output overwrite behavior, validates GeoPackage schema integrity, and integrates with QGIS feedback mechanisms for progress, warnings, and error reporting. Outputs include classified raster files with embedded QML styling and optional auxiliary reports.

name: Generate snapshot view
desc: The script enables users to generate a temporal-spatial snapshot view of geospatial features stored in an audit schema. It retrieves the earliest available snapshot date from the 'audit.snapshot' table, constrains the user-selectable date range between that first date and yesterday, allows defining a spatial extent via exploitation/municipality selection, map canvas extent, or manual drawing, and then executes the 'gw_fct_getsnapshot' database procedure with the selected date, WKT polygon, and feature types. The resulting layers are dynamically created as temporary QGIS vector layers with rule-based styling (red=Deleted, yellow=Updated, blue=Existent) grouped under a 'Snapshot - YYYY-MM-DD' TOC group.

name: Encode raster image features with SAM
desc: The script encodes input raster imagery into high-dimensional feature embeddings using the Segment Anything Model (SAM) image encoder. It accepts a raster layer, selects up to three bands (defaulting to first available), rescales pixel values to [0,255] based on min-max statistics within a user-defined extent, reprojects and resamples to target CRS/resolution (converting geographic CRS to UTM if needed), samples patches via a grid sampler with configurable stride, runs the SAM encoder (vit_b/vit_l/vit_h) on GPU/CPU, and saves output feature rasters (GeoTIFF) with metadata and an index CSV. Outputs include encoded feature tiles aligned to spatial bounding boxes and a summary CSV tracking patch locations, CRS, resolution, and model type.

name: Split samples into train test
desc: The script partitions a vector layer of geospatial sample points or polygons into two disjoint subsets—train and test—using a user-specified percentage (default 70%) for training. It first randomly extracts the specified percentage of features from the input 'Samples' layer using QGIS's native:randomextract algorithm, then computes the set difference (remaining features) as the test subset using native:difference. Outputs are two vector layers: 'Train subset' containing the randomly selected training samples, and 'Test subset' containing the complementary hold-out samples—both preserving original geometry and attributes.

name: Search vector layer features
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin for searching vector layer features using text-based, parcel-number (tiban), or owner-based queries. It supports configurable search fields, fuzzy matching, field alias resolution, full-width to half-width character normalization (via jaconv), PostgreSQL database layer loading, and multi-layer result aggregation with tabbed display. Key operations include building QgsExpression queries, executing QgsFeatureRequest searches, zooming/panning to selected features with CRS transformation, applying map themes, and handling both current and named layers. Outputs include a ResultDialog showing tabulated feature attributes and interactive zoom-to-feature functionality.

name: Calculate holding racetrack area
desc: The script computes aviation holding pattern or racetrack geometry based on aircraft performance parameters (IAS, altitude, bank angle, time) and wind conditions, using ICAO-standard wind models. It calculates turn radius, rate of turn, TAS, and wind-drift offsets, then constructs a vector layer in QGIS with four segments: outbound leg, inbound leg, and two circular arcs representing the 180° turns. The output is a memory-based QgsVectorLayer named 'HLDG/RACETRACK X KTS' rendered in magenta, added to the QGIS project.

name: Export marine survey session data
desc: The script exports QGIS vector layers representing marine wildlife sightings, environmental observations, and observer/follower logs from a SammoSession database. It applies environment attributes, adds geometry-derived fields (lon/lat for points, WKT for lines), computes effort identifiers (effortGroup, effortLeg, _effortId), derives date/time fields from 'dateTime', adds focalId for followers, and performs multiple layer joins (environment → species, observers [left/right/center], platform, transect). It removes internal join fields during export and appends synthetic 'END' effort features to environment layers before writing final CSV or GeoPackage files. No satellite imagery, remote sensing analysis, or geospatial modeling is performed — the workflow is purely GIS data curation, attribution, and export for marine mammal survey documentation and post-cruise reporting. Study area, time range, satellite data, and geographic coordinates are not specified in the code.

name: Compute RUSLE soil erosion
desc: The script computes the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) to estimate potential soil erosion rates. It supports two spatial input modes: clipping by a user-provided shapefile or by manual coordinate extents (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax). Normalization is optionally applied for EOF of EVIs processing. For RUSLE, it executes rusle_1.first() (which internally loads and processes GEE-based geophysical inputs — though not visible in this QGIS plugin script — likely including precipitation, slope, land cover, soil erodibility, and management factors), exports intermediate and final rasters, and adds the resulting 'RUSLE.tif' as a raster layer in QGIS. For 'EOF of EVIs', it reads a precomputed EOF raster and an external UNCCD reference raster (e.g., land degradation indicator), performs linear normalization using robust statistics (mean ± 3.5×std) to align EOF scores with the UNCCD scale, and exports a normalized GeoTIFF. No satellite data loading, cloud masking, or time-series filtering occurs in this script — all Earth Engine computation is delegated to the imported rusle_1 module and assumed to be pre-executed or handled externally. The script itself is a QGIS plugin UI wrapper with no embedded GEE client calls, no explicit sensor/band references, and no hardcoded study area or time range.

name: Search and add geographic locations
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin tool that searches for Polish geographic locations (e.g., cities, administrative units) using GUGiK's UUG geocoding service (http://services.gugik.gov.pl/uug/), parses returned WKT geometries and attributes (name, type, voivodeship, county, commune, x/y coordinates), and adds the selected location as a feature to a memory vector layer named 'UUG_obiekty_fizjograficzne' in EPSG:2180. It supports duplicate detection by coordinates, zooms to the added feature, and uses a custom QML style. The workflow includes UI interaction (line edit input, list view selection), HTTP GET requests, JSON parsing, WKT geometry creation, attribute assignment, layer management via QgsProject and QgsLayerTreeGroup, and coordinate transformation for canvas zooming.

name: Transform Slovenian coordinate system
desc: The script performs a national-scale, piecewise affine coordinate transformation between the two official Slovenian coordinate reference systems: D48/Gauss-Krüger (EPSG:3794) and D96/Transverse Mercator (EPSG:3912). It uses the official nationwide triangulation-based transformation model v4.0 (released 29 May 2017) distributed by the Slovenian Surveying and Mapping Authority (e-prostor.gov.si). For each input vector feature (points, lines, or polygons), it spatially locates the containing triangle from precomputed parameter files (PRM4.csv and VVT4.csv), applies the corresponding 2D affine transformation (e = a + b·x + c·y, n = d + e·x + f·y, or inverse), and outputs a new vector layer with transformed geometries, preserved attributes and metadata, and updated CRS. Output layers are saved to user-specified or source folders with suffixes '_96TM' or '_48GK', optionally with geometry fixing and automatic project loading.

name: Calculate thematic slope from DEM
desc: The script calculates terrain slope from a user-provided digital elevation model (DEM) using GDAL's slope algorithm. It first checks whether the input DEM is in a geographic CRS; if so, it reprojects it to a user-specified projected CRS (e.g., UTM) using gdal:warpreproject with bilinear resampling to ensure geometrically valid slope computation. Then, it computes slope either in percentage (%) for FAO, USDA/NRCS, and Embrapa thematic classifications or in degrees (°) for the CAR / Brazilian Forest Code classification. The output is a classified slope raster with appropriate thematic symbology applied via the 'lftools:magicstyles' algorithm, and the layer is renamed according to the selected style (e.g., 'Slope FAO (%)').

name: Generate AORC-based precipitation forcing
desc: The script generates ADHydro-compatible meteorological forcing files (specifically precipitation rate in m/s and other variables like temperature, humidity, wind, radiation) by spatially intersecting AORC (Atmospheric/Oceanic Regional Climate Model) gridded data with ADHydro hydrologic mesh and channel elements. It reads hourly AORC netCDF files (e.g., 'AORC_Charlotte_YYYYMMDDHH.nc4') and higher-resolution MRMS-disaggregated 15-minute precip files ('AORC_MRMS_Charlotte_YYYYMMDDHHMM.nc') from a local directory structure organized by year. It performs geometric intersection using QGIS spatial indexing and Shapely geometry operations to map each ADHydro element (polygon or line) to the best-fitting AORC grid cell — either by centroid containment or by largest area/length intersection. Precipitation is converted from accumulated mass (kg/m²) to rate (m/s) using water density (temperature-dependent rho function) and time intervals derived from adjacent timestamps. Outputs include time-series forcing arrays for mesh and channel elements, domain-level mass balance diagnostics (saved to 'domain_precip_rates.csv'), and diagnostic plots. The study area is implicitly defined by a shapefile 'sub9_catchment.shp' projected into ADHydro sinusoidal coordinates; the script processes only AORC cells intersecting this sub-basin, identified via geopandas overlay and percent-intersection calculation.

name: Convert AORC precipitation to ADHydro forcing
desc: The script converts NOAA's Atmospheric River Observing System (AORC) and MRMS-disaggregated precipitation data into ADHydro-compatible forcing files. It reads hourly AORC NetCDF files (e.g., 'AORC_Charlotte_YYYYMMDDHH.nc4') and 15-minute MRMS-precipitation NetCDF files (e.g., 'AORC_MRMS_Charlotte_YYYYMMDDHHMM.nc') from a local directory structure organized by year and subdirectories like 'Precip*'. It performs spatial intersection between ADHydro mesh/channel geometries and the AORC sinusoidal grid (projected using '+proj=sinu +lon_0={meridian}...'), assigning each ADHydro element to the AORC cell with largest geometric overlap (or nearest neighbor if no intersection). Precipitation mass (kg/m²) is converted to rate (m/s) using temperature-dependent water density (rho(T)) and time intervals derived from consecutive timestamps in 'all_times'. Other meteorological variables (TMP_2maboveground, DLWRF_surface, UGRD_10maboveground, etc.) are mapped to ADHydro variable names (T2, GLW, U, V, etc.) and written into shared memory arrays for output. The script includes real-time visualization of gridded precipitation over a user-provided basin polygon ('adhydro_extent.shp'), computing and plotting domain-wide mass accumulation and precipitation rates. Study area is implicitly defined by the 'adhydro_extent.shp' file and AORC grid bounds intersecting it; time range is user-specified via command-line arguments '--startTime' and '--endTime'.

name: Generate watershed map from DEM
desc: The script creates a publication-quality watershed map using QGIS processing. It loads a filled digital elevation model (DEM), generates a hillshade raster for terrain visualization, styles watershed boundaries with a QML file, overlays river networks, and exports a high-resolution (300 DPI) PNG image. The study area is Aberdeenshire (inferred from output filename 'aberdeenshire_watersheds.png'), and inputs include local raster and vector files: 'data/processed/dem_filled.tif', 'data/processed/watersheds.shp', and 'data/processed/streams.shp'. No satellite or time-series data is used; all inputs are pre-processed local geospatial files. The hillshade is generated using GDAL with azimuth=315° and vertical angle=45°. Output is a static PNG map at 'output/aberdeenshire_watersheds.png'.

name: Estimate rice planted area by municipality
desc: The script estimates rice-planted area (in hectares) for each municipality (ADM3_PCODE) in the Philippines using PRiSM raster files and a municipal boundary shapefile. It performs zonal histogram analysis on each PRiSM raster to count pixels per class (interpreted as planting dates, inferred from legend symbology labels like '01-Jan-2020'), then converts pixel counts to area using a fixed conversion factor (0.04 ha/pixel, corresponding to 20 m × 20 m pixels). The output is an Excel file ('rice_area_planted.xlsx') with columns for ADM3_PCODE and one column per planting date (datetime-indexed), containing area in hectares. The study area is explicitly the Philippines at administrative level 3; PRiSM is confirmed as the sole raster source; no classification model or spectral index is used — only histogram aggregation and unit conversion. Legend parsing relies on hardcoded string splitting of QgsRasterLayer.legendSymbologyItems(), extracting date strings from legend item labels (e.g., 'HISTO_1' → '01-Jan-2020').

name: Generate XYZ tiles from orthophoto
desc: The script generates tiled web map (XYZ) raster tiles from a local ECW orthophoto file (Ortofoto_Itagui_2021.ecw) using QGIS GDAL's 'gdal:tilesxyz' algorithm. It loads the raster into QGIS, configures tile parameters (zoom levels 0–18, 256×256 px tiles, TMS convention disabled, JPEG quality 75), and exports tiles to a local directory. No classification, modeling, or spectral analysis is performed — only reprojection-free tiling for web visualization. The study area is implied by the filename ('Itagui'), a municipality in Colombia; time is indicated as 2021. Input is a single pre-processed orthophoto (not satellite-derived raw data), so no sensor/bands, cloud masking, or time-series processing occurs. Output is a filesystem directory of PNG/JPEG tiles organized by zoom/x/y structure.

name: Generate XYZ tiles from orthophoto
desc: The script generates XYZ tile pyramid files (e.g., for web mapping) from a local ECW orthophoto raster file. It uses QGIS’s GDAL-based 'gdal:tilesxyz' algorithm with fixed parameters: zoom levels 0–18, 256×256 pixel tiles, JPEG quality 75, DPI 96, and TMS convention disabled. The input is a single pre-processed orthophoto (Ortofoto_Itagui_2021.ecw), not satellite imagery; no classification, modeling, or spectral analysis is performed. Output is a directory tree of georeferenced image tiles (PNG/JPEG) under 'E:\entrenamientomaquina\tiles generados\2021'. Study area is Itagüí (Colombia), time reference is 2021 (in filename), but no temporal processing occurs. No satellite, sensor, or band usage — this is a raster tiling utility, not an Earth observation analysis script.

name: Apply RGB contrast enhancement
desc: The script performs RGB band reordering (red=band3, green=band2, blue=band1) and applies synchronized min-max contrast stretching across all three bands using global per-band statistics to generate a visually enhanced RGB GeoTIFF output file (_rgb_render.tif). It computes per-band minimum and maximum pixel values from the full raster extent, then sets identical stretch limits (pixMin = max of band mins, pixMax = min of band maxs) for red, green, and blue contrast enhancements — effectively implementing a conservative common stretch that avoids clipping in any channel. The output is a rendered GeoTIFF with QGIS raster rendering applied programmatically, not a classification or quantitative analysis product. Input source raster path is provided via command line; no satellite, sensor, time, or location metadata is embedded or inferred from the code. All geospatial operations are local to the input raster’s native CRS and extent.

name: Extract country-specific raster statistics
desc: The script extracts vector features for a specific country (identified by ISO_SOV1 code) from the 'eez_v11_clipped.shp' shapefile, masks a provided TIFF raster to that country's boundary using GDAL Warp with cutline cropping, and computes mean, median, 50th percentile, and standard deviation of valid pixel values within the masked extent. The study area is implicitly defined by the EEZ v11 dataset (Exclusive Economic Zones), which is maritime and coastal; the raster input (TIFF) is unspecified in source, resolution, or content — no satellite, sensor, bands, time range, or geographic region beyond ISO-coded countries is declared in the code. Outputs are a Python dictionary containing summary statistics and temporary files (shapefile and cropped TIFF) are deleted after computation.

name: Optimize pipeline routing cost
desc: The script performs A* shortest-path network routing on a 2D grid graph (170×141 nodes) to compute minimum-cost pipeline routes between specified start and end nodes, incorporating terrain slope, rocky surface exposure (via vector overlay with 'area_geo'), pipe diameter-dependent construction costs (stringing, welding, coating, hydrotesting, trenching, backfilling, cathodic protection, pipe hauling), and compressor station penalties. Costs are derived from QGIS vector layers ('grid_slope' — containing attributes 'left', 'top', 'slope'; and 'area_geo' — used for rocky surface identification), Excel input ('grid_points.xlsx' with 'RemovedPoints' sheet for node exclusion), and hard-coded engineering unit costs. The output is a list containing the optimal path (as node coordinates), its Euclidean length, and its total adjusted cost (including 39% contingency markup and optional compressor installation). No satellite or Earth Engine imagery is used; all geospatial operations occur in QGIS via QgsVectorLayer, QgsGeometry, and native processing algorithms (e.g., 'native:difference'). The study area geometry is implicitly defined by the extent of the loaded QGIS project '/design_optim.qgz' and the 'grid_slope' layer, but no explicit coordinate system, CRS, or geographic name is provided in the code.

name: Optimize pipeline network expansion
desc: The script performs a mixed-integer nonlinear optimization (MINLP) to design the least-cost expansion of a natural gas pipeline network, integrating geospatial terrain analysis (slope, rocky surface extent), engineering cost modeling (stringing, welding, trenching, hydrotesting, compression), and operational simulation via external MATLAB/GRail. It constructs a 2D grid graph (170×141 nodes) representing candidate pipeline routes, removes excluded grid points using an Excel-specified list, computes path costs via A* search with terrain- and diameter-dependent cost functions (e.g., trenching cost weighted by rocky vs. light soil length derived from QGIS vector overlay), enforces logical constraints on node connectivity and compressor placement, and couples capital expansion costs with simulated 10-year operational costs (demand scenarios). Outputs include optimal binary decision variables (x), objective function history (obj_list.txt), convergence trace (conv_list.txt), and GRail-compatible CSV input files for pipes, nodes, compressors, and flow data — all generated from local GIS layers ('grid_slope', 'area_geo') and Excel inputs ('grid_points.xlsx', 'tech_flow.xlsx'). The study area is implicitly defined by the QGIS project '/home/controllab/Downloads/design_optim.qgz' and associated vector layers; no satellite or Earth observation data is used.

name: Count soil class occurrences in HRUs
desc: The script counts the occurrence of each SOILGRIDS soil class within each hydrologic response unit (HRU) polygon in a catchment shapefile, using QGIS's zonal histogram algorithm. It loads a vector layer representing HRUs (named 'merit_hydro_basin') and a raster layer containing soil classes (named 'soilgrids_soil_classes'), then computes frequency histograms per polygon for raster band 1. The output is a shapefile with appended attribute columns prefixed 'USGS_' containing counts per soil class ID. The study area is defined implicitly by the input catchment shapefile and SOILGRIDS raster — both paths are controlled via an external 'control_active.txt' file, but no specific domain name, basin name, or geographic identifier is hardcoded or revealed in the script. Data sources are local files (not GEE assets), with no satellite, sensor, or band information applicable — the raster is a categorical soil class map (e.g., from SOILGRIDS 250m or 1km), and the vector is a pre-processed HRU/catchment boundary. No time dimension is involved.

name: Count soil class occurrences in HRUs
desc: The script intersects a catchment shapefile (representing Hydrologic Response Units, HRUs) with a SOILGRIDS-derived soil class raster to compute the frequency distribution of soil classes within each HRU polygon. It uses QGIS's native zonal histogram algorithm to count pixel values (soil class IDs) per polygon, outputting a new shapefile where each HRU feature contains attribute fields prefixed with 'USGS_' corresponding to counts for each soil class present in the raster. The study area is inferred from control file paths and naming conventions (e.g., 'merit_hydro_basin', 'soilgrids_soil_classes'), but no explicit domain name or geographic identifier is hardcoded; inputs are dynamically resolved via control file settings ('catchment_shp_name', 'parameter_soil_tif_name') pointing to user- or default-specified local file paths. Data sources are local vector (.shp) and raster (.tif) files — not GEE-hosted assets — with no satellite, sensor, or band involvement. The output is a vector layer with appended soil class count attributes, saved to a user-configurable or default path under 'shapefiles/catchment_intersection/with_soilgrids'. No time-series analysis, visualization, or export to GEE occurs.

name: Count IGBP land classes in catchments
desc: The script counts the occurrence of each IGBP (International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme) land class within each hydrologic response unit (HRU) or catchment polygon, using MODIS-derived land cover raster data. It loads a user-specified catchment vector layer (e.g., 'merit_hydro_basin') and a MODIS-based land classification raster ('modis_land_classes'), then applies QGIS's native zonal histogram algorithm to compute per-polygon frequency counts of each land class value (raster band 1). The output is a shapefile with appended attribute columns prefixed 'IGBP_' (e.g., 'IGBP_1', 'IGBP_2') representing counts for each IGBP class code. The script logs execution metadata and copies itself and the control file into a workflow log folder. Study area is inferred from domain configuration but not explicitly named; time range is not specified; MODIS is the source of land class data, but version, product, and year are not stated in the code.

name: Count IGBP land classes in catchment HRUs
desc: The script counts the occurrence (frequency) of each IGBP land class within each hydrologic response unit (HRU) polygon in a catchment, using MODIS-derived land cover raster data. It loads a vector layer of HRUs (catchment shapefile, named 'merit_hydro_basin') and a raster layer of MODIS IGBP land classes (named 'modis_land_classes'), then applies QGIS's native zonal histogram algorithm to compute per-polygon counts for each land class value (i.e., histogram bins correspond to IGBP class codes). The output is a vector shapefile (user-specified or default path under 'shapefiles/catchment_intersection/with_modis') where each HRU polygon contains new attribute fields prefixed with 'IGBP_' (e.g., 'IGBP_1', 'IGBP_2') representing the count of pixels of that IGBP class falling within the polygon. No time-series analysis, classification, or modeling is performed — only static spatial intersection and frequency tabulation. Study area is inferred from control file inputs but not explicitly named; data sources are MODIS land cover (IGBP classification) and a catchment/HRU vector derived from MERIT Hydro (as indicated by layer name 'merit_hydro_basin').

name: Navigate to XY coordinates
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin dialog that allows users to input X/Y or longitude/latitude coordinates in a specified CRS, pan and zoom the map canvas to that location, optionally create a point marker layer, maintain a history of entered coordinates, and support coordinate capture from the map canvas. It performs coordinate transformation between input CRS and project CRS using QgsCoordinateTransform, sets canvas center and scale, and manages vector layer creation for markers. No remote sensing data processing, classification, or time-series analysis is performed; it is purely a GIS navigation and coordinate management tool.

name: Calculate spectral vegetation and water indices
desc: The script calculates user-selected two-band spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, NDMI, MSI, NBR, AVI, SAVI) from locally loaded raster bands in QGIS. It reads two input rasters (higher- and lower-numbered bands), validates their spatial dimensions, computes the index using band math with numerical safeguards (e.g., 1e-10 offset for division), writes the result to a GeoTIFF output raster, and reports band alignment guidance via warning message. The script does not ingest or process GEE image collections — it operates purely on local GDAL-readable raster layers provided by the user; no study area, time range, cloud masking, temporal filtering, or GEE server-side computation occurs. All satellite band mappings (e.g., Sentinel-2 Band 8 for NIR) are hardcoded lookup tables used only for user guidance and validation warnings — not for data fetching. Outputs include a single-index GeoTIFF raster and an info string summarizing satellite/index selection and expected vs. selected bands.

name: Execute SQL query on vector layers
desc: The script executes a user-defined SQL query against one or more input vector layers using QGIS's virtual layer provider. It supports aliasing layers as 'input1', 'input2', etc., in the query, handles geometry type and CRS specification, optional UID field definition, and outputs the result as a new vector layer (feature sink). It includes logic to persist temporary memory layers to disk when needed (e.g., in Graphical Modeler context) to ensure virtual layer validity. No remote sensing, raster, time-series, or satellite data processing occurs — it is purely a vector SQL execution utility within QGIS Processing Framework.

name: Navigate to XY coordinates
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin dialog that allows users to input X/Y or longitude/latitude coordinates in a specified CRS, transform them to the project's destination CRS, pan and zoom the map canvas to that location, optionally create a point marker layer, maintain a history table of entered coordinates, and support coordinate capture from the map canvas. It performs coordinate transformation using QgsCoordinateTransform, sets canvas center and scale, and creates memory vector layers for markers. No remote sensing data processing, classification, or time-series analysis is performed — it is purely a GIS navigation and coordinate management tool.

name: Calculate spectral vegetation and water indices
desc: The script calculates user-selected two-band spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, NDMI, MSI, NBR, AVI, SAVI) from raster bands provided as QGIS layers. It performs pixel-wise arithmetic operations (e.g., normalized difference, ratio, or empirical formulas) on co-registered input rasters, validates band resolution compatibility, processes data in memory-efficient chunks using GDAL, and writes the result to a GeoTIFF output raster. The script does not ingest or filter time-series imagery, apply atmospheric correction, perform classification, or define a study area — it is a deterministic, band-level raster algebra operator. Inputs are arbitrary local raster files loaded in QGIS; satellite type and index selection only drive band-number validation logic and formula choice — no remote GEE asset access, no temporal filtering, no geometry or region definition occurs. Outputs consist solely of a single-band GeoTIFF index raster and an info string summarizing selected satellite, index, and band names.

name: Calculate villa development feasibility
desc: The script calculates the maximum number of villas that can be built on a given land parcel in Koh Phangan, Thailand, based on locally prescribed building regulations (zone type, elevation, slope). It does not use satellite imagery or remote sensing — all inputs are vector boundary geometry, precomputed slope raster, and hardcoded regulatory rules. The workflow loads a site boundary from File_Paths.py, optionally computes average slope from a local slope raster file, selects applicable regulation parameters (e.g., max building percentage, max unit size, height limits), then computes three development scenarios (Premium, Balanced, MaxYield) using pure geometric area math and floor assumptions. Outputs include: (1) console-printed scenario summaries with unit counts, sizes, footprints, coverage percentages; (2) three QGIS memory layers visualizing villa footprints with directional arrows and legal setbacks; (3) a branded A3 print layout showing site map (if boundary available), regulation inputs, scenario comparison boxes, compass rose, and villa orientation indicator. Study area is explicitly Koh Phangan (from regulation filename 'koh_phangan_building_regulations_clean.txt' and comments); no time range is involved as this is a static regulatory compliance calculator.

name: Reproject geospatial raster and vector layers
desc: The script reprojects all .tif (raster) and .shp (vector) files from an input directory to a user-specified coordinate reference system (CRS), writing the reprojected outputs to a designated output directory. Raster reprojection uses GDAL's 'warpreproject' algorithm with DEFLATE compression and predictor settings; vector reprojection uses QGIS's 'native:reprojectlayer'. Input paths, output paths, and target CRS are selected interactively via a QGIS plugin dialog.

name: Generate FHAST template files
desc: The script generates a standardized set of dummy input files required by the FHAST (Fish Habitat Assessment and Simulation Tool) modeling framework. It copies pre-defined shapefiles (e.g., 'dum_centerline.shp', 'dum_aoi.shp') and CSV files (e.g., 'dum_fish_population.csv', 'dum_enviro_hydrograph.csv') from an internal 'dummy_files' directory into a user-specified output folder, reprojects the shapefiles to a user-selected CRS, and programmatically adds them to the QGIS project inside pre-named layer groups (e.g., 'Grid Centerline', 'Fish Population File', 'Environmental Input File'). No geospatial analysis, remote sensing processing, or time-series computation is performed — the script is purely a file templating and project scaffolding utility. All inputs are local static files; no Earth Engine datasets, satellite imagery, or dynamic data sources are accessed or referenced.

name: Compute OHWM-project footprint overlap
desc: The script computes the geometric intersection (overlap) between an Ordinary High Water Mark (OHWM) vector layer and a project footprint vector layer.
