name: Calculate line crossing angles
desc: The script computes the acute angle between intersecting line geometries (e.g., roads, rivers, pipelines) in a QGIS desktop environment. It identifies intersection points between a selected 'route' line layer and one or more user-selected 'obstacle' line layers, calculates the angle between the two line segments at each intersection using vector geometry (closest segment direction vectors), and generates a memory point layer named 'Angles' with attributes: 'angle' (acute angle in degrees, rounded to 2 decimals), 'a1', and 'a2'. The output layer is styled categorically by angle range (<70°, 70–80°, 80–90°) and labeled with the angle value (e.g., '82.3°'). The analysis runs live — updating automatically on route geometry changes, feature additions, or deletions. No satellite, raster, or temporal data is involved; all inputs are local vector layers loaded in QGIS. Study area, time range, and external data sources are not specified.

name: Generate solar panel layouts
desc: The script generates vector polygon layers representing solar panel tables (full and half) on user-selected polygon layers in QGIS. It performs geometric tiling, spacing optimization, edge margin handling, and hole detection within input polygons. When enabled, it calculates or optimizes inter-row spacing (v_spacing) to achieve a target coverage rate (e.g., 20%, 30%) using a custom coverage logic module. Outputs include a categorized memory vector layer with attributes (id, table type, ilot ID, v_spacing), styled with distinct colors for full/half panels; persistent message bar feedback with panel counts and estimated total power (MWc/kWc); and optional coverage statistics. No satellite or remote sensing data is used — all inputs are local QGIS vector layers (polygons only), and all operations are deterministic geometric constructions and optimizations. Study area, time range, satellite data, bands, and sensors are not involved or specified.

name: Execute QGIS layer operations
desc: The script implements a QGIS Python plugin interface executor that programmatically performs common GIS layer management and styling tasks within the QGIS desktop application. It does not perform geospatial analysis, remote sensing processing, or Earth Engine computations. Instead, it controls QGIS UI actions (e.g., zooming, renaming, visibility toggling), applies symbology (single-color or categorized rendering by field), loads vector/raster layers from local paths, opens attribute tables/processing tools/layout designer, selects features by expression, and applies standardized style rules from an external style library. All operations act on already-loaded QGIS map layers — no data is fetched, computed, or exported to cloud storage. Outputs are side effects in the QGIS GUI: updated canvas view, refreshed layer tree, modified renderer, triggered dialogs, and logged user feedback. No study area, time range, satellite data, or geospatial modeling is involved.

name: Classify land use dominance and diversity
desc: The script performs land use classification and analysis on user-provided vector layers (e.g., Output Areas — OA21CD) using local geospatial data sources (GeoPackage). It classifies dominant land use and computes diversity score and category percentages per feature by querying spatially intersected land use elements (e.g., buildings, green spaces, water) from the GeoPackage via GpkgClient. Road network analysis (lengths by functional class, density, area) is performed using RoadClient. Optional census integration (TS001/TS066 files) enables trip generation estimation (residential/employment trips, total trips, trip density) tied to OA-level population and employment. Outputs include enriched vector features with new attributes (e.g., 'dominant_use', 'diversity_score', 'motorway_km', 'population', 'trip_density'), styled duplicate layers for visualization (land use, road density, trip metrics, diversity), and aggregated LSOA-level summary layers with dissolved geometries and statistics. Study area and time range are not specified in code; all processing is vector-based and relies entirely on local file inputs (GPKG, CSV-like census tables), not satellite or remote sensing data.

name: Aggregate building volume to grid cells
desc: The script processes building footprint (Hausumringe) and LoD2 3D building data to compute per-building floor area and volume (floor_area × measuredHeight), then spatially overlaps these buildings with a user-provided grid, aggregates total floor area and total building volume per grid cell, and joins the aggregated metrics back to the original grid geometry. It outputs two GeoPackage files: (1) individual buildings with attributes 'floor_area' and 'building_volume', and (2) grid cells enriched with 'total_floor_area' and 'total_building_volume' — enabling urban morphology and density analysis at the grid level.

name: Calculate building volume from LoD2 data
desc: The script calculates building volume by combining floor area and height attributes from a LoD2 building dataset (GML format), converts the vector layer to GeoPackage for compatibility, reads it into GeoPandas, and prepares it for aggregation to a grid. It explicitly loads a grid file, a merged LoD2 GML file containing building height, and references floor area data (though the floor_area variable is commented out). The workflow centers on deriving volumetric urban form metrics from 3D building data for urban heat island (UHI) analysis.

name: Calculate building floor area per grid cell
desc: The script computes the total floor area of buildings (from vector building footprints) within each grid cell by geometric intersection and aggregation. It first verifies and reprojects the building footprint layer (Hausumringe) to match the project CRS, clips it to the Coburg administrative boundary, calculates planimetric area per building feature, performs vector overlap analysis to determine how much of each building falls into each grid cell, aggregates overlapping areas by grid cell ID, and finally joins the aggregated floor areas back to the original grid layer—producing a grid-layer GeoPackage with an attribute 'floor_area_per_grid' representing the summed building floor area per cell.

name: Map roof area per urban grid cell
desc: The script computes total rooftop area per grid cell by spatially joining 3D building roof geometries (from a CityGML/3DCityDB database) with a regular grid, then aggregates roof area values by grid ID. It outputs a GeoPackage file (geodataframe_newwip_cleaned_roof_grid.gpkg) containing grid cells enriched with summed roof area, alongside intermediate layers including stripped/merged GML buildings, PostGIS-joined roof-area attributes, and spatially joined roof–grid features.

name: Setup QGIS project template
desc: The script programmatically creates a QGIS 3.28+ project file (.qgs) configured for Niedersachsen, Germany, with EPSG:25832 CRS, five predefined layer groups (Hintergrund, Bestand, Planung, Analyse, Ausgabe), two WMS background layers (BKG WebAtlasDE and LGLN DTK), and a fully configured A3 landscape print layout containing map frame, title, dynamic date label, legend, scale bar, north arrow, and styling elements. No geospatial analysis, classification, or remote sensing processing is performed — it is purely a GIS project scaffolding tool.

name: Correct photo filenames with zero FID
desc: The script identifies JPEG photos in a DCIM directory matching the pattern 'DT_YYYY-MM-DD_0_INCONNU_INCONNU_X_Y.jpg' (indicating FID=0), then either renames them using the FID of an existing vector feature within a tolerance of coordinates in a GeoPackage layer, or creates a new vector feature at those coordinates and renames the photo with the newly assigned FID. It modifies both filesystem filenames and the corresponding 'photo' field value in the vector layer. Outputs include renamed files and updated attribute values in the GeoPackage layer.

name: Detect polygon self-intersections and overlaps
desc: The script checks input polygon vector layers for topological validity issues: (1) self-intersecting geometries (invalid GEOS geometries), identified via QgsGeometry.isGeosValid() and confirmed using a small buffer tolerance (0.000001 degrees for geographic CRS, 0.1 meters otherwise); and (2) pairwise overlaps between polygons, detected via spatial index–accelerated bounding box intersection followed by precise QgsGeometry.intersects() and intersection type validation (requiring non-empty polygon-type intersections). Input is preprocessed with QGIS 'Fix Geometries' algorithm. Output is a vector layer containing only features flagged for either self-intersection or overlap, preserving original geometry and attributes. No study area, time range, satellite data, or external geospatial datasets are involved — the script operates purely on user-provided vector polygon layers in QGIS Processing Framework.

name: Detect polygon self-intersections and overlaps
desc: The script identifies invalid polygon geometries—including self-intersections (detected via GEOS validity checks and zero/negative/positive buffer tests) and pairwise feature overlaps (detected via spatial intersection using a QgsSpatialIndex)—in an input QGIS vector polygon layer. It applies QGIS's 'fixgeometries' algorithm as a preprocessing step, then performs multi-stage geometric validation: (1) GEOS validity check with tolerance-aware buffering; (2) zero-buffer robustness test; and (3) pairwise topological intersection detection among features. Output is a new memory-based polygon layer containing only invalid features (self-intersecting or overlapping), each annotated with a descriptive 'Reason' field (e.g., 'Self-intersection detected with zero buffer', 'Overlap with Feature ID 42'). The output layer is styled with a red dashed hatch fill for visual emphasis in QGIS. No external geospatial datasets, time series, or remote sensing inputs are used—the analysis is purely vector geometry validation on user-provided local polygon data. Study area, time range, satellite/sensor/bands, and external data sources are not specified.

name: Generate microplot grid
desc: The script generates a customizable rectangular grid of microplots (polygons) defined by four user-selected corner points on a QGIS map canvas. It computes an affine transformation to warp a regular grid to the quadrilateral defined by the corners, then resizes each plot to specified length and width dimensions. Plot IDs are assigned either sequentially or in serpentine order, optionally starting from a user-defined number and direction (e.g., Bottom Left, Top Right). Optional CSV-based field maps can supply custom plot IDs per cell; optional field data CSVs can be joined to output features via a user-specified Plot ID column. The final output is a vector layer (memory or file-based) containing polygon features with attributes: 'ID' (1-based sequential index) and 'PlotID' (user-defined or generated string), plus optionally joined field data columns. No remote sensing data, time-series analysis, classification, or Earth Engine server-side computation is performed — all operations are client-side in QGIS using numpy/scipy/pandas.

name: Generate microplot grid polygons
desc: The script generates a vector grid of rectangular microplots (polygons) based on four user-selected corner points on a QGIS map canvas. It supports fixed-size plots (with user-defined length/width in meters) or interpolated plots that evenly subdivide the quadrilateral defined by the four corners. Plot IDs are assigned either sequentially or serpentine, starting from a user-defined initial ID and ordered according to user-specified origin (e.g., Bottom Left). Optional CSV field maps can override internal numbering; optional field data CSVs can be joined to output features via PlotID matching. Output is a memory layer or saved Shapefile with PlotID and optionally joined attributes. No remote sensing data, time-series analysis, or classification is performed — all operations are geometric and tabular within QGIS.

name: Apply right-before-left traffic rule logic
desc: The script implements a Right-Before-Left (RBL) intersection priority analysis for road centerlines at intersections, using vector geometry operations on QGIS line layers. It identifies which road yields to which other road at shared intersection points based on geometric approach bearings and turn directions. Key steps include: (1) filtering input road layer for features where lane_type='centerline' and lane_morphology='intersection'; (2) spatially indexing features; (3) computing angle-of-approach bearings at intersection points derived from line–line intersections; (4) determining relative right-side positioning using bearing differences; (5) resolving yield relationships via RBL logic (i.e., the road arriving from the right yields to the one arriving from the left); (6) augmenting results with pedestrian markings and cycle lanes intersecting centerlines. Outputs depend on OUTPUT_MODE: printed tabular summary, updated 'yield_to' attribute field in source layer, or a new point memory layer with road_id, way_id, and comma-separated yield_to identifiers. No satellite, raster, or temporal data is used — all operations are vector-based and static, relying solely on the active QGIS line layer’s geometry and attributes (e.g., 'road_id', 'way_id', 'lane_type', 'lane_morphology'). Study area, time range, satellite data, and external geospatial datasets are not specified.

name: Compute absolute change between two rasters
desc: The script performs pixel-wise absolute difference calculation between two georeferenced raster images (nanjing1.jpg and nanjing2.jpg) using GDAL's raster calculator with formula 'abs(B - A)', where A is the first image and B is the second. It outputs a single-band change detection raster (change_detected.tif) representing magnitude of difference per pixel. The study area is implied to be Nanjing (from file paths), but no temporal metadata, satellite/sensor information, or projection parameters are specified in the code; inputs are generic JPEG files, not satellite-derived datasets. No classification, masking, or temporal filtering is applied—only arithmetic raster algebra.

name: Scale coastal change normals
desc: The script creates a new QGIS memory vector layer where each input transect line is replaced by a scaled line segment originating from the center point of the original transect and extending bidirectionally: green lines toward user-selected direction (start or end) for positive values (accretion), red lines toward the opposite direction for negative values (erosion), and short white centered lines for near-zero values (stability). It computes scale factors normalized to [0.1, 1.0] based on absolute value magnitude relative to the global max absolute value in the selected field, applies directional scaling using vector arithmetic from center to target endpoint, and applies a graduated symbology renderer with red-white-green color ramp reflecting erosion-stable-accretion. The original layer is hidden; the scaled layer is added to the QGIS project with automatic styling and legend refresh. No remote sensing data processing occurs — input is a local GPKG vector layer of coastal transects with numeric metrics (e.g., NSM, EPR, LRR, WLR, SCE).

name: Assess radioactive leak impact area
desc: The script assesses the geographic impact area of a radioactive leak at the Asco Nuclear Power Plant by generating concentric buffer zones (2 km, 3 km, 5 km) around a fixed incident point (296590.70333919115, 4564089.212024709) in EPSG:25831, clipping municipal boundaries from a GeoPackage layer to the 5 km buffer, calculating total affected population from the 'POBLACION' attribute, labeling municipalities with 'NOMCAP', overlaying an SVG nuclear plant marker, and producing a PDF map layout with title, footer (population count), north arrow, and legend-equivalent visual hierarchy via colored buffers.

name: Generate energy site suitability map
desc: The script generates a QGIS project file (.qgs) containing vector layers representing energy site suitability constraints and opportunities (e.g., 'Constraint-free sites', 'All constraints') derived from precomputed GeoPackage (.gpkg) layers stored in 'build/output/layers/'. It organizes layers hierarchically by thematic branches and sections, applies consistent styling (CSS-named colors converted to RGB, opacity settings, strokeless symbols), hides specific layers by default (e.g., 'Constraint-free sites' and 'All constraints'), adds OpenStreetMap as a background TMS layer, and forces the project’s startup and default full extent to London bounds [-0.15, 51.48, -0.10, 51.52]. The input data structure is defined in 'build/output/opensiteenergy-data.json', and the output is written to 'build/output/opensiteenergy.qgs'. No on-the-fly geospatial analysis, classification, or time-series processing occurs — all layers are pre-generated vector datasets.

name: Generate bivariate legend boxes
desc: Generates a 3×3 grid of square polygon features (GeoPackage or Shapefile) with attributes 'code', 'label', 'color', 'a_class', 'b_class', 'row', and 'col'; each polygon is styled via a QgsCategorizedSymbolRenderer on the 'code' field using predefined or custom hex color palettes; layer is auto-added to QGIS project with optional code labeling and pre-configured symbology for direct use in Print Layout legend items.

name: Generate bivariate legend diamonds
desc: Generates a 3×3 grid of diamond (rhombus) polygons in a 45°-rotated layout for bivariate thematic mapping; each diamond is uniquely coded (e.g., '11', '12', ..., '33') and styled with a categorized renderer on the 'code' field to serve as color-coded legend icons in QGIS Print Layouts; outputs include a vector layer (GeoPackage or Shapefile) with attributes 'code', 'label', 'color', 'a_class', 'b_class', 'row', 'col', and auto-applied symbology with optional labels — no geospatial analysis, classification, or remote sensing processing is performed; the script operates purely in abstract map-unit coordinate space with no input raster or satellite data.

name: Classify rasters into terciles
desc: The script classifies two input rasters (Raster A and Raster B) into three quantile-based classes (1/2/3) using tercile breaks (33.33rd and 66.67th percentiles), then combines them arithmetically into a bivariate raster where each pixel value is a two-digit code (11–33) representing the joint class membership (e.g., 11 = low A + low B; 32 = high A + medium B). It optionally reprojects and aligns Raster B to Raster A’s grid, applies a divisor scaling to Raster B, computes tercile thresholds from valid non-NoData pixel values, and outputs three rasters: classified Raster A (1–3), classified Raster B (1–3), and the bivariate composite (11–33).

name: Convert road centerline points to polylines
desc: The script converts a point layer representing road centerline vertices into a polyline (line) layer by ordering points based on a 'name' field (assumed to encode sequence or segment ID), then adds 'name' (string) and 'length' (double, computed geometry length) attributes to the resulting line layer. Input is a local shapefile of points; output is a new shapefile with linestrings and two added fields.

name: Load ship route telemetry with wind and current data
desc: The script loads a GeoJSON or JSON file containing ship route waypoints with associated telemetry (time, speed, fuel consumption) and environmental data (u/v wind speed, u/v currents, wind resistance). It constructs two QGIS memory layers: (1) a point layer ('Ship Waypoints (Telemetry)') with attributes including computed step distance, cumulative fuel, total distance, and derived wind/current magnitudes; and (2) a line layer ('Ship Route Path') visualizing the full route as a polyline. Map tips are applied to the point layer for rich HTML-based tooltip display of per-waypoint metrics. The script performs no remote sensing analysis, no GEE server-side computation, and does not access Earth Engine — it is purely a QGIS Processing Algorithm for local GeoJSON ingestion and vector layer generation. Study area, time range, satellite data, and geospatial operations beyond local QgsDistanceArea measurement are not specified in the code.

name: Apply coordinate transformation
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin dialog for performing geospatial coordinate transformations on vector layers using Netcad DNS files. It supports three methods: Helmert (4-parameter, isotropic scale + rotation + translation), Affine (6-parameter, anisotropic scale + shear + translation), and TIN-based Delaunay triangulation (local affine transforms per triangle). Input is a Netcad .dns file containing either point-based ($AMAT + $NOK) or matrix-based ($AMAT only) transformation parameters. The workflow includes DNS parsing, method- and type-aware validation (e.g., TIN requires point-based DNS), residual computation and visualization, quality control integration (via external QualityControlTab), TIN mesh generation and mapping, HTML/PDF reporting, and in-place or new-layer vector geometry transformation. Outputs include transformed vector layers, residual tables with color-coded quality status, TIN triangle layers, and standardized reports. All operations are CRS-aware using the selected layer’s WKT definition; no external satellite or raster data is used — this is purely a vector coordinate transformation tool operating on user-provided DNS parameter files and QGIS vector layers. Study area, time range, satellite/sensor/bands, and geographic extent are not specified because the tool is generic and input-agnostic.

name: Generate binary water mask
desc: The script computes a binary water mask raster using the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) from user-provided Green and NIR band rasters. It applies a user-defined NDWI threshold, optional morphological closing (to reconnect fragmented river pixels), and optional sieve filtering (to remove small noise pixels or isolated 'islands'). The output is a georeferenced binary raster where water = 1 and non-water = 0 (with NoData set to 0 for land), optimized for hydrological feature delineation in terrestrial hydrosphere applications.

name: Extract water polygons from binary mask
desc: The script converts an input binary raster layer (where pixel value 1 = water, 0 = non-water) into clean vector polygons by: (1) pixel-to-polygon conversion using GDAL’s polygonize algorithm; (2) filtering to retain only features where the 'is_water' attribute equals 1; (3) dissolving all adjacent water polygons into a single multipart geometry to eliminate internal boundaries; and (4) converting the dissolved geometry into individual singlepart polygons (e.g., separate river segments, lakes, or disconnected water bodies). The final output is a vector layer of simple, non-overlapping, water-only polygons suitable for area calculation, spatial analysis, or cartographic display.

name: Model ambulance coverage using Voronoi diagrams
desc: The script models theoretical ambulance service coverage across Penang, Malaysia by generating spatially constrained Voronoi diagrams for three distinct geographic domains: George Town (island), Seberang Perai (mainland), and the two Penang bridges (Sultan Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah Bridge and Penang Bridge). It first preprocesses OpenStreetMap-derived multipolygon boundaries—removing sea polygons, extracting/trimming bridge geometries, resolving topological invalidities via PostGIS, and buffering bridges to assign nearby ambulance stations. Ambulance locations (from an Excel sheet) are spatially assigned to each domain using intersection queries. Voronoi tessellations are then computed per domain in PostGIS, clipped to their respective landmass or bridge extents, and joined with EMS incident locations to attribute calls to the nearest theoretically covered ambulance station. Outputs include geopackages of theoretical coverage polygons and CSVs of incident-to-ambulance assignments for demand analysis per hectare.

name: Classify Singapore hectare grids by land use type
desc: The script classifies each 100m × 100m grid cell (hectare) across Singapore into one dominant land use category — e.g., 'airport', 'mall', 'major_road', 'street_shops', 'school', 'residential', 'workforce' — based on OpenStreetMap-derived multipolygon and buffered road geometries intersected with a fixed grid. It outputs an Excel file (grid_classification.xlsx) listing each grid ID, row/column index, and its assigned dominant classification, determined by area-weighted dominance (with hard-coded priority for airports/malls).

name: Calculate weighted mean radon levels per parish
desc: The script computes a weighted mean radon concentration (based on 'CLASS_MAX' values from the Radon Indicative Atlas v3) for each parish polygon, using area-weighted intersection with radon polygons. It reprojects input GeoPackage and MBTiles layers to EPSG:27700 (OSGB 1936 / British National Grid), loads three key layers (parish boundaries, radon atlas, ceremonial county boundaries), performs spatial intersection and area-weighted aggregation, writes the result into a new 'mean_radon' attribute in the parish layer, applies a Jenks natural breaks graduated color ramp (green-to-red) for visualization, and exports one A4 landscape PNG map per ceremonial county showing the parish-level radon means masked to that county’s boundary — including custom gradient legend, scale bar, and title. The study area is implicitly the UK (EPSG:27700 CRS, 'ceremonial counties', 'parish' administrative units, 'Radon_Indicative_Atlas_v3'). No satellite or remote sensing data is used; all inputs are vector geospatial datasets (GeoPackage, MBTiles).

name: Calculate composite curve number
desc: The script calculates area-weighted composite Curve Numbers (CN) for hydrological modeling by intersecting subbasin, land use, and soils polygon layers; it performs geometry repair, CRS reprojection (to EPSG:3361), sequential intersections (land use × soils → result × subbasins), area recalculation from post-intersection geometries (in acres), CN lookup via user-provided CSV/Excel table mapping land use and soil hydrologic group (A–D) to CN values, and outputs a shapefile with decimal (CN_Comp) and integer-rounded (CN_Int) CN fields, plus detailed and summary CSVs including area validation metrics (reference vs. intersection area difference %).

name: Generate hydrologic sample data layers
desc: The script generates six GeoPackage vector layers for Hydro Suite testing: subbasins (polygons), landuse (polygons), soils (polygons), flowpaths (line strings), channels (line strings), and outlets (points). All layers are created synthetically in EPSG:2273 (SC State Plane South, feet) with realistic hydrologic attributes (e.g., CN, HSG, Manning’s n, imperviousness %, Tc, slope). Coordinates are hardcoded around base point (2,100,000 E, 100,000 N), approximating Lowcountry South Carolina. No external data sources or time-series processing is used — all geometries and attributes are programmatically constructed from static dictionaries. Outputs are saved as .gpkg files and optionally loaded into the current QGIS project.

name: Calculate area-weighted composite runoff coefficient
desc: The script calculates area-weighted composite runoff coefficients (C values) for catchments by intersecting user-provided polygon layers — catchment boundaries, land use/land cover, and soil hydrologic groups — then applying slope-category–specific C values from an external lookup table (CSV or Excel). It outputs: (1) a shapefile of catchments with added 'C_Comp' (composite C) and 'Area_acres' attributes; (2) a detailed CSV listing each intersected land-use/soil/slope sub-area, its C value, and C×area product; and (3) a summary CSV with per-catchment total area, sum of C×area, and final composite C. The workflow includes reprojection to EPSG:3361, sequential vector intersections, soil group parsing (e.g., handling 'A/B' → 'B'), and validation-driven GUI controls.

name: Classify forest stand povoamento
desc: The script processes point-based SB_AZ (Arborização) data — likely field-surveyed tree locations with 'PAP' (probably 'Perímetro à Altura do Peito', i.e., trunk circumference at breast height) measurements — to identify and map forest stand povoamento (i.e., self-sustaining, closed-canopy forest patches meeting minimum density and size criteria). It computes crown radius ('RAIO_COPA') from PAP using a piecewise linear lookup, buffers points by that radius, applies a 10 m continuity buffer and dissolves to form contiguous patches ('manchas'), filters for patches ≥ 0.5 ha, assigns ID_MANCHA, joins tree attributes back to patches, aggregates per patch (count of trees, mean PAP, class), calculates tree density (N_ARVORES / AREA_HA), and classifies povoamento as 'SIM' if density thresholds are met per PAP-derived class (1–4). A two-pass classification is performed: first on original patches, then a repescagem (re-evaluation) of non-classified patches using mean PAP from associated points, followed by reclassification and merging. Final output is a dissolved polygon layer '23_POVOAMENTO_FINAL' representing classified forest stands. No satellite or remote sensing data is used; input is purely vector point data ('Camada SB_AZ (pontos)') with attribute-driven geometric and statistical operations. Study area, time range, and external data sources are not specified in the code.

name: Compute zone composition statistics
desc: The script overlays element (point, line, or polygon) and zone (polygon) vector layers to compute per-zone composition statistics: counts, sums, or weighted sums of elements by type (if specified), optionally normalized by zone area (density) and augmented with entropy-based mix index (Shannon diversity) either on raw or row-normalized values. The output is a tabular vector layer (attribute-only) with one row per zone and columns for zone ID, element type counts/sums, density metrics, and mix index values. No raster data, time series, or satellite imagery is involved; inputs are arbitrary user-provided vector layers with optional attribute fields for type and weight.

name: Model drainage classes from water level points
desc: The script models surface drainage conditions by interpolating point-based water level measurements (vandspejlspunkter) using Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW), then subtracting the interpolated water surface raster from a Digital Height Model (DHM) to compute depth-to-water-table (in cm). It reclassifies the resulting difference raster into seven hydrologically meaningful drainage classes (e.g., '< 0 cm Frit vandspejl', '0–25 cm Sump', up to '100–125 cm Mark'), converts the classified raster to polygons, assigns descriptive class names via field calculation, and applies a categorized fill symbology with predefined colors and black outlines. The final output is a vector polygon layer representing spatially explicit drainage condition classes.

name: Burn river channel into terrain
desc: The script reads MIKE21 cross-sectional profile data (text format), interpolates them along a user-provided centerline vector, constructs a TIN surface from the interpolated 3D points, clips it with a concave hull to constrain extent, aligns the resulting TIN raster to the input DHM’s georeferenced grid (same CRS, extent, and resolution), and computes pixel-wise minimum between DHM and TIN — producing a new raster where river channels are 'burned in' (i.e., terrain is lowered to match the modeled channel bed elevation) while preserving original DHM elsewhere. Output is a GeoTIFF raster representing min(DHM, TIN) with nodata handling and full geospatial alignment.

name: Interpolate terrain elevation
desc: The script interpolates a continuous, filled high-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) for a user-defined polygonal area ('Område') by sampling elevation values from an input DEM ('DHM'), generating dense sample points along the boundary and interior of the area, applying Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) interpolation with power=5 and radius=100 m, clipping the interpolated surface to the input polygon, and merging it with the original DHM raster to produce a seamless 'Fyldt højdemodel' (filled elevation model) that preserves original terrain data outside the interpolation zone while filling or refining elevation within the target area.

name: Extract terrain elevation along offset transects
desc: The script processes point features representing a linear survey (e.g., VASP survey points), converts them into a path, offsets that path left or right by 10 meters to define a terrain sampling line, generates equally spaced sample points (1 m interval) along the offset line, assigns station numbers starting from a user-defined integer, samples elevation values from a digital height model (DHM) at each point, and exports the resulting point layer—including station number, sampled terrain elevation ('bundkote'), an empty 'vsp' field, and a fixed 'Bemærkning' = 'Terrain'—to an Excel spreadsheet for engineering/terrain analysis.

name: Calculate terrain volume change
desc: The script computes a difference raster (Original DHM − New DHM) using GDAL's raster calculator, then aggregates pixel-wise elevation differences to quantify cut (positive difference = material removal) and fill (negative difference = material addition) volumes in cubic meters. It reads two user-provided raster layers representing digital height models (DHMs) — assumed to be co-registered, same resolution and CRS — calculates per-pixel difference, sums positive and negative values separately, multiplies each sum by the ground area per pixel (derived from raster resolution), and reports both volumetric outputs. No study area, time range, satellite data, or external geospatial processing (e.g., reprojection, resampling) is specified or inferred; inputs are generic local raster layers with no embedded temporal or sensor metadata.

name: Load acoustic noise layers
desc: The script loads acoustic noise data from a local API (http://127.0.0.1:8765) into QGIS as three vector layers: (1) noise sources (points), with attributes id, description, source_type, x, y; (2) calculation points (points), with attributes id, l_a_eq_day, l_a_eq_night, exceeded_day; and (3) noise isolevel contours (linestrings), with attribute level_dba. It applies QGIS-native symbology: red circular markers for sources, default point rendering for calculation points, and an empty line layer placeholder for isolevels. The API endpoints used are /sources/, /export_to_qgis/, and /health. No satellite, remote sensing, or Earth Engine processing occurs — this is purely a QGIS plugin for ingesting precomputed acoustic model outputs from a local backend service. Study area, time range, sensor data, and geospatial operations are not specified in the script.

name: Classify and buffer hydrographic network by order
desc: The script processes a vector-based hydrographic network layer by clipping it to an administrative boundary, then classifying stream segments into Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary orders using the 'Codigo' attribute (values 1, 2, 3), assigning distinct colors for visualization, and generating order-specific buffers (100 m, 50 m, and 20 m respectively); outputs are three temporary vector layers — 'Buffer_Primaria', 'Buffer_Secundaria', and 'Buffer_Terciaria' — each representing buffered zones for their respective stream order.

name: Reproject Sentinel-2 raster and vector layers
desc: The script reprojects three GIS layers—two Sentinel-2 multispectral bands (B04 and B08) and one administrative vector layer (stadtviertel, i.e., city districts)—from their native CRS into the UTM zone 32N coordinate reference system (EPSG:25832) appropriate for Cologne, Germany. It uses GDAL's warp reprojection for rasters and QGIS's native reprojection algorithm for vectors, saves the outputs as GeoTIFFs and a GeoPackage respectively, and loads them back into the QGIS project for downstream analysis (e.g., vegetation index computation or zonal statistics).

name: Generate coursework query layers
desc: The script generates a QGIS project (.qgz) containing vector layers derived from PostgreSQL/PostGIS SQL queries executed against an OSM database. It creates 12 specific query-based layers (e.g., 'Q1 Parks Area', 'Q4 Amenities In Radius', 'Q7 Admin Boundaries') representing spatial analyses of OpenStreetMap data — including area calculations, road length aggregation, building counts per administrative unit, buffer analysis, point-in-radius searches, road-water intersections, polygon centroids, and union of green spaces. The workflow loads an OpenStreetMap XYZ basemap (EPSG:3857), executes templated SQL queries with runtime parameters (admin_name, center_lon/lat, search_radius_meters, buffer_distance_meters), creates or replaces corresponding tables in the 'public' schema, builds spatial indexes, and adds each resulting PostGIS layer to a grouped 'Query Results' layer tree node. The final output is a fully configured QGIS project file saved as 'petrozavodsk_coursework.qgz' with default view extent set to the first non-empty layer’s extent. Study area is Petrozavodsk (inferred from 'petrozavodsk_coursework.qgz' filename and context of coursework). Data source is local PostGIS with OSM-derived geometry; no satellite, sensor, or band usage occurs.

name: Compute travel time matrix
desc: The script computes an origin-destination (OD) travel time matrix (in minutes) between regional centroids using either (A) direct CSV pass-through with validation and name alignment, or (B) QGIS network analysis via Dijkstra’s algorithm on a line-based road/network layer. In mode B, it constructs a graph from the network layer, ties regional centroids to the nearest network nodes, computes shortest-path travel times using speed-aware edge weights (length × detour factor ÷ speed converted to min), enforces symmetry, and outputs a square CSV matrix indexed by region names. The script explicitly requires projected CRS for accurate distance calculation and validates unit consistency (km/h → min). No satellite, imagery, or temporal data is involved; inputs are vector layers (regions, network) and optional CSV — all user-provided local GIS data. Study area, time range, and remote sensing sources are not specified.

name: Calculate polygon interior angles
desc: The script calculates interior angles at each vertex of a selected polygon feature (single or multipart) using vector geometry. It extracts ordered vertices, computes the angle between consecutive edge vectors via dot and cross products, handles closed-ring topology with proper index wrapping, and outputs a point layer where each feature represents a vertex and stores the computed angle (in degrees or radians). Optional visual arc geometries are generated to illustrate angles. The output layer includes configurable fields (angle value, vertex index, source feature ID) and automatic labeling showing angle values with unit symbols.

name: Calculate shortest path through points
desc: The script calculates the shortest path visiting all points in a QGIS point layer using Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) heuristics — specifically Nearest Neighbor and optional 2-opt improvement. It supports manual start/end point selection via dialog or automatic selection (e.g., northernmost, closest-to-center). Input is a QgsVectorLayer of points; output is a QgsVectorLayer of type LineString containing a single polyline feature representing the optimal route. The output layer optionally includes attributes: total path length, point count, and semicolon-separated segment lengths. Distance is computed in map units using Euclidean geometry (QgsPointXY), with no CRS transformation applied during distance calculation — i.e., assumes planar coordinates. Layer storage options are temporary (in-memory) or permanent (GeoPackage/Shapefile).

name: Create convex hull from points
desc: The script creates a convex hull polygon geometry from all point features in a selected QGIS vector layer using QgsGeometry.fromMultiPointXY() and .convexHull(). It generates a new polygon layer (temporary or permanent GeoPackage/Shapefile) with configurable attributes: source layer name, point count, convex hull area/perimeter, and creation timestamp. The output layer is added to the QGIS project, optionally zoomed to, and recorded in the history manager with full feature and layer metadata.

name: Create line from point
desc: The script creates a line geometry starting from a user-selected point feature in QGIS, using user-specified length and direction (0° = North, clockwise). It computes the end point via trigonometric delta calculation (delta_x = length × sin(direction_rad), delta_y = length × cos(direction_rad)), constructs a QgsGeometry.fromPolylineXY([start_point, end_point]), and outputs a new vector layer (temporary or permanent) containing that single line feature. The layer includes attribute fields: id, length, direction, created_from, and created_at. Styling (color, width, dash pattern) is applied based on configurable settings, and optional zoom-to-extent and success messaging are performed.

name: Extract polygon boundary as line
desc: Creates a new vector line layer from the exterior ring of a selected polygon feature. The script extracts the boundary geometry using QgsGeometry.boundary(), with fallback manual extraction of exterior rings for single/multipart polygons. Outputs include a new QgsVectorLayer (temporary in-memory or permanent file-based), optionally with metadata fields (source_feature_id, source_layer, created_at), and supports CRS preservation, zoom-to-result, and history recording for undo/redo.

name: Create complete point connection graph
desc: The script creates a complete graph of lines connecting every pair of points in a selected QGIS point or multipoint layer. It iterates over all unique point pairs (i, j where i < j), constructs LineString geometries between their coordinates, and writes them to a new vector layer (temporary or permanent GeoPackage/Shapefile). The output layer optionally includes distance (in CRS units, rounded to specified decimal places) and 'from'/'to' point identifier fields. The action supports undo via layer removal and integrates with QGIS history manager for atomic layer creation tracking.

name: Extract polygon boundary lines
desc: Creates a new vector line layer by extracting the exterior ring(s) of all polygon or multipolygon features in the input layer. The script processes each polygon feature, calls QgsGeometry.boundary() (with fallback manual extraction of exterior rings), validates geometries, preserves source CRS, and optionally adds metadata fields (source_feature_id, source_layer, created_at). Output is either a temporary in-memory layer or a permanent file-based layer (GeoPackage or Shapefile).

name: Create point at location
desc: The script creates a point feature at a user-specified click location on the QGIS map canvas, either in an existing point layer or a new temporary memory layer. It handles CRS transformation between canvas and target layer, adds configurable attributes (ID, X/Y coordinates, timestamp), stores the feature in project scope (persisting until QGIS closes), records the action in an undo/redo history system, and optionally zooms to the point or shows confirmation. The core geospatial operations include QgsPointXY instantiation, QgsGeometry.fromPointXY(), QgsCoordinateTransform for CRS alignment, and QgsVectorLayer editing via dataProvider().addFeatures(). Outputs are a vector feature with attributes in a QgsVectorLayer (memory or existing), plus UI feedback and undo-capable history payload containing layer descriptor and feature backup.

name: Create bounding rectangle layer
desc: Creates a rectangular polygon layer that fully encloses the extent of a target line vector layer, with optional padding (in map units) applied to the minimum bounding rectangle; outputs either a temporary memory layer or a permanently saved shapefile or GeoPackage layer; applies an invisible fill symbol (no fill, no outline) to the resulting polygon layer.

name: Create square polygon around point
desc: The script creates a square polygon geometry centered on a user-selected point feature in QGIS, with configurable side length and rotation angle. It generates a new vector layer (temporary or permanent) containing only that square, applies outline-only styling with user-defined color and width, adds it to the project if requested, optionally zooms to its extent, and records the operation in an undoable history stack. The square's attributes include ID, side length, source reference, and timestamp. All operations use QgsGeometry, QgsVectorLayer, and QgsCoordinateTransform APIs for CRS-aware geometry creation and layer management.

name: Create squares around point features
desc: Creates square polygons centered on each point feature in a QGIS vector layer, with user-configurable side length and rotation; outputs a new vector layer (temporary or permanent) containing the squares, styled with customizable outline color/width and transparent fill, and optionally zooms to the extent of the generated squares.

name: Fill polygon gaps to create seamless coverage
desc: The script analyzes a user-provided QGIS polygon vector layer to detect and fill geometric gaps between adjacent polygon features. It supports three gap-detection modes ('bounding box', 'convex hull', 'enclosed only'), applies area filters (min/max gap area), and assigns each gap to the neighboring polygon with the longest shared boundary—using direct intersection, buffered intersection, and distance fallback logic. The output is a new polygon vector layer (temporary or permanent) where all qualifying gaps are merged into adjacent polygons, preserving original attributes optionally. The script performs iterative union-and-gap-detection up to 10 passes to handle cascading gap resolution after initial merges, and includes QGIS-specific functionality for layer registration, zoom-to-result, success messaging, and undo/history support.

name: Generalize line layer geometry
desc: The script generalizes line and multiline features in a QGIS vector layer using the Douglas-Peucker algorithm (via QgsGeometry.simplify()). It reduces vertex count while preserving overall shape, supporting two output modes: (1) in-place modification of the original layer (with optional auto-commit and edit-mode handling), or (2) creation of a new memory-based (or optionally permanent) generalized copy layer. Input parameters include tolerance (distance threshold in map units), selection filtering (all vs. selected features), and storage options. Outputs include updated geometry, vertex reduction statistics, success/warning messages with quantitative summaries (e.g., 'Total vertices: 12456 → 3892 (reduced by 8564, 68.8%)'), and history records for undo/redo via stored WKB geometry payloads.

name: Generalize polygon layer geometry
desc: The script generalizes polygon and multipolygon features in a QGIS vector layer using the Douglas-Peucker algorithm (via QgsGeometry.simplify()) with a user-specified tolerance in map units. It supports two output modes: (1) creating a new temporary or permanent memory-based layer containing simplified geometries while preserving original attributes, or (2) in-place editing of the source layer’s geometries. Vertex counts before/after simplification are computed and reported, and history is recorded for undo support via base64-encoded WKB geometry backups. The action respects feature selection, handles edit mode automatically, and includes rollback-on-error and auto-commit capabilities.

name: Generate point density heatmap
desc: The script generates a kernel density estimation (KDE) raster heatmap from point vector layers using QGIS's 'qgis:heatmapkerneldensityestimation' algorithm. It calculates spatial point density with configurable radius, pixel size, kernel shape (Quartic/Triangular/Uniform/Triweight/Epanechnikov), decay ratio, and optional numeric weight field. Outputs include a styled pseudocolor raster layer (blue→cyan→green→yellow→red gradient representing increasing density), with support for temporary or permanent GeoTIFF storage, automatic extent-based parameter calculation, and integration into QGIS project with optional zoom and success messaging.

name: Rotate line layer geometry
desc: The script rotates line or multiline features in a QGIS vector layer by a specified angle (degrees) around their centroid. It supports two execution paths: (1) creating a new memory (or optionally saved) rotated copy layer with identical attributes and MultiLineString geometry, or (2) modifying the original layer in-place in edit mode. For in-place edits, it records undo payloads containing base64-encoded WKB representations of old and new geometries for each processed feature. The script validates input layer geometry type (QgsWkbTypes.LineGeometry), respects selection state, handles empty/invalid geometries, and provides user-configurable options including default angle, copy vs. in-place behavior, storage type (temporary/permanent), auto-commit, edit-mode automation, and rollback on error. Outputs include a rotated layer (new or modified), success/warning messages with counts, and history entries for undo/redo support.

name: Rotate polygon layer geometry
desc: The script rotates polygon or multipolygon features in a QGIS vector layer by a specified angle (degrees) around their centroid. It supports two execution paths: (1) creating a new memory (or optionally permanent) rotated copy layer with identical attributes and CRS, or (2) modifying the original layer in-place via editing session, updating geometries while preserving attributes. For in-place edits, it records undo payloads containing base64-encoded WKB of old and new geometries per feature for robust undo/redo support. The dialog collects user inputs including rotation angle (±360°), selection scope (all vs. selected features), and output mode (copy vs. modify), and displays success/warning messages with counts of processed and skipped features.

name: Calculate line segment lengths
desc: Creates a point layer with labeled points at the midpoint of each line segment, displaying the Euclidean length of that segment in map units; supports single/multi-line geometries; outputs include a temporary or permanent point vector layer with attributes for segment length, optional segment index and feature ID, invisible point symbols, and PAL-based labels configured per user settings (decimal places, size, color, placement).

name: Calculate line segment lengths
desc: The script computes the Euclidean length of each straight-line segment in a clicked line or multiline feature, places a point at the midpoint of each segment, and labels that point with the segment's length (optionally prefixed by segment index). It creates a new point vector layer (temporary or permanent) with attributes 'segment_length' and optionally 'segment_index', applies invisible point symbology, and configures PAL labeling using QgsPalLayerSettings with customizable formatting (decimal places, size, color, placement). Total length is computed and optionally reported. The action operates on individual QGIS vector features via right-click context menu and requires line/multiline geometry.

name: Display polygon area label
desc: Creates a temporary or permanent point vector layer with a single feature at the centroid of a clicked polygon, labeled with its area value (calculated in appropriate projected CRS), with invisible point symbols and configurable label formatting (decimal places, size, color, placement, units). The layer is optionally added to the QGIS project, zoomed to, and recorded in history with style/labeling metadata.

name: Calculate polygon interior angles
desc: The script calculates interior angles at each vertex of all polygon features in a QGIS vector layer, creates a point layer with angle measurements (in degrees or radians) at each vertex location, and optionally generates arc geometries visualizing those angles. It handles both single and multipart polygons, supports selected-feature-only processing, skips invalid geometries by default, and outputs labeled point layers (temporary or permanent) with optional vertex index and source feature ID fields. Arc radius can be auto-calculated or user-specified, and labeling displays angle values with degree symbols for degrees.

name: Calculate polygon area values
desc: The script calculates the planimetric area of each polygon feature in a QGIS vector layer, transforms geometries to an appropriate projected CRS (UTM or Web Mercator) when input is geographic, computes centroids, creates a new point layer with area and feature ID attributes, applies labeling to display area values at centroids, and optionally saves the result as a permanent GeoPackage or Shapefile. It supports processing all features or only selected ones, handles invalid geometries optionally, formats labels with configurable decimal places, units, feature IDs, and styling, and makes point symbols invisible so only labels are visible.

name: Calculate polygon side lengths
desc: The script computes the Euclidean or CRS-aware geodesic length of each side (segment between consecutive vertices) of all polygon and multipolygon features in a QGIS vector layer. It extracts exterior ring vertices using multiple fallback methods (asPolygon(), boundary(), exteriorRing()), removes duplicate closure points, calculates distances between consecutive vertices (with UTM projection for geographic CRS), computes midpoints, and creates a point layer with attributes for side length, optional side index, and optional feature ID. Labels are rendered at midpoints showing formatted length values (with configurable decimal places, color, size, and placement), while point symbols are made invisible. The output is a labeled point layer — either temporary or saved to disk (GeoPackage/Shapefile) — with optional zoom-to-layer and success messaging including total perimeter.

name: Calculate polygon side lengths
desc: The script calculates the Euclidean or CRS-aware length of each side of a polygon (exterior ring only) by extracting vertex points, computing distances between consecutive vertices (including wrap-around for closure), and generating a point layer with labeled midpoints. It supports both geographic and projected CRSs—using on-the-fly UTM projection for accurate distance in geographic CRS—and outputs a temporary or permanent point vector layer with attributes 'side_length' (and optionally 'side_index'), invisible point symbols, and PAL-based labels showing formatted lengths at side midpoints. Perimeter is computed as the sum of all side lengths and optionally reported.

name: Smooth continuous line geometry
desc: The script processes line or multiline vector features from a QGIS layer, verifies they form a single continuous (end-to-end connected) line by analyzing endpoint adjacency and graph degree conditions, orders them into a topologically consistent sequence, merges them into one polyline, applies iterative Chaikin-style smoothing (via QgsGeometry.smooth() with iterations and offset parameters), and updates the original layer’s feature geometries with smoothed segments proportionally resampled along the total smoothed length. Outputs include in-place geometry updates to the source layer, full undo support via history recording (update_geometry type), and progress dialogs for sampling and application. No new raster or external data is used — all operations are vector-based within QGIS using native QgsGeometry methods.

name: Smooth line layer geometry
desc: The script applies Chaikin smoothing to line or multiline features in a QGIS vector layer, either modifying the original layer in-place or creating a new smoothed memory layer. It uses QgsGeometry.smooth(iterations, offset) with user-configurable iterations (1–10) and offset (0.0–1.0), supports selected-feature processing, preserves attributes, handles edit mode automatically, and implements full undo/redo via geometry backups and layer creation payloads. Outputs include updated feature geometries or a new vector layer named '<original_name> - smoothed', with success messages and history recording via HistoryManager.

name: Smooth polygon layer boundaries
desc: The script smooths the borders/edges of polygon or multipolygon features in a QGIS vector layer using Chaikin's corner cutting algorithm (via QgsGeometry.smooth()). It accepts configurable iterations (1–10) and offset (0.0–1.0) parameters to control smoothing strength. The workflow supports two output modes: (1) creating a new temporary or permanent memory-based layer with smoothed geometries (preserving original), or (2) editing the original layer in-place with optional auto-commit and rollback on error. Input is a selected vector layer (or detected polygon feature’s layer); processing scope is configurable to all features or only selected ones. Outputs include the smoothed layer (new or modified), geometry-level undo metadata (base64-encoded WKB backups), and optional success/warning messages with counts and parameters.

name: Split line layer by attribute
desc: The script splits a QGIS vector line layer into multiple new layers based on unique values in a user-selected attribute field. Each output layer contains all line or multiline features sharing the same value in that field, preserves all original attributes, and supports both temporary (in-memory) and permanent (disk-based GeoPackage) storage. The action includes interactive UI elements: field selection dialog, split preview with feature counts per value, confirmation dialog with optional original-layer deletion, and post-execution history recording for undo support. Output layers retain CRS, styling (renderer/symbol properties), labeling configuration, and are optionally added to the QGIS project.

name: Split point layer by attribute
desc: The script splits a QGIS point vector layer into multiple new layers based on unique values in a user-selected attribute field. Each output layer contains all point features sharing that value, preserves all original attribute fields and geometry, and supports optional permanent (disk-based) or temporary (in-memory) storage. Output layers can be added to the QGIS project, and the original layer may be optionally deleted with associated files (e.g., .shp/.dbf for Shapefiles, .gpkg for GeoPackage). The action includes validation for point geometry, field selection, value grouping, name sanitization, style/labeling preservation in history, and robust file deletion retry logic with Windows permission handling.

name: Split polygon layer by attribute
desc: The script splits a QGIS vector polygon layer into multiple new layers based on unique values in a user-selected attribute field. Each output layer contains all features sharing that value, preserves all original attribute fields and geometry, and supports both temporary (in-memory) and permanent (disk-based GeoPackage) storage. The action includes preview confirmation, optional deletion of the original layer and its associated files (e.g., .shp/.dbf for shapefiles, .gpkg for GeoPackage), history recording for undo, and automatic project addition. It operates exclusively on polygon/multipolygon layers and handles edge cases like NULL values, invalid paths, file locks, and Windows read-only permissions.

name: Trace polygon layer outline
desc: The script unions all valid polygon geometries in a QGIS vector layer into a single geometry, computes its convex hull, and extracts the exterior ring as a single (multi)line feature representing the tightest outer boundary enclosing all input polygons. It supports invalid geometry repair via makeValid(), outputs a new line layer with metadata fields (src_count, src_layer), and offers temporary/permanent storage options with project integration, zoom-to-result, and undo support.

name: Delineate catchments and compute flow rates
desc: The script delineates upstream catchments and flowpaths for user-provided pour points (or culvert network), snaps pour points to the nearest high-flow-accumulation cell within a specified pixel distance, and computes runoff-based flow rates per catchment ID using a selected rainfall-runoff method (e.g., rational or modified rational) and area sensitivity factor. Outputs include GeoJSON or shapefile layers for catchments and flowpaths, a snapped pour points layer, and a JSON file mapping each catchment ID to its computed peak flow rate (m³/s).

name: Estimate equal area slope
desc: The script computes equal-area slope (EAS) values for line features by sampling elevation along each line segment from a raster DEM, applying trapezoidal integration to compute the area under the elevation–distance profile, and deriving slope as the height difference between bounding elevations of an equivalent rectangle with same area and length. It processes vector line layers against a raster elevation layer, performs forward and backward sampling passes to improve robustness, averages the two EAS estimates per feature, and appends the result as a new 'EAS' attribute. Optionally exports results to CSV. No raster output is generated; output is strictly vector attribute-based.

name: Simulate urban wastewater and runoff flow
desc: The script performs hydraulic simulation of urban wastewater and stormwater runoff using the MLA (Modèle de Lois d'Assainissement) model developed by INSA Lyon. It integrates rainfall time-series data (mm/min), daily wastewater discharge patterns (m3/s), observed spill flows (m3/s), pipe network geometry and hydraulics (slope, length, lag), and urban catchment characteristics (imperviousness, population, soil infiltration parameters, initial losses, etc.) to compute produced runoff volumes per catchment. Outputs include: (1) a dictionary of simulated volumes keyed by watershed number; (2) updated 'volume_produit' attribute in the input watersheds vector layer; and (3) for the companion algorithm, derived urban catchment polygons from DEM-based watershed delineation along sewer pipes. The core workflow involves preprocessing spatial layers (reprojection, clipping, sampling), DEM depression filling and flow direction computation via pysheds, catchment aggregation per pipe sample point, raster-to-vector conversion, and morphological buffering/erosion to merge fragmented catchments.

name: Extract OSM buildings and roads
desc: The script queries the Overpass API to extract OpenStreetMap (OSM) building and road features within a user-defined polygon area. It constructs an Overpass QL query targeting 'way' elements with 'building' or 'highway' tags, parses the JSON response, reconstructs geometries from node coordinates, assigns relevant OSM tags as attributes, reprojects to the project's CRS if requested, clips the extracted features to the input polygon, and outputs three layers: (1) a clipped polygon layer of individual buildings, (2) a dissolved polygon layer of merged (adjacent/touching) buildings, and (3) a clipped line layer of roads.

name: Create sewer scenario geopackage
desc: The script creates a GeoPackage file containing a set of pre-defined sewer network layers (sinks, pumping stations, lifting stations, sewer pipes, roads, buildings, info_network), a treatment trains layer (one feature per WWTP, validated by unique 'sink_coords'), and a metadata layer with scenario name, current datetime, and UUID. It packages all layers into a single output GeoPackage using QGIS's 'native:package' algorithm, then explicitly saves all layer styles into the GeoPackage's QGIS layer_styles table using the OGR provider's saveStyle method.

name: Generate sewer pipe network
desc: The script generates a gravity- and pressure-driven sewer pipe network by optimizing pipe routing along roads, connecting buildings to wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) using DEM-derived elevation constraints and hydraulic design rules. It leverages pysewer — a Python package for sewer network optimization — to compute pipe diameters, slopes, depths, flow directions, peak flows, and sub-network partitions. Inputs include building points (with population attribute), road lines, DEM raster, and optional WWTP points; outputs are seven GeoPackage layers: WWTP, pumping stations, lifting stations, sewer pipes (with 6 QGIS styles: diameters, gravity-driven, flow direction, depth, peak flow, sub-networks), buildings, roads, and network information (non-spatial table). All layers are CRS-consistent and styled programmatically via OGR provider API.

name: Snap buildings to road vertices
desc: The script projects building centroids onto the nearest road vertices within a user-defined maximum distance (default 40 m), aggregates population values and building counts at each snapped vertex, and outputs: (1) an aggregated point layer with fields for summed population, building count, and status ('Projected'/'Not projected'); (2) line features representing projection paths from original centroids to snapped vertices; and (3) a split road layer (using native QGIS 'splitlinesbylength' with default max length 15 m). It enforces CRS consistency, removes spurious 'order' fields added by splitting, and applies a QML style post-processing step. The core snapping logic uses geopandas spatial indexing (sindex) and exact vertex extraction from LineString coordinates, with rounding to 1e-6 precision for deduplication.

name: Generate synthetic coastal vulnerability index tracts
desc: The script generates in-memory QGIS vector layers representing synthetic coastal segments around Italian minor islands, with pre-calculated CVI (Coastal Vulnerability Index) values derived from four input parameters (geomorphology, slope, land use, exposure) scaled 1–5. Each feature contains a LineString geometry approximated via elliptical distribution within a bounding box, plus attributes: GEOMORF, PENDENZA, USO_SUOLO, ESPOSIZ, TRATTO, ISOLA, CVI (sqrt((g*p*u*e)/4)), RISCHIO (risk class), and CVI_COLOR (hex color). The layer is immediately ready for visualization and plugin testing without real geospatial data.

name: Clip and dissolve land units by project area
desc: The script performs a vector-based spatial clipping of a land unit layer (UC) using a national project boundary layer (AreaProyecto), then dissolves the clipped features by the 'SimboloUC' attribute to aggregate contiguous or identical land units. The final output is a dissolved shapefile representing the areal distribution of land unit symbols within the project boundary, enabling percentual area calculation of each symbol class (e.g., for ADP — Área de Distribución de Proyectos). No raster analysis, classification, or temporal processing is performed; it is purely geometric vector overlay and aggregation.

name: Clip and dissolve administrative boundaries by project area
desc: The script clips an input vector layer (GestoresCatastrales municipal services layer) using a polygon mask (ANLA MAGNA AreaProyecto), dissolves the clipped features by the 'gestor_cat' attribute, reprojects the result to EPSG:9377 (MAGNA-SIRGAS / Colombia Bogota zone), then computes and appends two new fields: 'Aha' (area in hectares, calculated in the target CRS) and 'APD' (Area Percentual Distribution — percentage of each dissolved feature’s area relative to the total area of all dissolved features). The final output is a reprojected, dissolved, area- and APD-annotated shapefile.

name: Clip vector layers by boundary
desc: The script clips all shapefiles (.shp) in an input directory to the spatial extent of a provided polygon clipping layer (ReseneUzemi_p.shp), retaining only features that intersect the clipping geometry. It performs geometric intersection between each input feature and the unified clipping geometry, writes clipped features (with original attributes) to new shapefiles in the output directory, skips layers with no intersection or invalid geometries, and reports processing statistics. The core geospatial operations are QgsGeometry.unaryUnion, geom.intersects(), geom.disjoint(), and geom.intersection().

name: Derive slope and stream networks
desc: The script processes a digital elevation model (DEM) mosaic to compute terrain slope, reclassify slope into restriction classes (0–25°, 25–45°, ≥45°), extract stream networks and spring points (as vector features), and clip all outputs to a user-provided polygon area of interest. It uses GRASS GIS hydrological tools (r.fill.dir, r.stream.extract) for flow direction and stream delineation, GDAL slope computation, raster reclassification, and vector clipping to generate five final products: (1) clipped slope raster, (2) raster of areas with slope >45°, (3) raster of areas with slope 25–45°, (4) clipped stream network vector, and (5) clipped spring point vector.

name: Delineate riparian and spring protection areas
desc: The script delineates Areas of Permanent Preservation (APP) in Brazil by generating buffer zones around hydrographic features (rivers/streams) and springs (point sources), merging and dissolving the buffers into a single polygon layer, and clipping the result to a user-provided administrative or study area boundary. It outputs a vector layer ('APP') representing legally mandated environmental protection zones adjacent to water bodies and headwaters, as defined by Brazilian environmental legislation (e.g., Law 12.651/2012).

name: Clip airports buffer to county boundary
desc: The script selects the 'Nueces' county from a counties shapefile, creates a new layer containing only that county, loads an airports point layer, generates a 5000-meter buffer around airports (without dissolve), and clips that buffer layer to the Nueces county boundary. The output is a clipped polygon layer ('clippedbufferAirports.shp') representing only the portions of the airport buffers intersecting Nueces County.

name: Generate hunting lot-parcel intersection layers
desc: The script processes vector layers representing hunting lots and land parcels to generate two new output layers: (1) a parcel-lot intersection layer ('parclot') containing geometric intersections with calculated surface area and proportional 'contenance' (a land management attribute), and (2) a dissolved lots layer ('nwlots') aggregating intersected geometries by lot ID, enriched with total contenance per lot; both outputs are saved in a GeoPackage, styled with categorized symbology, aliased field names, and inserted at the top of the QGIS layer panel.

name: Calculate hydropower generation potential
desc: The script computes the annual economic value of hydroelectric power generation (EVHP) for run-of-river (RoR) and reservoir-based hydropower stations across administrative municipalities (CODIMUNI), comparing baseline (BC) and scenario (SC) conditions. It integrates SWAT+ hydrological model outputs (daily channel flow and reservoir release), spatial layers of hydropower station locations and derivation points, and municipal boundaries to estimate gross head, technical minimum flow, environmental flow constraints, and turbine-generation-transformer efficiency losses. The workflow calculates daily usable flow (Qdisp), turbine flow (QPTurb), hydraulic energy (QPTxSB), gross head per station-day (SaltBrutCH), and finally electricity revenue (DEVhp, DEVhpEmb), aggregated first by station, then by municipality, and ultimately as net change (EVHP_SC − EVHP_CB) per municipality. Output is a vector layer of municipalities with attribute 'EVHP' representing the scenario minus baseline annual economic value (currency units).

name: Quantify urban land area near rivers
desc: The script calculates the surface area (in hectares) of urban land cover (LULC classes DN=1 and DN=2) within 50 m of rivers (SWAT-referenced waterways), then computes an aesthetic service metric (Hpd) by multiplying the urban area (ha) by a fixed coefficient (194.129488213811). It also clips urban LULC to a 500–50 m buffer annulus around rivers for comparative spatial analysis. Outputs include a vector layer with a new 'Hdp' attribute representing the computed aesthetic service value per feature.

name: Classify bird movement by gender and tag identity
desc: The script preprocesses bird movement point data from Movebank by (1) joining gender information from an external CSV metadata file using 'tag-id' as key; (2) removing 17 unnecessary sensor, status, and auxiliary fields (e.g., 'battery_vo', 'speed', 'heading'); (3) shifting the 'timestamp' forward by 17 hours (not backward — despite `timedelta(hours=17)` being subtracted in code, the comment states 'shifting 17 hours forward for daily purpose' and the logic is misaligned: `adjustedTimeStamp = regularTimeStamp - timedelta(hours=17)` *actually shifts backward*, but the stated intent and documentation ('shifting 17 hours forward') dominate interpretation for task summary; however, per strict code reading it's a 17-hour backward shift to align with a daily 19:00 origin — i.e., converting to a custom local day starting at 19:00 UTC, making timestamps effectively 'day-aligned' for aggregation; (4) adding two new fields: 'Gender' (string) and 'mod_time' (string-formatted datetime); and (5) splitting the preprocessed layer into individual shapefiles per unique 'tag_ident', producing one shapefile per bird. Outputs are gender-annotated, time-adjusted, field-minimized, and tag-wise split vector layers stored in the Outputs/Preprocessing folder.

name: Compute concave hull geometry
desc: The script computes a concave hull polygon from an input point layer using the alpha shapes algorithm. It performs Delaunay triangulation, calculates maximum edge lengths per triangle, filters out triangles with longest edge > alpha × global max edge length, dissolves the remaining triangles into a single polygon (optionally removing interior rings/holes), and outputs either singlepart or multipart polygon geometry based on user parameters. The output is a vector polygon layer representing the concave hull envelope of the input points.

name: Convert CSV point data to shapefile
desc: The script converts CSV files containing longitude and latitude columns into ESRI Shapefile format vector layers. It uses QGIS's delimited text layer driver to ingest CSVs with 'longitude' and 'latitude' fields (hardcoded), assigns EPSG:4326 CRS, validates feature count and layer validity, then writes output shapefiles to a newly created 'Shapefile' subfolder within the input folder. No reprojection, attribute filtering, or geometry transformation is performed—only coordinate-based point layer creation and export.

name: Simplify boundary geometry
desc: The script simplifies the input polygon boundary layer using the Douglas-Peucker algorithm with a user-defined tolerance (in meters), after reprojecting to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) for metric consistency; it computes and appends vertex counts before and after simplification, then reprojects the result back to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) and fixes geometries to ensure topological validity. The output is a vector layer of simplified polygons with two new integer fields: 'vertices_boundary' and 'vertices_simplified'.

name: Convert as-applied points to lines
desc: The script converts point-based agricultural as-applied data (e.g., from precision agriculture equipment) into continuous line features by grouping sequential points based on heading alignment (within a user-defined angle tolerance) and proximity (bounded by twice the majority distance value in the input). It sorts points by a timestamp or sequence field, optionally groups by a vehicle or pass ID, computes geodesic distances using WGS-84 ellipsoid, calculates azimuth of resulting line segments, and outputs a line vector layer with attributes: heading (adjusted to forward direction), total segment distance (meters), and number of constituent points. Output CRS matches input CRS, reprojected if needed.

name: Convert application points to rectangles
desc: The script converts point features representing agricultural as-applied data (e.g., fertilizer, pesticide, or seed application) into oriented rectangular polygons. It reads heading (azimuth), distance (length), and width attributes from input points; converts units from feet to meters; computes rectangle vertices by rotating and translating a centered axis-aligned rectangle; reprojects input points to UTM using an automatically computed zone (based on extent centroid longitude/latitude); constructs polygons in UTM coordinates; then reprojects the resulting rectangles back to WGS 84. The output is a polygon vector layer where each rectangle represents the spatial footprint of an application event, oriented per heading and sized per distance and width.

name: Convert as-applied points to straight lines
desc: The script converts sequential GPS point features (e.g., from agricultural machinery) into straight-line segments based on heading consistency and proximity. It groups points by a user-specified field (e.g., 'VehicleID'), sorts them by a timestamp or sequence field, filters points whose heading falls within ±angle of the dominant heading (or its opposite), then chains consecutive points into polylines if their inter-point heading difference ≤ angle and distance < 2× majority distance. Output is a line layer with attributes: heading (azimuth of line segment, adjusted +180° if <181°), total accumulated distance (meters), and number of points. Distance uses Vincenty ellipsoidal calculation on WGS-84 coordinates. Input CRS is reprojected to EPSG:4326 for accurate geodesic distance, and output is reprojected back to input CRS.

name: Reclassify land cover raster
desc: The script reclassifies an input land cover raster using a user-defined lookup table, then reprojects it to an equal-area CRS (ESRI:54009) and resamples to a specified pixel size (e.g., 1000 m); the primary output is a reclassified and reprojected land cover raster ('LC_reclassified'), intended for subsequent CoE (Convergence of Evidence) layer computation in a QGIS plugin context.

name: Attribute Google Places points
desc: The script retrieves additional attributes (rating, user_ratings_total, price_level) for existing Google Maps Places point features using the Google Places API 'place' endpoint. It takes an input vector layer of points containing place_id values, makes individual API calls per feature to fetch specified attributes, and outputs a new point layer with original geometry and attributes augmented by the retrieved numeric attributes. The processing involves dynamically adding fields to the input layer, calling googlemaps.Client.place() with session_token=None and requested fields, parsing the response result dictionary, and populating corresponding output fields with values or None if absent.

name: Download topographic DEM data
desc: The script downloads a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) raster file from OpenTopography.org for a user-defined geographic extent. It supports 11 DEM products (e.g., SRTM 30m, Copernicus GLO-30, EU DTM 30m, GEDI L3 1km), performs on-the-fly coordinate transformation of the input extent to WGS84 (EPSG:4326), constructs an API request URL with bounding box coordinates and selected DEM type, authenticates using an API key (stored in QGIS settings), downloads the GTiff-formatted DEM via QGIS’s native file downloader, and optionally loads the resulting raster into the QGIS project. Output is a georeferenced GeoTIFF DEM file.

name: Compute area-weighted average attribute
