desc: The script downloads Digital Height Model (DHM) data for Flanders, Belgium, specifically selecting from three variants: 'I DHM', 'II DTM', or 'II DSM', at resolutions of 1m, 5m, 25m, or 100m — subject to compatibility constraints (e.g., 'I DHM' excludes 1m; 'II DSM' excludes 25m/100m). It determines relevant map sheets ('kaartbladen') intersecting the user-provided study area polygon (via spatial join against a local 'Kbl/Kbl.shp' layer), downloads corresponding GeoTIFFs from Azure Blob Storage URLs (e.g., 'https://downloadagiv.blob.core.windows.net/digitaal-hoogtemodel-vlaanderen-raster-1m/...'), extracts and loads them as raster layers, builds a virtual raster (VRT) with nodata = -9999, and clips the merged raster to the input polygon using GDAL's 'cliprasterbymasklayer'. The final output is a clipped, resolution- and model-type–specific DEM/DSM/DTM raster saved to the specified destination. No time dimension, classification, or spectral analysis is performed — purely data acquisition and geospatial subsetting.

name: Extract hill segments from roads
desc: The script processes road centerlines to identify and extract hill segments—defined as road sections with net grade exceeding a user-defined minimum grade (default 2.5%)—by draping elevation from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM), computing climb/descent per segment, calculating net grade and height, filtering short segments (if enabled), and outputting vector features representing individual uphill or downhill hill segments (dissolved by direction and road name, then split into single parts) with attributes: 'name' (road name), 'direction' (1=uphill, 0=downhill), 'length', 'height', 'grade_net', and 'CAT' (grade_net × height). The workflow includes buffering/reprojecting the DEM extent for spatial alignment, densifying and splitting roads, z-draping, grade computation, directional classification, and attribute cleanup.

name: Linear reference event mapping
desc: The script performs linear referencing by projecting point events (e.g., infrastructure assets, inspection points) onto a single-part alignment line (e.g., road, pipeline, or rail centerline), computing the perpendicular distance from each event to the line, the measured distance along the line to the nearest projection point, side-of-line classification (Left/Right/On Line), and consolidated start/end records for duplicate event IDs. It outputs a vector table (MultiPoint geometry) with attributes including fid, event_id, event_layer, comment, distance_away, distance_line, formatted distance string, side_of_line, projected x/y coordinates, and event_type (Unitary, Start, or End). Input validation enforces planar CRS in feet, single-feature alignment, and CRS-matched event layers.

name: Compute near-distance matrix between layers
desc: The script computes a distance matrix between features in an input vector layer and a near vector layer, generating line geometries representing the shortest distance between each pair of features. It reprojects the near layer to match the input layer's CRS if necessary, extracts specified attribute fields from both layers, calculates Euclidean distance using QgsGeometry.distance(), constructs shortest-line geometries with QgsGeometry.shortestLine(), and outputs a feature sink containing input ID, near ID, distance value, and connecting line geometry.

name: Burn FMask cloud mask into image
desc: The script burns an FMask-derived cloud, shadow, snow, water, land, or null pixel mask into a source raster image by first aligning the mask to the image's projection, extent, and resolution using GDAL warp; then reclassifying the aligned mask into binary (0/1) based on user-selected FMask classes; and finally applying the binary mask via OTB BandMathX multiplication (im1*im2b1) to produce a masked output raster where masked pixels are set to zero.

name: Split line features by point locations
desc: The script splits input line vector features (e.g., rivers, roads, boundaries) at the geometric locations of input point features (e.g., sampling points, intersections, or markers), producing a new set of contiguous sub-line segments. It achieves this by extracting line vertices, snapping input points to the nearest line geometry, joining snapped points to their closest vertex indices along the line, and then reconstructing ordered polyline geometries between consecutive split points — preserving original line attributes and optionally appending beginning/ending point attributes with prefixed field names. The output is a vector layer of segmented lines with enriched attribute tables.

name: Count points in polygons by time
desc: The script counts point features within polygon features for user-defined time intervals. It takes polygon and point layers, a datetime field from the point layer, and start/end datetime strings; then divides the time range into equal intervals (in seconds), iterates over each interval and polygon, and counts points that fall both spatially within each polygon and temporally within each interval. Points are removed from the spatial index after counting to avoid double-counting. Outputs a new polygon layer with added fields: 'from_datetime', 'to_datetime', and 'pointcount'.

name: Join attributes by nearest centroid with condition
desc: The script performs a spatial join between a source layer and a join layer based on the nearest centroid distance, optionally filtered by a user-defined field comparison condition (e.g., equality, inequality, greater-than). It supports joining up to N nearest neighbors within a maximum distance, applies optional filter expressions to both layers, allows selection of specific join fields, prefixes joined attributes, and outputs a new layer with original source attributes, matched join attributes, and a distance field. The algorithm uses QgsSpatialIndex for efficient nearest-neighbor search and handles CRS reprojection if needed.

name: Join attributes by nearest with condition
desc: The script performs a spatial join between two vector layers (source and join layers) where features from the source layer are matched to the N nearest features in the join layer based on geometry (either full geometry or centroid), optionally filtered by a maximum distance and a user-defined attribute comparison condition (e.g., field equality, inequality, containment). It supports expression-based pre-filtering of both layers, optional field subset selection from the join layer, customizable prefixing of joined fields, and outputs a new vector layer containing all source attributes, selected (or all) join attributes, and an added distance field. When no matching neighbor satisfies the condition (or distance/neighbor limit), source features are retained with nulls for join attributes.

name: Estimate school-age population
desc: The script estimates single-year-of-age population counts (0–29 years) by sex (male, female, total) for user-defined administrative polygons, using WorldPop-style 5-year age-group raster datasets and Sprague multipliers. It then aggregates these into custom school-age groups (pre-primary, primary, lower secondary, upper secondary) based on configurable starting ages and durations. Outputs include a polygon layer enriched with age-specific population columns and two Excel files: one containing the estimated school-age populations per administrative unit, and another storing the input parameters (country code, year, age group definitions).

name: Correct PPK tag elevations
desc: The script processes GNSS-derived PPK (Post-Processed Kinematic) point positions (eventpos), samples a geoid height raster (geoideenformatoraster) at each point, and computes orthometric height by subtracting the geoid undulation (REDNAP1) from the ellipsoidal height (height(m)). It also constructs a standardized photo naming convention, populates orientation placeholders (phi/omega/lambda), and computes horizontal/vertical precision metrics (p_h, p_v) conditioned on GNSS solution quality (Q). The output is a reprojected and styled vector layer (PPK_tags) containing corrected heights and metadata suitable for photogrammetric control or UAV survey QA/QC.

name: Calculate earthwork volumes
desc: The script computes cut-and-fill earthwork volumes by differencing pre- and post-construction digital elevation models (DEMs) within a user-defined area polygon. It clips both DEMs to the area at a specified resolution, calculates three raster layers: total difference (POST − PRE), terra (positive difference = fill/volume added), and desmo (negative difference = cut/volume removed). Zonal statistics sum pixel values per polygon feature, then converts sums to volumetric units (m³) using resolution² scaling. Optionally applies bulk density to compute mass (tons). Outputs a vector layer with fields TOTAL (net volume m³), TERRA (fill m³), DESMO (cut m³), and TONS (mass if density provided), styled with predefined QML files.

name: Subdivide polygons into equal-area grids
desc: The script takes an input polygon shapefile with a 'GridID' field and subdivides each polygon into an n-by-n grid of smaller, equal-area polygons. It computes grid vertex coordinates using bilinear interpolation across the four corner points of each input polygon's bounding geometry, constructs new rectangular features for each grid cell, assigns hierarchical 'GridID' identifiers (e.g., 'A.1', 'A.2'), and writes results to a memory-based QgsVectorLayer. The workflow relies on QGIS Python API (PyQGIS) geometry operations, feature iteration, and attribute propagation — no remote sensing or time-series analysis is performed.

name: Calculate network-based travel time statistics
desc: The script computes network-based and linear (Euclidean) distance statistics between source points (e.g., origins like neighborhoods or facilities) and multiple target point layers (e.g., services such as schools, hospitals, shops) using a street network. It outputs: (1) a grid-like source layer enriched with max/Q3/mean network travel times (converted from cost in meters to minutes assuming 83.33 m/s ≈ 300 km/h — likely a placeholder speed; actual interpretation depends on network units and context), (2) convex hulls centered on source points formed by nearest targets per layer (only geometrically valid for ≥3 target layers), (3) a category-level summary table aggregating statistics per target layer (e.g., 'Hospitals', 'Schools'), and (4) a target-layer output enriched with origin-wise travel time statistics. The core method uses QNEAT3’s OD matrix (m:n) over a provided line network, followed by per-origin/per-destination aggregation, duplicate removal, geometry extraction, and unit conversion (cost → time).

name: Drop pins grab values aggregate
desc: The script implements a QGIS Processing algorithm that (1) generates a grid of points aligned to agricultural rows within a bounding polygon using row vector direction and spacing parameters, (2) attaches tabular or panel-based data to those points via a pin dropper, (3) samples raster values at each point using an external raster file (bypassing QGIS memory limits via QgsProcessingParameterFile), and (4) aggregates the sampled values into a regular grid using configurable cell dimensions and statistical functions. Outputs are a vector layer of points with sampled values and a vector grid layer of aggregated statistics.

name: Locate grab and aggregate field points
desc: The script implements a QGIS Processing algorithm that (1) generates a grid of points within a user-defined bounding polygon using row spacing and point interval parameters aligned to a direction vector, (2) extracts raster values at those points from an external raster file (e.g., crop health or soil moisture), and (3) aggregates the point values into a regular grid using user-specified fields and aggregation functions. Outputs are a vector layer of points with extracted raster values and a polygon grid layer summarizing aggregated statistics.

name: Generate perpendicular lines along line
desc: The script generates a set of perpendicular line segments at user-specified intervals along input line or polygon boundary geometries. It first reprojects the input layer to a target CRS (e.g., UTM), then places points along the lines using a distance-based sampling (with optional start/end offsets), and finally constructs perpendicular segments at each point using geometry expressions involving `project()`, `radians()`, and `extend()` — specifically computing a 90° offset from the local line direction (via `"angle"-90`). The output is a vector layer of line geometries, reprojected to the specified output CRS.

name: Generate plot grid and centroids
desc: The script processes an input vector layer (e.g., field boundaries or administrative polygons) to generate: (1) a memory-layer of square buffers (50×50 units) centered on each input feature using 'native:rectanglesovalsdiamonds'; (2) a regular point grid (5×5 unit spacing) aligned to the extent of those squares via 'native:creategrid'; (3) centroids of each grid cell; and (4) all vertices of the grid cells. All four derived layers — squares, grid polygons, centroids, and vertices — are added to the QGIS project as temporary in-memory layers for spatial sampling or field plot design.

name: Manage aerial film metadata
desc: The script manages aerial film metadata in a QGIS plugin interface, enabling users to input, edit, search, and export film records (e.g., film number, flight date, camera specs, weather code) stored in a SQLite/SpatiaLite database. It supports spatial queries to list associated archaeological sites or images intersecting the film’s flight path, extracts GPS points from image EXIF data to generate flight paths, and exports film details as a PDF with a map composed of vector flight path layers and tiled basemaps (basemap.at). Key operations include relational SQL model binding, dynamic combobox population, weather code translation via lookup table, and QgsComposition-based PDF report generation with embedded geospatial visuals.

name: Manage archaeological find spot records
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin dialog for managing archaeological find spot (fundstelle) records in a Spatialite database. It supports viewing, adding, editing, cloning, and deleting find spots; loading associated geometries (polygons/points) into QGIS; exporting details to PDF; and maintaining change logs. Key operations include SQL-based data binding via QSqlRelationalTableModel, dynamic combobox population from database queries (e.g., 'zeit', 'phase', 'kultur'), geometry centroid generation, and relational UI mapping of fields like 'fundart', 'datierung_zeit', and 'sicherheit'.

name: Map tourism pressures and opportunities
desc: The script performs MOPST (Mapping Opportunity & Pressures for Sustainable Tourism) analysis by integrating landcover sensitivity, seasonality scores, pressure areas, opportunity areas, and user-provided factor rasters. It computes weighted seasonal (summer/winter) pressure and opportunity scores for a baseline and multiple user-defined scenarios, rasterizing vector-based sensitivity attributes using pressure raster geometry as template, applying factor-specific weights and scenario multipliers, and aggregating results via pixel-wise summation. Outputs include four rasters per scenario (pressure-summer, opportunity-summer, pressure-winter, opportunity-winter) saved in scenario-named subdirectories, plus baseline rasters, all in GeoTIFF format, along with an execution log.

name: Create spatial grid over buffer area
desc: The script creates a regular polygonal grid (as a shapefile) aligned to the extent of a single-feature input buffer layer, where each cell is sized by a user-defined cell_size (500 units). It uses OGR to generate axis-aligned rectangular polygons, filters them to retain only those intersecting the input buffer geometry, and writes the result to an output shapefile. The workflow includes QGIS initialization for extent extraction, progress reporting via ASCII bar, and strict validation that the input layer contains exactly one feature.

name: Link point features to nearest line vertices
desc: The script creates line features connecting each point feature in a Point Layer to the closest vertex (or closest segment point) on a Line Layer, using spatial proximity within a user-defined buffer distance. It computes the shortest distance from each point to candidate line features clipped by that buffer, constructs a line geometry between the point and the closest location on the line, stores the distance and optional ID attributes (from both layers), and outputs a new memory vector layer named 'relations'. Optionally, it also selects and exports points that failed to find a matching line within the buffer as a separate layer named '_rel_failed'.

name: Assess green space accessibility
desc: The script computes multi-scale green space and vegetation indicators around individual residential addresses using both Euclidean and network-based (street network) distance buffers (100–1500 m in 100-m increments). It calculates: (1) public green space area (PGS) accessible within network distance (m²), (2) NDVI mean values within Euclidean buffers (B100–B1500) and network service areas (SA100–SA1500), (3) semi-public (SPGS) and private (PRGS) green space area per individual (after subtracting building footprints), and (4) green space use diversity and total count (GS_play, GS_sports, GS_walk, GS_gard, GS_social, GS_other) across all distances. Outputs include joined attribute tables with fields like PGS_in_SA1100, NDVI_SA1500, GS_uses_sum_BSA1200, GS_uses_div_BSA800, and PGS_ACC (minimum access distance), delivered as vector feature sinks aligned to the input individuals layer.

name: Clip rasters by pastoral district
desc: The script clips four types of raster datasets—Growth Probability, Percentile Growth (at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months), TSDM (Total Standing Dry Matter), and TSDM Percentile—from the AussieGRASS system using pastoral district boundaries as masks. It iterates over each district polygon, selects it, extracts its name field (e.g., 'BARKLY' → 'Barkly'), and applies GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer algorithm to produce district-specific outputs in ERDAS IMAGINE (.img) format. Outputs are organized into three separate folders: one for Growth Probability rasters, one for Percentile Growth rasters (named with month suffixes), and one for TSDM and TSDM Percentile rasters.

name: Extract land system unit areas
desc: The script extracts and calculates land system/unit areas for property-level (dissolved paddocks), paddock-level, and watered-area-level (3km and/or 5km buffers around waterpoints) geometries. It spatially intersects a land types polygon layer (e.g., land systems or mapping units) with user-provided paddock polygons and optionally dissolved paddocks or buffered waterpoint zones, computes area metrics (m², ha, km², % of parent geometry) using either ellipsoidal (geodesic) or planar measurement, preserves selected attribute fields from the land types layer, and outputs vector layers in user-specified formats (GPKG, SHP, etc.). An optional Excel summary report aggregates all output layers’ attributes and geometry-derived area statistics.

name: Summarize fire risk classes by district
desc: Creates an Excel spreadsheet containing counts and percentages of pixels classified as low (0–20), moderate (20–30), and high (30–40) fire risk — excluding special values (0=no data, 253=firescar, 254=water) — for each pastoral district polygon; outputs include per-district counts, normalized percentages (relative to total risk-class pixels only), and a checksum validation column.

name: Calculate maximum distance to water
desc: The script calculates the maximum Euclidean distance from any point within each input paddock polygon to the nearest water point (e.g., bore, trough, dam) using raster-based proximity analysis. It first transforms input layers to a common projected CRS (prioritizing input projection or defaulting to EPSG:9473 Australian Albers for geographic inputs), then for each paddock: (1) extracts intersecting water points, (2) rasterizes them into a binary mask at user-specified resolution, (3) computes a GDAL proximity raster (distance in map units), (4) clips the proximity raster to the paddock boundary, and (5) determines the local maximum distance (in meters). Outputs include individual clipped proximity rasters (one per paddock with ≥1 water point), an optional Excel report listing paddock name, area (ha), water point count, and max distance to water (km), and — if enabled — automatically loaded and styled rasters in QGIS with a gradient color ramp scaled to the global maximum distance across all paddocks.

name: Plot pasture growth trends
desc: The script generates stacked, median monthly pasture growth graphs for pastoral districts in the Northern Territory of Australia, using raster time-series data from three consecutive financial years (e.g., 2021–2022 FY to 2023–2024 FY). It computes zonal statistics (mean and median) per district over monthly growth rasters, aggregates cumulative growth month-by-month across financial years, and plots smoothed or unsmoothed line graphs comparing current and prior financial years against long-term district-specific medians. Outputs are PNG files — one per district — showing monthly growth (kg/ha) across a July–June financial year cycle, with region-specific y-axis scaling and labeled legends.

name: Compute cumulative pasture growth medians
desc: The script computes stacked, median monthly pasture growth values for each pastoral district in the Northern Territory of Australia across three consecutive financial years (e.g., 2022–2023 FY, 2023–2024 FY, 2024–2025 FY), using pre-processed raster (.img) time series from a local directory. It performs pixel-wise summation (cumulative stacking) over sequential monthly rasters per financial year, then applies zonal statistics (mean and median) over polygon boundaries of pastoral districts to extract district-level cumulative growth metrics. Outputs are structured as an Excel spreadsheet with one tab per district, containing columns for financial year, calendar year, month, district name, cumulative mean growth, long-term median baseline (hardcoded per district), and cumulative median growth.

name: Calculate district-level burnt area percentage
desc: The script calculates the percentage of each pastoral district that has been burnt by wildfires, using vector-based spatial overlap analysis between a pastoral districts polygon layer and a NAFI (National Assessment of Fire and Fuel) firescar polygon layer. It computes two summaries: one filtered to firescarring events occurring from July onward (financial year), and another including all months (calendar year). For each district, it reports district area (km²), burnt area (km²), and percentage burnt. Results are exported to an Excel spreadsheet with two sheets: 'Area Burnt Summary Financial Year' and 'Area Burnt Summary Calendar Year'.

name: Summarize percentile growth by district
desc: The script counts pixels in seven percentile-based growth classes (Extremely low, Well below average, Below average, Average, Above average, Well above average, Extremely high) for each pastoral district using an input percentile growth raster and a pastoral district vector layer. It clips the raster to each district, computes pixel counts and percentages per class using GDAL and NumPy array operations, and exports the results—including counts, percentages, and a validation checksum—to an Excel spreadsheet.

name: Summarize TSDM pixel counts by pastoral district
desc: The script computes pixel count and percentage summaries for two raster datasets—AussieGRASS Total Standing Dry Matter (TSDM) and TSDM Percentile—within each Australian pastoral district polygon. For TSDM, it classifies pixels into four biomass classes (Low, Low-Moderate, Moderate, High) using region-specific thresholds (northern vs. southern districts), excludes NoData (0), and calculates percentages relative to non-zero pixels. For TSDM Percentile, it classifies pixels into three percentile-based categories (Below Average: 0–30, Average: 30–70, Above Average: 70–100), excludes special values (253 = fire scar, 254 = water, 0 = NoData), and computes percentages relative to the sum of the three main classes. Outputs are two tabular sheets in an Excel (.xlsx or .ods) workbook: one for TSDM biomass classes and one for TSDM percentile classes, both with district-level counts, percentages, and validation check sums.

name: Summarize total pasture growth by district
desc: The script stacks monthly raster layers of pasture growth (in kg/ha) for the current financial year, then clips the summed raster to each pastoral district and counts pixels falling into four growth classes (low, low-moderate, moderate, high), with class thresholds differentiated between northern and southern districts based on regional growth patterns. It outputs an Excel spreadsheet containing absolute counts and percentages of pixels in each class per district, plus a checksum validation column.

name: Manage raster attribute table
desc: The script implements a Python class hierarchy (RAT and RATField) for managing Raster Attribute Tables (RATs) in QGIS, supporting reading, modifying, inserting/removing columns and rows, setting colors, and saving RATs in DBF or GDAL XML formats. It integrates with QGIS raster rendering (QgsPalettedRasterRenderer, QgsSingleBandPseudoColorRenderer) to synchronize RAT color data with layer renderers, and uses GDAL's RasterAttributeTable API to persist changes to disk. Key operations include color field insertion/removal, row/column editing, validation against GDAL usage types, and conversion between RAT data and QgsFeature/QgsFields for vector export.

name: Densify polyline vertices
desc: The script resamples (densifies) the vertices of input polyline vector layers in QGIS using either a fixed distance or a specified number of segments per line. It supports processing selected features or all features, validates geometry type (line only), checks editability, and optionally creates a new copy of the layer before editing. The densification uses QgsGeometry.densifyByDistance() and removes duplicate nodes. Outputs are the modified (or newly created and modified) vector layer with increased vertex density.

name: Synchronize UAV video with GPS track
desc: The script synchronizes a UAV video with a GPX-formatted GPS track by matching video frame timestamps to GPS timestamps (1 trkpt per second), computes speed and course using GeographicLib's geodesic inverse calculation, and exports synchronized spatiotemporal metadata (latitude, longitude, elevation, speed, course, time) to a .vgp project file. It also supports creating an associated ESRI Shapefile database for POI annotation with linked video frames and coordinates.

name: Generate center points along well lines
desc: The script generates regularly spaced point features along line geometries representing wells, constrained by DSU (Drilling Spacing Unit) polygon boundaries. It reads a wells line layer and an acreage (DSU boundary) layer, computes interpolated points at specified intervals (or divides each line into equal segments), checks whether each generated point falls within its corresponding DSU polygon, and optionally nullifies the DSU ID attribute in the source line layer if the point lies outside. Output is a memory vector layer named 'center points' containing points with attributes 'api14', 'xValue', and 'yValue'.

name: Digitize median line between polygons
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin tool that digitizes a median line between two adjacent polygons by interactively selecting corresponding vertices on each polygon boundary. It collects vertex coordinates from two sides (side1_x/y and side2_x/y), computes the median polyline using a distance-based pairing algorithm in median_polyline(), constructs a QgsGeometry polyline from the computed points, and adds it to a memory-based CAD layer named 'CadLayer Lines'. The workflow requires an editable polygon layer, uses Qt signal-slot connections for vertex selection, and resets state after completion.

name: Generate digital surface model
desc: The script generates a Digital Surface Model (DSM) by combining a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) raster with building height data from OpenStreetMap (OSM) or user-provided polygon layers. It downloads OSM building data within a user-defined bounding box (transformed to WGS84), converts it to a shapefile, computes building heights using 'height', 'bld_hght', or estimated values from 'bld_levels' multiplied by a user-specified floor height, performs zonal statistics to extract mean elevation under each building polygon, adds this to building height to compute height above sea level ('height_asl'), sorts polygons by height to prevent lower buildings from overwriting higher ones during rasterization, and finally rasterizes the sorted polygons onto a DEM-aligned grid. Outputs include a DSM GeoTIFF file and optionally a processed building shapefile with height attributes.

name: Reclassify vector land use to UWG building types
desc: The script reclassifies polygon vector layers (e.g., building footprints or land use parcels) into Urban Weather Generator (UWG) building classes (e.g., 'LargeOffice', 'Hospital', 'SuperMarket') based on user-defined mapping from an existing attribute field. It adds two new string fields — 'UWGType' and 'UWGTime' — populated via a lookup dictionary built from UI inputs (old class values mapped to UWG types and time periods: 'Pre80', 'Pst80', 'New'), then writes the reclassified layer as a new Shapefile and adds it to the QGIS project.

name: Load and style OpenQuake hazard output layers
desc: The script loads OpenQuake Engine output files (NPZ/CSV) as QGIS vector layers, applies thematic styling based on output type (e.g., damages-rlzs, hmaps, ruptures), supports zonal aggregation, and handles metadata, projection validation, and layer rendering with graduated/categorized/single-symbol renderers using QGIS PyQGIS APIs. Outputs include styled vector layers in memory or loaded into the QGIS project, optionally aggregated by user-provided polygon zones.

name: Merge shapefile layers
desc: The script merges multiple input shapefiles into a single output shapefile, preserving geometry type and consolidating attributes by field name and type. It supports two input modes: directory-based (with optional geometry-type filtering) or explicit file list. The workflow includes reading each shapefile, building a unified field schema with length adjustment for string fields, handling encoding, and writing features to a new shapefile using QgsVectorFileWriter. Outputs include the merged shapefile and optional automatic addition to QGIS canvas.

name: Display what3words grid overlay
desc: The script dynamically fetches and renders the what3words (w3w) grid as a vector line layer overlaid on the QGIS map canvas based on the current map extent and zoom level (17–25). It transforms the canvas extent to WGS84 (EPSG:4326), calls the what3words API's getGridSection method with a bounding box, parses returned grid lines (each with start/end lat/lng), stores them as LineString features in a memory vector layer with attributes for bounding box (south/west/north/east), applies context-aware symbology (black/transparent for vector basemaps, white/semi-transparent for satellite basemaps), and supports saving the rendered grid to GeoJSON. The grid auto-updates on map pan/zoom when enabled.

name: Compute travel time isochrones
desc: The script computes raster-based travel time isochrones from user-defined starting points along a road network. It clips the road layer to an extent, rasterizes road speeds (km/h), assigns off-road speed (20 km/h) to nodata areas, calculates per-pixel travel time in minutes using resolution and speed, then performs cost-distance analysis (using GRASS r.cost.full) to generate a continuous travel time surface. The output is a styled raster where pixel values represent cumulative travel time from nearest starting point, with optional discrete styling at user-specified intervals (e.g., 5,15,30 minutes) and unit conversion (minutes/hours).

name: Draw 100 km radius circle
desc: The script creates a 100 km buffer polygon (circle) centered on Fort Nelson, British Columbia, using geocoded coordinates from the Nominatim API. It reprojects the point from WGS84 (EPSG:4326) to UTM zone 30N (EPSG:32630), generates a circular buffer with 64 segments, and exports the resulting polygon as a shapefile ('circle_100km.shp'). The layer is added to the current QGIS project. No time-based filtering or remote sensing data is used.

name: Draw 100km radius circle
desc: The script creates a 100 km buffer polygon around Fort Nelson, British Columbia, using geocoded coordinates (or fallback lat/lon), reprojects the point to the appropriate UTM zone (EPSG:32610), buffers it in meters, and exports the resulting circular AOI as a shapefile with metadata fields including center coordinates and radius. The output is added to the QGIS project and saved to disk.

name: Perform geocoding and reverse geocoding
desc: The script implements geocoding (address-to-coordinate) and reverse geocoding (coordinate-to-address) functionality within QGIS using web services (Nominatim/OpenStreetMap and Google Geocoding API). It provides a GUI plugin with dialogs for entering addresses, selecting results, configuring geocoders and API keys, and clicking on the map for reverse lookup. Results are displayed in QMessageBox popups and saved as labeled point features in a memory vector layer with CRS-aware coordinate transformation and on-the-fly reprojection handling.

name: Grid-based feature subdivision
desc: The script subdivides selected non-multipart vector features into a regular grid of square cells (2.4 units) using QGIS's creategrid algorithm, then intersects the grid with the original layer to split features spatially. It deletes the original selected features and appends the intersected grid cells as new features, assigning incremented FID values and marking them with 'y' in a 'Cut' attribute. Area calculation using WGS84 ellipsoidal mode filters out cells smaller than 1000 m² before insertion.

name: Parse and extract cadastral reference fields
desc: The script parses the Italian National Cadastral Reference (NCR) string field 'NATIONALCADASTRALREFERENCE' in an active QGIS vector layer, extracts structured components (comune, sezione, foglio, allegato, sviluppo, particella) using regex pattern matching and a lookup dictionary (mappa_codici_comuni), adds missing output fields to the layer schema, updates feature attributes accordingly, and optionally saves a detailed log file with parsing results and change records. It handles WFS/memory layers by duplicating them into editable memory layers first.

name: Mapillary vector tile coverage
desc: The script fetches, caches, and renders Mapillary vector tiles (overview, sequence, image layers) for the current QGIS canvas extent using Web Mercator tiling. It converts canvas extents to WGS84, computes tile ranges via deg2num/num2deg, downloads .mvt files from Mapillary's vector tile endpoints, decodes them as QgsVectorLayer objects, applies QML styling, and inserts them into a 'Mapillary' layer group in the QGIS project. The workflow includes proxy-aware HTTP requests, local filesystem caching with TTL-based expiration, zoom-level–dependent layer visibility, and integration with QGIS map canvas refresh events.

name: Finalize mining claim documents
desc: The script validates and aligns claim grid geometry, processes claims on the server to compute PLSS descriptions, corner coordinates, monument positions, and filing deadlines, then generates location notice documents and corner certificates. It reads user-adjusted monument positions from QGIS layers (discovery, sideline, endline), merges them into processed claims and waypoints, creates a styled Claims Waypoints layer with categorized symbology and labeling, and saves documents to the QGIS project. Outputs include validated/aligned vector layers, processed claim metadata, waypoint layers with UTM/WGS84 coordinates, and bundled document packages.

name: Optimize cellular antenna azimuth
desc: The script optimizes azimuth angles of cellular antenna sectors in a vector layer to minimize interference and maximize coverage. It groups features by site ID and band, computes neighbor proximity using planar distance (converted from km to degrees), calculates optimal azimuths using 3GPP antenna radiation pattern modeling (A(θ) = -min[12*(θ/θ_3dB)², A_m]), and supports three optimization modes: 'Minimize Overlap', 'Maximize Coverage', and 'Balanced'. Input fields include site ID, current azimuth, beamwidth, band, and optional lock flag; output is a new memory vector layer with an added optimal azimuth field.

name: Predict radio coverage area
desc: The script predicts radio signal coverage (RSRP in dBm) from cellular base stations using vectorized propagation modeling. It processes vector layers of transmitter sites, extracts antenna parameters (height, azimuth, beamwidth, power, gain, frequency), applies propagation models (Free Space, Okumura-Hata, COST-231 Hata, Ericsson 9999), incorporates clutter loss from OpenStreetMap land use/building data, and terrain diffraction loss from SRTM-derived elevation grids. Outputs are GeoTIFF rasters visualized with a pseudo-color ramp for RSRP values (-140 to -70 dBm), added to the QGIS project.

name: Analyze cellular sector interference
desc: The script performs radio frequency interference analysis for cellular network sectors in QGIS, detecting co-channel, adjacent-channel, and PCI (Physical Cell Identity) conflicts based on vector layer inputs containing site geometry, frequency, PCI, band, azimuth, beamwidth, site ID, and sector ID. It computes angular beam overlap between sector pairs within a user-defined interference distance, flags violations using configurable thresholds and detection rules (e.g., PCI mod3/mod6), creates a styled memory line layer visualizing interfering links with severity-based symbology, and generates a mitigation report with frequency, tilt, and PCI change suggestions.

name: Plan PCI and RSI assignments
desc: The script plans Physical Cell Identity (PCI) and Root Sequence Index (RSI) assignments for cellular network sites represented as vector features in QGIS. It groups features by technology and band, respects locked cells using existing PCI/RSI values, assigns new PCIs considering reuse distance and modulo-3/6 conflict avoidance, calculates required RSI counts per cell based on 3GPP-specified cell range and PRACH format, and assigns non-overlapping RSI ranges respecting reuse distance. Outputs include a new memory vector layer with added PCI plan, RSI plan, and RSI_COUNT fields, visualized in the QGIS project.

name: Generate RF sector coverage polygons
desc: The script creates RF sector coverage polygons and connection lines from vector point layers containing antenna parameters (azimuth, beamwidth, coordinates). It reads source vector layers, extracts site locations and sector attributes, constructs sector polygons using azimuth and beamwidth, applies nested sizing logic for multi-band sectors, generates connection lines for remote sectors, and applies categorized color rendering based on azimuth ranges or band values. Outputs include three memory layers: 'Sectors' (polygons), 'Sectors_Links' (lines), and 'Sectors_Sites' (points), all added to the QGIS project with appropriate styling.

name: Optimize antenna electrical tilt
desc: The script calculates optimal electrical downtilt angles for cellular base station antennas based on antenna parameters (height, vertical/horizontal beamwidth, transmit power, gain, frequency), propagation model selection (Free Space, Okumura-Hata Urban/Suburban, COST-231 Hata), target coverage distance, and neighbor interference analysis. It processes vector layers containing antenna site features, extracts geometry centroids, computes geometric tilt, path loss, signal strength adjustments, beamwidth-based corrections, and neighbor-aware interference mitigation, then appends an 'optimal tilt' field (in degrees) to a new memory layer with identical geometry and attributes. Output is a QGIS vector layer named '<input_layer_name>_Tilt_Optimized' with a new double-precision field containing rounded tilt values (0.0–15.0°).

name: Visualize permanent scatterer time series
desc: The script computes and visualizes time series of displacement speed for Permanent Scatterers (PS) derived from satellite interferometry. It selects a point feature from a vector layer (e.g., PS locations), identifies the corresponding time-series data by joining via identifiers (e.g., 'id_dataset'/'code_target' for Oracle, 'code' for PostGIS/SpatiaLite), extracts date-value pairs (e.g., 'data_misura'/'spost_rel_mm' or 'dataripresa'/'valore'), converts dates from 'yyyyMMdd' format, and plots the resulting time series. Outputs include an interactive plot dialog showing displacement over time and metadata from non-date fields.

name: Calculate road longitudinal slope
desc: The script calculates longitudinal slope (%) for forest paths and roads by segmenting a 2D line vector layer (road network) into user-defined lengths (default 250 map units), draping each segment onto a DEM to assign elevation (Z) values at vertices, extracting first and last Z values per segment, computing segment length, and deriving slope as |z_first − z_last| / length × 100. Outputs a new segmented line vector layer with two added fields: 'Length' (actual segment length, including residuals) and 'Slope_%' (longitudinal slope in percent). It explicitly warns against use on engineered national roads without high-precision DSM due to terrain smoothing artifacts.

name: Remove topographic artefacts
desc: The script removes topographic artefacts by applying user-defined Python expressions (e.g., 'H>500') to raster elevation data within polygon masks. It rasterizes input vector polygons, evaluates expressions on the topography array (H), sets matching pixels to NaN, and optionally interpolates the resulting NoData areas. Outputs include a modified topography raster (GeoTIFF) or an interpolated version, with optional saving of mask polygons as a Shapefile.

name: Generate hypsometric curves from DEM
desc: The script generates hypsometric curves from a digital elevation model (DEM) by first loading the 'dem_terrain.tif' raster, extracting its extent to create a boundary polygon shapefile ('boundary.shp'), and then running the QGIS 'hypsometriccurves' algorithm with a 100-unit elevation step and percentage-based output. The result is histogram files prefixed with 'histogram_' saved in the working directory.

name: Generate hypsometric curves from DEM
desc: The script generates hypsometric curves from a digital elevation model (DEM) named 'dem_terrain.tif'. It first loads the DEM in QGIS, extracts its spatial extent and CRS, creates a boundary polygon matching that extent as a shapefile ('boundary.shp'), then runs the QGIS 'hypsometriccurves' algorithm with a 100-meter elevation step and percentage-based histogram output. The result is saved in the working directory as histogram files prefixed with 'histogram_' — indicating elevation distribution analysis by area percentage.

name: Extract PRISM temperature statistics
desc: The script computes mean temperature values from PRISM raster layers (identified by names starting with 'PRISM') for each zip code polygon in the 'Zip_Codes' vector layer using zonal statistics. It iteratively joins the resulting mean temperature fields—prefixed by the last two characters of each PRISM layer name (e.g., '01' for January)—to a growing result layer, producing a single vector layer ('Zip_Codes' extended with multiple PRISM-derived mean temperature columns) that is added to the QGIS project.

name: Dissolve features by attribute and sum field
desc: The script performs a dissolve operation on vector features based on a user-selected attribute field, then computes the sum of values from another specified numeric field for each dissolved group. It uses QGIS Processing's native:dissolve algorithm, aggregates sums via Python dictionary accumulation, and outputs a new vector layer with dissolved geometries and summed attributes. Input parameters include source vector layer, dissolve field, and sum field; output is a feature sink with two fields: the dissolve field (string) and 'SUM_' + sum_field (double).

name: Generate internal points for polygons
desc: The script creates an internal point (using the GEOS pointOnSurface operation) for each polygon feature in a user-selected vector layer. It handles multipart geometries by selecting the largest part, validates geometry integrity, skips invalid or empty geometries with logging, and writes output as a new point shapefile. Optionally, the resulting point layer is added to the QGIS map canvas. The plugin is implemented as a QGIS Python plugin with a GUI dialog for layer selection, output path configuration, and options for processing selected features only or all features.

name: Calculate cadastral map cost
desc: The script calculates the estimated cost of ordering a Polish cadastral (basic) map for user-selected polygon areas. It clips a built-in administrative boundaries layer (powiat-level) to the selected input polygon, computes the clipped area in hectares, and applies a tiered pricing model based on area size and map scale (1:500, 1:1000, 1:2000, 1:5000), where larger areas receive discounted rates per hectare. Outputs include a table showing powiat names, clipped area (ha), and calculated costs per scale, rounded to nearest 0.10 zł.

name: Define soil texture from sand and clay
desc: The script defines soil texture classes using raster inputs of sand and clay percentages, applying a polygon-based classification rule file (with vertices in sand-clay coordinate space) to assign texture codes (e.g., 'sand', 'loam', 'clay') pixel-wise. It reads sand and clay rasters, processes them row-by-row using matplotlib.path.Path.contains_point() to determine which texture polygon each (sand, clay) point falls into, writes the classified result as a GeoTIFF with byte data type and -9999 NoData, loads the output raster into QGIS, optionally converts it to a thematic vector polygon layer with labeled texture classes using gdal.Polygonize(), and exports a CSV for ternary plot generation (CLAY,SAND,SILT).

name: Overlay selected feature
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin dialog for overlay analysis using user-selected vector features. It extracts selected features from the active layer, constructs a temporary memory vector layer with identical geometry and attributes, and optionally includes an approximation distance parameter entered by the user. The output is a dictionary containing 'operation': 'feature', 'input': {'layer': QgsVectorLayer}, and optionally 'aproximacao' (float), emitted via a signal to trigger downstream overlay processing.

name: Evaluate IDW and TIN interpolation accuracy
desc: The script evaluates the accuracy of multiple spatial interpolation methods (IDW with varying power and search radius parameters, TIN, nearest neighbor, natural neighbor, kriging, and Topo to Raster) against a high-resolution global bathymetry/elevation reference dataset (ETOPO 2022). For each interpolated raster, it computes: (1) absolute pixel-by-pixel difference from ETOPO; (2) Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI) for both ETOPO and interpolated rasters; and (3) TRI difference. It generates histograms and statistical summaries (min, max, mean, std dev) of both difference rasters, plus timing logs for performance benchmarking across QGIS, GDAL, SAGA, GRASS, and ArcGIS implementations.

name: Compute watershed delineation
desc: The script performs watershed delineation using a selected raster layer (e.g., DEM or flow direction) and a vector shapefile (e.g., pour point or basin boundary) as inputs. It validates input layers, checks coordinate system consistency between raster and vector layers, warns if CRS mismatch exists, ensures output path is valid and non-Korean, executes an external watershed processing tool via command-line arguments built by _util.GetWatershed(), converts the resulting GeoTIFF output to ASCII format, and adds the output raster to the QGIS project. The workflow includes pre- and post-processing steps such as .prj file backup/restore and CRS comparison display in a dialog.

name: Generate Flight Simulator flight plan
desc: The script generates a Flight Simulator 2020-compatible flight plan (.PLN file) from a user-provided point layer of waypoints. It extracts departure and destination points (first/last waypoint or custom ICAO airports), formats coordinates in DMS with elevation, retrieves airport metadata (ICAO ID, short name) from an embedded 'strips.gpkg' vector layer using spatial indexing, and writes a structured XML flight plan containing departure/destination airports and user waypoints with type-specific tags and formatting. Output is a single .PLN file.

name: Geotag and import photos
desc: The script imports geotagged digital photographs (JPEG/JPG) from a specified directory, extracts EXIF GPS metadata (latitude/longitude with hemisphere references), converts them to WGS84 point geometries, and writes them into a QGIS vector layer (shapefile). It supports recursive directory traversal, appending to existing layers, custom EXIF tag extraction, and handles field mapping for non-GPS EXIF tags. Outputs are point features with geometry and attribute fields including filepath, filename, and selected EXIF tags.

name: Blur point layer locations
desc: The script performs spatial blurring of a point vector layer using a user-defined radius, optionally constrained by an envelope polygon layer. It reads a QGIS vector layer, applies a geometric blur algorithm (likely generating buffered polygons or displaced points), exports the result to a Shapefile, and optionally adds it to the QGIS map canvas. Key parameters include blur radius (in meters), selection-only processing, centroid export, radius attribute export, and CRS validation. The UI is defined in 'blur.ui' and the core logic resides in Blur and LayerIndex classes.

name: Calculate incidence density
desc: The script calculates incidence or density metrics for administrative polygon layers using either point case data or case-count fields. It computes values as count/area (density) or count/population (incidence), applies optional ratio scaling, writes results to a new shapefile with added attribute fields, optionally generates statistical summaries (min, max, mean, median, variance, etc.), plots the distribution, and applies graduated symbology based on user-selected classification modes (e.g., quantile, Jenks). Outputs include a new vector layer, statistics table, and plot.

name: Manage urban entrance features
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin for managing urban entrance point features, including creating new point layers with attributes (E_ID, E_Category, E_SubCat, E_Level), loading existing entrance layers, applying thematic styling, auto-populating attributes upon feature creation, updating selected features' attributes, and assigning sequential IDs. It uses PyQt4 and QGIS Python API to interact with the map canvas, legend, vector layers, and dockwidgets, and supports both memory-based and file-based (ESRI Shapefile) layer creation.

name: Create frontage layer from building polygons
desc: The script creates a frontage (linear) layer from building (polygon) layers by converting polygon boundaries to lines and exploding them into individual segments. It adds standardized attributes (F_ID, F_Group, F_Type, F_Length), populates F_ID sequentially or from feature ID, computes geometry length for F_Length, applies thematic QML styling, and supports attribute transfer from building layers via spatial intersection. Outputs include a new vector layer (shapefile or memory layer) with frontage features and attributes, styled according to thematic rules (including NULL-aware styling), and integrated into the QGIS legend and editing workflow.

name: Create land use layer
desc: The script creates a new land use (LU) vector layer in QGIS, either as a memory layer or saved to disk as a Shapefile. It supports defining ground floor (GF), lower floor (LF), and upper floor (UF) attributes with categorical fields (Cat, SubCat, SSx, NLUD, TCPA, Descrip), plus numeric fields (LU_ID, Floors, Area). The layer is initialized with polygon geometry, CRS-matched to the canvas, and optionally populated from an existing building layer by copying geometries and linking via a selected ID column. It applies thematic styling (landuseThematic.qml), auto-generates LU_IDs, computes area on feature creation/update, and enables interactive editing of floor-specific attributes via dockwidget UI controls.

name: Generate vector tiles from QGIS project
desc: The script generates MBTiles vector tiles from a QGIS project file (.qgs or .qgz), processing only valid vector layers. It reads layer styling (color, line width, point size, fill opacity), renderer types (categorized/graduated), field metadata, and computes combined WGS84 bounding box. It supports optional layer filtering by ID, zoom level range, custom extent (WGS84 bbox), and merging into an existing MBTiles file. Outputs include the generated MBTiles file, layer styles JSON, source layer metadata, bounds, and merge status.

name: Identify features near point location
desc: The script performs a spatial point-identification query on a QGIS vector layer loaded from a .qgs project file. Given input longitude and latitude (WGS84), it transforms the point to the layer's CRS, constructs a tolerance-based search rectangle, retrieves candidate features intersecting or within distance of the point, and returns up to a specified limit of matching features with their IDs, geometry type, WKT geometry, and attribute values. Output includes success status, project path, layer name, input coordinates and tolerance, count, and feature list with properties.

name: Extract vector layer metadata
desc: The script loads a QGIS project file, initializes QGIS core libraries using the provided QGIS_PREFIX environment variable, reads the project, and iterates over all valid vector layers. For each layer, it extracts ID, name, geometry type (point/line/polygon), data source path, CRS authority ID, native extent, and WGS84-transformed extent. It handles coordinate transformations using QgsCoordinateTransform and outputs the structured metadata as JSON.

name: Extract QGIS project metadata
desc: The script loads a QGIS project file (.qgs or .qgz), initializes the QGIS application, and extracts structured metadata including project CRS, extent (in project CRS and WGS84), default view extent, map scales, layer list with names, IDs, CRS, extents (project and WGS84), provider type, cacheability, geometry type (for vectors), remote source details (for XYZ, WMS, WMTS), and map themes. It outputs a JSON object containing all extracted metadata, written to stdout.

name: Generate map tiles for QGIS project
desc: The script generates raster map tiles (PNG) from a QGIS project using QgsMapRendererParallelJob, supporting multiple tiling schemes (XYZ, WMTS, custom), CRS-aware extent calculation and reprojection, tile matrix presets, and abort/resume capability. It reads layer or theme definitions, computes tile bounding boxes in target CRS, renders each tile at specified zoom levels, saves them atomically with size validation, and updates an index.json file with metadata including extent, zoom ranges, CRS, and tile matrix set definitions.

name: Process WFS GetFeature requests
desc: The script is a persistent QGIS worker that processes geospatial rendering and OGC WFS/WMS service requests via stdin JSON. It supports tile rendering (WMTS/XYZ), WFS ListTypes, DescribeFeatureType, GetFeature (GML/JSON), Transaction (Insert/Update/Delete), FeatureInfo, and Legend generation. It loads QGIS projects, resolves vector layers by sanitized typename, handles CRS transformations, renders maps using QgsMapRendererCustomPainterJob for stability, and serializes outputs to files (PNG, JPEG, GML, JSON, XSD) with atomic writes. All operations are headless and optimized for server deployment.

name: Generate vector tiles from QGIS project
desc: The script converts vector layers from a QGIS project file (.qgz or .qgs) into MBTiles vector tiles. It reads the project, filters vector layers (optionally by ID), extracts geometry type, styling metadata (color, line width, point size, fill opacity, renderer type), field definitions, and computes combined WGS84 bounding box. It uses QGIS Processing's 'writevectortiles_mbtiles' algorithm (native or qgis provider) to generate MBTiles output with specified min/max zoom levels. Outputs include success status, algorithm used, layer count, styling metadata, source layer schema, and bounds in EPSG:4326.

name: Generate points along line
desc: The script generates point features at raster pixel centroids that lie along input line vector features. It uses a raster layer to define the pixel grid, converts line segment endpoints to pixel coordinates using GDAL geotransform, and applies a line-drawing algorithm (Bresenham-like) to identify all pixels intersected by each line segment. For each such pixel, it computes the corresponding map-coordinate centroid point, assigns attributes (id, line_id, point_id), and writes them to a new point vector layer. The algorithm handles both single-part and multi-part lines, and processes features incrementally with progress feedback.

name: Generate points from polygon centroids
desc: The script generates point features at raster pixel centroids that fall inside input polygon features. It reads a raster layer to obtain geotransform information, iterates over each polygon's bounding box to identify relevant raster pixels, converts pixel coordinates to map coordinates, tests whether each centroid lies within the polygon geometry using prepared geometry engines, and writes resulting points to an output vector layer with attributes 'id', 'poly_id', and 'point_id'. The algorithm is implemented as a QGIS Processing GeoAlgorithm named 'Generate points (pixel centroids) inside polygons'.

name: Calculate network service area
desc: The script computes service areas from a vector line network layer and a vector point start layer using QGIS network analysis algorithms. It builds a graph from the network, applies Dijkstra's algorithm to find reachable vertices within a specified travel cost (distance or time), and outputs boundary nodes (as multipoint features) and convex hull polygons representing the service area extent. The workflow includes direction-aware routing, optional speed-based costing, topology tolerance handling, and advanced parameters for field-based direction/speed configuration.

name: Calculate service area from point
desc: The script computes a network-based service area from a user-specified start point on a vector line layer representing a transport or utility network. It builds a graph using QgsVectorLayerDirector and QgsGraphBuilder, applies either shortest-distance or fastest-time routing strategy (via QgsNetworkDistanceStrategy or QgsNetworkSpeedStrategy), runs Dijkstra's algorithm to find reachable vertices within a given travel cost, and outputs both boundary nodes (as MultiPoint) and convex hull polygons (as Polygon) representing the service area. Inputs include network layer, start point coordinates, travel cost threshold, optional direction/speed fields, and topology tolerance.

name: Calculate shortest path layer to point
desc: The script computes the shortest or fastest path from multiple start points (vector point layer) to a single end point using a network vector layer (lines). It constructs a graph using QgsVectorLayerDirector and QgsGraphBuilder, applies either QgsNetworkDistanceStrategy or QgsNetworkSpeedStrategy depending on user selection, and uses Dijkstra's algorithm via QgsGraphAnalyzer.dijkstra to compute paths. Output is a line vector layer containing each computed path with attributes 'start', 'end', and 'cost' (distance or time). The script is a QGIS Processing algorithm named 'Shortest path (layer to point)' in the 'Network analysis' group.

name: Calculate shortest path from point to layer
desc: The script computes the shortest or fastest path from a user-defined start point to each point feature in an end-points vector layer using a network (line) layer as the transport graph. It constructs a QgsGraph using QgsVectorLayerDirector and QgsGraphBuilder, applies Dijkstra's algorithm via QgsGraphAnalyzer.dijkstra, and outputs a line vector layer where each feature represents one shortest path with attributes 'start', 'end', and 'cost'. The path type (shortest distance or fastest time) is configurable, and network directionality and speed-based costing are supported through optional fields and parameters.

name: Calculate shortest path between points
desc: The script computes the shortest or fastest path between two user-specified points on a vector line network layer using QGIS's graph-based network analysis. It constructs a directed graph from the input line layer, optionally incorporating directionality and speed fields, then applies Dijkstra's algorithm to find the optimal path. Outputs include a line vector layer representing the shortest path geometry and a numeric travel cost value.

name: Compute zonal statistics for raster values
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (min, max, sum, count, mean, std, unique, range, var, median, and optionally mode) of a raster band within polygon zones defined by a vector layer. It uses GDAL and NumPy to read raster data, rasterize vector geometries, mask raster values by zone geometry, and compute statistics on the masked arrays. The output is a vector layer (same geometry as input) with added attribute fields prefixed by user-defined string containing the computed statistics.

name: Generate voronoi polygons from random points
desc: The script generates a set of 1500 randomly distributed points within a predefined BC-Albers coordinate bounding box (EPSG:3005), computes a full distance matrix between all point pairs, and constructs Voronoi polygons from those points — producing vector geometry outputs (memory layers) for spatial pattern analysis, tessellation, or proximity modeling. No raster or time-series data is used; the workflow is purely vector-based geometric processing using QGIS native algorithms.

name: Calculate polygon indicators classify layout
desc: The script processes a vector layer of world polygons to compute geometric indicators (e.g., area, elongation, compactness), applies k-means clustering to classify polygons into 10 classes based on those indicators, and then generates three spatial layouts—naive, advanced bounding-box packing, and fast brick-like arrangement—each preserving all input attributes. Outputs include indicator.shp, classified.shp, naiveLayout.shp, boundingBox.shp, otherLayout.shp, boundingBox2.shp, and otherLayout2.shp, all written as ESRI Shapefiles.

name: Perform k-means clustering classification
desc: The script performs unsupervised k-means clustering on numeric attribute values from a QGIS vector layer, scales the input features, assigns each feature to a cluster, and exports a new memory vector layer with a classification attribute (integer class ID) plus optionally copied original attributes. It uses scikit-learn's KMeans with 'k-means++' initialization and 10 random initializations, and outputs a QgsVectorLayer object containing geometry and classification results.

name: Calculate polygon morphometric indices
desc: The script computes morphometric indices for polygonal features in a QGIS vector layer, including area, oriented minimum bounding rectangle (SMBR) metrics (area, angle, width, height), convexity (two variants), elongation, compactness, area-perimeter ratio, and complexity. It creates a new memory vector layer with these computed attributes plus optionally copied original attributes (excluding the specified ID field). The computation relies on QGIS geometry methods (e.g., geom.orientedMinimumBoundingBox(), geom.area(), geom.length()) and external functions from morpho.py.

name: Generate POP location map
desc: The script generates a multi-scale PDF map showing the spatial location of a PostGIS-stored 'POP' (Plan Operativo Plurianual) polygon layer within administrative boundaries (municipality, department, country) using QGIS Python API. It loads a QGIS project template, adds layers via PostgreSQL/PostGIS SQL queries (including geometry dumping, intersection, and extent buffering), applies named QML styles, configures labeling and symbology (e.g., red outline box around POP, transparent municipality fill, green department fill), sets up three inset maps (country, department, municipality scale) and one main map with scale rounding logic, and exports two PDFs—one with Bing Maps background and one with OSM background.

name: Fix and clean road geometries
desc: The script loads a local shapefile of roads (brgm.shp), applies geometry validation and correction using QGIS Processing's 'native:fixgeometries', then performs topological cleaning using GRASS 'v.clean' with tool=1 (snap) and threshold=0.0001 to resolve small geometric inconsistencies (e.g., dangles, overlaps, gaps); outputs are a cleaned road layer ('clean.shp') and a separate error layer ('errors.shp').

name: Compute obstacle-avoiding shortest path
desc: The script computes an obstacle-avoiding shortest path between two geographic points using a QGIS-based angle-turn and grid refinement method. It loads obstacle polygons (e.g., buildings), transforms them to EPSG:3395, constructs a multipolygon geometry, builds a grid-based representation, incrementally generates candidate path segments with angular deviation checks, validates line-of-sight against obstacles using QgsGeometry.distance(), prunes redundant vertices to shorten the path, constructs a QgsGraph for Dijkstra-style shortest-path search, and outputs visualized layers including raw path points, shortened path lines, shortest tree graph, and final minimum path features — all written to local Shapefile paths.

name: Plan obstacle-avoiding path
desc: The script implements a randomized roadmap grid method for pathfinding in a constrained 2D space using QGIS Python bindings. It constructs a grid over a defined hall area, populates it with random points (including start/target points and surrounding expansions), builds a visibility graph by connecting nearby points only if the connecting line does not intersect obstacle geometries (derived from a vector layer of buildings), then applies graph search (via GdalGraphSearcher) to find the shortest path between start and target points. Outputs include visualized random points, the visibility graph, the shortest-path tree, and the final optimized path geometry, all saved as vector layers. Input obstacles are transformed to EPSG:3395, coordinates are in projected meters, and runtime is bounded by a configurable time limit.

name: Compute randomized roadmap path
desc: The script computes a collision-free shortest path between two points (starting and target) within a constrained polygonal area (hall) using a randomized roadmap method. It generates random points inside the hall, adds points around start/target, builds a visibility graph by connecting nearby points only if the connecting line does not intersect obstacle polygons (transformed to EPSG:3395), performs Dijkstra-based shortest path search on the graph, and outputs multiple visualization layers: random points, graph edges, shortest tree, and optimized final path. Input obstacles are loaded from a local Shapefile ('Строения.shp'), and coordinate transformations use EPSG:3395.

name: Convert building polygons to multipolygon
desc: The script processes a vector layer of buildings ('Строения.shp') by reprojecting each polygon feature from its source CRS to EPSG:3395 (World Mercator), then constructs either a full multipolygon geometry containing all features or a filtered multipolygon containing only those polygons intersecting a hardcoded bounding box polygon. It uses QgsCoordinateTransform for reprojection, QgsGeometry.fromPolygonXY and addPartGeometry to assemble multipolygons, and relies on distance == 0.0 as a proxy for spatial intersection. Outputs are QgsGeometry objects representing multipolygons.

name: Generate road sampling points
desc: The script converts a road network vector layer into evenly spaced point features along each line segment using the Qchainage plugin in QGIS. It loads a road shapefile, applies the chainagetool.points_along_line function with a fixed distance of 20 units (no unit specified in code), outputs a new point layer named 'london_road_point', reprojects it to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), and saves it as an ESRI Shapefile. The input path is provided via command-line argument, and output path is also passed as a command-line argument.

name: Generate offset lines from polygon vertices
desc: The script processes selected polygon layers (specifically quadrilateral polygons with exactly 5 points, implying closed 4-vertex polygons) to generate three sets of offset line features: two front-line sets derived from the first two vertices and one rear-line set derived from the third and fourth vertices. It computes rotated and translated points using user-specified angles and distances, constructs line segments between original and computed points, and writes results to three new memory-based LineString vector layers named 'LINES_FRONT_SET1', 'LINES_FRONT_SET2', and 'LINES_REAR_SET'. The plugin only operates on a single selected polygon layer and enforces geometry type validation.

name: Package central database and layers for field use
taskType: Database packaging and mobile project deployment
desc: The script prepares a portable field-work package by (1) exporting selected PostgreSQL layers from a central database into a ZIP archive using PostgreSQL binaries (psql/pg_restore), including optional UID column addition and audit triggers; (2) converting non-PostgreSQL vector layers into a single GeoPackage file with styles preserved; and (3) generating a mobile-optimized QGIS project file that references the exported PostgreSQL ZIP and GeoPackage. Outputs include a status code, success message, lizsync.zip, layers.gpkg, and a modified .qgs project in a '_mobile' subdirectory.

name: Generate timezone boundary map
desc: The script converts a timezone boundary shapefile (e.g., 'combined-shapefile-with-oceans.shp') into a PNG image where each timezone is rendered in a unique color derived deterministically from its tzid (e.g., 'America/New_York') via SHA-1 hashing, and outputs a JSON mapping of hex colors to Qt-formatted timezone IDs (e.g., 'UTC+05:00'). It uses QGIS Python bindings to load the vector layer, apply categorized symbology with no stroke, render the map at a specified height (default 2000 px), and write outputs to disk.

name: Calculate population-weighted population density
desc: The script computes population-weighted population density (popop) by performing zonal statistics on administrative polygons (world_geolev1_2019.shp) using two LandScan raster layers: pop_robinson.tif (population) and pop2_robinson.tif (population squared). It calculates the mean of each raster within each polygon, then derives popop as the ratio of pop2_mean to pop_mean. The output is a CSV file (popop_geolev1.csv) containing polygon attributes plus the two zonal means, intended for post-processing to compute the final popop ratio.

name: Map harbor infrastructure and local constraints
desc: The script generates a QGIS layout map visualizing spatial constraints for harbor development near Dikili, Turkey. It creates and styles vector layers including candidate harbor point, 1 km and 2 km buffers, OSM-derived buildings, roads (filtered to 'trunk','tertiary','unclassified','service'), waterways, nearest mapped waterway, coastline, marine structures, and an existing harbor point. It applies symbology (fill, line, point), labels candidate and existing harbor points, sets a custom map extent, adds legend, scale bar, and title, then exports a high-resolution PNG and saves the QGIS project. Input data comes from local OSM GeoJSON files and processed GeoPackage buffers.

name: Screen harbor site candidates
desc: The script performs local harbor site screening near Dikili, Turkey, using OpenStreetMap (OSM) data queried via Overpass API for coastline, roads, waterways, buildings, and marine structures, combined with candidate point locations from a GeoJSON file. It styles and layers these vector features in QGIS, overlays EMODnet bathymetry WMS, generates two map layouts (with and without bathymetry), exports PNGs, saves a QGIS project, and writes a summary JSON with feature counts and export paths.

name: Generate centroids and buffers
desc: The script processes a vector layer to compute centroids and circular buffers (radius=2.0 units) for features intersecting a predefined polygon area (6.3 -14, 52 -14, 52 -40, 6.3 -40). It filters input features by spatial intersection with that bounding polygon, extracts the 'NAME' attribute, computes geometry centroids, buffers them with 100 segments, and writes both resulting point and polygon layers to GeoPackage files at fixed local paths ('C:\489\centroids.gpkg', 'C:\489\buffers.gpkg'). The CRS is preserved from the input layer.

name: Map police points and emergency routes
desc: The script creates and visualizes geospatial vector layers for police points (using custom PNG icons), emergency response lines, key area polygons, and concentric circular zones (e.g., for security perimeters) in QGIS. It transforms input WGS84 coordinates (EPSG:4326) to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), saves each layer as GeoJSON, applies symbology (raster markers for points, colored strokes/fills for lines/polygons), and composes them over custom XYZ tile basemaps (‘Base-Tile’ and ‘Main-Tile’) served from an internal GIS server. Outputs include a saved QGIS project (.qgz), GeoJSON files in D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/output/projects/, and rendered map layers with categorized styling for multi-level circles.

name: Generate警务部署图 layout
desc: The script generates a QGIS print layout for a 'Zhengzhou Phase II Police Deployment Map', adding vector layers (points, lines, polygons, and concentric circles) representing police locations, emergency routes, key areas, and security zones; styling them with custom icons and colors; saving GeoJSON outputs; loading XYZ tile basemaps; and exporting a QPT layout template and QGZ project file. All geometries are transformed from WGS84 (EPSG:4326) to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and the final map extent is auto-calculated from non-basemap vector layers.

name: Generate警务部署 map
desc: The script generates a QGIS-based警务部署 (police deployment) map for Zhengzhou, integrating point (e.g., police officers), line (e.g., emergency routes), polygon (e.g., key areas), and concentric circle (e.g., patrol zones) vector layers with custom icons and styling. It loads WMS tile layers (custom XYZ services hosted at 172.31.100.34), transforms input WGS84 coordinates (EPSG:4326) to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), saves all vector layers as GeoJSON files, applies categorized or single-symbol rendering (including raster marker icons for points), and exports a print layout (A4 landscape) with title, map item, and legend — ultimately saving the full QGIS project (.qgz) and layout template (.qpt).

name: Deploy police and emergency zones
desc: The script generates a QGIS layout for a Zhengzhou Phase II public security deployment map, adding point layers (police officers), line layers (emergency roads), polygon layers (key areas), and concentric circle layers (security perimeters) with custom icons, colors, and opacities. It transforms input WGS84 coordinates to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), saves each layer as GeoJSON, applies symbology (raster markers for points, single-color fills for polygons/lines, categorized fill symbols for concentric circles), and composes a print layout with title, legend, and remarks box on A4 paper. Outputs include GeoJSON files in D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/common/output/projects/, a QGIS project file (demo13.qgz), and a rendered print layout.

name: Deploy police and emergency zones
desc: The script generates a QGIS project with geospatial layers representing police deployment points, emergency roads, key area polygons, and concentric security circles (control, alert, core zones) around a central point. It saves the vector layers as GeoJSON files, applies custom symbology (including base64-encoded icons for points), sets up a print layout with title, legend, and remarks box using A4 paper size, and exports the final project as a .qgz file. The layout includes map extent derived from all non-tile layers and excludes 'BaseTile' and 'MainTile' from the legend.

name: Deploy police and emergency resources
desc: The script creates a QGIS-based警务 deployment map by adding vector layers for police points, emergency roads, key areas (polygons), and concentric security zones (circles) with distinct styling. It loads base and thematic tile layers (WMS), transforms coordinates from EPSG:4326 to EPSG:3857, saves each vector layer as GeoJSON, applies symbol rendering (raster markers for points, rule-based multi-width lines, categorized fill symbols for concentric circles), constructs a print layout with title, legend, remarks box, and vertical index label, and exports the final layout as a high-resolution PNG image. Outputs include GeoJSON files for each vector layer, a QGIS project (.qgz), and a rendered map image.

name: Deploy police and emergency response assets
desc: The script generates a QGIS-based operational map for public security deployment in Zhengzhou, visualizing police points, emergency roads, key areas (polygons), and concentric security zones (three-ring circles) using vector geometry creation, coordinate transformation (WGS84 to Web Mercator), GeoJSON export, rule-based and point-cluster rendering, and print layout generation with legend customization, title, remarks box, and vertical index label. Outputs include a saved QGIS project (.qgz), exported PNG image of the layout, and multiple GeoJSON files for each layer.

name: Generate警务部署图 layout
desc: The script generates a QGIS print layout for a 'Zhengzhou Phase II Police Deployment Map' by adding base tile layers (WMS), vector layers (points, lines, polygons, and concentric circles) with custom symbology and clustering, saving them as GeoJSON, and assembling a layout with title, legend, remarks box, and vertical label. It exports the final layout as a high-resolution PNG image and saves the QGIS project. Key operations include coordinate transformation (EPSG:4326 → EPSG:3857), rule-based and point-cluster rendering, font-based marker labeling, and layout item positioning using millimeter-based measurements.

name: Generate警务部署图 layout
desc: The script generates a QGIS print layout for a 'Zhengzhou Phase II Police Deployment Map', including vector layers for police points, emergency roads, key areas (polygons), and concentric security zones (circles), rendered with custom symbols and labels.
