It loads XYZ tile basemaps, saves the project as .qgz, exports the layout to PNG at 300 DPI, and writes GeoJSON files for each vector layer to D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/common/output/projects/. The layout includes title, legend, remarks box, and a vertical right-side label.

name: Map emergency response infrastructure
desc: The script creates a QGIS-based emergency response map layout with vector layers for police points, emergency roads, key areas (polygons), and concentric security zones (circles) around a central location. It applies custom symbology including raster icons for points, dashed line styles for roads, categorized fill colors for concentric circles, and clustered point rendering. The workflow includes coordinate transformation from WGS84 (EPSG:4326) to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), GeoJSON export of all vector layers, layout composition with title, scale bar, legend, remarks box, and index label, and final export to PNG, PDF, and SVG formats. All operations are executed headlessly using QgsApplication without GUI.

name: Generate thematic map layout
desc: The script generates a QGIS print layout containing vector layers (points, lines, polygons, circles) representing police locations, emergency roads, key areas, and concentric security zones, overlaid on WMS tile layers. It applies custom symbology (raster markers, clustered points, categorized polygons, dashed lines), adds layout elements (title, legend, scale bar, arrow, remarks box), and exports the final layout to PNG, PDF, and SVG formats. Input coordinates are in WGS84 (EPSG:4326), transformed to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), and output GeoJSON files are saved to 'D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/common/output/projects/'. The layout uses A4 paper size in landscape orientation with defined margins and styling.

name: Plot police point locations
desc: The script loads two XYZ tile layers (a base map and a health valley orthophoto) into QGIS, creates a new point vector layer in EPSG:3857, transforms two WGS84 coordinates (111.4775222, 40.7290133 and 111.4766598, 40.7282033) to Web Mercator, adds them as features with names 'mingjing-Point1' and 'mingjing-Point2', assigns a custom raster marker symbol ('民警.png'), saves the layer as a Shapefile at '/common/output/projects/Transformed_Points.shp', and saves the QGIS project to 'D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/output/projects/demo5.qgz'.

name: Plot police station points
desc: The script plots two predefined police station points (minjing-Point1 and minjing-Point2) in Hohhot (inferred from tile URL path '/gis/hhht/' and Chinese label '%E5%81%A5%E5%BA%B7%E8%B0%B7%E6%AD%A3%E5%B0%84' decoded as '健康谷正射') onto a QGIS project using custom XYZ tile layers, transforms the points from WGS84 (EPSG:4326) to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), saves them as a GeoJSON file, styles them with a custom PNG icon ('民警.png'), and exports the QGIS project (.qgz). The output includes a styled vector layer of two points, a GeoJSON file at '/common/output/projects/MinJing_Points.geojson', and a saved QGIS project at 'D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/output/projects/demo6.qgz'.

name: Plot police point locations
desc: The script loads two XYZ tile layers (base and main map tiles) from internal WMS endpoints, creates a memory-based point vector layer in EPSG:3857, transforms two WGS84 (EPSG:4326) coordinate points (111.4775222,40.7290133 and 111.4766598,40.7282033) into Web Mercator, adds them as labeled features ('minjing-Point1', 'minjing-Point2') with x/y attributes, saves the layer as a shapefile, applies a custom raster marker symbol ('民警.png') sized at 5 units, adds the styled layer to the QGIS project, and saves the project as 'demo7.qgz'.

name: Visualize emergency response infrastructure
desc: The script creates and visualizes geospatial vector layers (points, lines, polygons, and concentric circles) representing public security infrastructure in Hohhot, China. It adds point features (e.g., 'MinJing_Points') using custom PNG icons, line features (e.g., 'yingji' emergency routes), polygon features (e.g., 'zhongdian' key areas), and multi-level concentric circles ('cir_key_1') with distinct colors and opacities to indicate graded response zones. All layers are transformed from WGS84 (EPSG:4326) to Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), saved as GeoJSON files in 'D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/output/projects/', styled with QGIS symbol renderers, loaded into a QGIS project, and overlaid on custom XYZ tile basemaps (Base-Tile and Main-Tile). The final project is saved as 'demo8.qgz'.

name: Plot emergency response points
desc: The script creates and visualizes geospatial vector layers (points, lines, polygons) in QGIS using PyQGIS. It adds WMS tile layers as basemaps, then generates point features (e.g., 'MinJing_Points') from WGS84 coordinates transformed to EPSG:3857, styled with custom PNG icons; line features (e.g., 'yingji') styled with solid color (#e77148); and polygon features (e.g., 'zhongdian', 'cir1') styled with semi-transparent fill color (#e77148, #2f99f3). All layers are saved as GeoJSON files in 'D:/iProject/pypath/qgis-x/output/projects/', loaded back into QGIS, rendered, and added to the project. The final QGIS project is saved as 'demo8.qgz'.

name: Compute center points of short line segments
desc: The script processes a vector line layer to build a dictionary mapping endpoint coordinates to line feature IDs, then identifies short line segments (length < 10 units), computes their midpoint coordinates, and attempts to update adjacent line geometries by replacing endpoints with the computed center point. The workflow relies on QgsVectorLayer, QgsGeometry.asPolyline(), and QgsGeometry.fromMultiPolylineXY() for geometric manipulation, and includes logic to match shared endpoints across lines. Output includes modified line geometries stored in a dictionary (new_line) and attempted layer updates via changeGeometryValues().

name: Extract provinces by name expression
desc: The script extracts vector features from a provincial shapefile (nxprovincias.shp) using a SQL-like expression to filter features where the DPA_DESPRO attribute contains 'GUAYAS'. It uses QGIS's native 'extractbyexpression' algorithm to produce a new shapefile (nile.shp) containing only matching provinces. The output is the file path of the resulting shapefile, printed to console.

name: Detect polygon topology errors
desc: The script checks a user-provided Shapefile for geometric topology errors including self-intersection, polygon overlap, and invalid interior rings (holes). It loads the layer into QGIS, iterates over features to test GEOS validity, computes intersections between polygons to detect overlaps, and validates inner rings of polygons. Invalid geometries are collected into a new in-memory vector layer with attributes indicating error type (e.g., '自相交', '重叠', '空洞'), then saved as a temporary ESRI Shapefile at '/tmp/topology_errors.shp' and added to the QGIS project.

name: Merge TIFF images
desc: The script merges multiple GeoTIFF files from a specified input folder into a single output GeoTIFF. It optionally reprojects input rasters to EPSG:4326 using GDAL Warp, builds a VRT as an intermediate virtual mosaic, applies bilinear resampling during final warping, and supports configurable output data type (e.g., Float32). Outputs include the merged GeoTIFF and optionally a temporary VRT file.

name: Map LandScan population density
desc: The script generates a styled QGIS print layout visualizing LandScan population density raster data overlaid on administrative boundaries, hillshade, and capital city points. It classifies the LandScan raster using a discrete color ramp with 9 predefined density thresholds (1–maximum), applies symbology to vector layers (e.g., country outlines, ROI highlight, capitals), adds a title and subtitle listing selected countries, inserts a legend with custom labels and styling, sets map extent based on buffered administrative geometry for the input ROI, and exports the final layout as a PNG image ('landscan.png'). Input layers are loaded from files in a specified directory matching patterns like 'landscan', 'hillshade', 'adm', and 'places'.

name: Extract TELEMAC water level contours
desc: The script extracts contour polygons from TELEMAC hydrodynamic simulation results (.res files) for a specified variable (e.g., 'HAUTEUR D'EAU' — water depth) and user-defined level thresholds. It loads SELAFIN-formatted mesh data, applies optional X/Y translation, identifies the requested time iteration and parameter index, computes contour bands using matplotlib.tricontourf, separates outer/inner polygon rings based on vertex winding order, spatially indexes inner rings, and constructs multi-polygon features with min/max level attributes by subtracting inner rings from outer rings. Outputs a vector layer of multi-polygon contours in the specified CRS.

name: Sample hydrodynamic parameters at points
desc: The script performs point-based sampling of hydrodynamic simulation outputs (e.g., water depth, velocity) from TELEMAC or ANUGA mesh files. It reads a user-selected point vector layer, reprojects each point to the mesh coordinate reference system, uses a pre-built interpolator to extract time-slice parameter values (e.g., 'Water level', 'Velocity') at those locations, appends the sampled values as new double-precision fields to the output shapefile, and adds the resulting layer to the QGIS project. The output is a point shapefile named with the source layer name, mesh name, displayed time step, and '_sample.shp' suffix.

name: Generate contour shapefiles from Selafin hydrodynamic model output
desc: The script converts Selafin binary hydrodynamic simulation outputs (e.g., water elevation, velocity) into vector contour shapefiles at user-specified levels. It reads mesh geometry and variable values via the posttelemac_selafin_parser, uses matplotlib's tricontourf to compute isolines on triangular meshes, classifies outer/inner polygon rings using coordinate winding direction and spatial indexing, optionally inserts inner rings as holes into outer polygons (for topological correctness), applies CRS transformation if specified, and writes the result as a multi-polygon ESRI Shapefile with 'min' and 'max' level attributes. Output file naming incorporates the input Selafin filename, parameter name, and time step.

name: Interpolate weather station wind forecasts
desc: The script downloads the latest Canadian nowcasting weather matrix file (SCRIBE.NWCSTG) from Environment and Climate Change Canada, filters for Ontario weather stations (using on_stn_codes.csv), extracts current and 1–5 hour temperature and wind forecasts, joins with station lat/lon coordinates (latlon.csv), creates a point layer in GeoPackage format, applies inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation across 9 predefined Ontario subregions to generate 6-hour forecast rasters (0–5 hours ahead) for both temperature and wind, merges regional rasters into province-wide composites, samples these rasters onto a grid layer (ref_layers\grid_join.gpkg), and exports the final gridded forecast attributes as split GeoJSON files for web deployment. Outputs include 12 merged GeoPackage layers (t0–t5, w0–w5), 18 IDW raster TIFFs (9 regions × 2 variables), 6 merged temperature/wind GeoTIFFs, and tiled GeoJSONs keyed by 'grid_tilename'.

name: Apply affine transformation to building layer
desc: The script applies an affine transformation to a vector layer of Penn State buildings, scaling coordinates by factor 2 in x and y dimensions and rotating 30 degrees counter-clockwise around the z-axis, with no translation or z/m scaling. It loads the input shapefile, executes QGIS's native:affinetransform algorithm using processing.run, handles output filename conflicts by incrementing suffixes, saves the result as a new shapefile in a specified plugin workspace directory, and adds the transformed layer to the current QGIS project.

name: Apply affine transformation to building layer
desc: The script applies an affine transformation to a vector layer of Penn State buildings using GRASS GIS's v.transform tool within QGIS. It scales the x- and y-coordinates by a factor of 2.0, applies no shift or z-scaling, and rotates around the z-axis by 30 degrees. The transformed layer is saved with an auto-incremented filename in a specified output directory and loaded into the current QGIS project as a new vector layer named 'PennStateBuildingsTransformed'.

name: Generate virtual soil boring profile
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin that allows users to click on the map canvas to generate a virtual soil boring profile at the clicked location. It transforms the point coordinates to EPSG:25832, queries a remote API (geoareaid=1) with x/y coordinates, model ID, depth, and API key to retrieve subsurface stratigraphy data, stores the point in a memory vector layer named 'GAL - Virtual Boring', and displays results in a dockable UI. The model selection is dynamically updated based on available models for the clicked location using priority-based fallback logic.

name: Join fishnet polygons with GADM boundaries
desc: The script performs a spatial join between fishnet grid polygons (stored as GeoPackage files) and GADM administrative boundary polygons (level 0, simplified). It uses QGIS's 'qgis:joinattributesbylocation' algorithm with the 'contains' predicate (index 0 in PREDICATE list) to transfer GADM attributes to each fishnet polygon. The output is a set of GeoPackage files in the Fishnet_Arc/ directory, each containing the original fishnet geometry plus joined GADM attributes.

name: Calculate night-time light statistics
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, median, min, max) of night-time light (NTL) raster data over fishnet polygon layers using QGIS's native zonal statistics algorithm. Input rasters are harmonized DMSP-OLS and VIIRS NTL products (2000–2018), named 'Harmonized_DN_NTL_YYYY_calDMSP.tif' (2000–2013) or 'Harmonized_DN_NTL_YYYY_simVIIRS.tif' (2014–2018). Each fishnet .gpkg layer is processed against each year’s NTL raster, producing a new geopackage with prefixed statistics columns (e.g., 'DV2000_mean'). Output files are saved as 'FishnetName_YYYY.gpkg' in the 'Data/Fishnet_Arc_DMSP/' directory.

name: Compute zonal statistics for VIIRS nighttime lights
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, median, standard deviation, and maximum) of VIIRS nighttime light raster data (VIIRS_mustl_X_25.tif) over fishnet polygon layers (stored as GeoPackage files). It iterates through each fishnet layer in 'D:/Paper2/Data/Fishnet_Arc/', overlays it with eight VIIRS rasters (indexed 1–8), applies 'native:zonalstatisticsfb' to extract statistics prefixed with 'V_X_25_', and saves the results as new GeoPackage files in 'D:/Paper2/Data/Fishnet_Arc_VIIRS_25/'. The output includes attribute-extended vector layers containing VIIRS-derived light intensity metrics per fishnet cell.

name: Compute VIIRS nightlight statistics for fishnet polygons
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, median, standard deviation, and sum) of VIIRS nightlight raster data (VIIRS_mustl_X_Y.tif) over vector fishnet polygons stored in GeoPackage files. It iterates through each fishnet layer, applies QgsNativeAlgorithms' 'native:zonalstatisticsfb' with a fixed threshold value (50), and writes the results to new GeoPackage files named using the pattern '{fishnet_name}_{X}_{Y}.gpkg'. The output includes attribute-extended vector layers containing VIIRS-derived statistics prefixed with 'V_X_Y_'.

name: Compute zonal statistics for LandScan population raster
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean, sum, min, max) of LandScan annual population rasters (2000–2019) over vector fishnet grid layers stored as GeoPackage files. It uses QGIS's native 'zonalstatisticsfb' algorithm to aggregate raster values per polygon, prefixes output columns with 'L' followed by year (e.g., 'L2000'), and saves results as new GeoPackage files. Input fishnets are read from 'D:/Paper2/Data/Fishnet_Arc/', and LandScan rasters are loaded from 'D:/Paper2/Data/LandscanTS_tif/lspopYYYY.tif'.

name: Summarize population by administrative boundary
desc: The script loads an Ethiopia administrative shapefile (EAS.shp) and a WorldPop 2020 raster (eth_ppp_2020_UNadj_constrained.tif), filters features to 'Tahtay Adiyabo' admin3 units (and optionally by population sum outside 2000–3500), fixes geometries, computes zonal sum statistics of population values per polygon, then sorts and prints results by vertex count with formatted population sums and GAT IDs.

name: Compare administrative unit population estimates
desc: The script compares population estimates from a raster dataset (MetaFocus_v1.tif) against existing polygon-level population values (Met_Pop) in an Ethiopia administrative shapefile (eth_verification_gat_v2.shp). It loads and fixes the vector layer, optionally filters by administrative name ('Tahtay Adiyabo'), overlays it with the raster using zonal statistics (sum), computes geometric metrics (centroid, area in km², Polsby-Popper compactness index, bounding box height), and outputs a sorted tabular summary showing vertex count, bounding box height, original vs. raster-derived population, feature ID, area, and compactness — flagged with ↑/↓ indicators when outside user-defined thresholds (2000–3500). Summary counts report how many units fall below, within, or above the threshold range.

name: Load geospatial layers by user role and moldura filter
desc: The script authenticates a user via IDTMIL and password against a PostgreSQL database, retrieves their functional role (e.g., HID, TRA, INT, VEG, REC), identifies their active work unit (moldura) based on phase-specific assignment fields and timestamps, fetches the corresponding geometry (buffered union of aux_moldura_a features), sets the QGIS map canvas extent to that geometry, and loads filtered vector layers from two PostgreSQL databases (combater_2024_2 for moldura and classes) — including auxiliary layers (aux_obj_ponto_p, aux_obj_linha_l, aux_obj_area_a) and all schema 'base' feature layers intersecting the moldura geometry — organized into hierarchical layer groups by geometry type (Pontos, Linhas, Polígonos) and prefix. Outputs include loaded QGIS vector layers, grouped in the layer tree, and console status messages.

name: Merge correct damage polygons
desc: The script merges vector polygon layers (.fgb) corresponding to correctly classified aerial imagery (where 'Correct' == TRUE in the input CSV) into a single output .fgb file. It reads inference results from a CSV, normalizes boolean values in the 'Correct' column, maps image filenames (e.g., 'IMG_123.png') to matching .fgb files (e.g., 'IMG_123.fgb'), locates those files in a specified directory, loads them as QgsVectorLayer objects, and uses QGIS's native:mergevectorlayers algorithm to unify them while preserving CRS. The output is a merged GeoPackage (FlatGeobuf) file containing all validated damage polygons.

name: Merge damage polygons from correct classifications
desc: The script merges GeoPackage (.fgb) vector layers corresponding to aerial photo classification model predictions where 'Correct' == TRUE in an input CSV. It reads the CSV, converts image filenames (e.g., 'IMG_001.png') to matching .fgb filenames, locates those files in a specified directory, loads them as QGIS vector layers, and merges them into a single output .fgb file using QGIS's native:mergevectorlayers algorithm. The output is a unified vector layer containing only the ground-truth damage polygons associated with correctly classified images.

name: Model COVID-19 confirmed cases and deaths
desc: The script analyzes US state-level COVID-19 statistics by joining a US state boundary vector layer (s_11au16.shp) with a delimited text CSV layer (us_covid19.csv) on state names, then generates descriptive visualizations including bar charts of top/bottom states by confirmed cases, deaths, recovered cases, negative tests, and false positives; pie charts for hospitalized and ventilated patients; time-series bar/line plots for NY and MP states; and logistic, linear, and exponential curve fitting for NY death and confirmed case trajectories using scipy.optimize.curve_fit. Outputs include saved PNG figures (e.g., 'Top5_cases.png', 'NY_NJ.png', 'Ventilated.png', 'cases_NY.png') and printed summary statistics.

name: Forecast COVID-19 cases and deaths
desc: The script forecasts COVID-19 cases and deaths in Italian regions (Lombardia and Molise) using parametric curve fitting (logistic, linear, exponential models) on time-series data from a CSV layer joined to an administrative boundary shapefile. It loads vector layers (ITA_adm1.shp and covid_italy.csv), performs attribute-based spatial join, extracts region-specific time series (e.g., 'total_case', 'deaths', 'data'), fits logistic curves via scipy.optimize.curve_fit, and generates forecast plots with confidence intervals. Outputs include static PNG visualizations (e.g., Prevision_lombardia_numberofcases.png) and forecasted values for 30 days ahead.

name: Map COVID-19 cases by administrative level
desc: The script creates choropleth and labeled maps of COVID-19 case counts across three administrative levels in Australia (LGA, region, country) using spatial joins between vector boundary layers (AUS_adm0.shp, AUS_adm1.shp, AUS_adm2.shp) and CSV case data. It applies graduated symbol rendering with custom class breaks and colors, adds white-background labels for case numbers, and exports four PNG map images: aus.png (LGA-level labeled), aus_vermelho.png (LGA-level graduated), aus_regions.png (region-level labeled), and aus_regions_vermelho.png (region-level graduated), plus aus_country.png (country-level labeled). All maps use a cyan background (QColor(1, 255, 255)) and fixed 900×900 output size.

name: Export COVID-19 case layers
desc: The script exports 13 PostgreSQL-based vector layers (including concelhos, distritos, RAA regions, RAM islands, and epidemiological situation tables) from a QGIS project into a GeoPackage file named 'covid-pt-{date}.gpkg'. It then updates and exports three QGIS layout compositions ('distritos', 'concelho_continente', 'madeira') as PNG maps with dynamic date-stamped titles. The workflow uses PyQGIS headless mode, QgsProject loading, native:package algorithm, and QgsLayoutExporter.

name: Capture AOI boundary extent
desc: The script captures the user-defined Area of Interest (AOI) either from a selected vector layer or the current QGIS map canvas extent, validates whether it lies within Italy using the is_within_italy utility, and automatically generates a standardized boundary polygon layer (GeoPackage) in an appropriate CRS (3003 or 3004 if within Italy). The boundary layer is styled with a light brown semi-transparent fill and red dashed stroke, added to the QGIS project, and exposed via API for downstream OSM compatibility and processing. Outputs include the captured extent and CRS, a warning label if outside Italy, and a project-local boundary.gpkg file.

name: Identify species presence cells
desc: The script identifies grid cells containing at least one occurrence point for each target triatomine species (e.g., 'san', 'rub', 'rec') by spatial join (intersect, contain, overlap, within) between species presence points (CSV with DecimalLongitude/DecimalLatitude in EPSG:4326) and a fixed 0.05° vector grid (grid_005d_process4.shp). It then creates a binary 'count' attribute (1 = cell contains ≥1 point), exports per-species CSVs listing all grid cells with presence (including geometry and attributes), and repeats the process for buffered zones (0.5° radius) to generate 'b_05' presence buffers. The study area is implicitly defined by the spatial extent of the grid and presence points, but no explicit geographic boundary or coordinate range is given in the code. Outputs are CSV files per species in /cell/ and /buffer/ directories, each containing the full grid geometry plus presence/buffer indicators.

name: Identify electrical substations
desc: The script identifies electrical substations (transformers) by querying OpenStreetMap (OSM) data using the 'power=substation' tag within a user-defined polygon area of interest. It downloads OSM data via Overpass API, processes multipolygons and lines into valid polygons, extracts centroids for point representation where needed, clips to the study area, and performs spatial joins with a user-provided reference point layer (e.g., official transformer locations). It harmonizes naming (comparing OSM 'name' vs. reference 'nome'), flags whether names and geometries originate from OSM ('nome_osm', 'geometria_osm'), and outputs a cleaned, attribute-structured point layer ('Transformadores_P') with standardized fields including osm_id, nome, nome_no_osm, nome_osm, geometria_osm, and other metadata fields aligned with IBGE/BNGb schema.

name: Convert land break features to georeferenced TIFF
desc: The script converts vector features representing land surface change (break events) into georeferenced 3-band TIFF rasters. Each output TIFF encodes the mid-date of a break interval (as integer YYYYMMDD in bands 1 and 2) and a binary break mask (value 1 in band 3), rasterized over a D=3000 m square extent centered on the feature geometry, reprojected to EPSG:32629. Input is a GeoPackage vector layer with 'Data0' and 'Data1' date fields; outputs are named with break date and bounding box coordinates and saved to a local directory. The script supports both QGIS console (selected features) and standalone (filtered by FID) execution.

name: Generate break date raster mask
desc: The script computes the midpoint date between two date fields (Data0 and Data1) of a manually selected vector feature, formats it as YYYYMMDD (break_date), and creates a 3-band GeoTIFF raster centered on that feature’s geometry. Band 1 and Band 2 contain the break_date value only at the pixel(s) intersecting the feature (all other pixels = 0/NoData); Band 3 contains 1 at the feature location and 0 elsewhere. The raster has 10 m resolution, CRS EPSG:32629, and filename derived from break_date and integer-rounded extent coordinates (left, right, bottom, top). Output is added to QGIS as a raster layer.

name: Convert PNG labels to GeoTIFF
desc: The script converts PNG-formatted semantic segmentation labels into georeferenced GeoTIFFs using spatial metadata from corresponding prediction TIF files. It computes per-file classification accuracy against ground-truth PNG labels, stratifies predictions by accuracy and non-zero pixel count, selects 12 representative samples (4 per accuracy tier), converts only those selected PNGs to GeoTIFFs with uint8 dtype and LZW compression, and loads the before/after imagery, labels, and predictions as grouped raster layers in QGIS with appropriate paletted or multiband rendering.

name: Select intersecting TIF chips
desc: The script selects and copies TIF raster files that spatially intersect with selected features in a QGIS vector layer (e.g., 'ardida_2024'), transforms the selection geometry to match the CRS of the TIF chips for accurate intersection testing, loads the intersecting rasters into the QGIS project, and copies them to a configured destination folder for downstream processing (e.g., by split_tifs.py). It also cleans up non-target layers and ensures the reference layer is visually prioritized.

name: Visualize burned area by month
desc: The script loads an ICNF burned area shapefile (or other reference shapefile) into QGIS, applies categorized symbology by month using a date field (configured via DATA0), labels features by day of month, sets the project CRS to match the layer, and zooms the map canvas to the layer extent. Optionally, it merges and loads CCD vectorized results from GeoPackage files for visual comparison, applying distinct symbology and labeling. The output is a QGIS project with two layers (reference burned area and optional CCD vector results), each styled with month-based color categories and day-based labels.

name: Buffer vector features
desc: The script performs geoprocessing buffer operations on input vector layers (Shapefiles) in either batch mode (multiple .shp files within selected folders, recursively processed with output written to auto-generated '_output' subdirectories) or single-file mode (one .shp input → one buffered .shp output). It uses QGIS native 'qgis:buffer' (batch) or 'native:buffer' (single) algorithms with user-defined distance, no dissolve, default cap/join styles, and fixed segmentation. Outputs are new Shapefile (.shp) layers containing polygon buffers around input geometries, saved with '_output.shp' suffixes, alongside console/log feedback and error handling.

name: Export vector layer features
desc: The script provides a QGIS dialog for exporting selected vector layer features to multiple geospatial formats (GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON, KML, CSV, DXF). It allows users to choose source layer, export scope (all/selected/visible features), output format and file path, CRS transformation option, and post-export behavior (add to map, overwrite). The core operation uses QgsVectorFileWriter.writeAsVectorFormatV3 to perform the export, with progress feedback and error handling. Outputs include the exported file in the chosen format and optionally adds it as a new layer to the QGIS project.

name: Shred vector or raster layer into grid pieces
desc: The script shreds an input QGIS vector or raster layer into a user-specified number (2–10) of spatially disjoint pieces using a grid-based partitioning approach. It supports three modes: vertical strips (equal-width columns), horizontal strips (equal-height rows), or square tiles (grid with equal spacing in both dimensions). For vector inputs, it clips features per grid cell and saves each as a separate shapefile; for raster inputs, it uses GDAL’s mask-based clipping to extract sub-rasters. Optionally, it applies random spatial shuffling (translation) of the shredded pieces — either pure permutation of positions or collage-style jittered repositioning — before adding all outputs to the QGIS project. The original input layer is removed, and temporary grid layers are cleaned up.

name: Calculate area-weighted average perimeter
desc: The script computes the area-weighted average perimeter (AwaP) of building blocks (polygonal urban fabric features) intersecting or contained within a user-defined boundary. It first preprocesses input vector layers (fixing geometries, reprojecting, dissolving touching polygons, removing holes), optionally applies a morphological buffering 'dead-end removal' operation to smooth block outlines, then selects qualifying blocks based on spatial predicates (intersects, within, or percent-in-boundary threshold), computes each block’s perimeter and area, and finally calculates AwaP = Σ(Perimeter × Area) / Σ(Area). Output is a memory vector layer named 'AwaP_X' (where X is the computed value in meters), visualized in QGIS with a custom red color, and the scalar AwaP result is displayed in the plugin dialog label (e.g., '124.3 m').

name: Merge multiple shapefiles
desc: The script merges multiple shapefiles into a single output shapefile. It supports two input modes: directory-based (scanning for .shp files) or explicit file list. It handles geometry type filtering, field mapping to unify attribute schemas across inputs, CRS and geometry type inheritance from the first input layer, and progressive progress reporting via threading. Outputs include a unified vector layer with merged geometries and harmonized attributes, optionally added to the QGIS canvas.

name: Map ecological connectivity opportunities
desc: The script processes a set of preloaded QGIS vector and raster layers—representing habitat types (woodland, wetland, grassland), ecological networks, erosion risk, water regulation opportunities, restoration ease, and multi-benefit areas—against a grid-based zone file (grids.geojson). For each grid cell (identified by unique 'id'), it extracts: (1) vector-derived categorical attributes (e.g., 'Core', 'Catchment', 'Legend') from overlapping features, normalized via string cleaning (removing punctuation, lowercasing, underscore substitution); and (2) raster-derived normalized min/max statistics (0–1 range) from continuous rasters (e.g., water runoff moderation, ecological network resistance, precipitation erosion risk), using zonal statistics after masking nodata and polygonizing valid data areas. The final output is a GeoJSON (gridsout.geojson) where each grid feature’s properties include a nested 'legends' object aggregating per-map vector lists and ramp-normalized min/max values per grid ID.

name: Assess ecological network connectivity
desc: The script processes QGIS vector and raster layers to compute per-grid (5 km WGS84 grid) summaries of ecosystem service indicators. For vector layers, it extracts attribute values (e.g., 'Catchmnt', 'Core', 'Legend') or layer presence intersecting each grid cell, deduplicates and normalizes strings via regex-based formatting. For raster layers, it computes zonal min/max statistics over data-covered areas (after nodata masking and polygonization), then normalizes those values to [0,1] using user-provided or auto-derived global min/max, optionally applying custom stop-based interpolation or inversion. Outputs are embedded as nested 'legends' objects in a GeoJSON grid file, structured by thematic map group (e.g., 'moderate_surface_water_runoff', 'woodland_ecosystem'), with vector results as string lists and ramp results as {'min': x, 'max': y} per grid ID. The study uses pre-loaded QGIS layers — no GEE server-side computation occurs; this is a QGIS Python Processing script, not a Google Earth Engine script — and relies on local files ('wgs84_5k_grid.geojson') and a QGIS project with a layer group named 'English'. Data sources are internal to the QGIS project and not programmatically loaded from remote repositories or Earth Engine assets.

name: Clip imagery and DEM to AOI
desc: The script extracts and exports georeferenced imagery and DEM data clipped to a user-defined vector-based Area of Interest (AOI) in QGIS. It renders visible map layers at a specified CRS and resolution, applies a vector-derived mask to the rendered image, auto-crops the masked image to its opaque bounds, and clips a DEM layer to the corresponding geographic extent using GDAL warp with reprojection and optional resolution matching. Outputs include a cropped PNG texture image (TIFF_Textures/Tile__0__0.png) and a georeferenced GeoTIFF DEM file (e.g., output_name.tif), both aligned to the AOI’s geometry and coordinate system.

name: Generate terrain map from OSM and SRTM
desc: The script generates a terrain map by first querying OpenStreetMap (Overpass API) for administrative boundaries matching a user-provided name and admin_level, converting the result to GeoJSON, then downloading SRTMGL1 30m DEM data from OpenTopography using the boundary's extent, clipping the DEM with the boundary vector layer, and applying a single-band pseudo-color renderer (blue-to-red gradient) to visualize elevation. Outputs include a clipped GeoTIFF DEM file and a rendered raster layer added to QGIS.

name: Resolve dangle errors in line networks
desc: The script resolves dangle errors in selected line vector layers in QGIS by detecting unconnected endpoints (dangles), snapping them to nearby line features within a user-defined buffer distance, splitting intersecting lines at snap points, and generating a memory point layer marking resolved error locations. It supports both EPSG:4326 and projected CRS, performs geometry validation (line/polygon only), handles multipart geometries, and reports progress via a GUI progress bar.

name: Detect road network junction errors
desc: The script detects geometric inconsistencies at road network junctions by analyzing azimuth angles between connected line segments in selected features of a QGIS vector layer. It computes azimuths of terminal and adjacent vertices, buffers endpoints, identifies intersecting features within the buffer, calculates angular differences between approaching and departing segments, and flags junctions where the angle falls outside expected thresholds (75°–105° or >165°). Outputs include a memory-based line layer ('MANEUVERS_LINE') with corrected maneuver lines connecting nearest points on adjacent segments, and optionally an error point layer. The processing operates on user-selected vector layers loaded in QGIS, using QgsVectorLayer, QgsGeometry, and QgsFeatureRequest APIs.

name: Extract glacier outline from NetCDF mask
desc: The script loads a user-selected NetCDF file and a specified variable (e.g., a binary glacier mask), polygonizes it to create vector polygons, filters for glacier pixels (DN = 1), converts those polygons to lines, isolates closed-loop line features (i.e., glacier perimeter contours), sorts them by length, selects the second longest closed loop (intended as the primary glacier outline, excluding outer domain or artifact loops), saves it as a new line layer, extracts its vertices as point features, and exports the vertex coordinates (X,Y) to a CSV file. Outputs include: (1) raster layer of the NetCDF variable, (2) polygonized vector layer, (3) line layer of glacier boundaries, (4) memory layer containing only the second longest closed loop, (5) point layer of its vertices, and (6) CSV file listing all vertex coordinates.

name: Merge shapefile layers
desc: The script merges multiple input shapefiles into a single output shapefile. It supports two input modes: directory-based (scanning for .shp files in a selected folder) or file-list-based (user-selected individual shapefiles). It optionally filters input shapes by geometry type (e.g., point, line, polygon), handles encoding, deletes existing output files before writing, and writes features using QgsVectorFileWriter. Progress is tracked per shapefile and per feature. The output is a unified vector layer saved to the user-specified path, optionally added to the QGIS canvas.

name: Upload GIS layers to cloud platform
desc: The script uploads vector and raster layers from QGIS to GIS Cloud via its REST API. It accepts multiple vector (e.g., .shp, .kml, .geojson) and raster (e.g., .tif, .jpg, .png) files, optionally creates a new map with user-defined extent and name, zips associated files (e.g., .shx/.dbf for shapefiles), posts them to GIS Cloud's file manager, and registers them in the map using layer metadata (geometry type, source path). Outputs include uploaded files in GIS Cloud's file manager and optionally a newly created map containing those layers.

name: Reproject GPS shapefile to WGS84
desc: The script reprojects a user-specified local CRS (EPSG:25830) shapefile to WGS84 (EPSG:4326), writes the reprojected layer as a new Shapefile, then converts it to GPX format using ogr2ogr. It also removes any pre-existing GPX file with the same base name and executes an external batch script (cargagps.bat) on the generated GPX file. The workflow is triggered via PyQt4 QInputDialog for filename input and uses QGIS Python API (PyQGIS) for vector layer handling and reprojection.

name: Convert GPX to Shapefile layers
desc: The script prompts the user for a GPX file name, executes a batch script to download GPS data to a predefined path, then loads the GPX file and exports its 'waypoint', 'track', and 'route' layers as separate ESRI Shapefiles reprojected to EPSG:25830. It adds each resulting Shapefile layer to the QGIS interface with names derived from the input filename and layer type.

name: Perform unsupervised spectral classification
desc: The script performs unsupervised classification of APEX (Airborne Prism Experiment) hyperspectral imagery using Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) with optional Truncated SVD dimensionality reduction. It supports two modes: full-scene classification or restricted subset classification via getSubset(). Outputs include classified raster maps (GeoTIFF), uncertainty indicators (distance-to-class), spectral plots of class means and covariances, statistical summaries per class (e.g., mean, std, min, max), and multi-page PDF reports containing visualizations and classification results. The plugin integrates with QGIS as a toolbar tool and uses spectral, sklearn, matplotlib, GDAL, and PyQt4 libraries.

name: Assess road inundation from flood polygons
desc: The script assesses road exposure to flood inundation by intersecting road vector layers with flood polygon layers. It filters flood polygons based on a hazard classification field (e.g., 'flooded' values), unions valid inundated geometries, clips roads to the analysis extent, splits roads by inundated areas, and marks road segments as inundated (1) or not (0). It computes total and inundated lengths per road type, generates an HTML impact report, and returns a styled vector layer of flooded roads with categorized symbology for mapping. The output includes impact summary metadata, map title ('Roads inundated'), legend title ('Road inundated status'), and a ZeroImpactException if no roads are flooded.

name: Identify flooded roads
desc: The script identifies road segments inundated by floodwater using a raster-based flood hazard layer and a vector road exposure layer. It converts flood raster cells exceeding user-defined depth thresholds into polygon features, spatially indexes them, then intersects them with road geometries to classify each road segment as flooded (1) or not flooded (0). Outputs include a new line layer with flooded status attribute, impact summary report, categorized symbology for mapping, and road length statistics by road class.

name: Flood inundation building impact assessment
desc: The script performs flood vector impact analysis on buildings using QGIS-based InaSAFE. It identifies which buildings intersect with flooded polygons in the hazard layer based on a user-defined 'wet' classification in the hazard's attribute field (e.g., 'flooded', 'high'), marks each building as inundated (1) or not (0), aggregates results by building type, generates an HTML impact report, and outputs a styled QgsVectorLayer (converted to InaSAFE Vector) with categorized symbology for inundation status. Key operations include spatial indexing, bounding-box pre-filtering, exact geometry intersection, attribute mapping via value_map, and consolidation of small/unknown building types into 'other'.

name: Inspect NGII map delivery data
desc: The script performs quality inspection of delivered geospatial map data for the National Geographic Information Institute (NGII) of South Korea. It compares original 'nfsd' layer data against newly received 'extjob' data using PostgreSQL-based spatial SQL queries to detect additions, deletions, geometry changes, and attribute changes. It visualizes differences in QGIS with categorized symbology, enables manual review/acceptance/rejection per feature, and generates a Word-based inspection report with screenshots and tabulated results. Outputs include updated inspection records in 'extjob.inspect_main' and 'extjob.inspect_objlist', QGIS vector layers showing change types, and a .docx report containing metadata, change statistics, and rejected feature details.

name: Map nightlife popularity grid
desc: The script generates a point-based grid layer representing Zomato Nightlife Index values across a user-defined area of interest. It uses the Zomato API v2.1 geocode endpoint to fetch 'nightlife_index' for each grid point (lat/lon), constructs a memory vector layer with EPSG:4326 CRS, assigns the index as a double attribute, and optionally exports it as an ESRI Shapefile. The grid resolution is set by user input (point interval), and bounding coordinates are extracted from a Google Maps web interface embedded in a Qt dialog.

name: Classify hazard zones affecting population
desc: The script computes population exposure to classified polygon hazard zones (e.g., 'wet', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'dry') by intersecting hazard and population polygon layers, calculating affected area ratios, and estimating affected population counts per zone using uniform spatial distribution. It outputs a categorized vector impact layer with population counts per hazard class, an HTML impact summary report, and style definitions mapping hazard classes to colors and numeric impact levels.

name: Flood polygon road inundation
desc: The script computes road inundation impact from flood polygon hazard layers using QGIS vector operations. It filters hazard polygons by a user-defined 'wet' classification (e.g., 'flooded', 'inundated') via the 'field' and 'value_map' keywords, unions matching geometries, clips road exposure features to the analysis extent, splits roads by the unioned flood geometry, and marks intersecting road segments as inundated (1) or not (0). Outputs include a classified vector layer of roads with inundation status, length-based statistics per road type, an HTML impact report, and categorized symbology for mapping.

name: Identify flooded roads
desc: The script identifies which road segments are flooded based on raster flood depth values exceeding user-defined thresholds (min/max threshold parameters). It converts the flood raster into vectorized rectangular cells, spatially indexes them, and performs geometric intersection/difference operations between road line features and flood polygons to classify road segments as flooded (1) or not flooded (0). The output is a new line layer with an added binary target field indicating inundation status, along with impact statistics by road class, HTML report, and categorized symbology for mapping.

name: Flood building inundation impact
desc: The script computes flood impact on buildings by spatially intersecting a flood polygon hazard layer with a building exposure layer (points or polygons) in QGIS. It uses the hazard's 'field' keyword to identify inundated areas via a value mapping (e.g., 'wet' class), projects geometries between CRSs, builds a spatial index for efficient intersection, and classifies each building as inundated (1) or not (0). Outputs include a new vector layer of buildings with inundation status, an HTML impact report summarizing affected building types, and styled symbology for map visualization. The process validates field existence, handles CRS transformations, consolidates rare building types, and raises exceptions for zero impact or missing fields.

name: Assess tsunami flood impact on roads
desc: The script assesses tsunami inundation impact on road networks by raster-to-vector conversion of hazard depth values, spatial intersection between road segments and flood polygons, and classification of road segments into five hazard zones (Dry, Low, Medium, High, Very High) based on user-defined depth thresholds. It outputs a reclassified line layer where each road segment (or part thereof) is attributed with an affected class, along with length-based statistics per road type and hazard zone, styled for visualization with categorized symbology.

name: Find highest and lowest points
desc: The script identifies the highest and lowest elevation points within each polygon feature of a vector layer using a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) raster. It reprojects polygon geometries to match the DEM's coordinate system, rasterizes each polygon to create a mask, extracts masked elevation values via NumPy arrays, computes argmax/argmin indices, converts those indices to map coordinates, and writes resulting points (with attributes, type 'max' or 'min', and height) to an output shapefile. The plugin is implemented as a QGIS tool with GUI controls for selecting input raster and polygon layers and specifying output path.

name: Load MongoDB geojson layers
desc: The script creates QGIS memory vector layers from GeoJSON documents stored in a MongoDB database. It connects to MongoDB using configurable host, port, authentication, and database parameters; lists databases and collections via PyMongo; optionally filters features by spatial intersection with the current QGIS map canvas extent using $geoIntersects; infers field types (String, Int, Double, Date) from sample document properties; handles geometry conversion from GeoJSON to WKT via OGR; and populates a QgsVectorLayer with attributes and geometries. Outputs include a dynamically generated memory layer added to QGIS's layer registry.

name: Smooth and schematize grid-based data
desc: The script performs spatial smoothing and schematization of tabular or vector point/polygon data onto a regular grid using R-based algorithms (btb_LissageGrille and btb_Schematisation_de_carreaux). It accepts input layers with attributes to smooth, optionally uses user-provided grid geometry or generates one, computes centroids for point assignment, exports data to CSV for R processing, applies bandwidth- and cell-size-controlled kernel smoothing, and outputs a smoothed shapefile with joined attributes. The workflow includes CRS selection, quantile configuration, temporary file handling, and layer joining via ID field.

name: Create quadrats along line
desc: The script creates rectangular quadrats of user-specified length and width along selected line geometries in a vector layer. It interpolates points along the line, constructs temporary line segments of quadrat length, buffers them to form polygons, splits each polygon along the base line into two halves, and optionally generates centroid points for each quadrat. Outputs include a memory polygon layer named 'Quadrats' and/or a memory point layer named 'Centroids', both inheriting the CRS of the input line layer.

name: Download FAOSTAT agricultural data
desc: The script downloads FAOSTAT statistical data (e.g., crop production, yield, area) by group, domain, element, and item; joins the time-series values (1961–2014) to a template vector layer (e.g., country boundaries) by FAOSTAT code; adds yearly numeric attributes; and renders the latest year (2014, or fallback to earlier non-null year) using graduated symbology. Outputs include a GeoPackage/shapefile with appended annual attributes and an optionally added QGIS vector layer styled by value.

name: QGIS workflow: Data processing, Vector spatial analysis
desc: This workflow contains 7 core geospatial operations, including Data processing, Vector spatial analysis, Data editing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Calculate catchment area from points
desc: The script calculates the upslope (contributing) catchment area for each point feature in an input vector layer using a digital elevation model (DEM). It iterates over each point, uses SAGA's 'upslopearea' algorithm to generate a raster catchment mask where cells draining to the point are assigned value 100, then polygonizes that raster and exports only the DN=100 polygons as individual ESRI Shapefiles (one per point) into a user-specified output folder. The workflow relies entirely on local QGIS processing algorithms ('saga:upslopearea' and 'gdal:polygonize') and does not use Earth Engine APIs or remote sensing imagery processing.

name: Calculate point-based catchment areas
desc: The script calculates upslope catchment areas for input point features using a digital elevation model (DEM). It iterates over unique values in a specified field (or feature IDs if no field is provided), runs SAGA's 'upslopearea' algorithm for each point to generate a raster catchment, polygonizes the raster, selects only pixels with DN=100 (indicating flow accumulation area), and exports the resulting polygons either as individual ESRI Shapefiles or as layers within a single GeoPackage. Outputs include a directory of vector files and a list of output layer URIs.

name: Calculate stage-volume curve from DTM
desc: The script computes a stage-volume relationship from a digital terrain model (DTM) by iterating elevation levels from the minimum to the maximum in 10 increments. It uses QGIS's raster surface volume tool to calculate the volume below each level, converts volumes from cubic meters to cubic kilometers, and merges the results into a single vector layer containing elevation level and absolute volume for each stage.

name: Compute stage-volume curve
desc: The script computes the stage-volume relationship from a DEM by calculating surface volume at multiple water levels derived from the elevation range, producing a merged table with level and absolute volume in cubic kilometers.

name: Buffer polygon centroids
desc: The script computes the centroid of each input polygon feature and generates a circular buffer around each centroid with a user-specified distance. The output is a vector polygon layer containing the buffered geometries, one per input polygon. No raster operations, spectral analysis, or temporal aggregation is performed; the workflow consists solely of two QGIS native vector processing algorithms: 'native:centroids' followed by 'native:buffer' with round end caps and 5 segments.

name: Split samples into train test
desc: The script splits a vector layer of labeled samples into two disjoint subsets: a training subset (containing a user-specified percentage, default 70%, of randomly selected features) and a test subset (containing the remaining features), using QGIS native algorithms 'randomextract' and 'difference'. The outputs are two vector feature sinks—'TrainSubset' and 'TestSubset'—each preserving the original geometry and attributes of the input 'Samples' layer.

name: Extract forest stand data by perimeter
desc: The script extracts forest stand vector and raster datasets from the TBk (Bestandeskarte) inventory dataset using a user-defined extraction perimeter (a GeoPackage polygon layer). It first filters the main stand layer (TBk_Bestandeskarte.shp) by spatial intersection with the perimeter, then creates two buffered/dissolved versions of the extracted stands: a tightly buffered (0.0001°) version for vector-layer clipping (using 'are within' predicate), and a coarsely buffered (10 m) version for raster clipping (using GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer). All listed vector datasets (e.g., TBk_local_densities.gpkg, stands_simplified.shp) and raster datasets (e.g., dg_layer.tif, VHM_10m.tif, classified_smooth_2.tif) are clipped to their respective buffered perimeters. Outputs include the filtered stand layer and all clipped vector/raster layers written to the specified output directory.

name: Extract forest stand perimeters and associated raster/vector layers
desc: The script extracts forest stand polygons (TBk_Bestandeskarte), local density vector features, and a 10m canopy height model (VHM) raster clipped to a buffered and dissolved extraction perimeter. It first builds spatial indexes on input vector layers, then extracts TBk_Bestandeskarte features intersecting the user-provided 'Extraction Perimeter', buffers and dissolves those stands twice — once with a user-defined buffer (default 10 m) for raster clipping and once with a tiny buffer (0.0001) for vector containment filtering — then clips the 'vhm_10m' raster using the larger buffered polygon and extracts 'local_densities' features that are fully within the tiny-buffered polygon. Outputs are three geospatial products: a clipped VHM raster ('vhm_10m_extracted'), an extracted TBk stand vector layer ('TBk_Bestandeskarte_extracted'), and an extracted local densities vector layer ('local_densities_extracted').

name: Delineate forest stand classes
desc: The script generates a forest stand delineation (BK) raster-to-vector workflow using a Vegetation Height Model (VHM) at 1m resolution. It applies a multi-step classification: (1) reclassifies VHM into six height-based forest development stages (Ju, SH1–SH2, BH1–BH2) using user-defined upper limits (e.g., LIMIT_JU=7 m); (2) performs two focal statistics passes — first over SH1-inclusive cells (window size=5, 40% majority threshold), then over all cells (window size=25, majority); (3) converts the final smoothed raster to polygons; (4) simplifies geometry (simplify_threshold=2); (5) merges polygons smaller than min_area_bk=2000 m² with neighbors; and (6) clips and dissolves outputs by a user-provided perimeter shapefile (dissolved on field 'Eigentue_1' by default), optionally split and cleaned using forest roads. Outputs include a final merged and attribute-filtered shapefile ('bk_final.shp'), intermediate rasters and vectors in timestamped subfolders, and a processing log.

name: Reclassify and focal process VHM rasters
desc: The script processes Vegetation Height Model (VHM) rasters by (1) clipping them to individual polygon features (identified by 'id' attribute in perimeter_dissolve), (2) reclassifying pixel values using a lookup table (e.g., mapping original classes to new integer codes), (3) applying focal statistics (majority or SH1-weighted classification) over a user-defined window radius, and (4) converting the final reclassified/focal rasters to vector polygons. Outputs include clipped TIFFs, reclassified TIFFs, focal-processed TIFFs, and polygonized shapefiles — all named per feature ID (e.g., 'vhm_1.tif', 'vhm_recl_1.tif', 'vhm_focal_1.tif', 'vhm_poly_1.shp').

name: Calculate coniferous proportion per stand
desc: The script calculates the mean coniferous proportion for each forest stand by applying zonal statistics (mean) from a coniferous raster to a vector stands layer, adding an NH field. If calc_main_layer is True, it processes a canopy cover raster: resamples to 1m, aggregates sum per 10m grid cells, thresholds at 40% cover to create a mask, multiplies with the coniferous raster, and computes zonal statistics to generate NH_OS and NH_OS_PIX fields, removing temporary fields and intermediate rasters.

name: Clip stands and eliminate gaps
desc: This script clips forest stand polygons to an exact perimeter boundary and removes small gaps by merging them with neighboring stands using QGIS processing tools. It first clips the merged stand layer and a tree highest point layer to the perimeter. It then identifies gaps via difference and union operations, merges selected polygons with eliminate, and deletes remaining unprocessed gaps. Optionally, it clips a VHM raster to the perimeter using gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer. Outputs include the clipped stands shapefile and the clipped raster.

name: Merge similar forest stands
desc: The script merges small forest stand polygons with geometrically adjacent and spectrally/structurally similar (based on relative height dominant difference and type) larger stands. It computes adjacency via spatial intersection/touching, filters candidates by area threshold (min_area_m2), relative hdom difference (min_hdom_diff_rel), and neighbour type ('classified'), resolves one-to-one merge eligibility, dissolves selected small stands into their dominant neighbours, preserves original attributes of the largest stand in each merge group, and outputs a merged GeoPackage layer (stands_merged.gpkg) with a 'merged' flag (1=merged, 0=not merged) and cleaned attribute schema (dropping 'layer', 'path', 'fid_input').

name: Simplify forest stand boundaries
desc: The script post-processes raw forest stand boundary polygons (from a TBk classification) by eliminating small polygons (based on area_m2 < min_area), simplifying geometry using GRASS v.generalize with Douglas-Peucker method (tolerance = simplification_tolerance), re-eliminating newly small polygons after simplification, recalculating area_m2 for all features, and updating hmax and hdom attribute values for 'remainder' type polygons using hmax_eff and hp80 fields. Outputs include a cleaned and simplified GeoPackage ('stands_simplified.gpkg'), a temporary highest-tree point layer derived from 'hmax.tif', and intermediate buffers and reduced layers. All operations are vector-based and rely on QGIS processing algorithms.

name: Generate forest stand delineation
desc: The script processes a canopy height model (VHM 10m) and an optional coniferous raster to delineate forest stands using a classification algorithm with user-defined tolerances and minimum stand sizes. It then applies post-processing steps: simplifying geometries, eliminating small stands, merging similar neighbours based on height similarity, clipping to a perimeter, and gap elimination. Subsequently, it calculates dominant height (DG) from a higher-resolution VHM (150cm), adds coniferous proportion if a mixture raster is provided, computes additional attributes, appends vegetation zone and forest site categories via spatial joins, and finally cleans up the output layer to produce a final forest stand map (TBk_Bestandeskarte.gpkg) and a QGIS project.

name: Detect forest stand upper layer change
desc: The script computes two raster outputs: (1) 'change_DG' — a byte raster encoding four states of upper-layer presence/absence change between old and new TBk versions using the formula '(A*10 + B) + 1', where A is old DG (0 or 10) and B is new DG (0 or 1); resulting values are 1 (no upper layer in both), 2 (gain), 11 (loss), 12 (maintain); (2) 'change_DG_hdom' — a byte raster extending change detection to identify cleared areas in stands with hdom_old ≥ thresh_hdom (default 25 m) where hdom reduction exceeds thresh_hdiff (default 7 m), encoded as value 100; all other pixels retain original change_DG codes or are zeroed if hdom_old < threshold. Inputs are vector stand boundaries (with 'hdom' attribute) and co-registered DG rasters for old and new TBk versions.

name: Clean forest stand geometry
desc: The script cleans a forest stand map (TBk Bestandeskarte) by removing features with area < 100 m² and null area values, fixing invalid geometries, dropping the original 'ID' field, and replacing it with a new auto-incremented 'ID' field. All operations are performed using QGIS native processing algorithms within a PyQGIS processing model; no Earth Engine (GEE) code is present—the script is purely a QGIS Processing Algorithm.

name: Extract TBk project data by perimeter
desc: This QGIS script extracts all polygons from a TBk (Toolkit Bestandeskarte) forest stand map that intersect a user-defined perimeter polygon. It also selectively extracts associated raster and vector layers (degree of cover rasters, vegetation height models, coniferous rasters, intermediate processing layers, local densities, and additional user-specified materials). The algorithm uses 'extract by location' for vector layers and 'clip raster by mask layer' (or extent) for rasters. Outputs preserve the original folder structure and file naming.

name: Compute hdom deviation from VHM
desc: The script computes the difference raster 'diff_hdom_vhm' by subtracting a rasterized stand-level hdom (height dominant) attribute — derived from the vector layer 'tbk_bestandesgrenzen' (forest stand boundaries) — from the input VHM_10m (vegetation height model at 10 m resolution). It also generates a point layer 'vhm_10m_points' by converting each pixel of the VHM_10m raster to a point with its value. The workflow uses GDAL rasterize (with hdom field, 10 m resolution, Float32), GDAL raster calculator (B − A, where B is VHM_10m and A is rasterized hdom), and QGIS native pixel-to-points conversion.

name: Classify local forest density zones
desc: The script computes local density zones within forest stand polygons using a canopy cover (Deckungsgrad, DG) raster layer. It applies focal statistics with user-defined circular moving windows (radii per class) to the DG raster, reclassifies resulting focal means into discrete density classes (e.g., '1' for 85–100% cover with 7 m radius), polygonizes each class, removes small holes (<400 m²), optionally applies buffer smoothing (minus/plus buffering), filters out polygons <1200 m², intersects resulting density polygons with stands >1200 m², and computes zonal statistics (mean DG, optional NH/coniferous %, and DG sublayers KS/US/MS/OS/UEB) for each intersected geometry. Outputs are three GeoPackage files: clipped local density polygons (TBk_local_densities.gpkg), unclipped versions (optional), and the original stand map augmented with per-class metrics (area, area_pct, mean DG, mean NH, etc.).

name: Merge forest stand maps with unique IDs
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm merges multiple TBk forest stand map vector layers into one. It first sorts the layers spatially (northernmost first, then westernmost) using bounding box coordinates. It renames the original 'ID' field to 'ID_pre_merge', then adds two new fields: 'ID_meta' containing a unique prefix (alphabetical A, B, C... or numerical 1, 2, 3...) for each layer, and 'ID' combining the prefix and the original ID to ensure uniqueness. Finally, it merges the layers using the native merge tool and removes the extra 'layer' and 'path' columns. The output is a single merged vector layer with unique stand identifiers.

name: Prepare VHM and MG input rasters
desc: The script prepares Vegetation Height Model (VHM) and Mixing Degree (MG) rasters for forest stand mapping. It accepts a detailed VHM raster, an MG raster, and a polygon mask. It can optionally convert VHM to byte, reclassify values, clip to mask, and rescale MG values. The VHM is resampled to 10m and 1.5m resolutions. If specified, it generates a binary MG layer reclassified based on deciduous/coniferous thresholds. Outputs include VHM detail, VHM_10m, VHM_150cm, MG_10m, and optionally MG_10m_binary.

name: Prepare vegetation height model rasters
desc: The script prepares vegetation height model (VHM) raster inputs for a forest stand mapping toolkit. It takes a detailed VHM raster (TIFF) and a polygon mask shapefile, optionally converts the raster to byte data type, clips it to the mask extent, reclassifies values outside user-specified min/max range to NoData, and then aggregates the processed raster to 10 m and 1.5 m resolutions using maximum resampling. The outputs are three GeoTIFF files: vhm_detail.tif (clipped and reclassified), vhm_10m.tif (10 m aggregation), and vhm_150cm.tif (1.5 m aggregation). The algorithm is part of the TBk QGIS plugin and includes options for deleting temporary files and for rasterizing the mask before clipping.

name: Prepare VHM and mixture degree rasters
desc: The script processes high-resolution Vegetation Height Model (VHM) and optionally Forest Mixture Degree (coniferous proportion) raster data into standardized inputs for forest stand mapping. It includes steps like converting VHM to byte data type, clipping to a polygon mask, reclassifying outlier values to NoData, aggregating to 150cm and 10m resolutions with pixel alignment options, rescaling mixture degree values, and creating a binary coniferous/non-coniferous layer. Outputs are raster files used as input for subsequent forest stand map generation.

name: Optimize spatial join for forest stand mapping
desc: The script performs an optimized spatial join between two vector layers: a primary 'layer to join attribute on' and a secondary 'attribute layer' (expected to be polygonal, e.g., vegetation zones). It ensures performance by first checking and creating a spatial index on the primary layer if missing; converting the secondary layer to singlepart geometries; fixing geometries using the 'Structure' method; indexing the resulting singlepart layer; and finally executing a one-to-one spatial join ('largest overlap only') with intersection predicate. Outputs a vector layer identical in geometry to the primary layer but enriched with selected attributes from the secondary layer, prefixed as specified (e.g., 'VegZone_'). The workflow is explicitly designed for the TBk (Toolkit Bestandeskarte) QGIS plugin used in forest stand map generation.

name: Create LiDAR base data rasters
desc: The script processes airborne LiDAR point clouds to generate rasters for ground point density, low vegetation density, a digital elevation model via TIN gridding, and an IDW interpolation. First, if not classified, it classifies the point cloud. It then optionally converts LAZ to LAS. Using WhiteboxTools LidarPointDensity, it computes ground point density (excluding non-ground classes) and low vegetation density (excluding other classes). It also runs LidarTINGridding and LidarIdwInterpolation for DEM and IDW. Each raster is resampled to the specified cell size and warped to the target CRS. Finally, these rasters are loaded into the QGIS project if their respective checkboxes are enabled.

name: Calculate DFM confidence map
desc: This QGIS algorithm calculates a DFM (Digital Feature Model) confidence map based on the CRAN decision tree, incorporating ground point density, low vegetation density, and slope. It resamples input rasters to a user-specified cell size, classifies ground point and vegetation densities into confidence categories, reclassifies slope, and combines them using weighted raster calculations to produce a confidence raster. The output is a confidence map that can be used for quality assessment of the DFM and to determine optimal resolution.

name: Hybrid DFM interpolation from IDW and TLI
desc: The script performs hybrid interpolation of a digital feature model (DFM) by blending inverse distance weighting (IDW) and triangulation with linear interpolation (TLI) raster inputs based on a DFM confidence map. It resamples all inputs to a common cell size, reclassifies the confidence map into low and high confidence zones, grows the high-confidence areas, and uses a raster calculator to combine TLI and IDW rasters with the weighted zones. The resulting hybrid DFM is patched with the TLI where only one method exists, reprojected, and optionally loaded into QGIS. This yields a seamless hybrid DFM that prioritizes TLI in high-confidence areas and IDW in low-confidence areas.

name: Generate archaeological terrain visualizations
desc: The script is a QGIS processing algorithm that generates archaeological terrain visualizations from a user-provided DFM/DEM. It optionally computes Sky-View Factor (SVF), Visualization for Archaeological Topography (VAT via RVT Blender), Openness, Difference from Mean Elevation (DME using WhiteboxTools), and Hillshade. Each output is loaded as a project layer with a name prefix. The algorithm orchestrates multiple child processing steps and provides user-configurable options.

name: Burn drainage lines into DEM
desc: The script burns vector-based drainage networks into a digital elevation model (DEM) by rasterizing the drainage layers, converting both DEM and drainage to PCRaster format, preparing a boolean drainage mask using cover, and applying a custom 'burndem' algorithm that creates a smooth drop over a user-defined buffer distance and an additional sharp drop directly at the drainage line. The output is a modified DEM raster where elevation values are lowered along and near drainage features to enforce hydrological connectivity.

name: Delineate stream catchment
desc: The script delineates a stream network and its corresponding catchment boundary from a user-specified outlet point and study extent. It downloads a DEM from OpenTopography (e.g., SRTM or Copernicus), reprojects it, converts it to PCRaster format, computes flow direction using lddcreate, derives Strahler-order streams, snaps the outlet to the nearest stream within a tolerance, calculates the catchment raster via catchment(), and outputs vectorized streams (as line features) and a polygonized catchment boundary (as a single-polygon feature). Intermediate rasters (DEM, flow direction, river, outlet buffer, snapped outlet, catchment) are written to a user-specified folder in PCRaster .map format.

name: Snap and fix utility network geometries
desc: The script corrects vector geometries by snapping infrastructure layers (aerial boxes, D-cables, F-cables, drop cables, D-ducts) to reference layers (poles, termination boxes, risers, DPs, COs, HPs) and fixes geometries where necessary. It uses QGIS native snapping (with tolerances) and geometry fixing algorithms in a multi-step process to improve topological connections in a utility network.

name: Snap telecom infrastructure geometries
desc: The script corrects and snaps geometries of telecom network layers (aerial boxes, ducts, drop cables, D‑cables, F‑cables) to corresponding point features (poles, termination boxes, risers, distribution points, central office, household points). It uses QGIS native fix geometries and snap geometries algorithms with a 0.005 tolerance. The workflow first snaps aerial boxes to poles, then snaps ducts to the corrected aerial boxes, and sequentially snaps each cable type to a chain of points after fixing invalid geometries. The outputs are five snapped vector layers: snapped aerial boxes, snapped D‑ducts, snapped D‑cables, snapped F‑cables, and snapped drop cables.

name: Snap utility network geometries
desc: The script snaps endpoints of cable and duct line features (D-Cables, D-Ducts, F-Cables, DropCables) to reference point layers (Aerial Boxes, Paal, Termination Box, Riser, DP, HPs) within a tolerance of 0.005 degrees. It first fixes geometry errors for cables, then uses QGIS snapgeometries with move-end-points-only behavior. Outputs include five snapped feature layers for aerial boxes, d-ducts, d-cables, f-cables, and drop cables.

name: Compute confined valley index
desc: The script calculates the Confined Valley Index (CVI) along a river by generating perpendicular transects at a fixed step, intersecting them with left/right river banks and valley bottom polygon to measure distances. It computes the ratio (valley bottom width)/(river bank width) from minimum distances, producing a point layer with attributes: SEZ-ID, VB_RB-index, RB-W, VB-W, minimum distances to each bank, and transect distance.

name: Calculate river bank distances
desc: The script calculates distances from a river centerline to its left and right banks along the river course. It first generates points at a user-specified step distance along the centerline, creates a simplified centerline from those points, generates perpendicular transects of a given width, and assigns a sequential SEZ-ID to each transect. It then intersects the transects with the left and right riverbank line layers, calculates the coordinates of intersection points, computes the minimum and maximum distances from the centerline to each bank for each transect, and finally joins these attributes back to the transect layer. The outputs include point layers of left and right bank intersections and a transect layer containing fields for the minimum and maximum distances to both banks, enabling river morphology analysis.

name: Compare riverbank distances between two epochs
desc: The script performs a two-epoch comparison of distances between a river centerline and left/right riverbanks. It creates evenly spaced nodes along the centerline, generates perpendicular transects, intersects them with riverbank lines from two different times, computes per-transect min/max distances for each side and epoch, and outputs a transect layer with delta attributes showing bank migration.

name: Generate riverbank safety bands
desc: The script generates safety bands (offset lines) from riverbank vectors using erosion rates. It applies single-sided buffers on left and right banks using a multiplicative factor of the erosion rate field, unions the buffers, dissolves them, deletes holes, and converts the resulting polygons to lines. The output is a multiline vector layer representing safety bands at a calculated distance from the riverbanks.

name: Segment riverbanks and join centerline attributes
desc: The script segments left and right riverbanks using river reach transect limits, calculates the maximum length of transects, and then performs a spatial join by nearest neighbor to transfer attributes from the river centerline reaches to the resulting riverbank segments. The outputs are two vector layers: LRB (left riverbank segments) and RRB (right riverbank segments).

name: Analyze shop catchment demand
desc: The script computes isochrones (travel-time polygons) around candidate retail shops using the ORS Tools plugin, joins census-based demand points (population per LSOA) to those isochrones, aggregates total population demand per shop-time combination (e.g., 'shopID_5' for 5-minute access), and exports a CSV summarizing total demand per shop and travel time threshold. Inputs are local shapefiles: '_demand_points_census.shp' (census LSOA centroids with 'pop2011_al') and 'candidate_shops.shp' (with 'shopID'); output is 'shops_isochrones_demand.csv' containing columns '_shopID', '_AA_MINS', and 'total'.

name: Compute agricultural suitability by county
desc: The script computes mean agricultural suitability values for each U.S. county (administrative level 2) using a raster suitability dataset and outputs the results as a CSV file containing county attributes plus the zonal mean suitability value (stored in a field prefixed with '_' per 'COLUMN_PREFIX': '_'). The workflow includes reprojecting the suitability raster to WGS84, simplifying the county vector layer by dropping non-essential fields, adding a unique integer ID ('cid') to each county feature, running zonal statistics (mean) to extract raster values per county polygon, and exporting all attribute fields—including the computed mean suitability—to a CSV at 'C:/Users/se.4537/Dropbox/PoliteconGIS/LBS_2020/PhD/lecture_2/gis_data/_output/counties_agrisuit.csv'.

name: Compute mean agricultural suitability per US county
desc: The script reprojects an agricultural suitability raster to EPSG:4326, preprocesses US county boundaries (drops fields, adds unique ID), and computes zonal mean suitability for each county. Outputs: reprojected suitability raster and county vector with mean suitability attribute.

name: Calculate country areas
desc: The script computes the area in square kilometers for each country polygon from the Natural Earth 10m admin 0 countries dataset. It retains only the 'ADMIN' and 'ISO_A3' attributes, reprojects to the World Cylindrical Equal Area projection (ESRI:54034), fixes geometries, calculates the area using $geometry area divided by 1,000,000, and exports the result as a CSV file.

name: Calculate country area
desc: The script calculates country land areas in square kilometers from the Natural Earth 10m administrative boundaries shapefile. It drops attribute fields, reprojects to world equal-area projection (ESRI:54034), fixes geometries, computes area field 'km2area' using $area/1e6, and reprojects back to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326). The output is a vector layer with the area attribute.

name: Clean language boundary geometries
desc: The script cleans and standardizes a vector layer of language boundaries (langa.shp) by fixing invalid geometries, adding a unique autoincremental GID field, copying the 'NAME_PROP' attribute into a shorter 'lnm' field, and dropping all other attributes except 'GID', 'ID', and 'lnm'. The final output is a simplified shapefile 'wlds_cleaned.shp' containing only those three fields and topologically valid geometries.

name: Compute country-level population statistics
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean values) for raster datasets—land quality, and population density for years 1500 AD, 1990 AD, and 2000 AD—using country boundaries (ne_10m_admin_0_countries.shp) as zones. It fixes geometries, drops all attribute fields except 'ADMIN' and 'ISO_A3', appends zonal statistics prefixed by 'lqua_', 'pd15_', 'pd19_', and 'pd20_' to the vector layer, then exports the resulting attribute table—including original country fields plus computed statistics—to a CSV file at 'C:/Users/se.4537/Dropbox/PoliteconGIS/LBS_2020/PhD/lecture_3/gis_data/_output/country_level_zs.csv'.

name: Count languages per country
