name: Identify dangle overlap status
desc: The script identifies dangles (unconnected line endpoints) in a user-provided vector line layer using the 'Continuous_Network_Analysis:Identify Dangles' algorithm. It then buffers selected project layers (points, lines, and polygons) by 0.000001 decimal degrees, merges the buffered geometries, and performs spatial intersection and non-intersection operations to classify dangles into two outputs: (1) 'DANGLES_Overlapping' — dangles that intersect/overlap with any of the selected layers, and (2) 'DANGLES_Non_Overlap' — dangles that do not intersect/overlap with any selected layer. The output layers preserve original dangle attributes and add a 'layer_overlap' field indicating which overlapping layer contributed to the match.

name: Extract river headwater points and lines
desc: The script identifies and extracts river headwaters (springs) from a vector stream network layer using topological dangle detection and length-based filtering. It first dissolves the input line layer, detects dangles (endpoints with degree 1) as candidate headwaters, splits the dissolved network at duplicate vertices (to isolate individual segments), extracts segments intersecting the dangle points, computes segment lengths ($length), filters segments by user-defined length criteria (Minimum Value: ≤ VALUE; Maximum Value: ≥ VALUE; ALL: no filter), removes segments overlapping a buffer around the provided 'River Mouth' point layer (to exclude mouth artifacts), and outputs two results: (1) Headwater_Lines — filtered line segments retaining only a 'Compri' (length) attribute, and (2) Headwater_Points — point features derived from the intersection of original dangles and filtered headwater lines, preserving original layer attributes plus length.

name: Detect pseudo-node topological connectivity
desc: The script detects pseudo-nodes (line endpoints that are not properly connected to other line vertices) in an input line layer, then determines whether each pseudo-node spatially coincides (topologically connects) with vertices from user-selected vector layers (points, lines, or polygons). It outputs two point layers: (1) 'Pseudo-node Non_Overlap' — pseudo-nodes with no spatial coincidence to any vertex of the selected layers; and (2) 'Pseudo-node Overlapping' — pseudo-nodes that do coincide, enriched with a 'Layer_Name' attribute identifying which source layer contributed the coincident vertex. Vertex extraction is performed per geometry type: points are copied directly; polygon vertices are extracted from outer rings; line vertices are extracted from polylines (including multipart handling). Spatial matching uses QGIS native 'extractbylocation' (predicate=2 → 'contains') and 'intersection' algorithms.

name: Count polygon overlaps per point
desc: The script counts and concatenates ISO codes from intersecting polygons for each point feature, then computes statistics (count) grouped by the concatenated ISO values. It loads two vector layers (polygons and points), adds a 'poly_boundary' string field to the points layer populated with comma-separated 'iso' attribute values from all polygons that intersect each point, commits the edits, runs 'Statistics by Categories' to count occurrences per unique 'poly_boundary' group, and finally drops all statistical fields except the count, saving the result to 'output.gpkg'. The script prints field names of the polygon layer and the computed 'poly_boundary' values for verification.

name: Smooth Voronoi polygons by jittering vertices
desc: The script generates smoothed Voronoi tessellations from input point features, constrained to a base polygon layer (e.g., country or administrative boundary). It first computes standard Voronoi polygons, clips them to the base map, densifies polygon boundaries with additional vertices, randomly perturbs each vertex within a user-defined tolerance, reconstructs closed polygon paths from the jittered vertices, buffers the resulting lines to fill gaps, clips again to the base map, and finally joins original point attributes back to the smoothed polygons. The output is a vector layer of smoothed, topologically valid Voronoi-derived polygons retaining original point identifiers and attributes.

name: Generate dialect coverage polygon
desc: The script generates a dissolved polygon layer representing the combined geographic extent of specified countries, using QGIS Python API (PyQGIS). It loads a countries shapefile, filters features by country name using a subset expression, selects those features, creates a temporary memory layer containing them, merges the selected features, and then dissolves them into a single polygon. The final dissolved layer is added to the QGIS project map canvas.

name: Minority language spatial scoring
desc: The script processes minority language points and language area polygons to compute a scoring model. It overlays minority language points with type A and type B language polygons to extract intersecting language codes. It calculates the maximum distance to the minimal bounding circle of each type A language polygon (D) and the minimum distance to the polygon boundary (b), then computes D-b and a function fx(a) = 21.6679 * ln(101 - 100*(D-b)/D). It also extracts up to three type B language codes from overlaps and retrieves their confidence scores from an external table. The output is a vector layer with added fields including overlap lists, distances, scores, and concatenated confidence values.

name: Generate polygon-based sampling points
desc: The script generates a vector point layer of sampling locations within user-provided polygon geometries, supporting two methods: (1) random point placement inside buffered polygons, or (2) regular grid-based point placement with optional minimum inter-point distance enforcement and subsequent clipping to the buffered polygon extent. Buffering applies a negative distance (in meters) to shrink polygons and avoid edge effects. Output includes X/Y coordinate fields added to the resulting point layer.

name: Sample raster pixel values
desc: The script performs spatial sampling of a user-provided raster layer by generating point features at pixel centers and selecting a user-defined number of points either randomly (unstratified) or stratified by reclassifying the raster into quantiles, equal intervals, or K-means classes. For stratified sampling, it first applies a custom classification algorithm ('Precision Agriculture:R - Classification'), converts the classified raster to points, filters out 'nan' values, then performs random selection within each class subset. The final output is a vector layer of sampling points with added X/Y coordinate fields.

name: Sample vector points by attribute
desc: The script performs point sampling on a user-provided vector layer (points) using either random or stratified sampling. For stratified sampling, it classifies the input layer’s numeric field into classes using either quantiles or equal intervals (via a custom QGIS algorithm 'Precision Agriculture:V - Classification'), then performs random selection within each class. The output is a new vector point layer containing the sampled points, with added X and Y coordinate fields.

name: Create convex hull envelope
desc: The script computes the convex hull polygon enclosing all input point features. It first dissolves the input point layer (though dissolution has no effect on points without grouping fields), then applies QGIS's native convex hull algorithm to generate a single polygon output representing the minimal convex envelope around the point set. The output is a vector layer (polygon geometry) written to the specified destination.

name: Orient grid to row direction
desc: The script generates an oriented vector grid aligned with the dominant direction of points in an input point layer, where point order reflects data acquisition sequence (e.g., along crop rows or machine pass). It computes the median heading angle from consecutive point pairs, rotates a buffered extent-based grid around the centroid by the negative of that angle, and outputs the rotated grid as a vector layer. The grid cell size is user-defined in meters, and manual rotation override is supported.

name: Interpolate soil attribute values
desc: The script performs spatial interpolation of a user-specified numeric field (e.g., soil nutrient concentration, pH, or moisture) from point vector data to generate a continuous raster surface. It supports four methods: Thiessen (nearest-neighbor tessellation), Voronoi (geometric partitioning), Delaunay triangulation (with attribute joining), and Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) via GRASS v.surf.idw. For tessellation methods, it first creates polygons (Thiessen/Voronoi/Delaunay), clips them to the convex hull of input points, then rasterizes the resulting vector layer using the specified field and pixel resolution. For IDW, it directly invokes GRASS IDW interpolation. Outputs are a single GeoTIFF raster at user-defined grid resolution (meters).

name: Merge two agricultural zonings
desc: The script merges two polygon vector layers representing agricultural zonings (e.g., management zones, soil zones, or yield zones) using geometric union and topology cleanup. It first repairs geometries of both input layers, performs a vector union operation to compute their spatial intersection and overlay, converts multipart features to singleparts, adds geometry attributes (area, perimeter), and appends a unique auto-incremented ZONE_ID field. The output is a single vector layer where each polygon represents a non-overlapping atomic zone resulting from the logical combination of the two input zonings.

name: Generate tessellation polygons from points
desc: The script generates spatial tessellations (Thiessen/Voronoi polygons or Delaunay triangulations) from an input point vector layer. For Thiessen/Voronoi methods, it computes the tessellation, derives a convex hull from the input points, and clips the tessellation to that hull. For Delaunay, it performs triangulation and joins attributes from the original points via spatial location. The output is a raster destination layer (though the algorithm logic actually produces vector geometries — indicating a mismatch between parameter type and actual processing, as QgsProcessingParameterRasterDestination is used but all underlying algorithms produce vector layers).

name: Classify raster into within-field zones
desc: The script performs classification-based zoning of a user-provided raster (e.g., yield, NDVI, or soil property map) within a field boundary polygon. It first buffers the input contour, clips the raster to that buffer, classifies the clipped raster into N classes using Quantiles, Equal-intervals, or K-means, applies modal filtering via GRASS r.neighbors, vectorizes the result, repairs geometries, intersects with the original contour, removes small polygons using GRASS v.clean with a user-defined minimum area threshold, computes zonal statistics (mean and standard deviation) of the original raster per zone, and smooths zone boundaries using GRASS v.generalize with Douglas, Douglas Reduction, or Snakes method. The final output is a vector layer of smoothed, attribute-enriched within-field zones.

name: Identify flow pathways from DEM
desc: The script identifies flow pathways using a filled DEM and flow accumulation raster via GRASS r.stream.extract, applies a user-defined area threshold (converted from hectares to pixel count), generates flow direction and Strahler order rasters using GRASS r.stream.order, converts the Strahler raster to vector, filters short stream segments (≥3 m), joins Strahler order values to the original stream vector, adds a 'StreamType' field initialized to 5, renames 'cat' → 'Strahler', and removes auxiliary fields ('label', 'stream_typ', 'type_code', 'network'). Outputs include a line vector layer with 'Strahler' and 'StreamType' fields, a streams raster, and a flow direction raster.

name: Fill DEM and generate hillshade
desc: The script fills sinks in a digital elevation model (DEM) using the SAGA 'fillsinksxxlwangliu' algorithm with a minimum slope of 0.0, then computes flow accumulation using GRASS 'r.watershed' with a threshold of 500000 and stream extraction enabled, and finally generates a hillshade raster from the filled DEM using QGIS native hillshade with fixed azimuth=315°, vertical angle=45°, and user-defined Z factor. Outputs are three rasters: filled DEM, flow accumulation, and hillshade.

name: Simulate detainment bund locations
desc: The script identifies potential locations for detainment bunds (DBs), also known as WASCOBs, by processing flow accumulation rasters and stream networks to derive ephemeral/intermittent flow paths within agricultural fields. It generates two outputs: (1) a line vector layer ('PotentialDB') representing candidate DB placements perpendicular to flow direction, filtered by contributing area (2–50 ha), elevation constraints, bank height sufficiency (left/right range > DB height), incision criteria, and exclusion near perennial streams and field boundaries; and (2) a point vector layer ('All DB simulated points') containing all initially spaced candidate points along flow lines, enriched with attributes including contributing area, elevation, azimuth, and DB height — after upstream elevation drop filtering and sorting.

name: Estimate detainment bund catchment storage
desc: The script estimates the storage pond volume (in m³), contributing area (in m²), and storage-to-catchment ratio for potential detainment bund (DB) locations using topographic analysis. It first derives watershed boundaries from flow direction and DB pour points via GRASS r.stream.basins; then computes fill depth (difference between filled and original DEM) over each watershed; rasterizes DB IDs and heights; burns DB heights into a modified DEM; fills sinks with SAGA's Wang-Liu algorithm; calculates volumetric storage by multiplying fill depth (adjusted by Z factor) by pixel area; aggregates storage volume and area per DB catchment via zonal statistics; joins attributes to output polygons; smooths geometries; removes auxiliary fields (_sum, value, cat, fid); and sorts final catchments by storage:contributing-area ratio in descending order. Outputs are a vector layer of catchment polygons with attributes DB_ID, Contr_area, Height (m), Volume(m3), Area (m2), Ratio, and an optional raster of catchment depth (fill depth).

name: Simulate detainment bunds placement
desc: The script identifies potential locations for detainment bunds (DBs) — also known as WASCOBs — by processing flow pathways derived from a flow accumulation raster and field boundaries. It filters ephemeral/intermittent stream segments (2–50 ha contributing area), places candidate DB points at regular spacing (e.g., 60 m) along those streams, assigns multiple heights (e.g., 2,3,4 m) and lengths (e.g., 20,30 m), evaluates elevation drop sufficiency upstream, computes left/right bank height ranges via buffered perpendicular transects, filters out overly incised sites if enabled, and removes spatially redundant DBs within 10 m while ensuring DBs lie outside perennial streams (>25 m) and inside agricultural field boundaries. Outputs are: (1) a line vector layer of final potential DBs (perpendicular transects), and (2) an optional point vector layer of all simulated DB candidates before filtering.

name: Install r.stream.order and r.stream.basins
desc: The script installs the GRASS add-ons 'r.stream.order' and 'r.stream.basins' within QGIS by first checking if they exist using g.extension.list, then installing missing ones via g.extension.manage, and finally copying the executable and description files to appropriate QGIS/GISBASE directories for hydrological stream analysis.

name: Install r.stream.order and r.stream.basins extensions
desc: The script installs the GRASS GIS extensions 'r.stream.order' and 'r.stream.basins' for QGIS Processing. It first checks if the extensions are already installed by listing GRASS extensions, then installs them if missing. After installation, it copies the corresponding description files (.txt) from a local GRASS descriptions folder to the GRASS provider's description folders, ensuring that the tools appear in QGIS Processing Toolbox. This algorithm is part of the DB simulator group and requires no user inputs.

name: Burn cut lines into DEM
desc: The script burns linear cut features (e.g., drainage cuts or ditches) into an input unfilled DEM by buffering the lines, computing minimum elevation values within those buffers via zonal statistics, rasterizing those minima, and merging the result with the original DEM. It then fills sinks in the modified DEM, computes flow accumulation using GRASS r.watershed, and generates a hillshade. Outputs include: (1) OutputNewDEM (cut-burned DEM), (2) OutputFillDEM (filled version), (3) OutputFlowAcc (flow accumulation raster), and (4) OutputHshd (hillshade).

name: Generate stream reach and catchment layers
desc: The script identifies main stream reaches from an input flow network vector layer using a user-defined numeric field (LimitField) and classification threshold (ClassValue), then rasterizes the selected reaches. It processes D8 flow direction and filled DEM rasters through TauDEM's AreaD8 and StreamNet tools to compute flow accumulation and derive topologically correct stream networks and associated sub-catchments. Outputs are two vector layers: (1) 'Output Stream Reach' — a line layer of stream reaches with original attributes preserved, and (2) 'Output Sub-catchments' — a polygon layer of delineated catchments, dissolved by value, derived from TauDEM's watershed raster output.

name: Extract flow pathways from accumulation raster
desc: The script extracts stream networks (flow pathways) by thresholding a flow accumulation raster (converted to hectares), binarizing it, thinning the raster using GRASS r.thin, and converting the thinned raster to vector line features. The output is a vector layer of streams where each line represents an approximate flow pathway; the script explicitly notes that line direction may be incorrect and that this tool is intended for quick visualization rather than accurate hydrological analysis.

name: Estimate detainment bund catchments
desc: The script estimates the storage pond volume (in m³), contributing area (in m²), and storage:catchment ratio for potential detainment bunds (DBs) by processing user-provided DB location points, a filled DEM, and a flow direction raster. It iterates over unique Height (m)–Length (m) combinations in the input vector layer; for each combination, it buffers DB locations, derives watershed basins using GRASS r.stream.basins, burns DB heights into a modified DEM, computes fill depth via sink-filling (SAGA fillsinksxxlwangliu), calculates volumetric storage per cell (applying Z factor and pixel area), aggregates storage volume and catchment area per DB_ID via zonal statistics, and outputs a dissolved, smoothed, attribute-enriched vector layer of catchments with fields: DB_ID, Contr_area, Height (m), Length (m), Volume(m3), Area (m2), Ratio, and sorted by descending Ratio. An optional depth raster (FillReg) is also generated.

name: Export contour lines to 3D CAD
desc: The script exports vector contour line layers to a 3D DXF file preserving Z-elevation values. It first checks if the input layer is already 3D (via WKB type >1000); if not, it converts 2D contours to 3D using GRASS v.to.3d with a user-specified numeric elevation field. Then it exports the resulting 3D layer to DXF using QGIS native:dxfexport, respecting target CRS and AutoCAD version compatibility (R2000–R2018). Output is a single .dxf file with 3D geometry and embedded elevation as Z-coordinates.

name: Calculate Curve Number from land cover and soil data
desc: The script calculates the Soil Conservation Service (SCS) Curve Number (CN) raster for a user-defined polygon study area using two global datasets: ESA WorldCover 2021 (land cover classification) and ORNL HYSOG (hydrologic soil groups). It processes these rasters by clipping to the study area extent, aligning their spatial resolution and extent, performing a pixel-wise lookup using a CSV-based CN table indexed by land cover code and soil group (A/B/C/D → 1/2/3/4), and applying hydrologic condition (Poor/Fair/Good) and antecedent runoff condition (I/II/III) parameters. Outputs include an optional ESA land cover raster, an optional soil group raster, and a mandatory final CN raster clipped to the input polygon. The script also computes and reports mean CN, potential retention (S), and direct runoff (Q) statistics.

name: Divide parcels by lot width
desc: The script divides input polygon parcels into smaller lots of a specified width (LOT_WIDTH) using geometric division lines derived from shortest polygon sides and oriented minimum bounding boxes for irregular polygons. It identifies regular (rectangular, 5-vertex) polygons directly and computes oriented minimum bounding boxes for irregular ones; then constructs horizontal division lines between midpoints of the two shortest sides, generates perpendicular lot-divider lines spaced at the desired lot width (with optional uniform corner distribution), extends all lines by 5 cm, clips them to the original parcel boundaries, splits the input parcels along those lines, and performs two iterative passes of merging small resulting polygons (below MERGE_THRESHOLD % of average area) based on shared boundary length. The output is a new vector layer of divided parcels with merged small lots.

name: Watershed basin delineation
desc: The script delineates a watershed basin from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and a pour point. It optionally clips an input stream network to the basin. It first resamples the DEM if necessary to reduce its size, then fills sinks using GRASS r.fill.dir, calculates flow direction and accumulation with r.watershed, delineates the watershed with r.water.outlet, converts the raster basin to vector polygon with r.to.vect, smooths the polygon boundary, and finally clips the input stream network if provided. The outputs are a polygon layer of the basin and an optional line layer of the clipped stream network.

name: Extract and order stream network
desc: The script generates a smoothed stream network vector layer from a digital elevation model (DEM), applying GRASS GIS hydrological tools (r.fill.dir, r.watershed, r.stream.extract) to derive flow direction, accumulation, and streams; then applies QGIS native geometry smoothing; and finally computes Strahler and Shreve stream orders via recursive topological traversal of line features based on upstream/downstream connectivity using start/end point matching and spatial indexing. Outputs include a line feature class with 'Strahler' and 'Shreve' integer attribute fields.

name: Identify altitude and slope-based environmental zones
desc: The script processes a Digital Elevation Model (DEM/DTM) to generate three vector layers: (1) APP areas above 1800 m elevation, (2) APP areas with slope >45°, and (3) restricted-use areas with slope between 25° and 45°. It reprojects the input DEM to a user-specified projected CRS (e.g., UTM), computes slope in degrees using GDAL’s slope algorithm, applies binary thresholding via LFTools to classify elevation and slope ranges, and converts resulting binary rasters to polygon vector layers by extracting pixels with DN = 1. All outputs are polygon layers with distinct styling applied post-processing.

name: Convert auxiliary line to polygon
desc: The script converts an input line layer ('Linha_Auxiliar') into a polygon buffer of user-defined width (in meters), reprojects dynamically to the appropriate UTM zone for metric accuracy, intersects the buffered polygon with the 'ATI' (Área Total do Imóvel) polygon layer, fixes geometries, and injects the resulting clipped polygon features directly into a target destination layer—specifically one named starting with 'RIO' or 'SA' (e.g., 'RIO_1', 'SA_2')—within the current QGIS project. The output is not a new layer but an in-place edit: features are added to the selected destination vector polygon layer, with automatic CRS transformation and commit.

name: Triangular coordinate transformation between D48/GK and D96/TM
desc: The script performs coordinate transformation on vector layers between the Slovenian national coordinate systems D48/GK and D96/TM using a triangular transformation model. It reads transformation parameters from CSV files, applies per-triangle affine transformation to vertices of each input layer, outputs transformed layers to files with appropriate CRS, and optionally fixes geometries and loads result into QGIS project.

name: Generate noise exposure grid and contours
desc: The script creates a vector grid layer (square cells) over a user-defined extent at a specified resolution, then rasterizes an input vector layer (e.g., noise source or receiver points) using a specified attribute field (e.g., dBA), fills NoData pixels, applies a custom pseudo-color ramp for noise levels (35–80 dB(A)), generates contour lines at a user-defined interval, and produces polygonized isopleths with area calculation (Area_mq). Outputs include: (1) a shapefile of the square grid; (2) a rendered raster layer named 'Raster noise distrubution' with 13 explicit dB(A) color stops; (3) a contour vector layer; and (4) a polygonized isopleth layer with area-in-square-meters attribute.

name: Generate building facade receiver points
desc: The script generates noise receiver points positioned at fixed distances (0.1 m) outward from building facades, using three distinct methods: (1) 'middle' places two points per facade segment (midpoint offset perpendicular to segment), filtering out points that fall inside any building; (2) 'spaced' uses QGIS processing algorithms (buffer → polygon to lines → points along lines) to place points at user-defined spacing along buffered building outlines, then filters interior points and assigns each to its nearest building; (3) 'case2b' buffers building outlines, converts to polylines, and places points at regular intervals (5 m) along the buffered perimeter using linear interpolation, rejecting points intersecting buildings. All methods output a point layer with attributes: id_pt (sequential integer ID), id_bui (source building feature ID), and facadeP (percentage position along facade length or fixed spacing value).

name: Estimate floodwater depth
desc: The script estimates floodwater depth by subtracting a distance-transformed flood boundary raster (grown from the flood polygon outline) from a clipped DEM, producing a raster where each cell value represents estimated water depth (m) within the inundated area. Key steps include: (1) clipping the input DEM to the flood polygon extent; (2) converting the flood polygon to polyline boundaries; (3) rasterizing those boundaries; (4) extracting DEM elevation values along the rasterized boundary; (5) computing Euclidean distance-to-boundary (i.e., proximity to flood edge) using GRASS r.grow.distance; and (6) calculating depth as max(0, distance-derived surface elevation − clipped DEM), yielding a flood depth raster. A Gaussian-filtered version is also generated but not returned as primary output.

name: Estimate floodwater depth
desc: The script estimates floodwater depth from a flood extent polygon and a digital elevation model (DEM) using a multi-step geoprocessing workflow: (1) it fixes geometries of the input inundation polygon; (2) converts the polygon to polylines; (3) clips the DEM to the inundation polygon; (4) rasterizes the flood boundary polyline at the DEM’s native resolution; (5) extracts underlying DEM elevations along the boundary using raster multiplication and division; (6) applies GRASS7's r.grow.distance to compute Euclidean distance-based elevation interpolation (nearest boundary elevation assigned to interior cells); (7) computes preliminary water depth as the difference between interpolated flood level and clipped DEM, zeroing negative values; and (8) applies SAGA's Gaussian low-pass filter for smoothing. Outputs include a raw water depth raster ('waterDepth.tif') and a smoothed version ('*_low_pass.tif'), optionally saved to user-specified paths.

name: Rasterize species range polygons
desc: The script converts vector polygon layers representing species range distributions into individual species-specific raster maps. It first adds a presence field (named 'presence' by default, populated with value 1) to the input polygon layer using QGIS field calculator; then iterates over unique values in the user-specified attribute field (e.g., species name), selects features per species, saves each as a separate shapefile, and rasterizes each into a GeoTIFF with fixed dimensions (2000×1000 pixels), using the presence field for pixel values. Outputs are one GeoTIFF per species, named after the species value (with spaces replaced by underscores), saved to the specified output directory.

name: Compute slope-based terrain inclination classes
desc: The script computes terrain slope from DGM (Digital Ground Model) raster data, classifies slope values into five inclination classes (1–5) based on mean slope per polygon (Einzelflächen), and writes both the class ID ('neigkl') and mean slope value ('neigung') back to the 'flaechen' table in the QKan SQLite database. Key steps include: (1) reprojecting the 'Einzelflächen' vector layer to a target EPSG; (2) determining DGM tile coordinates (1 km grid) covering the layer’s bounding box; (3) downloading DGM1-32 tiles (e.g., 'dgm1_32_x_y_1_nw*') via HTTP directory listing parsing; (4) merging downloaded GeoTIFFs into a single 'dgm_gesamt.tif'; (5) computing slope raster ('neigung.tif'); (6) performing zonal statistics to extract mean slope per polygon; (7) classifying mean slope using nested 'if' expression thresholds (≤1°→1, ≤4°→2, ≤10°→3, ≤14°→4, >14°→5); and (8) updating the 'neigkl' and 'neigung' fields in the database-linked 'flaechen' layer.

name: Cut overlapping surface areas
desc: The script performs geometric operations on surface area polygons stored in a QKan SQLite/SpatiaLite database to resolve overlaps between different surface types (e.g., based on 'abflussparameter'). It creates a temporary table 'temp_flaechencut', computes non-overlapping geometries using ST_Difference and ST_Union, then updates the original 'flaechen' table with cut geometries. Additionally, it generates Voronoi-based catchment areas ('tezg') for selected sewer pipes ('haltungen') by converting pipe centerlines into thin polygons, computing Voronoi skeletons via GRASS v.voronoi.skeleton, clipping to selected subcatchments ('teilgebiete'), and inserting results into the 'tezg' table — all while enforcing topological consistency and validating for intersecting pipes.

name: Generate basin routing GeoJSON
desc: The script processes basin delineation shapefiles (subbasin polygons, river lines, connected and non-connected lake polygons) to produce GeoJSON routing products. It reprojects layers to WGS84, simplifies geometries with varying tolerances to keep file sizes under 100 MB, calculates new attributes (e.g., 'rvhName'), and exports them as GeoJSON. It then merges selected features (rivers and lakes) into a final 'routing_product_lake_river.geojson' file, handling lake connectivity and attribute cleaning. The workflow is part of a basinmaker toolkit, designed to prepare spatial data for hydrological routing modeling.

name: Generate grid polygon from NetCDF
desc: The script generates two shapefile outputs from a NetCDF file: (1) Nc_Grids.shp — a point layer where each point represents the centroid of a NetCDF grid cell, with attributes FGID, Row, Col, Gridlon, Gridlat; and (2) Gridncply.shp — a polygon layer where each polygon approximates the boundary of a NetCDF grid cell using bilinear interpolation of corner coordinates derived from adjacent grid nodes (for rotated grids) or axis-aligned averaging (for non-rotated grids), with identical attributes. It also writes Gridcorr.csv containing the same coordinate/ID table. A second function performs area-weighted spatial overlay between two polygon layers (Target_Ply_Path and Mapping_Ply_Path), producing Overlay_Polygons.shp (the dissolved union geometry with computed area field 's_area') and GriddedForcings2.txt (a text file encoding area-proportional mapping weights from mapping-grid polygons to target-HRU polygons). Both functions rely on QGIS processing algorithms via PyQGIS API and netCDF4 for coordinate extraction.

name: Reproject and clip raster to mask extent
desc: The script reprojects a source raster to match the coordinate reference system and spatial properties (cell size, CRS) of a mask raster, then clips the reprojected raster using a vector mask layer (shapefile). Outputs are two GeoTIFF files: one reprojected ('_proj.tif') and one clipped to the mask geometry ('.tif'), both stored in the GRASS database directory. The workflow uses QGIS Processing algorithms 'gdal:warpreproject' and 'gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer', with no resampling or nodata handling specified, and exits QGIS cleanly after execution.

name: Delineate subregion watersheds
desc: The script delineates nested hydrologic subregions (subbasins) from a digital elevation model (DEM), iteratively tuning the flow accumulation threshold to achieve a target number of subbasins (9–13), then integrates lake features into the watershed network, computes bankfull channel geometry parameters (k and c), generates outlet/inlet point vectors and catchment polygon masks per subregion, and finally merges subregion results into a unified, topologically consistent watershed hierarchy with updated drainage area, Strahler order, and routing attributes. Key outputs include packed GRASS rasters (FDR, ACC, STR_R, STR_V, DEM), shapefiles for subregion masks (HyMask_region_*.shp), outlet/inlet points (Sub_Reg_Outlet_v.shp, sub_reg_inlet.shp), subregion metadata (Sub_reg_info.csv), and combined final catchments (finalcat_info.shp) and rivers (finalcat_info_riv.shp).

name: Process population raster data
desc: The script processes a user-provided population raster by clipping it to individual study area polygons (from a GeoPackage layer named 'study_area_clip_polygons'), expanding each clipped raster to align with the bounding box of its corresponding study area, resampling to a specified cell size using gdalwarp with 'sum' resampling method, reclassifying the resampled rasters into three equal-interval classes based on global min/max population values across all resampled rasters, and generating VRT mosaics for clipped, resampled, and reclassified outputs. Outputs include per-study-area GeoTIFFs at each processing stage and final VRT files: 'clipped_population.vrt', 'resampled_population.vrt', and 'reclassified_population.vrt', plus a QML style file for the reclassified output.

name: Aggregate GeoE3 scores by subnational boundaries
desc: The script calculates majority-class GeoE3 Score (5 classes: 0–5) and GeoE3 × Population Score (15 classes) for each subnational administrative polygon using zonal statistics (majority mode) on precomputed VRT rasters. It processes up to four raster inputs — 'GeoE3_Score_combined.vrt', 'geoe3_by_population_score.vrt', 'geoe3_score_ghsl_masked.vrt', and 'geoe3_score_by_population_ghsl_masked.vrt' — against a user-provided aggregation vector layer (e.g., provinces or districts). Outputs are GeoPackage layers with columns 'fid', 'name', 'geoe3_score', and 'geoe3_pop_score', styled with QML files ('geoe3_score_vector.qml' and 'geoe3_by_population_vector_score.qml'). Geometry is pre-processed via 'native:fixgeometries' and field-retention to preserve 'fid'.

name: Process Geospatial Data CRS and Geometry
desc: The script provides utility functions for geospatial data processing in QGIS. It assigns CRS to raster layers using gdal:assignprojection and to vector layers using native:assignprojection. It subsets vector layers by intersecting with a given geometry using native:extractbyextent. It converts a QgsGeometry to a memory vector layer. It fixes geometries with native:fixgeometries and reprojects layers to a target CRS with native:reprojectlayer if needed. It combines multiple rasters into a VRT file via gdal:buildvirtualraster and optionally copies a QML style. The outputs are processed layers returned to the caller.

name: Calculate multi-buffer accessibility distances
desc: The script computes concentric isochrones (distance-based or time-based) around point features (e.g., health facilities, schools) using QGIS native network analysis on a road network layer. For National/Local scales, it generates non-overlapping distance bands (e.g., 500m, 1000m, 2000m) via sequential difference operations on dissolved isochrones, then assigns inverted distance scores (5 for closest band, 1 for farthest). For Regional scale, it uses simple Euclidean buffering and scores grid cells (e.g., H3 hexagons) based on percentage intersection with the buffer, mapping overlap percentages to discrete scores via configurable thresholds. Outputs are rasterized layers per study area, combined into a VRT; intermediate outputs include clipped road networks, isochrone GeoPackages, band layers, and scored vector grids.

name: Calculate multi-buffer travel distances to points of interest
desc: The script calculates concentric isochrone buffers (travel time or distance) around points of interest using OpenRouteService (ORS) API, processes them in subsets due to ORS request limits (max 5 features per call), merges and difference-creates non-overlapping bands, assigns Likert-scale scores (1–5) inversely proportional to buffer distance thresholds, rasterizes the scored bands, and outputs georeferenced TIFFs scaled to the likert scale; results are combined into a VRT and added to QGIS. Inputs include a study area polygon, a vector layer of points (e.g., health facilities, schools), travel mode (Walking/Driving), measurement unit (Distance/Time), and user-defined distance/time thresholds.

name: Reclassify environmental hazard raster
desc: The script reclassifies an input environmental hazards raster (e.g., fire, flood, landslide, cyclone, or drought) into a standardized 0–5 severity scale using layer-specific threshold rules. It loads the raster via QgsRasterLayer, applies QGIS native 'reclassifybytable' with predefined min/max/value triplets per hazard type, clips the result to the study area’s mask layer, and saves the output as a GeoTIFF (e.g., 'fire_reclassified_0.tif') in the workflow directory. The reclassification logic is hardcoded per layer_id and uses range boundaries (e.g., 2 for landslide, 0 otherwise), and logging confirms rule application and file output.

name: Process GHSL settlement data
desc: The script processes Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) settlement data for a study area defined in study_area.gpkg. It first checks for an existing 'ghsl_settlements' vector layer in the GeoPackage; if absent or empty, it downloads GHSL raster tiles intersecting the study area's EPSG:4326 bounding box, reclassifies them, polygonizes the reclassified rasters, combines the resulting vector features in ESRI:54009 (Mollweide), and appends them to the GeoPackage as 'ghsl_settlements'. The workflow then iterates over study area polygons (from 'study_area_polygons'), subsets input features or rasters per area, executes workflow-specific processing (_process_features_for_area, _process_raster_for_area, or _process_aggregate_for_area), masks outputs to aligned clip geometries, and combines all area outputs into a single VRT file. Outputs include a VRT mosaic of processed rasters and optional error logs.

name: Generate Vienna DSM mosaic
desc: The script downloads, unzips, reprojects (EPSG:31256 → EPSG:4326), and merges 96 individual DSM GeoTIFF files from the City of Vienna's official open data portal (ma41.geodaten.dom_tif) into a single merged GeoTIFF raster named 'dsm.tif'. The input files follow a grid naming convention (e.g., '22_4_dom_tif.zip') covering Vienna’s administrative area; all outputs are stored in local QGIS temporary paths and registered as a QGIS raster layer with EPSG:4326.

name: Download and mosaic Vienna DTM
desc: The script downloads Digital Terrain Model (DTM) GeoTIFF files for 104 specific grid regions (e.g., '22_4', '32_2') from the official Vienna city portal (wien.gv.at/ma41), unzips them, reprojects each from EPSG:31256 (MGI / Austria Lambert) to EPSG:4326 (WGS84), and merges all into a single georeferenced raster file dtm.tif. The final merged raster is registered as a QGIS raster layer with CRS 4326.

name: Download and reproject Vienna orthophotos
desc: The script downloads 84 individual orthophoto ZIP files from the official Vienna city portal (ma41), unzips them, reprojects each TIFF from EPSG:31256 (MGI / Austria Lambert) to EPSG:4326 (WGS84), merges all reprojected TIFFs into a single ortho.jpg raster, and updates the QGIS project with this merged orthophoto layer. All operations are hardcoded for Vienna's administrative grid tiles (e.g., '22_4', '32_2'), and file paths are fixed to local macOS user directory '/Users/arthurrufhosangdacosta/qgis_data/temp/ortho/'. The final output is a georeferenced, globally aligned orthophoto mosaic of Vienna.

name: Generate 3D city model from DSM and footprints
desc: The script generates a 3D city model in QGIS by extruding building footprints using heights derived from a digital surface model (DSM). It uses various zonal statistics or raster sampling methods (GRASS, SAGA, QGIS native) to compute building heights and assigns them to footprint features. It then applies 3D polygon symbols with extrusion height from the computed attribute, sets up phong material colors, and adds additional layers (streets, trees, water) to the QGIS project. Output layers can be saved to user-specified file paths.

name: Normalize city model input layers
desc: The script normalizes geospatial layers for 3D city modeling by reprojecting raster and vector layers to match the project CRS and clipping them to a user-defined polygon. It processes orthoimagery, DTM, DSM, and optionally street, tree, and water layers using GDAL warp, QGIS reproject layer, GDAL clip raster by mask, and native clip algorithms. The normalized layers are saved to a temporary folder and updated in the application context for subsequent model generation.

name: Expose QGIS layers, features, and map extents to R
desc: The script provides a QGISAPI class that exposes QGIS functionalities for listing, retrieving, and inserting map layers, querying project state, exporting selected features, and capturing user-drawn bounding boxes and points. It acts as a server for R through a dispatch method, facilitating geospatial data exchange between QGIS and R.

name: Generate cross-section sample frames
desc: The script generates sample frame polygons by splitting a polygon layer with cross-section lines. It extends the cross‑section lines by a tiny distance (0.000001) to guarantee intersection, splits the polygon into multiple parts using the extended lines, and writes each resulting polygon to an output vector layer. Each feature is assigned a sample_frame_id and a sequential display_label, producing a set of frames suitable for further sampling or analysis within a QGIS processing task.

name: Vectorize Elevation Threshold Polygons
desc: The script processes a raster elevation model by applying a threshold to extract areas below (or above) a specified elevation value. It then vectorizes these areas into polygons, smoothing, simplifying, and removing small polygons. The final output is a GeoPackage layer with area attributes, suitable for floodplain mapping or terrain analysis.

name: Earthworks Cut and Fill Grading
desc: The script modifies a DEM by carving and filling based on a platform vector layer with specified absolute level and cut/fill slopes. It creates multi-ring buffers at distance 1 for 100 rings, adds fields for platform level, cut slope, fill slope, then computes cut_level and fill_level for each ring. It rasterizes these levels, and combines with the original DEM using a min-max operation to enforce cut and fill design, producing a graded terrain DEM.

name: Create LRS marks along road axis
desc: The script takes an input line vector layer (road axis), generates points every 25 meters using the 'Points along geometry' algorithm, and applies a QML style to create visual LRS marks and labels for 25m and 100m intervals. The output is a point vector layer.

name: Reservoir Flooding Simulation
desc: The script creates a dam on an existing DEM and calculates the flooded area. It first generates a multi-ring buffer around the dam vector layer, computing fill levels for each ring based on the dam top level and wall slope. The buffered layer is rasterized with the fill level values and merged with the original DEM using a conditional raster calculation, resulting in a new DEM with the dam structure. Then, using a seed point inside the reservoir and a specified water level (dam top minus water depth), the GRASS r.lake tool determines the inundated area and produces a lake raster. Outputs include the modified DEM with dam and the lake raster (water depth).

name: QGIS workflow: Data processing, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing
desc: This workflow contains 5 core geospatial operations, including Data processing, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data editing, Buffer Analysis. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Estimate dam removal reservoir volume
desc: This script provides a QGIS pre-processing widget for dam removal and reservoir estimation. It guides the user to digitize a dam area polygon, estimate the reservoir shape using a negative buffer technique based on dam height and side slope, and then simulate the dam removal by creating a channel and merging the modified terrain raster with the original DEM. Additionally, it includes a raster unit converter. The outputs include a new DEM raster representing the terrain after dam removal and a text summary of the estimated reservoir area and volume.

name: OSM land use classification
desc: The script processes OpenStreetMap (OSM) landuse raster data to produce a classified landuse vector layer for FLO-2D modeling. It extracts land use classes from a multi-band OSM raster using band value thresholds, combines binary class rasters through raster calculator operations, and then vectorizes the resulting raster, clipping it to a provided grid layer. The output is a vector landuse map with landuse codes ('DN' field).

name: Merge Italian Cadastral GML Datasets
desc: The script downloads Italian cadastral GML data from the Agenzia delle Entrate WFS for selected provinces and municipalities, extracts map (MAP) and parcel (PLE) files, merges them into single GPKG files, optionally adds derived attribute fields (foglio, particella, sezione_censuaria, comune), reprojects to a target CRS, and loads the output layers into QGIS.

name: QGIS workflow: Format conversion, Projection
desc: This workflow contains 28 core geospatial operations, including Format conversion, Projection, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Vector spatial analysis. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Align rasters to reference grid
desc: The script aligns multiple input rasters to a reference raster by resampling them to the same CRS, pixel size, and origin. Supports multiple resampling methods, optional masking with vector layer and buffer, and outputs aligned GeoTIFF files using GDAL Warp and ClipRasterByMaskLayer.

name: Modify land cover using vector field
desc: The script modifies a land cover raster by replacing pixel values within polygons using a numeric attribute field from a vector layer. It first copies the original raster via clip by extent to preserve the original, then runs GDAL rasterize overwrite to burn the field values into the raster, producing a modified land cover raster.

name: Modify Land Cover by Name
desc: This QGIS algorithm modifies a land cover raster by changing pixel values to a new land cover code in areas defined by a polygon vector layer. It uses a lookup table mapping land cover names to codes, copies the original raster with cliprasterbyextent, then rasterizes the polygons with the selected code to overwrite the raster. The output is a modified land cover raster.

name: Modify Land Cover by NLCD or C-CAP
desc: The script modifies a land cover raster by replacing pixel values within user-defined polygon areas with a selected NLCD or C-CAP land cover class value. It copies the input raster, then rasterizes the vector overlay using the chosen class code, effectively overwriting areas of interest.

name: Calculate material transport accumulation
desc: The script provides utility functions for QGIS-based sediment or pollutant transport modeling within the QNSPECT plugin. The key functionality, `grass_material_transport`, uses GRASS `r.watershed` to compute flow accumulation from an elevation raster and a weight raster (representing material to transport) with an option for multiple flow direction. It then replaces no-data values and applies a raster math correction to restore original no-data cells, returning a material transport accumulation raster. Additional utilities manage QGIS layer styling, group organization, matrix filtering, and GDAL raster calculator wrapping to support the transport workflow.

name: Rasterize soil HSG and K-factor
desc: The script converts a vector polygon soil layer into Hydrologic Soil Group (HSG) and/or K-Factor rasters. It validates that HSG field values are among the allowed categories (A, B, C, D, A/D, B/D, C/D, W, Null). If a K-Factor field is specified, it rasterizes that field using GDAL rasterize with a given cell size. If an HSG field is provided, it first maps the string HSG codes to numeric values via a field calculator expression, then rasterizes the result. Both outputs are single-band rasters with user-defined cell size and extents matching the input layer.

name: Remove small polygons and holes
desc: The script removes small polygonal objects and holes from a polygon vector layer. It first selects features based on a specified field value, then removes polygons with area below a minimum threshold, and finally deletes holes smaller than a given area, outputting a cleaned vector layer.

name: Generate DSM and Land Cover from LiDAR
desc: The script processes Swedish national LiDAR point cloud (class 2 ground, class 1 building) together with a building footprint vector layer to produce a digital elevation model (dem.tif), digital surface model (dsm.tif), canopy height model (cdsm.tif), land cover classification (lc.tif: paved, building, deciduous forest, grass, and optionally water from OSM), and leaf area index (lai_10m.tif). It clips the LiDAR, extracts ground and building points, generates DEM/DSM/CDSM using FUSION CanopyModel and GridSurfaceCreate, derives land cover from intensity thresholding and building/vegetation masks, and estimates LAI from return density ratios.

name: LiDAR-based DSM and land cover generation
desc: The script generates Digital Surface Models (DSM), Digital Elevation Models (DEM), Canopy Height Models (CDSM), land cover maps, and Leaf Area Index (LAI) from Swedish national LiDAR point cloud data and building footprint vector layers. It processes multiple tiles of .laz files by clipping building points, extracting ground and vegetation points, and applying filtering and classification steps. Outputs include DEM, DSM, CDSM, land cover (lc.tif), and optional LAI raster, merged across tiles.

name: Road network intersection extraction and routing
desc: The script initializes a network from a linestring layer, extracts intersections by dissolving the network, finding line intersections, and removing duplicates. It then provides a routing method that builds a directed graph using QgsVectorLayerDirector and computes the shortest path between two points via Dijkstra's algorithm. Outputs include intersection geometries and the vertex points along the calculated shortest path.

name: Clip linear network to trajectory buffer
desc: The script clips a given linear network (e.g., roads or paths) to the vicinity of a trajectory (point layer) by converting the trajectory points to a path, buffering that path with a user-specified radius, and then clipping the network to the buffer area. The resulting clipped network is split into single-part features. This QGIS processing algorithm is intended as a preprocessing step for offline map matching, reducing the network to the relevant area around a trajectory.

name: Clean building polygons and generate Voronoi diagram
desc: The script processes a polygon building layer by deleting holes, removing null geometries, converting multipart to singleparts, and eliminating features with duplicate centroids. It then generates a Voronoi diagram from building centroids, clipped to a 50-meter buffer around the buildings, and saves the cleaned building layer and the Voronoi polygons into a GeoPackage.

name: Clean road network topology
desc: The script cleans a road vector layer using GRASS GIS v.clean tools (snap, break, rmdupl) to fix topological errors. It snaps line ends, breaks overlapping segments, removes duplicate geometries, and filters out features with errors via a join. The cleaned layer is saved as a GeoPackage file.

name: Generate hexagon and Voronoi building density maps
desc: The script generates hexagon tessellations and Voronoi polygons from an input vector layer of centroids (e.g., building points) for visualization. It computes spatial aggregations by hexagon grid at varying spacings, filtering hexagons intersecting the original layer, assigning nearest 'osm_id', and summarizing numeric attributes and count of buildings per hexagon. It also creates Voronoi polygons clipped to a buffer around the input layer. Outputs are saved as GeoPackage layers, and layers are added to the project.

name: QGIS workflow: Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing
desc: This workflow contains 508 core geospatial operations, including Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Vector spatial analysis, Vector data attribute editing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: OSM Sidewalk Creation Utility Functions
desc: The script provides a collection of reusable PyQGIS functions to support an OSM sidewalk creation workflow. It includes functions for spatial operations (buffering, clipping, intersects, dissolves, polygonize), geometry processing (line splitting, point angle calculations, vertex selection), attribute manipulation (field creation, area/perimeter calculation), spatial indexing, and coordinate transformations to local Transverse Mercator projection. These functions prepare street network data, generate sidewalk polygons, handle spatial relations, and manage layer outputs for the main sidewalk generation algorithm.

name: Clip and buffer river hierarchy levels
desc: The script is a QGIS plugin that clips an input vector layer using a clip boundary, then separates the clipped hydrological network by three hierarchy levels (Principal, Secondary, Tertiary), assigns distinct colors, creates buffer zones of 100m, 50m, and 20m respectively, and adds all resulting layers to the QGIS project.

name: Collect natural resource data from feature server
desc: The script loads natural resource data from a Queensland government feature server for user-specified property extents. It supports search by lotplan (using property layer bounding boxes) or direct extent string. It retrieves features in batches, applies a zero-distance buffer for geometry cleaning, clips to property polygons, merges results, saves as a GeoPackage, and adds styled layers to the QGIS canvas.

name: Classify and buffer water network levels
desc: The script performs a clip operation on a user-provided vector layer using a clip layer, then classifies the clipped layer into three water network levels (Principal, Secundaria, Terciaria) based on the 'Descripc' attribute, applies distinct colors, and generates buffer zones of 100m, 50m, and 20m respectively for each level. The results include the clipped layer, filtered level-specific layers, and buffer layers displayed in the QGIS map.

name: Extract and merge FiC flood extents
desc: The script extracts flood extent polygons from the FloodsInCanada (FiC) database for a given area of interest and date range. It loads the FiC polygon feature class, selects features using a date expression, clips them to the AOI, dissolves overlapping polygons, and exports a merged, cleaned vector layer. The outputs include intermediate raw selections and final dissolved inundation polygon files.

name: Extract Raster Values for Field Polygon
desc: The script extracts raster values at point locations generated within an agricultural field polygon, optionally applying an internal buffer. It clips each input raster to the polygon extent, creates a point grid matching the first raster's resolution, clips the grid to the buffered polygon, then samples all raster bands at those points. Column names are derived from raster file names, and multi-band rasters are handled with band suffixes. The final merged attribute table is exported as a GeoPackage point layer and a CSV file, both automatically loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Compute DTM slope raster
desc: The script processes a digital terrain model (DTM) raster to produce a slope map expressed as percent slope. It first clips the DTM to a user-specified extent and resamples to an output cell size using GDAL Translate. Then it computes slope in degrees using QGIS native slope algorithm. Next, it warps the slope raster with mode resampling to match the output cell size and extent. Finally, using a raster calculator expression, it converts slope from degrees to percent via 100*tan(angle*pi/180) and clips values to a user-defined lower and upper limit, outputting the resulting slope raster.

name: Evaluate Rasterization Quality
desc: The algorithm evaluates the quality of the rasterization process by comparing vector polygon areas with their rasterized counterparts. It takes a source vector layer and a mask vector layer, rasterizes both using a specified burn field and cell size, clips vector areas to the mask, computes area sums per category, then calculates the masked raster area per value, and finally joins the two tables to compute squared error and combined RMSE, producing a quality index as a percentage of the mask area.

name: Rasterize tabular data from distribution maps
desc: The algorithm distributes the values of all numeric fields from a source table onto raster maps based on a polygon distribution map and a reference raster's georeferencing. It joins the table to the vector layer using a common ID field, then rasterizes each numeric field into ASCII raster files, outputting them to a specified folder.

name: Load and validate Maharashtra administrative boundary data
desc: The script loads district and village boundary layers from GADM and hospital points from GeoJSON, validates feature counts and CRS, reprojects all layers to UTM zone 43N (EPSG:32643), and extracts only Maharashtra districts using an attribute filter. Outputs include reprojected geopackages and a Maharashtra districts layer.

name: Identify underserved villages for hospital access
desc: The script analyzes hospital accessibility in Maharashtra by clipping hospital and village point layers to the state boundary, creating a 5km buffer around hospitals, extracting villages outside the buffer to identify underserved areas, and computing hospital counts per district. Outputs include geopackage layers: fixed geometries, clipped hospitals, clipped villages, 5km hospital buffer, underserved villages, and districts with hospital counts, along with printed coverage area and top districts by hospital count.

name: Extract features within point buffers
desc: The script iterates over a point layer, selects each point by its ID, generates a buffer around it, and extracts features from a second layer that intersect the buffer using PyQGIS processing algorithms (native:extractbyattribute, native:buffer, native:extractbylocation). The result is a per-point spatial extraction.

name: Compute slope from DEM rasters
desc: The script computes slope from a list of input DEM rasters. It first checks if the raster data type is not Byte, ensuring the raster contains continuous elevation values rather than thematic data. If the raster's CRS is geographic, it reprojects the raster using gdal:warpreproject to a projected CRS for proper slope calculation. The slope algorithm (native:slope) is then applied, and the resulting slope rasters are saved with a 'slope_' prefix in a destination folder.

name: Stochastic DEM interpolation simulation
desc: The script performs iterative simulation of digital elevation models (DEMs) by randomly extracting a subset of points from a dataset (likely a point layer) and then interpolating them using a cubic spline method (SAGA tool) to produce a raster surface. It generates multiple output rasters (s000.sdat, s001.sdat, ...) for a specified number of steps, likely for Monte Carlo-style uncertainty analysis or stochastic terrain modeling.

name: Optimize feature selection gain
desc: The script iteratively samples three random parameters, applies a formula to calculate distances in a layer using the field calculator, buffers the result, extracts features from a reference layer that intersect the buffer, counts them, computes a gain as count minus a penalty of the parameters, and tracks the best gain and corresponding distances layer across iterations.

name: Select agricultural land patches near urban fabric
desc: The script processes Urban Atlas 2018 land cover data for Poznan, Poland, to select agricultural and other land cover patches within the urban core. It first clips the land cover layer to the urban core mask, then extracts areas with codes 21000 (arable land), 22000 (permanent crops), 23000 (pastures), 24000 (complex cultivation), and 13400 (land without current use) as selected areas. It also extracts urban fabric classes (11100, 11210-11240) as attached areas and railway areas (12230) as detached areas. Buffers of 200 m are applied to attached areas and 250 m to detached areas, and the selected areas are intersected with the attached buffer then differenced with the detached buffer. The resulting polygons are split into single parts and filtered to retain only those with an area >= 10 hectares. The final layer is added to the QGIS project.

name: Clip landcover raster to point buffers
desc: The script clips a landcover raster to 1000-meter buffers around each point in a vector point layer. For each feature in the point layer, it extracts the point by its feature ID, creates a buffer of 1000 meters, checks if the buffer intersects the raster extent, and if so, clips the raster using the buffer as a mask, saving the clipped raster as a PNG image in the user's Documents folder.

name: Compute slope from DEM rasters
desc: The script computes slope rasters from a set of input Digital Elevation Model (DEM) rasters stored in a local directory. It first checks each raster’s data type and coordinate reference system; if a raster is not a Byte type and its CRS is geographic (latitude/longitude), it reprojects it to EPSG:2180 using gdal:warpreproject. Then it calculates slope using native:slope and saves the output to a ‘slopes’ subdirectory with a ‘slope_’ filename prefix.

name: Compute minimum distance buffers for points
desc: The script computes a distance matrix for a point layer against itself to find the minimum distance for each point to its nearest other point (using statistics). It then creates circular buffers around each point with a radius equal to that minimum distance. The result is a polygon layer added to the QGIS project.

name: Address point density grid calculation
desc: The script creates a grid overlay over an address point layer ('punkty_adresowe.gpkg'), counts the number of points within each grid cell, and visualizes the resulting polygon layer with point counts. The grid is created from the point layer's extent buffered by 100 map units, with dimensions 21 columns by 30 rows, resulting in a point density map.

name: Simulate cubic spline interpolation variability
desc: The script performs a Monte Carlo simulation of cubic spline interpolation by repeatedly extracting random subsets of 80 points from 'probkowanie.gpkg', interpolating attribute 'SAMPLE_1' using SAGA cubic spline, and generating 20 raster outputs (s000.sdat to s019.sdat). It then computes cell‑wise mean and standard deviation across all rasters to evaluate spatial uncertainty of the interpolation.

name: Optimize transmitter coverage of address points
desc: The script optimizes three distance parameters for buffering transmitter locations to maximize the number of address points covered, while penalizing uneven distances. It loads transmitter and address point vector layers, then iterates a random search (100 steps) adjusting distances (sum constrained to 6000, each between 0.2 and 0.6) using a field calculator to assign distances per transmitter feature, buffers with per-feature distances, selects intersecting address points, and computes a gain metric (covered address count minus standard deviation penalty). It retains the best-performing distances and finally buffers the transmitters with those optimal distances, adding the result to the QGIS project.

name: Generate elevation profile from DEM
desc: The script generates an elevation profile along a specified line using a DEM raster. It creates points along the line at a given distance interval (100 meters), samples the raster value at each point, extracts distances and elevation values, and plots the profile.

name: Analyze slope position distributions
desc: The script computes terrain slope position attributes (slope height, valley depth, normalized height, standardized height, midslope position) from a DEM using the SAGA 'Relative Heights and Slope Positions' algorithm, generates 1000 random sample points within the raster extent, extracts the attribute values at those points, and plots kernel density estimates for each derived variable. Outputs include a vector layer with sampled raster values and KDE distribution plots.

name: Generate transit walksheds by route
desc: The script generates walking-distance service areas (walksheds) around transit stops by route using a pedestrian network. It buffers stops, clips the network, splits lines, computes service areas, derives convex and concave hulls, and dissolves polygons by route. Processing is done in fixed-size batches to manage memory, with intermediate and final outputs saved as GeoPackages.

name: Generate transit stop walksheds
desc: The script generates walksheds (service area polygons) for transit stops using QGIS processing tools. It processes stops by route, creating individual walksheds based on a pedestrian network and a walking distance of 804.672 meters (1/2 mile). The workflow involves preparing the network by buffering all stops, clipping, and splitting lines; then for each route, further clipping the network, performing service area analysis, creating convex and concave hulls, clipping, and dissolving by route. Outputs include merged individual walksheds, dissolved walksheds by route, and service lines (network segments within walking distance).

name: Classify interior exterior zones from roads
desc: The script classifies areas as interior or exterior relative to a 12.5-unit buffer around road features (RVFundamental.gpkg) within a reference area (RPFGC_PPSM.gpkg). It buffers the road layer, clips the buffer to the reference area to get the interior zone, computes the difference to get the exterior zone, and merges both into a single output layer of interior and exterior zones.

name: Generate interior-exterior buffer zones
desc: The script buffers a vector layer (RVFundamental.gpkg) by 12.5 units, clips the buffer with another polygon layer (RPFGC_PPSM.gpkg) to get the interior intersection, computes the difference to get the exterior (non-overlapping) part, and merges both into a single output layer (faixasIntExt.gpkg).

name: Create interior-exterior buffer strips
desc: The script performs vector geoprocessing to delineate interior and exterior buffer zones. It applies a 20-meter buffer to the RVFundamental layer, clips the buffer with the RPFGC_PPSM boundary layer to define interior zones, uses difference to obtain exterior zones, and merges both into a single output layer. The final layer is added to the QGIS map canvas.

name: Buffer-based polygon interior-exterior partitioning
desc: The script partitions a polygon layer (RPFGC_PPSM) into interior and exterior regions relative to a buffer of another layer (RVFundamental). It creates a buffer of distance 20 around RVFundamental, clips the buffer to RPFGC_PPSM to obtain interior areas, computes the difference between RPFGC_PPSM and interior to get exterior areas, then merges both into a single output layer. The result is exported as a GeoPackage file.

name: Identify suitable school locations
desc: The script identifies suitable areas for new schools by spatially analyzing population density, proximity to existing schools, and proximity to rivers within a user-defined administrative boundary. It loads four user-uploaded shapefiles (population, schools, rivers, boundary), clips population data to the boundary, filters for high-population areas above a user-defined threshold, buffers existing schools and rivers by user-specified distances, merges those buffers, and computes the difference between high-population areas and merged buffers to yield suitable zones. The final output is a vector layer of suitable areas added to the QGIS project.

name: Filter structures near rivers and roads
desc: The script filters and relocates point-based 'structures' by computing line intersections between 'cours_eau' (rivers) and 'routes' (roads), merging those intersections with the original structures, buffering the merged points by 50 meters, dissolving overlapping buffers, computing centroids of the dissolved polygons, and finally extracting only those centroids within 100 meters of the 'cours_eau' layer. The output is a new point vector layer ('New_structures') containing filtered and spatially adjusted structure locations that are both proximal to road-river intersections and near rivers.

name: Join PtRef with lotic width data
desc: The script filters point reference features (PtRef) to retain only those whose 'Id_UEA' matches any 'Id_UEA' in the river network layer ('Riv_Net') and where the attribute 'Valide_bv' is true; then joins the filtered points with the 'PtRef_Mod_Lotique' layer on the 'Id_PtRef' field to attach the 'Largeur_mod' (modeled width) attribute. The output is a vector layer ('PtRef_largeur') containing only the matched, validated points enriched with the modeled width value.

name: Calculate stream segment land use impact indices
desc: The script calculates four environmental indicators (A1, A2, A3, F1) for each stream segment in a river network. It first extracts outlets and computes watersheds using D8 flow direction raster, reclassifies land use into four classes (forest, agriculture, anthropic, water), then computes watershed areas and land use constituent areas. A1 is derived from forest/agriculture ratios, A2 from dam watershed area fraction, A3 from anthropic+agriculture fraction and a dam penalty, and F1 from structure density within 1 km buffer. The output is a vector layer with the original stream attributes plus Indice A1, Indice A2, Indice A3, Indice F1 fields.

name: Calculate river obstruction indicator F2
desc: The script computes the F2 indicator for each river network segment by measuring the mean unrestricted distance from the river to the first anthropic obstacle, based on normal transects and land use reclassification. It first buffers the river network, clips the landuse raster to the buffer, reclassifies it into three anthropic classes (300, 360, 1), and vectorizes the raster. For each river segment, it generates points along the segment, determines the segment’s mean width via nearest neighbor lookup in a point reference layer, constructs normal transects to both sides, computes the distance to the nearest anthropic feature from the transect endpoints, calculates the mean unobstructed length, and maps it to an integer score (5, 3, 2, or 0). The output adds the 'Indice F2' field to the input river network layer.

name: Compute river fragmentation index F3
desc: The script calculates the F3 indicator for river network segments to assess watercourse fragmentation by anthropogenic pressures and land use. For each river segment, it splits into equal-length subsegments, creates single-sided buffers, intersects with provided anthropogenic vector layers and reclassified land use polygons, and then computes an index (0, 2, 3, or 5) based on the proportion of unobstructed subsegments. The output is a vector layer with appended 'Indice F3' field.

name: Calculate F5 river sinuosity indicator
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm computes the F5 sinuosity index for each river segment in the network. It first generates 50 equidistant points along each segment, then constructs perpendicular transects at each point whose lengths are based on a reference width layer and a transect ratio. The intersection of each transect with a riparian buffer polygon is measured to obtain a sequence of buffer widths. The F5 index is then derived by thresholding the proportion of widths exceeding 30m and 15m, resulting in an integer score from 0 to 4 indicating sinuosity/continuity. The output is a line vector layer with an added 'Indice F5' field.

name: Compute canopy height from GEDI and terrain rasters
desc: The script computes canopy height as the difference between a canopy elevation raster and a ground elevation raster, clamping negative values to zero. It then merges the resulting canopy height raster with an optional GEDI input raster (likely for co-location or validation), and converts the merged raster pixels to vector points with elevation/height values stored in the 'VALUE' field. The output is a point vector layer (GeoPackage) containing spatialized height measurements.

name: Generate land use vector polygons from raster
desc: The script provides a workflow for land use/land cover classification post-processing. It includes raster reclassification, polygonization of raster classes, field calculations, removal of small areas, fixing geometries, and dissolving polygons by 'Landuse_ID' field. The functions also support clipping rasters and vectors, joining attributes, and extracting features by attribute values.

name: Clean land cover polygons
desc: The script performs vector geometry cleaning on an input vector layer by sequentially applying geometry repair, polygon dissolution, multipart-to-singlepart conversion, hole removal (for holes < 20 m²), topology-preserving simplification (with user-defined tolerance in meters), and iterative smoothing (with user-defined iterations and offset). The output is a cleaned, simplified, and smoothed single-part polygon vector layer with topological integrity preserved and small artifacts removed.

name: Save URock wind model outputs
desc: The script post-processes and saves output data from the URock wind model. It computes horizontal wind speed, wind direction, and vertical wind speed from 3D wind components (u, v, w) at specified heights, creates point vector layers (GeoJSON, SHP, FGB) and raster grids (GeoTIFF) for each output height level, optionally generates a NetCDF file with the full 3D wind field and vertical wind profile, and applies building footprint masks to set wind speed to zero inside buildings during vector-to-raster interpolation. It also exports Röckle zone points for building and vegetation regions.

name: Prepare building and vegetation height layers
desc: The script generates two vector layers: (1) a building footprint layer with an added height attribute (ROOF_HEIGHT by default), computed as the median DSM value within each building polygon (optionally adjusted by subtracting DEM to derive above-ground height); and (2) a vegetation layer either rasterized from a canopy DSM (CDSM) — where polygons are created per rounded height class, dissolved by VALUE, and filtered to exclude 0 m — or derived from point data (trunk locations) via buffering using radius/height fields and aspect ratio (0.75 default) to infer missing attributes, then calculating VEG_HEIGHT. Both outputs are vector files (e.g., .shp, .geojson) with user-specified height field names.

name: Calculate solar panel coverage area
desc: The script computes the geometric coverage area (as a polygon) of solar panel installations grouped by 'ilot' (island/block), calculates total surface area in hectares, counts full and half tables, and computes a coverage rate (%) as the ratio of total panel area to the enveloping polygon area. It outputs a memory vector layer named 'recouvrement' with attributes: ilot (integer), surface (ha), table (full count), demi_table (half count), and taux (coverage percentage rounded to 1 decimal). The layer is styled with transparent fill, red outline, and labeled with 'taux' values using red text with white halo.

name: Fix and dissolve polygon boundaries
desc: The script processes multiple polygon shapefiles by fixing invalid geometries (using native:fixgeometries), dissolving them to create single-part features (native:dissolve), and then merging all dissolved shapefiles into a single output (native:mergevectorlayers). Input shapefiles are located in 'Polygonized_shapes', and the final merged output is saved as 'abp49_id001-054_merged.shp', with intermediate fixed and dissolved files stored in separate directories.

name: Load cadastral parcels
desc: The script loads and processes cadastral parcel data from the Slovenian national WFS service (ipi.eprostor.gov.si/wfs-si-gurs-kn/wfs). It implements asynchronous QGIS tasks to: (1) verify WFS server accessibility via HEAD request; (2) fetch list of cadastral municipalities (KO_ID, NAZIV) either from cached CSV or live WFS; (3) query parcel numbers (ST_PARCELE) for a given KO_ID; (4) load specific parcel geometries by KO_ID and ST_PARCELE; (5) load predefined QLR layer definitions; (6) extract parcels intersecting a user-defined area (with optional buffering and geometry fixing). Outputs include validated WFS layers, memory-based scratch layers with transferred metadata, flash-zoomed parcel geometries, and updated project layers with OGC:WFS metadata links.

name: Process trail network geometry
