desc: The script processes trail shapefiles by reprojecting to EPSG:3857, removing redundant attributes (OBJECTID, PERMANENT_, etc.), snapping geometries within 30 map units, fixing invalid geometries, dissolving by NAME and TRAILNUMBE fields, merging lines, splitting lines with themselves (self-intersection), then splitting into ~0.5-mile segments using GRASS v.split (length=1 unit in EPSG:3857 ≈ 1 meter → units=5 [meters] yields ~0.5 miles), merging all processed trails, simplifying geometries with tolerance=1, adding auto-incrementing ID field, calculating length in miles ($length * 0.000621371), and extracting start/end vertices as junctions. Final outputs are two ESRI Shapefiles: 'trails_merged_simp_4326_2.shp' (reprojected to EPSG:4326) and 'juncts_merged_4326_2.shp' (also EPSG:4326).

name: Export DSO-compliant GML
desc: The script exports QGIS vector layers to DSO-compliant GIO-GML and GIO-XML files following Dutch national standards (STOP/IMOP/geo). It performs reprojection, geometry validation (fixgeometries), optional dissolve by attribute, simplification (Douglas-Peucker), snapping to grid, and attribute-based filtering. Outputs include a GML file conforming to https://standaarden.overheid.nl/stop/imop/geo namespace, an accompanying XML metadata file generated via XSLT transformation, SHA-512 hash embedding, and FRBRExpression-compliant identifiers (e.g., /join/id/regdata/gm1234/...). The workflow is triggered from a QGIS plugin dialog with user-configurable parameters (projection, filter field/value, dissolve, simplify distance, snap grid spacing, decimal precision).

name: Anti-erosion measures geoprocessing
desc: The script provides QGIS processing functions for anti-erosion measure design, including DEM filtering (depressionless DEM), watershed delineation, contour generation, and vector geometry operations such as buffering, line offsetting, point sampling along lines, and shortest line calculation. It supports terrain analysis and feature extraction for anti-erosion workflows.

name: Land use code assignment and layer stacking
desc: The script processes multiple Czech vector layers (LPIS, ZABAGED, etc.) to create a unified land use layer. It assigns LandUse_code attributes based on YAML configuration rules, buffers line/point layers according to attribute values, clips to an area of interest, edits codes per feature attributes, and stacks polygon layers by priority to resolve overlaps. The final merged layer is styled with predefined symbology and added to the QGIS project.

name: Download and Clip WFS Land Layers
desc: The script downloads WFS vector layers (including ZABAGED and LPIS) configured via a file, gets spatial extent from map canvas or a polygon, fetches layers using bounding box requests, and clips them to the exact extent using QGIS geometry operations. The resulting clipped layers are prepared for further land use/land cover analysis.

name: Generate aggregated isochrones for transit accessibility
desc: The script generates aggregated isochrones (travel-time polygons) from point locations using OpenTripPlanner (OTP) REST API. It iterates over user-defined datetime ranges at specified intervals, constructs OTP isochrone requests (with configurable transport modes, walk/bike speeds, wheelchair support, etc.), downloads zipped shapefile responses, processes them via dissolve or union aggregation per input feature, and appends results to a memory vector layer with rich metadata including AggIsochrone_UID, AggIsochrone_ID, AggIsochrone_Error, AggIsochrone_URL, time intervals, request dates/times, and statistical summaries (e.g., time_min, time_mean, time_stddev) depending on selected aggregation mode (MaxDissolve, AllUnion, or NoAggRaw). Output is a QGIS memory vector layer with MultiPolygon geometry in EPSG:4326.

name: Map ATKIS and LBM land cover to Talsim land use
desc: The script maps German national land use/cover datasets (ATKIS Landnutzung and LBM-DE2021) to the Talsim hydrological modeling land use classification system. It performs: (1) for ATKIS: recursive discovery of shapefiles (e.g., 'veg01_f', 'sie02_f') in a user-specified folder, merging them, optional clipping with a polygon layer, dissolving by OBJART_TXT and code fields, then attribute-based mapping using 'atkis_talsim_zuordnung.csv' to assign 'OBJART_NEU' values; (2) for LBM-DE2021: direct mapping of 'LB_AKT' codes with SIE_AKT (surface imperviousness) range conditions using 'lbm_talsim_zuordnung.csv'. Outputs are two GeoPackage layers: 'Landuse' (mapped but undissolved) and 'LanduseDissolved' (dissolved by 'OBJART_NEU', with all other attributes deleted).

name: Map soil texture types
desc: The script processes ISRIC SoilGrids raster data (clay, silt, sand, and bulk density) to derive TALSIM-compatible soil texture classes (e.g., 'Ss', 'Sl2', 'St3') for multiple depth horizons (0–5 cm, 5–15 cm, ..., 100–200 cm). It reprojects input layers to Homolosine projection, downloads clipped rasters, converts mass fractions from g/kg to %, validates polygon geometries, performs point-in-polygon classification using a pre-defined 145-entry lookup table (boa) of clay-silt-sand coordinates, polygonizes resulting soil ID arrays, dissolves adjacent polygons by soil type and horizon, and outputs combined GeoPackage vector layers: 'soil_types.gpkg' (with talsim_soilid, soil_type, layer_thickness), 'bdod.gpkg' (bulk density classes 1–5), and a final merged 'Soil Types BDOD Combined' layer with all horizons and BDOD classes attributed per polygon. All outputs are added to the QGIS project under a 'QTalsim Soil Layers' group.

name: Process sub-basin hydrologic parameters
desc: The script processes a user-provided sub-basin polygon layer to compute: (1) maximum and minimum elevation per sub-basin using a DEM via zonal statistics; (2) sub-basin area in hectares; (3) mean imperviousness per sub-basin, either by raster zonal statistics (if imperviousness layer is raster) or by vector intersection + weighted area aggregation (if imperviousness layer is vector); (4) longest flow path (LFP) per sub-basin using WhiteboxTools' LongestFlowpath algorithm on a burn-and-fill preprocessed DEM clipped per sub-basin; (5) LFP rotation (flow direction) relative to south; (6) ZOUT point (outlet) derived as the intersection of the lowest-elevation border sub-basin with the outer boundary of the full sub-basin set. Outputs include: a processed GeoPackage layer with all computed attributes; a GPKG LFP layer; optional SQLite database export conforming to QTalsim schema (with SystemElement and SubBasin tables, WGS84-transformed geometries, and scenario metadata); and optional ASCII-formatted EZG file for Talsim NG4 with fixed-field layout based on a template.

name: Extract polygon boundary edges
desc: The script extracts the edges of input polygon geometries by buffering the polygon boundaries inward and outward by half the specified width (in tenths of millimeter), then computing the difference between the external and internal buffers to produce a new polygon layer representing the edge strip. The output is a vector layer with an added 'h' attribute set to braille.DIM['f'], and all intermediate geometries are processed through multipart-to-singlepart conversion, geometry fixing, and simplification at 0.0001 m tolerance.

name: Select tectonic features for node grid
desc: The script selects tectonic line features (ridges, isochrons, subduction zones, passive margins, rifts, cratons, collision zones, hotspots, etc.) from a plate model and polygon layers based on a specified appearance age. It computes derived attributes such as feature age, ridge depth, sediment thickness, and converts line geometries to densified versions (tolerance 1 km) and multipoint geometries. Polygon features are generated for rifts, cratons, and hotspots. All intermediate outputs are saved as GeoJSON files for subsequent node grid generation.

name: Create node grid from geological features
desc: The script processes geological node features (ridges, isochrons, hotspots, etc.) from plate polygons and other shapefiles to create a cleaned and harmonized node grid for subsequent modeling. It performs spatial cleaning to remove overlapping nodes based on type and distance thresholds, cuts profiles against continental polygons, calculates bearing and perpendicular profiles, converts coordinates, and applies a plate cooling model to estimate depth and age relationships. The final outputs are GeoJSON node layers for each setting and a merged all-nodes layer with attributes like type, age, depth, and plate.

name: Interpolate preliminary plate rasters from nodes
desc: Generates preliminary raster surfaces from tectonic plate nodes for a given age using TIN interpolation. Filters nodes by plate name and Z_DEM, interpolates field index 3, clips by plate polygons, fills nodata, and merges clipped rasters into a mosaic.

name: Paleo-topography raster generation
desc: The script generates paleo-topographic elevation rasters for each geological age by interpolating node point data (with water-load corrected elevation) using TIN interpolation within plate polygons, applying nodata filling, and mosaicking per-plate rasters into a global raster. It reprojects plate polygons and nodes to ESRI:54034 (World Cylindrical Equal Area), clips by plate boundaries, and outputs final filled rasters for each age.

name: Convert SU OBJ to 3D polygon
desc: The script converts a 3D OBJ file representing the top surface of an archaeological Stratigraphic Unit (SU) into two 3D polygon shapefiles: one in local coordinates (e.g., unprojected or site-relative) and one projected to EPSG:32632 (UTM zone 32N), with attribute fields 'Year', 'Trench', and 'SU' populated from user inputs. It uses Blender (with BlenderGIS addon) in headless mode to import the OBJ and export a temporary shapefile, then applies QGIS processing steps — geometry fixing, dissolving, hole deletion, coordinate translation (ΔX=452000, ΔY=4413000), projection assignment, and field calculation — before saving both outputs and loading the projected version into QGIS.

name: Convert SU 3D OBJ to 3D polygon
desc: The script converts a 3D OBJ file representing the top surface of an archaeological Stratigraphic Unit (SU) into two cleaned, attribute-enriched 3D polygon shapefiles: one in local coordinates (saved as 'SU_X_LC.shp') and one projected to EPSG:32632 (UTM zone 32N, saved as 'SU_X_EPSG_32632.shp'). It uses Blender (with BlenderGIS addon) in headless mode to import and export the geometry as POLYGONZ, then applies QGIS processing steps including geometry fixing, dissolving, hole deletion, coordinate translation (ΔX=452000, ΔY=4413000), projection assignment, and field calculation to add 'Year', 'Trench' (derived as floor(SU_number/1000)*1000), and 'SU' fields. The final projected shapefile is loaded into QGIS for verification.

name: Sample flood hazard raster values
desc: The script samples flood hazard raster layers (e.g., water surface level or inundation depth rasters) against a vector-based exposure inventory (finv) to generate exposure datasets ('expos'). It supports three sampling modes: (1) point-based direct raster value extraction using 'qgis:rastersampling'; (2) polygon/line-based global statistics (e.g., 'Max', 'Mean') via 'native:zonalstatisticsfb' or custom point-along-line + statistics-by-categories workflows; and (3) inundation area/percentage calculation for polygons or lines, requiring a DTM raster and depth threshold — which triggers on-the-fly depth raster generation ('top - bottom'), threshold masking, and zonal pixel counting. Outputs include a vector layer with added raster-derived attribute fields (named after input rasters), optionally saved as CSV, and optional histogram/boxplot visualizations of sampled values.

name: Calculate Volume from DEM Height Layers
desc: The script calculates earthwork volume (cut/fill) from DEM height layers for user-defined polygon areas. It supports multiple base level methods (min/average height, separate base DEM, manual constant) and volume counting options (above, below, subtract, etc.). Accurate volume estimation is performed by sampling heights at regular step sizes within each polygon and summing prism volumes. Results are written as new attributes to the polygon layer, and an optional normalized difference DEM (nDOM) raster is generated showing the height differences.

name: Compute fire risk hazard matrix
desc: The script computes a fire risk hazard matrix by combining two raster inputs (e.g., vegetation intensity and ignition/susceptibility layers) using a predefined combinatorial lookup table. Key methods include rasterization of vector features (e.g., vegetation codes), reclassification via searchsort mapping, categorical binning using user-defined bounds, morphological buffering, clipping by mask, reprojection, and aggregation of vegetation classes to intensity values. Outputs include a classified hazard raster (integer-coded risk levels 1–6), temporary GeoTIFFs, and optionally saved shapefiles — all processed within QGIS Processing Framework using GDAL and SciPy operations.

name: Calculate wildfire hazard probability
desc: The script computes wildfire hazard probability (P) per hazard class (1–12) by dividing the total burned pixels in each class by the product of class pixel count and number of years (len_years); it also supports rasterization, clipping, reprojection, slope/aspect calculation, distance mapping, vegetation code aggregation, susceptibility classification via quantiles, and hazard matrix combination of two categorical rasters (e.g., susceptibility × ignition). Outputs include probability rasters, clipped/reprojected rasters, slope/aspect layers, proximity rasters, reclassified vegetation/susceptibility maps, and hazard-classified rasters.

name: Wildfire risk assessment
desc: The script implements a wildfire risk assessment workflow by integrating vegetation type, susceptibility, slope, aspect, and distance-to-ignition-source layers. Key steps include rasterizing vegetation and ignition point vector layers, calculating topographic derivatives (slope and aspect), generating proximity (distance) rasters from ignition points, aggregating vegetation codes to intensity values, classifying susceptibility into quantile-based classes, combining susceptibility and vulnerability via a hazard matrix, applying sliding-window max/average filters for spatial aggregation, and reclassifying rasters using custom code mappings. Outputs include processed temporary rasters (e.g., buffered ignition masks, aggregated vegetation maps, classified susceptibility, hazard matrices) and shapefiles, all handled via QGIS Processing algorithms and GDAL/Numpy operations within a QGIS plugin context.

name: Create forest belts from DEM
desc: The script generates forest belt line features from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM). It first allows the user to interactively select points on the map to define an area, creates a buffered polygon, clips the DEM to that polygon, reprojects it to EPSG:3857, and extracts min/max elevations. Contour lines are then generated at an interval computed as h*j*tan(angle) (with h=15, j=20, angle=3°), filtered to the elevation range, and added to a QGIS memory layer named 'Forest Belts' with a categorized color ramp. The final layer is displayed in the current project.

name: Hierarchical contour-based point clustering
desc: The script performs hierarchical clustering of point features based on topographic containment derived from a digital elevation model (DEM). It first resamples the DEM and generates contour polygons with elevation intervals. Points inside each contour polygon are counted, and empty polygons are removed. Polygons are merged by ascending elevation levels, producing a hierarchical structure with parent‑child relationships between polygons. Each polygon records contained point IDs and child polygon IDs. The second function then assigns a cluster ID to each point by traversing the polygon hierarchy: starting from the highest‑level polygon containing the point, it recursively selects the closest child polygon until reaching a leaf, which becomes the point's cluster. The outputs are a polygon layer ('Изолинии') and a point layer with a 'cluster' field, both saved as GeoPackage files.

name: Merge river and stream vectors
desc: The script merges river and stream vector layers from OpenStreetMap data for a given spatial extent using QuickOSM. It first loads river (waterway=river) and stream (waterway=stream) layers, then merges them into a single layer, dissolves all features into a single multipart geometry, and finally splits into single-part features. The resulting merged river network layer is saved to a file and loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Rasterize water bodies and rivers
desc: The script builds a water mask raster by buffering river vectors, unioning them with water body polygons, clipping to the DEM extent, rasterizing at the DEM resolution (burn value 1), and warping to EPSG:3857.

name: Extract River Max Height Points
desc: The script processes river line vectors and a DEM to compute elevation at start and end points, calculate maximum height per line, and extract points representing the highest endpoint of each segment that is not shared. It merges and dissolves OSM-derived river and stream layers, and uses SAGA Fill Sinks to generate watershed basins. Outputs include a geodatabase of rivers with elevation attributes, a max height points layer, and a basins raster.

name: Extract slope and hillshade from DEM
desc: The script processes a digital elevation model (DEM) raster to generate three derivative rasters: slope in percent, slope in degrees, and hillshade. It uses GDAL's DEMProcessing function with 'slope' and 'hillshade' algorithms, computes edges, and applies specific output file paths. The resulting rasters are loaded into QGIS as layers named 'SLOPE (DEGREE)', 'SLOPE (PERCENT)', and 'HILLSHADE', with the percent-slope layer styled using a predefined QML style. A 10m USGS DEM is optionally loaded if the 1m DEM is not used.

name: Identify road-suitable slope points
desc: The script identifies candidate road alignment points based on slope values (in degrees) extracted from a precomputed slope raster (1820_SLOPE(DEGREE).tif), filters them into five slope ranges (0–24°, 24–32°, 32–40°, 40–45°, and 0–45°), writes each as point shapefiles, then excludes points within a 10-meter buffer of existing streams (1820_Streams-2225.shp) to generate a final 'GENERATED ROAD POINTS.shp' layer containing only slope-appropriate, stream-distant candidate road points.

name: Compute Canopy Height Model from LiDAR
desc: The script computes Canopy Height Model (CHM) from LiDAR-derived DSM and DTM by subtracting DTM from DSM using QGIS raster calculator. It supports multiple LiDAR campaigns, optional clipping to area of interest, removal of negative values, and max height thresholding. Outputs are CHM rasters saved in user-specified format and CRS, with optional merged clipped result.

name: Predict fire risk from climate and fuel data
desc: The script generates fire/no-fire point samples for British Columbia (2000–2001) by spatially clipping and reprojecting GRIB-based climate rasters (u10_wind, v10_wind, dew_temp_2m, temp_2m, tot_precip, lai_high) and a national fuel type raster (FBP Fueltypes 2014b) to EPSG:3347; it extracts monthly hotspot points from provincial fire records, generates matched random non-fire points within BC, merges and samples raster values at all points, filters out missing values, and exports cleaned, georeferenced CSVs per month — ultimately combining them into a single tabular dataset for fire risk modeling.

name: Prepare wildfire risk dataset
desc: The script is a QGIS processing workflow that prepares a spatially explicit dataset for wildfire risk prediction in British Columbia, Canada, from 2000 to 2024. It loads fire hotspot point data from shapefiles, clips them to the BC boundary, generates random non-fire points, merges fire and non-fire layers, and then samples pixel values from multi-band climate reanalysis rasters (wind components, temperature, precipitation, leaf area index) and a national fuel type raster. After cleaning features with missing values, the script exports monthly CSV files and a combined CSV for machine learning or risk modeling.

name: Preprocess mangrove potential spatial data
desc: The script provides QGIS utility functions for preprocessing spatial data in a mangrove potential mapping workflow. It initializes QGIS environment, sets up processing algorithms, and offers functions for raster reprojection, raster calculation, nodata filling, compression, vector rasterization, VRT clipping, extrapolation, and Voronoi polygon generation from GTSM points. These operations prepare input data for further analysis.

name: Apply direct fuzzifier to indicator raster
desc: The script applies a linear fuzzy membership transformation to a rasterized indicator layer, using min/max bounds retrieved from the 'Indicators' table in PostGIS. It first constructs a WKT polygon geometry, creates a grid over its extent, joins indicator point values to grid cells via nearest-neighbor, rasterizes the joined grid, applies either direct (min→low, max→high) or inverse (min→high, max→low) linear fuzzification using QGIS's 'fuzzifyrasterlinearmembership', converts the fuzzy raster back to points, appends the indicator_id, and exports the resulting fuzzy points to the 'fuzzy_view' table in PostGIS.

name: Convert raster pixels to point features
desc: The script converts a raster input layer into point vector features, reprojects it to EPSG:3857, clips it to a user-provided polygon study area, adds a static integer field 'project_indicator_id' (supplied as a parameter) to each point, and exports the resulting point layer to a PostGIS table named 'pixels' in the 'public' schema of the 'integral' database. The output is not a new raster or statistical summary but a persisted spatial table of pixel centroids with indicator metadata.

name: Convert raster pixels to point features
desc: The script converts an input raster layer into vector point features where each pixel becomes a point with its value stored in a 'VALUE' attribute; it then adds an 'indicator_id' field with a user-provided integer value and exports the resulting point layer to a PostGIS table named 'pixels' in the 'integral' database under schema 'public', updating the 'Indicators' table with min/max value statistics and a randomly selected palette code for that indicator_id.

name: QGIS Raster and Vector Processing Utilities
desc: The script defines a reusable QGISTools class containing static methods that wrap common QGIS processing algorithms for raster and vector data manipulation. Methods include clipping rasters by mask layer, polygonizing rasters, reprojecting rasters and vectors, raster calculator (including weighted average), extracting raster extents, vector difference, zonal statistics, rasterizing polygons, merging rasters, fixing geometries, dissolving, creating grids, clipping rasters by extent, and deleting holes. These methods leverage the QGIS processing framework (native and GDAL providers) and save outputs to specified file paths. The script serves as a modular geoprocessing library for building QGIS workflows.

name: Calculate renewable opportunity area statistics
desc: The script computes area statistics for renewable energy opportunity maps by intersecting the 'Opportunities' polygon layer with a user-selected area layer (e.g., administrative boundaries). It dissolves the selected opportunity features, clips the area layer with the dissolved layer, calculates the overlapping area and percentage, and applies a land exclusion factor. Results are displayed as a formatted HTML summary in the plugin's dock widget. Additionally, it provides an AHP tool to calculate weightings for criteria layers, supporting multi-criteria decision analysis for renewable energy siting.

name: Generate solar PV panels and estimate energy output
desc: The script is part of a QGIS plugin for assessing renewable energy deployment in cities. It provides tools to configure PV module parameters (from an Excel model or manual input), generate PV panel geometries over available land areas (opportunities) using either automatic optimization (based on weather data and the PV model) or custom user settings, and calculate energy output per panel and aggregated statistics. It also includes a function to generate north- or south-facing suitable sites using DSM-based aspect reclassification and intersection with building sites. Outputs include vector layers of PV panels (with tilt angle, orientation, energy, inter-row spacing) and summary reports in the plugin's interface.

name: Extract Monthly Climate Rasters for BC
desc: The script extracts monthly climate data from GRIB files covering years 2000-2024 for British Columbia. It iterates through each month, selects all raster bands matching the target month and year (adjusting for cumulative precipitation), merges them into a multi-band GeoTIFF, clips to the BC boundary, reprojects to EPSG:3347, and fills NoData gaps using the gdal:fillnodata tool. The filled single-band rasters are then stacked into a final multi-band raster per month, producing a time series of preprocessed climate rasters ready for analysis.

name: Wildfire prediction point sampling
desc: The script prepares a point dataset for wildfire prediction in British Columbia from 2000 to 2024. It extracts monthly fire hotspot point locations, generates corresponding random non-fire points within the BC boundary, reprojects all layers to EPSG:3347, clips fuel type and climate rasters to the province, and samples climate variables (wind, temperature, precipitation, etc.) and fuel type at each point. The final output is a merged CSV file combining all months with fire/non-fire labels and environmental attributes for model training.

name: Delineate catchment areas for points
desc: The script calculates upslope catchment areas for a set of input points using a DEM. For each point, the SAGA Upslope Area algorithm creates a catchment raster, which is then polygonized (gdal:polygonize) and filtered to keep the catchment polygon (DN=100). Results are written as GeoPackage or Shapefile and can be loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Multiple Basin Delineation from DEM and Points
desc: The script delineates multiple watershed basins from a digital elevation model (DEM) and a set of input point locations. It first generates a stream network using GRASS GIS algorithms based on a flow accumulation threshold and applies smoothing. Input points are snapped to the nearest stream segment. Then, for each snapped pour point, watershed basins are delineated using GRASS r.water.outlet, converted to vector polygons, and smoothed. Basins are filtered to retain the largest polygon if multiple result. Drainage areas are calculated in square miles and square meters. The script outputs a global stream network with Strahler and Shreve stream orders, snapped pour points, watershed basin polygons with drainage area attributes, and basin-specific clipped stream networks.

name: Optimized Parcel Division
desc: The script divides input polygons (parcels) into smaller polygons based on a specified lot width. It first separates regular (rectangular) and irregular polygons; for irregular ones, it computes oriented minimum bounding boxes. It generates horizontal division lines connecting the midpoints of the two shortest sides of each bounding box, and perpendicular lines at intervals matching the lot width. These lines are extended, clipped to the original parcel extents, and used to split the polygons. After splitting, two passes of merging small polygons below a threshold size (based on average area and merge threshold percentage) remove slivers. The output is a new polygon layer containing the divided parcels.

name: Generate tree planting points
desc: The script generates tree planting points with different patterns (triangular, rectangular, five of diamonds, keyline, random) inside polygon features, optionally using a DEM for slope analysis. It calculates plant counts, produces a comprehensive report, and outputs a point layer with fields for id, pattern, x, y, and slope.

name: Watershed Basin Delineation with Strahler Orders
desc: The script delineates a watershed basin from a DEM and a user-specified pour point. It resamples the DEM if too large, fills sinks using r.fill.dir, computes flow accumulation and drainage direction with r.watershed, then extracts the basin with r.water.outlet. The basin is converted to polygon, smoothed, and used to clip an input stream network. Strahler stream orders are calculated in three stages: standard (sthr_original), extended along longest paths (sthr_extend), and main channel to headwaters (sthr_final). An optional longest flow path from the basin boundary to the outlet is computed using r.drain, intersected with the stream network, and topologically merged.

name: Stream Network Extraction and Ordering
desc: The script generates a stream network from a DEM, smooths the lines, and calculates Strahler and Shreve stream orders. It first checks DEM size, resamples if necessary using GDAL Warp. Then it runs GRASS r.fill.dir to fill sinks, r.watershed for flow accumulation, r.stream.extract to extract streams with user-defined threshold, native:smoothgeometry for smoothing, and custom algorithms to assign Strahler and Shreve orders based on upstream/downstream connectivity. Output is a line vector layer with order attributes.

name: Valley floor delineation via cost-distance
desc: The script delineates valley floor polygons from a DEM and river network using a cost-distance approach. It first computes slope from the DEM, conditions it by multiplying with pixel size, and uses it as the cost surface for GRASS r.cost, starting from the river network. An initial user-defined cost threshold creates a coarse mask, then the mean cost within that mask is used to refine the mask. The refined mask is polygonized and post-processed with hole deletion, smoothing, and gap-filling buffer operations to produce the final valley floor polygon.

name: Create valley boundary
desc: Subtracts valley floor polygons from microsheds that intersect the valley floor, then converts the resulting difference polygons to lines, smooths, and dissolves to produce a single valley boundary line layer.

name: Generate microsheds
desc: The script generates microsheds (watershed basins) from a DEM using GRASS r.watershed with a user-provided flow accumulation threshold. It takes an input DEM, a threshold cell count, and GRASS memory allocation; runs GRASS r.watershed to produce a uniquely labeled basins raster, then optionally polygonizes the raster to create a vector layer of microshed polygons. Outputs include the basins raster and an optional microsheds polygon layer.

name: Calculate watershed morphometric parameters
desc: The script performs morphometric watershed analysis using a DEM. It first delineates watersheds using r.watershed based on a minimum basin area threshold. Then it computes basic elevation statistics (max, min, mean) and mean slope via zonal statistics. An extended workflow (cuencaIndex) also calculates morphometric indices (area, perimeter, relief, compactness factor, circularity, Melton’s ruggedness number, total channel length, drainage density) using SAGA channel network extraction and field calculators. The final output is a vector layer (GPKG) with watershed polygons and attribute columns for each calculated parameter.

name: Hydrologically condition DEM
desc: The script performs hydrological conditioning of a digital elevation model (DEM) by optionally resampling it, carving stream networks using blue-line vector data (with user-defined depth), and inserting artificial walls (barriers) using wall vector data. It then computes flow accumulation and extracts stream networks based on a user-specified threshold in km², converted to cell count using the DEM's ground resolution. Outputs include: (1) raw DEM (_DEMraw.tif), (2) conditioned DEM (_DEMconditioned.tif), and (3) extracted stream raster (_streams.tif). All operations use GRASS GIS and GDAL algorithms within QGIS Processing Framework.

name: Compute hydrological derivatives
desc: This script processes a conditioned DEM and raw DEM to produce hydrological derivatives for the Continuum model. It uses GRASS GIS r.watershed to compute flow accumulation and drainage pointers, then converts drainage into the HMC pointer format. Masked outputs are produced if an outlet section is provided. A stream network is defined from a user-supplied threshold (km²), and alpha and beta angles describing flow direction and channel slope are computed through a custom iterative routine. Additional rasters for latitude, longitude, and cell area are generated. All outputs are exported as ASCII grids (domain.*.txt) for ingestion into the Continuum hydrological model.

name: Buildable area constraint analysis
desc: This PyQGIS script generates a buildable envelope by excluding setback zones, steep slopes (>35° default), and high-flow drainage corridors from a parcel boundary. It expects a polygon boundary and rasters of slope (degrees) and flow accumulation, applies interior buffering, reclassifies raster values, polygonizes steep/drainage areas, and subtracts all exclusion polygons from the interior area to produce a final buildable envelope GeoPackage, alongside individual constraint layers and area statistics.

name: Calculate terrain suitability scores
desc: The script calculates terrain suitability scores for building placement on Koh Phangan by reclassifying slope into suitability based on steepness thresholds, scoring aspect according to compass directions (favoring south/southwest), measuring access distance from roads, and assessing drainage safety from flow accumulation or slope proxy. These individual scores are combined using weighted sums (40% slope, 20% each for view, access, drainage) to produce a final 0-100 suitability raster, with outputs as individual and combined rasters.

name: Identify buildable envelope
desc: The script analyzes terrain and boundary constraints to determine buildable areas for villa layout. It applies setback buffers from parcel boundaries, excludes steep slopes (>35° default) and drainage corridors, and generates a final buildable envelope polygon. Outputs include setback zones, steep slopes excluded, drainage corridors, and the buildable envelope in GeoPackage format.

name: Calculate building site suitability scores
desc: The script calculates terrain suitability for building villa placements by scoring slope (0-100), view orientation (0-100), access distance (0-100), and drainage safety (0-100) from input DEM-derived rasters. It combines them with weights (40%, 20%, 20%, 20%) into a final 0-100 suitability raster, with distribution validation.

name: Calculate terrain slope and aspect
desc: The script calculates terrain derivatives including slope (degrees), aspect (compass direction), drainage flow accumulation, and hillshade from a DTM raster using QGIS processing algorithms. The outputs are saved as GeoTIFF files and serve as inputs for further scoring in a villa layout planning tool.

name: Contour enhancement for presentation
desc: This script generates professional topographic contour maps from a DEM or existing vector contours. It applies smoothing, classifies index and intermediate contours based on elevation interval, styles them with distinct colors and line widths, and adds curved labels with buffer for readability. A print layout is automatically created with a coordinate grid, legend, scale bar, north arrow, and project metadata sidebar. Exports include high-resolution PNG and PDF maps, a text report, and JSON statistics.

name: DEM Terrain Analysis
desc: The script processes a DEM to derive terrain attributes including slope, aspect, and multi-directional hillshades. It first reprojects the DEM to UTM zone 47N, optionally clips to a site boundary, then computes slope (raw and classified) and aspect using GDAL and QGIS processing tools. Four hillshade layers are generated from different illumination directions. The results are loaded into QGIS with hypsometric and classification styling, and a professional print layout is created and exported as PDF and PNG.

name: QGIS workflow: Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data import
desc: This workflow contains 32 core geospatial operations, including Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data import, Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Data export. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Generate terrain analysis products
desc: This QGIS script automatically detects DEM and optional boundary/road/orthomosaic files in a project folder, then computes terrain derivatives: slope (degrees), aspect, hillshade (315° azimuth, 45° altitude), and flow accumulation via GRASS r.watershed. Results are saved to an output directory and loaded into the map canvas for visual inspection.

name: Calculate terrain attributes for villa planning
desc: The script automates preprocessing for a villa layout generator. It first prompts the user to select a parcel boundary polygon, a DTM raster, optional orthomosaic and road access line, and loads building regulations from a JSON file or dialog. It validates these inputs for geometry type, feature count, CRS, and required parameters. Then, using QGIS processing, it calculates slope in degrees, aspect (compass direction), flow accumulation (drainage corridors), and a hillshade from the DTM. All derived rasters are saved as GeoTIFFs in a specified output directory for later site suitability scoring and villa placement.

name: Create Koh Phangan terrain base dataset
desc: The script processes AW3D30 DEM (30m) for Koh Phangan island, Thailand, to produce a comprehensive terrain base dataset in UTM Zone 47N. It reprojects the DEM, generates four multi-angle hillshades, calculates slope (in degrees and classified into five categories), aspect, contour lines at 10m intervals, and performs hydrological analysis including D8 flow direction and accumulation (via NumPy), stream network extraction (threshold-based), and optionally watershed delineation. Outputs are saved in a structured folder with styling for QGIS, and optional client AOI clips are created.

name: Slope classification and map production
desc: The script performs slope analysis on a DEM to calculate slope in degrees, reclassifies into five LandWise categories (0-5°, 5-15°, 15-25°, 25-35°, 35°+), generates a hillshade, applies professional styling, creates a print layout with title, scale bar, north arrow, and legend, and exports high-resolution PNG and PDF maps along with statistical reports.

name: QGIS workflow: Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing
desc: This workflow contains 37 core geospatial operations, including Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data import, Data export. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Generate catchments and streams from DEM
desc: The script processes a digital elevation model (DEM) to generate stream lines with Strahler and Shreve stream orders, catchment polygons linked to streams, and dissolved network polygons. It fills depressions, computes flow accumulation, extracts streams above a threshold, and converts basins to polygons using GRASS algorithms. Custom code then calculates stream orders by traversing upstream/downstream segments. Catchments are joined to streams by location, and networks are created by dissolving on network identifier. Output layers are styled with Viridis graduated symbology for streams, categorized colors for catchments, and labeled blue outlines for networks.

name: Detect ponds from DEM
desc: The script identifies pond depressions in a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) by filling sinks, calculating a pond depth raster (filled minus original), applying user-specified minimum depth and area thresholds, and polygonizing the valid depth areas. It then computes zonal statistics to derive attributes such as maximum and minimum elevation (PONDRLmax, PONDRLmin), pond volume, area, and depth statistics. The final output includes a vector layer of pond polygons with associated labels, as well as optionally generated intermediate rasters (filled DEM, pond depth, and thresholded depth raster).

name: Retrieve and export machine tracking data
desc: The script is a QGIS plugin for retrieving, processing, and exporting machine GPS tracking data. It allows the user to fetch machine tracking points from a remote server (via Recup_data.dll) and from local SQLite databases. Users can filter by project (chantier), date range, and machine. The workflow includes selecting machines from a tree, building queries with parameters, and exporting points as GPX files or creating merged shapefile layers (points, lines, polygons) with optional processing steps: applying a processing width, gap elimination, road splitting, pause and speed analysis. Additionally, the tool updates a GeoPackage with track data from local databases, deduplicating by timestamp, and reprojects to a chosen CRS. Output layers are displayed in QGIS.

name: Delineate watershed and flow path
desc: The script performs hydrological analysis for culvert sizing by delineating the watershed and flow path for a user-specified pour point. It downloads digital elevation models (MRNF LiDAR and NRCan CDEM), ancillary vector data (CanVec hydrography and elevation contours), and surface deposits (WFS). The core processing uses GRASS7 algorithms (r.fill.dir, r.watershed, r.water.outlet, r.drain) or WhiteboxTools as fallback to generate filled DEM, flow direction, flow accumulation, watershed boundary, and flow path. It calculates watershed area, stream length, elevation statistics, average slope, and 85-10 slope. Results are added as map layers in QGIS, including the watershed polygon, flow path line, and pour point.

name: Process machine GPS tracking data
desc: The script provides a GUI for retrieving and processing GPS tracking data from construction machinery, performing spatial analysis such as distance filtering, road splitting, and gap handling, and exporting results as shapefiles (points, lines, polygons) and GPX tracks.

name: Delineate machinery production activity zones
desc: The script processes GPS tracking points from a SQLite database to delineate agricultural machinery production activity zones. It first filters points by minimum distance and classifies them as 'Production', 'Traction', or 'Pause' based on speed and time intervals, then connects successive production points into lines, buffers them, dissolves overlapping buffers, removes small holes, and exports the resulting polygons with area calculations.

name: Generate production zone polygons from GPS
desc: The script processes GPS point data from a SQLite database to create polygon layers representing machine working zones. It reads points with latitude, longitude, and timestamp, filters them by spatial distance (minimum 10m between consecutive points), calculates speed and time intervals, and classifies each point as Production, Traction, or Pause based on configurable thresholds. Then it builds line strings from consecutive Production points within a distance limit, buffers the lines, deletes small interior holes, and optionally subtracts road buffers if a road layer and cutting option are enabled. The final output includes shapefiles of the lines, buffered polygons, and cleaned polygon layers with attributes for machine name and area in hectares.

name: Compute parcel flow connectivity matrix
desc: The script computes parcel-to-parcel surface water flow connectivity by downloading and processing elevation data from the USGS National Elevation Dataset (NED). It buffers parcel boundaries, clips a DEM, fills depressions using GRASS r.fill.stats, runs r.watershed to derive flow accumulation and direction, then analyzes flow at parcel boundary points to determine how much flow goes from each parcel to neighbors or to a sink, producing raw and percent flow matrices saved as CSV files.

name: Calculate area-weighted R factor for parcels
desc: The script computes the area-weighted rainfall erosivity (R factor) for each parcel in a shapefile by intersecting climate zone polygons, generating random points within each intersected piece, obtaining point-specific R values from a USLE climate API (UsleClimateApi.get_r_value), and aggregating per parcel using grouped sum of area-weighted R. The output is a JSON of summed area-weighted R values per parcel.

name: Compute area-weighted R-factor for parcels
desc: The script calculates the area-weighted rainfall erosivity factor (R-factor) for agricultural parcels using RUSLE methodology. It processes parcel and climate boundary shapefiles through a QGIS workflow: fixing geometries, reprojecting to Albers Equal Area, computing areas, intersecting parcels with climate zones, calculating area overlap percentages, generating random points within intersections, retrieving R-values per point via a climate API, and aggregating weighted R-factors by parcel ID. The output is a JSON summary of R-factor per parcel.

name: Generate Hachure Points
desc: The script generates a vector point layer from a DEM to support monochrome hachure mapping. It first creates contours at a user-defined interval, then computes slope and aspect rasters from the DEM. Points are placed along the contour lines at the specified spacing, and slope/aspect values are sampled at each point. The output points include fields for elevation, contour angle, aspect_1, and slope_1. This layer is designed to be styled with a geometry generator that draws hachure lines perpendicular to contours, with opacity based on aspect (simulating sun illumination) and line length based on slope.

name: Align thematic borders to reference data
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm aligns thematic vector borders to reference borders using a configurable alignment process. It loads thematic and reference data, optionally downloads reference on-the-fly (GRB parcels, cadastral data, OSM, etc.), applies a border alignment engine (brdr) with parameters like open domain strategy, snap strategy, threshold overlap percentage, and relevant distance. The algorithm can use prediction mode to evaluate multiple distances and automatically select the best alignment. Outputs include an aligned result layer, difference layers (diff, diff_plus, diff_min), and a correction layer highlighting changes beyond a review percentage.

name: Reconcile thematic geometries to reference
desc: The script provides utility functions for a QGIS plugin (brdrQ) that aligns thematic vector geometries (e.g., building footprints, parcels) with authoritative reference datasets (such as GRB in Belgium or BRK in the Netherlands). It supports multiple boundary reconciliation processors, generates correction layers with status flags (auto-updated, to-review), and visualizes alignment differences. The workflow involves preparing thematic data, buffering to select relevant reference data, applying a chosen alignment algorithm, and saving results to GeoPackage. Outputs include modified geometries and attribute fields indicating the alignment status and differences.

name: Generate hillshade from clipped DEM
desc: The script clips an SRTM digital elevation model using a shoreline mask shapefile and then generates a hillshade raster from the clipped DEM. It first runs the GDAL Clip raster by mask layer algorithm with crop to cutline enabled, then uses the QGIS native hillshade algorithm with azimuth 300 and vertical angle 40. The final output is saved as hillshade_clipped.tif.

name: Calculate zonal elevation statistics for seismic zones
desc: The script computes zonal statistics (mean) of SRTM elevation for each seismic zone polygon. It first fixes invalid geometries in the seismic zones shapefile using the Fix Geometries algorithm, then uses Zonal Statistics (with statistics option 2, presumably mean) to aggregate the SRTM raster band 1 values within each zone, outputting a memory layer with the prefix '_' added columns.

name: Extract NDVI vegetation pixels
desc: The script extracts NDVI values only for pixels classified as vegetation (classes 4 or 5) from an input NDVI raster, using a band stack ('A') to derive land cover class labels and applying a conditional expression ('IF ("A@3"=4 OR "A@3"=5, "B@1", 0/0)') where 'A@3' refers to the third band of the 'bands' raster (assumed land cover classification) and 'B@1' refers to the first band of the 'ndvi' raster (assumed NDVI layer). It then selects a single plot by ID attribute, buffers it inward by 10 units, and computes zonal statistics (count, mean, std dev) of the filtered NDVI raster over the buffered plot geometry. The output is a vector layer (shapefile) with added attributes containing these statistics.

name: Extract NDVI vegetation statistics for plot
desc: The script processes a list of JSON configuration objects to extract NDVI-based vegetation statistics (count, mean, standard deviation) for a user-specified plot ID within an input vector layer (plots). It first selects the target plot by attribute value, buffers it inward by 10 units (negative buffer), calculates a masked NDVI raster where only pixels with band A@3 values equal to 4 or 5 are retained (else NoData), and then computes zonal statistics of that NDVI raster over the buffered plot geometry. The final output is a shapefile containing the original plot geometry augmented with NDVI statistics fields (e.g., 'mean', 'std'), written to the path specified in the JSON's OUTPUTS section.

name: QGIS workflow: Data processing, Vector data attribute editing
desc: This workflow contains 94 core geospatial operations, including Data processing, Vector data attribute editing, Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Forest area delineation from CHM
desc: The script converts a Canopy Height Model (CHM) to forest/non-forest binary raster and vector polygons using a user-defined height threshold, minimum cover density, minimum area, and minimum width. It performs morphological filtering (closing and opening) to connect forest patches and remove small gaps, then removes areas below the minimum size constraint. Optional user-provided forest and non-forest masks are integrated to refine the output. The result is a forest area raster and optionally vectorized polygons with area calculation.

name: Extract pavement edge vertices by tiles
desc: The script processes a vector layer named 'PAVEMENT_EDGE' by first generating a coarse grid of 2500x2500 ft cells (EPSG:2263) over a specified extent. It then intersects the pavement edge layer with each grid cell, extracts the vertices of the resulting intersection geometries, and exports the vertex coordinates to CSV files named by grid indices (i_j.csv). This produces tile-based extraction of pavement edge points for further analysis or tiling workflows.

name: Simplify drone flight waypoints
desc: The script simplifies a drone flight path defined in a CSV file by reducing the number of waypoints while preserving 3D trajectory fidelity relative to a DEM. It loads CSV points (with longitude, latitude, altitude(m)), samples elevation values from a user-provided DEM raster, reprojects the points to a projected CRS, converts them into a line ordered by 'original_index', simplifies that line using Douglas-Peucker tolerance, extracts vertices of the simplified line, buffers those vertices, joins original reprojected points to the buffers to identify which original points fall within the simplified geometry’s vicinity, and finally filters the input CSV to retain only rows corresponding to those retained indices. Outputs include a simplified CSV file compatible with Litchi, optionally added as a point layer; a trajectory line layer with arrow styling; and original CSV points layer — all configurable via boolean parameters.

name: Calculate linear project impact percentage
desc: The script computes the percentage of area impacted by linear infrastructure projects (e.g., roads, pipelines) after sequentially excluding buffered zones around BAEA nests (804 m), BUOWL habitats (300 m), raptor nests (402 m), and GBH rookeries (no buffer — direct overlay). It first buffers each sensitive feature layer, then performs a series of geometric differences to isolate the portion of the linear project buffer not overlapping any protected or sensitive areas. Area (in ha) is calculated for the original linear buffer and the final non-overlapping polygon; impact area is derived as the difference, and impact percentage is computed as (impact_ha / original_area_ha) × 100. The output is a vector layer with an 'impact_pct' attribute.

name: Convert DXF boundary lines to polygons
desc: The script processes DXF line files from a specified directory, selects features with layer attribute 'LIMIT' or 'LIMITS', filters for LineString or LineStringZ geometry types, converts selected lines to polygons using QGIS 'linestopolygons' tool, and merges them into a single GPKG file.

name: Generate boxplot of raster pixel values
desc: The script generates a boxplot of raster pixel values from a user-selected raster layer within QGIS. It clips the selected raster to either the map canvas extent or a selected feature from an active vector layer, converts the resulting raster pixels to points, extracts the band 1 values, and plots their distribution using matplotlib.

name: Generate sampling strata polygons
desc: The script provides an interface to delineate strata polygons within a user-selected sampling area in QGIS. It supports three methods: drawing freehand lines, placing points for Voronoi tessellation, and drawing polylines with optional horizontal/vertical constraints. Input geometries are combined with the boundary of the sampling area, polygonized, and clipped to the sampling area. Resulting strata polygons are assigned an ID, a strata name, and area (in square meters) and saved as a shapefile. The shapefile is added to the QGIS project.

name: Analyze cattle GPS movement and water distance
desc: The script processes GPS collar data for cattle in a specific paddock. It clips GPS points to the paddock boundary buffered by 100 m, adds datetime and date fields, calculates distance to the nearest water point within the paddock, and exports the results to a GeoPackage and an Excel spreadsheet. It also computes daily movement track statistics, producing additional GeoPackage and Excel outputs. The analysis uses custom QGIS processing algorithms for datetime conversion, distance-to-water computation, and daily movement statistics.

name: Calculate GPS collar distance to water and daily movement
desc: The script processes a GPS collar CSV file by clipping points to a buffered paddock boundary, adding datetime and date fields, computing distance to the nearest water point within the paddock, and generating daily movement statistics including distance traveled. Outputs include a GeoPackage with points and distance fields, and spreadsheets with results.

name: Ant GPS collar movement and water distance processing
desc: The script processes a single GPS collar CSV file from an ant tracking study. It clips the points to a buffered paddock polygon ('No_4_plus_100_asymmetrical'), adds a QDateTime field and a separate Date field, then computes distance to the nearest water point in the paddock using the 'ANT_waters_plus_waterholes' layer clipped to paddock 'No_4'. The result is saved as a GeoPackage. Daily movement statistics are calculated with the 'dailymovementstats' algorithm, producing another GeoPackage containing daily tracks and an associated XLSX spreadsheet. The outputs also include an XLSX spreadsheet of the distance-to-water points.

name: Compute ant distance to water and daily movement
desc: The script processes GPS collar data of ants (collar No.4, ID 1123) from a CSV file. It clips points to a buffered paddock polygon, adds date-time and date fields, computes distance to water points, exports to GeoPackage and Excel, and calculates daily movement statistics. Outputs include a distance-to-water GeoPackage, an Excel spreadsheet, and daily track files.

name: Calculate collar distance to water and daily movement
desc: The script processes GPS collar data from a CSV file to compute distance to water and daily movement statistics for a specific animal within a paddock. It clips points to a buffered paddock boundary, adds date/time fields, calculates nearest water point distance using the 'ditt-lid:adddist2water' algorithm, exports results to GeoPackage and Excel, and finally runs the 'ditt-lid:dailymovementstats' algorithm to produce daily tracks as GeoPackage and spreadsheet.

name: Process GPS collar daily movement stats
desc: The script processes GPS collar data for a specific paddock (No5 West). It reads a CSV file of collar locations, clips points to a buffered paddock boundary, adds datetime and date fields, calculates distance to the nearest water point, and outputs a GeoPackage with distance-to-water attributes. It then generates daily movement statistics (distance traveled, duration) and saves results as GeoPackage and Excel files.

name: Clip GPS points to paddock boundaries
desc: The script batch processes CSV files containing GPS point data with longitude and latitude fields, clips each set of points to the Rocklands paddocks polygon layer, and saves the clipped features as individual GeoPackage files in a heatmap_points folder. It then adds the resulting layers to the QGIS map canvas.

name: Compute maximum distance to water per paddock
desc: For each paddock in the Mt_Sanford_Paddocks layer, this script selects intersecting waterpoints from Mt_Sanford_Waterpoints, rasterizes them to a binary raster (1 at water locations), calculates Euclidean distance using GDAL proximity, clips the distance raster to the paddock boundary, and saves the resulting proximity raster as a GeoTIFF named after the paddock in the specified output directory.

name: Compute home range pasture attribute statistics using Cibo TC and TSDM
desc: The script calculates zonal statistics (median, min, max) of Cibo Tree Cover (TC) and Total Standing Dry Matter (TSDM) rasters within livestock home range polygons (50%, 75%, 95% levels) and entire paddock boundaries for each month of GPS collar data. It dissolves home range polygons by percentage category, runs zonal statistics, and writes a CSV table with summary statistics for each paddock, month, and raster type.

name: Calculate maximum distance to water
desc: The script calculates, for each input paddock polygon, the maximum Euclidean distance (in meters) from any point within the paddock to the nearest water point. It does so by: (1) harmonizing CRS between paddock and water point layers (transforming geographic layers to EPSG:9473 if both are geographic, or aligning one to the other’s projected CRS); (2) for each paddock containing ≥1 water point, creating a temporary point layer of intersecting water points; (3) rasterizing those points at user-defined resolution (burn value = 1); (4) computing a GDAL proximity raster (distance in map units); (5) clipping the proximity raster to the paddock geometry; (6) extracting the maximum pixel value (i.e., max distance to water) from the clipped raster; and (7) optionally generating a spreadsheet report listing paddock name, area (ha), water point count, and max distance (km), plus styling and loading proximity rasters with a gradient renderer scaled to the global maximum distance across all paddocks.

name: Calculate maximum distance to water points within paddocks
desc: The script computes, for each input paddock polygon containing at least one water point, a clipped proximity raster where pixel values represent Euclidean distance (in map units) from each location to the nearest water point. It outputs one GeoTIFF file per qualifying paddock, named after the paddock’s name field value, containing the clipped proximity surface bounded by the paddock geometry.

name: Calculate maximum distance to water points
desc: The script computes, for each input paddock polygon, the maximum Euclidean distance from any location within the paddock boundary to the nearest water point. It achieves this by (1) spatially intersecting water points with each paddock, (2) rasterizing those water points at 25 m resolution within the paddock’s bounding box, (3) computing a GDAL proximity raster (distance-to-nearest-1 pixel), and (4) clipping that proximity raster to the exact paddock geometry. The final output is a set of clipped GeoTIFF files—one per paddock—where pixel values represent distance (in map units) to the nearest water point, enabling extraction of the maximum distance per paddock (e.g., via zonal statistics).

name: Calculate maximum distance to water
desc: The script calculates, for each paddock polygon, the maximum Euclidean distance from any location within that paddock to the nearest water point. It does so by: (1) harmonizing coordinate reference systems between paddock and water point layers; (2) for each paddock, extracting only the water points that intersect it; (3) rasterizing those water points into a binary raster (value 1 at water locations); (4) computing a GDAL proximity raster (distance in map units to nearest pixel with value 1); and (5) clipping the proximity raster to the paddock boundary. The output is a set of clipped proximity rasters — one per paddock containing at least one water point — saved as GeoTIFF files named after the paddock (e.g., 'PaddockA.tif'), where pixel values represent distance in the CRS units (e.g., meters). No aggregation or summary statistics (e.g., max value extraction) is performed beyond raster generation; the rasters themselves are the final outputs.

name: Calculate maximum distance to water
desc: The script calculates the maximum Euclidean distance from any point within each input paddock polygon to the nearest water point, producing a clipped proximity raster per paddock (in meters) and an optional Excel report listing paddock name, area (ha), number of water points, and maximum distance to water (km). It handles CRS alignment between inputs: if one layer is geographic and the other projected, it reprojects the geographic layer to match; if both are geographic, it transforms both to EPSG:9473 (GDA2020/Australian Albers); if both are projected but differ, it reprojects water points to paddock CRS. Rasterization uses GDAL’s rasterize to create binary water-point rasters, GDAL’s proximity tool computes distance rasters, and GDAL’s cliprasterbymasklayer clips each proximity raster to its corresponding paddock boundary.

name: Extract land type areas for paddocks
desc: The script extracts land type areas for each paddock by intersecting an input land types polygon layer with a paddocks polygon layer. It dissolves land types by a unique map unit field, computes intersection geometries, calculates area (planar or ellipsoidal) in square meters, hectares, square kilometers, and percentage of paddock area, and saves the results as a vector layer. Optionally, it also computes whole-property land types by dissolving all paddocks.

name: Extract land type areas for property and paddocks
desc: The script processes a land types polygon layer, a paddock boundary layer, and optional water points to compute intersection areas of each land type within whole property (if selected), individual paddocks, and optionally within 3km and/or 5km buffer zones around water points. It calculates area in m², ha, km², and percentage relative to the parent feature using either ellipsoidal or planar measurement. Outputs are saved as vector polygons in formats like gpkg or shp, with attributes including the unique land type identifier, area measures, and percent, and can be loaded into the map.

name: Extract land type areas
desc: The script extracts and calculates areas of land systems or units (e.g., land types) within property paddocks, optionally for the whole property (dissolved paddocks) and/or watered areas (3km and/or 5km buffers around waterpoints). It performs spatial intersection and area calculation (ellipsoidal or planar), dissolves land types by a unique unit field, transforms CRS based on input paddock layer (to EPSG:9473 if geographic), and outputs vector layers per analysis scope (property, paddock, watered area) with attributes including area in m², ha, km², and percent. An optional Excel summary report aggregates all output layers.

name: Random point TIN interpolation
desc: The script generates a raster surface via TIN interpolation from random points created inside input polygons. It first creates random points within a polygon layer, then assigns each point a random value between 1 and 100 using field calculator, and finally runs the TIN interpolation algorithm over a fixed extent (EPSG:4326) to produce a continuous raster output.

name: Calculate pastoral property burnt percentage
desc: The script calculates the percentage burnt for each pastoral property in the Northern Territory using firescar data from the NAFI firescar to date shapefile (fs2023shp) for months August to November. It performs geometry fixing, clipping to buffered NT boundary, reprojection to EPSG:9473, clipping to pastoral properties, extraction by month expression, dissolving, overlap calculation, and adds area in km2 and percent burnt fields. Results are saved as geopackages and a spreadsheet.

name: Calculate pastoral property burnt percentage
desc: The script calculates the percentage of each pastoral property burnt by fires from January to June 2024 using NAFI firescar polygon data. It fixes geometries, clips firescars to a buffered NT boundary, reprojects to EPSG:9473, clips to pastoral properties, extracts fires from months 1-6, dissolves them, checks area consistency, computes vector overlaps between properties and firescars, adds area burnt in km2 and percentage burnt fields, and exports results as a geopackage and an Excel spreadsheet.

name: Calculate pastoral property percent burnt
desc: This script calculates percentage burnt for each pastoral property from NAFI firescars to date shapefile via multiple processing steps. Firescar geometries are fixed, then clipped to a buffered NT boundary, reprojected to epsg:9473 to match the property layer and clipped to the pastoral properties. Firescar features are then extracted for relevant months and dissolved (areas checked pre/post dissolve). Overlap analysis is run for firescars & properties and fields are added for rounded area in km2 and rounded percent. Finally, the result is saved to a spreadsheet. Some intermediate result layers are also saved as geopackages.

name: Calculate waterpoint proximity in paddocks
desc: The script computes distance to waterpoints for each paddock in the Mulga Park area using QGIS processing. It reprojects waterpoint points to UTM Zone 52, rasterizes them into a binary raster, applies a proximity distance algorithm, and clips the resulting distance raster to each paddock boundary. The processed layers are loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Summarize TSDM pixel counts by pastoral district
desc: Creates an Excel workbook with two sheets: (1) counts and percentages of pixels in 'low', 'low-moderate', 'moderate', and 'high' TSDM biomass classes—using region-specific thresholds ('Northern' [0,1000,2000,3000] or 'Southern' [0,250,500,1000]) per pastoral district; and (2) counts and percentages of pixels in 'below average' (0–30), 'average' (31–70), and 'above average' (71–100) TSDM percentile classes per district. Districts are filtered from a vector layer using the 'DISTRICT' field, and rasters are clipped per district using GDAL's cliprasterbymasklayer before pixel counting via NumPy boolean indexing.

name: Compute district relative growth zonal statistics
desc: The script calculates district-level zonal statistics (mean, median, min, max) for relative percent vegetation growth rasters (3-month and 6-month) across pastoral districts. For each growth raster, it first masks values exceeding 100% as nodata, then computes zonal statistics per district, and exports the results as Excel spreadsheets.

name: Provide QGIS spatial processing utilities
desc: This PyQGIS function library offers reusable wrappers for common geospatial operations within QGIS. It encapsulates processing algorithms for layer loading (PostGIS views/tables with key column), SQL execution via native:postgisexecutesql and direct QSqlDatabase queries, spatial joins (joinattributesbylocation, joinattributestable, joinbylocationsummary), selections (selectbylocation, selectbyexpression, extractbyexpression, extractbyattribute), field management (add, drop, retain, rename, refactor, field calculator for row IDs and coordinates), geometry conversions (points along lines, centroids, explode lines, polygons to lines, fix geometries, delete holes, bounding boxes, multi to single parts), and generic layer utilities (dissolve, merge, clip, difference, reproject, duplicate). It also includes UI input dialogs and file/folder selectors. The library is intended to support QGIS data processing workflows, particularly those involving PostGIS data and systematic layer manipulations.

name: Prepare landslide susceptibility conditioning factors
desc: The script prepares input data for landslide susceptibility mapping by deriving topographic attributes from a digital terrain model (DTM). It first fills voids in the raw DTM, then generates slope, aspect, plan curvature, and profile curvature using SAGA and native QGIS algorithms; computes eastness and northness from aspect; calculates the topographic wetness index (TWI) from upslope contributing area and slope. It also rasterizes vector datasets of roads, rivers, faults, land use, and lithology to serve as additional conditioning factors. All outputs are single-band rasters at consistent resolution.

name: Landslide susceptibility factor sampling
desc: The script generates training and testing sample points for landslide susceptibility mapping by defining no-landslide zones based on slope and lithology strength, merging them with landslide inventory polygons, assigning hazard labels, splitting into training/testing polygons, creating random points inside them, and extracting environmental factor values at those points. Outputs include sampled point vector layers for training and testing.

name: Calculate landslide susceptibility class areas
desc: The script provides utility functions for landslide susceptibility mapping. It includes vector-to-raster conversion (vec2raster) using QGIS 'gdal:rasterize', conversion of SAGA GIS .sdat files to GeoTIFF (sdat2tif), removal of related .sdat auxiliary files, and a function (cal_classes_area) that reclassifies a landslide susceptibility raster into 4 or 5 classes via raster calculator expressions, then computes class areas (unique values report) and converts them to square kilometers. The expressions LSM_4CLASSES_RANGE and LSM_5CLASSES_RANGE define susceptibility class thresholds. Outputs are raster layers, classification rasters, and area tables.

name: Export flood depth and water level map
desc: The script generates contours from a water level grid, applies styles to depth and contour layers, composites these with base map layers, and exports a georeferenced PDF map using a predefined print layout template.

name: Generate aerial spray buffer zones
desc: The script provides QGIS processing utilities for loading vector layers, managing attributes, spatial filtering, buffer generation, interpolation, and heatmap visualization. Specifically, the aeroAlert function generates buffer zones around aerial spray application features based on weather condition (dry, rain, or other), using different buffer distances (200m, 1000m, 3000m). The interpolate function creates IDW interpolation rasters from vector field values. The rasterValues function extracts raster pixel values to point attributes. The divideLayers function splits a base layer by a unique field value and clips other layers to each subset, exporting geopackages. Outputs include buffer shapefiles, interpolation rasters, and geopackages.

name: locate favorable zone via buffer intersection
desc: The script identifies the most propitious area (Eldorado) in the Lyon region by performing a multi-criteria proximity analysis. It takes four user-supplied vector layers (train stations, metro stations, green spaces, swimming pools) and their associated buffer distances, creates buffer polygons, then sequentially intersects them (train ∩ metro, result ∩ green spaces, final ∩ swimming pools). The output is a vector layer of areas that meet all four distance criteria simultaneously.

name: Locate features within buffer distance
desc: The script implements a proximity analysis algorithm in QGIS. It takes a source layer and a superposition layer, creates a buffer zone around the superposition features using a user-defined distance, then intersects the buffer with the source layer to identify source features that fall within the buffer. The output is a new vector layer of the intersecting features.

name: Identify nearby places using buffer and intersection
desc: The plugin performs a proximity analysis by buffering a user-selected layer of interest with a specified distance, then intersecting that buffer with a second superposition layer. The result is a layer containing features from the superposition layer that lie within the buffer distance of the interest features. QGIS native processing algorithms (buffer and intersection) are used, and the output is loaded into the map if a file path is provided, or stored in memory.

name: Compute hillshade and slope from SRTM DEM
desc: The script loads a Brazil administrative boundary shapefile and SRTM DEM raster. It adjusts symbology of the vector layer, reprojects it to EPSG:102033, then uses processing algorithms to generate hillshade and slope rasters from the DEM, saving outputs to temporary files and loading them into the project.

name: Create rotated point grid
desc: The script generates a regular point grid within a user-defined extent, with optional rotation. It computes the horizontal and vertical spacing from given row/column counts or vice versa, creates a point grid using QGIS's native CreateGrid algorithm, and then rotates the points around the extent center by a specified angle. The output is a point vector layer.

name: Compute water depth raster
desc: The script computes water depth rasters for flood mapping using a terrain DEM and CRGENG water surface outputs. It runs CRGENG for each model associated with a scenario, merges the resulting ASC rasters, clips the DEM to the water extent, and calculates depth via raster calculator (B*less(A,0)+A*greater(A,0)-B). Output is a single depth raster with QML style, and temporary files are cleaned.

name: Compute hydraulic envelope rasters
desc: The script computes maximum velocity and depth envelope rasters from a set of hydraulic simulation scenarios using a digital terrain model. It executes the crgeng tool for each model, merges resulting ASCII grids into GeoTIFFs, and for depth additionally computes water depth using raster calculator. The outputs include raster layers styled for visualization.

name: Map flood hazard from depth and velocity rasters
desc: The script processes water depth and velocity rasters to generate vector polygon layers of isodepth and isovelocity contour polygons using GDAL contour and a blurred raster smoothing step. It polygonizes contour lines, classifies depth and velocity zones, and optionally intersects them to create a hazard classification map based on user-defined depth/velocity class thresholds and a hazard matrix (e.g., faible, modéré, fort). Outputs include vector maps of isodepth, isovelocity, and hazard zones with QML symbology.

name: Generate water velocity raster
desc: The script generates velocity rasters from a terrain layer using the crgeng hydraulic model for multiple scenario models. It creates a control file for crgeng, runs crgeng to produce ASCII velocity grids, merges them per model into GeoTIFF, and then composites them into a single virtual raster (VRT) for the specified time step. The output is a styled raster layer added to the current QGIS project.

name: Slice 3D vector layers along profile
desc: The script generates a 3D slicing tool: it buffers an input linestring, converts to single parts, translates vertically to a given Z min, extrudes to Z max to form a 3D wall, then iteratively intersects each input polygon layer with that wall, producing sliced layers in a new group. Each output layer inherits the style of its source.

name: Create missing sidewalk map
desc: The algorithm takes a road network and sidewalk layer as input, buffers sidewalks to create coverage polygons, subtracts them from roads to identify road segments without sidewalks, then snaps and cleans the resulting geometries. Outputs a new line layer representing missing sidewalk segments.

name: Export map layers to mbtiles and COG
desc: The script provides a QGIS dialog for exporting map layers into mbtiles (vector tiles) and COG (Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF) formats for web viewing. It allows users to define map views, select layers, set zoom levels, and specify extents. Vector layers are cleaned, packaged, and converted to mbtiles using ogr2ogr or QGIS native processing. Raster layers are rendered with transparency, clipped, reprojected, and converted to COGs. The outputs are tile files for a QuickWebViewer application.

name: Create TUFLOW Catch project
desc: The script creates a TUFLOW Catch project within QGIS, including saving project settings (e.g., CRS, GIS format, executable path), optionally creating folder structure, empty GIS files, domain check file, and control file templates. It also loads the domain check layer with a predefined style if available.

name: Assign Elevations to TIN Polygons
desc: The script densifies input polygon vertices at a user-defined interval, extracts vertices, removes duplicates, and samples raster (DEM) values to assign elevation data (Z field). It produces a point layer with Z values and a polygon layer with Shape_Width attribute set to -1, intended for TUFLOW TIN surface generation.

name: QGIS workflow: Data export, Format conversion
desc: This workflow contains 43 core geospatial operations, including Data export, Format conversion, Vector data attribute editing, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Estimate 24-hour surface temperature
desc: The script estimates surface temperature over 24 hours for a set of points using a surface energy balance model. It loads ground material properties (albedo, emissivity, thickness, thermal conductivity, thermal capacity, vegetation coefficient) from the active vector layer, hourly shadow values from UMEP, and weather data (dry bulb temperature, global horizontal radiation, precipitation) from a project weather layer. Evapotranspiration potential is taken from a city-specific layer (ICE_ETo).
