desc: The script creates orientation (orienteering) maps by downloading OpenStreetMap vector data for the current map canvas extent, exploding HSTORE fields into attribute tables, filtering layers into multipolygons (surfaces), lines, and points, applying pre-defined QGIS layer styles, and saving the styled layers into a new QGIS project file.

name: Map IBGE census sector attributes
desc: The script downloads census sector boundary shapefiles and corresponding aggregated tables from IBGE's FTP for Brazilian states, joins selected demographic variables onto the spatial layer, and creates thematic maps with a derived categorical field computed as sum of selected variables optionally divided by another sum. It also loads municipal, district, and subdistrict boundaries for context.

name: Assess vector thematic classification accuracy
desc: The script performs thematic accuracy assessment on vector cartography. It compares two vector layers (evaluation and reference) by allowing the user to select classification fields and establish category relations. It offers three sampling methods: systematic, simple random, and stratified random. Sample points are generated within the overlap extent of the layers, then spatially intersected to extract class labels from both layers. A confusion matrix is built, and accuracy metrics including overall accuracy, kappa statistic, user’s and producer’s accuracy are computed. Results are displayed in the plugin dialog and can be exported as an HTML report, along with a sample point layer added to the map.

name: Generate hazard-stakes intersection atlases
desc: The script automates the generation of maps crossing hazard (alea) and stakes (enjeu) layers in a QGIS project. It extracts spatial intersections from a PostgreSQL database, creates print layouts with legends and titles, optionally with atlas coverage based on administrative statistics, and exports the results as multi-page PDFs or styled GeoPackages, grouped by alea, theme, or individually.

name: Box-counting fractal analysis of polygons
desc: The script performs a box-counting fractal analysis on an input vector polygon layer. It first computes the bounding box of the input feature, then creates a variable-distance buffer around its centroid to define the analysis extent. For each of seven levels (0 to 6), it calculates a grid cell size as width/2^level or height/2^level and generates a grid layer. Each grid is spatially joined with the input features to count intersecting polygons per cell, building successive count fields (Nivel_0 through Nivel_6). The final output 'Fractal' layer contains all count fields after cleaning intermediate columns, suitable for fractal dimension estimation.

name: Automated fire foci mapping and reporting
desc: The script automates the generation of reports and maps of fire foci (hot spots) for the state of Amazonas, Brazil, using FIRMS/NASA active fire data (MODIS and VIIRS) and ancillary geospatial layers. It downloads fire data (MODIS C6.1, VIIRS NOAA-20, NOAA-21, Suomi-NPP) and base layers (hydrography, cities, roads, municipalities) from cloud storage; performs geometric validity checks, field mappings, spatial intersections with municipalities; computes kernel density estimation; extracts high-density contours to delineate priority areas; integrates historical INPE fire statistics; and exports a comprehensive PDF report and individual priority area maps and fire situation maps.

name: Process NLS GML to clipped GeoPackage
desc: The script downloads NLS GML files, converts selected layers to a GeoPackage, dissolves features by product type, clips them to a user-defined area, and applies styles.

name: Merge selected polygon features
desc: The script merges selected polygon features from an input vector layer into a single feature using dissolve, computes area in hectares, and combines the merged result with the original unselected features. It extracts selected features, adds a constant 'IdToMrg' field, dissolves on that field to merge all selected polygons, calculates area in hectares, then inverts the selection to extract unselected features, merges both groups, and recalculates area for all features. The output is a vector layer with the merged selected feature and the unchanged unselected features.

name: Download DEM from OpenTopography
desc: The script is a QGIS processing algorithm that downloads a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) from OpenTopography.org. It takes a user-specified extent, DEM type (e.g., SRTM 30m, ALOS World 3D 30m), and API key, then constructs an API request to download a GeoTIFF file. The downloaded DEM is loaded as a raster layer into the QGIS project. The algorithm also handles coordinate transformation to EPSG:4326 and validates the extent against ANADEM coverage if that dataset is selected.

name: Dissolve small polygons into adjacent
desc: The script dissolves small polygons from an input polygon layer into adjacent larger polygons based on user-specified criteria. It first converts multipart to singleparts, fixes geometries, calculates area in map units, and selects polygons smaller than a given threshold. Then it eliminates selected polygons by merging into the largest adjacent polygon, smallest adjacent polygon, or the one with the largest common boundary, according to the user's choice. The final output is a dissolved polygon layer with recalculated areas.

name: Noise level prediction from point source
desc: This script estimates noise levels (dBA) from a point source at receptor locations using the BS 5228 standard. It reprojects input DEM and receptor polygons to a projected CRS, performs a viewshed analysis from the source point to account for line-of-sight barriers, creates a hexagonal grid over the receptor area, computes distances, applies attenuation factors (distance, ground type, soft ground percentage, reflections, screening, and duration corrections) via field calculations, and outputs a noise level layer (dBA_activity) and a styled noise source point. The workflow integrates QGIS processing algorithms: point to layer, reprojection, viewshed, grid creation, centroid extraction, zonal statistics, distance to nearest hub, attribute joins, and field calculator steps.

name: Apply noise threshold layer style
desc: The script applies a predefined QGIS layer style (from a QML file) to a vector polygon layer containing noise prediction results, visualizing noise levels according to the IFC General EHS Guidelines with threshold categories for residential and industrial zones, and loads the styled layer into the QGIS project.

name: Calculate surface runoff Curve Number
desc: This QGIS processing plugin calculates surface runoff depth (Q) and related coefficients (Curve Number, runoff coefficient CE, infiltration coefficient CF, and initial abstraction coefficient CIo) using the SCS Curve Number method. The workflow takes a study area boundary, soil hydrological group layer, land cover/vegetation layer, and precipitation (numeric value or raster). It reprojects, clips, and intersects these layers, then joins with a Curve Number lookup table based on a composite soil-vegetation code. The algorithm computes potential retention S, initial abstraction Io, runoff Q, and the coefficients CE, CF, CIo. Outputs are vector layers with pre-defined symbology.

name: Buffer without overlaps
desc: The script creates non-overlapping buffers around input vector features (points, lines, polygons) with options for end cap and join styles. It first fixes geometries, applies a buffer with chosen distance and styles, then uses polygon self-intersection and area filtering to remove overlapping regions, finally saving the result as a shapefile added to the QGIS project.

name: Compute hourly ground surface temperature
desc: This script computes hourly ground surface temperatures for a specified date by solving a surface energy balance equation. It creates a point grid over a ground description polygon layer, assigns material properties, extracts hourly shadow fractions from precomputed rasters, reads weather data from an EPW file, and then applies a thermal equilibrium model that considers solar radiation, sky temperature, air temperature, conduction to deep ground, evapotranspiration, and thermal inertia. The output is a CSV file and a point vector layer with hourly, minimum, mean, and maximum temperatures for each point, excluding building footprints.

name: Create OSM sidewalk geometries
desc: The script processes OSM road line layers to create sidewalk polygons. It primarily uses QGIS processing functions including buffering, polygonizing, splitting, snapping, clipping, and spatial relationship extraction. Specialized functions handle intersection resolution, removal of disconnected segments, and rejoining of split sidewalks to produce cleaned sidewalk geometries. The plugin is designed to automate the generation of sidewalk features from OpenStreetMap data for urban infrastructure mapping.

name: Generate tile drainage order and bury depth
desc: The script generates tile drainage network ordering ID, burying depths, and flow direction. It processes a DEM raster and a tile lines vector layer: first, it adds an ordering ID field based on tile sequence and flow direction; then it runs QGIS processing algorithms to create auto-incremented ordering, extract terrain profiles along lines using SAGA, rename elevation field to SurF_Elev, and delete unwanted columns. Finally, it computes bury depths using user-defined slope, upper/lower depth limits, and elevation constraints, and outputs shapefiles containing ordered lines, profiles, and buried lines split by individual laterals.

name: Generate hydro network from DEM
desc: The script generates a hydrological network vector layer from a digital elevation model. It uses GRASS r.watershed to compute flow accumulation and extract stream grid cells based on a user-defined watershed size threshold, producing a temporary stream raster. Then r.to.vect converts the stream raster into a vector layer, yielding the final hydro network lines. This algorithm is part of a dispersion analysis toolset.

name: Delineate affected watersheds and hydro network
desc: The script uses a DEM and an occurrence point to delineate the watersheds and hydro network affected by an invasive species. It runs GRASS GIS r.watershed for flow accumulation, r.water.outlet to delineate the watershed upstream of the point, then vectorizes and clips to produce affected watershed polygons and stream lines.

name: Watershed delineation from point
desc: The script delineates the upstream watershed (drainage basin) for a given point location using a Digital Elevation Model (DEM). It first computes flow directions with GRASS r.watershed, then uses r.water.outlet to extract the contributing area, producing a watershed dispersion raster. This process identifies the upstream terrain that drains to the specified point.

name: Create species distribution grid overlay
desc: The script creates a point grid (TYPE=2) over the extent of an input species distribution vector layer, with user-defined horizontal and vertical spacing. It then performs an extract by location to retain only grid points that intersect the species distribution, producing a filtered grid layer that represents the species spatial coverage.

name: Alien species hydro network boundary monitoring
desc: The script generates monitoring points where a hydro network intersects watershed or administrative boundaries. It first converts the input polygon layer to lines, then computes line intersections with the hydro network, and finally adds X and Y coordinate fields to the resulting intersection points.

name: Calculate potential range distribution
desc: The script calculates the potential range of a species by buffering the input species distribution layer by a user-specified dispersal distance and extracting the reference grid polygons that intersect the buffer, resulting in a range layer.

name: Calculate potential range using grid dimension
desc: The script computes a potential species distribution area by first buffering the input species distribution layer by a specified dispersal distance, then creating a regular grid over the buffer extent using user-defined horizontal and vertical spacing, and finally extracting grid cells that intersect the buffer. The output is a vector layer of grid cells representing the potential range.

name: Calculate species range with exclusions
desc: The script calculates potential species range distribution by buffering species distribution points by dispersal distance, intersecting with a reference grid, and then subtracting areas that intersect buffered ineffective areas (barriers, unsuitable ecosystems). The result is a vector range layer.

name: Coordinate System Harmonization
desc: The script reprojects a raster and a vector layer to a target coordinate reference system (default EPSG:3435) using GDAL warp and native QGIS reprojection, providing harmonized coordinate systems for drainage analysis. Outputs are a reprojected raster and vector layer with custom names.

name: Geometrically Fix Tile Drainage Lines
desc: The script performs geometric cleaning of a proposed tile drainage line layer to produce topologically sound and connected line segments. It extends line ends, dissolves, extracts vertices, snaps points, converts to paths, fixes geometries, adds geometry attributes, explodes segments, removes nulls, validates, adds an ID field, and retains key fields (vertex_part, begin, end, ID). The final output is a geometrically fixed line layer ready for building tile networks.

name: LiDAR thinning analysis for drainage sites
desc: The algorithm processes a LiDAR DEM and a field boundary polygon to perform drainage site analysis. It clips the DEM to the boundary, resamples to a desired pixel size, converts the resampled raster to points, generates pixel centroids along the boundary, and exports boundary and interior point profiles with XY coordinates. Outputs include a resampled raster, boundary point profiles, interior point profiles, and a merged point layer.

name: Generate Tile Layout Grids
desc: The script creates two grid line vector layers (linear and perpendicular) over a specified extent using QGIS native processing algorithms. It first generates a regular grid with user-defined horizontal and vertical spacing and CRS, then rotates that grid by a given angle around an anchor point. The outputs are styled with dashed gray lines and are intended for field tile layout planning.

name: Compute longitudinal slope of drainage network
desc: The script processes a drainage tile line network and a DEM to extract elevation profiles and compute longitudinal slope per segment. It splits lines into equal-length segments, derives Z values from the DEM, calculates the slope as absolute elevation difference divided by segment length, retains key attributes including Tile_ID, Elev_First, Elev_Last, and Seg_Slope, and generates point layers with endpoint elevations and terrain profiles along lines.

name: Identify surface water flow paths in agricultural fields
desc: The script identifies surface water flow paths (laylines) on an agricultural field using LiDAR DEM data. It buffers the field boundary, clips the thinned DEM, fills sinks, extracts channel networks from unfilled and filled DEMs, generates contour lines, and computes a depression areas raster. The outputs include unfilled laylines vector, filled contour lines, filled laylines, and depression areas raster.

name: Export tile spreadsheet readout by ID
desc: The script adds a unique Line_ID field to a vector line layer, exports the attribute table to a spreadsheet file, and splits the layer by a specified unique field into multiple files for further drainage analysis or reporting.

name: Simulate earthworks cut and fill
desc: The script modifies a DEM by performing cut and fill earthworks based on a platform vector layer, platform base level, cut slope, and fill slope. It generates a multi-ring buffer around the platform, computes cut and fill levels for each distance using advanced Python field calculators, rasterizes these levels onto DEM copies, combines them with the original DEM using a conditional raster algebra formula, and stamps the platform level onto the output. The result is a modified DEM raster layer reflecting the designed earthworks.

name: Generate linear referencing route marks
desc: The script generates linear referencing system (LRS) marks along input line geometries by creating points at 25 m intervals using the QGIS native Points Along Geometry algorithm, then applies a predefined style (QML file) to represent marks and text at 25 m and 100 m intervals.

name: Simulate reservoir water depth
desc: The script models a dam on an existing DEM by generating fill levels from a multi-ring buffer around the dam crest line, rasterizing them to raise terrain according to a specified crest elevation and wall slope, and then using GRASS r.lake to simulate reservoir flooding, producing a water depth raster and a modified DEM with the dam.

name: Extract line vertices as points
desc: The script converts selected line features into points by first exploding lines to segments, then extracting vertices from those segments, and finally removing duplicate geometries. The resulting point layer, named 'Exploded line as points', is styled with red symbols of size 2 and added to the current QGIS project.

name: Explode polygon into lines and vertices
desc: The script processes a selected polygon feature from the active layer in QGIS. It applies the native:polygonstolines algorithm to generate a line layer, then explodes these lines into individual segments (native:explodelines). The resulting line layer is styled in red and added to the map. Additionally, it extracts all vertices of the original polygon (native:extractvertices), removes duplicate geometries (native:deleteduplicategeometries), and adds a point layer of unique vertices also styled in red. The tool is designed for interactive use within QGIS, expecting exactly one selected polygon feature as input.

name: Estimate NRCS peak flow parameters for HEC-HMS
desc: The script guides a user through a multi-step QGIS processing workflow to determine basin properties for NRCS peak flow estimation in HEC-HMS. It fills sinks in a user-selected DEM, computes Strahler stream order, extracts channel networks and drainage basins, and delineates a main watershed boundary via upslope area and polygonization. It re-processes the terrain within the boundary, identifies subbasin pour points from junctions, generates fake subbasins for each point, removes overlapping subbasins, and merges them into a final catchment layer. It computes area, centroid, flow length, average CN (from a user-selected land cover raster via grid intersection), contour slope, SCS lag time, and time of concentration. Finally, it writes an HEC-HMS basin file (.basin) and project file (.hms) with subbasins, junctions, reaches, and sink elements, and calculates peak discharge using the NRCS unit hydrograph method. Outputs include intermediate rasters and vectors, the final catchment shapefile, and HMS model files.

name: Align rasters to reference grid
desc: The algorithm aligns one or more raster layers to a reference raster by resampling to match the reference's CRS, pixel size, and origin. It optionally applies a mask layer with a buffer to clip outputs. It uses GDAL warp and clip operations, and outputs tiles as TIFF files in a specified directory.

name: Modify land cover by vector field
desc: The algorithm modifies a land cover raster by replacing pixel values in areas defined by an input polygon vector layer, using a numeric field from that layer. It first copies the original raster (clipping by extent to preserve coverage) to create a temporary output, then performs a rasterize operation with overwrite mode using the specified field value, changing the land cover values in the overlapping areas. The output is a new raster with updated land cover codes.

name: Modify land cover raster using lookup table
desc: The script modifies a land cover raster by changing the pixel values under specified vector polygons to a new land cover class identified by name from a custom lookup table. It first retrieves the numeric land cover code from a lookup table having fields 'lc_name' and 'lc_value', clips the input raster to its extent, then rasterizes the polygon areas with the new value to produce a modified land cover raster.

name: Modify land cover using NLCD/C-CAP
desc: The algorithm modifies a land cover raster by changing pixels that intersect a polygon vector layer to a specified NLCD/C-CAP land cover class. It first clips the input raster to its extent, then rasterizes the vector polygons over the clipped raster with a burn value equal to the integer land cover code of the selected class, producing a modified land cover raster.

name: Compute material transport accumulation
desc: The script provides common utility functions for the QNSPECT plugin, including a layer post-processor for pseudocolor rendering, a GDAL raster calculator wrapper, and a GRASS r.watershed-based material transport function. The material transport function computes flow accumulation from elevation and a weight raster (representing pollutant load or erosion factors), fills nodata, and combines outputs to preserve original nodata cells.

name: Rasterize soil properties
desc: The algorithm converts a vector polygon layer of soil properties into Hydrologic Soil Group (HSG) and/or K-Factor rasters. It validates the HSG field values, maps them to numeric codes via field calculator, and uses GDAL rasterize to generate the HSG raster. If a K-Factor field is provided, it directly rasterizes that field to produce the K-Factor raster, with both rasters using the specified cell size and extent.

name: Divide Parcel by Road
desc: This script divides a single parcel polygon using a road feature (line or polygon) by computing the geometric difference between the parcel and the buffered road (if line) or direct road polygon. For line roads, a buffer is created from the specified domain width; for polygon roads, the geometry is used directly. The resulting multipolygon replaces the original parcel geometry. Optionally, new virtual vertices (type 'V', method 'PA1') are added to a vertex layer at points present in the difference but not in the original parcel.

name: Perform inverted clip on vector layer
desc: The script implements an inverted clip geoprocessing algorithm that creates a polygon layer representing the part of a given extent that is not covered by a source vector layer. It takes a source vector layer and an extent as inputs, generates a layer from the extent, assigns EPSG:4326 projection, clips the source layer with this extent layer, then performs a difference operation to extract the area of the extent not occupied by the clipped source. The final output is a vector layer of the inverted clip suitable for further routing or wind forecast analysis.

name: Densify Lines With Nearest Points By Condition
desc: The algorithm densifies line layers by inserting new vertices derived from a point layer. For each line feature, nearest points within a maximum distance (optionally filtered by attribute conditions) are either used directly or interpolated onto the line to define new vertices. Duplicate nodes can be avoided. The output is a densified line layer with original attributes.

name: Extend lines to nearest points by condition
desc: The script extends line features to the nearest points from a point layer, optionally applying attribute-based condition comparisons. It supports extending start/end of whole lines or individual parts, allows setting maximum extend distance, minimum distance to skip extension, and controls duplicate point usage (layer/feature/part). It evaluates filter and comparison expressions on both layers, uses spatial indexing for nearest neighbor search, and prevents self-crossing if desired. Output is a new line layer with extended geometries.

name: Nearest neighbor conditional attribute join
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm joins attributes from a join vector layer to a source vector layer based on nearest features, with optional filtering expressions, comparison expressions, and join distance limits. It produces a new layer containing the source geometry, selected join fields with an optional prefix, the distance to the nearest match, and the shortest line as WKT. The algorithm supports ordering of source features and options to join multiple or single matches, and handles cases where source and join layers are the same.

name: Snap Vertices to Nearest Points by Condition
desc: This algorithm snaps selected vertices of a source vector layer (lines, polygons, or points) to the nearest point from a point layer, using optional attribute-based condition matching and a distance tolerance. It first reprojects the points to match the source layer CRS if needed, converts multipoints to single points, builds a spatial index on the points, and evaluates comparison expressions between source and point attributes. Based on user-chosen vertex snap methods (start/end vertices of whole geometry or parts, or mid-vertices) and a 'snap multiple' rule (once per layer, feature, part, or unlimited), it moves each qualifying vertex to the nearest matching point. The output is a new vector layer with the snapped geometries.

name: Split Lines at Nearest Points by Condition
desc: This QGIS algorithm splits lines at their nearest points from a points layer, optionally filtered by attribute conditions. It first evaluates filter expressions on lines and points, reprojects points if necessary, builds a spatial index, then for each line finds nearest points within a maximum distance. It evaluates comparison expressions (using optional operators like equals, contains) to decide which points to use. The line geometry is densified with these points (either using the nearest points themselves or interpolated points on the line), then the line is split into segments between consecutive split vertices. Finally, it removes invalid geometries, duplicate nodes, and drops short segments based on a length threshold. The output is a new line layer with the split segments, retaining original attributes.

name: Create perpendicular lines from nearest points
desc: The script generates a line layer of perpendicular lines connecting each input point to its nearest line feature. It first filters points and lines, optionally orders points, then for each point calculates the nearest line using a spatial index, optionally with a condition based on expressions evaluated on both layers. It determines the closest point on the line, interpolates the angle, and constructs a perpendicular segment of a given length. The resulting layer includes all source point attributes plus fields for the source feature ID, intersection point, cross line ID, angle, distance, and inclination.

name: Lot Numbering along Block Boundaries
desc: The script numbers lot parcels along block boundaries in QGIS. It dissolves selected block polygons to obtain the boundary line, intersects with lot polygons to determine order along the block, reorders vertices based on the intersection point, and assigns numbers either sequentially or based on cumulative frontage length (major, minor, or sum). Output is a new polygon layer with a 'NLATUAL' field containing the assigned numbers.

name: Create point density heatmap
desc: The script creates a styled density heatmap from an input point vector layer. It generates a rectangular, diamond, or hexagonal grid over a specified extent, counts the number of points (or weighted sum) in each grid cell, filters cells with at least a minimum count, and applies a graduated color ramp. The output is a vector polygon layer representing density distribution.

name: Compute polygon overlap density
desc: The script computes polygon overlap density from an input polygon layer. It first performs a union to split overapping polygons into unique fragments. Using aggregation by geometry, it counts the number of overlapping polygons per fragment (NUMPOINTS) and optionally lists the contributing polygon IDs. A filter threshold retains fragments with overlap counts greater than or equal to a minimum value. The output is a polygon layer containing overlap counts and optionally ID lists.

name: Calculate geodiversity index
desc: The script calculates a geodiversity index for a user-defined boundary area using a grid-based approach. It creates a grid of user-specified cell shape and spacing, and for each cell computes variety indices for geology and pedology (distinct categories intersecting the cell), geomorphon variety and maximum Strahler stream order from a DEM, presence of lakes, and mineral/fossil occurrence diversity from point layers. These sub-indices are then summed to produce a final geodiversity index, optionally normalized to 0-1. Outputs include the final grid layer with the index, intermediate thematic grids, and a manifest file summarizing analysis parameters and output files.

name: Compute active channel block metrics
desc: The script processes active channel polygon and valley bottom blocks to derive segmented blocks of the active channel. It removes islands, generates centerlines, intersects with valley bottom blocks, calculates block area and centerline length, joins them by distance, computes mean width, and exports the resulting layer as Geopackage and CSV. Outputs include a vector layer of active channel blocks with attributes: ID, distance, area_m2, length_m, mean_width_m, and a CSV table.

name: Valley bottom block processing and width calculation
desc: The script processes a valley bottom polygon layer by deleting holes, generating centerlines, optionally reversing direction, creating cross-sections at specified width and spacing, creating river kilometer points, splitting the polygon into blocks along cross-sections, joining attributes (distance, length), calculating area and mean width, reordering fields, and exporting the blocks as a polygon layer and CSV table. Temporary centerline, cross-section, and river km layers can be loaded.

name: Adapt species coordinates for Maxent
desc: The script adapts species distribution point data for Maxent compatibility by spatially filtering points within a given area of influence, removing specified fields, and adding X/Y coordinate fields. Inputs: species point layer, optional fields to omit, polygon area of influence. Output: point layer with coordinates adapted for Maxent.

name: Delimit Maxent model zones
desc: This script reclassifies a Maxent output raster using a classification table (with Min, Max, and Category fields), then converts the reclassified raster to vector polygons, producing both raster and vector outputs that delimit territorial zones of model success.

name: Generate distance influence variable
desc: The script generates a continuous distance raster for environmental variables to be used in Maxent species distribution modeling. It clips the input vector layer to the area of interest, rasterizes it at the specified resolution, computes distance up to a maximum distance, fills null values with a control value, and masks the result using a reference raster to ensure alignment with other environmental layers.

name: Calculate continuous raster statistics for distribution points
desc: The script generates zonal statistics for continuous environmental raster data at species occurrence points. It first creates a buffer around each input point using a user-specified radius, then calculates all available zonal statistics (e.g., count, sum, mean, median, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, range, minority, majority, variety, variance) of the environmental raster within each buffer polygon. Finally, it converts the buffers to centroids to produce a point output layer with the statistical attributes attached to each original point location.

name: Reduce raster extent by negative buffer
desc: The script trims a raster layer by creating a zero-value raster from the input, polygonizing it, applying a negative buffer to shrink the polygon boundaries, and then clipping the original raster using the buffered polygon mask. This process omits potential peripheral values (e.g., borders, coastlines, islands) by reducing the raster's working area.

name: Fill linear or isolated environmental variables
desc: The script prepares a gap-filled raster layer from a vector environmental variable layer for use in Maxent species distribution modeling. It clips the vector layer to a specified territorial boundary, rasterizes it using a categorical field at a user-defined pixel resolution, fills null cells with a control fill value, and masks the result to match the extent of a reference raster. The outputs include the processed raster with filled gaps, suitable for Maxent input.

name: Rasterize Categorical Environmental Variables for Maxent
desc: Rasterizes categorical vector environmental variables to a standardized pixel resolution for Maxent modeling. The algorithm clips the input variable to the Ebro basin boundary, rasterizes it using GDAL with the categorical field and specified resolution, then clips the result to the territorial limits mask.

name: Generate distance influence variable for Maxent
desc: The script generates a continuous distance influence raster from a vector environmental variable, constrained by territorial limits and aligned to a reference raster. It clips the vector layer to the study area, rasterizes it, computes proximity (distance) up to a maximum distance, fills null values with a user-specified control value, and masks the result to the reference raster extent, producing a standardized distance variable for use in Maxent species distribution modeling.

name: Generate Litchi-compatible UAV flight path
desc: The script generates a drone flight path in the form of waypoints (points) with Litchi-compatible attributes (latitude, longitude, altitude, heading, etc.) for a given area of interest (AOI). It uses camera parameters (field of view, image dimensions, altitude) and overlap percentages to compute ground sampling distance and spacing between parallel flight lines. It then creates parallel lines offset from a user-drawn input line, clips them to the AOI polygon, extracts vertices, reorders them to create a zigzag path, and exports the points as a CSV file. Flight time and total distance are also calculated.

name: Split DEM by field and generate scaled STL
desc: The script generates 3D printable STL files from a digital elevation model (DEM) raster layer split by polygon features of a vector layer. It first checks and sets the no-data value, reprojects the vector layer to match the DEM's CRS, splits the vector layer by a chosen field, clips the DEM to each polygon, computes a scaling factor to fit the clipped DEM into a specified 3D printer bed size, and then generates an STL mesh file for each clipped raster with user-defined model height and base thickness.

name: Generate scaled STL models
desc: This QGIS processing script generates 3D printable STL files from a digital elevation model (DEM) raster and a vector layer. It first splits the vector layer by a chosen field, clips the DEM by each resulting polygon, merges clipped rasters to compute overall dimensions, calculates a scale factor based on nozzle line width and user-specified total width/length to ensure all STL models fit within the print bed, and finally calls another algorithm to produce scaled STL files for each clipped area. Outputs are STL files saved to a user-specified folder.

name: Create groundwater buffer raster
desc: The script produces a groundwater buffer raster from water surface elevation (WSE) input. It samples WSE raster values at points generated along vector lines, interpolates them using grid nearest neighbor with an expanded extent (by a user-defined buffer distance), and clips the interpolated raster to the area outside the vector polygon but within the expanded extent. The output is a raster layer representing groundwater elevation buffer.

name: Extract polygon centerline and skeleton
desc: The script provides geometry processing functions for QGIS, including skeleton/medial axis extraction from polygons via Voronoi-based workflows (points generation, Voronoi polygons, line extraction, simplification, directional merge, and optional longest centerline), wedge and spiral buffer generation with customizable sectors and radii, polygon splitting using random point generation and K-means clustering with Voronoi intersection, longest line inside polygon calculation, and lines of sight visibility analysis. It leverages QGIS processing algorithms and numpy for numerical operations.

name: Voronoi-based geometric vector analysis
desc: The script provides a library of functions performing Voronoi/Delaunay-based geometric analyses on QGIS vector layers. The splitpolygon function partitions polygons using random points, k-means clustering, and Voronoi tessellation. The skeleton function computes line skeleton via Voronoi, filtering, dissolve, simplification, and directional merge. The isolation function finds the most isolated point by Delaunay triangulation, edge extraction, distance measurement, and per-category statistics. The lec function computes the largest empty circle center by clipping Voronoi vertices with convex hull and finding the vertex with maximum distance to nearest point. The closestfarthest function identifies closest and farthest point pairs using Delaunay edges and convex hull segments. Outputs are temporary memory layers with computed geometries.

name: Identify most isolated point
desc: This script finds the most isolated point from an input point layer by computing the maximum distance to the nearest neighbor using Voronoi diagram analysis. It first calls the 'isolation' function to determine the isolated point's unique ID and its isolation distance. Then it extracts that point using attribute extraction, and creates a buffer circle around it with radius equal to the isolation distance. Outputs include the isolated point feature and the buffer circle layer.

name: Compute largest empty circle from point layer
desc: The script computes the largest empty circle (the maximum-radius circle containing no points) for an input point layer using a Voronoi-based algorithm from the becagis library. It identifies the center point and radius, converts metric radius to degrees for geographic coordinate systems using ellipsoid parameters, and outputs a centroid point layer and a buffer polygon layer representing the largest empty circle.

name: Calculate maximum inscribed circles
desc: The script computes the maximum inscribed circle for each polygon in a vector layer. It processes selected or all features, applies a tolerance parameter for CRS adjustments, and generates two output layers: a point layer of circle centers and a polygon layer of the circles by buffering the points.

name: Map sustainable tourism opportunity and pressure
desc: The script joins a landcover polygon layer with sensitivity and seasonality tables, calculates summer and winter sensitivity scores, rasterizes them using a pressure template, and multiplies by user-defined factor weights to generate baseline pressure and opportunity rasters. It then applies scenario-specific multipliers from a matrix to produce per-scenario rasters for summer and winter. Outputs include GeoTIFF files for baseline and each scenario, organized in folders, and layers added to the QGIS project.

name: Determine sewer network asset characteristics
desc: The script determines asset characteristics for wastewater and combined sewer networks by processing node, pipe, structure, and area vector layers. It assigns unique area and system IDs, selects relevant sewer types, creates buffer polygons, and computes aggregated pipe and node storage volumes, structure properties (pump capacities, overflow levels), and discharge relationships. Outputs include storage and structure summary layers, pump station data, discharge points, and a discharge tree for further hydraulic modelling.

name: Compute wastewater contribution per sewer district
desc: The algorithm determines the wastewater contribution within a sewer district's own drainage area. It takes as input BAG buildings, BGT inflow table, drinkwater points, plan capacity polygons, and sewer district polygons. It performs spatial joins and intersections to count addresses per district, compute connected surface areas for different drainage systems (mixed, rainwater, improved rainwater, DWA, infiltration, surface water, ground), and calculate theoretical peak overflow capacity (POC) from those areas. It also sums drinking water consumption and VE units to compute DWA from addresses and VE. It then adds plan capacity extra flows for future periods. The outputs include various intermediate layers and the final result: sewer districts with aggregate wastewater contribution data (DWA from BAG/VE, drinking water totals, and planned extra flows).

name: Calculate upstream wastewater supply and capacity
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm is step 3 of the GeoDyn GWSW plugin, which determines upstream sewer areas and wastewater supply. It takes as input the sewer discharge tree, discharge points, discharge relations, and sewer catchment areas with their own wastewater supply from previous steps. The algorithm computes upstream contributing subcatchments using custom tools (lis2graph, calc fields upstream) and iteratively propagates upstream contributions. It calculates various hydraulic parameters including wastewater supply (based on BAG addresses, drinking water use, and population equivalents), theoretical and practical peak overflow capacity (POC), available capacity, filling and emptying times, and combines own and upstream contributions into total loads for each sewer area. It produces multiple output layers: a graph representation of the sewer network, an updated sewer tree and relations, discharge points with key performance indicators, and a layer identifying areas where wastewater supply exceeds the discharge capacity.

name: Link BGT to drainage area statistics
desc: The script links BGT land use data to drainage areas by intersecting the two layers, computing area-based proportions of various sewer types (mixed sewage, stormwater, infiltration, open water, surface runoff, etc.) weighted by paving percentage, then aggregates these by drainage area ID, performs attribute joins to attach summed values and counts, and calculates a total sewer area for each drainage area.

name: Summarize external inflow contributions per drainage area
desc: The script connects additional source layers (plancap, drinking water points, waste water discharge points VE, and address points VBO) to drainage areas via spatial intersections. It performs spatial joins and intersections to compute counts and sums of attributes (ExAFW categories 2124, 2529, 3039, 4050; par_result and zak_result for drinking water; GRONDSLAG count and sum for VEs; fid count for VBO). Intersection and duplicate removal ensure unique plancap-to-area assignments. The final outputs aggregate ExAFW sums and other source contributions per drainage area, flag areas with multiple plancaps and plancaps spanning multiple areas, and produce joined statistics layers.

name: QGIS workflow: Raster spatial analysis and calculation, Spatial Analysis And Modeling
desc: This workflow contains 227 core geospatial operations, including Raster spatial analysis and calculation, Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Format conversion, Projection. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Determine geological surface orientation
desc: This script computes strike and dip orientation of geological surfaces from user-provided point shapefile and DEM raster. It sets z-values from the DEM, calculates normal vector components for each three consecutive points using the three-point vector method, derives centroid coordinates, and computes orientation attributes: strike, dip direction, and dip. The output includes a vector point layer with these attributes and a centroid point layer, both with appropriate symbology and labels.

name: Prepare building and vegetation height layers
desc: This algorithm prepares spatial inputs for the URock urban wind model. For buildings, it computes median height from a DSM (with optional DEM subtraction) per building footprint polygon, outputting a polygon layer with a height attribute. For vegetation, it either creates polygons from a canopy height model (CDSM) by rounding, vectorizing, and dissolving by height, or buffers vegetation point locations using tree height and/or crown radius fields to generate circular polygons with a height attribute.

name: Construct median line from point pairs
desc: The script constructs an equidistance line (median line) between two sets of input points representing base points of two states. It merges the point layers, generates Voronoi polygons, extracts vertices that are approximately equidistant to both point sets, filters and orders them, and draws a line connecting these ordered median points. For adjacent state configurations, it also includes the midpoint of the two closest base points. The final output is a 'Median_Line' layer symbolizing the estimated boundary.

name: Compute graph edge weights from custom formula
desc: The script calculates edge weights for a network graph using a user-specified cost function. It supports a wide range of variables and operators, including raster pixel values (with sampling along edges), distance metrics (Euclidean, Manhattan, geodesic, ellipsoidal), shortest path weights computed via A* on raster data, polygon intersection checks, and vector field attributes. The class iterates over all edges, evaluates the cost function for each edge by sampling raster points or performing A* searches, and sets the computed weights in the graph. Optionally, it generates visualization layers of shortest paths on rasters.

name: Build vector-based connectivity graphs
desc: The script builds spatial graphs from QGIS vector layers (points or lines) or random vertices using connection strategies like complete, nearest neighbor, distance-based, cluster, and line-layer-based. It uses a KD-tree for nearest neighbor searches, supports directed/undirected edges, allows exclusion of edges intersecting forbidden polygons, and computes advanced edge costs using raster data and custom formulas. Workflow: set options and layers, then call makeGraph to generate vertices (from point layer or random), create edges via chosen strategy, optionally remove intersecting edges, and compute costs. Outputs are vertex and edge layers added to the QGIS canvas with edge weight labels.

name: Calculate Green View Index
desc: Calculates the Green View Index (GVI) for sample points from Google Street View images. The script groups images by point ID, extracts green pixels using Li et al. (2015) or Dong et al. (2018) thresholding on RGB or HSV, computes per-image GVI as the ratio of green pixels, averages across multiple views per point, and generates a point layer with point IDs and GVI values. Optionally writes masked images highlighting vegetation.

name: Download Google Street View Images
desc: The script downloads Google Street View images for a set of sample points, given a point layer with unique IDs. It validates input IDs for uniqueness and non-null, then for each point queries the Street View metadata API to check availability and date. If metadata-only is not selected, it downloads images at specified headings and pitches, saving them as JPG files with filenames including point ID, heading, and pitch. Optionally, images are geotagged with coordinates. A CSV file recording point ID, status, and date is written to the output folder.

name: Generate Sample Points
desc: The script generates random sample points within a polygon, along a road line network, or a combination clipped by the polygon, based on user-specified parameters (number of points, minimum distance). It reprojects input layers to a global projected CRS (EPSG:3395) to enforce distance in meters, runs QGIS's 'randompointsinsidepolygons' or 'randompointsalongline' algorithms, then reprojects the result to WGS84, converts from multipart to singlepart, and exports a point layer with an integer ID field, intended for use in the Green View Index plugin.

name: Compute topographic luminance
desc: The script defines an execution context for the Terraform QGIS plugin to compute topographic luminance based on solar geometry. It calculates slope (in radians) and aspect (in radians) from a DEM layer using GDAL processing algorithms, then computes the cosine of solar illumination using solar zenith and azimuth angles. The results are stored as temporary raster files, and bands can be merged using GDAL merge. The context supports both in-memory and file-based processing, with logging and cancelation feedback for QGIS processing algorithms.

name: Compute slope class per drainage area
desc: The script computes mean slope and slope class categories for each drainage area polygon (Einzelflächen) using a digital elevation model (DGM). It obtains DGM tiles for the study area from a server (likely DGM1 NRW 2022), merges them, calculates slope, then performs zonal statistics to compute mean slope per polygon. A slope classification field is derived using threshold rules (1: ≤1°, 2: ≤4°, 3: ≤10°, 4: ≤14°, 5: >14°). The results are written back to the 'Einzelflächen' layer and spatialite database.

name: Delineate drainage catchments using Voronoi
desc: This QKan plugin script delineates drainage catchments around selected sewer pipes by generating Voronoi tessellations. It first cuts overlapping surface polygons in the 'flaechen' table using spatial SQL, then uses GRASS v.voronoi.skeleton to create Voronoi areas around pipes that are flagged as having rainwater connections. The resulting geometries are inserted into the 'tezg' table as new surface catchments with attributes from existing covered areas. The tool leverages QGIS processing, SpatiaLite, and GRASS algorithms to update the QKan drainage database.

name: Convert Bebauungsplan polygons to XPlanGML
desc: The script converts a QGIS polygon layer representing Bebauungsplan (local development plan) boundaries into the XPlanGML standard format for spatial planning. It collects polygons into a single multipart geometry, reprojects to a selected coordinate reference system, ensures counter-clockwise orientation, removes duplicate vertices, and drops Z/M values. An XML template is populated with user-provided metadata (plan name, number, municipality, legal status, date) and the cleaned geometry transformed to GML. The resulting XPlanGML document is compressed into a ZIP archive for use in xPlanBox and other planning systems.

name: Convert Bebauungsplan polygons to XPlanGML archive
desc: The script converts polygon vector layers representing development plan boundaries (Umringpolygone) into an XPlanGML 6.0 archive. It collects features, reprojects to a selected coordinate reference system, forces counterclockwise polygon order, removes duplicate vertices, drops Z/M values, and generates a GML MultiSurface geometry. It then constructs a complete XPlanAuszug XML document with metadata fields (name, number, municipality, AGS, plan type, legal status, etc.), assigns UUIDs, sets bounding box coordinates, and packs the GML into a ZIP archive.

name: Clip raster land-use plan by polygon
desc: The script clips a raster land-use plan layer to the boundaries of a polygon vector layer. It first removes all fields except necessary ones from the polygon layer, then densifies polygon edges using a maximum segment length of 0.01. The raster is clipped using GDAL's clip raster by mask layer tool, cropping to the cutline and optionally setting the first palette index (0) as NoData. The result is a new clipped raster file.

name: Subtract polygon from raster plan
desc: The script subtracts a polygon area from a raster plan by creating a difference mask from the raster extent and the polygon, then clipping the raster with that mask. It first generates an extent layer from the input raster, retains the polygon's geometry and segments it, computes the difference between the extent and the polygon, and finally clips the raster using the resulting mask. Optionally, palette index 0 is set as no data value.

name: Convert land use plan boundary to XPlanGML
desc: This script converts a polygon vector layer containing the boundary(ies) of a land use plan (Flächennutzungsplan) into an XPlanGML-compliant XML file (xplan.gml) packaged in a ZIP archive. It performs geometric processing (collect, reproject, force CCW, remove duplicate vertices, drop Z/M) and then builds an XPlan XML structure with user-supplied metadata (plan name, number, municipality, legal status, etc.) and the geometry. The output is a ZIP file containing the XPlan archive for subsequent use in planning systems like xPlanBox.

name: Convert landscape plan to XPlanGML
desc: The script converts landscape plan boundary polygons from a QGIS vector layer into an XPlanGML 6.0 archive (ZIP file). It collects input polygon features, reprojects to a selected coordinate reference system, enforces counter-clockwise vertex order, removes duplicate vertices, drops Z/M values, extracts geometry as GML3, and embeds it into an XPlanGML template with user-supplied metadata (name, municipality, plan type, legal status, etc.). The final output is a ZIP file containing the xplan.gml document.

name: Replace XPlanGML spatial scope polygons
desc: The script replaces the spatial scope polygon of an XPlanGML planning document with new polygon geometries from a QGIS vector layer. It reprojects the polygons to the GML's CRS, ensures proper orientation and topology (CCW, duplicate removal, drop Z/M), generates GML3 geometry, updates boundedBy elements, and replaces the raeumlicherGeltungsbereich element in the XML tree. The output is a new XPlanGML file with the updated spatial boundary.

name: Map point density with tessellation grid
desc: The script generates an intensity grid map from point or line vector layers. It creates a tessellation grid (rectangle, diamond, hexagon, triangle, or fisher net) based on user-defined width/height and extent, aggregates point counts or line lengths within each cell using native QGIS processing algorithms, optionally clips the grid to a mask polygon, and styles the result with a graduated color ramp (Jenks classification) and heatmap mode for point layers. The final styled layer is added to the QGIS map.

name: Extract BD TOPO topographic data
desc: The script extracts topographic vector data from the BD TOPO® WFS service based on a user-defined extent. It allows selecting specific layers, applies clipping and reprojection, optionally saves output to file formats (GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON) and adds styled layers to the QGIS project.

name: Network temporal kernel density estimation
desc: The script implements a Network Temporal Kernel Density Visualization (NTKDV) algorithm as a QGIS plugin. It processes input point events with timestamps, downloads the road network from OpenStreetMap for the data extent, splits the network into equal-length lixels, projects points onto the network to compute distances, and applies temporal kernel density estimation along the network. Results are saved as multiple GeoPackage line layers (one per time slice), each styled with a graduated color ramp representing kernel density values.

name: Network Kernel Density Visualization
desc: Downloads OpenStreetMap road network for the extent of input point layer, splits road edges into lixel segments, projects input points onto nearest edges, computes network-constrained kernel density estimation using a specified bandwidth, lixel size, and kernel type, and outputs a graduated line vector layer colored by density value.

name: Cluster points by distance
desc: The script performs distance-based clustering of point features. It takes a point vector layer and a buffer distance in meters. The workflow: creates a spatial index, buffers points, dissolves buffers to form clusters, assigns a unique cluster ID using field calculator, counts points per cluster via spatial join with summary, transfers cluster ID and count back to original points, and renames the count field to a user-specified name. The output is a point layer with cluster membership (CLUSTER_ID) and cluster size (CLUSTER_SIZE) attributes.

name: Generate aerial perspective hillshade
desc: The script creates an aerial perspective effect on a hillshade raster by dynamically adjusting contrast based on elevation. It calculates DEM statistics to determine elevation min and max, converts the input hillshade to Float32, and applies a contrast transformation formula that decreases contrast in lower elevations and increases it in higher elevations using user-defined min and max contrast parameters. The intermediate result is then normalized to 0-255 byte range, producing the final aerial perspective hillshade raster output.

name: Generate Grid-Based Point Visibility Offset
desc: The algorithm creates a multi-scale grid of points over a user-defined extent and assigns a visibility offset attribute to each point in an input vector layer based on proximity to the nearest grid point at each zoom level. It generates a single point layer with a new attribute that controls feature visibility in webmaps, enabling dynamic display adjustment as the user zooms.

name: Create shaded relief with aerial perspective
desc: The script generates two hillshade layers (top and bottom) from a user-provided DEM using two light sources at adjustable angles, applying an aerial perspective effect that enhances contrast for higher elevations. It computes DEM and hillshade statistics, then uses raster calculator to apply a contrast formula based on elevation. The output rasters are post-processed with brightness/contrast filters and blend modes for overlay in QGIS.

name: Identify helicopter landing zones
desc: The script identifies possible helicopter landing zones (HLZs) based on slope suitability and land cover classes. It downloads elevation data (Copernicus GLO‑30 or USGS 10m DEM) and land cover raster for a user‑defined area of interest (lat/lng, point, or polygon), clips them to the AOI, computes a Helicopter Landing Suitability (HLS) raster using slope caution and limit thresholds, then locates suitable touchdown points of a given diameter. Outputs include an HLZ point vector layer and an HLS raster, both with predefined styles.

name: Identify helicopter landing zones
desc: The script identifies potential helicopter landing zones (HLZs) by processing an Area of Interest (AOI). It downloads DEM data (Copernicus GLO-30 or USGS 3DEP 1m/10m/1/9 arc-second) and land cover raster (Living Atlas lulctimeseriesv003 2025 collection) for the AOI, mosaics and clips them to the AOI boundary, computes slope from the DEM, reclassifies slope into caution (< slope_caution) and limit (< slope_limit) categories, and reclassifies land cover based on suitable classes (e.g., 5,8,11). Combining these produces an HLS (Helicopter Landing Suitability) raster with values 0 (unsuitable), 1 (caution), 2 (suitable). It then vectorizes HLS pixels, filters by minimum area (based on TDP diameter), dissolves adjacent suitable areas, and computes centroids as final HLZ point locations. Output points are styled via QML files.

name: QGIS workflow: Data Filtering, Data management
desc: This workflow contains 523 core geospatial operations, including Data Filtering, Data management, Data extraction, Vector spatial analysis. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Fetch building footprints from OSM
desc: The script downloads building footprints from OpenStreetMap via Overpass API for a user-defined extent, reprojects to a target Cartesian CRS, applies a buffer to the extent, snaps geometries, dissolves them, and assigns a default height attribute. It outputs a building vector layer with a HISTORY field for tracking.

name: Fetch SRTM Elevation Data
desc: The script downloads SRTM GL1 elevation data tiles from NASA Earthdata (e4ftl01.cr.usgs.gov) for a user-specified extent, merges them into a single raster using gdal:merge, optionally warps to a target CRS using gdal:warpreproject, clips to a buffered extent with gdal:cliprasterbyextent, and converts to elevation points via native:pixelstopoints. The outputs are a digital elevation model (DEM) raster and optionally a vector point layer with elevation attributes.

name: Initialize elevation point altitude
desc: The script initializes elevation points for noise modeling by taking an optional point layer, reprojecting it to a Cartesian coordinate reference system, and optionally setting the Z value from a user-specified field. It then adds standardized fields: a primary key (PK) as a sequential integer, a HISTORY field recording the current process, and an alti field containing the altitude derived from the point geometry's Z coordinate. The output is a point layer suitable for subsequent H-RISK noise modeling steps.

name: Initialize Noise Receiver Points
desc: The script initializes receiver point features for noise modeling. It takes an input point layer, optionally uses the geometry's z-values or assigns a default elevation, reprojects to a target Cartesian CRS, and adds attribute fields 'PK' (sequential integer), 'HISTORY' (current process identifier), and 'alti' (elevation from geometry). The output is a receiver point layer with consistent attributes and coordinate system.

name: Initialize road noise modelling attributes
desc: The script initializes road line features for traffic noise modelling according to CNOSSOS-EU. It re-projects the input layer to a Cartesian CRS, sets Z values (existing or a default height), and adds required fields with default values. These fields include vehicle counts and speeds for light, medium, heavy, moped, and motorcycle categories across day, evening, and night periods, octave-band sound power levels, pavement type, temperature, studded tyre parameters, junction distance/type, slope, and traffic direction. The output is a feature sink with the prepared road layer.

name: Calculate road traffic noise emissions
desc: The script calculates noise emission levels on road features using the NoiseModelling software integrated into QGIS. It reads a road vector layer, prepares input arguments for a Groovy script that runs the noise modelling calculation (likely based on traffic data), executes the noise modelling process, and then joins the resulting noise level attributes (LW_ROADS) back to the original road features using a primary key. The output is a road layer with appended noise emission attributes and a history field recording the current processing step. The script optionally allows to just prepare the files without running the calculation.

name: Initialize sound source features
desc: The script initializes a vector layer of sound sources for noise modelling. It reprojects input lines or points to a Cartesian CRS, optionally sets Z values from geometry or a default, and adds/overwrites fields for octave-band sound power levels (day, evening, night) at frequencies 63–8000 Hz, source orientation angles, and a direction ID, along with a primary key and process history. Default values are assigned, ready for subsequent noise propagation calculations.

name: Format NoiseModelling receiver levels
desc: The script processes noise model output point layers from NoiseModelling (versions 4 or 5) containing receiver-level noise values for various periods. For NM4 outputs, it adds a PERIOD field, concatenates day, evening, night, and Lden layers into a single long-format layer. If group fields (e.g., PERIOD) are provided, the data is pivoted to wide format with period-specific columns. A HISTORY field is appended to record the processing step, and the final vector layer is colored using a graduated symbol on a chosen attribute (e.g., LDEN_LAEQ).

name: Noise isosurface contour generation
desc: The script generates noise isosurface vector layers from point sound level data and a triangle mesh using the NoiseModelling library. It takes a point layer with sound levels (e.g., LAEQ) and a polygon layer representing triangles (with PK_1, PK_2, PK_3, CELL_ID fields). It runs a Groovy script via NoiseModelling to compute contours at specified sound level breaks, smoothing with Bezier curves. The output is a contour vector layer with attributes including ISOLVL_MEAN, and post-processing applies graduated symbol rendering with specified opacity.

name: Fetch building footprints from tile map
desc: The script fetches building footprints from the Japanese Cyberjapan experimental vector tile map service within a specified extent, buffered area, and target coordinate reference system. It parses tile URLs, downloads vector tiles concurrently, applies affine transformations to adjust coordinates, merges layers, reprojects to the target CRS, snaps geometries, dissolves overlapping features, extracts by the original fetch extent, and initializes building attributes for noise modeling, outputting a processed building layer.

name: Fetch Japanese building footprints
desc: The script downloads building footprint vector tiles from the Japanese GSI BVMap service, applies affine transformations to convert tile coordinates to EPSG:3857, merges multiple tiles, reprojects to a target CRS, snaps and dissolves geometries, clips to a buffered fetch area, initializes building heights, and outputs a processed building layer.

name: Fetch elevation raster and points from Japan DEM
desc: The script downloads DEM tiles from the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan's XYZ tile service (DEM-10B, DEM-5A, DEM-5B, DEM-5C) based on a user-specified extent and selected grid resolution. It stitches the tiles into a GeoTIFF raster, clips to the buffered extent, optionally converts to a point vector layer, reprojects to the target CRS, and outputs an elevation raster and an elevation point layer with styling.

name: Fetch Elevation Points from Japan GSI
desc: The script fetches digital elevation data from Japan's GSI experimental DEM10b vector tile service. It first defines the user-provided extent and target CRS, then buffers the area. Using the tile map URL, it retrieves vector features at zoom level 18, transforms CRS to the target, extracts elevations from the 'alti' attribute to set Z-values, refines elevation points via an internal processing algorithm, and saves the points as a vector layer. It also rasterizes the raw elevation features into a raster DEM using the 'alti' field, applying a pixel size of 0.4 arc seconds and a pseudo-color symbology. Both vector and raster outputs are generated with postprocessing for visualization.

name: Fetch Japan road centerlines
desc: The script fetches road centerline vector data for Japan from the GSI experimental tile service. It takes a user-defined extent, buffers it, calculates required Web Mercator tiles at zoom level 16, downloads GeoJSON tiles concurrently, merges them, reprojects to a target Cartesian CRS, dissolves the lines, and processes them with the 'hrisk:initroad' algorithm to produce a final road centerline layer with history tracking.

name: Generate elevation points along lines
desc: The script generates evenly-spaced points along input line features at a specified interval and assigns a constant elevation (Z) value to each point. It uses 'pointsalonglines' to create points, then 'setzvalue' to set a constant height, and finally initializes the elevation points with a target CRS. The output is a point layer with elevation history metadata.

name: H-RISK noise modelling utilities
desc: Provides core utility functions for the H-RISK with Noisemodelling QGIS plugin, including managing CRS transformations, executing NoiseModelling workflows, downloading external resources, handling layer renderers, and generating tiling systems for spatial analysis.

name: Generate noise receiver cross-section points
desc: The script generates a vertical cross-section of noise receiver points along a given line for the H-RISK with noisemodelling plugin. It reprojects the input line layer to a Cartesian CRS, splits multipart features into singleparts, then runs pointsalonglines to create points at a specified horizontal interval. For each point, it generates multiple copies at heights ranging from a user‑defined minimum to maximum height, using the same interval as vertical spacing, via the setzvalue algorithm. The output is a PointZ layer with PK (primary key) and HISTORY fields, intended for noise propagation modeling.

name: Estimate building populations from raster
desc: The script estimates the population of each building by distributing population counts from a raster layer to building polygons. It first computes building centroids and projects them to match the population raster CRS, then samples raster values at centroid locations. The population per building is then calculated as (sampled raster value / total weight in that mesh) * building weight, where building weight is either the provided weight field or the building area. The output layer is a vector polygon layer with additional fields including mesh index, mesh code, number of buildings in mesh, total weight in mesh, population of mesh cell, and estimated population per building.

name: Estimate building populations
desc: The script estimates population for each building polygon by distributing the total population of a containing population polygon proportionally based on a building weight field (or building area if weight field not provided). It computes building centroids, reprojects them to the population layer CRS, joins population attributes, then aggregates building counts and total weight per population polygon. The output is a new building layer with estimated population and associated fields (population polygon ID, number of buildings in polygon, building weight, total weight in polygon, polygon population).

name: Summarize noise-related health risk
desc: The script aggregates building-level health risk indicators by noise exposure groups. It takes a building layer containing population and noise level (LDEN_LAEQ_max), optionally groups by noise level using specified breakpoints, and calculates sums of population, building count, building area, and health risk metrics (nHA, nHSD, nPatientIHD, nIncIHD, nDeathIHD). The output is a vector layer with grouped or ungrouped summaries.

name: Environmental noise propagation modelling
desc: The script executes environmental noise propagation models using the NoiseModelling library within QGIS. It prepares spatial input data—vector layers converted to GeoJSON and raster DEMs to ASCII format—then invokes a Java-based Groovy script to run noise propagation calculations. Progress and console outputs are streamed to the QGIS processing feedback, and results are collected from the output directory.

name: H-RISK noise modelling utilities
desc: This script provides utility functions for the H-RISK QGIS plugin, including coordinate transformation, file downloading, vector layer processing (dissolve, pivot wider, output with history), and parameter management, to support risk assessment and noise modelling workflows.

name: Waterfall Detection using Fuzzy Logic and OSM
desc: The algorithm detects waterfalls using a fuzzy logic approach. It computes slope from a DEM and uses flow accumulation to identify steep drainage areas. It queries OpenStreetMap for known waterfalls, reprojects and buffers them, then uses spatial joins to influence fuzzy scoring. Points generated from a mask of areas with slope >= 10 degrees and flow accumulation >= 1000 cells are sampled for slope, variance of slope, and flow accumulation values. A fuzzy value (m_value) is computed for each point based on flow accumulation, slope, error, minimum thresholds, and proximity to known OSM waterfalls. Points below an alpha cut are discarded, and only the highest-scoring detection per spatial group is retained. The output is a vector layer of waterfall detections with m_value.

name: Calculate Sub-Irrigation Region of Influence Area
desc: The script determines the area within the region of influence of a sub-irrigation tile network. It buffers the tile line layer by half the specified drain spacing, intersects the buffer with a field boundary polygon layer (optionally using selected features), adds geometry attributes, computes area in acres, dissolves the result, and outputs a vector layer named 'Region of Influence'.

name: Generate sub-irrigation zones from DEM
desc: The script creates sub-irrigation zones from a DEM by calculating elevation-based zones at 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 foot intervals. It converts the raster to points, computes zone indices using minimum elevation or a user-specified base value, rasterizes the points back to zone rasters, polygonizes each raster to vector polygons, and generates a hillshade for visualization. Outputs include four raster zone layers, four vector zone layers, and a terrain hillshade.

name: Map FLO-2D simulation outputs
desc: The script is a QGIS plugin that creates maps from FLO-2D model output files. It reads simulation results (e.g., DEPTH.OUT, VELFP.OUT) and configuration files (CONT.DAT) to determine simulation type (flood, sediment, mudflow, two-phase). It generates raster maps styled with depth/velocity color ramps, vector flood extents, hydrodynamic risk maps, storm drain plots, and print layouts.

name: Generate flood hazard maps from FLO-2D
desc: The script converts FLO-2D ASCII output files (e.g., flood depth, velocity, maximum deposition, ground elevation) into georeferenced raster layers, creates flood extent vectors, and applies predefined styles to visualize flood hazard maps. It reads point XYZ ASCII data, determines cell size and raster dimensions, writes GeoTIFFs, and applies color ramps for different output types (flood depth, velocity, risk, bed difference, etc.). It also generates SVG-symbolized velocity vector layers from point data.

name: Export vector symbology for Illustrator
desc: The script processes QGIS vector layers for export to Adobe Illustrator via the PlugX plugin. It clips layers to the project extent, reprojects to project CRS, then exports individual shapefiles per category/range for categorized and graduated renderers, or a single shapefile for single symbol renderers. JSON metadata files with symbology information and associated graphic assets are generated.

name: Health risk assessment using noise modelling
desc: The script supports health risk assessment by providing utility functions for a QGIS processing algorithm. It integrates with the NoiseModelling tool to execute noise simulation commands, handles input parameters such as CRS, extent, and vector layers, downloads necessary data, performs GIS operations (e.g., dissolve, validity check), and processes output features with history tracking.

name: Delineate urbanized area from street map
desc: The script delineates an urbanized area polygon from a street vector layer. It rasterizes the streets with a specified resolution, fills background NoData cells with a value of 1, polygonizes the raster to create polygons for streets (DN=10) and open spaces (DN=1), computes areas, extracts streets and small open spaces (area below a user-defined threshold), and merges them into a single urbanized area layer.

name: Build AOI centroid layer
desc: The script builds a temporary centroid point layer from AOI features stored in a QGIS project file. It filters features by AOI IDs, dissolves them into a single polygon, computes the centroid, and returns the centroid point layer for downstream mapping or analysis.

name: Generate Sample Frames from Cross Sections
desc: The script generates sample frames by splitting a polygon vector layer using cross-section lines. It extends the cross-section lines by a tiny distance, then splits the polygon layer with those lines to create multiple polygon features. Each feature is assigned a sample frame ID and a sequential display label, and saved to an output file. The process runs as a background QGIS task.

name: Extract elevation zones from DEM
desc: The script vectorizes a raster by thresholding on a specified value (with optional inverse condition), then polygonizes the result, computes area and elevation attributes, and applies geometric refinements (buffer, simplify, smooth, fix geometries) before exporting to a GeoPackage. It is designed for processing DEM/LiDAR elevation data to extract elevation zones (e.g., areas above/below a certain elevation) as vector polygons, with small polygon removal.

name: Calculate reservoir area-volume curves
desc: The QGIS plugin CAV calculates the area and volume of a digital terrain model at specified elevation intervals, generating elevation-area-volume curves and tables. It processes a user-selected DEM raster (and optional polygon mask) by iterating over a user-defined elevation range using the 'Raster Surface Volume' algorithm. The outputs include a temporary vector table (cota, area, volume), a matplotlib graph, and optionally a PDF report with fitted polynomial and logarithmic curves (R² values) and descriptive statistics. When two DEMs are provided (reference and updated reservoirs), it compares them, generates a difference raster, and performs a t-test for significant sedimentation change.

name: Buffer vector layer geometry
desc: Buffer vector layer features using safe geometry operations, dissolve, and simplification.

name: Map land cover to Talsim categories
desc: The script maps various land use/land cover datasets (ATKIS, LBM-DE2021, ESA WorldCover) to Talsim hydrological model land use categories. It provides a QGIS dialog for user-selected input, merges and clips vector layers for ATKIS, reprojects and resamples ESA raster, polygonizes, dissolves, and classifies based on CSV lookup tables. Output is a GeoPackage with classified and dissolved land use layers added to the QGIS project.

name: Classify soil types and bulk density
desc: The script downloads ISRIC SoilGrids clay, silt, sand, and bulk density data for a user-defined extent, then classifies soil types using the German soil texture classification (Bodenarten) by comparing the particle size fractions to predefined polygon boundaries. It also assigns bulk density classes based on threshold values. The results are combined into a single vector layer containing soil type codes, thicknesses, and bulk density classes for each soil horizon, exported as a GeoPackage for use in the QTalsim hydrological model.

name: Sub-basin hydrologic parameter preprocessing
desc: The script processes a sub-basins layer in QGIS to compute for each sub-basin the maximum and minimum elevation from a DEM, area in hectares, average imperviousness (optional), and the longest flow path geometry with length and rotation. The results are saved to a GeoPackage and optionally exported to a SQLite database (Talsim format) or an ASCII .EZG file for use with the Talsim hydrological model.

name: QGIS workflow: Data processing, Spatial Analysis And Modeling
