desc: This workflow contains 155 core geospatial operations, including Data processing, Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Geometry, QgsGeometry.fromPolylineXY. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Triangular transformation between D48/GK and D96/TM
desc: The script performs triangular coordinate transformation of vector layers between the Slovenian national coordinate systems D48/GK and D96/TM using the statewide triangular transformation model version 4.0. It processes input vector layers, optionally fixes geometries, transforms each vertex based on the triangle it falls in, assigns the target CRS, and saves the new layer with updated metadata.

name: Grid-shift urban cluster extraction
desc: The script performs a grid-based cluster analysis of urban vs non‐urban areas using a land cover layer (e.g., Urban Atlas). It creates a base grid and three shifted versions (horizontal, vertical, diagonal), intersects them with the land cover, dissolves the results, and selects fully covered grid cells (area > 0.999). These representative cells are joined with group‐statistics CSV files from external k‑means clustering (GeoDa) to extract and merge cluster groups, yielding two urban/non‑urban systems and their interface zone. Output layers include the shifted grids, intersections, joined grids, and the final cluster extraction layers.

name: Create connectivity land cover raster
desc: The script creates a unified land cover raster for Graphab connectivity analysis by rasterizing vector features (with buffer and encoding options) and merging them with reclassified raster layers into a single raster with consistent projection, resolution, extent, and nodata value.

name: Reclassify raster land cover codes
desc: The script provides a dialog for loading a raster layer, extracting its unique pixel values, and allowing the user to define a reclassification mapping (encoding) of old values to new integer codes. It runs QGIS processing algorithms 'rasterlayeruniquevaluesreport' and 'listuniquevalues' to obtain the unique values, then populates an editable table. The user can assign new codes, optionally setting nodata, and the dialog returns a dictionary with the raster layer, encoding map, and status for subsequent connectivity analysis.

name: QGIS workflow: Spatial Analysis And Modeling
desc: This workflow contains 1 core geospatial operations, including Spatial Analysis And Modeling. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Forest structure and biodiversity analysis
desc: The script implements tools for forest structure and biodiversity analysis using QGIS and GDAL. It includes algorithms for tree detection from Canopy Height Models (CHM) via local maxima (focalMaximaCHM, createTreeMap), habitat suitability interpolation (hsAnalysis using IDW and raster sampling), point-to-area conversion with buffering, biodiversity index calculation (Simpson's index with Gaussian kernel weighting), Getis-Ord Gi* hotspot analysis (go_gaussian) on tree attributes, and distance calculation to nearest features. The code processes vector and raster layers to derive tree maps, habitat suitability scores, biodiversity metrics, and spatial patterns, supporting forest inventory and ecological assessment.

name: Plan retention tree groups
desc: The script plans retention tree groups by extracting individual tree tops from a Canopy Height Model (CHM) and weighting ecological indicators such as phosphorus retention, depth to water index, tree diversity, and dead wood potential. It clips input rasters and vectors to the planning area, performs spatial joins to assign forest grid and vegetation zone attributes to tree points, calculates distance to the nearest waterbody, and then applies the essence model to select retention trees based on weighted ecosystem service values. The outputs are a point layer of selected retention trees and a polygon layer of delineated retention tree groups.

name: Plan retention tree groups
desc: The script plans retention tree areas within harvesting area polygons by evaluating ecological indicators (tree diversity, heterogeneity, deadwood potential, depth-to-water) from vegetation zones, forest grid, canopy height model, and depth-to-water rasters. It applies user-specified weights to these indicators, deducts potential tree locations, calculates ecosystem service indicators, and performs spatial planning to propose retention tree groups. Outputs include a point layer of trees and a polygon layer of retention tree groups.

name: Identify retention tree areas from field data
desc: The script processes point tree data to create retention tree areas. It first buffers points to generate planning areas, then clips environmental raster and vector layers (DTW index, forest grid, vegetation zones, water bodies) and performs spatial joins and raster sampling. It computes ecosystem service weights (phosphorus retention, DTW, biodiversity, dead wood potential) using a custom model to select trees, outputting classified tree points. Finally, it aggregates selected trees into retention tree groups (polygons) and applies predefined styles.

name: Generate IMSGS Multi-scaled Grid
desc: The script generates a multi-scaled grid following the Indonesian Multi-scaled Grid System (IMSGS) standard. It accepts either an input vector layer for extent or a user-defined bounding box in WGS84. A grid resolution is selected from predefined options (30'x30' down to 5"x5"). The algorithm reprojects and fixes input geometries if provided, otherwise uses the bounding box coordinates. A fishnet grid is created over the transformed extent with the chosen resolution. Each cell is assigned an IMGSID code derived from its centroid coordinates using a hierarchical coding scheme based on latitude/longitude zones. Optionally, the grid can be clipped to the input vector layer. The output is a polygon layer with IMGSID field.

name: Assess Food Energy Carrying Capacity
desc: The script contains three QGIS processing algorithms that compute food energy carrying capacity based on the Indonesian Multi-scaled Grid System (IMSGS). The first algorithm calculates annual food energy needs per grid cell using population and a per capita energy value. The second algorithm distributes administrative-level food energy production to grid cells by intersecting with administrative boundaries and an environmental performance index layer, computing available energy. The third algorithm subtracts needs from availability and determines carrying capacity status (exceeded or not). Outputs are vector polygon layers with attributes like IMGSID, Population, AKEGrid, Energy_Available, Difference, and Status.

name: Water Carrying Capacity Assessment
desc: The script assesses water carrying capacity using the Indonesian Multi-scaled Grid System (IMSGS). It first computes water needs per grid cell by combining household water usage (population × standard need × correction factor) and vegetation water usage (area × crop intensity × water standard). It then calculates water availability per grid cell by distributing watershed-level total water availability proportionally to each grid cell's area-weighted environmental performance index. Finally, it joins the need and availability layers to compute the difference, classify status (Exceed/Not), and determine threshold population. Outputs are vector grid layers containing population, water needs, water availability, difference, status, and threshold.

name: Distribute Populations to Grid
desc: The script distributes population from administrative boundaries to an IMSGS grid layer using land cover and road layers to compute weights. It reprojects all input layers to EPSG:4326, clips the grid to the admin boundary, computes admin area, and aggregates by grid ID to assign the dominant admin name and population. For each admin subset, it intersects land cover (polygon) and road (line) layers, calculates area or length per feature, computes feature-level weights as (feature_measure/total_grid_measure) * user-specified weight, sums them per grid, then normalizes by administrative unit total weight. The final population per grid cell is calculated as (grid_weight/admin_total_weight) * population. The output is a vector grid polygon layer with fields IMGSID, WRT, WLC, WGrid, Wadmin, Admname, and Population.

name: Disaggregate Fluvial Corridor Polygons
desc: The script disaggregates a single input polygon into sub-polygons (discrete geomorphic units) along a centerline using a specified step distance. It merges multiple centerline features if needed, simplifies geometry, generates points along centerline and polygon boundary, computes the average width (distance from boundary to centerline doubled) at each centerline point, creates Voronoi polygons from centerline points, joins the width attribute, and clips by the original polygon to produce a disaggregated polygon layer with DGO_FID and DGO_WIDTH fields.

name: Delineate valley bottom polygons
desc: The script delineates valley bottom areas from a detrended DEM and a stream network. It first extracts pixels where detrended DEM height is between user-specified min and max heights. The stream network is simplified and a large buffer is created. The extracted raster is clipped to this buffer. Binary closing merges close objects, and a sieve filter removes small regions. The resulting raster is polygonized to produce valley bottom polygons, which are then simplified and smoothed. Outputs include a valley bottom raster and a valley bottom polygon layer.

name: Detrend DEM with stream network interpolation
desc: The script detrends a digital elevation model (DEM) by removing a trend surface derived from the stream network. It simplifies the stream network using Douglas-Peucker, generates points along lines at a given distance, computes focal mean DEM values at these points (15x15 window), creates Voronoi polygons, rasterizes the Voronoi polygons with these values, and subtracts the trend raster from the original DEM.

name: Remove small polygonal objects
desc: The algorithm processes an input polygon layer by first extracting features where a specified field equals a given value, then removes polygons with area less than a minimum threshold and eliminates holes with area less than a minimum hole threshold. The result is a cleaned polygon layer.

name: Fluval network inflection disaggregation
desc: The script disaggregates a sequenced line network (e.g., a river centerline) into planform segments on the basis of inflection points. It simplifies and smooths the input lines, runs planform metrics (fct:planformmetrics) to detect inflection points by maximum distance, minimum amplitude, and maximum angle, and outputs the disaggregated line network, inflection point vector, and inflection line vector.

name: Attribute polylines with elevation and slope
desc: The script attributes input polyline features with elevation and slope statistics derived from a digital elevation model (DEM). It first adds a unique identifier field, then drapes the polylines onto the DEM to assign Z coordinates. Using a custom linestring Z slope tool, it calculates slope along each polyline. It computes summary statistics (first, last, mean, median, stdev, min, max) for both Z (elevation) and slope values, and joins these attributes back to the original line features. The output is a vector layer with appended elevation and slope attributes.

name: Transform point measurements to river curvilinear coordinates
desc: The script converts point measurements from Cartesian (X,Y) to curvilinear orthogonal (S,N) coordinates along a river. It first generates a bounding polygon using concave hull on selected points, creates a river centerline via Voronoi skeleton, splits the polygon into left and right sides, computes the S coordinate as distance along the centerline (points along lines), and calculates the N coordinate as the nearest distance to the centerline signed by side (positive left, negative right). The same transformation is applied to a user-defined regular point grid, and an IDW interpolation can be performed on a chosen attribute field. Output shapefiles contain the transformed points with S and N coordinates.

name: Create web map viewer from QGIS project
desc: The script configures and exports a QGIS project into a web map viewer format. It processes vector layers to MBTiles and raster layers to cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs (COG). For vector layers, it applies cleaning steps (remove duplicate vertices, fix geometries, force right-hand rule, clip, multipart to singlepart) and writes MBTiles using ogr2ogr or native QGIS processing, with zoom-level control. Raster layers are rendered to RGBA, clipped to extent, reprojected to EPSG:3857, and translated to COG. Outputs are placed in a specified directory for use in a web viewer.

name: Extract CORINE land cover roughness polygons
desc: The script extracts CORINE land cover polygons for a user-defined bounding box polygon in QGIS. It first reprojects the input mask layer, constructs a query to a CORINE API, downloads polygons, buffers to fix geometry, reprojects to input CRS, clips to mask, joins a roughness lookup table (containing z0 and d), and outputs a vector layer with land cover IDs, roughness length, and displacement height attributes. The script also enables project snapping settings and applies a style to the output layer.

name: Create bounding box from lat/lon
desc: The script generates a square polygon bounding box centered at a user-specified latitude and longitude point with a given extent (in meters). It first validates the user-selected coordinate reference system to ensure it is metric and compatible with WAsP, suggests the appropriate UTM zone if mismatched, creates a point in WGS84, reprojects to the chosen CRS, buffers the point by the extent to form a square polygon, and outputs the polygon layer with a predefined style. The output is a vector layer named 'Bounding box' for use in wind resource assessment workflows.

name: Extract landcover roughness polygons
desc: The script downloads ESA CCI landcover raster (or GWA4 WorldCover) selected by the user, clips it to a buffered input polygon, polygonizes the raster into a vector layer, and joins it with a roughness lookup table to assign roughness length (z0) and displacement height (d) attributes. The output is a vector polygon layer named 'ESA-CCI landcover polygons', styled for use in WAsP wind energy modeling.

name: Save WAsP boundary lines
desc: The script saves a 'no attribute' or boundary line layer (LineString geometry) to a WAsP .map file for use in wind resource assessment. It checks that the CRS is not geographic, optionally converts polygons to lines, drops Z values, and splits multiparts. It reads an EPSG-WAsP lookup table to set the projection header, then writes the map file with two fixed points, a scaling factor, and the coordinates of each line feature.

name: Convert elevation lines to WEng raster
desc: The script converts elevation contour lines to a raster in WEng .grd format for wind energy assessment using WAsP. It first checks that the input vector layer is in a metric CRS and that the output raster dimensions (based on horizontal grid spacing) are below 1000x1000 cells. It uses TIN interpolation to create a raster from the line geometry and an elevation attribute (e.g., 'ELEV'), fills nodata, and exports via GDAL. An optional vector extent layer can be provided to align with roughness maps.

name: Convert roughness polygons to WEng raster
desc: The script converts roughness polygons (vector with 'z0' attribute) to a raster with given grid spacing and saves it as a WEng .grd file for wind resource assessment. It uses gdal:rasterize to rasterize the polygon layer and gdal:translate to export as .grd. The output is a roughness raster file in WEng format.

name: Extract GWA elevation contours
desc: The script extracts elevation contour lines from a Global Wind Atlas (GWA) digital elevation model for a user-provided polygon area. It downloads a cloud-optimized GeoTIFF (either SRTM Viewfinder-corrected DEM or Copernicus DEM 30 m) via vsicurl, clips it to the extended bounding box, handles zero elevations by adjusting them to near-zero, and then generates contour lines at a specified interval and offset using GDAL contour. If the terrain variation falls below the interval, it produces a boundary line with the mean elevation. The output is a vector layer with an 'ELEV' attribute, styled for use in WAsP mapping.

name: Generate roughness map from ESA WorldCover
desc: The script generates a WAsP-compatible roughness map from ESA WorldCover 2020 landcover data. It downloads WorldCover tiles for a user-defined polygon area, merges and clips rasters, resamples to a coarser resolution, polygonizes, and joins a roughness lookup table to assign roughness length (z0) and displacement height (d) attributes. The output is a vector layer with polygons representing landcover classes and their roughness parameters.

name: Export contours to 3D CAD
desc: The script exports contour vector lines to a 3D DXF file preserving elevation values from a specified attribute field. It first checks if the input is already 3D; if not, it uses GRASS v.to.3d to assign Z values from the selected numeric field. Then it exports to DXF using native:dxfexport with configurable CAD version and CRS, outputting a 3D CAD file.

name: Global Curve Number Calculation
desc: The algorithm computes a Curve Number (CN) raster for a study area polygon using ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m) land cover and ORNL HYSOG tiled hydrologic soil groups. It downloads required soil tiles, fills nodata, reprojects, aligns rasters, applies a CN lookup table based on hydrologic condition and antecedent runoff condition, and clips the result to the study area. Optional outputs are ESA land cover and soil group rasters. Summary statistics include mean CN.

name: Optimized parcel division
desc: The script implements an optimized parcel division algorithm that processes input polygon features representing land parcels, splitting them into smaller lots based on a desired lot width. It treats rectangular polygons directly and approximates irregular polygons with oriented minimum bounding boxes to compute division lines. It generates horizontal (midline) and perpendicular division lines, clips them to the parcel boundaries, splits polygons, and performs two passes of merging small polygons below a threshold percentage of average area to avoid slivers. The output is a polygon layer of subdivided parcels with the original attributes.

name: Generate tree planting point patterns
desc: The script generates tree planting points with five spatial patterns (triangular/quincunx, rectangular/square, five of diamonds, keyline, random distribution) inside polygon features. It applies a user-defined border margin, parses a flexible spacing string to determine planting distances, and optionally uses a DEM raster to perform automatic slope analysis, sampling slope values at each point and adding a 'slope' field. For the keyline pattern, it generates contours and stream networks from the DEM. The output is a point vector layer with attributes id, pattern, x, y, and optionally slope, along with a comprehensive report of counts per pattern and planting density per hectare.

name: Delineate watershed basin and stream order
desc: The script delineates a watershed basin from a DEM and a pour point using GRASS GIS algorithms (r.fill.dir, r.watershed, r.water.outlet, r.to.vect). It smooths the basin boundary and clips an input stream network to the basin. Three Strahler stream order calculations are performed: standard (sthr_original), main channel extension along longest paths (sthr_extend), and extension to all headwaters (sthr_final). The outputs are a watershed basin polygon and a stream line layer containing the three Strahler order fields.

name: Extract and order stream network
desc: The script extracts a stream network from a DEM using GRASS GIS r.watershed and r.stream.extract, applies smoothing, and calculates Strahler and Shreve stream orders. It resamples the DEM if raster size exceeds 100 million cells. The output is a line vector layer with Strahler and Shreve order attributes.

name: Bathymetric data anisotropic IDW interpolation
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin for bathymetric data interpolation. It takes point measurements of depth, a centerline vector, and an ROI polygon. It computes S (along-stream) and N (cross-stream) coordinates and flow direction for each point. Then, it generates a regular grid of sample points within the ROI extent and interpolates depth values using an anisotropic Inverse Distance Weighting (EIDW) method that accounts for anisotropy ratio and max distance. The result is rasterized to a DEM and optionally evaluated with RMSE against original points.

name: Create bathymetry sampling points grid
desc: This script creates a constant raster grid with user-defined extent and pixel size, then samples one point per pixel in the center using the 'pixelstopoints' algorithm. The sampled points layer is prepared for interpolation by adding fields for S, N, and Interpolated values. Additionally, it converts a raster output to a layer and assigns a nodata value to band 1, intended for post-processing of bathymetric flow DEM outputs.

name: Raster-point difference RMSE calculation
desc: The script validates a raster surface by comparing it to point measurements using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). It clips the input point layer to a specified extent, samples raster values at the clipped point locations using the QGIS native raster sampling tool, and aggregates the actual values (from a point attribute field) and predicted values (sampled raster). It then computes the RMSE between the two arrays and prints the mean squared difference and RMSE. The processed point layer with sampled raster values is returned and named 'Data validation - differences'.

name: Convert vector layers to GPX format
desc: The algorithm converts any vector layer (points, lines, polygons) to a GPX file with tracks. It first fixes geometries, then converts polygons to lines if necessary, dissolves features unless a name field is specified, optionally splits multipart features into single parts, and refactors fields to add a 'name' attribute from a user-defined display name or an attribute field. The output is written using QgsVectorFileWriter with GPX-specific options (FORCE_GPX_TRACKS, GPX_USE_EXTENSIONS). The resulting file is a GPX file suitable for Garmin devices.

name: Export QGIS data to ur-scape
desc: The script exports an active QGIS layer (raster or vector) to the ur-scape data format by converting it into grid CSV files with metadata, categories, data values and masks. It handles rasterization of vectors, reprojection to EPSG:4326, aggregation of raster cells (weighted average or summary), no-data masking, and special outputs for municipal budget and road network reachability graphs. Output files are location-specific and the script also updates layers.csv to register the layer.

name: Hexagon binning point count
desc: The script performs hexagonal binning on an input point layer using H3 spatial indexing. It projects the layer to geographic coordinates (EPSG:4617), generates hexagon grids at user-specified resolution covering the layer's extent, counts points within each hexagon, writes shapefiles with a 'numpoints' field, and applies graduated color symbology. The output hexagon layers are added to the QGIS project.

name: Assemble Raster and Point Cloud Layers
desc: The script merges raster and point cloud layers from a specified group in the QGIS project. It iterates over child layers, separates them into GDAL raster layers and PDAL point cloud layers, then runs the 'gdal:merge' or 'pdal:merge' processing algorithms using Float32 data type and temporary output. On completion, the merged temporary layer is added to the map with the name 'Assemble' using the appropriate provider ('gdal' for raster, 'pdal' or 'copc' for point cloud).

name: Geotagged photo import and 360° viewer
desc: The script provides a QGIS plugin to import geotagged photos into a GeoPackage point layer, extract EXIF metadata (timestamps, azimuth), add custom attributes from filename patterns (road number, street, section, mileage), and launch a 360° equirectangular image viewer docked in QGIS for selected features. Workflow includes creating/updating GeoPackage, removing duplicates, and interactive map selection tools.

name: View street-level panoramic photos
desc: The script implements a QGIS dockable widget for viewing equirectangular images associated with point features from a vector layer. It loads the image file based on a filename attribute, extracts metadata (timestamp, road name, street name, section name), and uses OpenGL to render the panoramic image with interactive yaw rotation. It updates a map canvas rubber band arrow to indicate viewing direction, computes hotspots by buffering the selected point in EPSG:3857 with mercator compensation, filters adjacent points, and places clickable navigation markers. It supports screenshots and fullscreen toggling, and reprojects coordinates between layer CRS, EPSG:4326, and EPSG:3857 as required.

name: Clean and Snap Points to Roads
desc: The script processes measurement points and OSM road data. It optionally converts multipart road segments to single parts and removes roads tagged as 'construction' or 'proposed'. Then it snaps the points to the nearest road segment within a user-defined tolerance. The output is a point layer with snapped geometry.

name: Extract spot heights from DEM
desc: The script identifies local maximum elevation points (spot heights) from a DEM. It first uses a circular neighborhood maximum filter (r.neighbors) to find the maximum elevation in a user-defined neighborhood around each cell. The original DEM is then compared to the neighborhood maximum via raster calculator, retaining only cells where the values are equal (local maxima) and setting others to zero. Zero cells are set to null, and the resulting raster is converted to point features. A coastline polygon extracts onland points. The output is a point layer of spot heights with an elevation attribute.

name: Disconnected Network Segments
desc: The script identifies topologically connected and disconnected line segments of a river network. Starting from an input river mouth point layer, it iteratively selects vertices that intersect already-selected vertices to propagate connectivity through the network. It then separates the line features into disconnected (no path to river mouth) and connected segments, outputting two vector layers.

name: Detect attribute discontinuities in network
desc: The script identifies discontinuities of a user-selected attribute across a line vector network. It splits the network at intersections, extracts endpoints, and detects nodes where the attribute changes or becomes null. Using buffer and intersection, it locates adjacent segments with differing values, then merges all discontinuity points into a single output point layer.

name: Classify dangles by overlapping selected layers
desc: The script identifies dangles (line sections that do not connect to other lines) in a vector network layer, then checks spatial overlap of these dangles with multiple user-selected layers. Dangles are intersected with a merged overlay of the selected layers (points buffered, lines buffered, polygons merged). Two point output layers are generated: DANGLES_Overlapping (dangles that overlap or intersect) and DANGLES_Non_Overlap (dangles with no overlap).

name: Extract Springs
desc: The algorithm extracts headwater springs from a vector line network. It first dissolves the network, identifies dangling vertices (ends), splits dissolved lines at these vertices, extracts line segments intersecting dangling points, calculates their length, filters by user-specified length threshold (minimum, maximum, or all), removes segments intersecting river mouth buffer to exclude false positives, and outputs the filtered headwater lines and corresponding points with original attributes.

name: Classify pseudo-node connectivity
desc: The script analyzes pseudo-nodes (break points) in an input line layer and classifies them based on their spatial relationship with vertices of user-selected map layers. It first extracts pseudo-nodes via an internal algorithm, then creates a point layer from all vertices of the selected layers, tagging each vertex with its source layer name. Using spatial join operations, it splits the pseudo-nodes into two outputs: a non-overlapping layer containing pseudo-nodes disjoint from all vertices, and an overlapping layer containing pseudo-nodes that intersect one or more vertices, retaining the source layer identifier.

name: Join features by transit time
desc: The script performs a spatial join between two vector layers based on transit time computed using the OpenRouteService Matrix API. For each input feature, it calculates the travel time to all features in the join layer using a user-specified transport mode (walking, driving, cycling, etc.) and joins attributes from the closest feature within a min-max time range. It outputs a new layer with appended fields and optionally a travel time field.

name: Convert polygons to singlepart lines
desc: The script converts an input polygon layer to a single-part line layer. It first applies 'qgis:polygonstolines' to extract polygon boundaries as lines, then 'qgis:multiparttosingleparts' to split multipart geometries into individual segments. It reassigns a unique integer 'fid' field to each resulting feature and transfers rendering properties (color) from the input layer to the output. The final output is a line layer suitable for further analysis.

name: Widen Taxiway Lines
desc: The script widens taxiway line features by buffering them with a user-specified distance, optionally dissolving and converting the result to linestrings. It reprojects the input to EPSG:3857, applies buffer, then reprojects back to EPSG:4326.

name: Calculate Longest Flow Path in Watershed
desc: The script extracts the longest hydrological flow path within a watershed basin. It selects stream channels that intersect the basin, extracts the first vertices of each stream segment, computes a distance matrix to the pour point to identify the farthest vertices, builds a shortest path network from the pour point to these vertices, and selects the path with the maximum travel cost (longest distance). The final output is a line vector layer of the longest stream, with an elongation ratio calculated and saved.

name: Watershed delineation and curve number
desc: The script delineates the upslope contributing watershed for a given discharge point from a filled DEM using SAGA upslope area algorithm, then processes the vector watershed polygon (fixing geometries, dissolving). It clips the DEM and channel network to the watershed, generates contours, computes watershed statistics (area, perimeter, elevation stats), and calculates Curve Numbers by intersecting the watershed with soil and Corine land cover layers to produce CN map and classification polygons.

name: Locate nearest meteo stations
desc: The script locates the nearest meteorological stations to the centroid of an input basin polygon. It first computes polygon centroids, adds an autoincrement field, then runs a distance matrix to identify the k-nearest stations (default 4) from a predefined stations dataset. It then extracts those stations by location and joins the distance attributes to produce a final vector layer of the nearest stations.

name: shred layer into grid fragments
desc: The script is a QGIS plugin that divides a selected vector or raster layer into a grid of vertical strips, horizontal strips, or rectangular cells, clips the layer to each grid cell, and optionally shuffles the positions of the resulting vector fragments. It then removes the original layer from the project and deletes its file from disk.

name: Query cadastral parcels from WFS
desc: The script provides functions to interact with the Slovenian e-prostor WFS service for cadastral parcel data. It can load a list of parcel numbers for a given cadastral municipality (KO_ID), retrieve the geometry of a specific parcel and add it as a QGIS layer, select parcels intersecting a user-defined area with optional buffer, and load cadastral municipality codes from WFS or a local CSV file. It also manages layer metadata and flashes geometries on the map canvas.

name: Create habitat patches for connectivity
desc: The script is a QGIS dialog for creating habitat patches from raster or vector land cover data. It extracts unique pixel values from a raster, allows user selection of habitat codes, sets minimum area and maximum size thresholds, and passes these parameters to the Graphab processing algorithms to generate habitat layers for connectivity analysis.

name: Create Graphab habitat connectivity project
desc: The script provides a graphical user interface (dialog) for configuring and launching the 'graphab3:create_project' QGIS processing algorithm. It allows users to select a landscape raster (as a file or map layer), define habitat codes by selecting from unique raster values, optionally set patch size and maximum size thresholds, specify nodata value, project name, and output directory. Upon confirmation, it executes the processing algorithm to create a Graphab project for landscape connectivity analysis.

name: Merge rasterized vectors with custom encoding
desc: The script provides a dialog for rasterizing vector layers and merging them with custom pixel value reclassification. Users add vector and raster layers, define encoding to reassign pixel values, set output resolution and extent, then the tool rasterizes vectors, replaces codes on rasters, splits rasters by code groups, and merges them into a single output raster file. The result is loaded as a new raster layer in QGIS.

name: QGIS workflow: Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data import
desc: This workflow contains 102 core geospatial operations, including Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data import, Projection, Spatial Analysis And Modeling. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Detect and dissect polygon overlaps
desc: The script processes an input polygon layer to detect overlapping features. It first fixes geometries, adds an identification field, performs polygon self-intersection (SAGA) to identify overlapping areas, selects intersecting features, and optionally zooms to overlaps. If 'dissect' option is selected, it extracts the overlapping parts into a new polygon layer named 'Intersected'. If 'dissolve' option is selected, it assigns the overlapping slivers to adjacent polygons based on user-specified criteria (largest adjacent, smallest adjacent, or largest common boundary) and outputs a 'Dissolved' layer.

name: Area-weighted data comparison by grid
desc: The script calculates area-weighted averages of a data field from a polygon layer intersecting a grid layer. It renames input fields, computes polygon areas, performs an intersection, computes intersection areas, and then calculates a weighted sum grouped by grid cell ID. The result is a grid layer with an area-weighted average attribute.

name: Select adjacent cell coverage polygons
desc: The QGIS tool allows users to interactively select neighboring polygons from a coverage layer and identify associated point features. It first processes a point layer to generate Voronoi polygons (cell coverage zones), then provides a map tool where clicking a polygon selects all adjacent polygons up to a user-defined depth using spatial touching/intersection analysis. The selected polygons are highlighted with color-coded rubber bands. For the clicked polygon and each neighbor polygon, the tool extracts point features that fall inside them and copies the main point attributes along with each neighbor point's attributes to the system clipboard for external use.

name: Clean building footprints and generate Voronoi polygons
desc: The script cleans building polygon layers by deleting holes, removing null geometries, converting multipart to singlepart, renumbering duplicate IDs, and removing features with duplicate centroids. It then creates centroid points, generates Voronoi polygons from these centroids, buffers the original buildings, and clips the Voronoi polygons with the buffer. The cleaned buildings and Voronoi layer are saved as a GeoPackage for further accessibility analysis.

name: Generate hexagon grids with aggregated building attributes
desc: The script generates Voronoi polygons and hexagon grids from an input polygon layer for accessibility visualization. It computes centroids, optionally creates Voronoi diagrams clipped to a buffer, generates hexagon grids at multiple spacings, filters hexagons intersecting the input layer, assigns the nearest source ID from centroids, and aggregates building counts and numeric attribute sums per hexagon. The final dissolved hexagon layers and the Voronoi layer are saved as GeoPackage files and loaded into QGIS.

name: Compute slope unit segmentation metrics
desc: The script evaluates segmentation quality for slope units (SU) using aspect homogeneity derived from a DEM and landslide inventory data. It processes multiple SU polygon layers, computing area (A), density (D), aspect-based vector (V), spatial autocorrelation (I), and combined metric (F), then derives final segmentation score S and exports results as CSV files.

name: Create boundary mesh layer
desc: The script creates boundary conditions for a Telemac mesh by validating and processing input mesh, contour polygon, and boundary line/point layers. It checks boundary layer fields and spatial containment, extracts vertices if polygon input is used, runs an external Telemac script to assign boundary values, and outputs updated mesh files (.slf and .cli).

name: Extend mesh from extended contour
desc: The script extends an existing mesh layer by defining an extended contour and optional other meshes, islands, constraints, and refinement areas. It converts the input Selafin mesh to MED format, runs a SALOME meshing script to extend the mesh using the specified mesh size, growth rate, and engine, then converts the output back to Selafin format.

name: Geological deposit spatial analysis
desc: The script provides QGIS processing functions for spatial analysis of geological/mineral deposit data. Key methods include select by location and attributes, buffering, difference (ring creation), aggregation of features by geological stage (concatenating attributes like notation, description, era, series, deposit type), centroid extraction, vertex extraction, reprojection, merging and cleaning duplicates, network centrality (degree, closeness, betweenness, eigenvector) using GRASS, node extraction, shortest path (distance and time-based via GRASS), path reconstruction, closest/furthest point identification from polygons. Outputs are temporary vector layers (memory or temp files) for each operation.

name: Extract high altitude and steep slope areas
desc: The script processes a Digital Terrain Model (MDT) and a property boundary layer to generate vector polygons representing areas with altitude above 1800 meters and slope greater than 45 degrees. It first reprojects the MDT to a projected CRS, then applies binary thresholding to isolate elevations >=1800 m and slope >=45° using the LFTools plugin and native slope calculation. The resulting binary rasters are polygonized and filtered to keep pixels with value 1 (meeting criteria), then clipped to the property boundary. The outputs are two separate layers: one for altitude exceedance and one for slope exceedance, both symbolized with hatch patterns in post-processing.

name: Auxiliary Line to Water Body Polygon
desc: Converts an auxiliary line layer into a polygon representing a water body or permanent preservation area using a user-defined width, then clips it to the property boundary (ATI). The script reprojects the line to a UTM zone based on the layer centroid, dissolves it, buffers by half the specified width with flat end caps, reprojects back to EPSG:4674 (SIRGAS 2000), intersects with the ATI polygon, cleans geometries, and adds the resulting features to a destination layer starting with 'RIO' or 'SA'.

name: Create atlas coverage from line
desc: Generates atlas control points and polygon coverage along a line based on paper size, scale, and overlap. Computes real-world dimensions, creates points along the line at regular intervals with a step distance that accounts for map scale and paper long axis minus overlap, and then creates rotated rectangular polygons representing atlas page extents aligned to the line direction. The output point layer includes an 'angle' field for rotation and the polygon layer shows page footprints.

name: Process DTB raster for excavation impact map
desc: The script processes DTB (Digital Terrain Model) raster data for excavation polygon areas by clipping to expanded extents, resampling to a specified resolution, and converting to TIFF. It also includes utility functions for vector layer JSON conversion, reprojection, file moving, and mapping pore pressure curve names for Norwegian translations in tunnel damage assessment.

name: Compute distance to features or raster values
desc: This script computes a distance raster from either specified raster cell values or vector features. For raster inputs, it uses gdal:proximity with a list of target pixel values; for vector inputs, it first rasterizes the vector layer to match the reference raster extent and pixel size, then applies proximity. The output is a single-band raster where each cell's value represents the distance to the nearest target cell or feature, in the same units as the raster (if units=1).

name: Simplify flight plan waypoints
desc: The script simplifies a drone flight plan by reducing the number of waypoints while preserving photo spacing and coverage. It takes a CSV file containing waypoints with longitude, latitude, and altitude, a DEM raster, a projected CRS, and a tolerance value. The algorithm creates 3D points, samples DEM elevations, reprojects, generates a flight line, simplifies the line using the Visvalingam method, extracts vertices, creates buffers, spatially joins with the original points to select waypoints, and outputs a filtered CSV. Optionally, it adds original points, the flight line, and simplified points as map layers.

name: Slice polygon layers by extruded line volume
desc: The script slices 3D polygon vector layers using a volume defined by a buffered linestring extruded between given Z minimum and Z maximum. It first buffers the input linestring, converts to singlepart, translates to Z minimum, extrudes to Z maximum, then performs solid 3D intersection with each input polygon layer. The results are styled like the source layers and added to a new group in the QGIS project.

name: Generate stratified sampling polygons
desc: The script provides functionality for creating stratified shapefiles in QGIS. It allows users to manually draw strata boundaries using three methods: freehand lines, polylines (with optional horizontal/vertical constraints), or Voronoi polygons from points. The tool uses a specified sampling area layer as the extent. It polygonizes the drawn lines merged with the boundary, clips to the sampling area, and generates a polygon shapefile with attributes for ID, strata name, and area. The output shapefile contains the delineated strata polygons for subsequent stratified sampling workflows.

name: Generate Manning's roughness coefficient raster
desc: The script generates a Manning’s roughness coefficient raster layer for a user-defined area of interest. It uses the ESA WorldCover 2021 land cover classification and predefined lookup tables (low, medium, high) to assign roughness coefficients. The workflow reprojects the AOI polygon to EPSG:4326, clips the ESA land cover VRT to a buffered extent, and applies a raster calculator expression to map land cover codes to Manning's n values. Outputs include an optional clipped ESA WorldCover raster and a Manning's roughness raster, both styled with QML layers.

name: Classify lateral spreading hazard zones
desc: The script classifies areas into lateral spreading hazard zones for seismic microzonation. It takes a digital terrain model (DTM) raster and a vector layer of liquefaction index (IL), clips the DTM to the IL layer, computes slope as percentage, polygonizes the slope raster, and intersects with the IL layer to combine slope and IL values. Using predefined threshold ranges for IL and slope, it extracts polygons for Low Susceptibility (Z0), Susceptibility Zones (SZ), and Respect Zones (RZ). The sub-zones are dissolved and assigned numeric codes (101, 102, 103, 104 for RZ; 201, 202, 203 for SZ; 300 for Z0) with a formula attribute describing the conditions. All zones are merged into a single vector output with fields code and formula. The script also outputs a slope percentage raster. Styles are applied from QML files.

name: QGIS workflow: Vector data attribute editing, Data processing
desc: This workflow contains 6 core geospatial operations, including Vector data attribute editing, Data processing, Spatial Analysis And Modeling. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Build GSM coverage plans
desc: The script identifies pivot localities and their satellite localities based on a distance threshold, creates coverage buffers, optionally generates Voronoi polygons, and outputs multiple layers for GSM coverage planning.

name: Interpolate point precipitation values to raster
desc: The script interpolates point meteorological measurements (e.g., precipitation) to a continuous raster surface using IDW or Nearest Neighbor methods, then converts the resulting raster to a NumPy array for subsequent weighted average raster generation. It leverages QGIS processing algorithms (qgis:idwinterpolation and gdal:gridnearestneighbor) with user-defined extent, cell size, and interpolation parameters.

name: Merge Italian cadastral map and parcel data
desc: The script merges Italian cadastral GML files (MAP and PLE) downloaded from Agenzia delle Entrate WFS. It filters by province and comune, extracts relevant GML files, merges them into GPKG format, adds calculated fields (foglio, particella, sezione censuaria, comune), optionally reprojects, and loads the layers into QGIS.

name: Radar precipitation calibration using stations
desc: The script calibrates radar reflectivity (dBZ) to precipitation (mm) using weather station data and an optional DEM for topographic correction. It aligns radar, DEM, and stations to a common grid based on DEM resolution, interpolates station elevation and precipitation fields, computes distance and elevation-based blending weights, creates a radar/precipitation relation map, and outputs a calibrated precipitation raster by merging station-interpolated and radar-derived precipitation.

name: Execute GEEST spatial analysis workflow
desc: The WorkflowBase module provides an abstract processing pipeline for the GEEST plugin to assess gender-enabling environments. It loads study area geometries from a GeoPackage, iterates over sub-areas, applies subclass-defined analysis on vector or raster layers per area, masks results with area polygons, and merges per-area outputs into a single VRT file. Other capabilities include coordinate transformation, nodata filling, rasterization of vector layers, and optional GHSL settlement data download and processing.

name: Generate multi-buffer distance rasters
desc: The script generates multi-buffer isochrones around point locations using road network travel distances. For national and local scales, it employs QGIS native network analysis to create concentric travel-time or travel-distance polygons. For regional scale, it uses a simple buffer approach with percentage intersection scoring. The resulting isochrone layers are scored and rasterized to grid cells, producing accessibility rasters that are combined into a VRT.

name: Multi-buffer isochrone accessibility scoring
desc: The script computes multi-buffer travel time/distance isochrones from OpenRouteService for user-provided points of interest, dissolves overlapping areas to create non-overlapping bands, assigns inverted accessibility scores, and rasterizes the result to produce a suitability layer for gender enabling environment analysis.

name: Environmental hazard reclassification
desc: This script reclassifies environmental hazard rasters (landslide, fire, flood, cyclone, drought) into a 0-5 scale based on predefined rules specific to each hazard type. It applies reclassification by table using QGIS processing, then clips the result to the study area mask. Outputs are reclassified raster files per area in GeoTIFF format.

name: Geospatial data preprocessing for GEEST plugin
desc: This script provides utility functions for the GEEST plugin to assign coordinate reference systems (CRS) to raster and vector layers, subset vector layers by area of interest, fix geometries, reproject layers, and combine multiple rasters into a virtual raster (VRT) file for subsequent analysis. It serves as a preprocessing module for gender enabling environments spatial assessment.

name: Reclassify population raster to three classes
desc: The script clips a population density raster to study area masks using GDAL cliprasterbymasklayer, resamples each clipped raster to a specified cell size with gdalwarp sum aggregation, reclassifies the resampled values into three classes based on the global minimum and maximum across all resampled rasters (native:reclassifybytable), and finally creates VRT files combining clipped, resampled, and reclassified rasters. The reclassified raster is styled with a three-class QML. This task is part of the GEEST QGIS plugin to support gender-enabling environment analysis.

name: Subnational Gender Enablement Score Aggregation
desc: The script aggregates gender enablement environment (GeoE3) scores and GeoE3 x Population scores to subnational boundary polygons. It reads precomputed VRT rasters for each score type (including optional GHSL masked variants), fixes geometry of the aggregation layer, and uses QGIS native zonal statistics to compute the majority score class per polygon. The output geopackages contain polygons with aggregated score attributes, and corresponding QML style files are applied for visualization.

name: Create Depth Raster from XYZ
desc: The script converts one or more XYZ text files containing Easting, Northing, and Depth data into raster layers. It supports multiple file processing, auto-detects grid size per file, and offers direct rasterization or IDW interpolation. The output is GeoTIFF rasters with depth values, optionally compressed, added to the QGIS project.

name: Merge MBES Depth Rasters
desc: Merge Multibeam Echo Sounder (MBES) raster layers into a single seamless raster using GDAL merge, preserving original depth values and correctly handling NoData values for transparency. The process optionally applies LZW compression to reduce file size. The output is a merged raster file containing continuous bathymetric data.

name: Create Rockyfor3D Input Rasters
desc: The script prepares input rasters for the Rockyfor3D rockfall simulation model by rasterizing selected numeric vector field attributes onto a grid matching a provided DEM. It ensures data alignment with the DEM's resolution and extent, converts to ASCII format, renames specific fields to match model requirements (e.g., rockdensit to rockdensity, conif_perc to conif_percent), and validates field type and value constraints. The outputs are ASCII raster files for each field, optionally loaded into QGIS.

name: Download Warsaw cadastral boundaries
desc: The script downloads cadastral vector data (parcels and buildings) for specified districts of Warsaw from a municipal server via HTTP requests, extracts shapefiles from ZIP archives, and loads them into the QGIS project. It merges all district data into a single layer or adds separate layers, assigns the Polish coordinate system EPSG:2178, and adjusts the map canvas extent. Network errors are logged, and temporary files are cleaned up.

name: Calculate flight route metrics
desc: The script calculates flight route metrics (distance, time, and fuel burn) for a line vector dataset in QGIS. It refactors origin and destination fields, computes distances in km and nm, extracts start and end point coordinates, and then uses user-provided speed and fuel burn rate to compute time taken and fuel consumption per route. The output is a new line layer with added attributes: dist_km, dist_nm, o_lat, o_lon, d_lat, d_lon, time_taken, fuel_lbs.

name: Generate contours and hillshade
desc: The script generates fine contour lines and hillshade shading from a DEM raster clipped to the current map canvas extent. It first clips the DEM using GDAL Clip Raster by Extent, optionally creates a hillshade layer with GDAL hillshade using user-specified azimuth and altitude, then generates contour lines at a fine step interval. It identifies coarse contours by checking if elevation is near multiples of the wide step using a ratio threshold, assigns a 'coarse' attribute, applies a predefined style, and optionally fixes contour altitude masking. The resulting contour and hillshade layers are added to the map.

name: Generate contour lines from elevation data
desc: This QGIS plugin tool generates contour lines from either a raster layer (e.g., DEM) or a point vector layer with a height attribute. For point inputs, it first interpolates a raster using TIN or IDW interpolation via processing algorithms (qgis:tininterpolation or qgis:idwinterpolation), then applies gdal:contour to produce vector contour lines. Parameters include contour interval, base contour, Z factor, and major interval. The output is a vector layer with an 'ELEV' field, which can be added to the project and optionally exported as SHP, GPKG, KML, or DXF.

name: Generate atlas grid cells
desc: The script creates a polygon grid layer for atlas mapsheets, calculating grid metrics from map scale and overlap percentage, generating a net of rectangular cells over a given extent, optionally deleting cells that do not intersect an area of interest, and numbering remaining cells sequentially and by disjoint AOI regions.

name: Extract polygon edge strips
desc: The script extracts edges from polygon geometries in a vector layer. It processes input polygons by converting to single parts, fixing geometries, simplifying to tenths of millimeter tolerance, then buffers inward and outward by half the specified width, computes the difference between the outer and inner buffers, dissolves the resulting strips, fixes geometries, adds a field 'h' with a value from braille.DIM['f'], and outputs the final polygon layer representing the edge strips.

name: Package Multiple GIS Layers to KMZ
desc: The script is a QGIS processing algorithm that packages multiple vector and raster layers into a single KMZ file. It first takes input layers, optionally reprojects them to a target CRS, and optionally preserves layer styles. Then it processes each layer: vector layers are exported to KML using QgsVectorFileWriter, while raster layers are reprojected and converted to KML using GDAL tools (gdal:warpreproject and gdal:translate with KMLSUPEROVERLAY). Finally, all KML files are combined into a ZIP archive (KMZ) with a master KML document. The output is a KMZ file containing all selected layers.

name: Generate random polygon layer
desc: The script generates a vector layer of random polygons within the current QGIS map extent. It allows user-defined parameters: number of polygons, maximum corners per polygon, percentage of allowed invalid geometries, and maximum extent percentage. Random polygons are created with a random string attribute and node count. After generation, optional generalization (simplification) and smoothing via native:simplifygeometries and native:smoothgeometry processing algorithms are applied. The resulting memory layer is styled with a random outline color and added to the map, with feature count displayed.

name: Download Top10NL topographic features
desc: The script is a QGIS plugin that downloads selected Top10NL topographic feature layers from the PDOK OGC API Features service using GDAL's convertformat with a user-specified extent, saving them into a GeoPackage file. It also performs deduplication of features by 'ID' attribute when appending, logs processing steps, and optionally adds the layers to the current QGIS project.

name: Generate Property Parcel Maps
desc: The script processes property plot and built-up area vector layers to generate parcel maps for the SVAMITVA scheme. It fixes geometries, creates spatial indexes, calculates plot areas (in square yards and metres), computes intersections between plinth and plot layers, extracts boundaries and vertices, and generates exploded line shapefiles for dimension tracking. It then applies QML styles, labels, and sets up an A4 atlas print layout with the property parcel number as the page name, producing a ready-to-print Property Parcel Map (PPM).

name: Create water network listening zones
desc: The script generates listening zones (zones d'écoute) around manually or layer-based points along a water pipe network. It first densifies line geometries at 1-unit intervals, then for each start point finds the nearest line and computes a travel cost based on the line's material (MATERIAU) and diameter (DIAMETRE) using a detailed lookup table. Using QGIS network analysis (service area from layer), it computes a service area with the travel cost, buffers the result by 1 meter, and merges all individual zones into a single output layer named 'Zones d'écoute'.

name: Generate drone flight restriction zones
desc: The script generates drone flight restriction zones around airfields and helipads by creating concentric buffer rings with varying radii corresponding to height restrictions (e.g., FRZ, ≤100ft, ≤200ft, ≤300ft, ≤400ft). For airfields, it processes a selected runway line feature, buffers the runway, creates lateral and head line features, and uses a sector at each runway end to split restriction zones into 'lado' (side) and 'cabeceira' (head) regions. For helipads, it creates simple concentric rings around a selected point. The outputs are styled polygon layers added to the QGIS map.

name: Create lateral buffers from lines
desc: This QGIS plugin creates lateral buffers on both sides of selected line features from the active layer. Using user-specified offset and buffer distances, it first runs the array offset algorithm to generate left (negative offset) and right (positive offset) parallel lines, removes any zero-offset features, then creates single-sided buffers on each side (left buffer with side=1, right buffer with side=0). The left and right buffers are merged into a single memory layer and added to the map.

name: Download BGT topography features
desc: The script downloads selected BGT topographic features (e.g., roads, buildings, water) from the PDOK OGC API Features service within a user-specified bounding box, saves them to a GeoPackage file, and optionally loads them into QGIS. It uses the GDAL OGR vector conversion tool to fetch features via OAPIF, deduplicates appended layers by attribute, and logs progress.

name: Design sewer network layout
desc: The script designs a sewer network layout by extracting street centerlines, clipping them to a study area, snapping an outlet point, creating a minimum spanning tree from shortest paths, and correcting flow directions and invert elevations to ensure proper gravitational drainage. It processes vector street data and a digital elevation model, producing sewer pipe and node layers with corrected elevation attributes.

name: Prepare urban drainage design inputs
desc: The script prepares input data for urban drainage system design. It processes building and street data to compute contributing areas, slopes, imperviousness, and connections to sewer nodes. It uses a DEM to derive slopes, determines pipe lengths and slopes, and aggregates subcatchments with population data for combined sewer systems. The outputs are CSV design files for nodes, pipes, and subcatchments.

name: Rank and merge skipped pipe links
desc: The script processes street/pipeline network layers to correct node elevations and calculate elevation differences, then adds aggregated flow (Q) and diameter data from tabular dataframes. It ranks links based on a weighted score of normalized length and flow, prioritizing non-head nodes. Finally, it merges a percentage of top-ranked previously skipped links into a designed network layer, retaining only essential fields such as LINK_ID, length, FROM_NODE, TO_NODE, slope, and Diameter.

name: QGIS workflow: Spatial Analysis And Modeling
desc: This workflow contains 1 core geospatial operations, including Spatial Analysis And Modeling. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Sentinel-2 Cloud Masking with Shadow Detection
desc: This script is a QGIS plugin that applies cloud masking to Sentinel-2 Level-1C imagery using the enhanced s2cloudless algorithm with adaptive thresholding and cloud shadow detection. It reads Sentinel-2 band files from a local product directory, reprojects them to a user-defined CRS, and crops to the current map canvas extent. The bands (B01–B12) are stacked, and the S2PixelCloudDetector is used to generate an initial cloud mask. Additionally, the Bare Soil Index (BSI) is calculated to create a bare soil mask that aids in identifying cloud shadows; the combined mask is then refined with averaging and binary dilation. The final binary mask is saved as a GeoTIFF, and masked versions of 10m/20m bands (B02, B03, B04, B05, B06, B07, B08, B8A, B11, B12) are produced for further analysis.

name: Mask and mosaic Sentinel-2 L1C imagery
desc: The plugin downloads Sentinel-2 L1C imagery over the current map canvas extent from Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, applies cloud masking using s2cloudless, and optionally creates a median composite mosaic from multiple dates. It outputs cloud-masked multi-band GeoTIFF files and true color image (TCI) previews.

name: Batch export map tiles and elevation rasters
desc: The script batch-exports atlas map tiles from a QGIS layout as GeoTIFF images and generates corresponding masked elevation rasters. It uses a user-provided DEM and a coverage grid layer. For each atlas feature, it exports the layout to a high-resolution GeoTIFF, then creates a mask raster from the grid layer with identical extent and resolution, warps the DEM to that extent, and applies the mask to clip the DEM, writing the result. The process is logged.

name: Export point coordinates to text file
desc: The script exports point features from a vector layer (or vertices from line/polygon layers) to a tab-separated text file. It includes user-selected fields for name and description, and X, Y, Z coordinates, where Z can be derived from the geometry's Z value, a numeric attribute field, or sampled from a DEM raster. The coordinates are transformed to a user-specified CRS. The output file includes a header row with the selected column order (e.g., Name, Descricao, X, Y, Z). The script uses QGIS processing tools to extract vertices and remove duplicates for non-point geometries, and applies decimal precision formatting.

name: Delineate watersheds and stream networks
desc: The script generates catchments, streams, and stream networks from a DEM. It fills sinks, computes flow accumulation and watershed basins, extracts streams based on a user-defined threshold, smooths stream geometry, generalizes catchments using GRASS v.generalize with snakes method, calculates both Strahler and Shreve stream orders, joins catchments with stream network attributes, and dissolves catchments to create network polygons. Outputs are three styled vector layers: streams (graduated by Shreve order with Viridis ramp), catchments (categorized by network with random colors), and networks (blue outlines with labels).

name: Identify Ponds from DEM
desc: This QGIS processing script identifies ponds (sinks) in a ground raster (DEM) by filling sinks, computing pond depth as the difference between filled and original DEM, filtering by minimum depth and area, and polygonizing the valid pond extents. It then performs zonal statistics to assign attributes such as maximum and minimum elevation, pond volume, and depth statistics to each pond polygon. The outputs include a vector layer of pond outlines with attached attributes, and optionally the filled DEM and pond depth rasters.

name: e-Stat mesh batch import merge secret values
desc: This QGIS algorithm batch-imports e-Stat regional mesh statistics from ZIP files, cleans and renames fields using Japanese metadata rows, normalizes mesh codes, handles secret-treated values by merging them into designated group codes, auto-generates mesh polygon geometries (1km/500m/250m) using mesh code to bounding box conversion, dissolves polygons by group ID, sums numeric fields, adds source row counts (SRC_COUNT), and optionally extracts meshes intersecting administrative boundary polygons. Outputs integrated mesh polygon layers with merged statistics.

name: Flood extent mapping from height classes
desc: The script provides QGIS processing tools for flood mapping, including raster classification by height thresholds, sieving of raster patches, polygon refinement (smoothing/simplification), and nesting of flood polygons (russian dolls analysis). It supports sensitivity testing with on-the-fly clipping of input layers. Outputs include final flood hazard layers and intermediate rasters/vectors.

name: Classify flood depth raster
desc: The script generates a classified flood depth raster from an input water depth raster and user-defined class breakpoints. It first sorts the breakpoints, constructs a r.mapcalc expression that sums binary condition layers (A > class_i) to assign integer classes, then applies a sieve filter to remove small polygons from the resulting raster. Output is a classified raster where pixel values indicate the highest class threshold that the water depth exceeds.

name: Vectorize water depth classes
desc: This script vectorizes water depth classes from a water depth raster. It uses a user-specified list of threshold values (in metres) and for each threshold, generates a binary raster indicating areas where water depth exceeds that value. The processing steps include raster algebra (A>B), null value conversion, sieve filtering to remove small areas, raster to vector conversion, geometry fixing, dissolving, and attribute field creation with the threshold value. The resulting polygon layers for all thresholds are merged into a single vector output, each feature attributed with its depth class.

name: Interpolate high water marks
desc: The script interpolates a vector layer containing high water marks (CPHE) to create a raster surface. It supports multiple interpolation methods: regularized spline with tension (v.surf.rst), bilinear, bicubic, and stepped (Voronoi polygon-based). If a mask is provided, processing is performed per zone, and results are merged. The workflow includes optional centroid calculation, buffering, rasterization, and optional projection onto a DTM if provided. The output is a raster of interpolated CPHE values.

name: Delete isolated flood polygons
desc: The script removes isolated flood extent polygons that do not overlap a reference overlay layer within a specified distance tolerance. It dissolves the input polygon layer, buffers the overlay layer, selects input polygons intersecting the buffer, and clips the original input to these selected polygons, producing a cleaned vector layer.

name: Cut disk geometries into rings
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm converts concentric disk polygons (e.g., flooded area extents at different water levels) into annuli by dissolving, splitting, and sorting features based on a user-selected attribute field. It then computes the geometric difference between pairs of consecutive layers using native:difference, and merges the resulting rings into a single polygon layer. Optionally, it removes an automatically created 'fid' column if it was not present in the original input.

name: Compute flood depth above minimum height
desc: The algorithm projects a high water level raster (CPHE) onto a digital terrain model (MNT) to compute water depths. It subtracts the terrain from the water surface, then extracts areas where the resulting depth exceeds a user-specified minimum height threshold. The output is a raster of heights above the minimum threshold, representing flood depths.

name: Refine height class polygons
desc: The script refines vector polygons representing height classes (elevation zones) using a buffer-based refinement strategy. It applies a sequence of positive and/or negative buffers, group-by-field dissolve, simplification, small area/hole removal, and smoothing. The output is a cleaned and smoothed polygon layer.

name: Assemble flood rings into disks
desc: The script assembles polygon ring geometries (e.g., flood extent rings) into filled disks. It takes a polygon layer, dissolves by a specified field, splits into per-value layers, then iteratively unions and dissolves the layers in sorted order to fill holes, producing solid polygon disks. The output is a merged polygon layer with the original fields, after deleting an extraneous 'fid' column.

name: Russian doll polygon nesting
desc: The script implements a Russian doll nesting algorithm for vector polygon layers. It takes a polygon layer and a field, sorts the polygons by that field, and then either unions or intersects them sequentially to create a nested arrangement where each polygon is contained within the previous one. Optionally, it can apply a buffer distance for inset/outset and snap geometries. If the ring option is enabled, it cuts out the inner polygon from the outer to produce distinct annular rings. Finally, it merges the resulting geometries into a single output layer and optionally outputs the overall footprint (the outermost polygon).

name: Safe raster patch assembly
desc: The script assembles multiple raster layers into a single output raster, handling edge cases with empty or single-layer inputs. For more than one layer, it uses GRASS GIS r.patch to merge rasters. For exactly one layer, it uses GDAL translate to copy the layer to the output. For no layers, it returns None. The script is designed as a safe processing algorithm to avoid failures when input is empty or contains only one raster.

name: Spatialize flood heights onto DTM
desc: The script interpolates a vector layer containing spatial data of highest water levels (CPHE) and projects them onto a Digital Terrain Model (DTM) if provided. It supports multiple interpolation methods: bilinear, bicubic, rst (r.fillnulls), and stair-step (Voronoi polygons). Inputs include vector data (points or polygons), a numeric field for CPHE values, a minimum height, optional DTM, buffer distance, and an optional mask for zonal processing. Outputs are a raster of heights above the minimum height and a raster of the CPHE values.

name: Interpolate highest water level points
desc: The script interpolates vector data containing Cotes des Plus Hautes Eau (CPHE) values into a raster surface using either stepwise Voronoi (escarpment) or r.fillnulls (bilinear, bicubic, rst) interpolation methods. Optionally, if a digital terrain model (MNT) is provided, it projects the interpolated CPHE onto the terrain to compute water heights above a minimum threshold, producing a flood height raster. Outputs include the CPHE raster and the height difference raster.

name: Create Base Point from Geographic Extent
desc: The script generates a base point layer by creating a polygon from a hardcoded geographic extent in WGS84, applying a placeholder extraction expression (id=99), extracting the polygon vertices, and refactoring fields to output a point layer in GPKG format. It is part of the Mavic 3 Enterprise group for drone mission planning.

name: Clear Safe Canopy Points
desc: The script filters a set of points created for drone flight planning by reprojecting them to EPSG:31981, applying a -10 m buffer to an optimized grid, and retaining only points that intersect both the buffered grid and the area plot polygon. The resulting 'Safe Points' layer represents locations valid for canopy photo capture.

name: Create mapping flight plan polygon
desc: The script generates a flight plan polygon by reprojecting an area plot and base point to EPSG:31981, buffering the plot and the shortest connecting line by 30 meters, merging them, and dissolving into a single KML output for UgCS drone flight software.

name: Generate canopy survey grid
desc: The script reprojects an input polygon layer to EPSG:31981, applies a 250-meter buffer, creates a regular grid (hexagon, rectangle, or diamond) with user-specified cell width, and adds an ID field to the grid cells.

name: Generate canopy photography sampling points from DSM
desc: The script generates sampling points for canopy photography by slicing a digital surface model (DSM) into vertical zones. For each grid cell, it clips the DSM to the cell, computes the maximum elevation, and for each height slice reclassifies the raster, derives contour polygons, selects the highest pixel points within each polygon, randomly picks one point per polygon, and ensures a minimum distance between points across slices using buffered exclusion zones. The outputs are a point layer (with id, hexagon, fatia, and maximum attributes) showing the selected photography locations, and a polygon layer of the processed slices.

name: Clip DSM to Buffered Plot
desc: The script clips a Digital Surface Model (DSM) raster to a vector polygon representing an area plot. It reprojects the plot to EPSG:31981, applies a 10-meter buffer with square end caps, reprojects the buffered polygon to the DSM’s CRS, then clips the DSM using the buffered layer as a mask, outputting a clipped DSM raster in WGS84 (EPSG:4326).

name: Order grid cells for canopy photography
desc: The script reprojects a base point and a grid layer to EPSG:31981, then iteratively computes shortest lines from the base point to the nearest grid features, buffers line vertices, and joins spatially to assign sequential order numbers ('hexagon' field) to grid cells. It merges ordered cells and sorts, producing an optimized grid for drone flight planning in canopy photography.

name: Order canopy survey waypoints
desc: The script reorders a set of points relative to a base point for optimized flight path planning in canopy surveys. It reprojects input points to EPSG:31981 (UTM zone 22S), dissolves them by a 'hexagon' attribute to group points, then within each group iteratively finds the nearest point to the base, then the next nearest point from the previous, creating a sequential chain. It assigns group and point index attributes, merges results, and outputs a line layer (lines between consecutive points) ordered by hexagon, group, and point, saved as a GPKG file.

name: Generate drone route for canopy zoom photos
desc: The script generates a UgCS-compatible JSON drone mission file for each hexagon cluster from a point layer of optimized canopy photography locations. It reads the point layer and a base point, processes them by hexagon and group, and creates waypoint segments with camera actions (dual capture at wide and zoom, then approach altitude zoom photo, then flight altitude waypoint) for each group of three points. Coordinate conversions are applied to fit the UgCS system. The output JSON files are saved to a specified folder, enabling automated drone flight for canopy zoom photography using a DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise.

name: Merge vector layers with field cleanup
desc: The script merges multiple selected vector layers into a single output layer using QGIS native merge algorithm. It first reprojects layers to a target CRS if necessary, then merges them, and optionally removes the 'layer' and 'path' fields that are automatically added by the merge process. The output is a merged vector file with the specified coordinate reference system.

name: Count cable overlaps on infrastructure
desc: The script counts the number of cable (CAVI) features that spatially overlap with each infrastructure line (INFRASTRUTTURA). It assigns unique IDs to both layers, applies a tiny buffer (1e-07 degrees) to cables to handle touch intersections, repairs and explodes infrastructure lines, then performs a spatial join with predicates 'contains', 'are within', and 'overlaps' to associate cable IDs. An aggregation step concatenates distinct cable IDs per infrastructure segment and computes the total count of overlaps. The output is the infrastructure layer with fields id_infr, concatenated cable IDs, and n_overlaps.

name: Multi-function vector processing toolbox
desc: The script provides a multi-function toolbox for QGIS that includes several vector processing algorithms: batch merging of layers with optional field removal, batch reprojection to a target CRS, counting overlapping line features, extracting duplicate geometries, and transposing attribute tables to CSV. The tools use QGIS processing frameworks and allow user-selected layers, selected features, output paths, and CRS settings. Results are loaded into the QGIS project or saved as files.

name: Generate polygons in empty regions
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm generates polygon features representing empty gaps (holes) inside a provided boundary frame. It first dissolves the frame to a single polygon, converts it to lines, and merges those lines with optional line and area layers. The merged line network is polygonized, and each resulting polygon is checked: it must lie within the frame, not be inside any existing area polygon, and have an area at or above a user-specified minimum. The output is a new vector layer with an 'id' and dynamically calculated 'area_otf' field.

name: Generate Fill Polygons
desc: The QGIS processing algorithm generates fill polygons in empty regions bounded by a frame and linear/polygonal delimiters. It prepares and merges input layers, polygonizes the linear network, filters candidate polygons within the frame's unary union, outside existing areas, and above a minimum area threshold. The output is a polygon layer with 'id' and 'area_otf' fields.

name: Identify shiftable parking spaces
desc: The plugin identifies street-side parking spaces that can be shifted into selected public parking garages based on available capacity and network distance. It computes service areas from parking garages along a street network within a user-defined radius, selects intersecting public parking spaces, evaluates capacity constraints including current utilization, target utilization, and restriction types (disabled, short-term, residential, etc.), and classifies parking spaces as fully, partially, or not shiftable.
