Outputs include a styled layer of parking garages with new utilization, a layer of parking spaces colored by shiftability category, and optionally CSV exports of results.

name: Simulate Blasting Vibration PPV Distribution
desc: The script simulates peak particle velocity (PPV) from blasting operations using a power-law attenuation model (PPV = a * charge^b * distance^c) derived from regression parameters. It processes input borehole (furo de simulação) data to compute charge weights and distances, integrates a topographic surface to obtain Z-elevations via barycentric interpolation within triangulated vertices, and then either employs Ordinary Kriging (if PyKrige is available and user opts) or fallback IDW 3D to interpolate PPV across a regular grid. The interpolated grid is exported as a GeoTIFF raster with discrete color symbology and used to generate contour (isovalue) lines at a user-defined interval. Output layers include a PPV raster and smoothed contour lines added to the QGIS project.

name: Estimate EV Charging Station Locations
desc: The script is a QGIS processing algorithm that estimates optimal locations for new electric vehicle (EV) charging stations by computing a weighted suitability score. It starts by creating a Voronoi diagram from existing charging stations to identify coverage gaps, then uses road network data (primary and secondary roads) to generate candidate points along roads at 500m intervals. These points are evaluated based on population density (from subdistrict polygons) and land price, normalized and combined into consumer and investor scores. The consumer score favors high population density and proximity to roads, while the investor score favors low land values and distance from existing stations. The final weighted score is a user-weighted average of these scores, and points with scores above 0.3 are selected as recommended locations. Outputs include the weighted score layer, final candidate points, coverage gaps, Voronoi vertices, and other intermediate results.

name: Biologically active surface classification from LiDAR
desc: The script classifies terrain into biologically active (PBC) and non-active surfaces using a pre-trained Random Forest model applied to LiDAR point cloud data aggregated into hexagonal grids. It loads point cloud layers with attributes Red, Green, Blue, Z, Intensity, ReturnNumber, NumberOfReturns; clips points to a mask buffered by 1.5 m to preserve neighborhood geometry; aggregates points per hexagon and computes spectral and geometric features including chromaticity, vegetation indices, brightness, coefficient of variation, and neighborhood statistics (planarity, std_Z, std_I, std_brightness, I_contrast). The model predicts class probabilities for 14 land cover classes, sums probabilities of PBC classes (e.g., grass, ruderal, farmland, dirt road), and applies a threshold of 0.65 to determine final binary PBC label. Outputs include hexagon polygon layers with detailed predictions and confidence, styled QGIS layers, and CSV files for each mask area.

name: Extract building heights and roof slopes
desc: The script extracts building heights and roof slopes from classified airborne LiDAR point clouds. It buffers building polygons, clips ground (Classification_2) and roof (Classification_6) point layers, assigns building and parcel IDs via spatial joins, and then uses DBSCAN segmentation and RANSAC plane fitting to compute roof slopes. For heights, it interpolates a ground surface, subtracts point-wise to get building heights, filters out superstructure outliers (chimneys/antennas), and determines ridge height. Results are written to the building layer, and the roof points are styled with a graduated turbo color ramp.

name: Calculate urban planning indicators for investment land parcels
desc: The script computes urban planning indicators (building coverage, gross floor area, floor area ratio, biologically active area) for investment land parcels. It first processes predicted PPNZ points (with label=1) by buffering and aggregating to compute PPNZ area per parcel, then integrates building data to calculate building-related metrics, and finally derives indicators such as WPZ (building coverage ratio) and WPBC (biologically active area ratio). The outputs include an aggregated buffer layer and a styled parcel layer with all computed indicators.

name: Create GTFS shapes from OSM
desc: The script creates GTFS shapes by assigning shape IDs to trips based on OSM road/rail networks. It downloads OSM ways (roads, railways, ferries) for a given extent, processes GTFS stop times to determine trip sequences, matches GTFS stops to OSM nodes using spatial joins and nearest neighbor operations, and generates routing networks with speed attributes. The output includes updated trips.txt with shape_id assignments and intermediate layer files for visualization and further processing.

name: Generate GTFS shapes using OSM routing
desc: The script generates GTFS trip shapes by computing shortest paths on multimodal OSM networks (roads, tram, heavy rail, funicular, ferry) between consecutive stops for each line and trip. It preprocesses OSM stops, snaps off-road stops to the nearest road, creates mini-trips between stop pairs using QGIS shortest path algorithms, merges mini-trips into full trips, and calculates cumulative shape distances. Final outputs are trip shape geometries (GPKG) and CSV summaries with stop sequences and traveled distances.

name: Generate RRIM base layers
desc: The script implements a QGIS processing algorithm to generate base layers for Red Relief Image Map (RRIM) visualization. It takes a single-band DEM raster as input, computes slope using the native QGIS tool, positive and negative openness using the RVT processing algorithm, then calculates differential openness as (positive - negative)/2. Optionally, it creates normalized versions: slope normalized to 0-90 and styled with a red color ramp with Multiply blending, and differential openness normalized to -50 - 50 styled in grayscale. Outputs include the original slope and differential openness rasters, and optionally the normalized rasters.

name: Classify directional slope into polygons
desc: The script computes directional slope (toward a user-specified azimuth) and perpendicular slope from a DEM using numpy gradient, keeps pixels where absolute perpendicular slope falls within given limits, bins directional slope into classes with a specified half-width, polygonizes the classified raster, optionally simplifies and filters polygons by area, and thins vertices. The output is a vector layer with slope class polygons and an attribute 'slope_deg'.

name: QGIS workflow: Data export, Vector overlay analysis
desc: This workflow contains 54 core geospatial operations, including Data export, Vector overlay analysis, Vector spatial analysis, Data extraction. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Identify Disconnected Poles and Chambers
desc: The script performs quality control on utility network vector layers. It first fixes geometries of the 'route' line layer, then extracts 'poles' points that are spatially disjoint (not intersecting or touching) from the fixed routes, storing the result as a layer named 'Diconnected_Poles'. Similarly, it extracts 'chambers' points that are disjoint from the routes, but using an intermediate touch-based selection to refine the disconnected chambers, outputting a layer named 'Disconnected_Chambers'. Both output layers are added to the QGIS project for inspection.

name: Optimize Distribution Point Population Coverage
desc: The script evaluates population coverage by distribution points within a planning area using WorldPop population data. It creates buffer zones around points, calculates covered and uncovered population percentages, generates a population hotspot heatmap, and optimizes coverage by relocating existing points or adding new points based on uncovered high-population areas. Results include updated point layers, coverage statistics, and an optional Excel export.

name: QGIS workflow: Format conversion, Projection
desc: This workflow contains 28 core geospatial operations, including Format conversion, Projection, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Vector spatial analysis. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Stream network extraction from DTM
desc: The script extracts a stream network from a digital terrain model (DTM) by first filling sinks using the Wang & Liu algorithm (native:fillsinkswangliu), then computing flow accumulation and delineating streams with GRASS r.watershed (including optional drainage directions, half basins, and topographic index), converting the raster streams to vector lines via r.to.vect, and finally smoothing the vector geometry. Outputs include a filled DTM, raw and smoothed vector stream networks, and optional rasters for stream, drainage, half basins, and ln(a/tan(b)).

name: QGIS workflow: Vector spatial analysis, Buffer Analysis
desc: This workflow contains 6 core geospatial operations, including Vector spatial analysis, Buffer Analysis, Image Masking. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Bathymetric Preprocessing Feature Generation
desc: The script preprocesses satellite imagery for bathymetric inversion by generating water masks (via polygon vector, Otsu NDWI, manual NDWI threshold, or 3-index NDWI/MNDWI/NWI), performing sunglint correction using the Hedley method on coastal, blue, green, and red bands, and computing a multi-band feature stack that includes raw bands, log-transformed bands, band ratios, and custom band math. It also applies deep water / optically shallow water (OSW) masking based on manual ROI or automatic NIR percentile thresholding, with optional median filtering, hole filling, and polygon extraction. Outputs are a land/water mask, sunglint-corrected image, feature stack, intermediate review bands, deep water threshold statistics CSV, and OSW mask and polygon.

name: Depth Map Cleaning and Slope Filtering
desc: The script provides functions to preprocess bathymetric depth rasters. It removes positive pixel values (>=0) by setting them to a nodata value, eliminating likely land or shallow artifacts. The clean_depth_map function clamps depth values beyond a 1.5× max_depth threshold using a mask from a feature stack raster, removing deep anomalies and edge noise. The slope_filter_depth function computes slope in degrees and masks depth pixels where slope exceeds a given threshold, filtering out steep erroneous features. The outputs are filtered depth rasters ready for further bathymetric analysis.

name: Create Voronoi diagram from points
desc: The script creates a Voronoi diagram from all points in a selected QGIS point layer. It first determines the boundary either from a user-chosen polygon layer that contains all points or by creating a convex hull of the points and adding a buffer. The QGIS processing algorithm 'qgis:voronoipolygons' generates the Voronoi polygons, which are then clipped to the boundary using 'native:clip'. The resulting polygon layer includes attributes such as point ID, area, source layer name, and creation timestamp.

name: Download Sentinel-2 land cover data
desc: The script provides QGIS processing algorithms to download Sentinel-2 land cover data from Esri's Living Atlas for a user-specified year (2017-2025). For latitude/longitude or point input, it creates a point, reprojects to Web Mercator, buffers to generate an area of interest (AOI), then calls a pipeline to download, mosaic, and clip the land cover raster. For AOI input, it reprojects the AOI to the same CRS and downloads directly. Outputs include a clipped land cover raster and optionally an AOI polygon layer, with QML styles applied for visualization.

name: Building Evacuation Time Estimation
desc: The script computes shortest walking evacuation routes and travel times for buildings within a flood zone to designated safe shelters. It uses OpenStreetMap road network data, optionally a digital elevation model for terrain-adjusted travel time using Tobler's hiking function. Buildings at risk are identified by intersecting building polygon layer with flood extent. Outputs include a building layer with assigned shelter and travel time, and an evacuation route line layer.

name: Assign Manning's n from CORINE 2018
desc: The script assigns Manning's roughness coefficient to CORINE 2018 land cover polygons within a user-defined area of interest. It subsets the CORINE vector layer by the AOI geometry (with reprojection if needed), clips, then adds Manning, area in square meters and hectares. Manning values are looked up from an internal CSV mapping CODE_18 to n. The result is loaded as 'CLC_Manning_AOI'.

name: Create Valley Boundary
desc: This algorithm creates a valley boundary line layer by subtracting valley floor polygons from intersecting microsheds polygons, converting the difference polygons to lines, applying smoothing, and dissolving to produce final valley boundary lines.

name: Generate microsheds from DEM
desc: The script runs GRASS r.watershed on an input DEM with a user-defined threshold to delineate uniquely labeled watershed basins (microsheds). Optionally, it polygonizes the resulting basins raster using GDAL to produce a vector polygon layer of microsheds.

name: Delineate Valley Floor Using Cost Distance
desc: The script delineates valley bottoms using a cost-distance approach. It takes a river network vector layer and a DEM raster layer as inputs. It computes slope from the DEM, conditions it, rasterizes the river, and runs GRASS r.cost to generate a cumulative cost surface from the river network. An initial cost distance threshold creates a coarse mask, within which the mean cost is computed and used to refine the mask. The refined mask is then polygonized, and polygons are cleaned by deleting holes, smoothing, and buffering to close narrow gaps. The final output is a valley floor polygon layer.

name: Export vector layers to file
desc: The script provides a QGIS plugin dialog for batch exporting vector layers to various formats such as GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, CSV, Excel, KML, GML, FlatGeobuf, MapInfo TAB, SQLite, and DXF. Users select layers from the project, choose output format and CRS, specify a directory, and the tool exports each layer using QGIS processing or QgsVectorFileWriter with progress feedback and logging.

name: Convert land cover to Manning roughness
desc: The script extracts Manning's n roughness coefficient for HEC-RAS hydraulic modeling from SIOSE land cover data. It reads a CSV mapping from SIOSE land cover codes (ID_COBERTURA_MAX) to Manning values, clips the SIOSE polygon layer to a user-defined area of interest, assigns Manning values based on the mapping, optionally dissolves polygons by Manning value, calculates polygon areas, and applies stable symbolization. Outputs a new vector layer with Manning values added.

name: Analyze hourly traffic congestion from Google Traffic tiles
desc: The script extracts Google Traffic XYZ tiles for user-specified days and hours, clips them to a boundary polygon, and exports GeoTIFF rasters. Using HSV color thresholds on the RGB tile data, it classifies traffic congestion into four levels (Free flow, Moderate, Heavy, Severe) and computes a weighted congestion index raster. It generates hourly statistics, animated GIFs/MP4s with time labels and metrics overlays, and summary plots (stacked bar and mean congestion line charts). The processed outputs include hourly traffic GeoTIFFs, classified congestion rasters, index rasters, CSV tables, and optional animated visualizations.

name: Landsat Collection 2 surface reflectance and temperature conversion
desc: The script applies scale factors to Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 surface reflectance and thermal bands to convert digital numbers to physical units. It automatically detects the Landsat satellite (5,7,8,9) by filename prefix, applies scaling (multispectral: (A*0.0000275)-0.2 to get surface reflectance; thermal: ((A*0.00341802)+149)-273.15 to get temperature in °C), merges multispectral bands into a single multi-band GeoTIFF with band descriptions, and outputs a separate thermal band GeoTIFF.

name: Scale Sentinel-2 L1C to TOA reflectance
desc: The script processes a Sentinel-2 Level-1C product folder, applying a scaling factor of 0.0001 to the digital number bands to convert them to top-of-atmosphere reflectance. It resamples the 20m and 60m bands to 10m using nearest neighbor resampling, and merges all scaled and resampled bands into a single 10-band multiband raster at 10m resolution. The output is a GeoTIFF with band descriptions set to Aerosol, Blue, Green, Red, Red_Edge1, Red_Edge2, Red_Edge3, NIR, SWIR1, and SWIR2.

name: Scale Sentinel-2 L2A to 10m reflectance
desc: The script processes Sentinel-2 Level-2A (L2A) bottom-of-atmosphere reflectance products. It locates the IMG_DATA folder within the product directory, identifies the R10m, R20m, and R60m subdirectories, selects specific spectral bands (B01–B08, B11, B12), applies the standard scaling factor (0.0001) to convert digital numbers to surface reflectance, resamples bands with native resolution of 20m or 60m to 10m using nearest neighbour resampling, and merges all bands into a single 10m multiband GeoTIFF raster. The output bands are named (Aerosol, Blue, Green, Red, Red_Edge1–3, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2).

name: Fault Spine Extraction from Earthquakes
desc: The script extracts fault spines from earthquake point catalogs by applying magnitude filtering, DBSCAN clustering, and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to each cluster. It generates a line vector layer representing smoothed fault orientations, including attributes such as average magnitude, strike angle, and length. The output is saved as a GeoPackage file and loaded into the QGIS project.

name: Urban facility network location optimization
desc: This script optimizes urban facility locations using network-based accessibility analysis. It processes a road network (with optional cleaning), a population raster to create demand grid centroids, and optional point of interest layers for attractiveness weighting. It builds a weighted graph, computes network service distances within a service radius, and performs facility audit of existing facilities (if provided) with status classification. For optimization, it either runs maximum coverage location problem (MCLP) greedy to achieve a target coverage or P-median heuristic with swap search to select new facility locations. Equity diagnostics include Gini coefficient and Theil index. Outputs include new facilities, demand points with before-after metrics, existing facility audit, combined facilities, CSV/TXT reports, and multiple PNG charts (histograms, bar chart, scatter, Lorenz curve, before-after comparison).

name: Reproject TransCAD Israel Layer
desc: The script fixes the coordinate reference system (CRS) of a vector layer that has coordinates in the TransCAD Israel TM projection but no assigned CRS. It first assigns the custom TransCAD CRS (get_transcad_crs()) without transforming the coordinates, then reprojects the layer to EPSG:4326, and finally reprojects to EPSG:2039 (Israel TM Grid). The output is a layer with the corrected projection.

name: Transit stop location optimization
desc: The script optimizes transit stop locations by building a road network graph, aggregating population raster to grid cells to compute demand, and incorporating POI attractiveness. Candidate stops are generated from road vertices or corridor lines, then filtered by minimum Euclidean spacing. Two optimization models are provided: greedy MCLP to reach a target population coverage within a walk radius, and P-median heuristic to minimize population-weighted network distance for a fixed number of stops. The workflow includes optional network cleaning for topology, regulatory spacing compliance (simple or advanced corridor with variable spacing based on local demand intensity), and AI demand smoothing via RandomForest. Outputs include selected stop points, demand points with access distance and coverage attributes, CSV/TXT summary reports with coverage and equity metrics (Gini, Theil), and an access distance histogram PNG.

name: Indicative traffic assignment with UE
desc: The script performs indicative traffic assignment without OD survey data. It generates synthetic origin-destination demand using a gravity model (with population raster and/or POI counts as mass, or zone area as fallback) inside a user-defined boundary. The road network is optionally auto-split at intersections, filtered by road class, and free-flow travel times and capacities are derived from fields or class defaults. Flows are assigned via All-or-Nothing (AoN) or Path-Size Logit (PSL) multi-path assignment. If User Equilibrium (UE) is enabled, the BPR congestion function updates link costs iteratively with MSA smoothing until convergence. Outputs: edge layer with assigned flow, travel time, volume/capacity ratio, and delay; zone polygon layer with origin/destination mass, generation/attraction, snapped node, and snap distance; OD desire lines; and optional CSVs for synthetic OD matrix and iteration log.

name: Analyze overlap of single polygon with multiple layers
desc: The script performs a spatial overlap analysis for the first polygon of a property layer against multiple input polygon layers. It uses the QGIS processing toolbox to extract intersecting features, fix geometries, compute geometric intersections, and calculate overlapping areas. For each analysis layer, it produces an area report (total overlap area and percentage) and a layer of intersection polygons that retains all original attributes from the overlaying layers. Outputs are a report table (no geometry) and an intersection geometry layer.

name: dNBR-based burned area detection
desc: The script calculates the difference Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) from pre- and post-fire NIR and SWIR raster bands. It first computes NBR for both time periods using the formula (NIR - SWIR)/(NIR+SWIR), then subtracts post-fire NBR from pre-fire NBR to produce a dNBR layer. A user-specified threshold is applied to classify burned areas (>= threshold). The resulting binary raster is vectorized to polygons, and only features with DN=1 (burned areas) are extracted as the final output vector layer.

name: Calculate traffic emission line sources
desc: The script processes OSM road lines and trajectory data to generate traffic emission line sources for ENVI-met. It filters OSM road classes, splits lines by length, counts unique trajectory IDs within a search radius per hour for each segment, merges adjacent segments with similar hourly patterns using a tolerance, applies a user-defined scaling factor, and computes hourly emissions of NO, NO2, PM10, and PM2.5 using provided emission factors and NO/PM ratios. The outputs are a GeoPackage containing the merged segments with hourly traffic volumes and an ENVI-met JSON database (.edb) file ready for microclimate simulation.

name: QGIS workflow: Data export, Data processing
desc: This workflow contains 14 core geospatial operations, including Data export, Data processing, Vector data attribute editing, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Map tsunami hazard zones from PTHA
desc: Generates tsunami hazard zone polygons using PTHA stage values and a DEM via Green's law amplification and bathtub approach.

name: Compute Curve Number (CN) from SIOSE and IGME
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin to calculate SCS Curve Number (CN) and initial abstraction (P0) from Spanish land cover (SIOSE), soil permeability (IGME), and slope. It loads a SIOSE polygon layer from a GPKG and an IGME permeability vector layer (from local file or IGME REST service), and a DEM raster. After clipping to an AOI, it computes slope percentage and classifies into two slope categories (<3% and >=3%). The land cover, soil group (GH and PRIMO_GH), and slope class are combined through spatial intersections. Using a master lookup table mapping a combined index (product of prime numbers PRIMO_U * PRIMO_GH * PTE_P) to CN and P0, the tool generates vector layers (CN_BASE, CAPA_FINAL_CN) with attributes including PRIMO_U, PRIMO_GH, PTE_P, VALOR_U, PO_MM, NC, and DEFINICION, and a raster NC_CURSO with a color ramp representing CN values. A summary report table is also produced.

name: Create PS point grid cells
desc: The script creates a grid (square or hexagon) over a user-defined extent, after handling CRS transformations between geographic (PS points) and projected CRS (project). It clips PS points to the extent, reprojects if necessary, generates the grid, and filters cells that contain both ascending and descending Persistent Scatterers. The output is a vector layer of valid grid cells, optionally saved to file.

name: InSAR East-West and Up-Down decomposition
desc: The script decomposes InSAR Line-of-Sight (LOS) velocities into East-West and Up-Down components using ascending and descending persistent scatterer (PS) point data. It aggregates PS point velocities into a regular grid by computing mean and count per cell, then applies geometric formulas based on satellite incidence and azimuth angles (right-looking convention) to derive horizontal and vertical motion components. Additional derived fields include total velocity magnitude, movement azimuth, and a classification flag (stable, up, down, east, west). Outputs are polygon and centroid vector layers containing the decomposed fields.

name: Generate clipped grid over polygon
desc: The script generates a grid (points, lines, or rectangles) over an input polygon vector layer. It first uses the QGIS native:creategrid processing algorithm to create a grid covering the input layer’s extent with user-defined horizontal and vertical spacing and grid type. Then it extracts only the grid features that intersect the input polygon using native:extractbylocation, producing a clipped grid layer. User preferences (spacing, grid type, verbose logging) are saved for the next run.

name: Reproject Selected Layers via Shortcuts
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin that allows users to assign keyboard shortcuts to target coordinate reference systems (CRS) and reproject selected vector or raster layers to those CRS instantly, replacing the original layers. It includes a management dialog to add, delete, and configure CRS/shortcut pairs, using QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem and processing algorithms for on-the-fly reprojection.

name: Calculate line center points
desc: The script processes a line feature layer by fixing geometries, reprojecting to a chosen CRS, and then using geometry by expression to compute the centroid of the line substring from the midpoint to the start of each line, generating a point layer of those centroids.

name: QGIS workflow: Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Projection
desc: This workflow contains 64 core geospatial operations, including Spatial Analysis And Modeling, Projection, Vector spatial analysis, Vector data attribute editing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Polygonize Outer Road Lines and Join to Zones
desc: The script filters a UIP line layer to extract outer road boundaries (where 'side' attribute contains 'outer'), polygonizes them to create road polygons, then performs a spatial join by location to assign attributes from a reference UIP zone polygon layer based on the largest overlap, producing a final road polygon layer with zone attributes.

name: Segment road frontage and assign coefficients
desc: The script processes road boundary lines from a master plan to segment them into 10-meter segments and assign road-type-based coefficients and frontage types. It first filters features where the side attribute is 'left_outer' or 'right_outer', then splits the resulting lines into 10-meter segments. For each segment, it maps the road type (yolTipi) to a coefficient value (e.g., motorway=2.5, divided road=1.6, road=1.0, pedestrian=0.4) and validates the frontage type from the 'type' field against a predefined list, then writes the output with added 'katsayi' and 'cephe_tipi' fields.

name: Quick Reproject Layers via Hotkeys
desc: The script implements a QGIS plugin to rapidly reproject selected map layers to preset coordinate reference systems (CRS) via keyboard shortcuts. It uses processing algorithms native:reprojectlayer for vectors and gdal:warpreproject for rasters. The plugin assigns shortcuts like Alt+2 to EPSG:32642, and allows users to manage (add/delete) up to 9 CRS-shortcut pairs through a dialog. Outputs are reprojected layers replacing the originals in the QGIS project.

name: Generate attribute-based cluster boundaries
desc: The script partitions input vector features (points, lines, polygons) into clusters based on a specified attribute field, producing a polygon layer of cluster boundaries with member counts. It supports optional boundary clipping, selected-feature-only mode, and applies Voronoi-based partitioning for non-polygon geometries or boundary-sampled polygon partitioning. The final clusters are polygonized, overlaps removed, and pruned to ensure topology. Output is a styled labeled layer.

name: Remove black border from raster
desc: The script removes dark/black borders from georeferenced raster images. It reads the input raster, applies a threshold to detect pixels above a certain value (indicating valid image content), generates a mask, optionally applies morphological closing to preserve valid dark interior features, vectorizes the mask into a polygon, and clips the raster to that polygon, removing the black border. The output is a new GeoTIFF file with the border removed, and optionally with an alpha channel for transparency.

name: Parcel subdivision from building blocks
desc: The script subdivides input polygon features representing building blocks into individual parcels with configurable parameters including target parcel width, width variation, row asymmetry, and fishbone offsets. It processes irregular polygons using oriented minimum bounding boxes, generates division lines along the short axis, and applies width variations and optional asymmetric splitting to create varied parcel sizes. A three-pass merging step removes small fragments below a user-defined threshold. Outputs include parcels with attributes for area, facade information, and unique parcel IDs.

name: API load accumulation in rivers
desc: The script accumulates pharmaceutical loads (APIs) along a river network to compute concentrations under mean and low flow conditions. It takes emission load points and a river network (lines or polygons), splits lines at emission points, accumulates loads downstream using a routing topology defined by NET_ID/NET_TO fields, and calculates concentrations (ng/L) based on accumulated flow (m³/s). It optionally processes monitoring points to extract modeled concentrations and computes dilution ratios using wastewater treatment plant effluent (Q_WWTP). The output includes an accumulated river network layer, monitoring point results, and a dilution ratio layer.

name: Fix river network connectivity
desc: This script preprocesses a river network and aligns it with subcatchment boundaries. It simplifies, snaps, fixes, and merges the river network, then extracts vertices and splits river sections at subcatchment boundaries. After snapping endpoints to subcatchment vertices, it intersects with subcatchments to assign CATCH_ID. It then traverses the network from a user-specified outlet point to assign unique NET_IDs and downstream connectivity (NET_TO), flipping line directions to flow toward the outlet. The outputs are a fixed river network layer with topology and catchment attribution, and a filtered subcatchment layer containing only those intersected by the river.

name: Flow estimation for ungauged subcatchments
desc: The script estimates mean flow and mean low flow for ungauged subcatchments and river sections using a Random Forest model trained on geofactors (elevation, area, slope, land use proportions, precipitation) derived from user-provided layers. It delineates gauged subcatchments, computes spatial statistics for both gauged and ungauged subcatchments, trains or loads a pre-trained model, predicts normalized flow per area, distributes flow to river segments by length, and accumulates downstream flow along the river network. Outputs include vector layers with estimated flows (m³/s) at subcatchment and river levels.

name: Optimize agricultural plot layout
desc: The script designs optimized agricultural unit layouts (strips or mosaics) for a given parcel, using geometric primitives arranged in rows or Hilbert curve patterns. It calculates cultivated area, aisle area, efficiency, and discards small fragments below a threshold. Outputs include vector layers (Layout_Strips, Layout_Mosaics, GPS_Guide_Lines, Hilbert_Path, Unit_Centers, Labels_Mosaics, Labels_Strips, Coord_Layer), labeled centers, coordinate labels, and terminal reports with area and efficiency statistics.

name: Convert raster to GeoPackage tiles
desc: The script converts raster files (GeoTIFF, JP2, ECW, IMG, ASC, VRT) into GeoPackage raster tiles using GDAL via QGIS Processing. It processes each input raster item by applying optional CRS reprojection via `gdal:warpreproject` or direct format conversion via `gdal:translate`, appending rasters as separate raster tables to a single GeoPackage. Output raster tables are configured with tile format (AUTO/PNG/JPEG/WEBP), tile size (256 or 512 pixels), and JPEG quality. The conversion supports dry-run mode, appending to an existing GeoPackage, and error collection through a unified ConversionResult. Progress callbacks report status.

name: Prepare Open Geospatial Enrichment Data
desc: The script prepares OSM roads and facilities, WorldPop population rasters, Copernicus DEM elevation/slope/ruggedness, and ESA WorldCover land cover for a user-defined area of interest (AOI) in QGIS. It downloads data from Overpass API, WorldPop, Copernicus DEM COG, and ESA WorldCover S3, clips or merges rasters to the AOI bounding box, caches data, and writes GeoPackage (vector) and GeoTIFF (raster) outputs along with a manifest file for tracking.

name: Clip vector layers to DWG
desc: The script clips visible vector layers in QGIS to a user-defined bounding box and exports the result as a DWG file. It first captures a box drawn on the map canvas, then clips each layer using QGIS processing algorithm 'native:clip', handles polygon boundary lines separately for accurate representation, applies symbology, writes a temporary DXF with QgsDxfExport, post-processes the DXF to remove invisible hatch entities and force ByLayer attributes, and finally invokes the ODA File Converter in a background task to convert the DXF to DWG.

name: Allocate origin-destination flows on Delaunay network
desc: The script performs All-or-Nothing (AoN) traffic allocation over a Delaunay triangulation network built from input centroids. It creates the network by triangulating centroids, extracting unique edges, and constructing a graph with edge lengths as cost. For each origin-destination pair, it runs Dijkstra shortest-path routing and loads the entire flow onto the least-cost path. The output is a line layer with total flow per edge and optional directional volumes (flow_ab, flow_ba).

name: Per-boundary kernel density estimation
desc: The plugin performs iterative kernel density analysis on point or line features across multiple polygon boundaries. It clips input features to each boundary, optionally converts lines to points, computes a per-boundary Silverman rule-of-thumb bandwidth or uses a fixed search radius, runs a heatmap KDE, composites the density on a zero-filled base to avoid gaps, clips the result to the exact boundary, and then merges all valid tiles using maximum cell value in overlap areas. The final merged raster is further clipped to the boundary union and edge-refined, loaded into the map canvas, and a log file with per-boundary bandwidth statistics is saved.

name: Vectorize Raster Values into Polygons
desc: The plugin processes a raster layer to generate polygon vector layers based on user-defined unique values or ranges. It first optionally clips the raster to a mask extent, reclassifies the raster to a binary mask per value/range, polygonizes the reclassified raster, clips the resulting vectors with a mask layer if provided, joins attribute tables with labels, and calculates areas in m² and ha. Outputs vector layers are added to the QGIS project.

name: Harmonize rasters for suitability analysis
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm aligns multiple input rasters to a common grid geometry (CRS, extent, pixel size) using GDAL Warp. It accepts optional snap raster, target extent, resolution, resampling method, and nodata value. Outputs include a preview raster (copy of the first aligned result), a folder with aligned GeoTIFFs named sequentially, and a manifest file summarizing alignment parameters. The process ensures all outputs have identical grid structure, making them directly stackable for multi-criteria decision analysis.

name: QGIS workflow: Vector spatial analysis, Projection
desc: This workflow contains 20 core geospatial operations, including Vector spatial analysis, Projection, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data import. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Waterbody extraction from multispectral indices
desc: The script extracts waterbodies from multispectral satellite imagery using a decision-tree based on NDVI, MNDWI, and NWI water indices. It computes these indices from user-specified bands (Blue, Green, Red, NIR, SWIR), applies a raster mask formula (MNDWI>0 AND NWI>0 AND NDVI<0.1), performs raster noise removal via sieve filtering, polygonizes the mask, extracts water features, and optionally smooths vector edges. Outputs include the three index rasters, the final binary water mask raster, and a smoothed waterbody polygon, all reprojected to EPSG:4326.

name: Calculate Water Utilization Capability Index
desc: The script calculates the Water Utilization Capability Index (IKP Air) for grid cells by integrating water supply, water quality, and water demand components. It first computes water availability per grid by intersecting a water provisioning index layer (JLH) with river basin boundaries (WS), distributing basin-level water supply proportionally based on a water service indicator (ije_pa). It then joins a pollution index table (Indeks Pencemar) to calculate contaminated and usable water. Population and land-use layers are joined to derive total water demand, combining land-based demand (using land class weights and area) and population-based demand (43.2 m³/year per capita doubled). The final IKP is computed as total demand divided by usable water, classified into five capability classes (Sangat Tinggi to Sangat Rendah), and assigned scores 1–5. Outputs include a polygon layer with fields IKPAIR, KIKPAIR, SIKPAIR, air_ws, air_layak, demand components, and auxiliary indicators.

name: Compute biodiversity utilization capacity index
desc: The script calculates the Biodiversity Utilization Capacity Index (IKP Kehati) for a given year by integrating two composite indicators: the Composite Index of Environmental Services (BCPI) derived from water regulation, carbon storage, food provisioning, and biodiversity grid layers; and the Biodiversity Index (BI) derived from karst/gambut distribution, habitat diversity, RTE (rare/threatened/endemic) taxa, and forest connectivity. Spatial processing includes field joins, field calculators, re-projection, buffering, intersection, union, and classification to produce polygon and grid output layers with the final index and categorical classes (very low to very high).

name: Calculate Land Utilization Capability Index
desc: The script calculates the Land Utilization Capability Index (IKP Lahan) for grid cells by integrating land cover, forest function, food provision capacity (KPGN), population distribution, and ecological footprint parameters. It performs a series of spatial intersections to determine eligible land for food and settlement, computes area in hectares, joins population data, and applies formulas to derive KEB_HA (ecological footprint need), KET_HA (available land), and ultimately IKPLHN. The index is categorized into classes (e.g., 'Sangat Rendah', 'Rendah', 'Sedang', etc.) and output as both a polygon layer of land availability and a grid layer with IKP values, supporting environmental carrying capacity assessments within D3TLH.

name: Compute Air Utilization Capability Index
desc: The script calculates the Air Utilization Capability Index (IKP Udara) by integrating PM2.5 concentration (from raster), climate projection (IPS vector with SKOR), and land carrying capacity (PKU year-based grid) to generate a per-polygon and per-grid index, including classification into five levels. It processes PM2.5 raster reclassification, calculates IP and IKU indices, interpolates IKU using IDW, performs zonal statistics, and intersects layers to compute the final IKP Udara index, classified into 'Sangat Rendah' to 'Sangat Tinggi'.

name: Calculate D3TLH Composite Index
desc: This script integrates multiple environmental carrying capacity indices (IKP Air, IKP Udara, IKP Lahan, IKP Kehati) and an environmental behavior index (IPRLH) into a single composite D3TLH index. It sequentially joins the input grids using a common ID field, computes a weighted average of the normalized scores for the four IKP components, classifies them into qualitative categories (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi), assigns quantitative scores, joins the IPRLH table by province, and then calculates the final D3TLH as the average of the integrated IKP score and the IPRLH. The output is a vector layer with the D3TLH field, designed for environmental planning and monitoring in Indonesia.

name: Calculate habitat biodiversity ecosystem index
desc: Calculates the Habitat and Biodiversity Supporting Ecosystem Service Index (IJLH_PHK) using land cover, ecoregion, and special criteria layers. The workflow intersects land cover with ecoregion, joins scoring tables for Keanekaragaman Bentang Alam (KBA), Keanekaragaman Vegetasi (KVA), and land cover (PL), computes a weighted index (weights: ecoregion 0.24, vegetation 0.16, land cover 0.60), applies overrides for special criteria (e.g., designated conservation areas, savanna in certain provinces, water bodies), and generates either a polygon or grid output with categorized index (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi). Supports national or island-specific scoring modes.

name: Calculate Air Quality Regulation Index
desc: The script calculates the Air Quality Regulation ecosystem service index (JLH_PKU) from land cover and ecoregion data based on D3TLH 2024 guidelines. It intersects the land cover and ecoregion layers, joins scoring tables for ecoregion (KBA), vegetation (KVA), and land cover (PL), computes a weighted sum (0.15*S_EK + 0.25*S_VE + 0.60*S_PL) to produce the index, and optionally aggregates to a grid by area-weighted averaging. The output includes the index value and a categorical classification (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi).

name: Calculate water regulation ecosystem service index
desc: The script computes the Flood Regulation Ecosystem Service Index (JLH_PGA) based on land cover, ecoregion, and scoring tables from the D3TLH guidelines. It processes user-provided vector layers: Penutup Lahan (land cover) and Ekoregion (ecoregion). The workflow includes intersecting land cover with ecoregion, joining scoring CSVs for KBA, KVA, and Land Cover (either national or island-specific), and calculating a weighted sum (0.28*S_EK + 0.12*S_VE + 0.60*S_PL). Special criteria reassign a score of 5 for water body types. The resulting index is categorized into five classes (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi). Output can be polygon (preserving original geometry) or grid (with proportional aggregation and dominant land cover via MCA). The final output is a vector layer with standardized field names and the index categories.

name: Map water provision ecosystem service index
desc: This QGIS processing algorithm calculates the Water Provision Ecosystem Service Index (JLH_PYA) by spatially intersecting land cover and ecoregion layers, joining attribute scores from CSV lookup tables for ecoregion (S_EK), vegetation (S_VE), and land cover (S_PL), then computing the weighted sum (0.32*S_EK + 0.08*S_VE + 0.60*S_PL). It outputs polygon or grid features with the index and categorical classification (Very Low to Very High). For kabupaten/kota analysis, water body classes are automatically assigned a perfect score of 5.

name: Calculate Food Provision Ecosystem Service Index
desc: The script computes the Food Provision Ecosystem Service Index (JLH_PGN) by intersecting land cover with ecoregion, joining ecological scores (KBA, KVA) from CSV tables, joining land-cover scores specific to each Indonesian island, and calculating a weighted sum using fixed coefficients (0.28, 0.12, 0.60). It can output the index as polygons or aggregate it into a user-supplied grid using area-weighting, and classifies the index into five qualitative categories (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi). The final output includes standardized fields for the index and category.

name: Calculate Carbon Sequestration-Storage Index
desc: This algorithm calculates the Carbon Sequestration and Storage Ecosystem Service Index (JLH PPK) by intersecting land cover and ecoregion vector layers, joining scoring tables for ecoregion (KBA_250), vegetation (KVA_250), and land cover (PL) based on national or Kabupaten/Kota settings, then applying a weighted formula (0.20 ecoregion + 0.20 vegetation + 0.60 land cover). The output can be polygonal or gridded; when gridded, values are proportionally weighted by area within each grid cell. The result includes a numeric index and a categorical classification (Sangat Rendah to Sangat Tinggi).

name: Model Population Distribution
desc: The script models population distribution by allocating population counts from administrative units to grid cells (SGSRI grid). It first uses a multi-criteria algorithm (MCA) to assign administrative region names to grid cells. Then, it calculates grid-level influence weights based on land cover types (using separate scoring tables for Papua and non-Papua) and road network classes, yielding weighted scores WPL and WJLN per grid cell. After summing total weights per administrative unit (WADM), the population count is proportionally distributed to each grid cell to produce POPGRIDYY. The final output is a vector layer of the grid with fields ID, WADM, POPM, WPLyy, WJLNyy, WGRIDyy, WADMyy, and POPGRIDyy.

name: Generate SGSRI grid with administrative attributes
desc: The script generates a hierarchical square-cell grid based on the Indonesian Multi-scale Grid System (SGSRI), using a specified spatial extent and grid size. It assigns unique grid IDs based on cell coordinates relative to the SGSRI origin (90°E, 15°S). Then, it enriches each grid cell with administrative region attributes (Desa/Kelurahan, Kecamatan, Kabupaten/Kota, Provinsi) by intersecting with an input administrative boundary layer and applying a maximum coverage area rule. Optionally, it clips the output grid to the input boundary. Output is a polygon vector layer with fields: ID, WADMKD, WADMKC, WADMKK, WADMPR.

name: Calculate dominant attribute per grid by MCA
desc: The script calculates the dominant attribute from a secondary polygon layer for each polygon in a grid layer based on the largest combined area of intersection (MCA method). It performs intersection, dissolve by ID and attribute, area calculation in EPSG:3857, finds maximum area per grid cell, and joins the dominant class back to the original grid. Output is a grid vector layer with a new column of the dominant attribute.

name: QGIS workflow: Geometry, Data processing
desc: This workflow contains 22 core geospatial operations, including Geometry, Data processing, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Spatial Analysis And Modeling. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

name: Calculate urban morphology metrics
desc: The script calculates urban morphology indicators (footprint ratio, floor area ratio, building volume, and building height standard deviation) for two sets of spatial units (SA1 and SA2) using building footprint geometry and height attributes. It loads unit and building layers, reprojects to EPSG:7856, computes unit grid area, intersects buildings with units, calculates per-unit building area sum and volume sum, then derives FP (total building footprint area / grid area), FAR (total building volume / grid area), V (mean building volume), and AHSD (standard deviation of building heights). Results are written back to output shapefiles after removing temporary unique ID fields.

name: Zonal mean calculation for remote sensing indices
desc: The script computes zonal mean values of multiple remote sensing indices (EVI, LST, NDBSI, Tasseled Cap Wetness, and three white-sky albedo components: nir, shortwave, vis) within statistical area polygons (SA2 for training, SA1 for prediction). It first reprojects the zone shapefiles to EPSG:7856, fixes any invalid geometries, then iterates over the raster files, warping each to the same CRS. Using QGIS native zonal statistics, it calculates the pixel mean of each raster band within each polygon, renames the output fields to meaningful index names (EVI, LST, NDBSI, WET, nir, shortwave, vis), and saves the enriched shapefiles (SA2_remote.shp, SA1_remote.shp) to the preprocessing intermediate folder, adding them as map layers in QGIS.

name: Calculate urban building morphology indicators
desc: The script calculates urban morphology indicators (FP, FAR, V, AHSD) for two statistical area layers (SA1 and SA2) using building footprint data. It reprojects both unit and building layers to EPSG:7856 for accurate area and volume computations, performs an intersection to associate building footprints with units, then for each unit computes footprint ratio (FP = total building area / unit area), floor area ratio (FAR = total building volume / unit area), mean building volume (V), and standard deviation of building heights (AHSD). The resulting indicators are written as new shapefiles (SA1_morphology.shp and SA2_morphology.shp) and added to the QGIS project.

name: Extract zonal means of remote sensing indices
desc: The script reprojects SA2 and SA1 shapefiles to EPSG:7856, then for each remote sensing raster (EVI, LST, NDBSI, WET, nir, shortwave, vis) in the training and prediction folders, it warps the raster to the same CRS, computes zonal statistics (mean) for each polygon, renames fields to corresponding index names, and saves the enriched shapefiles as SA2_remote.shp and SA1_remote.shp.
